outcome: oni-measure balance_kept: every input moves the fingerprint, no look does (twin), and on a scene every pixel-moving input moves the outcome while no look moves a bit of it, on a roll and alone; on roll #8 the kept half decode reads the filters LibRaw's own reads (twin: a shifted window reads others). oni-settings auto_balance: the key round-trips, a rewrite carries it, a Swift key survives the balance's write, a sidecar without it reads as before, none is seeded (twins). oni-measure kept: a reading that panics leaves the next to read (twin: its copy decoded again). oni-core: a kept outcome serves its own fingerprint alone (twin). Window balance_kept: a kept balance lands within the call with no reading, alone and six together (twins: an input moved reads each again, counting); De-dust's strokes are read once on leaving the tab (twin: in and out unchanged reads nothing). Window transition: the camera matched writes no setting, the frame opened keeping only its balance under Rust's key.

title: A measuring copy reads the half decode kept on disk, and Edit Together keeps its decodes there
detail: A RAW asked at a side LibRaw reads at half size is the editor's half decode pixel for pixel (pinned.c chooses half size on the sensor's side alone), so a kept half decode whose long side reaches the side asked serves it, in about 15 ms instead of LibRaw's 0.35-0.5 s; such a copy writes nothing to disk, so thumbnails and roll previews add no decode there. Edit Together decodes its frames at the editor's half size, kept on disk as the editor's are, so its balance read ahead and the frames reopened read them back. Every kept decode is keyed by the installed rendition table too, so a camera matched later never serves a decode folded without its matrix.
outcome: oni-decode half_kept on roll #8: the copy served from the kept half decode equals LibRaw's own bit for bit, and a preview-side copy keeps no decode (twin: a copy longer than half the sensor is LibRaw's whole decode, never the half one). oni-measure balance_kept roll8: the balance read through the kept decode equals LibRaw's on two frames.

title: A slide is edited as a plain RAW: no roll measure, no dyes or ceiling, decoded at 5500 K, Auto Levels on a click
detail: Owner's call beyond Swift, for ConversionMode::Positive only. Prepare the Roll on a slide roll walks Film and Flat-Field alone (Base, Flags and Window skipped), its key reads PREPARE N FRAMES and writes each frame on the roll's film and flat-field with no roll reference and its look at rest (roll::slide). An unmeasured slide raises no roll-guide banner nor Roll tab warning and opens in the editor without being sent to Prepare; Auto White Balance reads a slide as it stands and writes no roll (Outcome.reference is now optional). Dye Separation and Density Ceiling are hidden for slides; the render takes dose 0 and the axis' base ceiling, so an old sidecar's family, dose or ceiling no longer applies. A slide's RAW is balanced at 5500 K, tint 0 (oni_decode::SLIDE_KELVIN, Robertson's 175 and 200 mired nodes interpolated, Bradford to D65 as before); the reading, the disk decode cache and the kept previews key on it, the per-camera rendition still folds after it. AUTO LEVELS in the Levels block lays one black and one white read on the RGB composite (the darkest channel's low tail, the lightest's high one) on all three windows, gains at rest, one undo step over the targets; on any other film the same key is Classic's two steps. Levels has no master tab: equal per-channel windows are that RGB level at the density stage and keep the sidecar Swift's. Negative and B&W unchanged (5 frames of roll #8 measured byte-identical before and after). On the T7 slides (Sony ARW, own sidecars, dose 0.6 E-6, ceiling at base) the mean output B/G moves 1.13 to 1.07 on 326 and 2.42 to 2.64 on 329: dose 0 alone pushes blue up (1.15, 2.86), 5500 K pulls it back. Checks: window slides (twins: a negative roll walks to its measure, a negative's Auto levels aligns each channel), oni-measure positive_levels, oni-decode slide neutral and cache key, oni-pipeline dose and ceiling, prepare slides steps, roll guide predicate. The Swift check density_axis_sense_is_measured_in_every_mode now holds a slide's ceiling flat (its twin: a negative and a black and white frame still move).

title: The Scanner face renders a slide at a sensible exposure
detail: A positive on the Scanner face sat 1.1 to 1.4 stops over its Pro render (three ARW slides, mean luminance 2.2 to 2.7 times Pro's, on both machines): the ONI and Frontier looks add about a stop (OniLook exposure 0.9976 and its S), fitted on a negative entering them with Lighting's 1.5 rest left out, while a slide rests at 0 and loses nothing. The machine now enters the look at resting_exposure(mode) - 1.5: -1.5 for a slide, 0 for a negative or B&W, which render bit for bit as before. Slides land 0.25 to 0.4 stop over Pro, as negatives do (0.2 to 0.5), no clipping added. Pipeline::chain takes the machine's settings, so a check renders the former chain.
outcome: oni-pipeline/tests/scanner_positive.rs: a slide at rest within 0.5 stop of Pro on both machines and no more clipped (twin: the former entry sits +0.9 stop and fails); negatives and B&W on both machines bit for bit against the former settings with clicks and contrast (twin: a slide differs). Real files: Roll #8 frames 6432 and 6433 hash identical before and after on Pro and both machines.

title: Prepare the Roll on slides: one measuring window, each frame's own RGB Auto Levels
detail: Owner's call beyond Swift, positive only: Prepare the Roll on a slide roll walks Film, Flat-Field and the Window step again, the negative's component and gesture. The one window is laid on every frame as geometry.measure_window, in the scan's fractions as roll::start lays a negative's, so each frame sees it in its own crop. The final key, MEASURE N FRAMES, runs on each ticked frame the positive AUTO LEVELS key through that window (key::slide_levelled): one black and white on the frame's RGB composite, gains at rest, three equal per-channel levels, no roll reference; off the interface thread, counted and stoppable, landed as one gallery step through land_roll, so undo restores every frame's levels and window and a second run re-levels each frame. The measuring copies come from the measurer's decode cache. Base and Flags stay skipped: no roll vote, so a flag would keep nothing out; a flag a negative draft left counts for nothing on a slide roll. #706 holds: a slide never prepared opens with no window. Window step help, Film Type and Auto Levels help in English, French and Spanish. Negative and B&W paths untouched.
outcome: oni-measure/tests/slide_roll.rs: three synthetic slides of different exposures each get their own RGB black and white through the window, all three different, gains 0, per-channel equal; the same frames without their near-white border read the same (twin: a window over the whole scan moves the white); a negative roll of the same frames still combines into one reference with aligned gains; the window is the same absolute rect on frames of different crops (twin: their in-crop windows differ). Window check slides: the slide roll walks Film then Window, MEASURE 3 FRAMES lays one window and three different levels, the Crop tab shows the window unarmed, one gallery undo restores every frame and redo lays them again; an unprepared slide opens with no window. Real slides (temp copy of three test Positif sidecars, Swift's window): 326 black 1.0346 white 2.8871, 329 0.8195 / 2.4974, 331 0.9734 / 2.9755, about 0.2 s a frame.

title: The Auto levels key on a prepared slide finds Prepare's levels, press after press
detail: Measured before any change: on the owner's own frames (four Lumix DC-S1R RW2 of Photos Digitales, his camera table installed) and twelve T7 ARW slides, Prepare's per-frame levels then the key, and the key three times, land the same levels to the last digit, through oni-measure and through the real window (open folder, PREPARE, MEASURE, the key pressed four times). Both read the same pre-levels image (truncated lays the graduation on the windows), through the same window and decode, and write absolute ends. The owner's sidecars show why another result came: at 12:58:38 one write laid rest levels (0.90309/3) on every frame not touched since, as a step undone does, so the key then read from rest, not from Prepare's levels. title: A slide roll's black is picked, and each slide is levelled on it channel by channel
detail: Owner's call beyond Swift (2026-10-31): slides come out magenta even scanned well. Prepare the Roll on a slide roll walks the base step again, titled Pick the Black: a click on unexposed film (the black border or the gap between frames) is read as each channel's black at rest gains (key::base on the positive). Each slide then takes that black on its three channels and each channel's own white from its reading (auto_levels::slide_points, key::slide_read); with no black picked, the composite's one black and white on every channel stands as before (#920). Flags stay skipped. The editor's AUTO LEVELS keeps the composite, as no black is stored on a slide. Checks: positive_levels a_slide_on_a_picked_black... (twin: none picked gives the composite), prepare slides steps (twin: a negative walks base and flags). Texts in English, French and Spanish. A click on the scan moves on to the next step the roll walks (a slide's window, a negative's flags) and picks nothing on a scan not laid yet, whose size is none. ONI_BENCH=prepare starts on the gallery when no photo was left open and walks a slide roll's black.
outcome: ONI_BENCH=prepare on a copy of three slides of roll 2026-10-30 (P1073169-71): black picked on P1073169's border, 3 slides measured, landed and undone in 3.3 s. The window check slides now picks a black and finds one black for the roll and each channel's own white; it caught the pick going to the skipped flags step.

title: A slide's chroma is aligned on its 10 % and 90 %, then one black and one white are placed
detail: Owner's call (2026-10-31): with #997 a slide roll still came out red. Prepare the Roll and Auto Levels on a slide now read each channel's 10 % and 90 % of its counts at rest gains, bring them onto green's (CHROMA_SHARES), and place one black and one white on the aligned channels' outermost ends; both steps land as each channel's own window (auto_levels::slide_points). #997's black pick is withdrawn: a slide roll skips the base step again and the base click moves to the next step the roll walks. title: A slide's greys are read on its cells, three channels together
detail: #1002 aligned each channel's own 10 % and 90 % of counts, so red, green and blue were read on different parts of the frame and a coloured subject set the shadows' grey: magenta shadows stayed. The blocks reading now hands its kept cells (each cell's median, three channels together, and its luma) with the histogram; a slide's key sorts the cells by luma, takes the median of each channel over the cells between 5 % and 15 % and between 85 % and 95 % (CHROMA_MARKS, CHROMA_BAND), brings those two colours onto green's, then lays one black and one white on the aligned channels' ends. Each channel's black and white are no longer held inside 0…1: a held one darkened that channel's shadows against the others'. Auto Levels on a slide reads the same way (key::levels routes a slide to key::slide_read; keyed is Classic's alone). Check: positive_levels a slide's magenta shadows and bluish lights land grey with a red subject whose blue is the frame's darkest (twins: each channel's own 10 % and 90 %, each channel's own ends, the composite's one window leave the shadows magenta).
outcome: On the owner's slides of 2026-10-30, through each slide's own measuring frame, cells sorted by brightness after the curves: P1073170's shadows from ±0.030 to ±0.012 off grey, P1073151's about as before, P1073169's mid-dark tones still magenta (g -0.053, b +0.041 at 45-55 %), a cast or the subject's own colour.

title: A slide's greys are read at 10 % and 90 % of its tones, and its near-grey midtones land grey too
detail: #1003 read the greys on the cells ranked 10 % and 90 % darkest: on a slide whose frame is half black the 10 % fell in crushed blacks, and the magenta the eye sees sits in the midtones, which two points per channel cannot reach. The marks now stand at 10 % and 90 % of the way from the darkest cell's luma to the lightest's (a band of 5 % of that span each side, five cells at least). After the two-point alignment and the one black and white, the midtones (30 to 70 % of the span) are read on the quarter of their cells nearest grey; when those stand within NEUTRAL_CHROMA of grey (Auto Color's rule: a scene of colour, a blue sea, is left alone), red's and blue's black, white and mid are solved together (three_point, the gamma bisected inside the mid's range) so the shadows, the midtones and the lights all land on green's grey. Checks: positive_levels the magenta shadows, grey midtones and bluish lights land grey (twins: each channel's own 10 %/90 %, each channel's ends and the composite leave the shadows magenta), a slide whose midtones are a blue sea keeps them (twin: grey midtones snap).
outcome: Owner's slides of 2026-10-30, each through its own measuring frame, cells after the curves, 45-55 % band against the sidecars at rest: P1073169 g -0.057 b +0.064 to g -0.009 b +0.024; P1073172 -0.037/+0.047 to -0.009/+0.016; P1073170 within 0.02 of grey from the shadows to the midtones; P1073151 shadows back to grey, its sea still blue (+0.056 from +0.093).

Without it, ONI downloads the pinned 18.0 installer from Adobe's versioned link (1.8 GB, streamed with its count, a stall of 60 s gives up), checks Adobe's signature (pkgutil: Developer ID Installer Adobe Inc. JQ525L2MZD, notarised; Authenticode O=Adobe Inc. on Windows), opens it for the person's licence and password, then converts. Then the owner's choice: Keep the new DNGs only (Recommended, the NEFs to the system Trash through the injected discard) or Keep the incompatible NEF files; either way the listing drops an HE NEF whose DNG stands beside it. The editor then opens the frame's DNG, the roll comes back on its frames' DNGs. title: Contact sheets lie on black whatever their frames, the logo under a full row only
detail: Owner's call. Frames all positives no longer lie on a white sheet numbered in dark red: every sheet, on the canvas, in the export's column and in the file, is black with orange numbers and a white logo (Canvas.inks; positive(), the positive inks, Exporting.sheet-positive and edge-print-positive gone). The tree's pick knew nothing of a selection made elsewhere; a ⌘ or ⇧ click beside a photo now starts from the frames shown together when the tree's pick does not hold them. Seen on a shot of both columns slid over.

title: Version 1.5.4
detail: oni-app 1.5.4, carrying frames together's fixes and the editor's design changes (#1061-#1070); the 1.5 welcome and splash kept.

title: A Mac window's first frame owes nothing to the occlusion state, so a window can no longer stay away
detail: Report from an Intel MacBook Pro with a 4K screen (releases issue 13): the window does not show until the screen is unplugged and plugged back. wgpu's Metal surface refuses a drawable while AppKit's occlusionState lacks Visible, and Slint's backend then orders the window in at alpha 0 until a first frame lands; Apple says only that a fully transparent window may count as visible. Where it does not, nothing ever shows and the log holds no error, until any event turns the state over. Emulated on the 1.5.4 binary with an injected library (tools/window_recorder.m) answering not visible at alpha 0: the window stays on screen at alpha 0, no nextDrawable in 9 s; the answer turned truthful, the window shows at once. On this M2 Max the real answer comes 12 to 55 ms after ordering in. vendor/wgpu-hal is 30.0.1 with upstream's #10302, merged but in no release: a surface never seen visible acquires. The first frame is now drawn before the window is ordered in, so Slint's alpha 0 never engages on any Mac (recorded: nextDrawable before makeKeyAndOrderFront, no setAlphaValue); under the same emulation the window stands at alpha 1 with its frames. The x86_64 slice runs the same sequence under Rosetta and the 4K screen at 2x showed nothing different. Not run on an Intel Mac: whether this is the reporter's cause awaits their log, and their second symptom (resizing moves the elements, not the window) does not reproduce here. Check: first_frame::a_first_drawable_owes_nothing_to_the_occlusion_state on real AppKit and Metal with no window on screen (twins: seen visible then covered, a window is refused; visible again, it acquires); it fails with upstream's gate put back.

title: The log says what the system shows of the main window
detail: A window that stays away or keeps its old size raises no error, so a report could not tell them apart. on_screen.rs writes the screens (pixels, scale, rate) when the window is shown; three seconds later, and once settled after each resize or change of screen, AppKit's alpha, ordering and occlusion answer, the frame, the view, the Metal layer and the drawable, with the frames drawn (hz::frames); main.rs writes each turn of the occlusion state. Read on the Mac under the emulation of #1072: alpha 1.00, frames drawn, occlusion says not visible.

title: Version 1.5.5
detail: oni-app 1.5.5, carrying a Mac window's first frame free of the occlusion state and the log of what the system shows (#1072, #1073); the 1.5 welcome and splash kept.

title: Auto De-dust: a reading past the roll's window under a veil, then one patch per speck ringed
detail: Beyond Swift, owner's ask. De-dust's Automatic block holds two keys and neither runs unasked. DETECT reads the framed frame whole at full resolution (oni-measure/src/dust.rs, about 220 ms on 26 Mpx once decoded) and shows, under a veil, every pixel past the window: the roll's black and white and its gains when the frame is on one, else the frame's own. REMOVE writes one correction per speck ringed, one undo step, its patch made as a hand's. A shape stays out unless it is 3 to 8192 pixels, 16 clear of the frame's edge, and its edge jumps sharply and neutrally: 2 pixels off, the least channel's median jump is 0.2 density or more and 0.6 or more of the most's. Measured on 47 frames (roll #8, Lumix 2026-10-30): pixels past the window alone are shadow grain, lamps and glints, thousands of shapes a frame; a glint's jump is 0.05 to 0.17 with its blue up to five times its red, the one real speck's 0.34 on all three. Exactly that speck is kept on the 47 frames, and a second reading over its patch finds nothing. A stroke follows the shape's longest walk, its radius the farthest pixel plus 8: at plus 4 the speck's soft edge left a ghost, at plus 8 none. Known limit: dust inside the window is not read (the three strokes painted on P1073209 stand at density 0.66 to 1.09 under a white of 1.16 to 1.27), which the owner's next look decides. Checks: oni-measure dust tests with twins, app/dedusting/auto.rs tests, window check auto_dust, ONI_BENCH=autodust on a real frame, dust_census for the whole roll.

title: Auto De-dust's Sensitivity slider reads further inside the roll's window and never loses a speck it found
detail: Owner's ask, once use had met the constants of #1075. At rest it reads as #1075 did; along its track it moves the window's dense end up to 0.8 density inside the window, by levels of 0.2, and lowers the jump a speck must make from 0.2 to 0.1. The clear end stays, the scene's own shadows crowding it. A single threshold loses a speck as it rises: the hook on P1073201 merges with the highlight beside it at 0.6 inside. So every level is read once, 226 to 866 ms on 24 to 26 Mpx, each shape keeps its level and jump, and a sensitivity only filters them, so a notch reads no pixel and everything found below stays found, a speck read at two levels counting once, whole. Measured on nine frames at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %: the roll #8 frames, which the owner calls clean, read 0, 0, 0 to 3, 1 to 32, 3 to 82, all of it image; P1073201 reads 1, 1, 1, 4, 55. The rings let the eye judge before REMOVE writes. Kept across photos and launches under autoDustSensitivity; a double press rests it. Checks: dust tests (reads further inside, a speck stays found, nested shapes count once, with twins), window check auto_dust along the track and back, by callback and by the window's own pointer, ONI_BENCH=autodust. The three strokes on P1073209, used as ground truth in #1075, carry the same radius and point count and lie in a screenshot tool's folder: they may be scripted, not a hand's.

title: Auto De-dust reads the window's dense end alone, and a notch of its slider is one dispatch of a kernel
detail: Owner's two asks. A negative shows what passes its whites, a positive what passes its blacks, nothing at the other end: on P1073201 the pixels shown at rest fall from 20 851 683 to 21, and the side that told them apart goes. The owner also felt the slider slow and named the cure: all is known once read, only a texture is left to draw. A notch laid a 25 MB mask on the CPU and uploaded it, 32 ms on the hand's thread on the dev build. The reading now keeps, per texel of a 3072-side map (Rg8Uint, 12.8 MB), the first notch its pixels show from, past the window then as dust, each cell the earliest of its pixels so nothing fades; display/dust.wgsl compares it with the notch into a texture Slint samples, rewritten in place, its CPU reference dust_mask beside it. Measured through the track in the real app: 75 to 138 us a notch on the hand's thread, nothing read or uploaded; the rings are renewed only where a speck comes or goes. Past pixels now grow continuously with the slider instead of by levels; the shapes stay read at five insets. Reading a frame takes 194 to 695 ms, down from 226 to 866 ms, the clear end no longer gathered. The same pixels read at two insets now count once, which the first version's filter hid and the map's order showed. Checks: dust tests with twins on both films, the kernel against its reference with a twin, window check auto_dust by callback and pointer, ONI_BENCH=autodust.

title: A Detect pressed while the frame decodes reads once the frame lands, on every route
detail: Owner's report: pressed before the photo finished loading, the key stayed on Reading the photo for good, and took no further press. The ask was looked at again only when a full-resolution build landed, and an opening that brings the full resolution itself runs no build: the Settings' whole decode on a RAW, or a frame no larger than the preview, once its thumbnail is drawn and no preview is in memory, as on a second launch. The ask is now looked at on the 100 ms pulse, whichever way the full resolution came, and the build's landing no longer calls it; a frame that cannot be read, or leaving De-dust, drops it. Seen in the owner's log (fullDecode on, no build line in the session) and reproduced by the window check auto_dust::a_detect_pressed_before_the_frame_landed_reads_once_it_lands, which times out before the fix and needs no RAW.

title: The log says nothing of the person using the app: every line masked on its way out, names marked in the notices
detail: Owner's question: do the logs leak personal data? Measured on the 1.5.5 binary: the raw oni.log held whole paths ('Not found' with a disk's and folders' names), as only a sealed report was scrubbed; a sealed report kept a phone's name and whatever followed a comma or a bracket in a path. Every line is now masked on the log thread (anonymity::scrubbed), so the file, stderr, the console's Copy and a report read the same. A name inside a notice goes through oni_i18n::named (Unicode's isolates): the log masks it as <name>, told, say and advise lift the marks for the screen, which shows what it showed. Marked: opening refusals, thumbnails, phone names, a measure's left-out frames, a carry's and a trash's refused files, a frame with nothing to balance. A path ends at a clause's separator, a bracket it did not open or its last closing quote, so commas, brackets and apostrophes in folder names stay inside; a network path starts one. scripts/release-build now builds both Mac architectures, source paths remapped and the linker's debug map stripped, so a binary and a panic's backtrace name no folder or account of the build machine. Checks: timing's child writes a real log file with private names (twin: the same line unmasked holds them); every catalogue template naming something bare must mark it or be listed as never logged (twin: a planted template is caught); a window check that the screen shows the path whole, without marks. Real app, French: 'shown · Ouvrir · Introuvable : <name>', no private word in the file or on stderr. Limit: a bare name with no slash inside an error text from outside the app is not seen. Not run on Windows.

title: Two real-roll checks state the roll and the rule as they are
detail: Both fail only with ONI_RAW_DIR set. Reset to Default drops every crop (owner's call of 2026-10-31); its check still asked for the crop kept, and passed on any roll without a crop. It now asks for the crop gone, undo bringing the bytes back being its twin. The sidecar round trip accepts a frame the app has rewritten at the current format, as a working copy holds some.

title: CLAUDE.md's hard rules: the log says nothing of the user, and never a patch
detail: Owner's philosophy: nothing is patched; a problem is rectified at its source, simplifying rather than adding. Rule 8 states it for every agent.

title: The app's own window opens as the starter, naming each step of the launch, then grows into the app
detail: Owner's call after releases issue 13 (an Intel MacBook Pro whose interface never appeared behind the splash): no floating splash window, no 3.33 s minimum. The main window opens at once at the starter's size (the version's picture over a band in the app's grey), runs each step of the launch one event-loop turn apart, a frame of the band drawn between two, says the step under way, the launch's time, the steps done with their times and a bar, then waits on the kernels' compilation (counted, n of 27) and takes the app's size in the same turn. Each step is written to the log ('boot: <step> in N ms'), with the macOS version and whether an Intel build runs under Rosetta, so the next report from that Mac says where a launch stops. The two-window hand-over, the cause class the issue pointed at, is gone. The kernels read finished however their thread ends, a panic included. Checks: launch::the_starter_says_each_step_then_grows_into_the_app_and_the_notice_covers_the_window (each step on the band while it runs, the window at the starter's size then the app's, the app opened once; twin: kernels under way hold the starter past its last step); the bar's fraction (twin: counts past their totals never pass full); the kernels' finishing (twin: a compilation under way is not finished). Real app on the M2: starter at 1.9 s, app at 2.3 s, visible. Not run on an Intel Mac.

title: Building the app is six steps on the starter's band, its own parts timed in the log
detail: Owner's ask: the launch's longest step (2.1 s on the M2 with the owner's library) said as much as it can. Shell::with_window is now standing (state and controller: render worker, canvas device, painter and disk state, preferences and language, library index, display kernel, flat fields with the navigator and the export card, the controller, each a 'boot: Building the app · <part> in N ms' line) then rising, six steps in the order the shell always took: wiring the interface, the screen's colours, the gallery laid out, the ONI Trash counted, updates, the paired phone. The starter runs them as its own steps, a frame of the band between two; Shell::new runs them in a row, so every check builds the same shell. Checks: the app's unit checks, the window checks on the shell (launch, told, gallery); a real launch logs each part and step.

title: The window keeps the system's own title bar, its traffic lights in it
detail: Owner's call: no unified bar on macOS. Of the window's attributes, the transparent, hidden and full-size title bar is the one the main window carried and the splash did not, on the Intel Mac where only the splash ever showed (releases issue 13); the window now takes the system's defaults. Gone with it: the attributes hook, the lights laid back in the app's bar on every resize, the bar's room for them and its empty room dragging the window, which the system's bar does. chrome.rs keeps the Dock's icon. Checks: canvas_layout (the GALLERY key still takes its press) and the launch check; the parity row says the change.

title: The unified bar is back: the title bar transparent over the content, the traffic lights in the app's bar
detail: Owner's call after seeing #1084: the system's solid title bar spoils the look, and no report found ties a transparent, full-size title bar to a window that never shows (searches on winit, Slint, AppKit forums: only looks, a bar drawn anyway on macOS 26, transparency lost on refocus). #1084 is reverted whole: the attributes hook, the lights laid in the bar, its empty room dragging the window, the parity row and the canvas_layout check.

title: Version 1.5.6
detail: oni-app 1.5.6, carrying the logs without the user's names (#1079), the starter in the app's own window with each step of the launch (#1082, #1083) and the unified bar kept (#1085); the 1.5 welcome and splash picture kept.

title: The UX and UI benches' criteria
detail: Owner's ask: the twelve criteria proposed for an in-depth review become the UX bench (docs/ux-bench.md), the owner's eight categories the UI bench (docs/ui-bench.md). The UX bench rates the app in use (tasks, counts, timings, behaviour, words), the UI bench one still screen in one of its states; a criterion bordering on the other bench names it, so nothing is rated twice. Each gives what it judges, what to look at and the two ends of its scale; how a bench runs and scores comes with the owner's procedure.

title: One flat key for every action, a keycap for the mode, a screen's commit and the automatic actions
detail: Evaluation R0 (UI): the same heavy keycap on every key, colour marking which key it is rather than a meaning, disabled keys at full colour, Crop and Compare with no lit state while De-dust turned white and swapped its glyph. `Button` is flat by default: the keycap's grey laid flat, the hand's veil over it, a stronger one pressed. `keycap: true` at the use site keeps a cap for EDITOR/GALLERY, EXPORT in the bar and the sheet, ADD FOLDER… (plain, the accent left to export), PREPARE ROLL, the prepare footer's NEXT, every DONE, AUTO WHITE BALANCE (40 pt, at its own width), AUTO PAPER CORRECTION, DETECT and REMOVE. The kinds are plain, accent, destructive (a light red, 4.5:1, on a plain key's glyph or word) and ghost: caution, update, confirm and sheet go with their tints, ButtonSize.key and small with them. `on` lights the face with the accent sunk into the ground on every key and keeps its glyph; out of reach the whole key fades, face and glyph. A plate is one flat face whose key under the hand or on lights alone, a flat key on the middle of a row of keycaps. The picker's chevron and the stepped slider's keys are flat; the keycaps' relief is 0.6 of Swift's, the light higher, the dish and the socket quieter; the wells, the rails and the tab bar's hollow lighter.

title: Block titles a step heavier, the quiet words legible, tabular figures
detail: Evaluation R0: section titles shared size, weight and colour with the labels under them; helper text at 2.07:1, placeholders, captions and the empty ONI Trash under AA; readouts changed width as they moved. A section title is semibold; a note takes the secondary ink; the tertiary ink is white at 53 %, 4.5:1 on the panel's ground with small type's edges, and placeholders and a disabled field's words take it; a ghost key's glyph lifts to the primary ink under the hand, and a row's chevron, a single pixel's line, takes it too; a folder not on the disk reads in it instead of fading to 40 %. fonts/Inter.ttf maps 0 to 9 and + − × to Inter's own tabular glyphs (zero.tf and its kin, the cmap edited once with fontTools), so every value keeps its width, on screen and in a contact sheet's numbers.

title: One visual language: flat medals, the stock's glyph among the rows, a plain readout
detail: Evaluation R0: metallic coins, a coloured canister among line glyphs and an LCD readout beside flat icons. A medal is a flat disc of its metal's colour, lit under the hand; a stock's artwork shows where the stock itself is shown (the picker's cells, the roll's hero), the film-roll glyph in rows and in the inspector's lines; LcdReadout is a count in a field's well, in the words' own ink. The foil's tunables, the readout's glow and the picker's key gauges go.

title: Guides that read on a light sky
detail: Evaluation R0: the crop's thirds and the compare split were bare white lines lost on a bright sky. `GuideLine` lays the light line on a dark band a line wider each side; the thirds and the split draw it.

title: A denser panel and menu
detail: Evaluation R0: 62 pt between sliders, 76 pt per folded block, 32 pt context-menu rows. A section's room before and after is Space.m; a slider's knob is 20 by 26 pt (Swift's 24 by 34) and the stepped slider's keys as tall; a menu line and a folder pill's choice are 24 pt.

title: The hand seen on keys and tiles
detail: Evaluation R0: no hover on photo tiles, barely any on keys. A gallery tile under the pointer rings in the marker's white, every tile reporting the hand, not only those with a note; a key lights under the veil (#1088), a medal under the hand (#1090).

title: 24 pt catches for the small marks
detail: Evaluation R0: the rating marks 12 pt, the favourite star 13, the help marks 18, the zoom keys 23 wide, the switch 20 tall. A help mark lays out at its glyph's size and catches the hand over a 24 pt square; the star is a 24 pt ghost key; each medal and the switch catch over 24 pt, overhanging their line so it keeps its height; a worded key is never narrower than tall.

title: The gallery opens on four columns
detail: Evaluation R0: at the 1100 pt window the six-column rung left tiles of 78 pt and 40 % of the card empty. The ladder gains a rung of four past Swift's twelve and six and the gallery opens on it; ⌘− steps to six then twelve, and a stored count keeps its own rung.

title: A README for developers: this is the working repository
detail: README rewritten for whoever reads, builds or changes the code, with the releases repository, website and manual named for everything else: stack, workspace map, build, checks, rules, keys, licences. Finder's .DS_Store files untracked and ignored.

title: One bar in every mode: the mode key and the history at the left, feedback, settings and the commit at the right
detail: Evaluation s-1d4fb9c3: Undo, Settings and Feedback changed place between the gallery, the editor and Prepare, and at the 1100 pt window the editor's EXPORT ran 12 pt past the window's edge, cutting EXPORT 25 PHOTOS. The bar now holds one layout: the mode key and Undo/Redo beside it, the mode's own keys centred in the room left, then Feedback, the phone, Settings and the commit slot, whose room stays, its key hidden, while a roll is prepared. The centre is the one zone that gives room, its faces narrowing to their labels first, so the compact bar fits the narrowest window in every mode. Feedback is a glyph at every width, as Settings beside it: its word turning into a glyph with the window's width made the bar's width loop through the window's. EXPORT keeps one word, the photos' count in its help (Export 25 photos (⌘E)), in the menu and on the export card's key; Bar.export-title goes. Checks: window toolbar::every_mode_lays_the_bar_alike_and_the_picture_opens_its_menu (the gallery, Prepare and the editor at 1100 pt keep the mode key, the history, Feedback and Settings to the pixel, EXPORT ends inside the window; twin: the keys between differ), toolbar::the_bars_keys_keep_their_widths_as_the_window_widens; real app at 1100 × 680 in the three modes.

title: The contact sheet's export key leaves the bar: the export panel's Export As chooses
detail: Evaluation: picking the whole roll inserted EXP. CONTACT SHEET and an empty black plate beside the export key, sliding the bar's keys about 150 pt, and its 3×3 grid was also Select the Whole Roll's glyph. The two keys opened the same panel, whose Export As (#1035) already offers Separate Photos or Contact Sheet first: the bar keeps one export key, which opens the panel on separate photos, the sheet one click away there. Act::ExportSheet and Ctl::export_sheet go; the welcome's line names Export As. The grid now means Select the Whole Roll alone. This withdraws the orange key of #1034 (owner's call then) on the owner's guideline for this round: merge what is alike. Checks: window toolbar (the whole roll picked adds no key and moves none), export_sheet (export opens on separate photos, Export As lays the five on one sheet, the next export opens on separate photos again).

title: The canvas header lays the Working Space between the column keys, and tells the preview only while it shows enlarged
detail: Evaluation: while a photo opened, '14% · preview' was drawn over the Working Space's name, and the name was cut to 'Display P3 · pho…', then 'p…' at 100 %, with room free beside it. The chip was centred on the card at the card's width less twice the zoom group, below its own words' minimum. It now takes the room between the Library's key and the zoom group, on the card's centre while that room allows, so it elides only when that room is short and never meets the readout. The readout's tag said the canvas read the preview whatever the zoom, seconds after each opening, at fit where nothing differs: it now shows only while the preview is stretched past its own pixels (viewport::enlarged: a zoom above the preview's share of the frame, the full resolution not read), with a tooltip saying what it means. Checks: viewport::the_preview_is_told_only_once_the_zoom_outgrows_it (twin: a rule on the full resolution alone tells it at fit), window space_chip; real app at 1100 × 680: 'Display P3 · phones & screens' whole at fit, '50% · preview' beside the elided name while the full resolution loads, '100%' once it has.

title: Crop, Compare and De-dust show their mode through the key's on, read off the state they open
detail: Evaluation: Crop and Compare looked the same on and off, while De-dust turned white and swapped its bandage for a check. The three keys now set on from the state itself, PanelState.tab for Crop and De-dust, Canvas.split for Compare, so a key cannot disagree with its mode; Bar.dedust, the copy Rust kept of the tab, goes, and De-dust keeps its glyph. The look of on is the design system's. Checks: window canvas_switch (De-dust's key reads the tab it opens, and goes dark with the tab bar), toolbar; real app: Crop, Compare and De-dust each lit while on.

title: Paste draws a clipboard apart from Copy's pages; Show the selected photo draws a photo between brackets
detail: Evaluation: Copy, Paste and Paste to the Roll read as three near-identical pages, and the crosshair meant Show the selected photo in the filmstrip while the help card's demo presses it for white balance. Paste is now a clipboard, drawn for this build in the Trinil set's stroke, and Paste to the Roll keeps the roll's canister: three silhouettes. Show the selected photo draws a photo between four corner brackets (icons/reveal.svg, Icons.reveal); the crosshair is the demo's white balance key alone. The demo is not filmed again, its photograph not mounted. Checks: oni-ui icons (every icon named is present); real app.

title: A right click on the picture opens the photo's own menu
detail: Evaluation: a right click on the image opened nothing, unlike the tiles, the filmstrip and the sidebar rows. The canvas now asks Rust (Canvas.menu) and shows the open photo's cell menu, on the frames shown with it when they show together, through the Library's own menu lines and actions (Ctl::canvas_menu beside Ctl::context), De-dust's brush area alike. A crop frame or an armed measuring window keeps the press on it for its own drag. Checks: window toolbar (a right click on the canvas lays Export… and Move to ONI Trash; twin: one on the bar lays none); real app.

title: The presets deck names itself on its resting strip
detail: Evaluation: an empty outlined tab sat half cut off at the canvas's bottom-left, with no name. The new card's top, all the strip shows of the deck at rest, now reads Presets, and the deck, the new card and each card carry an accessible role and name (Presets, New preset, the card's own). Its rise under the pointer was there: the testing tool hovers an element's centre, which for the deck's zone lies below the strip it shows. Checks: window preset_deck; real app at 1100 × 680.

title: Every mode is left alike: its key, Escape, and every photo opened
detail: UX evaluation, problems 15 to 18: the crop's key and ⌘K only ever opened the crop, Escape left neither the crop, Compare, De-dust nor a help card, and the crop and De-dust stayed on from one photo to the next, the gallery's included. One model now. A tool's key, menu item or shortcut opens it and leaves it for the last panel: Route::toggled and one toggle_tool serve the crop and De-dust, Swift's openCrop departing. Escape leaves the innermost thing open: a help card, then the sheets, Export and Prepare as before, then Compare over the canvas before the crop or De-dust. Every photo opens with no mode, at the one place a photo opens (open_photo), as the one still open shown again from the gallery (open_in_editor, which ⌘G and the EDITOR key now go through too), and leaving for the gallery. Leaving De-dust no longer disarms the measuring window: only leaving the crop does, as the route always said.

title: Prepare the Roll left unmeasured keeps nothing, and a bare frame shown again asks for its roll again
detail: UX evaluation, problem 21: Cancel kept the roll's draft, so the roll opened again on its Window step with every earlier step marked done; after Escape, the frame left open behind the gallery opened in the editor, its measuring window drawn, while another frame went to Prepare the Roll: the requirement ran only where a photo is loaded, never where the one open is shown again. Leaving the roll unmeasured (Cancel, Escape, GALLERY, a sidebar frame) now drops every frame's draft on the drafts' thread; a quit still writes it, so a roll resumes after a relaunch, where Swift kept it on leaving. The roll's frames are read on that thread too, after the drafts queued, so a roll opened again at once never reads a draft being dropped. The photo still open behind the gallery, shown again, is held to its roll's preparation as a loaded one is.

title: Prepare the Roll's panel: the step's controls first, its demo played once under them, the settings note once
detail: UX and UI evaluation, problems 8, 8b, 44 and 45: the Window step said to use a slider that stood below the fold, under a looping demo and a five-line warning the footer cut mid-sentence; the demo looped without end beside the frame measured; the orange Settings differ note stood on all five steps over each step's own choice. Each step now shows its controls first, then its demo, square at RollStyle.demo so it stands whole under the Window step's controls in a window 680 points tall, then the frames to pick from, the part that scrolls. A clip plays once and rests on its last frame (tutorial::Frames ends; a help card's demo, open while a hand rests on its mark, starts it again). The Settings differ note shows once, on the Flat-Field step, over the grid whose marks it names and whose light it concerns.

title: Prepare the Roll's step keys show a check on each step done
detail: UX and UI evaluation, problem 32: a step's progress was told by a lamp alone, green when done, black when not, the black one about 1.5:1 on its key. A step behind the current one carries the done glyph before its word; the current key stays lit, the others plain; the lamp is no longer laid on a key of the app.

title: A help card opens by its mark, never over the photo
detail: UX and UI evaluation, problem 46: in the editor panel every card opened left of the panel under its tab bar, over half the photo and far from the mark that opened it. A card now opens under its mark, or over it where more room stands, its demo shortening so the card keeps to the window, the mark's top reaching the layer through Tips.note; the panel's anchor, its four inputs and TipStyle.card-gap are gone. Escape closes a card first (#1111).

title: The shot date writes only what a hand typed, and every field of a roll is one undoable step
detail: UX evaluation (s-1d4fb9c3), data integrity: tabbing through Shot Date without typing wrote the default, the roll's first photo's capture, as the roll's own date, and Undo skipped it. The date fields commit as the focus leaves them; a commit holding the fields as they were shown now writes nothing, one rule with the drafts written before a scene hides them, so only a date typed is written. A folder's marker was written beside the gallery history: name, date, body and stock now go through one gallery step with the marker, as the stock already did, so Undo takes any of them back.

title: A medal laid is a gallery step: Undo takes it back
detail: UX evaluation (s-1d4fb9c3): rating a photo added no undo step, the medal written to the sidecar beside the history. The gallery history gains a medals part, the medal each photo wore and the one laid; the store lays the medal on each sidecar and records it, and undo and redo lay each photo's own back. The status bar's medals, the keys 0-3 and the Labels menu all go through it.

title: The roll the gallery shows stands for a pick, and a folder of photos is a roll: the roll guide merges into the roll card
detail: UX and UI evaluation: with a roll open and nothing selected the inspector read Select a roll, EDITOR was greyed and PREPARE ROLL disabled, though one photo picked then measured the whole folder; an unprepared folder read Not in a roll yet, said nothing of its measure, and a blue Move into a New Roll competed with PREPARE ROLL. One root: only a picked photo was ever the gallery's subject. The sidebar, Prepare the Roll and Reset the Roll now stand on the anchor's folder, else the folder opened; the editor's key opens the anchor, else the first photo shown, and the bar's key reads the menu's rule. A folder with no marker is a roll named after it, its marker made by the first field written, so the roll guide (#830) goes: Not measured yet and PREPARE THE ROLL… show on every unmeasured folder, and Move into a New Roll stays in the menus.

title: The status bar counts the photos the grid shows, on every surface
detail: UI evaluation: Projects said No Photos in a Project above 25 photos, the count read off the archive's bands whatever the surface. It reads the grid laid.

title: A click opens the ONI Trash, as a folder's click opens the folder
detail: UX evaluation: a click on ONI Trash opened nothing and said nothing; it folded the row, a double click opened it, and the empty row was greyed as a folder away. As every row of the navigator (D4), a click opens it, its empty grid saying so, the chevron folds its folders, and the row is never greyed.

title: The resets are named by what they do, and a photo's menu holds no reset of its whole roll
detail: UX evaluation: Reset Settings, Reset to Default… and Reset to Imported State sat side by side with no stated difference, and Reset to Default… on one photo's menu proposed to reset all 24 photos of its roll. Two gestures, two names: Reset Settings, the look back to rest with the measure and the crop kept, in the cell menu, the Edit menu and the bar's RESET key; Reset the Roll…, every photo of the roll back as scanned, in the Rolls menu alone, its confirm and undo step named the same and its message saying the crops go (owner's call of 2026-10-31).

title: The rating filter is ALL and the three medals, a press each, and a medal is shown as its medal
detail: UX and UI evaluation: the filter was one key cycling ALL, BRONZE, SILVER and GOLD, showing its state rather than that it filters by rating, Gold three presses away; ratings were medals in the status bar but words in the menu and the filter. The bar's filter is ALL and the three medals on one plate, each a press, the one kept lit; the cell menu's four medal lines go, the status bar's medals and the keys 0-3 laying one. ⌘L still cycles.

title: The Measured Roll's keys say what they do: Add Them to the Roll, Move into a New Roll…
detail: UX evaluation: JOIN THE 24 and ROLL OF THE 1 named the gestures by counts. The warning above them counts; the keys are now ADD THEM TO THE ROLL and MOVE INTO A NEW ROLL…, the menus' name for the same gesture.

title: One keyboard for every control: Tab walks them in reading order, one ring, a click gives the keys back to the photos
detail: Evaluation s-1d4fb9c3 (accessibility, blocker): Tab reached only the text fields; no key, tab, tile or slider took the keyboard and no ring was drawn. One model in the design system (`ds/keyboard.slint`): `KeyScope` is a control's place in Tab's order, ringed by `FocusRing` (the accent, a gap off the edge, `FocusStyle`) while it holds the keyboard, never given it by a click; `KeyMonitor`, the photos' keyboard, is passed over by Tab and gets every key a control lets through. Every key (Space or Return presses it), the tab bars as one control (← → pick), the switch, the picker (Space, Return or ↓ drops it), each medal, an editable title, a sheet's side list, the gallery grid (one stop, its current photo ringed, the arrows walking the photos), the navigator's rows beside the grid (one stop, the arrows walking the rows) and the open photo take Tab; a field wears the same ring while it is typed in. Any press gives the keyboard back to the photos (the window's pointer hook, a field's own press aside); a key whose holder vanished or hid goes to the monitor (`outside::keyed` in the window's key hook: Slint drops it otherwise); a new screen or a sheet takes the keyboard back. A sheet keeps Tab inside it: the monitor's two walls, Tab stops only while `Keyboard.covered`, hand the keyboard to its first control going forward and its last going back, the year view taking it back as a sheet does; the window no longer claims Tab under a sheet. `Keyboard.held`, the window's keyboard rather than a field's, gates the menus' bare keys as `KeyMonitor.held` did, a control holding the keys included. Checks: window keyboard::tab_walks_every_control_in_reading_order_each_answering_its_own_keys, keyboard::a_press_gives_the_keyboard_back_to_the_photos_and_a_key_whose_holder_is_gone_reaches_them, keyboard::a_sheet_keeps_tab_inside_it_while_it_covers_the_window (twins: Space on the photos presses no key, an unhooked press leaves the key holding the keyboard, an unhooked key after its holder went is dropped); headless walks Tab to the sidebar's first field; the real app driven through the gallery, the editor and Settings.

title: Every slider moves alike: a press lands the knob, the arrows step one shown unit
detail: Evaluation s-1d4fb9c3: Pro sliders took no arrow key and a click on the track did nothing, while the Scanner's stepped sliders jumped to the press. The shared `Slider` now does it for all: a press off the knob lands it under the pointer and the drag goes on from there (with ⌥ the knob stays and the drag is finer, as before); holding the keyboard, ← ↓ and → ↑ step, ⇧ ten units (three steps on a stepped slider, as its keys). A continuous slider's step is one unit of its readout's last digit, laid on that digit's grid so each press shows the next number (`slider_track::stepped`): Temperature +18.6 reads +19 and steps to +20, where 1 % of the range skipped every odd number; the band and quality sliders alike, and the De-dust brush (a pixel) and sensitivity (a percent) and Prepare's sliders get the step they lacked. Left as designed: the wheel scrolls the panel and moves a slider only along its track, as Swift's DSScrollAdjust; a one-point drag moves Temperature 0.7 of a unit on its 288-pt track, not two; no typed value, the arrows reaching every number shown. Checks: slider_track::an_arrow_moves_the_readout_by_one_and_lands_on_its_numbers (twin: the 1 % step lands on +22), window keyboard (an arrow is a step, ⇧ ten); real app: Temperature +23 → +25 → +34 by the arrows.

title: Assistive technology names every photo, the open picture and every field
detail: Evaluation s-1d4fb9c3: photo tiles, the canvas and every text field exposed empty names, so VoiceOver could not tell one frame from another. A tile is a list item named by its photo (`TileView.name`, the caption by default), selectable and saying its selection, its missing note as its description; the canvas's picture is an image named by its status line (the photo and its size); a field is named by its label (`TextField.name`: Name, Camera, Lens, ISO, Date, Artist, Copyright, Camera Body, Description, the report) and by its placeholder where it has none, the date's boxes Month, Day and Year and the size's Width and Height. Real app: the drive tree lists the tiles as ListItem "DSC_6432".

title: The medals' keys and Space shown in their controls' tooltips
detail: Evaluation s-1d4fb9c3: the keys 1 to 3 and 0 that lay the medals and Space for the editor were shown nowhere but the menu bar, which the evaluation tool cannot see. Each medal of the status bar names itself and its key, Bronze (1), Silver (2), Gold (3), the lit one the key that takes it off, No Medal (0), on hover and while it holds the keyboard; the mode key says Editor (Space or ⌘G) in the gallery, Gallery (Space or ⌘G) in the editor. French and Spanish filled in.

title: An export line opens on its roll's film stock
detail: UX evaluation (s-1d4fb9c3), problem 26: Export asked to pick a film though the roll named its stock. A line opened on the roll its sidecar names, which a folder made a roll leaves empty, its stock living in the folder's marker. Each target now takes the roll of the band holding it, as the roll's panel does: the folder's marker, else the sidecar's roll.

title: A text field keeps the width it is laid at; longer words slide under its edge
detail: UI evaluation, problem 7: Export's Camera value NIKON CORPORATION NIKON ran past its field and under the preview. The design system's entry took its text's width as its least, as Slint's TextInput asks, so a long value widened the field. The entry now clips at its owner's width and slides a long line to keep the caret in view, as AppKit's field and Slint's own line edit do, back to its start once left.

title: The export column starts at the top, level with the panel's title
detail: UI evaluation, problem 55: the form and the preview floated mid-column between empty bands of about 190 pt. The centring floor is gone: the column lays its lines from the top, as the settings panel beside it does, and scrolls past one screenful as before.

title: Every sheet sets the window back behind a scrim
detail: UI evaluation, problem 48: Settings opened with the toolbar and the sidebar at full strength around it. The design system's sheet, which every sheet and question inherits, lays the scrim token under its card; the click beside the card still reaches nothing.

title: One formatter for every readout
detail: UI evaluation, problems 11 and 50: Black point read -0 % at rest, +0 % sat beside 50%, and -4 used a hyphen where the zoom keys use the minus sign. Every value on screen goes through fields::number: a true minus, a plus where the value is signed, no sign on what rounds to zero, % ° and × against the digits, EV and px after a space. The sliders, the Scanner face and its screen, the spectrogram's bands, the levels, the zoom and loupe labels, the export quality, De-dust's brush and sensitivity and the base picker read through it; the levels' own formatter in oni-settings is gone.

title: Plain words for what the evaluation read as engineering: HDR, P3, a colour table, the diagnostic log, the Scanner screen spelled out
detail: UX evaluation, problems 65 and 6: HDR hack becomes HDR above its switch, Brighter on HDR screens (the switch was there, cut by the panel's scroll at 680 pt); DP3 becomes P3, the space's own short name, which five tabs hold in 340 pt (French and Spanish name Custom Profil and Perfil, which fit); the Frontier look's note says a colour table over ONI's conversion, in sRGB, edited as a .cube file; Console becomes the Diagnostic Log in its window, its menu item, its key and the report's switch; the Scanner screen writes CONTRAST, VIGNETTE, CHROME, NEGATIVE and POSITIVE, the panel's own words in the machine's capitals, and its FRAME line is translated as Prepare's is.

title: One name per concept: the film stock, the film type, colour density
detail: UX evaluation, problems 66 and 68: the stock was Film Stock, Roll Type, Stock or Film by panel, and Film also meant negative or positive. The stock is the film stock everywhere (Select Film Stock, No film stock set, the export's Film stock and Choose…), negative, positive or black and white the film type (Prepare's Film type field and its FILM TYPE step); the Spanish catalogue, which called both Tipo de película, names the stock Emulsión. Color density (same as saturation) is Colour density, its help saying what other apps call it. Select the whole film (⌘A) had already left with the roll guide (#1123).

title: One spelling, British, in every English text
detail: UX evaluation, problem 70: Favourites and digitised sat beside Color. Counted over the catalogue, British spellings led (favourite, grey, colour, centre, digitise, recognise: 46 words against 22 for color), so color becomes colour in every text, the Colour tab and block included; colorimetric, ColorSync and the stocks' own names stay as written.

title: One case style per role
detail: UI evaluation, problem 51: Halo limit and White point beside Brush Size, Frontier look beside Shot Date. Titles of sheets, sections, blocks and Settings pages take title case (Frontier Look, RAW Files, Phone Remote); slider and field labels sentence case (Brush size, Picker size, Export as, Pass order); a key's tooltip naming its command takes the menu's title case (Copy Settings, Zoom In, Show the Selected Photo, Reset Measuring Window, which the Measuring Window section names); the menu's empty line reads No Presets. A help text that describes a key stays a sentence.

title: ONI_WINDOW=<width>x<height> opens the window at that size in points
detail: The interface evaluations look at the app in the window a 16-inch MacBook Pro gives it when zoomed (1728 x 1017 points), whatever screen it opens on; their driver reaches the window through Slint's MCP server, which cannot size it. The starter grows the window to the asked size instead of the app's default, centred as before.

title: The catalogues after the first evaluation's four corrections
detail: scripts/i18n run on the merge of #1088-#1128: the texts the merged sources no longer show are dropped from the French and Spanish catalogues; every text left is translated.

title: The bar's check reads its keys along their middle row
detail: Since most keys are flat (#1088), their top edge no longer differs from the bar, so the check that every mode lays the bar alike saw one key. It now reads the row through the keys' middle: a cap or a plate by its face, a flat key by its glyph, strokes up to 4 px apart bridged.

title: The medals and the scanner's LCD keep their analogue look
detail: Owner's call on the art direction: ONI is digital and owns it, but its look nods to the analogue medium, playful like a film camera. The medals are spun foil again (DSMedal: the metal's ramp, its lobes, bevel, ruled ring and two shadows) and the LCD readout glows on the scanner's glass again, as before #1088; the medal picker keeps its 24-pt catch and its hover.

title: The benches rate the art direction: UI Art direction, UX Play
detail: Owner's ask: the reviews follow the project's art direction, a digital tool nodding to the analogue medium, playful and tactile like a film camera. The UI bench gains Art direction (one analogue vocabulary that never competes with the photo; large surfaces flat, texture only on small pieces such as labels and medals), the UX bench gains Play (controls that answer like a camera's mechanics without slowing the work).

title: A slider's arrow step follows the one readout formatter
detail: Merging #1131 (arrow steps on the readout's last digit) with #1149 (one formatter, its readout kinds merged): the step's unit now reads the kinds left, a percent one unit of a percent, every other two-place kind a hundredth, a ceiling a thousandth, pixels a tenth.

title: Two checks read the merged slider and readout as they now behave
detail: After the merge of #1131 and #1149: the arrow-step check expects the one formatter's percent, '+1%'; the auto De-dust check lands the Sensitivity knob with a press off it, then measures the drag's share from there, as a press on a track now lands the knob under the pointer.

title: The UI bench's Art direction asks for a mastered, balanced mix
detail: Owner's direction: the mix of flat digital surfaces and analogue pieces must be mastered and balanced. Art direction now says so: each analogue piece earns its place, with the same care and weight on every screen, never clustered while another screen reads as generic software.

title: A pressed slider holds the keyboard, one press rule for every slider, and Tab from the photo enters the panel
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (UX, major): a click on a slider left the arrows walking the photos, a click on the track meant to focus moved the value, and the first slider lay about 31 Tabs from the toolbar. A press on a slider now gives it the keyboard, ringed as Tab does: its arrows step it until a press elsewhere (the window's pointer hook, as every control) or Escape gives the keyboard back to the photos. One press rule, AppKit's NSSlider, for the continuous and the stepped slider alike: the knob pressed is grabbed where it stands and moves nothing until the hand does, a press on the rail lands the knob under the pointer, ⌥ keeps it put; the stepped slider's knob jumped to the nearest step under the pointer even when pressed, a click on the knob of a 97-step rail moving it up to three steps. The drag measures from the value's place, never from where the settle spring has the knob. Tab from the open photo enters the editor's panel at its tab bar (`Keyboard.inward`), the first slider a few stops on; ⇧Tab and the walk on from there reach the bar and the columns as before. Checks: window keyboard::a_pressed_slider_takes_the_arrows_until_escape_or_a_press_elsewhere (twin: a pressed tab bar takes none), scanner (the pressed rail takes the arrows, Escape gives them back), editor_routes (Tab from the photo, then →, picks the panel's next tab; the bar's first key would have walked the photos).

title: A number typed over a slider's value
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (UX, major, both rounds): double-clicking a slider's number did nothing. A double click on the value opens it, selected, to a number typed over it (`ValueHeader { typeable }`, the `RenameField` laid over the value outside the row's layout, so the slider below never moves); Return or a press elsewhere takes it, Escape gives the value back, a tooltip says so. The number becomes the steps an arrow takes (`Typing.steps`, answered by `slider_track::typed_steps`): one unit of the readout's last digit on a continuous slider, so the value lands on the number typed through the arrows' own path and every owner's `step`, and what one step reads on the Scanner's stepped sliders (`Lab.step-reads`: half a unit a letter, 5% or 0.1 EV an effect), held on their range. Signs +, - and U+2212, a comma for the point, and a unit typed after the digits are read. Return leaves the keyboard to the slider. The body's double clicks are unchanged: the second press on a continuous rail resets, a stepped rail's or name's double click rests it. Checks: slider_track::a_number_typed_over_a_readout_is_the_steps_an_arrow_would_take (twin: whole units fall fifty times short), lab::sliders::a_number_typed_over_a_scanner_readout_finds_its_steps (twin: the last digit makes 15% fifteen steps), window keyboard::a_number_typed_over_a_slider_readout_steps_it_there (twin: words move nothing). French and Spanish filled in.

title: The rail in soft hues, its ground at 3:1, and a hover the eye reads
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (UI and UX, major, owner's decision): Temperature, Tint and the Scanner's C, M, Y and TEMP ran full-chroma gradients beside the photo; the unfilled rail measured 1.83:1 against the panel; the hover grew the knob about a point. Every bipolar rail now runs between soft hues, its ends at 0.4 of their saturation and 0.85 of their value (`SliderStyle.hue-chroma`, `hue-light`), in the Rail itself, so the Roll tab's, Prepare's, the paper's and the bands' alike: the ends of Temperature, Tint, C, M, Y and TEMP keep 3.8:1 or more against the panel. The rail's bare ground is `SliderStyle.ground` (white at 36 %, about 3.2:1 on the panel) and its lit stretch `SliderStyle.lit` over it (white at 45 %, about 2.2:1 on the ground). The hand anywhere on the row, which a press answers, grows the knob by 1.15, three points across, and lights the value in the primary ink.

title: Every readout in its unit, one format on both faces
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Clarity and Consistency, major): Temperature, Tint, Highlights, Shadows and Contrast read bare numbers; Contrast read 0.00 on Pro and 0% on Scanner, Vignette 0.00 EV against 0.0 EV. Temperature and Tint are the print filters' gap in stops (red against blue, magenta against green) and read in EV, as the Colour help now says; Highlights, Shadows, Contrast and the flat-field's colour read in percent. The Scanner face's effects, on its sliders and its screen, read through the Pro slider moving the same quantity (`lab::field`), its own percent and stops formatters gone, so Chrome no longer reads +15% there and 15% on Pro. The bare and share-of-range readout kinds are gone; the density ceiling alone reads a bare density.

title: One name per control, one case per role
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Language and Typography): the Scanner's TEMP slider reads Temperature in sentence case like every slider label, its screen keeping TEMP among the machine's capitals; Pro's Colour density, which is saturation, reads Saturation on the panel and in the preset sheet's rows, so Density names a density alone (the Scanner's D, the Roll tab's ceiling); the compare split's labels read Before and After.

title: The face switch says what each face is
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Obvious without a tutorial): Pro and Scanner sat side by side with no hint of how they differ. Each tab of the face switch carries a tooltip, Pro every setting by hand and the place to start, Scanner a lab scanner's keypad of density and colour steps; `Tabs` takes a tooltip per tab, a swatch with none still showing its name.

title: One undo history for the session, the same in the gallery and the editor
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: moving to another frame emptied the editor's undo, the gallery kept a history of its own the editor could not reach, and the two reached differently. The editor's per-frame stack (oni-core history.rs) and the gallery's (oni-library gallery_history.rs) are one, oni-library history.rs: every step names each frame it wrote, an edit of the open frame as much as a gesture on several; an edit joins the step on top within 0.4 s on the same frame and setting, as Swift's coalescing; 200 steps under the 256 MB ceiling. Opening a frame resets nothing and the face it opens on is no step; undoing an edit of a frame left writes its sidecar. Every gesture and undo first records the step still waiting, so the steps keep the order they were taken in. The menus and the bar name the one history's step in both modes, ⌘Z and the phone's undo land through one host path (history_step, stepped), and a step that moves files writes the open frame first, its walk refused when that write is. Surface, the editor's companions attached by serial and the gallery undo's extra editor step are gone; parity: the gallery's own 100-step history departed.

title: A roll asked for while the gallery shows another folder is found whole once its own folder is back
detail: UX evaluation: after a walk through Roll #9, Roll #8's Roll tab read 'Acts on this photo, the only one measured with its roll' and '24 photos of this folder were not measured with the roll', its sidecars unchanged. The open frame stays in the store behind the gallery, so each bar publish asked its roll among Roll #9's paths, found none and kept that empty answer: EditorStore::set_archive_paths kept every roll whose found frames were all still laid, which an empty roll always is. A roll's frames are found among the library's paths, so the same paths keep every roll found (a lay still reads no sidecar) and any path come or gone has every roll scanned again. Checks: a_roll_asked_for_beside_another_folder_is_found_whole_back_in_its_own (1 beside Roll 9, 3 back in Roll 8; it read 1 before), a_roll_s_frames_found_outlive_a_lay_of_the_same_paths_alone (twins: a path come, a path gone).

title: The Measured Roll speaks of the roll the photographer sees, in a line of words, its keys one a row
detail: UX evaluation: the Roll tab set the folder apart from the roll ('24 photos of this folder were not measured with the roll', ADD THEM TO THE ROLL), large orange bands topped the panel on every frame, and MOVE INTO A NEW ROLL… ran past the panel's edge. The roll is the folder the photographer sees: 'Acts on the 25 photos of this roll.', else, in the warning ink of Prepare's notes, '24 photos of this roll were left out of its measurement, so these settings do not reach them.' over INCLUDE THEM and MOVE INTO A NEW ROLL…, each key a row of its own so no language runs it past the panel; the never-measured line is a plain note over PREPARE THE ROLL…. The Roll tab no longer draws a WarningBand. Checks: the catalogue check; the Roll tab's help card test reads the new note.

title: The Roll tab names its blocks for a photographer: Filtration, Highlight Detail, Auto White Balance
detail: UX evaluation: Source Balance, Density Ceiling and Balance Strength read as engine concepts beside the film type. They are now Filtration (the roll's colour, as an enlarger's filters are dialled for a film, with a help note it lacked), Highlight Detail (the photo's brightest parts, the negative's densest) and Auto White Balance (the share of the key's correction the roll takes); fields, sidecars and presets' ids keep Swift's names. The phone's panel and the presets' list name them alike. Spectrogram Finishing, Kept and Flags stand on other tabs. Checks: the catalogue check; the_roll_tab_lays_its_blocks_in_the_swift_order reads each renamed block under Swift's title.

title: Prepare's step bar is the faces' tab bar: a mark only on a step done, no key moving
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the step keys lit the current step in the accent beside NEXT's blue, gave a skipped step the check of one completed, and widened as each check appeared, shifting every key. `RollStepKeys` is now the design system's `Tabs`, as the editor's Pro/Scanner bar in the same place: the current step on the neutral pill, each tab an even share of a fixed bar (`RollStyle.step-tab`, 96 pt) so no mark moves one, a step the roll does not walk out of reach, all of them while it measures. A tab is marked (`Preparing.done`, `step::done`) only behind the current step and holding its value: a flat-field or base passed by SKIP, or not walked, carries none. The step titles leave the tooltips; the panel's heading names the step. Checks: prepare model test (a skipped flat-field, a base without its pick, a step not walked and the current one are not done, with twins), window prepare (film done, base done once picked). Left as designed: five screens with Flat-field and Base skipped, since any tab reaches its step in one click and nothing skips a step unasked (hard rule 1); 'RGB Passes' near its bar's round end, as the tab bar's even shares (Swift's DSTabBar) keep a label its 8 pt margin; the 'Prepare the Roll' tooltip under the bar, an artefact of the evaluation's clicks, since a real press hides every tooltip (Outside.presses).

title: The flat-field step's note on frames shot apart is measured whole, the grid below it
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (major): the 'Settings differ across the roll' advice was laid at one or two lines and the thumbnail grid covered the rest. Under the plain `controls` layout that grouped the step blocks, Slint 1.18 measured a wrapped note inside a step's block at the wrong width; the wrapper added nothing (the column has the same spacing), so each step's block now sits in the panel's column itself and every note of a step (left out, passes, grouping, mask) is measured at the panel's width. Seen on the headless window with the 245-character note: five lines, the grid under them, where it covered three.

title: A frame shot apart or flagged is told by a glyph or a word, not by colour alone
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: Prepare marked the frames digitised with other settings by an amber dot and flagged frames in the panel's grid by a red ring alone. A frame shot apart carries the warning glyph on the tile's state disc, the disc a missing original already shows (`StateDisc`, one component for both), in the corner the gallery gives its medal, so it never meets the flag; a flagged frame carries its FLAGGED seal on every Prepare tile, the panel's grid as the flags' sheet. `TileStyle.apart` goes with the dot.

title: The inspector's Prepare key reads as the toolbar's, flat
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the gallery showed 'PREPARE ROLL' as a keycap in the toolbar and 'PREPARE THE ROLL…' as a second keycap under the inspector's warning, one action under two names and depths. The inspector's key says PREPARE ROLL and lies flat: the keycap stays on the toolbar's, the gallery's commit. The Roll tab's key, in the editor, keeps its wording.

title: The Crop tab's plate spaces its words evenly and the Vertical switch shows only where it can turn
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: COPY and PASTE hugged their words while PASTE TO ROLL took the rest of the plate, so the three words stood unevenly apart. None of the three fills now: the plate shares its room out alike, each key growing by the same amount, so the words stand evenly apart. The Vertical switch was disabled under Free and 1:1 yet looked live, a click doing nothing: it now shows only with a ratio that has an orientation (`Framing.orientable`, formerly `portrait-enabled`). Checks: sidebars reads the three words' gaps off the drawn plate, its twin the former layout; panel_bindings finds no switch under Free and 1:1, its twin 3:2.

title: The measuring window's key says what it does: SET WINDOW, then APPLY WINDOW
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the key read MEASURING WINDOW, a noun repeating its block's title. It reads SET WINDOW until armed and APPLY WINDOW while armed; French RÉGLER LA FENÊTRE, Spanish AJUSTAR VENTANA.

title: The rotate key draws a photo under a clockwise arrow
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: Trinil's rotate-90, a diamond under an arc, did not read as a rotation. Icons.rotate is drawn for this build in the Trinil stroke: a landscape frame under a clockwise arc whose head points down past its corner, as the key turns the photo 90 degrees clockwise. Left as it was: the evaluation found Rotate, Mirror and the Measuring Window's keys missing from the element tree, an artefact of its tool: Slint's MCP server caps get_element_tree at 1000 elements in depth-first order and the panel's lower blocks fall past the cut. Each icon key carries its help as its accessible label (Rotate 90° Clockwise, Mirror left for right, Reset, Copy and Paste Measuring Window); their glyphs without words are the app's icon keys, named by their block and their tooltip.

title: The crop's thirds read on a light sky
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: over roll #8's sky (sRGB 192) the thirds' edges, at the idle contrast shade (30 % black), stood at about 2:1. The thirds now take GuideLine's own edge, the full contrast shade (55 % black), as the compare split does: 86 against 192, about 4.2:1; their faint light line still carries them over a dark picture.

title: A text field at rest ends a value too long for it on an ellipsis
detail: Evaluation R1: Export's Camera field cut 'NIKON CORPORATION N' mid-letter. Every DS text entry now shows its words at rest through a label that elides at the field's edge; the input takes over, the words sliding under the edge, only while it holds the keyboard.

title: Export lays each preview over its fields, in two columns of four
detail: Evaluation R1: the preview left the column's lower half empty while the EXIF crowded a 260 pt column. Each line is now its preview over its caption, always as tall, and its fields in two columns of four across the room: a lone photo fills the room's height, the fields' values get the room's width; the preview room handed to Rust follows.

title: Export's presets are tabs that light the preset the rows equal
detail: Evaluation R1: the Instagram / Display / Print row looked like a segmented control and showed no selection. It is now the DS tabs under a Presets label, the tab lit read off the settings by Preset::matching: a row set by hand lights none, set back it lights again (beyond Swift, whose plate lit no key).

title: No space tab is dimmed: ProPhoto stays pressable at full ink
detail: Evaluation R1: ProPhoto greyed in JPEG measured 2.20:1 and read as unavailable with no reason; the note meant to say why was shown only in a state that never held. The tab is drawn as the others: chosen, it takes the TIFF along, as before, and its purpose says TIFF 16-bit only. The Tabs' dimmed state, used nowhere else, is removed with its lab specimens.

title: Inputs and selects are flat: the text fields and the picker's field share one flat face
detail: Owner's decision: inputs and selects carry no well and no relief. FieldFace (ds/fields.slint) is dsTextField's chrome laid flat, the canvas's dark at a card's corner, its edge lit and ringed by the keyboard's ring while it holds the focus; TextField, SizeFields, DateFields and the picker's field face wear it. Inward loses its lit rim and ring, which only the fields used. PickerStyle, equal to the field's gauges, merges into FieldStyle, and FieldStyle.padding, read by nothing, goes. The lip check reads an Inset, as fields no longer have a lip; the lab's Fields page loses the well tunables no field shows, and its Inward board the lit-rim specimen.

title: The switch is a camera's slide lever: the slider's knob on a short rail of its own
detail: The evaluation read the cross-and-check toggle as a generic web idiom, not a switch or lever from the camera vocabulary. Toggle now sets the slider's own Knob on a Rail of its own: on, the knob stands one DSToggle cell along (ToggleStyle.travel) and the rail is lit up to it, both on the grab spring; the knob grows under the hand as a slider's.
