ToggleGlyph, the hollow and the white thumb go, and ToggleStyle keeps only the travel. A click on the lever or its words, Space or Return flip it as before, through one flip function.

title: The Favourites pill names the view in the primary ink, no longer dimmed as disabled
detail: With the favourites alone, the navigator's pill was disabled, its words at the disabled opacity (3.29:1 against its ground, under AA's 4.5:1). It only names what the column lists, so it is pressable: false, as the projects' pill, its words in the primary ink; the note under it, which named the folder no longer shown, is empty in that view, at its source in the navigator's header.

title: The keycap rule read alike on every screen: GOT IT, GET STARTED and SEND wear the cap
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Consistency): keycap depth seemed to follow no rule. The rule is the owner's list (the mode switch, each screen's or sheet's commit, the automatic actions); every DONE wore its cap, but three commits did not: the notice's GOT IT, the welcome's GET STARTED and the report's SEND, now keycaps as their sheets' DONE. CHECK FOR UPDATES and SELECT FILM STOCK stay flat by that rule; a question's answers and a passing notice's OK stay flat. The design system's README names the list.

title: Keycaps read at a glance on the dark ground, still quieter than Swift's
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Art direction): at 0.6 of Swift's relief under a light at 50°, the cap's top wall stood 7 levels over its face and its foot sank into the ground, so a cap read as an outlined flat key. The walls now at 0.8 of Swift's, the light at 40° (Swift's 33), the dish at 3 (Swift's 4), the foot lifted 0.5 (0.4 before the quiet pass) and the socket's rim back to Swift's 2: on #313131 the top wall reaches about 65 against a face of 40 to 56 and a foot of 38 on the 40 ground, where Swift's reached 72 over 34 to 61. The slider's knob, a level keycap, follows. The bar's layout check finds a cap's middle from its last row, as the dished face's top now matches the ground.

title: The accent spent on one primary: the bar's commit slot always, a lit key never
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Hierarchy): the gallery bar raised EDITOR, PREPARE ROLL and ADD FOLDER… at equal weight, and its loudest colour was the navy of the ALL filter, lit by default. The commit slot at the bar's right end is the screen's one primary in every face (ADD FOLDER…, EXPORT, the update), so it is always the accent; `ButtonStyle.on` no longer tints a lit key with the sunk accent but lights the flat face as a selected row is lit (white at the track's 15 %), so the rating filter, the prepare steps and the crop, compare and De-dust keys say on without competing with the primary or the photo.

title: The bar's centre keys named by their words while the room holds them
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310 (Obvious without a tutorial): crop, compare, whole roll, copy, paste and De-dust were bare glyphs explained by their tooltips alone. One `Tool` key now serves the whole centre: its word (CROP, COMPARE, WHOLE ROLL, COPY, PASTE, PASTE TO ROLL, DE-DUST, RESET) while the bar holds every word, its glyph alone once it is narrower, the rule RESET and PASTE TO ROLL already followed. In English the words add about 250 pt, so they show from about 1520 pt with the traffic lights and the phone key, the 1728 pt bar keeping some 200 pt to spare; French and Spanish filled in. Glyphs every app shares (undo, redo, trash, feedback, settings) stay glyphs. The bar's width check compares 1728 with 1990 pt, two bars that both hold every word.

title: Film canisters turned in metal, their labels in soft inks
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the canisters were flat pictograms with full-chroma labels beside finely rendered medals, and the Fujifilm green sat loud beside the thumbnails. Every artwork's shell is now turned metal: the spool and caps in the silver medal's foil ramp, lit across the barrel and rolled at their rims, the spool knurled, the barrel shaded round with a gleam on the lamp's side, the top cap's shade on the label and a contact shadow under the foot; the three inner-shadow filters per artwork are gone. Each label keeps its brand's hue, its chroma compressed to OKLab 0.10 and its white to paper. Check: no_canister_ink_is_more_chromatic_than_the_soft_hues_beside_the_photo (twin: the old Fujifilm green is caught).

title: Each medal carries its rank struck in the middle
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: Bronze, Silver and Gold were told by colour alone, their names only in tooltips. Every medal, on a tile, in the rating filter and in the status bar, now carries its rank, 1, 2 or 3, struck in the ruled ring's ink: the same figure as the key that lays it.

title: The status bar's medals at an icon's size, a medal not given an empty place
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the status bar's medals were 12 pt and told given from not given by opacity alone, the dimmed ones at 2.67:1. The picker's medals are now 16 pt, the icon's size, inside the bar's 18 pt row; a medal not given is its empty place, its edge and rank in the secondary ink (5.5:1 on the panel), and the hand over it shows the medal it would lay.

title: One type scale of six steps; a block's title a size over its labels
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: about nine type sizes, and block headers in semibold at the labels' 13 pt barely outranked them, the blocks read through their rules. `Type` moves to its own theme_type.slint and holds the scale: micro 9.5 pt (a seal, a mini key's legend), caption 11 (a caption, a value, a key's legend, a tooltip), label 13, section 15 semibold, title 17, heading 24. The value and chip sizes, both 11, merge into caption; the keys' legends leave their own 10.5 and 9 pt for caption and micro. A section's title now stands at 15 pt semibold over 13 pt regular labels.

title: The inspector's values never outsize their block's title
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the film stock's name, the roll's name and the shot date's digits were set at the 17 pt title size under 13 pt block titles. The inspector's name (`EditableTitle`) and the stock's name take a label's size; the stock's default and dyes, the shot date's default and an empty project's stocks are notes. The size and date boxes hold a field's digits in a hollow a field tall, so the export's W × H and the shot date read as the fields beside them; FieldStyle.boxes-height, a keycap tall for title digits, goes.

title: Notes and the help card at a label's size, their lines opened
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: descriptions and help were set at 11 pt in the secondary ink, and a help mark's card was a dense paragraph of 11 pt medium lines. A note takes a label's 13 pt, its lines opened by `Type.leading` (Inter's natural 1.21 em to about 1.4 em); the help card's note is a note in the primary ink, on a card 300 pt wide instead of 260, about 44 characters a line. Prepare's description, its left-out and passes notes and the welcome sheet's lines were notes written by hand at a value's size or without the role: they take the note role. The length of the longest notes (the Colour block's, 487 characters) is the panels' words, left as written.

title: A right click outside the selection selects its tile, the one its menu acts on
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: a right click on a tile outside the selection opened its menu on that photo alone while another tile stayed marked, so the menu's target showed nowhere. The click now selects its tile alone, anchored and under the keyboard's ring, before the menu opens, as Photos does; inside the selection it keeps the selection whole. The menu's photos are always the ones marked, in the archive, a project and the ONI Trash.

title: The cell menu copies a photo's settings
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the right-click menus offered Paste Settings but no Copy Settings. Copy Settings now heads the cell menu, live on one photo whose original is there: the open frame lends what it shows, any other photo its sidecar (`EditorStore::copy_settings_of`), onto the board the bar's Paste and the system's pasteboard share; an original away lends nothing and says why. Beyond Swift, whose cell menu had no Copy.

title: New Project names its photos and stands in the File menu
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: the line 'New Project from' read as cut, its one-photo words were never in the catalogue, and a project could be made only by a right click. The line now says New Project from This Photo, or from 3 Photos, in the cell menu and in a new File menu item that makes a project from the selection (or the open photo), dark in the ONI Trash. French and Spanish filled in.

title: One empty state says how a project is made
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: with no project, the column and the grid both said to right-click photos, the column's narrow copy ending on a lone word. The column now says No Projects alone; the grid beside it says to select photos in the Archive, then choose New Project in the File menu or their right-click menu.

title: The gallery inspector stands on the whole roll, whatever medal the filter keeps
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: with the Gold filter keeping no photo of Roll #8, the inspector said Select a roll while the navigator still lit Roll #8 as the folder opened. The roll the gallery stands on was looked up among the gallery bands, which the medal filter cuts; it is now the band of the shown anchor folder, else of the opened folder, read off the archive whole tree (`Archive::band`). The card, its Prepare key, the toolbar Prepare and Reset the Roll and every field written act on every frame of the roll, never on its medalled frames alone. The roll card window check holds the card and Prepare on the folder under an empty Gold filter, and fails on the former lookup; the archive check reads a folder band whole under a filter.

title: The generic colour stocks spelt as the rest of the app
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: Generic Color Negative broke the British spelling every other text of the app uses (the Colour tab, Colour density). The catalogue two generic colour stocks read Generic Colour Negative and Generic Colour Positive, in the inspector, the stock picker, a project stocks and the export Film field alike; their ids, which sidecars and markers hold, are unchanged, and brand names (Kodak ColorPlus, Lucky Color 200, Mira Color) keep their makers spelling.

title: A warning keeps its orange in its glyph
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: a large amber band (Not measured yet) sat beside the gallery thumbnails, as the Roll tab one beside the photo. `WarningBand` is now the warning triangle in the warning orange, then its sentence in the primary ink, on the panel own ground, in the inspector and the Roll tab alike: nothing beside a photo tints how its colours are judged. `Colour.warning-soft` and `Tone.on-warning`, which only the band read, are gone; the lab keeps Swift DSWarning as its reference.

title: The zoom ladder steps through fit, ⌘0 fits, and ⌘− / ⌘+ follow every zoom
detail: Evaluation: fitted at 35 %, ⌘+ went to 50 % and ⌘− from there to 25 %, then up to fit; ⌘0 did nothing. The ladder now holds fit at the fitted scale and only the rungs above it, so − never leaps under fit nor zooms in (beyond Swift, whose ladder ignores the fitted scale). View > Zoom to Fit (⌘0) fits the open frame. The zoom items were published only after a menu or key gesture, so a wheel, a pinch or a double click left ⌘− dark: they are published again whenever the zoom bubble's reach changes. The zoom bench fits by ⌘0 after its pinch.

title: The zoom keys draw the icon set's minus and plus
detail: Evaluation: the zoom keys were text glyphs, the minus tiny and dim beside a bold plus. They now draw Trinil's minus and plus, the stroke of every other glyph, as square mini keys like the column keys beside them.

title: De-dust names itself in the tab bar's place, beside a DONE key
detail: Evaluation s-db78d310: with De-dust on, the tab bar showed Roll, Crop, Colour and Details with none selected and nothing named the mode but the bar's lit key. De-dust is a pane the tab bar does not list, and its five labels cannot share the panel's width in French or Spanish; so while it is on, the bar gives way to a header at the bar's height, the mode's name in the title face and a DONE keycap that asks the same gesture as the bar's key and the menu's Done Correcting, landing on the last panel. The panel's rule does not move.

title: Every block of the panel has a note, so every header wears its help mark
detail: UI evaluation (Consistency): the help mark sat on some block headers and not on others, as the port copied Swift's notes and Swift left ten blocks bare. Aspect Ratio, Straighten, Rotate & Mirror, Measuring Window, Source Balance, Per-Channel Levels, Machine, Density and the Scanner's Colour and Look now say what they do, in English, French and Spanish. Window check every_titled_block_has_a_note reads each Section and Block of the panel at its own depth and finds none without a note; twin: Measuring Window's note taken away is caught, its keys' own notes never standing for it.

title: A block's title is engraved as the rule above it
detail: UI evaluation (Art direction): the analogue nods clustered on the Scanner face, the medals and the contact sheet while the Pro face read as generic flat software. Section's title is now a camera's marking, small and on labels alone: in capitals set apart by the seal's tracking, the Divider's groove shade one line above its letters and its lit edge one line below, at the section's size, no new type size. Every block of every screen takes it, the Pro face's first; the screen reader still hears the title as written. The Pro sliders keep no −/+ keys: the Scanner face is the detented one, and two keys on each of a dozen Pro rows would narrow every track and double the panel's controls.

title: The second round's sixteen corrections, merged
detail: Merging #1159-#1222: De-dust's header now lies over the tab bar, which stays laid out, hidden, so Tab's way into the panel keeps its target (the bar takes the keyboard only while it shows). The fields keep the flat face with the type scale's field-sized digits; Prepare keeps its new steps with the type scale's notes; the Roll tab keeps 'Filtration'. scripts/i18n dropped the texts no source shows any more.

title: The Temperature and Tint check reads the Pro face's tracks
detail: The Scanner's TEMP slider reads Temperature since #1164, so the check, which took the first Temperature label and the line under it, landed on the Scanner's key and read no end. It now reads the `high:` inside the Pro face's StoreSlider of that name, whatever its line layout; the Rail's softened ends keep the hue it names. Twin: the Temperature track's ends swapped on the panel fail it.

title: The ONI Trash wiring check reads the session's one history
detail: oni-library tests/trash_wiring.rs still looked for the store's gallery stack, which #1167 made the session's one history on purpose: Move to ONI Trash now lays its step through self.history.record_trash, and the check reads that call, so a mark that lays no step is still named.

title: The slider and the window's menus, one file per part
detail: The merged corrections took ds/slider.slint past the 400-line limit and app.slint past its ceiling. The slider is cut into its parts as Swift names them: knob.slint (DSBarHandle), rail.slint (DSRail and SliderFill), readout.slint (DSReadout, ValueHeader) and slider.slint (DSSlider, its step keys and Typing); controls, plots, ds.slint and the lab import each part from its own file. The menu bar's state (MenuTitles, MenuLive, Menus) moves to menus.slint, the menu bar itself staying in the window, as Slint wants it; app.slint falls under the limit, so its grandfathered ceiling goes. Behaviour unchanged.

title: The preset deck's check aims at the balance field where the sheet now lays it
detail: After #1221 the window check preset_deck clicked 20 px above the save sheet's White balance field, in the gap under its label, so its menu never opened and the balance stayed Not carried. The field moved on purpose: the switches above it are slide levers a knob tall (#1188) and the block titles a step larger (#1199). The check now aims at the field's middle and at Automatic, the menu's third line, where they stand; the stale aim, which failed on 0 against 2, is its twin.

title: The panel bindings' checks find each control by its accessible name where the layout puts it
detail: After #1221 the two panel_bindings window checks pressed fixed points the corrected interface no longer holds: in the Roll tab re-laid on purpose (the block titles a step larger, #1199; the roll's state a line of words, #1172), Flat-Field's chevron stood 32 px above the press, so Source Encoding's RESET was never reached; in the export column re-laid by the same merge, the Width box stood 29 px below its press, which typed nowhere. No binding was lost: aimed at the controls, every assertion holds. Each press now finds its control by accessible role and label through Slint's ElementHandle (i-slint-backend-testing, a dev-dependency) and lands on its middle; a block's RESET is the one on its title's row, and a control in a popup moves by the corner i-slint-core says the window shows it at, so the mask menu is asserted under its picker and the chip's popover is reached, its Custom tab's press asserted taken. Twins: the stale aims fail on ('96', false) against ('48', true) and on Some(Linear) against None; a size box no longer following its owner, a flat-field switch bound to a constant and a Load a Profile… key that leaves the popover open each fail their check.

title: The medals are spun foil again, without figures
detail: Owner's call: the medals stay 2.5D, as decided for the art direction; #1192 had struck their rank in the middle and drawn a medal not given as an outline. A medal is the foil disc again, and those not given rest at the idle opacity, lit under the hand; its name stays in its tooltip and accessible label, its key size is kept.

title: The trash stands on a plate of its own, apart from RESET
detail: Owner's call: on one plate, the trash read as part of RESET, as if resetting a photo removed it. The gallery bar now lays RESET and the trash on two plates.

title: The benches ask that a destructive key stand apart
detail: Two evaluation rounds missed the trash sharing RESET's plate, which the owner spotted at once. UI Hierarchy now says a key that removes, resets or empties never shares a plate with one that keeps; UX Trust says a destructive action stands apart from the harmless ones around it.

title: Flows, UX and UI owe the Swift app nothing; the result does
detail: Owner's call: the Swift app is deprecated and far behind in flows, UX and UI; its parity rule only served the rebuild. CLAUDE.md now keeps Swift as the reference for the result alone (the conversion's maths and constants, the sidecar format) and lets flows, UX and UI be rethought whole on the benches, as long as the result stays as good. UX Task fit asks that the structure follow the photographer's sequence; UI Spacing that a column's tab bar, header and rows share one inset.

title: Capitals are the keycap's alone; every column opens on one header
detail: Owner's call: ALL CAPS only on the keycap CTAs. The Button upper-cased every key unless told not to, and the block's Section upper-cased its title and spaced it, so flat keys (Copy, Paste, Select Film Stock, Cancel, a block's Reset) and every section title (Colour, Film Stock, Shot Date, Language) shouted. The key now writes its word in capitals, bold and spaced only as a keycap, a flat key's word as written and semibold; the capitals switch is gone. The texts that carried capitals in their source or were upper-cased in Rust (Settings', Missing's, the roll tab's and crop tab's keys, the confirm's and the mask dialog's keys, the banner's, the catch-up's, the seals FLAGGED and R MISSING, the news seals, the stock picker's brands, the Wrapped eyebrows and title, the empty filter's hint naming All) are in Title Case for keys and titles, sentence case for labels, French and Spanish to match. Section headers took three faces (letterspaced capitals in the editor, a large light heading in Export, Prepare and De-dust): SectionTitle, the engraved title a step over the labels, is now the one header of every column. De-dust's Detect no longer turns into HIDE: it stays lit while what it found shows, and a second press hides it. Seals lose the tracking that only capitals wanted. The LCD's legends, the date placeholders and the toolbar's keys stay for their own owners. Check: button_group::capitals_are_the_keycap_s_alone reads the drawn words (flat keys and a block's title as written, a keycap in capitals); its twin finds no text 'Done' where the keycap so named shows DONE.

title: The coloured rails keep their full hues on a thinner rail
detail: Owner's call: #1161 had softened every bipolar rail to 0.4 of its saturation and 0.85 of its value, so Temperature, Tint, the paper's gains, the Spectrogram's bands and the Scanner face's D, C, M, Y and TEMP read washed out. The rail now runs between its two hues as given (`soft`, `hue-chroma` and `hue-light` are gone) and is calm through its breadth instead: `SliderStyle.track` is 8 pt, round at its ends (`track-radius` half of it), where it was the 14 pt token, so every rail, the levels' and the switch's alike, is thinner under the same 26 pt row and knob. The hand's catch is the row, unchanged.

title: A slider pressed by the hand holds the keyboard without a ring
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (UX Hierarchy in use and UI Colour, minor): a touched slider kept the bright blue focus ring after release, an accent beside the photo. A hand's press still gives the slider the keyboard (#1159) but marks its `KeyScope` pressed, which hides the ring; Tab, or an arrow acting on the slider, rings it, as the keyboard then works it, and the focus leaving clears the mark. Checks: window keyboard::tab_walks_every_control_in_reading_order_each_answering_its_own_keys (Tab rings the slider) and keyboard::a_pressed_slider_takes_the_arrows_until_escape_or_a_press_elsewhere (the press draws no ring, the arrow then rings it; with the ring always on, the press assertion fails).

title: A slider's value is a field a click opens, and its rail tells its double click
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (UX Micro-interactions and Obvious without a tutorial, minor): the typed value opened only on a double click of its 49 by 16 pt number, which nothing said was editable, and a double click reset a slider with no hint. The value is now a field: its box, the typed number's own (88 pt by a field's 32, run a padding past the number), is the target, shows the flat field's face and a text cursor under the hand, and a single click opens it there, its tooltip 'Click to type a value'. The rail tells its double click on hover, 'Double-click to bring it back to rest', the Slider's `help` by default; a stepped slider's own help, on its name and now its rail too, already said so. French and Spanish filled in. Checks: window keyboard::a_number_typed_over_a_slider_readout_steps_it_there (a click 12 pt above the number's middle opens it, one 20 pt above nothing; the label-sized target fails the first), keyboard::a_slider_tells_its_double_click_and_its_typed_value_under_the_hand (twin: beside the slider nothing is told).

title: A light knob's grip lines in the dark ink
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (UI Consistency, minor): White point's knob was a plain white disc, its white grip lines on a white cap. The ink that once followed a white cap was lost when the knob moved into the design system; the knob now picks its grip ink from its cap: the text-on-fill white, or the on-light ink past an OKLab lightness of 0.6 (`SliderStyle.grip-turn`), where the two inks' contrasts cross. White point and the levels' white and light-grey handles carry dark lines; every darker cap keeps white ones.

title: The library column's tab bar, headers and rows share one inset, edge to edge
detail: Owner's review: the tab bar (Archive / Projects) and the header rows stood at Space.md from the column's edges while the navigator's rows lit a band from Space.sm and the tree's from CardStyle.inset, 8 pt wider on each side, and the tree's thumbnails sat Space.md inside their band again. One token, ShellStyle.column-inset (Space.md), now pads the tab bar, the navigator's header and rows and the tree's header and column; a line of thumbnails spans the band as a row does (sidebar::frames lays no inner inset, Metrics.medium removed), so every edge of the column lines up with the tab bar's. Checks: the frames' unit test asserts a pair of photos flush with the folder's band, its twin a pair inset by 16 pt off it; tree_leftovers reads the column's inset where it read the card's.

title: The folders' rows hold the keyboard only while Slint's focus says so, ringed; leaving the editor gives the photos the arrows
detail: Evaluation (UX Accessibility, major): after leaving the editor the focus was invisible and the arrows folded folders in the tree. Cause: a click on a navigator row set a Rust flag (nav.keys) that sent the arrows, Space and Return to the rows until a click on the grid, while Slint's focus stayed on the window's monitor, so no ring showed, and nothing else dropped the flag: the editor opened and left by the mode's key or the menu found it still set. The flag, its grid_took_keys resets and the rows' branch in the window's key path are removed; the rows answer their keys from their own KeyScope, which a click on a row (as on a slider) or Tab gives the keyboard and any other press or a change of screen takes back, so the arrows act on the rows only while the ring shows on the picked row. Return still renames the folder clicked, as approved for the explorer. Assistive tools name the holder by a list labelled Folders round the scope. The finding that the gallery's accessibility tree still listed the editor's sliders and keys was not reproduced: Slint's search and AccessKit drop hidden items and the panel is not instantiated in the gallery; the evaluation's shots show the editor still on screen. Checks: column_edges asserts the rows named as the keyboard's holder after a click, the grid's press and the editor's round trip handing the arrows to the photos with every fold kept, no slider listed back in the gallery (twin: the panel's sliders listed beside a photo); the navigator and explorer checks click their rows through the window's pointer hook, and the grid's twin presses before its click.

title: The column's header is one select naming the tree's layout in words, its menu the column's view
detail: Evaluation (UI Iconography): the filmstrip's and the Projects header's keys were small glyphs (a target, a grid, fold-all) read only through their tooltips, and the layout key cycled while naming the next layout. The plate of glyph keys and the pill beside it (the opened folder's name, or ONI Projects, both already on screen in the tree's pinned row and the tab bar) give way to one flat select across the column: it names the layout in words (Names only, Two thumbnails a line, One thumbnail a line) and its menu offers the three layouts, then Show the Selected Photo and, on the projects, Open or Fold every folder. Library.tree-layout-picked(int) replaces tree-layout-next and its help string; Layout::name and next go, and Navigator.opened-title and opened-help with the pill. A pill picker with a menu to drop now wears the chevron, so the navigator's ancestors pill shows it opens too. Checks: column_edges opens the select, finds the menu's lines, picks One thumbnail a line and reads the tree laid so and the select renamed (twin: the former name gone), and asserts the select spans the column's inset; sidebars asserts no control on the header needs its note to be read (twin: the former glyph keys are refused); tree_leftovers, tree_hand and library_column pick layouts by index.

title: Escape steps out of one thing at a time, the editor last
detail: UX evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Consistency of behaviour, major): Escape left Prepare the Roll but not the crop, Compare, De-dust or the editor. Measured first: the evaluation tool sends its keys and clicks into Slint, past the window's key and pointer hooks (`outside::keyed`, `outside::pressed`); once the Temperature slider it had dragged hid with the Colour pane, Slint dropped the keyboard and every later key went nowhere, which the key hook answers in the app. What the merges since #1111 did break: the pressed slider (#1132) spent Escape on itself while every other control holding the keyboard let it through, so one press left the crop or not by the control touched last, and a field's Escape left the mode behind it. One rule now, one thing a press: a help card, a sheet, a field's typing (ended as a press elsewhere ends it), a control's hold of the keyboard (the key monitor takes Escape from any control before it hears it, the slider's own branch gone), the export surface, Prepare, Compare, the crop or De-dust, the Lab (its Escape moved into the rule), then the editor for the gallery; a held Escape acts once. Checks: window escape::escape_steps_out_one_thing_at_a_time_and_each_tool_ends_by_its_done (the field's typing ends alone; the pressed Angle slider first, the crop second; Compare before the crop); editor_routes and scanner, a second Escape on Colour or Pro leaving the editor; the keyboard probe, Escape still handing a pressed slider's keyboard back.

title: The crop and De-dust are the canvas's two tools, each left by its DONE
detail: UX evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Trust, Consistency of behaviour): De-dust ended on a DONE key, the crop only by its bar key, ⌘K, Return or Escape, and it was a tab besides. The route already held both as modal tools left for the last panel; now they look alike. The tab bar lists the panes, Roll, Colour and Details; either tool, opened by its bar key or menu (⌘K for the crop), names itself in the bar's place beside a DONE keycap (`ModeHeader`, shared, `DedustHeader` gone). Return is either tool's DONE (`Validated::Leave`), the measuring window applied first as before; the bar's CROP key says Leave Crop while on, as De-dust's says Leave De-dust, and COMPARE shows the menu's Close Comparison. `PanelState.crop-closed`, which only greyed the Crop tab, goes with it; the bar's key and the menu stay out of reach while frames show together. French and Spanish filled in. Checks: tabs::return_disarms_the_window_first_then_leaves_either_tool (twin: Details takes no Return); window escape (DONE leaves the crop, no DONE beside a pane), together_tools, editor_routes (Tab enters the bar, its arrow reaching Details).

title: Return on the grid opens what Space opens
detail: UX evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Expert efficiency, Consistency of behaviour): Return on a selected tile opened nothing, as Swift's Return opened the keyboard's cursor alone where Space fell back on the selection. One key now (`GridKey::Open`): Return or Space opens the cursor, else the first photo picked, else the first shown; ⌘ or ⇧ held leaves it to the menus, a held key opens once. With #1244's last step, Escape and Return or Space carry the photo between gallery and editor; the mode key's tooltip says Gallery (Esc, Space or ⌘G), and Prepare's Gallery (Esc or ⌘G). Checks: organise::return_or_space_opens_and_command_a_completes_the_rolls_touched (a selection with no cursor opens its first photo; twin: the cursor first), window escape and editor_routes (Return on the grid opens the photo again).

title: Paste to Roll says how many photos it rewrote, its UNDO beside
detail: UX evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Trust): Paste to Roll rewrote 25 photos in one click with no count or notice of the change. The bar's PASTE TO ROLL key now shows the menu's title, Paste to Roll (25 Photos), before the click; after it, the notice over every surface says Settings pasted on 25 photos of the roll, its UNDO walking that step back while it is the last, and the crop's Paste to Roll says Crop pasted on … alike. The count is the photos of the step the paste laid; a paste that rewrote nothing, or failed (its own notice then standing), says nothing. `told_step` binds its UNDO to a step with no name too, an edit of the open frame as a roll's paste is. No confirmation added: the count before and the undo after keep the gesture one click. French and Spanish filled in. Checks: window escape (a paste rewriting nothing is silent; one photo rewritten says so, and UNDO takes it back).

title: Prepare's step key rises as NEXT once the step holds its value; before, a flat Skip
detail: UX evaluation: on the Base step the blue primary keycap read SKIP while no film base was picked, inviting the one skip that lowers the odds of a good conversion. The key's look now follows the step's state at its source (`key` beside `filled`): NEXT, the accent keycap, once the step holds its value; a flat Skip before, so the pick the step asks for stays its call to act. Flat-Field and a slide's white take the same rule; no step is cut, and a roll with no bare film can still go on without one. The footer key follows the design system's capitals like Cancel and Back beside it. Twin: a base picked raises NEXT, never Skip.

title: Prepare's demos play once when asked; the epilepsy warning is a caption
detail: UX evaluation: the step's clip started by itself under the controls, the Window step's for 26.5 s, so the step never settled beside the scan, with no way to keep it still. A Show How key now plays the step's clip once from its start, resting on its last frame; pressed again, or on another step, or while measuring, it goes. Nothing moves beside the scan unasked, which is the reduced-motion answer on both systems with no setting to read. The epilepsy warning under the Frame slider is a secondary caption in sentence case, below the step's own text, never orange capitals. The help card's looping demo is the card's own (app/help/clip.rs), outside Prepare. Twins: a step change puts the demo away; the film step offers none.

title: One name a concept in Prepare: the measuring window, and Prepare Roll for the measure
detail: UX evaluation: the Window tab, a Place the Measuring Frame heading and the editor's Measuring Window block named one thing three ways, frame also being a photo of the roll; the window step's key read MEASURE 14 FRAMES and the gallery's band Not measured yet where the key that opens Prepare reads PREPARE ROLL. The heading, both details and the empty-measure advice now say measuring window; the walk ends on PREPARE ROLL, the bar's own word, its count of measured frames left to the Frame slider (a flagged frame is prepared without voting, so a count on the key misled), and the band says Not prepared yet. French and Spanish follow.

title: Prepare's step bar numbers its steps and checks the done ones
detail: UI evaluation: the five steps looked like a segmented control, a corner dot the only sign of a step done. `Tabs` takes `ordered`: each tab leads with its place in a small disc (`TabsStyle.step`, the hollow's and the pill's lighter track), the disc showing the accent check once the step is done; the corner dot stays for the bars that mark a value. The bar keeps its hollow and sliding pill, 2.5D as the tabs stay, each step's tab a disc wider (`RollStyle.step-tab`).

title: A contact sheet is ONI's own file, never a frame of its roll
detail: Evaluation (UX Robustness and Task fit, major): roll #8 showed 25 photos, the 25th the Swift app's '2026-09-14 — contact sheet.tif', whose sidecar holds the sheet's grid and names the roll's reference; Whole Roll picked it, Export offered it as a frame, Roll Settings and Paste to Roll wrote it, and Prepare the Roll and Edit Together's numbering each read every sidecar again to leave it out. The rule now sits at the source, once: the index reads the grid off the sidecar's envelope with the rest of the row (a sheet column, schema 10, one rebuild), and the rows the gallery draws leave contact sheets out, so every band, count, pick, measure, numbering and export sees the frames alone. The guards that re-read each sidecar go (Prepare's, Edit Together's and the contact-sheet export's numbering), and with them Reset the Roll's trip of the sheet to the ONI Trash and its second wording: ONI leaves a file it never lists where it is. A sheet already in the ONI Trash still shows there. Departs from #1033's 'a sheet already on disk still opens on its grid'. Left: a file ONI exported carries no mark of its own, so one saved into a roll folder is still a scan to the archive; telling it needs a mark in every export, an owner's call on the export's metadata (none is written when nothing is stated). Twins: the same file with no grid in its sidecar is drawn; the index round trip holds the column set; the numbering reads the folder's order, reversed to the other numbers.

title: Temperature and Tint name the side they lean to beside their stops
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (UX Language, major; UI Clarity): Temperature and Tint read in EV, true since they move the print filters in stops, where a photographer expects kelvin or a cool–warm scale. A kelvin would be false, so each colour readout names the end of its track the value leans to before its number, which keeps its true unit: Warm +0.46 EV, Cool −0.30 EV, Green −0.06 EV, Magenta +0.12 EV, 0.00 EV at rest. The word goes first so the number holds the readout's right edge. The fields carry their colour axis (`fields::Axis`, `Readout::along`), so Pro's Temperature and Tint, the flat-field's in the Roll tab and in Prepare, and the phone's copies of them read alike. A number typed over such a readout leaves the word aside and reads its sign (`slider_track::read`); the typing field widens to the longest readout, Magenta −0.00 EV. Checks: fields::a_colour_readout_names_the_end_it_leans_to_beside_its_true_unit (twin: the bare formatter leaves the side to the reader), slider_track::a_number_typed_over_a_readout_is_the_steps_an_arrow_would_take (twin: the side without its sign steps the wrong way). French and Spanish filled in.

title: The Scanner face's sliders read what each key moves, in a true unit
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (UI Clarity): the Scanner face's D, C, M, Y and TEMP read bare counts with no unit or step size. The Lab's screen still counts the keypad's points, as a minilab's does; each slider under it now reads what its key moves. D, C, M and Y read the light in stops, from the measured Frontier click on the key's own channel (D the mean of the three): a press moves D 0.06 EV, C 0.03, M 0.03, Y 0.04, so +1.5 on D reads +0.17 EV. TEMP reads its share of the machine's warm or cool look, 5% a press, after the side it leans to: Warm +20%. A number typed over a letter's readout finds its steps through the exact size of one step (`Readout::scaled`). Checks: lab::sliders::a_letter_reads_what_it_moves_in_a_true_unit (twins: the screen's count says no unit; C read on green reads nothing), lab::sliders::a_number_typed_over_a_scanner_readout_finds_its_steps, window scanner.

title: The export summary at the panel's text size
detail: Evaluation (UI Typography): the export summary's four facts (bits, size, estimated weight) were set in the value face, 11 pt, a step smaller than every other line of the panel. They now take the label size, as the note under them. The export_panel window check measures them as tall as a field's label; its twin, the summary set back in the value face, fails, and the subtitle's smaller face measures smaller.

title: The space's note stands in no conditional block, so Quality keeps one step under the profile keys
detail: Evaluation (UI Spacing): Quality stood 3 pt under Load a Profile…, where other groups keep 16 pt. Measured on the headless window: the Space field and its two-line note sat in SpaceField's `if !compact` block, and Slint 1.18.1 sizes a block shown on a condition with the wrapped words inside it on one line, so the field was given 16 pt less than it drew and the keys ran onto Quality; the same field shown on no condition is sized right. The panel now lays the Space field on no condition, its tabs shared with the chip as SpaceTabs; the profile's trouble and the choice still to make, which wrapped in conditional blocks of their own, are the one note under the tabs, written by Rust (space-note replaces purpose, profile-note and pending-note), so a pending Custom no longer shows P3's purpose; the news badge leaves no empty row and gap when there is none; the chip's popover shows the tabs, their note and both profile keys in every space. The export_panel check asserts one step from the two-line note to the keys and from the keys to Quality, on P3 and on Custom; its twin, the field put back in a conditional block of SpaceField, fails.

title: The export's EXIF fields lie on the panel's ground, where their faces show
detail: Evaluation (UI Clarity): under the picture the placeholder 'Your name' read as a value. The fields stood on the canvas card, whose ground is the fields' own face colour, so no face showed and a placeholder sat like a fact in a table. Each line's eight fields now lie on a flat rounded block of the panel's ground (Surface gains `rounded`, Radius.card), as every other field of the app does, so each face shows dark and a placeholder reads as the hint inside it. The export_panel check reads the drawn pixels: the Artist field's face differs from the ground beside it; twin: the canvas has the face's colour, and the block set on it fails the check.

title: The export's date reads 2026-09-14 16:46:19, the file keeps EXIF's colons
detail: Evaluation (UI Clarity): the Date field showed EXIF's raw 2026:09:14 16:46:19. The field now shows and takes the date dashed, as the app names its contact sheets, while the sidecar and the file keep EXIF's form (export_card::dated): a date typed dashed is written with colons, one pasted in EXIF's form is kept, anything else is left as typed. A unit test with its twins (half a date, a day-first date, words, the time's colons untouched), and the export_panel check types a dashed date through the field's callback, reads EXIF's form in the row and the dashed one back in the line.

title: The Settings sheet keeps one height whichever section is open
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Spacing and density): the sheet grew between General and Editor, so the dialog and its DONE key jumped. The body laid only the page shown under a guessed 320 pt floor, which Editor passed. Every page now shares one grid cell and only the chosen one shows, so the cell is the tallest page's height in the language spoken; a page takes the card's width, so a hidden page's widest row never widens the one shown. SheetStyle.settings-height goes. Check: window sheet_layout::the_settings_sheet_keeps_one_height_across_its_sections, DONE at one place on General, Editor, Frontier Look and About (the former layout moved it 11.5 px); twin: General's last line ends more than 60 px above DONE, room a sheet fit to the page shown would close.

title: The switch reads on or off at a glance, never as a slider at its minimum
detail: Evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Clarity): off, the slide lever showed the slider's grey rail with the knob at its start, a slider at its minimum; on and off differed by a rail 9 % whiter. The lever keeps the slider's knob and its travel, but now runs in a slot of its own (ToggleStyle.slot, so a slider's rail made thinner never thins it): an Inward hollow cut to the canvas as the tab bar's, dark while off, lit up to the knob (the slider's lit) while on, never tinted, the accent staying the view's one primary. The knob uncovers the state's mark, an O ring on the hollow while off and an I on the lit stretch while on, as a power switch's. The design system's README and the ui-spec say so.

title: The crop's thirds read on a shadow as on a sky
detail: The evaluators found the crop grid mid-grey with no halo, nearly lost over the dark shed and the mid-tones. Its source: the thirds drew half a point at the faint guide's 35 % white, which a 1x screen halves into one grey pixel, a horizontal third losing its light core entirely between two rows. The thirds are now a whole point in the crop edge bars' rest ink (55 % white), edged a point either side by the contrast shade as every guide over a photo is, so the core reads over the shed as over the sky and stays quieter than the frame's own 90 % line. GuideLine gives its breadth (band), which the thirds take instead of repeating it. Seen on a 1x window check: a 139-164 core between 24-57 edges on dark green, deep red and magenta.

title: Compare's divider carries a slider's knob
detail: The evaluators found Compare's divider a bare 1 pt white line with no handle, faint over a light sky. The split is a slider laid over the photo, so it now wears the panel sliders' own knob (the small level keycap with its two grip lines) on its middle, growing under the hand as theirs does, over the line and its contrast edges; the whole height still grabs and a press anywhere on it still moves the split. Nothing new to tune: the knob is the sliders'.

title: The crop's kept size reads as every other value
detail: The evaluators found the kept dimensions in a one-off black bold pill. The crop tab set them on the scanner's LCD glass, which belongs to the scanner and the status bar's count. Kept is now a ValueHeader, the readout every slider uses: its name in the label ink, the size right in the secondary value ink, its real unit (px) kept.

title: The canvas header names the space first and glosses it after
detail: The evaluators found the canvas header dimming the working space's name (Display P3) and brightening its gloss (phones & screens), which inverts value and description. The Picker's secondary words came before its value, and the chip passed the name as those words and the gloss as the value. The secondary words now follow the value (note, replacing prefix, which only the chip used): the chip shows the name in the primary ink, then the gloss in the secondary, and short of room the gloss elides first. Its accessible name reads the same, name then gloss.

title: Rotate & Mirror's keys say what they do: Rotate ↻, Mirror ↔, Mirror ↕
detail: UI evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Iconography, raised twice): the block showed three bare 16 pt glyphs, the rotate one read as a cup rather than a turn, and the vertical mirror borrowed the horizontal glyph turned a quarter. The three keys are now worded and share one plate alike, as Crop's COPY, PASTE and PASTE TO ROLL above them, the sign after each word (↻, ↔, ↕, all in Inter) showing how the photo moves; tooltips unchanged. Measured in Inter at the legend's size, each catalogue's three words fit the 308 pt column in capitals, three glyphs and words would not. French Pivoter ↻, Miroir ↔, Miroir ↕; Spanish Girar ↻, Espejo ↔, Espejo ↕. Window check the_panels_switches_follow_their_owner_and_its_blocks_reset presses each key by its word and asserts a quarter turn, a flip top for bottom and a flip left for right, each its own, which Crop's RESET then clears; the_sidebars_lay_their_keys_on_plates_as_swift finds the plate spanning its block and stopping at its edge, its words evenly apart (twin: keys pushed past the edge are refused).

title: The Measuring Window's copy and paste are worded, and its reset is the block's own RESET
detail: UI evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Iconography): copy and paste were words in the toolbar and in Crop but bare glyphs in the Measuring Window; the block's reset glyph also shared their plate, against the rule that a key which resets never shares a plate with one that keeps. The block now resets through the RESET every block carries on its title's row, shown while a window is set; Set window / Apply window spans the column, lit while armed; Copy and Paste share a plate alike below it, worded as Crop's. On two rows the French Appliquer la fenêtre, in capitals, never crowds the copy keys off the column. The block's note says Reset takes the window away and Copy and Paste carry it from one photo to another. Window check the_panels_switches_follow_their_owner_and_its_blocks_reset copies the window, presses the RESET on the Measuring Window's row (one, and Crop's still leaves the window) and asserts it gone, then Paste lays it back.

title: The gallery's right column is the editor's panel wide, so the card's edge holds between them
detail: UI evaluation (Spacing): the gallery's Info column was 280 points, the editor's panel 340, so the canvas card's right edge jumped 60 points at each switch. The Info column takes ShellStyle.panel-width and ShellStyle.info-width is gone: one right column, the width Prepare's panel already had. That exposed a grid that told Rust its size only on a change: in a window built at its final size, the old narrow column's reflow had been the change, and without it gallery_cell and visible laid no tile. The grid now keeps its size in Library.grid-width and grid-height from its making, and Rust reads them once its handler listens. Window check panel_frame finds the gallery's Film Stock title and the editor's Colour title at the same point, a panel's width plus its inset from the window's edge; twin: a column 60 points narrower puts its blocks elsewhere.

title: A block's title row keeps its keys at the column's edge; titles in their own case
detail: UI evaluation (Consistency, Spacing): Spectrogram Finishing showed no fold key and the Roll tab's chevrons drifted right as titles lengthened. The title had its whole width whatever the row held, and in spaced capitals the longest pushed the always-laid RESET and the fold key past the column, 33 points out for Spectrogram Finishing. The title now yields on a short row (elided, never the keys), and is set in its own case, capitals being the keycaps' alone (owner's art direction), which also keeps every English title whole. Window check panel_frame finds the six fold keys of the Colour tab with one right edge on the column's inset; the old row fails it (Spectrogram Finishing's key at 1273 points for 1240 in a 1280-point window); twin: a key pushed three points is refused.

title: A help mark's card covers the column of the block it explains
detail: UI evaluation (Consistency): the Colour card opened 300 points wide from its mark, held a margin from the window's edge, so the block's first letters (Te, Tir, Sa) peeked out at its left. A Section's mark now names its block's column, the section's inset edges, and Tips.note takes that width: the card lies edge to edge with the inset, its demo as wide; a mark naming no column keeps its own width at the mark. Window check help_card asserts each panel card over its block's column; twin: the card at its own width from its mark leaves 16 points of the block out.

title: The Colour tab's help notes in short parts, each about its own block
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Typography, Language): the Colour card ran a thirteen-line paragraph and mixed the Roll tab's Balance strength and the roll's levels into the white balance. A note now comes in short parts a blank line apart, one per key or slider group, and says only what its block holds: Colour (Auto White Balance, Temperature and Tint by the colours their tracks show, Saturation), Paper Correction, Lighting, Effects (the Scanner's too), Spectrogram Finishing and Saturation Curve, in English, French and Spanish. The white balance key's own tooltip still names Balance strength. Window check help_demo_color reads the Lighting and Effects cards by their new words.

title: A key out of reach reads apart from a tab merely not chosen
detail: Evaluation round 2: a disabled key and an unselected tab or segment shared one grey, as PASTE and Scanner side by side in the editor's bar. Out of reach was a 0.4 opacity of the key's white ink, an idle label 0.55 of the primary ink: about 3.7:1 against 4.8:1 on the ground, no difference to the eye. State.disabled now has its own step, AppKit's disabled control ink at 0.25 (about 2.4:1), for every control that cannot act (keys, tabs, menu lines, pickers, readouts, preset cards); a missing original, a folder away and a frame left out keep the missing state's 0.4 as State.missing, their picture and name still read. A disabled switch's words fade with it instead of taking the secondary ink an idle label wears. The states window check reads the two inks apart; its twin, a key at the old fade, reads alike.

title: A destructive key turns red only while the hand or the keyboard is on it
detail: Evaluation round 2: the trash stayed saturated red in the gallery bar, even dimmed while disabled, a colour beside the photo the UI bench refuses. Its red was bound to the kind alone. A destructive key now shows the danger's red while it is hovered, pressed or holds the keyboard, the moment the hand is about to act, and keeps the plain ink at rest and out of reach; its own plate still sets it apart. The states window check reads no red at rest or disabled and red under the hand; its twin, a glyph worn red at rest, is seen.

title: The hand's ring stands on the ground round a gallery tile
detail: Evaluation round 2: a hovered tile showed no perceptible change. The hover ring lay over the picture's own edge in white at 47 %, lost on a light sky and grey on a dark one. It now stands an outset ring's width outside the picture on the canvas, about 4.7:1 there whatever the photo and covering none of it; the selection keeps its ring inside, so a selected tile under the hand shows both. The states window check reads the ring against the ground at 3:1 or more; its twin, a tile at rest, reads the bare ground.

title: A latching key carries a lamp, dark until its mode is on
detail: Evaluation round 2 (Play): CROP, COMPARE and DE-DUST on showed only a lighter grey face, no latch. Button's lamp, unused, becomes `latch`: a key that stays on until pressed again carries a lamp after its word, dark glass at rest so it tells it latches before the press, lit by `on` in the scanner LCD's phosphor, a glow with no hue beside the photo. The bar's mode keys and the Measuring Window's SET WINDOW latch; the lab's lamp row follows. The states window check reads the lamp lit and dark.

title: The straighten turns on a dial
detail: UI evaluation s-0abd2d65 (Art direction): no dial anywhere, metal only in the medals, and the Pro panel read as generic software. The straighten's angle, the panel's one true turn, is now a camera's command dial seen edge on (Slider { dial }, ds/dial.slint, DialStyle in theme_sliders.slint): a black-anodised ring in an Inward slot, its degree scale (a mark each half degree, a figure every two) foreshortened and shaded toward the ends under a fixed index, figures only within DialStyle.figures (66°) of it, so none is cut at the ring's ends. The scale moves with the hand, so a drag right brings the lower degrees under the index, and a press anywhere never jumps it; the ring turns DialStyle.turn (9°) a degree, a degree standing about 24 pt apart at the index against the rail's 18. The readout, the typed value, the keys, the scroll, the double click's reset and accessibility stay the slider's; Rust publishes the scale's ends (Framing.angle-lowest and angle-highest, from Geometry::ANGLE_RANGE). Window check dial::the_straighten_dial_turns_with_the_hand_and_a_press_never_jumps_it: a press on the ring leaves 0°, a 48 pt drag right lowers the angle by 48 pt over a degree's spacing within 0.05° (twin: the rail's sense, raising it as much, fails).

title: Every title is engraved, in its own case
detail: Owner's art direction: capitals belong to the keycap CTAs alone; and the UI evaluation s-0abd2d65 found the Pro panel, Settings and Export short of the analogue nods the Scanner face and the gallery carry. A block's title drops the capitals and the seal's tracking #1220 gave it and keeps its engraving, now one DS piece (Engraved, a Label whose three copies draw the groove's shade a line above, the lit edge a line below, then the ink, the root laying the words out unseen); every sheet's title (Settings among them, a question's too) and the export's heading take it, so the three screens bear the same camera's marking at their head. The screen reader hears each title once, as written.

title: The figures the app reports read on the glass
detail: UI evaluation s-0abd2d65: Export read as generic software, its summary a well of type smaller than the panel's; the crop's kept size sat alone on its LCD pill. What the export writes now reads as Kept does: each figure on the LcdReadout beside its label (the bit depth's line its size, Estimated size its weight), the well gone and the notes under them, so the column's one textured piece is small. The size reads in pixels, '6048 × 4031 px', from the formatter Kept uses (geometry::pixel_label), under each preview too. Settings > About shows the version on the same glass. The weight's labels are in sentence case, Estimated size and Estimated total size, French and Spanish with them. Checks: export_sheet's sizes read in pixels; export_window's caption still equals the summary's size.

title: The toolbar's flat keys speak in title case; capitals stay on its keycaps
detail: Owner's art direction: ALL CAPS only on the keycap CTAs. The bar's word key wrote every word in capitals whatever its face; it now writes them only on a keycap (EDITOR/GALLERY, PREPARE ROLL, the export slot), so Crop, Compare, Whole Roll, Copy, Paste, Paste to Roll and De-dust, and the filter's All, read in title case. French and Spanish follow, the mode keys sharing the panel's own words.

title: The accent lands on each screen's own commit
detail: Evaluation, UI Hierarchy (major): on a roll never measured the blue ADD FOLDER… outranked PREPARE ROLL, and it stayed the blue primary on the projects and in the ONI Trash, where it serves nothing. The bar now reads the roll's measure (Library.roll-unmeasured, cleared where no roll stands, so the projects and the Trash no longer keep the last roll's) and whether the gallery is on the archive (Bar.archive): PREPARE ROLL takes the accent while the roll waits for it, the slot keeps its keycap without it there, on the projects and in the Trash; EXPORT and an update keep theirs. The window check toolbar::the_accent_lands_on_each_screens_own_commit reads the blue on each key's face: ADD FOLDER… on an empty archive, PREPARE ROLL alone beside two unmeasured frames, none on the projects nor in the Trash; twin: the former rule (the slot always blue, PREPARE ROLL plain) fails it beside the unmeasured roll.

title: RESET is a glyph on its own plate, lighter than the keys that keep the work
detail: Evaluation, UI Hierarchy: the editor's bar was nine equal words, RESET weighing as much as COMPARE. The reset is now a square glyph key on its own plate in both modes, as undo and redo are, its gesture and shortcut in its tooltip; the words left are the modes and the clipboard.

title: The feedback key draws a bug, never a chat
detail: Evaluation, Iconography: the speech bubbles beside the gear read as a chat. The key draws a bug in the Trinil set's stroke, the report it opens; the bubbles' file goes, no other key drew it.

title: Every screen, flow and interaction may be rethought; only the result is fixed
detail: Owner's direction: ONI's work is now making the app better through its UX and UI, every screen open to a full rethink, the conversion untouched. CLAUDE.md drops what held the interface to one way: the design system's tokens owe DSTokens.swift nothing, the drag-and-scroll rule becomes the current state rather than a rule, ui-spec and the parity inventory's interface rows are history, and the parity inventory covers the result alone.

title: Hard rule 1 becomes: nothing is hidden from the person
detail: Owner's call: 'nothing decides on its own' did not hold, the app already acts on its own around editing. The rule is transparency instead: every automatic step and every value of the conversion stays visible and reachable, the levels and gains shown and editable even while the automatic mode sets them. UX Trust rates it.

title: One title component and one capitals rule after the merges
detail: Two correctors drew the engraved title apart: Engraved stays, SectionTitle goes, every column header at the section's step. The toolbar's word keys lose a property the button no longer has: the button writes capitals on a keycap alone.

title: Every figure the app reports reads on the glass, the crop's kept size with them
detail: Two correctors went opposite ways: the kept size left the LCD for a slider's readout while the export's figures and the version moved onto it, citing the kept size. One rule now: a figure the app reports, never typed, reads on the LcdReadout beside its label, the crop's kept size, the export's size and weight, the version, the status bar's count; a value the hand sets reads in its slider's header.

title: The merged wave's checks: one name per key, the guides in their own file, words as shown
detail: Crop and its measuring window both had a key named Copy and one named Paste, so a screen reader heard each twice: the window's keys now carry their tooltip as their name. The guides over a photo leave base.slint, past its 400 lines, for guides.slint. A spread field's name keeps its own height, centred on its row, so the export's figures measure as a label beside the glass. The straighten is wired on one line as every slider. The checks read Restore and Undo as shown, capitals being the keycaps' alone.

title: The art direction's model is the lab scanner's console
detail: Owner's call: ONI's analogue nods come above all from the old lab film scanners' consoles, their mechanical keyboards and physical faders, hence the keycaps and the slider tracks; a film camera is a lesser nod. UI Art direction and UX Play say so.

title: The art direction is a balance: ordinary software, perfectly designed, with a few real-world reminders
detail: Owner's call, replacing #1305: ONI should feel like ordinary, perfectly designed digital software with a few deeply satisfying reminders of the real world, a fair balance between pure minimal flat 2D and cues such as a discreet reflection, a shadow or a key that presses. The benches name no hardware to imitate: going further into the analogue reads as a costume.

title: UI Clarity: each control shows its own extent at rest
detail: Owner's catch: flat keys sharing one plate could be told apart only under the hand. A shared plate was a socket of keycaps; the bench now asks that every control show its own extent at rest, whatever groups it.

title: The file dialogs answer from ONI_ANSWERS, so an evaluation lives the import and the export
detail: An evaluation drives the app through Slint's MCP server, which reaches no system panel: Add Folder and every export stopped at the dialog. With ONI_ANSWERS set, each dialog takes the path laid in its folder's answer file once, a dialog with none answering as cancelled; unset, the panels show as before. Checks: an answer is taken once (twin: the second dialog finds none); a save into a folder keeps the suggested name (twin: a file path stands as given).

title: The fifth wave's merges: one rest, one reset carrying the stock's dyes, one copy sheet, one footer
detail: Correctors met in five places. A double click's rest is one function that lands the same value on every frame shown. A block's reset carries the stock's dyes and gives each frame shown its own rest. Copy Settings opens its carries sheet from the bar, the menu bar and a cell's menu, the gallery's one photo picked included. Prepare's footer is the shared sheet footer. The status line names the frame's place and the crop's kept size. The medal probes moved clear of the switches.

title: Frames edited together take each step value by value: a hand's move by its distance, nothing it left alone
detail: UX evaluation (Trust, Expert efficiency): on the Whole Roll a Temperature drag laid frame 1's whole print block on every frame, its Tint with it, and any slider set one absolute value on all, so balances measured frame by frame were lost. The store now keeps what the open frame took during a step and lays exactly that on each frame together: a knob the hand moved (Step) moves each frame by the same distance from its own value, clamped once from the step's start so a frame held at an end finds its offset again; a value set (Set, a double click's rest) lands on each through the knob, so Temperature never moves Tint; a scanner key presses each frame's own counts; a structured edit lays the values it moved, leaf by leaf (Field::patch), never a whole block. The sliders' drags, scrolls, arrows and typed numbers send Step, the double click Set. A block's reset key on frames together brings each to its own rest, as the bar's reset does (reset_each). The roll's propagation leaves the frames together to their own step, so a slide together moves once on its own measure. A step still waiting is recorded before the frames together change. Unit checks with twins in oni-core (store::tests::together, slides, fields); window check together_moves drags Temperature over three frames balanced apart.

title: A slider over frames shown together reads their span before any change
detail: UX evaluation (Expert efficiency): a value that differs across the selection showed the open frame's alone. Each slider's readout now reads the span of the frames shown together, lowest to highest with the unit once, the colour end named when both lean to it (Warm +0.37 … +1.21 EV), one value where all read the same; a drag shifts the span whole under the hand, and leaving the group gives back the single value. The span is read from the store's live frames, the step under the hand included. Window check together_moves; unit check fields::tests with its twin on the black point's inverted sense.

title: Crop and De-dust out of reach say why under the hand
detail: UX evaluation (Robustness): on frames together Crop and De-dust greyed out with no word. A key out of reach now still tells its help under the hand and takes no press (the design system's Button), and the two keys say Select one photo to crop it / to de-dust it while frames show together, in English, French and Spanish. Window check together_moves hovers both, and its twin hovers Crop on one frame alone.

title: The Scanner face shows every value acting on its frame
detail: UX evaluation (Trust): the Scanner face read D, C, M and Y at zero while the frame carried Pro's values. Read in the pipeline, the Scanner render takes the roll's conversion (Film Type, Filtration, Highlight Detail, Per-Channel Levels, Dye Separation) and Auto White Balance's correction at the roll's strength, and none of Pro's Lighting, Colour or Effects sliders. Per-Channel Levels, Dye Separation and Auto White Balance, which the face hid though they act, now stand on its Roll tab as on Pro's. The scanner's screen reads, in place of the finishing its own sliders already show, the balance its render prints with, taken from that render's own filters in Pro's Temperature and Tint readouts. The Machine help says what both faces share and that Pro's sliders stay Pro's own. No render changes; the Frontier's rest held in the gains still reads zero. Unit check the_screen_spells_every_count_and_the_balance_as_the_lab_does, twin: Pro's Temperature moved by hand never reaches the screen; window checks scanner and the_panel_lays_out_only_the_blocks_a_photo_and_a_face_have read the blocks on the Scanner face.

title: One readout at the panel's top, inset as its rows, alike on both faces
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Spacing, Craft in use): the histogram and the scanner's screen ran flush to the panel's edges and the canvas while every row kept the panel's inset, and switching faces swapped one for the other. The panel's top is now one readout, inset by the rows' 16 points at the sides and the top, its corner the plots' and the canvas card's: Pro's histogram, the Scanner face's screen and the loupe under Details each fill it, so a face or a tab changes only what it shows. The loupe's band is the readout's width; the screen's counts take equal columns with no gap, so the inset costs them no room. The scanner window check finds D's rail by its role and name, no longer at a fixed point.

title: One slider on both faces: no step keys, a tick and a detent at rest, the name's double click
detail: UX evaluation (Consistency, Play): the Scanner face's sliders carried − and + keys that Pro's had not, and neither held at rest. The step keys go: a Scanner slider is Pro's rail, its steps taken by the hand, the arrows (⇧ for three) or a number typed over the readout. Every slider with a rest, both faces alike, ticks it on its rail, holds a drag there for six points of the hand's travel (SliderStyle.detent) and then goes on from there without a jump, ⌥ passing through it for the finest move; a dial keeps its scale under the hand. A double click on the name now brings a Pro slider back to rest as on the rail and on the Scanner face, through the rail's one rest (Store.rests, Store.rest). A drag held on rest lands on its exact value. The keypad's dead legends and the keys' tooltips leave; the Scanner helps count half a point a step. Unit check a_drag_held_on_rest_lands_on_it_exactly; window checks slider_rest (twin: a knob left under the hand stands twenty points past rest) and scanner (zero holds ten moves more than +1; twin: the steps beside it take their own width), both failing with the detent at zero.

title: Each face says what it holds at the head of its Colour tab
detail: UX evaluation (Obvious without a tutorial): the faces were explained only in the switch's tooltip, and 'Pro' said nothing of what it holds. Both names stay; the Colour tab opens on one line in the switch's own words, Pro: every setting by hand, the place to start, or Scanner: a minilab's density and colour, in steps, at the same place on both faces. The Scanner's tooltip leaves its keypad with the keys. Window check scanner reads each caption at one height; twin: Pro's words leave with its face.

title: The Pro face decides the light first: Lighting with Contrast, then Colour, then Effects
detail: The Colour tab laid Colour before Lighting and filed Contrast under Effects, against the order a photographer decides in. Lighting now leads, Contrast right after Exposure as in every editor's basic panel, and its reset clears Contrast with the light; Colour and Paper Correction follow, Effects keep Vignette and Chrome. Only the panel and its reset groups move, the phone remote's mirror with them: the pipeline's order and every render stay as they are. The Effects help card's demo still films Contrast until the demos are filmed again.

title: Auto White Balance in one place: Balance strength under its key
detail: Auto White Balance stood twice, a key in the Colour block and a folded block of the same name in the Roll tab holding its dose. Balance strength now stands right under the key, shown wherever the key is, slides and RGB passes included, and says when it is shared by the roll's other photos. Its reset is its own double click, since the Colour block's reset would rewrite every photo of the roll; the block, its reset group and its demo leave the Roll tab.

title: Spectrogram Finishing, Source Encoding and Halo limit named by their effect
detail: Engineering words a photographer does not parse: the hue wheel is the Colour Mixer, the profile a file naming none is read as is the Scan Profile, and the sharpening's overshoot clamp is Halo suppression. The help cards name the technique; the preset rows, the folds remembered and the news take the new names.

title: A block's help card opens in its flow, pushing the block down
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Consistency, Hierarchy in use, Spacing): the help card floated over its block's column, ended just under its text, half-covered the Black point label and played its demo over the very sliders it explains. A help mark is now a ghost toggle: pressed, its note opens as a card (an Inset, one padding on all four sides) in the block's flow under the title, the sliders pushed down and still in reach; pressed again it closes, and another mark's card takes its place, one at a time. A stacked Field opens its note the same way; the De-dust row's fallback mark, one note for many rows, is a plain tooltip. The hover card's mechanism goes: the tooltip layer's card mode, Tips.note, a key's note and column, Escape's help card branch. The demo's frames are asked by the card while it stands, so a card gone with its panel costs nothing, and a card standing again in another language plays that language's clip. Window checks help_card and help_demo*.

title: Each help mark is named with its block
detail: UX evaluation (Accessibility): every help key was announced 'What this block does'. A mark is now named and tipped 'Help on <title>' (Help on Lighting), its card the same region, in English, French and Spanish; the mark tells assistive tools whether its card is expanded. Window check help_card.

title: A block's Reset keeps one place, dimmed at rest, apart from its fold key
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Hierarchy, Craft in use): a block's Reset sat 8 pt from its fold chevron and appeared only once a value moved. It now always stands at the row's end, out of reach and dimmed while nothing moved, 24 pt from the fold key so the two read as two. Window check help_card.

title: A slider's tooltip stays down through its drag
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Consistency, Hierarchy in use): tooltips seemed to stay up after a press and during a slider's drag. Through the real event path the window's pointer hook takes a tooltip down on the press and no step of a drag, along the rail or off it, brings it back: the evaluation tool's clicks skip that hook. Window check tooltip::a_slider_s_tooltip_stays_down_through_its_drag, its twin a hookless press that leaves the tooltip standing.

title: A click on a folder's row gives the rows the keyboard unringed; the keys ring the pick
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Colour, Micro-interactions): a click on a navigator row drew the accent ring on it at rest, a second vivid blue beside the main key. As a pressed slider does, a click now gives the rows the keyboard with no ring; Tab or a key acting on them (an arrow, Space, Return) rings the picked row, and losing the keyboard forgets the click. Checked through the window's real event path, its pointer hook first: a click on a photo already hands the grid the arrows and Return, and ⌘ and ⇧ clicks gather photos in the grid (window check gallery) and in the filmstrip; those findings came from the evaluation's tool, which skips the hook and the modifiers. Window check gallery_keys: a click rings nothing, twin an arrow rings the pick; through the hook a click on a photo gives → and Return to the grid, twin unhooked the rows keep the arrows; ⌘ then ⇧ in the filmstrip gather A to D, twin a plain click leaves one photo.

title: A selected tile's ring reads on a light photo: its dark edge lies inside the ring, no longer under it
detail: Evaluation, UI Colour: a selected tile was marked by a thin white outline alone, faint on light photos. SelectionRing laid its dark edge one line in, where the two-point ring covering the bounds hid it; the edge now lies just inside the ring in the contrast edge's ink, so the ring reads white, dark, then the photo, on a sky as on a shadow. The gallery, Prepare the Roll's frames, the column's thumbnails and the projects' drop ring share the fix. Check: gallery_cell's selected ring, the same tile unselected as its twin, failing on the former ring.

title: A roll still to prepare carries the panel's warning mark in the navigator
detail: Evaluation, UI Iconography: a prepared roll and an unprepared one differed only by a folder glyph, which tells a marked roll from a folder, never its measure. Each listed row now reads with its listing, off the interface thread, whether photos lie in it and none is measured or a slide, the roll card's own rule (roll_card::unprepared); the row then shows the warning mark in the card's ink and says Not prepared yet to assistive tools and in its tooltip. A sidecar the app writes lists its row's folder again, so Prepare Roll or Reset the Roll moves the mark at once. Check: unprepared, a measured roll, a slide's and a folder of folders as twins, failing without the relisting.

title: The favourites' view is a funnel key lit while on, and an empty list speaks at its top on the rows' inset
detail: Evaluation, UI Iconography and Spacing: the star marked a favourite folder and also toggled the favourites-only view; the view is now a funnel (filter.svg, drawn in Trinil's stroke) on a flat key lit while on, the star kept for the mark alone. 'No Projects' floated mid-column, laid over the whole column; it, No Favourites and an unreachable base now share RowsEmpty, at the list's top on the rows' text inset with the hint beneath, the projects' saying how one is made. Check: column_edges' empty lists, the grid's centred state as twin, and the key's checked state off then on.

title: A rounded row selected is the tab bar's raised pill
detail: Evaluation, UI Art direction: the gallery, the sidebar and Settings read as bare beside the editor's panel. One discreet touch within the art direction: the selection of the navigator, of Settings' and of the presets' side lists is the raised pill the tab bar slides under its tab (Outward on TabsStyle.pill), so a column's selection and its tab bar speak alike. A tree's list rows keep their flat band, which joins several selected; the tiles stay flat, being the photos, their medals and seals already the metal.

title: The bar's keys that reset or remove stand last and apart, and say their word
detail: UI and UX evaluation (UI Hierarchy, UI Overall, UX Obvious, UI Iconography): the gallery set Reset and Move to Trash right after PREPARE ROLL at the bar's rhythm, as two bare glyphs, Reset's circular arrow reading as rotation and as undo. Both modes now end their centre keys with one plate of their own, Reset and Trash, set apart by ShellStyle.bar-apart (twice Space.l, the bar's own gap when compact), each a word that gives way to its glyph only short of room, red under the hand; the editor gains the Trash its ⌘⌫ already reached. Reset's glyph is an arrow back to its stop, drawn in the Trinil stroke, so circular arrows stay rotation's and the history's; the unused circular one is removed. The report key stays where it is.

title: The photo's menu ends on Reset and the ONI Trash, and prints the menu bar's chords
detail: UI and UX evaluation (UI Hierarchy, UX Expert efficiency): the right-click menu grouped Reset Settings with Copy and Paste Settings and printed no shortcut. Reset Settings now opens a section of its own at the menu's foot, beside Move to ONI Trash, ruled off from every verb that keeps; each line prints the chord the menu bar answers for its gesture, right-aligned as AppKit's menus do (MenuLine.keys), and the menu widens to its widest line, word and chord, rather than elide it. platform::keys writes the Mac's modifiers in AppKit's order (⇧⌘, ⌥⇧⌘), as the native menu bar shows them, in every tooltip too, and gains the delete key. In the gallery ⇧⌘C copies the one photo picked, as the menu's Copy Settings does, rather than a frame open earlier. Unit checks: the menu's order and rules with Reset at the foot, and each printed chord equal to the one app.slint declares for the same act; twin: the menu bar's Reset moved to another chord is caught.
