Window check toolbar::the_keys_that_reset_or_remove_stand_last_and_apart opens the menu by a right click and reads its foot, its chords and its width on two photos against one.

title: Paste to Roll on a plate of its own, counting the frames it rewrites, on ⌥⌘V
detail: UX evaluation (Trust, Expert efficiency): Paste to Roll, which rewrites a whole roll at once, shared Copy and Paste's plate and had no shortcut. It now stands on its own plate; its tooltip and its menu bar title count the photos it reaches (Paste to 24 Photos of the Roll) and give its chord, ⌥⌘V, which the menu bar declares; the toast with its Undo stays.

title: One lamp for every latching key, and Undo names the slider it takes back
detail: UI and UX evaluation (UI Clarity, UI Consistency, UX Trust): the contact-sheet key read Whole Roll in both modes, meaning select all in the gallery and the roll together in the editor, and was the one latching key with no lamp; Undo's tooltip named no edit while Redo's named gestures. The key now says Select All in the gallery and Whole Roll beside a photo, and wears a lamp lit while every photo it picks is picked (Bar.whole, from the same rule its press reads). A step with no label of its own, an edit, is named by the one slider it moved, read on the open frame (Undo Exposure, Redo Exposure); an edit that moved several values keeps the bare word. Unit check menus::an_edit_is_named_by_the_one_slider_it_moved, with twins on two values and none; window check gestures reads Undo Exposure and Redo Exposure.

title: A lamp reads at rest, and a switch is lit as a lamp while on
detail: Evaluation R3: the unlit lamps of Crop, Compare, De-dust and Set window were dark glass in a dark groove, 1.6:1 on the key's face, and read as specks or unread badges at the legend's top right. A lamp is now dark glass in a light rim at rest (over 3:1 on the face, SurfaceStyle.lamp-rim) on the legend's middle line, its glass and rim glowing when lit. A switch differed by its lever's side and a grey I or O: what the knob uncovers now follows the lamps' rule, the slot lit in a lit lamp's phosphor while on (ToggleStyle.lit), a Lamp at rest in the hollow while off; the I and O marks and their three tokens go. The states check measures the lamp at rest against the face and the switch's slot against the lit threshold, each with a twin.

title: The primary keycap is calm, and a keycap out of reach keeps its relief
detail: Evaluation R3: the saturated system-blue EXPORT keycap was the brightest thing beside the photo on every editor screen. The accent key's face is now the accent sunk into the keycap's grey (ButtonStyle.primary), one accent still, calm beside the photo. De-dust's REMOVE, a keycap out of reach, faded whole and read as a flat key beside DETECT: a keycap out of reach now keeps its relief, its legend alone fading and the primary's tint going, while a flat key still fades whole; DETECT and REMOVE stand a gap apart rather than on one flat plate. The states check measures the relief kept, with a cap faded whole as its twin; the bar's width check picks its row by the four keys alone, a disabled cap across the bar now drawn whole.

title: One footer for every sheet: Cancel at the left, the commit keycap alone at the right
detail: Evaluation R3: the sheets' footers followed three patterns, and Cancel butted against NEXT or EXPORT on one plate. SheetFooter lays the flat key that leaves at the left with what the sheet adds beside it, then apart at the right a step back and the commit alone, the accent keycap, flat while it writes nothing (the prepare's Skip, a failure's OK). Prepare the Roll, Export, Save a Preset, the preset editor, Settings, Pair Phone, Report a Bug, the welcome, the RAW notice, the catch-up and the DNG converter all end on it: the preset's Save becomes its keycap, Back stands beside the step's key far from Cancel, and Forget Phones leaves DONE's plate. A question's answers keep their own row. A window check measures Cancel apart from SEND on Report a Bug, a question's flush plate its twin.

title: Escape and Cancel put back what the crop or De-dust changed; DONE and Return keep it
detail: UX evaluation s-9011e109 (Consistency of behaviour, major): Escape in the crop kept the crop as DONE did, where macOS reads Escape as a cancel. A canvas tool entered now keeps its frame's settings as found (`tool_entry`, taken where the route moves); Escape and the header's new flat Cancel write back the tool's own part, the geometry for the crop and the corrections for De-dust, as one undo step, then leave for the last panel. DONE, Return, the tool's bar key and a photo opened elsewhere keep the work, as before. The mode header shows both ways out, Cancel beside the DONE keycap, and the crop's "?" says which key does what. One rule for every mode: Escape still steps out of one thing at a time, Compare before the crop. Checks: window crop_session::escape_or_cancel_puts_back_what_a_tool_changed_and_done_keeps_it (Escape, Cancel, DONE, Return on the crop, Escape and Return on De-dust, Undo taking the cancel back; twins: DONE and Return keep).

title: The crop's pane names its keys by their scope, its reset beside the kept size, and the window says it is the photo's
detail: UX/UI evaluation s-9011e109 (Clarity, Consistency of behaviour, Task fit): the mode titled Crop opened on a block titled Crop again, holding Copy, Paste and Paste to Roll beside the bar's keys of the same names that carry the settings. The duplicate block goes: under the mode's name, untitled, the kept size with the crop's Reset beside it, as a block's sits on its title row, then Copy Crop and Paste Crop and, alone on its row, Paste Crop to Roll, so no two keys of one name do different things in any language's length. The measuring window's keys become Copy Window and Paste Window, and a note under its title says it acts on this photo alone: each frame holds its own window, copied with the crop, never with the roll's settings, so it stays where it is set. The crop's help, demo included, moves to a "?" beside the mode's name. French and Spanish filled in. Checks: panel_bindings (the crop's Reset on the Kept row, the window's keys by their names), sidebars (the crop's plate of two keys spans its block, each word centred in its share; twins kept).

title: One kept size: the crop's readout, its badge, the status bar and the export panel round one crop
detail: UX evaluation s-9011e109 (Trust): the crop read Kept 4031 × 4031 px while the status bar read 4034 × 4031 for the same frame, as the bar scaled the preview render's extent, whose crop covers partly covered pixels, back to full resolution. `Geometry::kept_pixels` rounds the crop on the turned photo once; the crop's readout, its badge, the status bar and the export panel's `cropped_size` all read it, so their figures cannot differ, and no render moves. `oriented_size` reads a quarter turn written backwards as the render does. The editor's full height is still the preview's proportion of the full width, so a file may be a pixel taller than every readout says. Checks: oni-settings the_kept_size_is_whole_pixels_on_the_turned_photo_whichever_way_the_turn_is_written (twin: −1 read as no turn); window crop_session::the_arrows_move_the_crop_and_every_readout_says_one_kept_size (a crop ending past half a pixel, readout and status alike; twin: the render's extent rounds otherwise).

title: The straighten dial prints every figure whole, and the arrows move the crop's frame
detail: UX/UI evaluation s-9011e109 (Typography, Accessibility): the dial faded and narrowed its outer figures with the ring's turn until −6° and 6° were barely legible; the marks keep their shading, the figures shown are printed whole and at full ink. The crop's frame existed only as a drawing for the pointer: beside the crop a bare arrow now moves the frame drawn innermost, the measuring window while it is set, else the crop, a point on the canvas, ten with Shift, its steps that follow each other one undo step as a slider's; beside a pane the arrows still walk the photos. Checks: window crop_session (the window first, then the crop moved by a point and ten, the left arrow back; twin: on Colour the arrow leaves the frame); editor_routes (beside the crop the arrow walks nowhere, B opened from the column ending both modes); dial.

title: The presets deck opens on its tab, the + card one entry inside it
detail: The strip on the canvas's bottom edge was the top of the + card, so a click on Presets opened Save a Preset, and the deck rose only under a hovering pointer. The tab is now the deck's own (PresetTab in the design system): it stays on the canvas's edge, a click opens the deck and a second closes it, the cards rising out of its top edge with the + card first among them; the pointer leaving the deck closes it, and the canvas's edge beside the tab stays the photo's. An empty deck's badge says how to make the first preset. The deck check, the presets check and the presets bench open it on its tab.

title: Copy Settings asks what it carries, with the preset sheet's boxes, and remembers the choice
detail: Copy and Paste to Roll carried the Colour and Details tabs whole; choosing what to carry existed only in a preset. Copy Settings (the bar's Copy, the menu, a photo's menu) now opens the save sheet as Copy Settings: the boxes of the look a paste lays, all ticked at first, no roll box and no balance choice, Return copying. The board's text names the rows when the copy carries fewer than all, and Paste and Paste to Roll give every row left out back to the photo they land on; a whole copy writes the codec's text alone, so a paste of the whole look is unchanged (parity check 78 holds on roll #8). The next copy opens on the last one's boxes (copyCarries), so the colour alone across a roll stays one copy and one paste.

title: Leaving Prepare the Roll asks first while it holds a choice; Cancel stands on a plate of its own
detail: UX evaluation s-9011e109, Trust: Escape or Cancel dropped every step done without asking, and Cancel shared a plate with Back and the step's key. Every way out (Cancel, Escape, GALLERY, a sidebar frame) now goes through take_off_roll: a roll holding a base picked, a frame flagged or a window drawn away from the one its first frame brought asks 'Discard This Roll's Preparation?' with a red Discard, the sheet's Cancel keeping the roll and its steps; a roll holding none leaves at once, keeping nothing as before (#1112). A sidebar frame opens once the roll is left. The DNG conversion's leave stays silent (drop_roll). The footer lays Cancel, or Stop while measuring, on a plate apart from Back and the step's key.

title: Prepare the Roll shows each frame as its scan on every step
detail: UX evaluation s-9011e109, Craft in use: the steps alternated a cyan-veiled preview, the negative complemented without its base, and the base step's raw negative, so the frame changed look at each step. The roll's tiles and card are now its frames framed (flat-field, mask, dust) on screen values, uninverted as the base's scan and the gallery's unprepared roll, so every step shows the one look; `RollPreviews.inverted` and its check are gone. Nothing measured changes: the measure and the base pick read the files themselves.

title: The base pick lands its ring with a click and waits for NEXT; the window clicks as it is taken and set down
detail: UX evaluation s-9011e109, Play: the base pick and the window gave no response under the hand; the pick even left its step at once, so its ring was never seen. A click on bare film now stays on the base step: the ring lands from 1.6 times its size onto the pick on the settle spring (`RollStyle.landing`) with a key's click, the key rises to the NEXT keycap and the loupe shows the pick, so the hand checks it and may pick again before going on. The measuring window clicks as a key goes down when taken up and as one comes up when set down. Both sounds follow Settings' key clicks.

title: Prepare's step bar spaces its steps evenly; an unprepared roll shows one Prepare Roll
detail: UI evaluation s-9011e109, Spacing and Hierarchy: the step bar's equal cells left uneven gaps between the five steps' words; an ordered Tabs now sizes each step to its words and shares the room left equally, so the gaps are even and a check replacing a number still moves nothing. Roll #9 showed two Prepare Roll actions, the bar's keycap and a flat key under the info column's notice; the notice now points to the bar's key in words, and the column's key and its callback are gone.

title: One name for the colour space on the canvas and in the export, said to be shared
detail: UI and UX evaluation (Clarity, Language): the canvas's chip opened a popover titled Working Space while the export called the same choice Space, and neither said they were one. Both now read Colour space; the popover says under its title that the choice is shared by the canvas and the export, the chip's tooltip and the export field's help say the same, in English, French and Spanish. Window check space_chip finds the popover's name and its tabs by role and name, the former name gone; export_panel finds the field's name.

title: The export's empty EXIF fields read as examples, never as values
detail: UI evaluation (Clarity): Artist read 'Your name' and Copyright '© 2026 Your name' in the placeholder's ink, already the quietest the panel keeps for AA, so they passed for typed values, as did ISO's 400 and the Date's date. Every placeholder of the export's fields now opens on 'e.g.', as Camera Body's in the roll's info does: e.g. Leica M6, e.g. Summicron 50 mm, e.g. 400, e.g. 2026-09-05 10:00:00, e.g. Jane Doe, e.g. © 2026 Jane Doe, in English, French and Spanish. Window check export_panel finds the empty Artist field's example, and its twin types a name through the field and finds it gone.

title: A mode's or a sheet's title stands a step over the block titles under it
detail: Crop, De-dust, Settings and every sheet's title read lighter than the semibold block titles beneath them. The title role is now bold at its 17 pt, the block title semibold at 15 pt, the label regular at 13 pt: title, block and label part by type alone. A role's size and weight live in one place, shared by a label and a field typed over it, so a roll's name keeps its weight while renamed.

title: Every key in Title Case, every ellipsis one character, both kept by the catalogue
detail: Set window and Apply window were the flat keys left in sentence case: they read Set Window and Apply Window, as macOS writes a key and as every other key of the app already did. The catalogue check now reads each key's words in the interface and fails on one out of Title Case, and fails on three periods in any text or translation; every ellipsis was already the one character, Inter's own spaced glyph.

title: Tab labels keep equal room and read with a margin over AA
detail: Every tab asked for the whole bar, so a long label took its bare 8 pt minimum while short ones floated: RGB Passes and Custom crowded their edges and the Prepare stepper's gaps ran uneven. A tab is now its label and an equal share of the rest, 12 pt either side where the bar holds it, never under 8 pt. An unselected label rises from 0.55 to 0.62 of the ink, 5.6:1 on its hollow. The Spanish DSLR Scan reads Cámara, which overflowed Prepare's bar.

title: Readouts end their digits at one edge; the status line starts at the card's inset
detail: A readout's unit (EV, %, °, ×, px) now stands in a column of its own, as wide as EV, so the tabular digits of every row end at one edge; Rust names the unit, what follows the last digit. The status line sat 8 pt in while the grid, the title and the presets' deck sit 24 pt, and hugged the window in full canvas: it now starts at the card's content inset in every layout, and the medals end there.

title: Each medal carries its rank sunk in the metal, at an icon's size
detail: Evaluation s-9011e109 (UX Accessibility, UI Iconography): bronze, silver and gold were 12 pt discs on the tiles and in the rating filter, told apart by colour alone. The art direction now allows a figure struck in a medal: each carries its rank, 1, 2 or 3, the key that lays it, sunk in the middle in bold Inter at 0.6 of its side, in the ruled ring's ink over a lip in the foil's light a rule below, so it reads as struck in the metal rather than printed on it. That ink is now opaque, for both ring and figure, so a figure holds 3:1 on bronze. Every medal, on a tile, in the filter and in the status bar, is one size, an icon's 16 pt: MedalStyle.key and the unused TileStyle.medal go. Window check states::every_state_reads_apart_from_its_neighbour reads the three medals' middles without their colour, their figures at least 6 of 64 pixels apart; twin: two golds read alike.

title: The dyes say where they come from: the editor names the film stock or flags another family, the roll card reads its frames
detail: UI evaluation (Clarity): on roll #8 the editor's Dye Separation showed Kodak while the gallery's card said Dyes: Fuji. The render uses each frame's separationFamily (Kodak C-41 on all 25 sidecars of the test copy); the card printed the family its stock, Fujifilm Fujicolor, names, from a marker written before the stock wrote its dyes (#831), so it claimed what no frame held. Render untouched; whether roll #8 should run on Fuji's dyes is the owner's call. Now the card reads the dyes its frames unmix off their sidecars, in the read that already finds the roll's measure, the open photo by its settings in memory and read again when they move: Dyes: Fuji, or Dyes: Kodak; the stock names Fuji. Under the Dyes tabs a note says From the film stock, <stock>, Not the film stock's: <stock> names <family>, or No film stock names these dyes. The block rests on the stock's family: its reset key shows only off it and lands back on it, the mode's own when no stock names one. Checks: store the_dye_separation_reset_lands_on_the_stocks_dyes_and_clears_the_dose_and_the_hand, roll_tab the_dyes_say_whether_they_are_the_film_stocks, roll_card the_card_reads_the_dyes_the_frames_unmix_in_the_tabs_order and the_card_names_the_frames_dyes_and_the_stocks_when_they_differ, each with its twin; window roll_card (Kodak picked under Superia flagged in the block and on the card, the reset back on Fuji) and roll_tab (the tabs follow a pick, an undo and a reset). English, French and Spanish.

title: The filmstrip numbers each frame on its roll, and the status bar says its place
detail: Evaluation, UX Robustness: the editor's filmstrip named frames by file alone, so on a long roll a frame's number was lost. The tree's walk lends each photo its rank among its folder's own photos, the number the contact sheet prints; a thumbnail's caption and a name row show it before the name in the tertiary ink. The status bar's line reads the open frame's name, then Frame 7 of 24, then its size. The archive finds a folder's roll in one place for the tree, the contact sheet and the line.

title: The status bar says Settings saved once the sidecar holds what the frame shows
detail: Evaluation, UX Trust: nothing showed that an edit was kept. The editor's status line ends with Settings saved while the open frame's sidecar holds its settings, written since or read as it opened; an edit hides it until its write lands 400 ms after the hand rests, and a read-only frame never shows it. No timer: the words follow the store's own state, set after each change and each deferred write.

title: Frontier Look names the table in use; its way back to the measured table is the section's Reset
detail: UI evaluation (Hierarchy): Settings > Frontier Look set its way back, a Measured key that looked disabled while the measured table was in use, in one row with Export… and Use a File…, and named the table in use in a note that read as a description. A Table in use row now reads Measured or the file's name, and the way back is the title row's Reset every block shares, shown while a file is in use, apart from the keys that keep one; the note says Reset returns to the measured table. One property, the file's name or empty, replaces the look's sentence and its flag. Window check frontier_look reaches the section and the Reset by the pointer, reads the file then Measured as the table in use; twin: the Reset is not on Export…'s row.

title: Crop mode's help opens under its header, in the panel's flow
detail: The block help card moved into each block's flow while the Crop mode's header still placed its card by column: the header's mark now names its subject, and its card opens under the header, pushing the pane down as a block's does.

title: Plates belong to keycaps alone; every flat key shows its own edge at rest and groups by spacing
detail: Owner's call: a plate only ever meant keycaps sharing one socket, yet flat keys stood flush on shared plates across the app, told apart only under the hand. A flat key now draws its face inside its own edge, the dividers' white at 10 % (ButtonStyle.edge), so it shows its extent at rest; ButtonGroup's plate is a socket of keycaps alone (the colour panel's AUTO WHITE BALANCE and AUTO PAPER CORRECTION), and every other group stands a group's gap apart (ButtonStyle.group-gap, Space.s): the bar's history, families, rating filter and removing keys, the crop, roll and export rows, the navigator's and the canvas header's keys, the questions, notices, banners and job cards. Unrelated or opposite keys stand twice that apart (ButtonStyle.apart): the canvas's Panel key after the zoom keys, a question's destructive answer, the presets editor's Delete; the bar's families keep its own gap at every width (ShellStyle.compact-gap removed). ButtonSize.plate, a regular key under another name, and the mini plate are removed. Window checks: button_group reads a plate's keycaps flush and a group's flat keys 8 pt apart with a lighter edge at rest (twin: a face read twice shows no edge); sheet_layout reads a question's Cancel a group's gap from its key and a destructive one twice that; toolbar, prepare and sidebars read the groups' gaps where they read plates.

title: The picture's histogram is counted and traced for the plots on screen alone
detail: On the Scanner face the scanner's screen stands where the output histogram is, and under Details the loupe does, yet every render still rendered the whole picture for its count, counted it on the GPU and traced the readout. Each render job now says whether a plot over the picture's histogram shows (the readout where neither the Scanner's screen nor the loupe stands, the saturation curve open on the Colour tab), the worker counts only then, and each plot is traced only while it shows. A plot shown again is traced at once from the kept count, and when none showed meanwhile the picture is asked anew, so Pro's face back traces its readout from its first render's count. The kept count moved into the frame's requests, so another frame's never stands under a new one. Checks: the worker counts nothing for a job with no plot on screen, twin the same picture counted once one shows; window picture_plots: no output trace while the Scanner face shows, the saturation curve opened is counted alone, Pro back traces a fresh readout, twin the same wait on Pro sees each render traced.

title: On the Scanner face the Curves editor's histogram reads what enters its curves
detail: Every reading took the frame through Pro's print, so on the Scanner face the Curves editor's histogram showed Pro's picture with no look, not what enters the curves being edited. `truncated` now keeps the frame's face past the print and lays the Scanner's own finishing at rest as Pro's, its contrast kept; in front of the print a reading still takes Pro's windows. Auto White Balance's pixels read Pro's render by their own door, the print its filters are written in, so the balance and the roll's measures read as before and no render moves. Checks: the Scanner curves' input differs from Pro's on a frame the look moves, a keypad step moves it and the face's own curve does not, twin the levels' input is the same on both faces; both renders identical after the readings, twin a curve moves one; the press finds the same filters and levels on both faces, twin the Scanner face's own picture parts from Pro's.

title: The checks follow the merged fifth wave; the dialog answer is emptied, never removed
detail: Eight checks still read the app as one corrector left it: the Pro face now lays Lighting first, so a slider check opens taller and the help card's twin reads the light above the colour; a block's Reset stays in place dimmed; Copy Settings ends on its ellipsis; Prepare's footer sets Back beside the step's key with Cancel apart; the dye block's reset index follows the panel; the medal probes sit on the tiles' ground. The dialog seam empties its answer file rather than removing it, as no crate removes a file.

title: The Scanner face's − and + step keys come back, as keycaps beside each rail
detail: Owner's call: the step keys are what makes the Scanner experience, so they stay, and as keycaps. Each of the Scanner face's stepped sliders sets a − and a + keycap at its rail's ends, as tall as the knob (SliderStyle.step-key, its sign at SliderStyle.step-legend), each in the colour of the rail's end beside it: a press is one step, three with ⇧. The keys' tooltips name the slider and the way, and assistive tools read them as the keys' names; the name's tooltip tells ⇧ makes three. What #1316 gave both faces stays: the tick and the detent at rest, the double click on the name, the arrows and the typed value; Pro's sliders keep no keys. The 2.5D lab tunes the keys again. Window check scanner: a press on D's − steps once, ⇧ on + three times (twin: deaf to ⇧ it would stand at zero), the press draws the cap sinking (twin: the block's flat Reset draws none).

title: Every input of frames together takes the store's one path: a reset lands as each frame's own rest
detail: Adversarial review of the writes while several frames are edited together. A block's reset, an editor's reset (curves, levels, colour mixer, saturation) and a Scanner group's reset were values written from the open frame, so another frame reset only what the open one had moved, and with frames together a block's reset left through a gesture that never reached the roll. They are now one command, Command::Each, an edit read off each frame's own settings, applied through EditorStore::apply like a slider, laid on the open frame and on each frame together; the single-frame write and the together gesture are gone. An action the open frame stands still for (a double click at its rest, Reset C at 0, a key at its click limit, a reset on curves already at rest) still lands on the frames together: apply takes the command whenever frames are together, and only what changed is written. Checks: store one_path an action the open frame stands still for (twin: each command left the open frame unchanged), app store a block reset together, editors stored a reset reaching a frame the open one left at rest.

title: What a roll shares reaches every frame of the open frame's roll by the roll's rule, and never another roll
detail: The together patch laid roll fields on frames it judged of the same roll by reference and decode, None counting as a roll: slides took the open slide's Auto levels, a frame of the roll on another decode took no roll step, frames on no roll shared roll settings, a contact sheet took a flat-field, and a reset of a roll block with part of the roll selected split it. The step's roll fields now go through one rule only: the open frame's roll, every frame of it, together or not, through roll_settings::copied with each slide's own measured gains and its own levels and film type, a contact sheet refusing the flat-field; the together patch never lays a field a roll shares, so frames on no roll and frames of another roll keep theirs, as a slider move always left them. A reset of a roll block behaves as a slider move on it; the dyes laid are the open roll's stock's, and a frame of another stock keeps its own. Settle writes the frames together and the roll's frames in one pass, each sidecar once. Checks: store one_path the roll block reset reaching the frame left out (twin: the selection's gesture splits the roll), dyes across rolls (twin: Kodak laid on the Fuji frame), mixed decodes, no roll and the contact sheet, slides together.

title: The phone's steps and drags move each frame together by their distance
detail: The phone panel turned a step and a drag into the open frame's value plus the move, which the frames together took as a value, wiping their own offsets. A step is now Command::Step by its hundredth of the track and a place on the track a step from the open face's value to it, as the desktop slider moves; a reset stays the double click's rest. Check: panel the phone moves each frame together by its distance (twin: the open frame's value laid whole).

title: A levels handle is a knob: a drag moves each slide together from its own window
detail: The Per-Channel Levels editor wrote whole windows, which the frames together took as values, so on a slide roll every slide lost its own Auto levels. A drag and a scroll now send each moved handle as a step of its Knob::Level, held by the window's own order; a double click on a handle sets its rest as a value. Checks: store one_path a levels handle moves each slide from its own window (twin: the window written as a value), editors stored a handle's drag through the editor (twin, run: the former write path fails it).

title: A move together lands on the face it was made on
detail: A knob's move was measured on the face of its moment but laid with the face read when the step was recorded, so a face switched mid-step laid Pro's move on the Scanner's finishing. Each move and value set now carries its face. Check: store one_path a move lands on the face it was made on (twin: both moves on the release's face).

title: A patched curve point stays between the frame's own neighbours
detail: A curve or saturation point moved on the open frame was patched index by index on another frame's curve, where it could cross a neighbour, and the render reads points in x order. A patched point is now laid through the curve's own move, Curve::move_point and SaturationCurve::move_point, held between that frame's neighbours. Check: fields ordered a patched point stays between the frame's own neighbours (twin: the leaves alone cross).

title: A reset key shows while a frame shown beside the open one stands off its rest
detail: Hard rule 1: every reset key read the open frame alone, so with the open frame at rest a frame beside it could not be reset. A block's, an editor's and a Scanner group's key now also show while a frame together that the reset reaches stands off rest by the open frame's own rule (EditorStore::together_where), read again only when what those frames hold, or the open frame's roll, stock or face, changes; the keys are published as a group opens and closes. Check: window together_moves the Colour key live for the frames beside the open one at rest, dimmed once every frame is reset (twin).

title: A selection changed under the hand keeps the drag held; a measure's writes refresh the frames shown together
detail: Changing the frames together recorded the step under way by releasing the hand, after which the drag recorded and wrote every sidecar at each notch; it now records the step and keeps the hold. A measure's sidecars, written directly, refresh the frames shown together, and a frame together that moves bumps the store's revision so the sheet draws it. Check: store one_path a selection changed under the hand writes nothing per notch (twin: the joined frame takes its notch at release).

title: The medals are numbered as a podium: gold 1, silver 2, bronze 3
detail: Owner: the figures were inverted, bronze 1 and gold 3. The number the interface passes for a medal is now its podium place, which is also the figure struck in it and the key that lays it: gold 1, silver 2, bronze 3, none 0 (library::medal_index and medal_of, MedalStyle's ramps in that order). The Labels menu reads None 0, Gold 1, Silver 2, Bronze 3; the status bar's picker and the rating filter list gold, silver, bronze; the picker's tips say Gold (1) and Bronze (3), French and Spanish filled in. A menu line lays its Medal directly, and the unused Medal::shortcut, which named the old keys, goes. What a sidecar stores does not change. Checks: window states reads the gold face striking a 1, against a 1 alone on a flat disc (twin: silver and bronze are no gold, bronze's 3 reads apart from a 1); window archive the key 1 lays gold (twin: the key 3 lays bronze); the picker, filter and headless key checks follow the places.

title: Both faces lay the colour first: Colour, then Lighting with its Contrast; C, M, Y and TEMP, then D
detail: Owner's call: the Colour tab opens on the colour, against the light-first order #1318 set. On the Pro face Colour leads, then Lighting with Contrast, Paper Correction and Effects as before; on the Scanner face the colour keys and TEMP's look stand before the density key, the keypad's news at its new head. Without the colour block, on black and white, the light leads with no rule above it. Only the panel and the phone remote's mirror move: the reset groups, the pipeline and every render stay. Checks: fields both_faces_lay_the_colour_first_contrast_with_the_light (twin: the light-first and density-first orders fail), phone_link each_face_lists_the_sliders_its_tabs_show, window help_card and panel_frame read the colour first.

title: Balance strength waits behind the balance key's settings, as the flat-field's settings do
detail: Owner's call, after live feedback from beginners: an advanced dose right under AUTO WHITE BALANCE raised questions and blocked them. The key's row now carries a settings key at its far right, the flat-field's own mechanism made one SettingsRow both blocks share; closed by default, one click shows Balance strength and its roll note, its value and reset unchanged. Checks: fields balance_strength_stands_behind_its_keys_settings_alone_in_the_panel (twin: the dose at the surface fails), window rolls the dose hidden until its key opens it (twin: open, it shows).

title: A project holds each photo by its full path: two rolls' copies of one file are two photos
detail: Evaluation: Add to Project silently added none of Roll #8 because Roll #10 held byte copies under the same names; members were keyed by print, so a copy counted as already there. A project's members are now the photos' paths, which every project gesture compares (new, add, remove, leave, reorder, exclusivity, merge), and the file writes no print map. A file written before reads each print at the path it recorded; a Swift file's prints are found by project_standing at the first row carrying them that no member holds, and written as that path. A move made in ONI or Locate carries the members; a path gone stands at its place as missing, never guessed onto a copy. In the Projects tree a file name another photo of the project bears shows its folder beside it (A.tif · Roll 10). Checks: project tests two_copies_of_one_file_are_two_members_each_found_at_its_path (twin: print-keyed, one joins), a_former_file_reads_each_member_at_its_recorded_path, project_standing a_swift_print_is_found_at_a_row_no_member_holds (twin: Kept's own row would be taken), roll8 the Swift prints found on the reference roll, window projects_tab two_rolls_copies_join_one_project_said_with_undo.

title: Add to Project says what it added and what was already there, with Undo
detail: Evaluation: the bulk action said nothing. Every gesture on a project's members is now one step of the session's history (history::Members, each changed project's list before and after, carried by a rename), which the store hands back to the host on undo or redo as it hands a roll marker. Add to Project says '24 photos added to “X”.' with Undo, and how many were already in it; when none joins it says they are all there, with nothing to undo. Remove from Project says what left, with Undo; a drop onto a project in the tree is the same step. Checks: history a_members_step_keeps_the_projects_it_changed_and_follows_a_rename (twin: an idle gesture opens no step), project rosters lay every project back, window projects_tab the notice, its Undo, the bar's Undo and Redo (twin: Redo lays the add again).

title: The rating filter acts in Projects as in the Archive; the empty Projects tab makes a project
detail: Evaluation: Gold lit in Projects while every photo stayed shown, and the empty tab offered no way to make a project. A project's band keeps the filter's one medal as an archive band does, the tree keeping every member; a filter that leaves nothing says No Gold Photos on any surface but the ONI Trash. The empty Projects grid carries a New Project key: an empty project, ringed, its name open to type, then filled by Add to Project; 'New Project from Selection' cannot stand there, as switching tabs keeps no selection the tab does not show. Check: window projects_tab the_empty_tab_makes_a_project_and_the_filter_acts_in_it (twin: All shows the project whole).

title: A project's stocks come from its members' rolls, a folder's marker first
detail: Evaluation: a project read No film stock set yet while its roll was set to Fujifilm Fujicolor: the stocks were read off the sidecars, and a roll made of a folder keeps its stock in the folder's marker. info::stocks reads each photo's roll as the archive does, its folder's marker else its sidecar's film; the markers beyond the opened folder are read once each off the interface thread, a folder the survey covers taking the survey's. Checks: info a_photos_stock_is_its_folders_marker_first (twin: off the sidecars alone, nothing is counted), window projects_tab Kodak Gold counted twice, Roll 8 opened or beyond.

title: The face turned is a view: one undo history spans both faces
detail: UX evaluation s-c82a3414 (Trust, major): after Pro's Contrast and a turn to the Scanner face and back, the Contrast seemed lost to undo. Each turn was an undo step, and its undo laid the frame's face back in the settings without turning the store's face, so the first undos changed nothing the panel showed. The face is now a view, never a step (EditorStore::turn): the step under way is recorded on its own face, then the open frame and the frames together take the new face, written as an opening writes it. An undo or a redo turns the view to the face its step was taken on, the frames together with it, so what it lays back shows; the app keeps that face for the next launch as the bar's and the phone's turns do (Ctl::faced, shared by the three). The face-alone rule of #1063 goes with the step it served. Checks: store scanner the_face_is_no_step_and_an_undo_turns_to_the_face_of_its_step (twin: turns as steps leave more to undo), store together the_face_turned_reaches_every_frame_together_and_is_no_step (twin: nothing left to undo), window face_turn (the undo still names Contrast after two turns, and a Scanner key's undo shows on the Scanner face; run on the former store, it fails).

title: Prepare the Roll ends on one frame alone; the whole roll together is its key's
detail: UX evaluation s-c82a3414 (Obvious without a tutorial, major): the measure landed on the whole roll together (#1037), so a newcomer's first Auto White Balance and edits silently reached 14 frames. land_measure now opens the open frame when it was measured, else the roll's first, alone; the bar's Whole Roll key lays the roll together on demand, the status bar then saying how many frames and the panel 'Acts on N photos'. The 1.5 welcome sheet's point now names that key, in French and Spanish too. Reverses #1037. Checks: window prepare (the first frame alone once measured; twin: no 'frames together' status), window slides (one frame picked).

title: Frames together leave a frame the grid stops showing: the whole roll ends when another roll opens
detail: UX evaluation s-c82a3414 (Trust, minor): with Roll #10 together in the editor, opening Roll #8 kept Roll #10's 24 frames together under an unlit Whole Roll key, so a step would reach a roll no longer shown. lay_grid kept the selection to the bands shown but not the group, which beside a photo is that selection; a group holding a frame the selection lost now follows it (follow_selection), so another roll opened, a medal filter or the projects leave the open frame alone, or the frames still shown together. Checks: window whole_roll the_whole_roll_together_ends_when_another_roll_opens (twin: together, the step reaches B; without the rule the check waits in vain for the open frame alone).

title: A press on a photo gives the photos the keyboard by itself, as a press on the open photo does
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414 (UX Expert efficiency, Consistency and Accessibility, major, two rounds): once a photo was clicked the arrows and Return did nothing in the gallery. Cause: only the window's pointer hook took the keyboard back from a folder's row or a control, so a press Slint alone sees, as the evaluation's tool sends, left the rows holding it, their arrows walking the folders and Return renaming one. The grid's own left press now gives the photos the keyboard (`Grid.refocused`, the canvas's `refocused` way), whatever the hook does: the arrows move the pick, ⇧ and an arrow extend it, Return or Space opens the photo the keys reached, nothing ringed by the click. Space keeps opening, the gallery's and the editor's round trip key (#1246), as the arrows already pick. Check: window gallery_keys, a click on a photo that skips the hook hands ⇧→, → and Return to the photos (twin: a press beside the photos that skips it leaves the rows the arrows; run: the grid without its own press fails with the rows holding the keyboard).

title: A slider worked by hand leaves the keyboard to the photos; Tab alone gives it the keys, ringed
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414 (UX Expert efficiency, minor): after a slider was pressed, the arrows nudged it instead of walking the frames, with no ring to say so (#1159, #1237). A press, a drag or a typed value no longer gives the slider the keyboard: the `pressed` mark and its unringed hold are gone, so the arrows walk the frames and the digits rate them after any work by hand, as AppKit's sliders do without full keyboard access; Return or Escape on a typed value hands the keyboard back to the photos (`Outside.released`), even a key that skips the window's hook. Tab still reaches every slider, Tab from the photo the panel first (#1159), and a slider holding the keyboard is always ringed. Checks: window keyboard a_slider_worked_by_hand_leaves_the_arrows_to_the_photos (twin: Tab gives it the keyboard, ringed, its arrows step it) and a_number_typed_over_a_slider_readout_steps_it_there (Return hands the arrow to the photos; twin: Tab steps on from the number typed), escape (one Escape leaves the crop after a pressed slider), scanner (the photos keep the keyboard after D's slide); run: the former slider fails both keyboard checks.

title: A sheet's default key holds the keyboard, named, so Return presses it and an assistive tool lands on it
detail: Evaluation: Copy Settings' COPY and the notices' OK reached the evaluator with no name. Measured in Slint's tree: every key of a sheet and a notice carries its name (COPY reads Copy, OK reads OK), but a sheet stands last in a tree of some 23,500 elements, past the 1,000 the evaluation tool's element tree returns, and the keyboard, which AccessKit reports as the focus, stayed on the window's unnamed key monitor behind the sheet. The design system's Button gains `default`: a sheet footer's commit, a question's confirming answer and a bar sheet's exit take the keyboard once a sheet covers the window, whether the sheet is built before or after the window moves its keyboard, a field the sheet opens on keeping it; Return (Slint's own key) presses it, Escape reaches the sheet from any key. A question whose key removes keeps no default, so Return takes nothing there; a passing notice takes no keyboard; the prepare and export panels' footers and the welcome's, which Slint would scroll to its key, away from its top, keep no default commit (`default-commit: false`), their keyboard as it was. A key's press through an assistive tool now honours its reach. Checks: window sheet_keys (twin: with no sheet, and once it closes, the photos hold the keyboard; a removing question leaves it to them). Window checks that pressed "\r", a code the window never delivers, now press Slint's Return.

title: Behind a sheet the window's bar reads out of reach, to the eye and to assistive tools
detail: The bar's keys followed two rules: Undo, Redo, Paste, Reset and the mode key read the menus' state, which a sheet blanks, while Crop, Compare, Copy, De-dust, Trash, the report and settings keys, EXPORT or ADD FOLDER… and the gallery's medals read the photo alone, so they stayed lit behind the scrim and an assistive tool could press them through it. The bar's own key types, the rating filter and the face and step tabs now say they belong to the bar (`in-bar`), out of reach while `Keyboard.covered`, faded as any key out of reach, the scrim unchanged. Checks: window sheet_keys (twin: the sheet closed, the bar is live again, and Settings pressed by an assistive tool opens only then; a passing notice leaves the bar live).

title: Both bars read by groups: one gap within a group, a bar's gap between; Reset names its photos, Trash stands last with its can
detail: UI evaluation (Hierarchy major, Trust, Spacing): Reset and Trash stood as twin keys in one group, 48 pt past the rest, and De-dust floated alone, so the bar's gaps varied and a reset read as a deletion. The bar now has two gaps alone, ButtonStyle.group-gap inside a group and ShellStyle.bar-gap between groups (ShellStyle.bar-apart and the Removing group go): De-dust joins Crop, Compare and Whole Roll as one family of latches; Reset and Trash are a group each, last of the centre in both modes; Reset says its scope in its word, Reset Photo or Reset {n} Photos (the plural the roll's reset already speaks), its key as wide as a roll's count so the bar holds still as the selection changes; Trash shows its can before its word at rest, red still under the hand alone; the app's glyphs (feedback, phone, settings) are one group, and the bar's full width reads that group whole. Nothing a key does changes. Checks: window toolbar the_bar_reads_by_groups_reset_names_its_scope_and_trash_stands_last (a group's gap within, a bar's between, Trash's word after its can against Select All's and Copy's at their padding, Reset Photo then Reset 2 Photos in the same room; twin: Reset and Trash are no one group, the one photo's Reset gone), the bar's widths and modes checks unchanged.

title: The preset editor's Delete stands alone at the footer's left end, the keys that keep beside DONE
detail: UI evaluation (Hierarchy major): Delete sat in the row and style of Duplicate, Share… and Copy Preset Code, 16 pt past them. SheetFooter gains a remove slot: a key that removes stands alone at the left end, and what the sheet adds then stands beside the commit; the preset editor's Delete takes it, so Duplicate, Share… and Copy Preset Code are one group a pair of gaps from DONE. Sheets without it lay out as before. Checks: window sheet_layout a_footer_sets_cancel_apart_from_the_commit reads the three keepers a group's gap apart, beside DONE, and Delete over four gaps from them (twin: Delete further from them than they stand from DONE; the old footer fails).

title: The photo's menu sets Move to ONI Trash last and alone, below Reset Settings
detail: UI evaluation (Hierarchy minor): Reset Settings and Move to ONI Trash shared the foot's section. A rule now stands above the ONI Trash too, so it is last and alone, Reset in a section of its own after every verb that keeps; chords and scopes unchanged. Checks: cells the_cell_menu_acts_on_the_selection_it_points_into_and_counts_each_verbs_own_scope reads the rules at 1, 3, 7, 9 and 10; window toolbar reads Show in Finder unruled, then Reset Settings and Move to ONI Trash each ruled.

title: Every DONE is the accent keycap: the crop's and De-dust's as a sheet's, EXPORT laying its accent down while a tool is open
detail: UI evaluation (Consistency minor): DONE was a dark keycap in Crop and De-dust and in the stock board's bar, a blue one in Settings and the sheets. The tools' DONE (ModeHeader) and a sheet bar's exit key now wear the accent as every SheetFooter commit does; while the crop or De-dust stands open its DONE is the view's one primary, so the bar's EXPORT (or update) slot shows plain until the tool is left. Checks: window toolbar_accent the_accent_lands_on_each_screens_own_commit (the accent checks moved out of toolbar.rs) reads, in the crop and in De-dust, DONE in the accent and EXPORT without it (twin: the tool left, EXPORT takes it back and no DONE shows; the old panel fails).

title: The preset sheets fit what they carry, under one heading order
detail: Evaluation r4: the Save a Preset sheet cut a row mid-line at a fixed 540 pt and the editor's settings scrolled under its footer at 420 pt, while the window had room; a small grey Carries sat over larger bold block titles. Both sheets now take their content's height, which the window's room caps, the form scrolling over a footer that stays once it runs short. The blocks stand in two columns (Colour alone in the first), the white balance, a choice and no box, over them at the sheet's width so its menu reads whole, and the name beside the colour; the save sheet fits a 1280 x 800 window and the editor the evaluation's 1728 x 1017. Carries is the section heading with its note, the block titles a step under it as the form's other labels. Only the sheets move: what a preset or a copy carries, and every render, stay. Checks: app presets each_column_opens_on_a_title_that_leads_it_alone (twin: a second lead in a column fails), window presets fits (the last box above the footer, a footer's step from it; twin: a card taller than its content fails), the editor's footer held in an 800 pt window (twin: its form's foot scrolled out of sight), no balance choice on the copy sheet (twin: the save sheet shows it).

title: A preset card is its colour and its name on one line; the deck's tab a 24 pt target
detail: Evaluation r4: the card broke its name over two lines under a large PRE monogram that read as a placeholder, and the Presets tab was 72 x 16 pt. The card is now the preset's tint at the 35 mm frame's 3:2 (96 x 64), its name on one line at its foot, elided past its width; the editor's list keeps the monogram in its badge. The tab is 96 x 24 and the cards' band is laid on it rather than centred in the deck, so a card's foot stays clear of the tab. Checks: window preset_deck the tab is 24 pt and its foot opens the deck (twin: a click just above it opens nothing), the card and the "+" card answer at their new size; lab the_lab_and_its_pages_compile.

title: Copy Settings can stop asking until the app quits
detail: Owner's decision after evaluation r4: Copy kept its sheet and gained Don't ask again this session; ticked and committed, Copy, the bar's, the menu's and a cell's alike, takes the last chosen boxes at once until the app quits, without opening the sheet. Escape or Cancel drops the choice. The choice lives in the session, never in preferences. Checks: window presets clicks the toggle through the pointer, Escape keeps the sheet asking (twin), then Return; the next Copy opens nothing and the paste lays the vignette moved since and leaves Lighting, the box left out.

title: De-dust's reading dims what it leaves out and rings the dust in white on a dark halo
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414 (UI, Color and contrast, major; Overall): Detect laid amber at 43 % over every pixel past the window and the specks at full amber, on a black veil at 65 % over the whole picture, and drew its rings in the same amber: on a light frame at a high sensitivity the photo drowned and the rings vanished. The veil now dims only what the reading leaves out, with the crop's own scrim (DustStyle.veil is Colour.scrim), and the pixels past the window show as they are, the specks' own pixels no longer painted over; the kernel writes that one colour (display/dust.wgsl, dust_mask its CPU reference) and the reading's map loses its dust channel (R8Uint, half the memory), which the display alone read. Found rings are the brush's white on a dark halo (Ring, guide tone), seen on any photo; a correction laid keeps its numbered orange ring, the one colour on the canvas. No found ring can be selected, so none is marked as such. Nothing rendered or written changes. Checks: oni-measure a_speck_ringed_stands_clear_of_the_veil_on_the_map (twin: the ground beside it stays veiled) and the map tests on one channel; display::dust the kernel against its reference (twin: another notch) and a texel's veil (twin: before its notch); window auto_dust, the speck's white ring left of the panel and the picture darker under the veil, back once the reading goes.

title: DETECT only reads: its reading and its count stay until REMOVE, a stroke or another photo
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414 (UX, Expert efficiency): after a first Detect the evaluator raised Sensitivity and pressed DETECT again, which hid the reading and its count, the key doubling as Hide since #1232; the count then said nothing. DETECT now only reads, and is out of reach while its reading shows, since that reading answers every sensitivity and the slider recounts it live; the reading and its note stay until REMOVE, a stroke, a crop or another photo. The bench's hiding press goes. The rest stays at 0 %, as measured in #1076: 0 and 25 % ring nothing on the clean roll #8 and keep the one real speck of P1073201, 50 % rings up to 3 shapes of image and 100 % up to 82, so a default that finds something on a clean roll invites REMOVE to patch the picture; no dusty frame yet shows a speck a higher rest would find. Checks: window auto_dust, DETECT taking a press with nothing shown (twin) and out of reach while its reading shows, a click on it leaving the reading and '1 speck of dust ringed', the reading over the patch saying 'No dust at this sensitivity', and Undo past the patch taking that reading away.

title: Prepare the Roll keeps one footer: NEXT in its place on every step, Skip a key apart, the base's pick shown with its colour
detail: Evaluation: on the base step Skip turned into NEXT in the same place, so the pick could be passed unknowingly, and the footer changed height between steps (a 40 pt keycap on the film step, flat 32 pt keys after). The step's key is now the NEXT keycap on every step, PREPARE ROLL on the last, lit once the step holds its value; while the flat-field or the base is empty a flat Skip stands at the left beside Cancel, far from the keycap, and goes once a value is picked. The footer is therefore the same on every step, its keys on one line. On the scan, the pick is drawn as the disc it read filled with the colour it sampled (the scan's mean inside the disc), never under 16 points wide so a 2-pixel disc still shows; the loupe keeps the true size. The flags' sheet copy that prepare.slint never used goes. Nothing in the measure or the conversion moves. Checks: oni-app prepare::card a_pick_reads_the_mean_of_its_own_disc_alone (twin: the picture's side and a disc across both read otherwise); model's keycap names (twin: no step turns its keycap into Skip); window prepare the base step's footer laid as the film step's, Skip beside Cancel and apart from the keycap, a click at the keycap's place passing no empty base, the pick's colour within the scan's in its disc (twin: not the far corner's); slides and the prepare bench follow Skip's own key.

title: The step bar's done check takes the number's ink: 3:1 on its dimmed disc
detail: Evaluation: a finished step's check was the accent's blue on the charcoal disc, under 2:1 once the idle tab dims it. The check now takes the ink the step numbers use. Check: window prepare_masks reads the check at 3:1 at least on its disc at 2 pixels a point (twin: the accent at the idle tab's 62 % reads under it, 2.18 measured with the old ink).

title: Prepare the Roll's cautions keep the orange in their triangle, the words in the panel's ink
detail: Evaluation: the flat-field step printed a six-line orange paragraph beside the negative. 'Settings differ across the roll' and 'Check the grouping' now share one block: the design system's WarningBand (the triangle in the warning's orange beside the title) and the reason under it as a note in the panel's ink, as the cells the roll marks wear the same triangle. Check: window prepare_masks finds no orange in the words (twin: the triangle before the title is orange; the old orange words fail with 1553 pixels).

title: Frames opened together after a measure wait for their own render instead of their stale thumbnail
detail: Evaluation: after Prepare the Roll the canvas showed the frames as raw orange negatives for about six seconds. The tiles stood in with thumbnails drawn before the measure, which the measure had just queued to be drawn again. The painter now knows the redraw under way as well as those queued (Paint::stale), and a frame whose thumbnail waits to be drawn again gets no stand-in: its tile fills in converted as its own decode lands, beside the opening's progress. Frames whose thumbnails are current stand in as before. Check: oni-app a_thumbnail_waiting_or_being_drawn_again_is_stale_and_no_other (twin: a photo no redraw waits for is current); window together checks unchanged.

title: The export's estimate weighs the file at the size it is written, not the full frame
detail: Evaluation: three Instagram JPEGs that weighed 4 MB read about 56 MB. The weigher extrapolated a 500 px sample over the full frame's pixels, the resize ignored (+833 to +1270 % on roll #8 at Instagram's size), and a JPEG's bytes per pixel climb as a frame shrinks. The sample is now the first photo rendered at the scale the file is written at (on a contact sheet its tile's), never past the reduced decode the editor holds, and weighed over the size the panel shows: on roll #8 Instagram reads within 0.0 %, full JPEG within 10 %, TIFF ZIP within 0.5 %. The first photo's decode is kept from its preview, so the weigher keeps nothing and never decodes the frame a second time; SAMPLE_SIDE goes. Checks: oni-export roll8 the_estimate_holds_on_roll_8 (twin: the former reading is off by more than 400 %), window export_flow the_estimate_weighs_the_file_the_export_writes, 220,462 bytes for a file of 220,802 (twin: the full frame's pixels read four times the file).

title: An export into a missing folder makes it, as a save does
detail: Evaluation: a folder named but missing failed on the first file after its full render, with OK as the only way out. The write now makes the folder it was given before anything renders; a folder that cannot be made says why over the surface, which stays open so EXPORT asks for another. A folder gone mid-batch still fails in the card. Checks: window export_flow writes three frames into a folder made for them (twin: a folder inside a read-only one cannot be made, the notice says so and no export begins), and a read-only folder still fails in the card past its stay.

title: Export's presets are three flat keys that fill the settings, lit while the settings equal one
detail: Evaluation: the presets' segmented control showed nothing selected, reading as a choice left unset. They were never a choice: each writes every row at once and locks none. They are now three flat keys in a filling group with a help mark saying so; the one the rows equal stays lit, read off the rows as before. Checks: window export_panel clicks Instagram, which writes JPEG and sRGB and alone is lit (twin: a quality step by hand lights none).

title: Under a rating filter, Export opens on the photos it keeps
detail: Evaluation: delivering the gold frames took filter, Select All, right-click, Export. With nothing picked in the gallery, Export now takes every photo a rating filter keeps, the set it was turned on to find; the selection still wins, the open photo in the editor, and the ONI Trash never. The File menu counts the same set, read from one State::export_targets; the export global's own menu title and switch, which no screen read, go. Checks: window export_flow labels two frames gold, filters on gold and opens the surface on them with ⌘E (twin: with every photo shown and none picked, Export stays dark).

title: Film canisters wear black caps and spool again, as the real ones do
detail: Owner's call: #1195 turned every canister's caps and spool to grey metal, so none matched a real canister. They are black lacquer again, as the owner's artworks drew them: the same lit ramp across the barrel in black, the lamp's sheen a mid grey on its side, the rims rolled more softly and the spool's knurls lit ribs. What else served stays: the soft label inks, the barrel's round shade and gleam, the cap's shade on the label and the contact shadow. Check: stocks every_canister_wears_black_caps_and_spool_as_the_real_one (twin: the silver ramp fails).

title: A roll's glyph is a film canister, told from a folder at a glance
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414: a prepared roll and a plain folder differed by a subtle folder-like glyph. The roll glyph is now a 35 mm canister drawn in the Trinil set's stroke, knob, flanged caps and leader with its holes, wherever a roll is drawn as a line glyph: the navigator's and the tree's rows, a stock at a row's size, a project card without pictures and Paste to Roll. Folders keep the folder glyphs; an unprepared roll keeps the warning mark its card shows, in the same ink.

title: Rotate and Mirror draw their moves in the icon family
detail: Evaluation s-c82a3414: the crop tab's keys carried typed arrows unlike the drawn glyphs elsewhere, the two mirrors differing by an arrow alone. Each key keeps its word and draws its move: Rotate a photo under a clockwise arc, Mirror a flip across an upright axis, the second Mirror a flip across a level axis, a glyph of its own drawn in the same stroke. A worded key's help is now its accessible description, so the two Mirror keys stay apart for a screen reader. Checks: window panel_bindings presses each mirror by its help, sidebars keeps the three keys evenly apart.

title: The status bar's medals at 20 pt: the given one struck, the others blank rims
detail: Evaluation: 16 pt coins with tiny figures, the given one and the others alike but for a fade. The picker's medals are a small key's square less a rule round, 20 pt (MedalStyle.picker); the given one stays the struck foil with its shadows, the others are blank: their rim lit on top and their figure alone in their metal, at 1.2 on its ramp (bronze's 3 at 5.6:1 on the panel), brighter under the hand yet never struck, so a click that takes a medal off shows at once under the hand. The podium and its figures as keys stay; tiles and the rating filter keep the 16 pt struck medal. Checks: window states a blank medal's middle is the bar's ground (twin: the given one reads filled), its bronze 3 reads as text (twin: a 3 in bronze's own body falls short).

title: The status bar's medals lead its line, named Rating, by the photo's name
detail: Evaluation: the coins sat unlabelled in the bar's far corner, and nothing said the keys 1 to 3 rate. The picker opens on its name, Rating (Note, Valoración), and leads the status bar's row where the line starts, the photo's name right after the bronze, in the gallery as beside a photo. At the start it never moves under the hand as the line's words change (Settings saved coming and going, a selection's count); each tip still names its key (Gold (1)). The row's far end is the status inset, as its start. Checks: window gallery the group's name starts the line on the grid's column, gold, silver and bronze in one row with the name at most the bar's inset after the bronze (twin: from the group's start the name stands the whole group away), the medals still while the line's words change (twin: the line did change).

title: One word per concept: the crop, the measuring window, the prepared roll, and the All Photos filter
detail: Evaluation r4: one concept carried several names. The crop is the crop everywhere: the undo step reads Paste crop, never framing, and so do the help's release note and the balance question. Window now means the measuring window alone: Per-Channel Levels speaks of each channel's range, De-dust of the roll's ends, and Reset the Roll of the measuring window drawn; the step tab and the block's keys keep the short Window, which names nothing else. The roll that PREPARE ROLL makes is the prepared roll in every word: the Roll tab's block is Prepared Roll, its notes, keys, undo step (Prepare the roll of N photos), Prepare's notes and the scanner's note say prepared, while Measuring the roll stays the run's progress. The gallery's rating filter key is All Photos (Filter: All Photos in the menu), apart from Select All. The Auto White Balance question over several frames, untranslated since its words lived in oni-measure, moves its words to the app and reads in French and Spanish, colour spelt as everywhere and no sidecar named. Checks: fields the_roll_tab_lays_its_blocks_in_the_swift_order (Prepared Roll read as Swift's Measured Roll), rolls balance_words every_wording_carries_the_count (twin: another count), window gestures (Undo Paste crop, Filter: All Photos), prepare (Undo Prepare the roll), help_demo_roll, catalogue.

title: The roll card's dyes say what the film stock calls for, as a photographer would
detail: Evaluation r4: Dyes: Kodak; the stock names Fuji read as a riddle. The roll card now reads Dyes: Kodak; this film stock calls for Fuji, under the stock it names, and the Dye Separation block's note says the same verb: Not the film stock's: Fujifilm Fujicolor calls for Fuji, No film stock calls for these dyes. Only words move. Checks: roll_card the_card_names_the_frames_dyes_and_the_stocks_when_they_differ (twin: matching dyes say no stock), roll_tab the_dyes_say_whether_they_are_the_film_stocks, window roll_card and roll_tab.

title: The ONI Trash titles each band and row by its folder's name, the whole path on hover
detail: Evaluation r4: the ONI Trash titled a photo's band with its path from the home, the account's folders included. The trash's folders are now named as the navigator names a folder (a standard home folder in the reader's words), with the folders above only where two of them share a name, as the favourites do; the folder row's tooltip holds the whole path. The path-from-home heading is removed, its last caller gone. Checks: trash the_trash_lists_its_folders_latest_deletion_first (twin: two folders of one name take their parents), window gallery reads the row's and the band's title, no trail, the path as the row's tooltip.

title: Every helper line takes the note: one size and one leading
detail: Evaluation r4: empty-state and status captions fell to the 11 pt caption with tight leading. Every helper line is now the design system's note, a label's size in the secondary ink with its lines opened: an empty list's hint, Prepare's base, flags and grouping status, the epilepsy warning, the navigator's first-run steps and welcome, an empty grid's detail, the export's subtitle and space note, and the messages of asks, notices, progress cards, a missing original and the DNG conversion. The caption stays for tiles, values and key legends. The design system's README says so. No render moves. Checks: window export_panel (the subtitle, now a note, measures taller than a label's line; the summary keeps the label's), column_edges, sheet_layout, told, sheets.

title: A tooltip goes with the screen or the sheet that replaced or covered its key
detail: Evaluation: a toolbar key's tooltip stayed over the export and over a sheet after the hand left. Measured through the window: the menu's Export under a resting hand removes the bar, and Slint tells a key removed or covered under a resting pointer nothing, so its tooltip stood until the next press. A new screen or a sheet shown or closed now takes the tooltip down where it already gives the keyboard back to the photos (app.slint), as a press does; a pointer leaving a key already hid it. Checks: window tooltip a_tooltip_goes_with_the_screen_or_the_sheet_over_its_key (failed before: the mode key's tooltip stood over the export; twins: back beside the photo and once Settings closed, the key hovered again tells its help).

title: A slider's tooltips stand over its own name, never over the next slider's
detail: Evaluation: a rail's tooltip, hung under the rail, covered the next slider's name (Shadows over White point). The rail's tooltip and a stepped slider's minus and plus keys' now rise over their own slider's name and value (Tips.rise, Tip.above, Button.rises), as the name's falls over its rail; every other tooltip still hangs under its control. Checks: window tooltip a_slider_s_tooltip_covers_no_neighbour, Tint's rail and M's two keys on their own slider and clear of the ones above and below (failed before; twin: the same box under the control lies over the next slider).

title: The frame's handles take a hand 12 points past their slim lines and follow it to the end of a drag
detail: UX evaluation (Micro-interactions): the crop's corner grabs were 22 x 22 pt and its edge grabs 12 pt thick, under the 24 pt a hand needs. Every grab of the frame overlay, the crop's and the measuring window's on the canvas and in Prepare Roll, now reaches DS.control-grab-size (24 pt) across its line: an edge 12 pt each side, a corner its 22 pt bracket inside and 12 pt outside, never deeper into the frame than a corner, so a small frame's middle third stays the body's; the drawn brackets and bars keep their slim lines. Found on the way: the edges' list carried the frame's geometry, so each step of a drag built the edge grabs anew and dropped the hand's hold after the first move (5 of 30 pt followed); the list now says only which edge, its place bound in the element as the corners' always was. Check: window crop_session::the_crops_handles_take_a_hand_past_their_slim_lines, presses 10 pt outside a corner and an edge hold them and follow a six-step drag to 30 pt, the badge gone once let go; twins: 16 pt outside holds nothing, the former overlay fails at the corner's press and, with the geometry back in the edges' list, follows 5 pt of 30.

title: One Escape leaves Compare turned on by its key, a slider dragged before
detail: UX evaluation (Consistency of behaviour): Escape seemed to leave Compare on. Escape already leaves Compare first, by the one route every mode takes (route.rs escape: Compare, then the crop or De-dust put back, then the Lab, then the editor). The evaluator had dragged Shadows, which holds the keyboard without a ring, then pressed Compare's key through a tool whose clicks skip the window's pointer hook: the slider kept its hold, which took that Escape, and the two shots match byte for byte. Through the real event path the press on the key gives the keyboard back to the photos and one Escape leaves Compare. Window check escape::one_escape_leaves_compare_its_key_turned_on_after_a_slider_held_the_keyboard; its twin, a hookless press, needs a second Escape. Left as it stands, the keyboard's rule: a slider pressed by the hand, then Compare from the View menu, which no window press reaches, keeps its unringed hold for the first Escape.

title: The readout's histogram names what it draws: a legend under it, the print curve and its dashed inverse on the Colour tab
detail: UI evaluation s-c82a3414 (Clarity): the Colour tab overlaid the print curves and a dashed reference on the histogram with no legend. The readout's box now holds the plot over one caption row, PlotLegend, each entry a sample of its ink and its name: Histogram (three bars, red, green and blue) on every tab the plot shows, Print curve (the solid guide line) and Its inverse (two dashes) while the Colour tab draws them. The box keeps its height on every tab, so the tab bar never moves; the plot gives the row its height. French and Spanish filled in. Window check picture_plots the_readout_names_its_curves_under_the_histogram: the three names on one row under the plot, above the tab bar; on the Roll tab the histogram alone at the same place, the bar unmoved (twin: a legend at the plot's top stands a plot's height above the bar).

title: Every slider readout ends on one edge, its unit with it
detail: UI evaluation s-c82a3414 (Spacing): percent readouts stopped about 7 pt short of the edge EV, px and × readouts reached, as #1361 set every unit in an 18 pt column after the digits. A readout is now right-aligned whole on the rail's edge, in Inter's tabular figures: the unit column, SliderStyle.unit, Readouts.unit and fields::unit_of go. Window check states readouts_end_at_one_edge: a bare number, a percent and a stop readout end within a pixel (twin: their digits set at one edge, the readouts end a unit apart).

title: The contact sheet's frame numbers take a soft amber
detail: UI evaluation s-c82a3414 (Colour and contrast): the frame numbers under every photo of a sheet were the system's saturated orange. Colour.edge-print, which the canvas's sheet and the exported sheet share, is now #cba372, the edge print's amber at OKLab chroma 0.08 (was 0.17), 9:1 on the sheet's black; De-dust's lit pixels keep the orange. Window check export_sheet reads the written sheet's numbers in that amber (twin: the saturated orange fails the measure).

title: A latching key's lit lamp blooms on its face, so on reads at a glance
detail: UI evaluation s-c82a3414 (Clarity): a latching key told on by its lit face, a selected row's grey the hand's light resembles, and a 6 pt lamp turning from ringed to filled. A lit lamp now spreads its phosphor on the face around it, a radial bloom SurfaceStyle.lamp-glow (6 pt) past the glass at lamp-bloom 0.5 in the middle, kept on the key's face where a glyph's square key holds the lamp 3 pt from its edge; it replaces the drop shadow, which the software renderer never drew. Window check states: the face two points past a lit lamp reads 1.5:1 over the face, a lamp at rest none (twin: a lit disc with no bloom leaves the face bare).

title: A prepared roll opens whole again, as the owner decided (#1037); #1415 withdrawn pending his word
detail: The fourth evaluation asked that Prepare end on one frame alone, so a newcomer's first edit never reaches the whole roll unseen (#1415). That reversed the owner's own call (#1037): a measured roll opens with every frame together on its contact sheet. Back to #1037 until the owner decides; the Whole Roll key and the panel's 'Acts on N photos' say how many frames an edit reaches.

title: Two checks follow the merged sixth wave
detail: Prepare's left-out notice now says 'prepared with another roll'. A pressed slider shows it holds the keyboard, and one Escape leaves Compare whether or not the window's hook saw the press, as the keyboard's rework settled; the check proves both paths.

title: A project's member keeps its path and its print, so another file at its path is never taken for it
detail: Review of #1410 (points 2, 3 and 8): a member held its path alone, so a Locate or a file replaced at that path made another file the member, and a former file's print was dropped at the first save. A member is now {path, print} (project::Member). A row stands for a member at its path while it carries the member's print, or while either print is still being read; a member gone from its path, or whose path holds another file, is looked for by its print in project_standing on a shown row no member stands at, the same file first where the volume ignores case, and only for that read (project::Found), never written. Locate leaves the photos whose place in the folder found holds another file where every record names them (identity moves before the folder's, for the projects, the history, the picks and the open frame), and the open frame is never reopened on a path that did not move. A former member's text is a path when it starts at a root (/, \ or a drive letter), a print otherwise, so a print holding a slash stays a print. Checks: project a_member_shows_only_on_the_file_its_print_names (twin: by path alone the other file shows), project_standing a_member_whose_path_holds_another_file_is_found_by_its_print (twin: path-only takes the other file), window locate::locate_onto_copies_carries_no_member_onto_another_file (twin: carried, B would name Roll 10's B; mutation without the stay list fails).

title: projects.json is read whole in any former format, written in format 2 only when something changed, the former file kept beside it once
detail: Review of #1410 (points 3 and 7): a former file's prints were swapped for their recorded paths as raw text, unchecked, and the conversion was saved at launch with no copy of the file. Reading converts in memory only: an earlier build's prints keep the paths beside them, its paths alone stay paths, a Swift print stays a print, each path spelt as the index spells it (composed on macOS, '/' on Windows), each photo once. Nothing is written by a read: read_standing no longer saves, and merge::save_projects writes only when the merged projects differ from the file's. The file now says version 2 (project::FORMAT) and names each member as its path and its print; before the first write over a version 1 file, it is copied byte for byte to projects-v1.json, once, never replaced. Swift-to-Rust reading holds; Rust-to-Swift writing was dropped by the owner. Checks: project file_tests a_former_file_reads_each_member_with_its_path_and_its_print (twin: a slash taken for a path loses the date-stamped print), only_a_change_writes_and_the_former_file_is_kept_beside_it_once (twin: a format 2 write sets nothing aside), a_former_files_stale_and_respelt_paths_are_found_by_their_prints (twin: by recorded paths alone the other file shows and the moved photo is lost), a_file_round_trips_through_the_disk_saying_its_format, window projects_tab::a_swift_file_is_read_without_a_write_and_kept_at_the_first_change.

title: A Swift print is found on a copy for one read only, so an original back from the ONI Trash shows again
detail: Review of #1410 (point 4): a print with no path was matched once at launch to the first copy shown and that path saved for good; with the original in the ONI Trash a backup became the member. The match is now the read's (project::Found), the member keeping its print alone until a gesture names a photo, so the next read chooses again as Swift did; a trashed member at its own path is hidden, never shown on its copy. Checks: project_standing a_print_whose_original_is_trashed_shows_its_copy_for_this_read_only (twin: the choice written holds the copy for good), a_swift_print_is_found_at_a_row_no_member_holds, a_project_resolves_beyond_the_opened_folder_and_never_shows_its_trashed_member.

title: Every change to a project's members is one step of the Undo key, which turns back only what that step changed
detail: Review of #1411 (point 1): a grid drag and a tree drop before a photo changed and saved the members with no step, and an undo laid each changed project's whole former list, so undoing an earlier Add to Project after a drag took the dragged photo out of every project.
