Every gesture on the members, New Project, Add to and Remove from Project, a drop onto a project, a drop before a photo in the tree and a drag in the Projects grid, goes through Ctl::regroup and records one step; New Project takes its photos out of their projects in that step. An undo or a redo lays what its step changed on the members as they stand (project::regroup, a three-way merge), so a member the step never touched stays; a project the step made is emptied, its name kept. Checks: project an_undo_turns_back_what_its_step_changed_and_nothing_else (twin: the former list laid whole loses the dragged photo), window projects_tab::every_drag_is_one_step_and_the_notice_undoes_its_own (mutation: an unrecorded grid drag fails it).

title: The notice's Undo walks back the very step it announced
detail: Review of #1411 (point 5): the notice named its step by label and photos, and a members step names no photo, so a later tree drop, also 'Add to Project', passed for it. Each step of the history bears a mark no other bears (History::undo_mark); the notice keeps the mark and walks back only while that step is on top. Checks: history each_step_bears_a_mark_no_other_does (twin: by name and photos the two steps are one), window projects_tab::every_drag_is_one_step_and_the_notice_undoes_its_own (mutation: a notice told by name undoes the drop).

title: A move landing a member on another of its project's photos leaves the photo once
detail: Review of #1410 (point 6): photos added from /Volumes/T7 1, then /Volumes/T7 located there, gave a project the same path twice. project::moved, a merge, an add and a drop keep each photo once (project::distinct: one path whose prints agree, or one print with no path), the first in place taking the print the other knew; two prints at one path are two photos and both stay. Check: project a_move_landing_on_a_member_leaves_one_photo (twin: two prints at one path both stay).

title: New Project with nothing picked makes no project
detail: Review of #1412 (point 9): the menu greyed File > New Project with nothing picked, yet its act made an empty project. project::new_from makes none from no photo; the empty Projects tab's key alone makes an empty one (project::new_empty). Checks: project a_new_project_takes_the_picked_photos_in_library_order_and_none_makes_none, window projects_tab::the_empty_tab_makes_a_project_and_the_filter_acts_in_it (the menu dark, its act making none).

title: A click's modifiers from Slint's MCP server are taken as sent
detail: Three evaluations reported that shift- and cmd-clicks never extended a selection. The app checks a click's Command and Shift against the keys the system says are down, so a release another app took never sticks; the MCP server, an evaluation's driver, presses no real key, so its modifiers were dropped. While the server is on (SLINT_MCP_PORT), the check is skipped, as the window checks skip it; the shipped app never runs that server.

title: The gallery's bar exports what is picked
detail: An evaluator with three Gold frames picked found no export in the gallery's bar: only the photo's menu or an unseen cmd-E delivered them. A flat key now stands after PREPARE ROLL, before Reset and Trash: it reads the File menu's own title and rule ('Export 3 Photos…'), so the two cannot disagree, keeps the width of a roll's count so the bar holds still, gives way to a glyph drawn in the Trinil stroke when the bar is narrow, and opens the export sheet on the selection. ADD FOLDER… stays the gallery's keycap, its help no longer pointing at cmd-E.

title: One medal drawing everywhere, in the shade until given
detail: The rating filter and the tiles drew the medals as foil coins, the status bar the ones not given as a rim and a figure, which read as two drawings. A medal not given is now the same coin in the shade, its face at a fifth of a given one's light (lifted under the hand), its rim and its figure lit as a given one's lip: gold's 1 reads at 4.5:1 on its face at least. The states check reads a disc, under half a given one's light, and a lit figure on it.

title: A medal laid lands with a short settle, still under Reduce Motion
detail: Rating, the most repeated gesture, gave no answer: the medal appeared. A medal given on the same holder (the tile's photo where it stands, the status bar's line) lands from 1.3 of its side and settles within 140 ms; one shown because a scroll or a selection brought it stands still. The system's Reduce Motion, read at launch (Motion.reduced), keeps it still. A window check measures the landing after the key 1 and its twins under Reduce Motion and on a selection moved.

title: The tile under the hand shows the podium's keys
detail: Rating lived in the status bar alone; nothing on the tiles said the keys 1 to 3 rate. The tile under the hand shows gold, silver and bronze over its medal's corner, the given one lit, each figure the key that lays it; a click lays that medal on that photo alone, or takes its own off, and selects nothing. The status bar keeps the selection's keys under the canvas and the grid; the ONI Trash and a missing original show none. One component, MedalKeys, lays both.

title: The bar reads by job: Reset and Trash end it as one group past a rule
detail: UI and UX evaluation s-f5b562fe (Trust and Hierarchy major, raised again; Hierarchy and Overall major): Reset Photo and Trash stood a bar's gap apart, as Paste to Roll and PREPARE ROLL did, and the editor's thirteen keys read as one flat row of single-key groups. The centre now groups by job: the canvas's views and tools (Select All, Crop, De-dust, Compare), the faces, then the settings carried from photo to photo (Copy, Paste, Paste to Roll, one group again); past an engraved vertical Divider, Reset Photo and Trash end it as one group, Trash last. The gallery's Select All and rating filter are one group, then PREPARE ROLL, then the same rule and end group. ShellStyle.bar-gap goes from Space.m to Space.l, three times a group's gap, so the groups read at a glance; the bar still has two gaps alone. Nothing a key does changes. Checks: window toolbar the_bar_reads_by_groups_reset_names_its_scope_and_trash_stands_last (a group's gap within each group, a rule and a bar's gap either side before Reset, the rule drawn; twin: the room between two groups with no rule is bare), the widths and modes checks.

title: Select All has one name and one place in both modes
detail: UI and UX evaluation s-f5b562fe (Consistency, minor): the bar's ⌘A key read Select All in the gallery and Whole Roll in the editor, first in one bar and last of the tools in the other. It is one action (Act::SelectAll, the ⌘A key path completing the selection with every photo of the rolls it touches); it now reads Select All in both and opens the centre's first group in both, its help still saying what it does beside a photo (Show the Whole Roll Together). The Whole Roll text leaves the catalogues. Checks: window toolbar (the editor's Select All a group's gap before Crop; no Whole Roll on the bar), window whole_roll presses it by its name.

title: One disabled rule for every key: its plate kept, its legend about 3:1
detail: UI evaluation s-f5b562fe (Color and contrast, Consistency, minor): a flat key out of reach faded whole, face, edge and legend, to 2.07:1 on the bar, while a keycap kept its relief, so two disabled looks stood side by side and Paste or a section's Reset nearly vanished. Every key now keeps its face and edge, or its relief, and fades its legend and glyph alone; State.disabled rises from 0.25 to 0.36 for every control that reads it: a legend 2.8:1 on its face as drawn, 3.2:1 on the bar, a glance's step (1.4:1) under an idle tab's label, which the 3:1 asked for leaves no room to hold at 1.5:1. Checks: window states every_state_reads_apart_from_its_neighbour (a flat key out of reach keeps its edge as an able key's and its legend reaches 2.7:1 on its face; twin: a key faded whole loses its edge and its legend falls under; out of reach reads 1.3:1 apart from an idle label, twin a key faded whole to that label's ink reads alike), the keycap checks unchanged.

title: A move to the ONI Trash says so, its Undo beside
detail: UX evaluation s-f5b562fe (Trust, minor): Trash moved a photo with no notice; only Undo's tooltip and the sidebar's count told. Every move that lands, from the bar's key, ⌘⌫ or the photo's menu, now shows the notice Paste to Roll and Add to Project show: Move to ONI Trash, One photo moved to the ONI Trash or {n} photos moved to the ONI Trash, its UNDO walking that step back while it is the last. A refusal keeps its own notice, with no Undo. French and Spanish filled in. Checks: window told a_refused_trash_in_the_gallery_opens_a_notice (the bar's Trash clicked through the event path is told with Undo, which puts the photo back; twin: a refused trash is told with no key).

title: Export settings saved as named presets beside Instagram, Display and Print
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Expert efficiency): every client delivery set format, space, size and quality again by hand. The presets' plate now lays the built-in keys and the saved ones three to a row at equal thirds; under them, unless a built-in key is lit, one name field: with nothing lit it names the settings and Save as Preset keeps them (a key lit at once), with a saved preset lit it renames it and Remove takes it off, apart from the keys that keep. A saved key writes every setting back in one press and lights while the settings equal it. Kept in the preferences under exportPresets, each preset's settings in their own preference's words, read back tolerantly. Window check export_panel saves, recalls, renames and removes through clicks (twin: Save with no name keeps nothing); unit check reads back what it writes (twin: a nameless item is left out).

title: Instagram writes 1080 on the long side; the summary one fact a row; the shared space said where it changes
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe. Task fit: the Instagram key wrote 2160 x 1440; it now writes the feed's 1080 on the long side in sRGB, a 3:2 frame at 1080 x 720, the framing the preview and its caption show (twin: the narrow edge's ceiling wrote 2160 x 1440). Clarity: the summary paired '8 bits per channel' with the pixel size; it reads Pixels, Bit depth and Estimated size, one row each. Trust: the colour space stays shared by the canvas and the export (owner's decision); the note under it, shown as soon as the space differs from the one edited in, now says the canvas and the previews show the new space, the one the export writes.

title: An export's progress and Stop in the status bar, its end told with Show in Finder
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Hierarchy, Task fit): the progress card covered the image's corner for a whole export and its end offered only OK. The card (JobCard, ExportProgress) is gone: the status bar's busy line counts the frames on its glass with its progress and a Stop key, the status bar's own key; the end is told in the app's one notice, the number written or where it stopped, with Show in Finder selecting the first file written, or the frame that failed. The Finder no longer opens by itself as an export starts. Window check export_flow clicks Stop in the bar (frames large enough that it lands mid-export) and reads the notice and its key.

title: Every readout says the size the file is written at: one rounding, stage 0's
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Trust): the export announced 2161 x 1440 and wrote 2160 x 1440, 6048 x 4031 and wrote 6048 x 4032. Two causes. The negative carried only the full width, so every readout took the full height from the preview's proportion, which the reduction rounds to its own grid (a 2048 side read 4031 for a 4032 frame); the negative now carries the full height, read off the decode before it is reduced. And the readouts rounded the crop while stage 0 cuts it on the full-resolution grid; the frame's quantisation moved from oni-pipeline into Geometry::frame_in, which stage 0 calls unchanged, and kept_pixels is the extent stage 0 keeps from it, so the crop's readout, its badge, the status bar, the export panel and the file share one size and no render moves. The frame in pixels is a part of its own, oni-settings geometry/pixels.rs. Checks: oni-settings the_kept_size_is_whole_pixels_on_the_turned_photo_whichever_way_the_turn_is_written (a crop ending past half a pixel, slivers at both edges, a tilt's bleed, a box of no whole height; twin: the former rounding a pixel off); window crop_session::the_arrows_move_the_crop_and_every_readout_says_one_kept_size (the render's extent now equals the readouts; twin: the rounded crop a pixel more); window export_window on roll #8: the panel's full height is the decode's 4032 and the file is the size announced (twin: the preview's proportion of the width reads 4031).

title: Prepare's frame keys are arrows either side of the frame's name, never Back's and NEXT's words
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Clarity, major): the Base step showed Previous and Next over the scan and Back and NEXT in the footer, two pairs of the same words for two objects. The pager, the Base and Window steps' alike, now lays a square key with a chevron each side of the frame's name, named Previous Frame and Next Frame for the hand that hovers and for assistive tools; the footer keeps the step's Back and NEXT. Icons.chevron-left is chevron-right mirrored. Window check prepare_frames: one key each named Previous Frame and Next Frame, none named Previous or Next, a click on each walks the base frame through the real event path (twin: the step stays, and the footer's Back and NEXT are found under them).

title: The base loupe's disc shows the film it reads: a guide ring's halo is a border, not a shadow
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Obvious): the bare film was hard to hit at 35% and no loupe confirmed the pick. The loupe was there under the pointer, but its ring's drop shadow, which the renderer draws as a filled box, darkened the whole disc it bounded, the very pixels being picked; De-dust's rings and the brush wore the same dark fill. Ring now draws its dark halo as a border either side of its white line, so the disc shows what lies inside it. The pick itself stays the person's. Window check prepare_frames: in the loupe the disc's middle reads as the film beside the ring, the white line and its darker halo drawn (twin: the shadowed ring of before leaves no halo in the check's renderer and fails).

title: The Flat-Field step says what the roll's mixed settings ask of the light panel, never to re-shoot
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Task fit): the step told a newcomer to re-shoot 9 of 14 frames in manual, a detour off the step. The note now says their exposure is evened out to the roll's settings, nothing to do; and when an aperture differs, to shoot the light panel at the aperture most of the roll shares, as a frame at another may keep slightly uneven corners. CaptureExposure::f_number writes the aperture as the label does. Unit check the_rolls_settings_differ_note_counts_the_frames_shot_apart (twins: a frame apart at the roll's aperture asks nothing of the panel; one without EXIF is never apart).

title: The card dissolves each frame in, one dissolve at a time, so a scrub never flashes and its epilepsy warning goes
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Language): an epilepsy warning about scrubbing sat in the Window step's instructions. The card swapped whole frames as fast as the hand asked them. It now holds two layers: a frame asked dissolves in over the one shown in 200 ms, and one asked during a dissolve waits for its end, the latest asked laid (prepare::card::Layers), so the card changes under three flashes a second (WCAG 2.3.1) and nothing moves, which a reduced motion setting asks. Each layer keeps its frame's own box and the window lies over the frame on top. The warning text goes. Unit check a_frame_dissolves_in_only_once_the_last_dissolve_has_ended; window check prepare_frames: a scrub asking a frame every 31 ms dissolves at most once in 200 ms and ends on the frame asked last (twin: the hand asked frames well under 100 ms apart).

title: The canvas takes the keyboard: its arrows place the crop, the measuring window and the base's picker, Return keeps them
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Accessibility, major): the canvas had no accessible name or action, and picking the base or cropping needed a pointer. The canvas's place in Tab's order is one element, `CanvasKeys`, the editor's and Prepare's alike: read as the photo (the status line, the scan's or the frame's name in Prepare), its description and a badge on it saying what its keys do. Holding the keyboard, its arrows place what it draws: the measuring window while it shows, on Colour too, else the crop, ⇧ ten times as far, ⌥ its right and bottom edges (one `framing::arrow`, laid through the drag's own `apply`); in Prepare the base's picker, its loupe with it, Return picking the film under it, and the measuring window. Return and the canvas's accessible default action keep the frame as the photos' Return does. The photos' own keys stay: their arrows walk the photos and Prepare's frames, and beside the crop move its frame, ⌥ resizing it there too, which the crop's help now says. Checks: window canvas_keys::the_canvas_holding_the_keyboard_places_the_window_the_crop_and_their_edges (twins: the photos' arrow moves no window; the bare arrow moves the left edge with it) and canvas_keys::prepares_floor_places_the_base_picker_and_the_window_by_the_keyboard (twins: the photos' arrow moves no picker, and walks the frames); unit framing::an_arrow_moves_the_body_and_with_option_the_right_and_bottom_edges.

title: Tab from the photos walks the bar, the sidebar, the canvas, then the panel
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Accessibility, minor): three Tabs from the photo landed on a section's fold key, the bar and the canvas passed over. Tab from the photo no longer jumps into the panel (`Keyboard.inward` and the tab bar's `take-keyboard` removed, #1159): it walks the window in reading order from its top, the editor as the gallery, the canvas one stop read as the photo between the sidebar and the panel (#1501). Check: window canvas_keys::tab_walks_the_bar_the_sidebar_the_canvas_then_the_panel (twin: ⇧Tab walks the same round backwards); editor_routes no longer expects the jump.

title: Lighting's sliders stay in the tree four frames together; the evaluation's tree stopped at 1000 elements
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Accessibility, minor) found Lighting's sliders missing from the accessibility tree with four frames together until the library hid. Slint's MCP server caps get_element_tree at 1000 elements, the evaluation's driver asks 20000 and never reads `truncated`, and the panel comes last in the walk: the library's rows and tiles pushed it past the cap, hiding them brought it back. In the evaluation's 1728 x 1017 window, four frames together beside the library, the Exposure slider is in the tree, 756 elements on with four tiles; the driver should page with query_element_descendants. Nothing in the app changes. Check: in canvas_keys::tab_walks_the_bar_the_sidebar_the_canvas_then_the_panel (twin: on Details, Colour's sliders leave the tree).

title: A slider's tick, its double click and its block's Reset share one rest
detail: A freshly prepared negative read Exposure +1.50 EV with its knob away from the tick, and Lighting's Reset dimmed: the tick and the double click took the slider spec's own base (0 EV, Sharpening's amount 0, a gain's 0) while the block's Reset wrote the frame's import state (+1.50 EV on a negative, amount 1, the roll's measured stops). The spec's base is gone: Field::base reads the frame's import state in its own mode and decode, a gain the roll's measure, and the tick, the double click, the block's Reset and its lit state all read it. No render moves; only what a double click writes and where the tick stands.

title: A block folds by the tree's chevron before its title; its Reset shows only off rest, at the row's end
detail: Both evaluators found a block's Reset beside its boxed fold key, and the boxed › of a folded block read as a key that opens a sub-page. A Section now folds by the library tree's own bare chevron leading its title, the app's one look for folding, and its Reset shows only while the block stands off its rest, alone at the row's far end, the whole title between it and the fold. The title row keeps a key's height, so nothing moves as the Reset comes and goes; the panel's right edge no longer holds a chevron beside the scroll knob.

title: The gear names the app's Settings alone; a block's options wear two sliders
detail: The gear opened the app's Settings, white balance's options and the flat-field's. A block's own options key, in the panel and in Prepare the Roll, now draws an options glyph, two sliders in the Trinil stroke; a check fails if the gear appears outside the toolbar's Settings key.

title: The panel's scroll knob stays dark when a double click opens the editor
detail: An evaluation saw the panel's knob lit at rest after a double click opened the editor; its shots show the knob widened over its track, the state the pointer resting on the knob's edge strip gives by design. Replayed through the window's real event path (the pointer parked in the corner, a double click on a tile), the knob stays dark until a wheel moves the panel and goes out after its linger; the window check keeps that proof. The overlay knob is unchanged.

title: The readout's legend and the column's layouts say what a photographer says
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Language): 'Its inverse' and 'Two thumbnails a line' read oddly. The readout's dashed line is now named Inverse curve, and the column's select offers Names only, Two per row and One per row, in its menu and at rest. Only words move. French and Spanish filled in. Window checks picture_plots the_readout_names_its_curves_under_the_histogram, column_edges the_column_lines_up_and_its_keyboard_shows_where_it_is, sidebars and tree_leftovers find the new names.

title: De-dust's empty reading says which way Sensitivity reaches further
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Language): 'No dust at this sensitivity' left the slider's direction to guess. A reading that rings nothing now says 'No dust found: raise Sensitivity to catch fainter specks', since a higher sensitivity reads deeper inside the window and asks less of a speck; at full sensitivity, where there is nowhere further to go, it says 'No dust found, even at full Sensitivity'. Check: dedusting auto none_found_says_which_way_the_sensitivity_reaches_further (twin: a notch short of full still says raise), window auto_dust reads the note at rest.

title: The roll card warns of dyes off the film stock's and offers the stock's beside the warning
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (UX Language, UI Clarity): 'Dyes: Kodak; this film stock calls for Fuji' was quiet grey text and a riddle with no way out. Frames unmixing other dyes than their stock's now raise the warning band, 'Frames set to Kodak dyes, but this film stock has Fuji dyes', with a flat Use Fuji Dyes key under it: one gallery step writing the stock's family on every frame of the roll, each frame's dose kept, as picking the stock does (lay_dyes, shared with New Roll's dyes). Matching dyes keep the quiet 'Dyes: Fuji'. The Dye Separation block's note takes the same verb: 'Not the film stock's: Fujifilm Fujicolor has Fuji dyes', and 'Not from a film stock' where no stock names any. No render moves until the key is pressed. Checks: roll_card the_card_warns_of_dyes_off_the_stocks_and_offers_the_stocks (twin: mixed frames name only those off the stock's), roll_tab the_dyes_say_whether_they_are_the_film_stocks, window roll_card clicks the key, sees the card fall quiet and one undo bring the warning back.

title: The canvas's band keys start and end on the card's content inset
detail: UI evaluation s-f5b562fe (Spacing and density): the Library's key and the zoom's group stood 40 pt in, on the picture's padding (CardStyle.padding), while the deck's Presets tab, the status line and the gallery's grid start 24 pt in. Both ends of the canvas's band now sit on StatusStyle.inset, the card's one content inset; the band's height and the picture's padding are unchanged, so no render moves. Check: window canvas_layout, the Library's key starts where the status line's Rating does and the Panel's key ends as far in, the column keys pressed where they now lie (twin: not on the picture's 40-point padding).

title: The colour space's select shows its face at rest on the canvas's band
detail: UI evaluation s-f5b562fe (Clarity): the Working Space chip had no ground until hovered and read as the canvas's title. Picker's chip face now wears a flat key's face within its own edge (ButtonStyle.face, ButtonStyle.edge), as tall and as round as the mini keys beside it and centred in the band as they are, lit by the hand's veil as a flat key; its chevron stays and its popover drops under it. One corner per face (Picker.corner) serves the face, its veil and its focus ring; the field and pill faces are unchanged. Check: window canvas_layout, the select's face drawn inside its edge at rest (twin: the band's ground beside it); space_chip and panel_bindings still open its popover where it lies.

title: The ONI Trash has its own inspector: its count, what it keeps, and its Restore key
detail: The fifth evaluation found the inspector reading 'Select a roll' over the trashed photos, with no Restore beside them. The sidebar now lays the trash as its own kind: the photos it holds, the note that a file stays untouched, and one plain key naming its reach, Restore Photo or Restore N Photos on the picks, as the menu bar's Restore does, else Restore All…, asked as the row's menu asks; an empty trash shows no key. No Empty Trash key: ONI never deletes a library member's file (the trash only marks the sidecar), so emptying would delete originals, the owner's call alone.

title: The preset editor's form ends above its footer, and what a preset carries reads whole in the list
detail: The fifth evaluation saw the Carries boxes cut by the editor's footer mid-row and the list's subtitle ellipsized. The form filled its scroll's content, which was its height plus both margins, so its rows were stretched two margins taller than the sheet measured: the content is now the form's own height, its margin inside it, as in the save sheet. The list's detail line wraps whole; Slint reads a row's height with a wrapped text at its one-line width, so the text's own height, read at the width it is laid at, sizes the row. The check now asks every box to end a step over the footer's rule and the carries to wrap inside their row.

title: A slider's relief is light at rest and deepens under the hand
detail: An evaluation found fifteen raised knobs over inset tracks per panel reading as texture rather than a few reminders. The rail laid dsRecessed's edge and lit rim twice, its own over Inward's: it keeps Inward's alone, and its opaque body, there only for its rim, goes. One state, the hand on the row or holding the knob (a demo's look too), now grows the knob and deepens the relief: at rest the hollow's shade and the knob's black edge stand at SliderStyle.idle-relief, half, and reach a well's whole shade and a black edge under the hand and through a drag, on the rise spring. Half keeps a white knob's edge 3:1 against the lit stretch it ends; the colours, the bipolar hues and the Scanner keys are untouched. The levels' rail deepens under the hand as a slider's. Check: slider_relief drives the pointer over, onto and off a slider: half a well at rest, a whole one and a black edge under the hand and while held off the row, at rest again once let go (twins: a whole well at rest is caught; the panel beside the rail never moves).

title: The gallery's inspector is headed by the roll's name, its first block Film Stock
detail: An evaluation found the inspector spending its first block, 'Roll', on the roll's name alone, which pushed Film Stock down. The name is now the column's own title, in the title face and typed over where it stands, with the not-prepared warning under it; Film Stock opens the blocks. A project's name heads its column the same way, the 'Project' block gone. The window check clicks the title, types the name and presses Return.

title: New Project stands in the Projects tab, the project named as it is made
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Task fit, major): filing rolls for a client took a right-click New Project, a default 'Project 1' and a hidden rename. The Projects tab's column holds a flat mini New Project key beside its view select, in the gallery and beside a photo, whatever the projects hold: it makes an empty project, ringed, its name field open (new_empty_project, the empty grid's key too), to fill with Add to Project. Left: rolls dragged from the sidebar onto a project. The column shows the Archive or the Projects, never both, so no project stands beside a roll to take it, and a press carried across the tab switch would lose its row as the Archive's column is unmade; a roll is filed whole by Select All then Add to Project. Check: window project_filing::new_project_is_made_and_named_in_its_tab_and_a_double_click_opens (the key pressed through the pointer makes the project with its name open, and stays beside its photos; twin: the Archive's column has no such key).

title: A project shows its photos roll by roll, under each roll's name, in the tree and the grid
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Robustness, major): a project's rows read 'DSC_6432.NEF · Rol…', so two rolls' copies of one file looked alike once cut. A project opens into its rolls (project_tree::by_roll: the folder each photo lies in, the rolls in the order their first photo takes in the project, each keeping the project's order): a row per roll, named as the archive heads it (its marker's name, else its folder's), above its photos, which read their file name alone; the grid lays a band per roll headed 'Project / Roll'. A roll's row selects its photos, opens their menu and carries them in a drag; a drop on it joins its project, before it lands before its first photo. The arrows and the editor's walk follow the order shown, across the project's rolls. A project's heading takes no rename (several bands name it; the tree and the inspector rename it), so a heading's naming is its folder alone. Checks: project_tree two_rolls_copies_of_one_file_stand_under_their_own_roll_in_the_project_s_order (twin: grouped by name the copies share one roll), project_drop a_photo_dropped_on_a_project_joins_it_and_before_a_photo_lands_there (a roll's row joins its project), window projects_tab::two_rolls_copies_join_one_project_said_with_undo (rows and headings by roll, a roll's row selecting its photos; twin: the photos' rows alone read alike), project_walk (the walk roll by roll), sidebar_reveal, gallery_leftovers (twin: a project's heading opens no field).

title: A double click opens everywhere; a project is renamed by Return or Rename…
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Consistency, minor): a double click opened a photo in the gallery but renamed a project in the column. A project's or a roll's row double-clicked is its click again, as a folder's; a photo's row opens its photo, as its tile does. A project is renamed by its menu's Rename… (beside Delete Project, a rule between them), by Return in the gallery on the project ringed with no photo picked (as the Finder renames the item selected; a photo picked, Return opens it as before), or by its name in the inspector. Checks: window project_filing::new_project_is_made_and_named_in_its_tab_and_a_double_click_opens (twin: with a photo picked Return opens it), tree_hand::the_trees_pick_open_their_menus_and_rename_as_swift (twin: a double click types over nothing).

title: A tab opens at its top; a long project name wraps in the inspector and shows whole where it is cut
detail: Evaluation s-f5b562fe (Craft and Robustness, minor): after Add to Project the project grid opened scrolled, its first row under the title, and a long name was cut mid-word in the inspector. A surface switched to (Archive, Projects, the ONI Trash) opens at its top; the open photo lands only back from the editor (land_gallery). The inspector's name wraps over as many lines as it takes (EditableTitle); a row's title and a band's heading cut short by their ellipsis show whole under the pointer, and a tip whose words change under the hand is taken down, as a key's. Check: window project_filing::a_project_opens_at_its_top_and_a_long_name_reads_whole (twins: back from the editor the open photo lands down the grid; a short name is one line and shows no tip; mutations: no wrap fails at the wrap, no cut tip at the row).

title: projects.json is written so the shipped 1.5.6 reads it, each member's exact path and print beside
detail: Second review of #1473 (point 1): version 2 wrote each member as an object, which 1.5.6 cannot parse, so it set the file aside and every project vanished from every build. Version 3 writes members as version 1's texts, a print the first time the file names it and the path after (a print alone first), each with its path in paths, which 1.5.6 reads and shows; each member's exact path and print go in exactMembers, which 1.5.6 drops. A project read with exactMembers whose texts still name them one for one takes them; one an older build wrote back is read as version 1, a path text as a print-less member, a print giving up a path another member is named by (1.5.6 records the copy it found for a stale print), a print shaped as a path read as none. A file whose version is newer than this build's is read as far as it can, never set aside, never written (the save says why); projects-v1.json is still kept once, and a version 2 file as projects-v2.json. Checks: project::shipped_tests (1.5.6's types and lookups from eac39604) the_shipped_build_reads_the_file_and_its_write_back_loses_no_member (twin: the copy named by its print is lost), the_former_object_members_are_what_the_shipped_build_cannot_parse (twin: a path as print agrees with no file), a_print_recorded_on_its_copys_path_keeps_both_members (twin: kept, the two are one), a_file_from_a_newer_build_is_never_set_aside_or_written (twin: a known version's unreadable file is set aside).

title: A member no file shows stands missing in its project, where it can be removed
detail: Second review of #1472 (point 2, hard rule 1): a member whose path holds another file, and a Swift print whose only rows other members hold, vanished from their project. Each stands missing under the file holding its place (project_standing::lost: a path under a file, which no file can have, ending in that file's name), found there by the read, so Remove from Project takes it; a stand-in carries its member whole into another project (Member::of). Checks: project_standing a_member_no_file_shows_stands_missing_where_it_can_be_removed (twin: by the rows alone Trip shows nothing), project::file_tests a_former_files_stale_and_respelt_paths_are_found_by_their_prints.

title: A member without a print takes it once its file is read
detail: Second review of #1472 (point 3): a photo added while its tile was read, or one a version 1 file named by its path, never got a print, so a later read could not find it once its path went stale. Each read of the members gives a print-less member the print its file at its path was read with (project_standing::learn), written at once; a member holding a print keeps it whatever file stands at its place. A merge and an undo take a print learned on one side as the same member on every side (project::printed). Checks: project_standing a_member_without_a_print_learns_it_from_its_file (twin: unlearned, the moved photo stands missing), merge a_print_learned_here_is_the_same_member_in_the_merge (twin: compared whole it falls to the end), project::shipped_tests the_shipped_build_reads_the_file_and_its_write_back_loses_no_member.

title: Undo of New Project takes the project away and Redo brings it back
detail: Second review of #1475 (point 4): an undo of New Project gave the photos back and left an empty project. A members step holds each project it changed whole (project::Rosters); its undo takes away the project it made while it holds nothing else, its redo makes the same project again, and a photo it sends to a project deleted since stays where it stands. Checks: project an_undo_of_new_project_takes_the_project_away_and_its_redo_brings_it_back (twin: the project held at both ends stays, empty), project a_redo_toward_a_project_deleted_since_leaves_the_photo_where_it_stands, window project_steps::an_undo_of_new_project_leaves_no_project_and_its_redo_makes_it_again.

title: An undo or a redo on the projects reads where their members stand again
detail: Second review of #1475 (point 5): a member an undo brought back beyond the opened folder showed only after the next folder read. Ctl::regrouped reads the members' standing again before laying the grid. Check: window project_steps::an_undo_shows_a_member_beyond_the_folder_at_once (mutation: without the read, Z stays hidden).

title: A lost member stands on its nearest copy, the same from read to read
detail: Second review of #1474 (point 6): the copy standing in for a member lost from its place was the first by date then path, a backup copy as likely as any. The copy one read chose stays the member's while it stays free, chosen before any other member's; else the copy at its own path, then the one bearing its file name, then the one in its folder, then the first by date then path. Check: project_standing a_lost_member_stands_on_its_nearest_copy_and_keeps_it (twin: by date then path the backup wins).

title: The inspector's check measures its column from the blocks' fold keys
detail: A block's title now stands past its fold chevron, so the column's edge is the chevron, where the roll's name heading the inspector stands too; the check found the name outside a column measured from the title.

title: An expandable key tells its state again: the help mark and the block's fold say open or closed
detail: The help mark ('Help on Lighting') and the block's fold ('Hide Lighting') set accessible-expandable and accessible-expanded at their use of Button, and Slint 1.18's interpreter, which dev builds and the checks run, read neither once #1491 took the opacity off Button's root: that opacity made Slint inline every Button; a Button is now a component of its own, and the interpreter reads a nested component's accessible-* from its root alone, never from its use site (the compiled interface reads the use site first and kept them). Bisected: the check passes at the seventh wave's second merge (59940e7a) and fails at its third (ecb384f2, #1491). Button now carries expandable and expanded and binds its own accessible-expandable and accessible-expanded, as it does accessible-checked; HelpMark and FoldMark set them. Check: window help_card::a_help_card_opens_in_its_block_and_pushes_it_down (the mark closed then open; the fold open then folded; twin: a key that opens nothing, Reset, claims no fold, which a Button stating every key expandable fails).

title: The scrolled surfaces leave collections.slint for scroller.slint
detail: collections.slint had grown to 419 lines, past the architecture check's 400. Its scrolled surfaces (ScrollKnob, Scroller, ListView) stand in scroller.slint, 181 lines, its tiles and their headings (TileMarks, TileView, TileHeading) stay, 242 lines; collections.slint re-exports the three, as controls.slint does its split parts, so ds.slint's exports are unchanged; containers.slint reads Scroller from its own file. Checks: oni-core architecture, window scroll::*, gallery_cell::*, design_system::*, visible::a_missing_tile_is_grey_on_its_own_layer, visible::a_triplet_with_a_pass_gone_is_marked, oni-i18n catalogue.

title: The curves check leaves the store's wait to the held clock that can prove it
detail: editors::a_point_dragged_on_the_curves_reaches_the_store_as_one_step failed two runs in three on 'the store waits for the hand's cadence': it read the store right after the first move and needed that move within the hand's interval (8.3 ms) of the press, but a debug build's press alone took 8.5 to 9.3 ms measured (10.6 ms with its frame), after which the store rightly takes the move. Asserted only when fast enough, the wait was never exercised, which proves nothing. The wait inside the interval is proven on a held clock by editors::tests::a_curve_drag_writes_at_the_hand_s_pace_and_undoes_in_one_step and track's hand tests; the window check keeps what only the window shows: the dot follows the pointer at once, thirty fast moves reach the store at the hand's pace (twin: a write per move), and one undo takes the drag back.

title: A member 1.5.6 named by its loading placeholder reads as a member with no print
detail: Third review of the projects (point 1): 1.5.6 names a photo added while its tile loads by its placeholder 'waiting-/path', its path beside; this build read that text as the photo's print, which no file carries, so the member stood as a missing tile and never learned its print. A text project::member::read rejects is no print: a version 1 text is then a member at its recorded path (else the path after the mark), with no print, and a version 2 or exact member's such print is dropped (file.rs is_print). The learned-print step then gives it its real print off its file. Check: project shipped_tests::a_member_1_5_6_named_by_its_placeholder_learns_its_real_print, a 1.5.6-shaped file (twin: the placeholder kept as a print stands missing and learns nothing; mutation: without the rule the check fails).

title: A drop in a project shown by roll lands where its line shows and writes the order shown
detail: Third review of the projects (point 2): in a project grouped by roll, a drop past a band's last tile or on the line above a roll's heading resolved to the next roll's first photo and spliced in the stored order, which by_roll no longer shows: Roll 10 read C A D for C D A, a roll's end was out of reach, a photo could move among another roll's photos or into the next project. A drop now lands beside a photo, before it or past it: the grid's boundary is a cell and a side (Layout::boundary), the tree's line before a heading or a project ends the roll above it, before the first photo under a heading starts that roll. project::reorder_drop splices in the project's order as shown, roll by roll, and writes that order back, a member no row shows keeping its place; only photos of the target's roll land beside it (project::lands_beside), so no line or ring shows where a drop would do nothing, a roll's heading takes only its roll's photos, and a photo joins another project only where the line stands in it. The Projects tab's bands keep the tree's roll order under the rating filter. Checks: project drop_tests::a_drop_past_a_roll_s_last_photo_ends_that_roll_and_writes_the_order_shown (twin: spliced in the stored order A stays inside Roll 10), gallery a_drop_lands_beside_the_nearer_half_and_past_a_band_s_last_cell_ends_that_band (twin: the next band's start draws a band lower), project_drop the_line_above_a_roll_s_heading_ends_the_roll_above_it, window project_rolls::a_drop_by_roll_lands_at_its_line_in_the_tree_and_the_grid (twins: Roll 8's B on that line, Roll 8's A beside Roll 10's D, the tile after Client's last is Other's; mutations: the old resolution in the tree or the grid fails it).

title: A project's name and place are no undo step; New Project is one, and its redo keeps the name typed
detail: Third review of the projects (point 6 and its minor points on undo): a project dragged among the others recorded a step whose undo laid back members alone, so ⌘Z did nothing; the Projects tab's New Project key recorded none, so ⌘Z after it undid the step before; an undo then a redo of New Project brought the project back under 'Project N', the name typed since lost. One rule: a step holds the projects' members and the projects a gesture made; a project's name, description and place are its own, which no step records or lays back. History::record_members opens a step only where members change or a project is made, so a reorder opens none; the key makes its project through Ctl::regroup, one step named New Project; a walk that takes a project away keeps it in its step as it went (History::keep_taken, from Ctl::regrouped), so the walk back brings it under the name it bore. Checks: history a_reorder_opens_no_step_and_a_redo_of_new_project_keeps_the_name_typed_since (twins: compared whole the reordered projects differ; the step as recorded brings back 'Project 1'), window project_steps::the_new_project_key_is_one_step_and_its_redo_keeps_the_name_typed (twin: a drag recorded as a step leaves Client; mutations: without keep_taken the redo reads 'Project 2', compared whole the drag takes the ⌘Z).

title: A member named by a 1.5.6 loading placeholder never takes a photo from the project naming its print; every former file is kept
detail: Fourth review of the projects (point 1): 1.5.6 names a photo added while its tile loads by its placeholder and leaves other projects by text, so a photo put in Trip while loading, then joined to Portfolio by its print, stood in both; this build read the placeholder as a print-less member at the photo's path, project::exclusive gave the photo to the newer project, and the print learned at launch saved that, undoing the person's last move. One rule in exclusive: of two members that are one photo, the one holding its print keeps it over one with none, whatever the projects' dates, as that print was read after the other was named and so marks the later gesture; else the newest project. It holds before any print is learned, so the launch learns nothing and writes nothing. A former format's file is now kept each time this format replaces it, the first as projects-v1.json, each later one numbered (projects-v1-2.json, ...), never written over and none twice: 1.5.6's newer file was lost once projects-v1.json existed. Checks: project shipped_tests::a_placeholder_never_takes_a_photo_from_the_project_naming_its_print, in both date orders, through the launch and the next save (twin: printed on both sides, the dates give the photo to the newer Trip; mutation: ranked by date alone it fails), file_tests::only_a_change_writes_and_each_former_file_is_kept_beside_it_once (twins: a file a copy holds sets no third aside, a change in this format sets nothing aside; mutation: one copy a version fails it).

title: An exact member holding a placeholder print stands at the path after its mark
detail: Fourth review of the projects (point 2): builds from ad672e6a to before #1550 wrote 1.5.6's placeholder into exactMembers as a print, without its path where another member was named by it; #1550 dropped that print but took no path after the mark, so the member read with neither, showed nothing and was dropped at the next save. One reading for every text that is no print (file.rs place): a path names itself, a placeholder the path after its mark; a version 1 text and an exact or version 2 member's print both take it where they hold no path. Check: project file_tests::an_exact_member_holding_a_placeholder_stands_at_its_path, a version 3 file with such members with and without a path, read then saved (twin: a member with neither path nor print is dropped by the write; mutations: spelt taking no place, or keeping a placeholder print as builds before #1550 did, fail it).

title: A redo never makes again a project deleted since its undo
detail: Fourth review of the projects (point 3): New Project, the project renamed then deleted, then ⌘Z found it gone and ⌘⇧Z made it again under the name it was made with, pulling the photos it was made from out of their projects again. A redo remakes only what its undo took away: the step just walked is told the projects as its walk found and left them (History::walked, from Ctl::regrouped, in place of keep_taken); one it took away is held as found, so the walk back brings the name it bore; one it found gone is put at the step's other end too, so no walk makes it again and its photos stay where they stand. Checks: history a_redo_never_makes_again_a_project_deleted_since (twin: the step as recorded makes 'Project 1' again and takes a out of Old; mutation: without the rule it fails), window project_steps::a_redo_never_makes_again_a_project_deleted_since (twin: before the delete, ⌘Z then ⌘⇧Z brings Client back; mutation fails it).

title: A drop shows its ring or line, and acts, only where it changes a project
detail: Fourth review of the projects (point 4): a photo carried onto its own project's row or its roll's heading rang that row, and the release changed nothing, against #1551's rule. One rule for every mark: a place shows its ring or line only where its drop would change the projects, weighed by laying the drop on a copy of them (project_drop::landing in the tree, State::reorders in the grid), once a place pointed at, and the release lands what the mark showed. It also hides the line beside a photo where it already stands and the line above the project just below the one dragged, whose reorder_root now writes nothing when the order stays. Checks: project_drop a_drop_lands_only_where_it_changes_a_project (twins: Other's row takes A, the line below C moves it, Other above Client moves Other; mutations: landing without the trial, reorder_root writing a reorder that keeps the order), window project_rolls::a_drop_by_roll_lands_at_its_line_in_the_tree_and_the_grid (no ring on Client's row or Roll 10's heading, no line above A itself; twin: Other's row rings, the line above D moves A; mutation: the tree's marks unweighed fail it).

title: Checks for the grid's line where no drop lands and the roll order under the rating filter
detail: Fourth review of the projects (point 5): removing the grid's line filter passed every check, as its twin asserted the members alone, and the bands' roll order under the rating filter was untested. Window project_rolls::a_drop_by_roll_lands_at_its_line_in_the_tree_and_the_grid asserts the line itself as the hand lets go (Hand::drag tells it): shown past A, none for Roll 8's A beside Roll 10's D, none past C itself (mutations: the line unweighed, or weighed by roll alone as before #1557, fail it). project_rolls::the_rating_filter_keeps_the_trees_roll_order: Client stores Roll 10's A, Roll 8's A, Roll 10's D; under Gold the grid shows D, then Roll 8's A (twin: Gold's photos in the stored order put Roll 8's A first; mutation: the filter applied before grouping fails it).

title: The file at its place decides between a 1.5.6 placeholder and a print, never a rank at load
detail: Fifth review of the projects (point 1): #1554 ranked a member holding a print over one with none at the same path at load, before any file is known, so a print 1.5.6 left stale by a new scan saved over the file beat the placeholder 1.5.6 recorded later for that new scan: the new scan stood in no project and the next save wrote Trip without it. The file alone cannot tell the two cases, so project::exclusive no longer settles a member with no print against one holding a print at its place (both stay, the most recent project keeping a photo among members alike), and project_standing::learn, at the launch's read where the file at that path is known, settles it: a member with no print takes the print its file carries, or gives the photo up to a member holding that print there, as that print was read after it was named. So Portfolio keeps a while the file at a carries its print (review 4's case), and Trip keeps the new scan otherwise, Portfolio's stale print standing as a missing tile whose place holds another file, as after any rescan; a pair whose file is not read yet stays in both until it is. project::holder is the slot lookup printed and learn share. Check: project shipped_tests::the_file_at_its_place_tells_a_placeholder_from_a_print, both files at a, both date orders, through load, the launch's learn, where the photo stands, and the next save (twin: once Trip's member has learned the print, the dates alone give a to the newer Trip; mutations: exclusive settling by same alone, or learn never giving way, fail it).

title: The check that a file in this format is never set aside writes over one
detail: Fifth review of the projects (point 4): the twin meant to stop former-file copies multiplying asserted projects-v1.json and projects-v2.json absent, where a file in this format would be copied to projects-v3.json, and the round trip saved once over no file; deleting keep_former's guard for this format passed every check. project file_tests::a_file_round_trips_through_the_disk_saying_its_format now saves twice, the second over a file in this format, and only_a_change_writes_and_each_former_file_is_kept_beside_it_once ends asserting former_path(support, FORMAT) absent after a change written over this format (mutation: keep_former without its guard fails both).

title: A check that a placeholder stands at its recorded path, not at its mark's
detail: Fifth review of the projects (point 5): every placeholder in the checks was recorded at its own mark's path, so nothing proved the recorded path wins over the one after the mark (file.rs spelt and former), which 1.5.6 produces: renaming a folder moves the recorded paths, never the member texts. project file_tests::a_placeholder_recorded_elsewhere_than_its_mark_stands_where_recorded reads a version 1 text and an exact member, both marked /Roll 8 and recorded at /Roll 8b, each at /Roll 8b (twin: the path after each mark is /Roll 8; mutations: spelt or former preferring the mark's path fail it).

title: A tree drop lands where its mark stands when the tree changes under the held hand
detail: Fifth review of the projects (point 2): #1557 kept a tree drop's landing per row number, so an undo or a folder read laying the tree anew under a held drag left the landing worked out for the row's former node while the line was drawn at that number's new row: D held on the line above C, then ⌘Z putting back C A D, released D before C (D C A) under a line above A. A landing now holds for the tree as laid when it was worked out: each lay of the projects' tree (tree_column::lay_column) aims the held drag again at its pointer (Ctl::aim_project_drag, also each move's), working its landing out afresh and drawing its mark, so the line, the ring and the release always read the same rows, a node's neighbours and the projects included. Check: window project_rolls::a_tree_drop_lands_at_its_line_when_the_tree_changes_under_the_hand, D held on the line above C, ⌘Z, a pixel's move, released: C D A (twin: before the undo the row under the line holds C; mutations: no aim at a lay, or a lay keeping the landing, read D C A and fail it).

title: A drop's trial weighs each place against the whole library, measured; a cost by the photos carried is left to do
detail: Fifth review of the projects (point 3): the tree (project_drop::landing) and the grid (State::reorders) weigh each place the pointer enters by laying the drop on a copy of every project against the reach cloned whole, every member resolved, once more for a reorder. Measured in the test profile (workspace at opt-level 1), on 30 to 60 projects of 100 members over rolls of 36 with 300 to 600 rows of the opened folder: the reach's clone alone 0.23 ms at 3,000 members and 0.43 ms at 6,000; a tree place that aims (a project's row, a line beside the carried roll) 1.6 ms mean, 2.1 ms max at 3,000, 3.0 ms mean, 4.0 ms max at 6,000; a grid cell 1.25 ms mean, 1.9 ms max at 3,000, 2.5 ms mean, 3.8 ms max at 6,000; the same with 1 or 20 photos carried, so the cost is the library's, about 0.5 ms a thousand members, once per place entered and once per lay of the tree under a held drag (#1562), negligible at the owner's 172 members, within the 8.3 ms frame below about 10,000. Left: resolve the holders and each project's shown order once per layout and weigh a place against them at a cost of the photos carried, without a second rule that could part from the gesture the release runs (#1557).

title: A 1.5.6 placeholder at a path a print also holds waits apart until its file is read, written back as 1.5.6 gave it
detail: Sixth review of the projects (points 1 to 3): #1559 kept Trip's placeholder and Portfolio's print at one path as two live members until learn read the file, while resolve, holders, the gestures, regroup and written each took them for one photo: a drop beside the photo in Portfolio sent b to Trip, Add to Project named Trip and later lost the photo, an undo in Trip lent it Portfolio's print and the save then settled by date, any save wrote it as a bare path whose 1.5.6 rewrite stripped Portfolio's print of its path. One invariant now holds for every reader: the members hold each photo once, and no member with a path and no print shares its path with a member holding a print. The read (project::unsettled::hold) holds such a member apart in Project.unsettled, with the text 1.5.6 gave it (its mark and the path it named), its recorded path, the prints standing at that path, its place; no gesture, undo, prompt or menu reads it, so the photo stands where the print is, a missing tile there while the file is unread. Only the file decides (project::settle, from learn): carrying a print held against it, or one a member holds there, it is dropped and the hand's later move stands, wherever the photo went since; another file, it joins its project at its place with that print, the stale print a missing tile. A file never read leaves it waiting. A folder moved in ONI carries its recorded path, its text kept as 1.5.6 keeps it; merges pick it as any field. Written at its place under its own text and recorded path, its exact member holds that text as its print and the project's new unsettled field its prints, which 1.5.6 and earlier builds ignore, so this build reads it back the same while 1.5.6 reads and shows Trip as it gave it; rewritten by 1.5.6, the read holds it apart again against the prints there. exclusive is again one project per photo, newest keeping it, the read having taken the pair out.

title: Checks on the 1.5.6 pair before its file is read
detail: Sixth review of the projects (point 5): every assertion of the_file_at_its_place_tells_a_placeholder_from_a_print ran learn first, so nothing saw the pair between load and learn. project unsettled_tests, on 1.5.6's file (Portfolio older with b then a by print, Trip with a's placeholder named before a folder rename, then c) and no row of Roll 9: a_drop_beside_the_pair_lands_in_the_project_its_line_shows (a one tile, in Portfolio; b dropped past it stays in Portfolio; twin: the placeholder a member, b leaves for Trip), an_undo_in_the_placeholders_project_leaves_it_apart (remove c from Trip and undo: c back, the placeholder apart and printless, read back as saved, then 1-a at a drops it and 2-a joins Trip; twin: as a member the undo lends it 1-a and exclusive takes a from Portfolio), a_save_1_5_6_rewrites_keeps_the_pair_as_it_gave_it (a rename's save writes Trip's texts and paths as given and 1.5.6 shows a there; through written_back the pair reads back as it was; twin: written as a bare path, Portfolio's print loses its path), the_file_read_at_last_settles_the_placeholder_whatever_moved_since (a moved to Client and Roll 9 renamed in ONI, then read with 1-a: Client keeps it, the text unchanged; a removed from Portfolio: 1-a leaves it in no project, 2-a joins Trip; no file: it waits, a missing tile in Portfolio, unchanged; twin: weighed against the members alone, 1-a brings it back into Trip). With the hold undone (every placeholder a member, exclusive keeping printless and printed apart) all four and the updated shipped check fail.

title: A drag held in a tree survives a re-lay of another row count under the hand
detail: Sixth review of the projects (point 4): tree_rows::replace reset both models (every row and the rows near the view) whenever a re-lay changed the row count, so Slint destroyed every row element, the one holding the press included, and dropped its mouse grab: after a ⌘Z adding or removing a photo in an open project, or a folder read landing mid-drag, no move reached the drag, its mark stayed where the hand was, a release on no row or over the grid never ended it, and the next click on a row dropped the held photo there. A re-lay now tells both models only what it did (tree_rows::Relaid): the rows drawing one node from the end on are kept, so the rows come or gone are told removed or added where the old and the new rows part, the window of rows near the view carried across the change, and every row kept is told changed in place, so it keeps its element and a held press its grab. The drag holds the row whose press it is and follows it at each lay (Ctl::follow_project_drag); a re-lay removing that row ends the drag there, its mark cleared, dropping nothing. No change to the press, the click or the drag distance. Note: same() never holds, as Slint's Image equality holds no empty image equal to another (stock, picture), so every row kept is still told changed, as before; making it hold needs a picture identity the rows lack, or thumbnails of like-named photos swapping places would keep their old pictures. Checks: tree_rows::relaid::tests::a_change_stands_where_the_rows_part_and_every_other_row_is_kept (twin: a row of another name ends the kept tail) and a_relay_of_another_count_keeps_the_element_of_every_row_it_keeps (a listener on both models replayed as a repeater: E gone, then B come, tell one removal and one addition, Q and A keep their elements; twin: the same re-lay told as a reset remakes Q's element; with the reset put back it reads [Reset] and fails); window tree_held::a_held_drag_follows_the_hand_through_an_undo_that_changes_the_rows, by pointer events: Q held on P's line, ⌘Z a row shorter, then a row longer, the mark at the hand after each move, a release on no row ends the drag dropping nothing; Q held again, ⌘⇧Z, a release over the grid ends it; E held over Client, ⌘Z removing E's row ends the drag, its mark gone, and the next click on C is a click, E dropped nowhere (mutations: the reset put back leaves the mark on the line and fails; no end when the drag's row goes keeps its mark, and with that assertion removed the click on C fails its own).

title: A 1.5.6 placeholder is an ordinary member by its text, which a member standing at its file hides, worked out at every read; the held-apart machinery removed
detail: Seventh review of the projects, and reviews 4 to 6 before it: each fix since #1554 added state (a rank, a learn-time decision, #1564's Project.unsettled with its against prints and its settle step) and each opened the next edge, the last a data loss in the merge (unsettled picked whole, so a placeholder 1.5.6 added since was lost). One stateless rule replaces it. Invariant every reader relies on: which member stands for each row is decided in project::resolve alone, from the projects and this read's rows (the opened folder, standing and found), never stored; a placeholder stands at the row at its path only where no other member stands, else for nothing, so holders, grouped, the tree's captions and openers, member_projects, leaving, the delete prompt and every gesture see a photo a print holds once, at the print. A member read from 1.5.6's placeholder (WAITING_MARK and the path it named) is a Member whose print is that text (Member::placeholder), at its recorded path, else the path after its mark, read so from version 1 texts and from exactMembers alike; it agrees with any file at its path, is one member only with a placeholder of the same text (same, slot), so exclusive keeps one project per text, newest first, as 1.5.6 does, never weighing it against a print; it never learns a print (learn fills only members with no print, holder and printed lend no placeholder text) and is written back as read: its text at its place in members, its recorded path in paths, its exact member {path, print: text}. resolve places it last, the newest project's first, after members at their own paths and those found by print; standing lets it claim no file, so a print lost elsewhere is found at the file it names, and never looks it up by print. So: a print agreeing with the file there, or recorded at that path while the file is unread, or found there by its print hides it; a file carrying another print shows at the placeholder while the print stands as a missing tile. A gesture taking a photo out of its projects (Add to Project, a drop into another project, New Project from it) takes every placeholder at that photo's file with it (gestures::taking, leave), the drop keeping the target's places; Remove from Project takes that project's own placeholders at the photo's file and leaves another project's, which then shows the photo there, as 1.5.6 shows it; a reorder acts on the members shown. Undo and redo hold members as they are, placeholders included, and merges take them three ways like any member. Removed: project/unsettled.rs (Unsettled, hold, settle, Read), Project.unsettled, the unsettled field of the file read and written, its merge pick, its carrying in moved, settle's call in learn. Captions already counted resolved rows; delete_prompt now takes the project's hidden placeholders (project::shadowed) out of its count and, where only those remain, says its photo stands in another project (French and Spanish added). FORMAT is 4: every format 3 build (ad672e6a to a22538b9) takes an exact member holding a placeholder for a print to learn, which loses its text at its next write; 1.5.6 (eac39604) parses any version, ignores exactMembers and writes version 1, so it reads and rewrites this format as before, while a format 3 build reads it as a newer file and never writes it; this build keeps a version 3 file beside as projects-v3.json at its first write. Left open: this build's own photo added while its tile loads is still a member with no print, written as a bare path, which 1.5.6's later move by text can leave beside a print whose path the named rule then strips (review 7, point 2); merge::unchanged still counts learn's giving up a member as this side's change (review 7, point 4); a placeholder whose recorded path went stale is a missing tile for good, as it has no print to be found by.

Rewritten for the rule: shipped_tests a_member_1_5_6_named_by_its_placeholder_stands_at_its_file_as_given (it stands at its file, learns nothing, is written back as given; twin: printless, it learns 1-a), the_file_at_its_place_tells_a_placeholder_from_a_print (both date orders, file carrying 1-a, 2-a or unread: both kept by the load and the save, one project shows a), file_tests an_exact_member_holding_a_placeholder_stands_at_its_path (now the placeholder at its path, written back by its texts, the version 3 file kept beside) and a_placeholder_recorded_elsewhere_than_its_mark_stands_where_recorded. Mutations, each undone after: placeholders resolved with the other members fails 10 checks; taking without the placeholders 2; Remove from Project leaving its own 1; standing letting a placeholder claim its file 1; spelt or former dropping the text 6 and 13; FORMAT left at 3 1; agrees taking the text for a print 6; same or slot by path 1 each; oldest placeholder first 1; delete_prompt or shadowed ignoring the hidden 1 each; the members merged by pick 1.

title: Each index schema keeps a file of its own: this build's index-10.sqlite beside the index.sqlite 1.5.6 and the Swift app keep at schema 9, neither ever dropping the other's tables
detail: Eighth review of the projects, the fact under its four points: 1.5.6 (index schema 9, eac39604 index.rs) and this build (schema 10) shared Caches/index.sqlite and each dropped the other's photos and stamps tables on opening it, so after every switch between builds every roll was read anew, and 1.5.6 filed any photo added during that wait by its placeholder. Source fix: LibraryIndex::default_path names the file by SCHEMA_VERSION (index-{version}.sqlite), so a later bump starts a new file by itself and never touches another schema's; open reads PRAGMA user_version before any write (before the WAL switch) and refuses a file of another schema (None), so even a path named by hand is left as its build wrote it; user_version is written on a new file only, never rewritten at each open. The first open of the new file builds it as a first launch does: empty, its rebuilt date now (so the thumbnail sweep waits SETTLED, 24 h), filled as each folder is read. What the shared file held that the new one must take over: nothing. At schema 9 (1.5.6 or the Swift app wrote it last) this build could read nothing of it: its own open dropped it. At schema 10 (left by a schema-10 build before this fix) every column of every row is read off the photo's file and sidecar (library::indexed, refreshed; the app's direct index writes, index_passes and the moves, mirror a sidecar written or a file moved), so the first read of each folder gives it again; the rows of folders not opened since, and of disks away, come back as each folder is read or its disk returns, as after any purge of the caches folder, which the system may do at any time; stamps make every file read once; projects.json and the sidecars hold the truth. The stale file: index.sqlite stays where it is for 1.5.6 and the Swift app, never opened, written or deleted by this build; a pre-fix schema-10 build still running would keep sharing it with 1.5.6, this build no longer; after a later bump index-10.sqlite stays likewise for builds of schema 10, each a cache the system may purge. Readers kept: the app (shell, retired_matrices sweep, tidy) all go through default_path; the window checks library_wide and locate now open LibraryIndex::default_path(Caches) instead of Caches/index.sqlite (gallery, archive and gestures already did); instance.rs sets ONI_INDEX; the upgrade_check example accepts another schema's copy left as given. Comments: the busy timeout now waits on another process of this schema, rebuilt's date covers a file made anew, tidy's settled likewise. Checks: index::file_tests::this_build_keeps_its_schema_in_its_own_file_and_leaves_1_5_6_s_as_written (1.5.6's schema-9 file with a row beside; this build's default path is index-10.sqlite, opens empty and dated now, keeps its own row; 1.5.6's file byte for byte as written, its row kept; twin: the former shared open's drop changes it) and a_read_into_the_new_file_gives_every_row_the_shared_one_held (a roll with sidecars carrying a medal, a roll and a trash mark: the new file's rows equal the shared file's, column for column; twin: a value the index alone held, written to no sidecar, differs); index::tests::a_file_of_another_schema_is_never_opened_nor_written (rewritten from a_schema_of_another_version_is_thrown_away: refused, bytes kept, row kept; twin: the same version reopens with its row) and a_file_made_anew_dates_the_rebuild_and_a_plain_open_keeps_its_date (the drop half removed, as no open drops).

title: A 1.5.6 placeholder standing alone at a read file takes that file's print and is written as it from then on, so 1.5.6's gestures, which match by print, reach it
detail: Eighth review of the projects, point 2, a regression of #1567: learn skipped every member holding a print, so a placeholder never took its file's print even alone at a read file (shipped_tests asserted it), where #1550 to a22538b9 read it as a member with no print and learned 1-a. In 1.5.6, which matches every gesture by the tile's print once read, such a photo offered no Remove from its project, did nothing on Remove from Project, stayed in both on Add to Project and took no drop beside it; each switch added more. Fix: project_standing::learn takes this read's standing (the app computes it once, learns against it, and reads it again only when a print was learned, as a member that learned is another key of found) and works out project::resolve on it before changing anything; each placeholder resolve gives a row carrying a read print, which means no other member stands there (a print agreeing at its own path, one found there by its print, a member with no print or a newer project's placeholder would hold it first), becomes Member {its path, that print}, written from then on as that print with its path in paths. A placeholder beside another member, behind a print at a read file, or at a file not read yet learns nothing. merge::unchanged forgives the change as it forgives a print learned: member::learnt lays, on each placeholder mine no longer holds, the member mine holds in its stead at its path with a read print that read lacks, so a project another app deleted since stays deleted when this side only learned; merges and undo still lend a placeholder no print. Checks: shipped_tests a_placeholder_alone_at_its_read_file_takes_its_print_and_is_written_so (rewritten from a_member_1_5_6_named_by_its_placeholder_stands_at_its_file_as_given: unread it learns nothing; read it learns 1-a, stands at its own file, is saved as "1-a" with its path, the text 1.5.6 matches a's tile by; a project deleted elsewhere stays deleted; twins: printed alone reads the learning as a change, and the given text matches no read print), the_file_at_its_place_tells_a_placeholder_from_a_print (the rescan case learns 2-a and keeps it through the save in both date orders, the 1-a and unread cases learn nothing; twin: learned beside Portfolio's 1-a, exclusive would give a to the newer Trip), placeholder_tests a_later_move_to_portfolio_stands_over_the_placeholder (nothing learned beside a print, read or not), project_standing a_member_without_a_print_learns_it_from_its_file (against the standing). Window project_placeholder: Tour's placeholder, alone at B once read, is written as B's print; Trip's, beside Portfolio's print, as given.

title: A placeholder at a file not read yet shows the photo beside the member there and counts as its project's photo; it is hidden behind a print only once the file is read to carry it
detail: Eighth review of the projects, point 3: at a file not read yet every print agrees, so a print recorded at a placeholder's path hid it before the file proved anything: its project read 0, would not open, and its delete prompt said another project kept the photo, which the read could then disprove (a rescan: the new scan in no project), and Delete has no undo. Fix: resolve (now resolve::stands, each row marked held or shown beside) lets a placeholder show a row another project's member holds when that row carries no read print, so it counts in its project's caption, opener, grouped rows and bands, and shadowed, which feeds the delete prompt, counts it as no photo of its own only behind a read print; once read, #1567's rule settles it: the print the file carries wins, or the placeholder stands alone and learns (#1570). A project never shows one row twice: its own placeholder beside its own member stays hidden. Gestures, each on what the hand sees: holders keeps the member holding the row, so New Project, Add to Project and a drop from elsewhere take the photo from every project showing it, as they took hidden placeholders, and Add to Project into the project showing it beside files it there by its print; leaving names every project losing it (the holder's and those showing it beside), so the ask says all; member_projects and Remove from Project see every project showing a photo (resolve::showing, gestures::shown_in), Remove taking its own members and placeholders there; a reorder inside a project moves the member it shows; a drop beside a tile two projects show names no one project and is refused until the read settles which. Checks: placeholder_tests a_rescan_shows_in_trip_and_the_stale_print_as_a_missing_tile (unread, the new scan shows in Trip and Portfolio, shadowed [0, 0]; twin: by the holders alone Portfolio's print hides it), a_drop_beside_the_pair_waits_for_its_file_then_lands_in_portfolio (rewritten: two tiles, Remove offers both, the drop refused; twin: the holder alone would land it in Portfolio; once read b lands past a in Portfolio, Trip as given), a_project_holding_only_a_hidden_placeholder_claims_no_photo_and_says_so (unread: Trip shows and counts a, shadowed [0, 0], Remove offers both), a_later_move_to_portfolio_stands_over_the_placeholder (unread both, read Portfolio), a_merge_keeps_a_placeholder_1_5_6_added_since (d once, at Client's print, once read); shipped_tests the_file_at_its_place_tells_a_placeholder_from_a_print (unread, shown in both, in both date orders).

title: Remove from Project says where a removed photo still shows
detail: Eighth review of the projects, point 4: Remove from Project leaves another project's placeholder, which then shows the photo there, often a filing made in 1.5.6 and never seen in this build, while the notice said only that the photo was removed. Fix: remove_from returns the paths that left, sorted, and project::removed_said appends, for each project still showing any of them after the gesture (gestures::shown_in on the same reach), "It now shows in “Trip”." for one photo, else "One of them now shows in “Trip”." or "{n} of them now show in “Trip”."; the cell menu's notice says it, with Undo as before. French and Spanish translated. Checks: placeholder_tests adding_the_photo_to_client_takes_the_hidden_placeholder_with_it (a removed from Portfolio alone: "One photo removed from “Portfolio”. It now shows in “Trip”."; twin: removed from Client with nothing else showing it, the plain sentence); window project_placeholder (Remove A from Portfolio says it now shows in Trip; twin: B out of Tour shows nowhere else, Portfolio's stale print a missing tile elsewhere, the plain sentence; both undone through the notice, the column back to Tour 1, Trip 0, Portfolio 2).

title: Every key of the bar stands vertical, its glyph over its word, all at one height
detail: Owner: the bar's keys read as words with a small mark; an icon comes back on every key, set over its title. Button gains the bar's form (`stacked`): glyph over word (ds/bar_face.slint) at ButtonStyle.bar-key, 48 pt, flat keys and keycaps alike; the bar grows to 64 pt (ShellStyle.bar-height) and its tab bars, the faces and Prepare's steps, stand as tall, so the bar's line holds end to end. Undo, Redo, Feedback, Phone and Settings take a word as every other key; short of room every flat key keeps its glyph alone on a 32 pt key, decided once the bar is laid (a binding would feed the history's widths back into the width that decides them). New icons in the Trinil stroke: back, edit, gauge (Prepare Roll), folder-add (Add Folder), update. Checks: window toolbar_keys every_bar_key_wears_its_glyph_over_its_word_and_a_key_on_is_pressed_in (every key of both bars 48 pt tall, each word centred under its key's middle with its glyph drawn over it; twins: the window's other keys are of other heights, nothing drawn beside the glyph); toolbar (Settings wider than Phone, sized by their words), canvas_layout (the card under the 64 pt bar).

title: A bar key that holds a state is pressed in while it holds, no lamp

On the bar the primary keeps the keycap's grey and wears the accent on its glyph alone (ButtonStyle.primary-glyph, 3.5:1 on the cap), never a fill: EXPORT, ADD FOLDER… on the archive, PREPARE ROLL beside an unmeasured roll, the update's face; its place at the right end and its keycap make it the main action. title: The rating filter leaves the gallery's bar
