The choice is the preferences key wholeRollAfterPrepare, flipped by Act::WholeRollAfterPrepare and remembered as Keep the Zoom is; a file written without it reads off, and 1.5.6 (eac39604), which parses any JSON object and writes back every key it read, ignores and keeps it. title: The export's presets in one picker: each line a preset's name over its summary, the one in effect named at rest with its own, Save as Preset… at the list's end
detail: Owner's direction: a Web preset is welcome, but more presets need another way to show them than the plate of keys three to a row. Saving and renaming ask in a sheet of their own (PresetNameSheet): its field takes the keyboard, its commit stays dark while the name is blank, Return commits, Escape keeps nothing, and closing gives the keyboard back to the key monitor. The file is unchanged: exportPresets keeps each preset as its name and its settings in their own preference's words, which 1.5.6 (eac39604) reads, writes back and never names a built-in preset by. Checks: window export_panel picks Web by a click and Print by the arrows and Return, saves (twin: Save with no name keeps nothing), recalls, renames through the sheet and removes, Escape keeps nothing; export_panel a_preset_saved_before_web_keeps_its_name_and_its_file (twin: the built-in Web's line, which holds the same settings, is not the one checked; the file's items keep their two words); sheets the_preset_name_sheet_holds_the_keys_and_answers_them (twin: Escape keeps nothing, Return keeps the name); unit kept a_summary_names_the_format_the_space_and_the_size (twin: the quality is not among what it says), the_presets_file_still_reads_in_1_5_6 (twin: settings named by a preset read as nothing).

The note under the space's tabs and the one naming the space the photos were edited in are now SteadyNote (design system): its room is the tallest of every text it may say (notes::space_notes, notes::edited_in_notes, published with each), so a preset or a tab changes the words, never the place of what follows. The edited-in note is said in every space ('This photo was edited in Display P3, the space the export writes.'), and in another one says the canvas and the preview now show it in the space the export writes. The format's own row stays one row, Compression's field as tall as Quality's slider, which the check guards; the Profile field always stands, the built-in space's own out of reach, Custom's profile or the choice still to make, so a saved preset bringing a profile moves nothing. ProPhoto's purpose is tightened to two lines in English, so the note's room is two lines there. The spaces' purposes and the chip's hints move from oni-colour to the app's notes, translated (they read English in French and Spanish), ProPhoto's in the app's spelling of colour. Closing the name sheet hands the keyboard back to the key monitor, as every sheet with a field does. Checks: window export_panel reads the format's tabs, the space's tabs, the profile keys, Compression, Quality, HDR and Pixels at the same height through No preset, Web, Print, Instagram and Display (twins: Adobe RGB's purpose takes another height than Display P3's, the edited-in note says another sentence in sRGB in the same room, and under Print the format's row holds Compression in place of Quality); Custom keeps the keys and Quality where they stood; unit notes every_note_the_field_says_is_among_those_its_room_is_fitted_to (twin: a list without the notes waiting for a profile misses one the field says), the_edited_in_note_is_said_in_every_space_and_its_room_holds_each (twin: one photo's room is not fitted to a batch's words).

title: Prepare the Roll has no Skip key: NEXT goes on past a step left empty
detail: Owner, after using the app: no separate skip button, a step not completed is passed by NEXT. The owner's call reverses the footers of #1248 and #1438. The keycap is live on every step that may go on (`action-enabled` false only on the window with nothing to measure) and raises the same `advance`; a step passed empty keeps no mark on the bar, as under Skip. `skippable` and the Skip key go, and the flat-field's help and a slide's white name NEXT and 'nothing picked' instead, in English, French and Spanish. Checks: window prepare_walk (a DSLR roll's empty flat-field and empty base each passed by the key found by its label, no Skip on any step, no mark left, Back returns; every frame flagged, PREPARE ROLL stays dark, twin: a frame to measure lights it; undone in Rust, it fails at 'an empty flat-field may go on'; a Skip key put back fails at 'NEXT alone goes on'), prepare's footer and its click at the keycap's place, slides' unpicked white; the prepare bench walks by the key.

title: A pick on the film base goes straight on to the next step
detail: Owner, after using the app: on the pick in the dark, go straight to the next step. This is Prepare's Base step (`Step::Base`, 'Pick the Film Base', the film's own black; 'Pick a White or Grey' on a slide roll, the same step and gesture). `base_clicked`, which a click and the floor's Return share, lays the pick, gives a key's click and walks on as NEXT would; a pick landing nowhere, or on a scan that cannot be read, stays with its reason shown. The value stays visible and reachable: the step's mark on the bar, and back on the step its ring, its colour and its note, where another pick replaces it (hard rule 1). The click moves from the slint to Rust, as the surface goes with the step; the ring's landing, never seen now, goes with `base-picks` and `RollStyle.landing`. `step_to` lets the scan's pointer go on a step change, or the loupe came back at the old place with no hand over it. Checks: window prepare_walk (a pick by the hand reaches the flags with one click and rides in every draft; the Base tab shows it, no loupe until the hand returns; a second pick replaces it and goes on; a pick outside the scan stays silent; undone, it fails at 'a pick goes straight on', the pointer kept fails at 'the hand left with the step'), prepare_loupe (an unreadable scan: a pick stays, its reason said, twin: NEXT goes on), canvas_keys (Return), slides, prepare.

title: The card's dissolve under a scrub lasts a third as long: 200 ms to 67 ms
detail: Owner, after using the app: divide the transition by three on the slide at the last step. That transition is the frame card's dissolve while the Frame slider of 'Place the Measuring Window' walks the roll (#1500); no slide runs between steps. Its length is now the design system's `Motion.dissolve`, 67 ms, in place of the 200 ms Rust handed over in `card-fade`. The same 200 ms also paced the dissolves, and two dissolves make a flash (WCAG 2.3.1), so the pace stands apart as `prepare::card::PACE`, unchanged: the card still changes at most 5 times a second, under three flashes. Checks: window prepare_frames (a frame asked lies whole on the card 100 ms after, its luma that of the settled frame, twin: the two frames read apart by over 60; the token a third of the pace; a scrub still dissolves once a pace; undone to 200 ms, it fails at 'the dissolve over within 100 ms'), unit card a_frame_dissolves_in_only_once_the_pace_allows (twin: past the pace, at once; two dissolves over a third of a second).

title: The navigator in two sections, Favourites then Computer, with no header row

Beside a photo, its folder's row is centred once the list has laid it: that list is made after the reveal is asked, so it never scrolled, which the extra headings brought to light (row_marks); Rust now publishes the row with every publish, -1 in the gallery, and each list owes the reveal until the row is there. title: A live check of the published Windows app: its update and a report through its own keys
detail: Owner's question: since 1.5.4 the downloads dashboard shows no Windows update at all. The Windows live workflow (by hand only, as each run reaches the real recorder) installs the release before the latest on a runner, with a support folder of its own marking that version launched and the welcome seen; it waits for UPDATE TO <latest> through the accessibility tree, presses it and Download, waits for the app to quit, for the helper to lay the latest ONI.exe (its hash the published one) and start it, for the former copy to go, and for lastLaunchedVersion to reach the latest, which the app writes only once the install ping is answered. With report, the updated app sends a feedback report through its Feedback key, the sheet's field and Send, until Done shows. Pictures, the tree of every missing key, preferences.json and oni.log are kept 14 days. Each run sends one real install ping, an update, and checks the feed twice.

title: Every Windows package starts the app it built
detail: The Windows package's last pictures showed the installer's finish page, never the app: the wizard runs in the setup's child process and takes no key once the install runs, so the Enter meant for Finish was lost, and neither its title nor the accessibility tree reached the key; a later run even lost an Enter before Install. Every package run now starts the ONI.exe it built, with a support folder of its own marked launched at that version so no install ping is sent, waits up to 120 s for its Settings key through the accessibility tree, keeps a picture and oni.log, and fails when the app ends or never shows its keys. The installer's walk ends on its last page.

title: The Windows CI's window checks see the interface again
detail: The Windows CI builds and tests in release, where the interface is compiled without its element names: every window check that finds an element by its role and label (common::the, placed) found none, 80 962 warnings in one run and most of its 97 failures. SLINT_EMIT_DEBUG_INFO is set for the whole job, so the compiled interface keeps the names the checks read, as the live preview does on the Mac.

title: The window checks read each system's own words and paths
detail: Of the Windows CI's 28 failures, the checks expected the Mac's words and spellings where the app rightly answers Windows' own: Show in Explorer and Ctrl+E through common::reveal and common::command (export_flow, gallery, navigator, told, tree_hand, updates, visible); paths spelt as the archive spells them, `/` between names, through common::spelt and paths::normal (balance_kept, locate's listing, oni-core's kept and oni_trash, made_roll); a field Tab brings the keyboard to selecting its text outside the Mac, as Slint does after Windows' own fields (keyboard); a help mark found in the app's language where the interface is compiled, as in the CI (help_demo); the Lab screen's twin overflowing with counts twice as long, whatever the system's monospaced font (scanner, ScreenProbe's count); the gallery's tile lookup naming the tiles it saw when one is missing (canvas_layout).

title: Every file checks out byte for byte as committed
detail: Windows' CRLF checkout changed the lines the checks parse and hash: the Mac words check never found its tests' module, fields' block reader and the French catalogue's lines missed their `\n`, the canisters' hashes moved. `.gitattributes` holds every file as committed, `* -text`, so no system converts a line end.

title: A favourite renamed in the Explorer is found by its file id on Windows
detail: bookmarks.json kept no file id on Windows, so a favourite renamed or moved outside the app was never offered back there. Windows now keeps NTFS's file index, read with GetFileInformationByHandle, and finds the folder holding it among the nearest folder's own, else opens it by id on its volume (OpenFileById) and names it by its final path, as the Mac's /.vol does; the volume's serial must match. The Mac's rename check runs on Windows too.

title: On Windows a watched folder can be renamed and its disk ejected
detail: ReadDirectoryChangesW holds each watched folder open, and Windows then refuses to rename it or a folder above it, or to eject its disk, and the watcher lets its handles go only later on its own thread, so even the app's own Rename raced it. Windows now watches by polling every two seconds, holding nothing open, as FSEvents holds nothing on the Mac; the watches' release around a rename is gone with its reason. Check: a watched folder and the folders above it rename while watched, and, on Windows, a ReadDirectoryChangesW watch is refused the same rename (twin).

title: The window checks' waits stretch on a software adapter
detail: A runner with no GPU renders on WARP or lavapipe, 20 to 50 times slower: a roll's drafts and an open photo's thumbnail missed waits sized for a GPU. Rig::until stretches its limit tenfold when the adapter is a CPU one, a cause outside the app named where the checks answer it; what the window times is left as it is.

title: The report sheet says this computer, not this Mac
detail: On Windows the feedback sheet said the log is encrypted on this Mac. It says this computer, in English, French and Spanish.

title: A Windows build not made for release never lays an update over itself
detail: On Windows any executable laid a verified update over itself: a check's binary started the helper, which waited for it to quit and then tried to swap and start it. As only a team-signed app installs itself on the Mac, only a build stamped for release does on Windows; any other keeps the archive in Downloads to open by hand. Window check updates on Windows: the archive kept, as on the Mac.

title: The Windows CI keeps the window checks' pictures of a failure
detail: A failing window check on Windows could only be read, never seen: the CI keeps target/tmp/shots for seven days when a check fails. Two checks say more when they fail: the project's pick names the gallery's order it was made in, the export's Stop names the job as the click found it.

title: Three window checks read what is drawn the way each build draws it
detail: From the Windows CI's pictures: the Lab screen cuts a count too wide just short of its column's edge where the interface is compiled, where the live preview lets it overflow, so the screen check looks within a point and a half of each edge, which a count that fits keeps clear by over two (scanner). The status bar gives its room to work under way and then shows the frame's line again, so the line is read as it is drawn rather than at one instant (filmstrip). The press with every balance kept is bounded tenfold on a software adapter, like every wait (balance_kept).

title: The readout is its plot alone
detail: Owner's ninth round: the small words under the histogram go. The legend (Histogram, Print curve, Inverse curve) and its tokens are gone; the plot takes the readout's whole 150 pt on every tab. Window check picture_plots: no word under the plot on the Colour and Roll tabs, the plot 150 pt tall (twin: a row of words would leave it shorter).

title: The bar holds every word on a 13-inch screen, in every language
detail: Owner's ninth round: the bar must not give way to glyphs on a 13-inch MacBook Air (1440 pt). The bar's caps keep 12 pt either side instead of 16 (BACK and EDIT, PREPARE ROLL, ADD FOLDER, EXPORT); EXPORT is 110 pt instead of 124; the Pro and Scanner faces 176 pt instead of 232. Words: Select All is the Sheet (Planche, Contactos), as film shows a roll whole; Paste to Roll on the key is Paste All (Tout coller, Pegar todo), the menu keeping its longer title; Reset Pro and Reset Scanner are Reset alone, its help naming the face; the update's face says UPDATE (MISE À JOUR, ACTUALIZAR), the version in its help. The bar publishes the width its words need (Bar.needed). Window check toolbar: with the Mac's traffic lights, the editor's bar needs at most 1440 pt in English, French and Spanish; whole at that width (twin: a point narrower, glyphs alone).

title: A favourite's star shows its press under the hand
detail: Owner's ninth round: a hover on the stars, to add and to remove. A favourite's star is filled and gold; under the hand the star shows what its press will make, filled gold to add, an empty grey outline to remove, and once pressed what it made until the hand leaves. Button gains under-hand; Icons.favourite-on is the filled star. Window check row_marks: the offered star, the hand beside it, is not gold (twin), under the hand it lights gold; a favourite's star, the hand away, is gold (twin), under the hand it goes out.

title: The canvas's tool shows on a tab of its colour at the card's edge
detail: Owner's ninth round: instead of a flat lit ground under a tool's key, a tab glued to the canvas card's top edge names the tool the canvas is in, each in its own colour: the Sheet orange, Crop verdigris, De-dust violet, Compare pink (ToolStyle, ToolTab, CanvasTools after the Library's key, the colour space's select starting after them). The tool's bar key shows its glyph in that colour while it holds and no lit face (Button on-ink). Window check toolbar_keys: each tool's key bare at rest with neither its colour nor its tab (twin), under the hand a ground, on its glyph in its colour and its tab in the same colour under the bar, bare again let go.

title: One system for the sheets and the notices
detail: Owner's ninth round: every modal and every notice follows the same rules, with motion and an ergonomic place (ds/README.md, Overlays). A sheet rests a little above the window's middle (SheetStyle.rest 0.42) and comes in as one at Motion.overlay-in, the scrim darkening as the card rises 16 pt; every footer puts Cancel at the left and the keys at the right, AskSheet's included. The notice rests at the bottom right of the view the hand works in, above its status bar, where a grid of photos and a frame leave room: at the window's top right it covered Crop's DONE, under the canvas's band it covered the gallery's first tiles and caught their drag. It slides in at Motion.overlay-in and away at Motion.overlay-out, with Dismiss beside its action at its foot (#1683); it leaves by Dismiss, its action or after its linger unread. Reduce Motion shows both at once. The update's prompt is a plain question. The Scanner's styles move to theme_scanner.slint and the notice and the banner to notices.slint, so the theme and the containers stay under their caps. Window checks sheet_layout (rest, footers), sheets (the export's replace prompt pressed where drawn), sheet_keys (the notice's close key), told (the notice's action a margin and its padding over the status line; twin: the library's tabs far outside).

title: A closed sheet hands the keyboard back
detail: A sheet closing while its own field held the keyboard left it with the field's dying element, so the shortcuts went deaf until a click; closing any sheet now gives the key monitor the keyboard, a field a sheet opens on still keeping it as the sheet opens. The window checks draw before they wait, as a window does, so what a change brings in (a sheet's entry, its field taking the keys) starts at once instead of at the next shot.

title: The notice and the tooltips lie in the window's own space
detail: Where Slint draws its own menu bar in the window (the checks' headless window, while macOS and Windows show the system's), the content lies under it while absolute positions count from the window's top: the notice and the tooltips, laid from those positions in the content's space, stood the menu bar's height too low in every shot. They now lie in a layer set back by the content's origin (app.slint), so the shots the owner judges show them where they are; on macOS and Windows nothing moves. Window checks told and tooltip read them against what they speak of.

title: Leaving full screen lays the traffic lights back in the bar
detail: Owner's report: back from full screen, the traffic lights sat at AppKit's top-left corner over BACK, the bar keeping no room for them. winit reads the window out of full screen only in windowDidExitFullScreen, after the last resize of the way out, so every resize of it read full screen: no room in the bar and the lights left where AppKit lays them. The end of each full-screen transition (NSWindowDidEnter/ExitFullScreenNotification) now lays the lights and the bar's room again on the loop's next turn (chrome::after_full_screen), followed from the moment winit has made the window (winit_window().await): before the loop runs there is no window to follow, which the first attempt missed. Each end is logged with the room the bar keeps. No window check reaches AppKit's full screen; the owner's eye and the log are the proof.

title: The bar's ends line up with the columns' content
detail: Owner's call: the header's content no longer stands out past the columns'. Its ends take the columns' inset (ShellStyle.bar-end, the column inset, 16 pt) instead of 8 pt; where the traffic lights show, their room starts the bar alone, as it keeps their own margin after them, so the windowed bar needs the same width as before (a 13-inch screen still holds every word). Window check toolbar: without the lights, BACK starts where the columns' leftmost control does and EXPORT ends where their rightmost does; twin: with the lights the bar starts at their room. The widening and accent checks read the new end.

title: The export's EXIF folds away beside each picture
detail: Owner's tenth round: the export screen is the pictures'. Each line's EXIF stands in a card, each label over its field, closed until the key left of the picture opens it, for every line at once (Exporting.exif-shown); open, the picture gives the card and its gap of its width. The card is 260 pt and a long word ends cut (owner: cutting words is fine), so the no-cut measure of every stock's and camera's name goes. The file's name stays under its picture on a band of the panel's ground, beside its size, card open or not; the panel says each file takes the name under its preview. Window checks export_columns (closed at first, the key opens and closes the card on both lines, labels over fields, the picture's width given back; twins) and export_panel (the lone photo centred on its whole line, the field faces on their ground).

title: A tool's tab under its key, not on the canvas
detail: Owner's tenth round, replacing #1672's tabs on the canvas and its coloured glyphs: while a canvas tool holds, its bar key shows a tab of the tool's colour under it, on the bar's bottom edge, as wide as the key and 5 pt tall (ToolStyle.marker), its top corners round, drawn with the tool's ring (#1681); the key itself stays bare (Button on-apart, no lit face, no coloured glyph). CanvasTools and ToolTab go. Window check toolbar_keys: at rest neither colour nor tab, under the hand a ground, on the tab in the tool's colour under the key, its ends at the key's and nothing beside it, the key without colour; let go, the tab gone (twins).

title: Square keys in the dense bar
detail: Owner's tenth round: short of room, a flat key's glyph alone stood on a key 32 pt wide and 48 tall, which read as squeezed. It now stands on a square a keycap tall (ButtonStyle.bar-glyph-key, 40 pt): 48 pt squares would run 67 pt past the narrowest window (1100 pt) with the traffic lights. The traffic lights' room in the checks is the 100 pt the app's log read on macOS 26. Window check toolbar_fit: on the narrowest window with the lights, every glyph alone on a square key, every key inside the window and none over another; twin: worded, a flat key is wider than tall.

title: A ring of each held tool's colour around the card
detail: Owner's tenth round: to make the app fun and show a mode plainly, each canvas tool held draws a ring a stroke wide (1 pt) of its colour around the card, the card's own corners kept, square where they are square. Tools held at once nest in their keys' order, Sheet outermost then Crop, De-dust, Compare, each ring a stroke inside the ones before it; each tool's tab hangs from its key down onto its own ring, over the rings outside it, an inner ring and its tab drawn over the outer ones, so no line crosses a tab. The rings lie in the window's own space over the card (ModeRings in app.slint, the design system's ModeRing); each tool key the bar shows publishes where it stands (Bar.place, its copies the bar measures with never do). Window check toolbar_keys: each tool's ring and tab, and Crop with Compare nested, Compare's tab over Crop's ring onto its own; twins at rest and let go. The presets check lets the copy sheet come in before its click on Don't ask again, as a hand does; it clicked during the sheet's entry, where the box stood 16 pt lower.

title: The EXIF card's own cross, a rangefinder key, tighter margins
detail: Owner's tenth round: closed, the key left of each picture wears Trinil's rangefinder, the camera the EXIF comes from; open, the key gives way to a cross at the card's top right, on its first label's line, that folds it. The card's padding is Space.s and its gap to the picture Space.m, the picture taking the rest. Window checks export_columns (the picture right after the key, open the card in the key's place and the picture giving it what the key took less, the cross over the first field at its right) and export_panel.

title: A denser notice with Dismiss; the EXIF card's cross a key
detail: Owner's tenth round: the notice is a tight card, its title then its words then at its foot Dismiss beside its action (Undo, Show in Finder), the accent key, the close cross gone; it leaves by Dismiss, its action or after its linger. The EXIF card's cross is a key with a face, as the key that opens the card, flat under the hand, no longer a bare glyph. Window checks sheet_keys (the notice's Dismiss and Undo), told (its action's foot over the status line).

title: A title typed over keeps the column's margins
detail: Owner's tenth round: renaming a roll's title in its column, the field ran from the column's very edge to its content's, its words led out to where the title stood (RenameField's outdent). The field now stands on the column's content as every field does, its margins the column's, in the roll's column and over the gallery's heading alike; outdent goes. Window check roll_card: the title's field as wide as the column's content, the stock's key; twin: it starts past the fold keys on the column's edge.

title: A pinned row hides what scrolls under it to the pixel
detail: Owner's report: a half-pixel line let the rows scrolled under the library tree's pinned row show through. Its square ground lay at a fractional place, so the device pixel it half covered was drawn half ground, half row. The ground now covers whole device pixels, its edges led out to them (row.slint).

title: The file's name under the picture itself
detail: Owner's report: the name's band under a picture stood at the slot's left edge while a frame narrower than the room stands in its middle. The name and the size now lie under the picture as it shows, the row set in by half what the frame leaves of the room. Window check export_columns: each picture centred in its slot with its name and size under it, an upright frame alone too; twin: that frame's name off the slot's edge.

title: The collection: bodies and lenses kept and offered
detail: Owner's call: ONI keeps the bodies and the lenses a hand types, the last used first, in the support folder's collection.json (oni_library::collection). It learns from a roll's Camera Body and from the camera and lens a hand types or picks on an export's line, never from a scan's own metadata, which names the camera that digitised the film. The Camera and Lens of an export's EXIF and a roll's Camera Body offer it by a chevron key (KnownField). Where nothing is picked in the archive, the right column shows it: its bodies and lenses, each forgotten by its row's key, and a field to add one. A click anywhere on the gallery's ground, under its last row included, drops the picks and turns the column to the collection until a photo is picked or a folder opened. Window check collection: the opened roll's column, then the collection after a click on the ground (twin before it), a body and a lens added and kept in the file, a pick showing the roll again, the roll's body joining first, an export's Camera filled from the collection's menu (twin: the lens untouched); unit checks for the order, the case, forgetting and the file. Window check gallery: a click under the rows now drops the picks (twin: B picked before), and the column stands on the roll again once a photo picked since leaves it.

title: A click on the gallery's ground reaches no cell
detail: Owner's report: a click on the gallery's empty room still picked a photo, so nothing could be deselected. The point resolved to the nearest cell, clamped to a band's last cell, column or row, which a drop needs and a click must not take: a gutter, a margin, the room past a row's last cell picked its nearest photo. A click, a right click's menu and a drag's start now take the cell whose frame holds the point (Layout::cell_at), none on the ground; a drop keeps the nearest. Unit check: the gutter, the room past the last cell and under the rows reach no cell (twin: the nearest is a cell). Window check gallery: a click in the gutter between two cells drops the picks (twin: B picked before).

title: The collection starts from the rolls' bodies; an empty list's key says how a name comes
detail: Owner's call: the collection takes in, once, the camera bodies a hand gave the rolls the library index holds (LibraryIndex::camera_bodies, the most photos first; Collection::take_in after the kept names; `seeded` kept in collection.json so a body forgotten never comes back; an index with no photo yet waits for a later launch). A known field's key now shows even with no name kept: its list holds one disabled line, 'No body yet' or 'No lens yet', with a note saying a name typed there joins the collection. Unit checks with twins for the query and take_in; the collection window check now starts from a seeded roll body and opens the empty Lens list.

title: An export stopped before any frame reached its writer ends stopped
detail: Seen on the Windows runner: Stop clicked while the first large frame was still decoding ended the batch as written, 0 photos exported. The writer marked a batch stopped only when a frame reached it after the stop, so a stop that held every frame back in the decoders or on the GPU stage left it Done. staged() now ends Stopped whenever the stop is set and fewer frames were written than asked. Check export::batch: a stop before any frame reaches the writer is a stop (it read Done before the fix).

title: The tree's cost check counts the open photo's thumbnail from the open
detail: On the Windows runner the open photo's thumbnail was drawn from its sidecar 2 s after the open, while the photo's own render took 11 s on the software adapter, so the check, counting from that render, waited for a second landing that never comes. Both waits in tree_cost count from the open.

title: A step taken before every frame is read writes its draft once the last one lands
detail: Prepare the Roll writes a step's draft only once every frame is read; a step taken earlier wrote nothing until the next step or the window's close, so a roll left then lost that step. Seen on the Windows runner, where the frames read slowly. The roll remembers a step that waited (Roll::step_drafts) and writes it as the last frame lands (Roll::draft_landed). Check prepare::model: a frame still unread keeps the step waiting, the last one writes it once.

title: The shell's layout check opens a photo by its place in the gallery's order
detail: On the Windows runner the check looked for Bad's tile among the tiles the grid had laid, A00 to A27, Roll B lying below the visible rows; it passed or not with the grid's scroll. It now opens a photo by its place in the gallery's order, as its tile's click does, laid on screen or not (canvas_layout).

title: The export's unwritable folder is unwritable on Windows too
detail: The export check made a folder unwritable through its read-only attribute, which Windows ignores on a folder, so a folder made inside it was made and no failure came. On Windows its writes are now refused through its access list (icacls /deny (W), then /remove:d), the read-only permission kept elsewhere (export_flow).

title: The projects' checks date their files, so the gallery lays them alike on every system
detail: On the Windows runner a pick from A to Z with Shift took C too: the gallery lays photos newest first, and Windows' file clock, which steps by about 16 ms, gave files written together one time, so the name broke the tie in one run and not in the next (B, C, A). The projects' hand dates each file a second after the one before, in the order given, the order the Mac's clock gave them (project_steps, project_filing, projects_tab).

title: Auto De-dust rings the dust its veil shows, from one pixel to a flake whose densest pixel alone passes the window
detail: Owner's report: about 90 % of the dust got through, too big or too small, though the veil showed it clearly; on P1072734 (Lumix, 47 Mpx, 2026-08-31, the owner's dustiest frame) the veil showed 66 shapes at rest, nearly all dust, and 4 were ringed. Measured causes: 35 shapes of 1 or 2 pixels were dropped as noise (MIN_AREA 3), yet they are tiny specks or a flake's densest pixel, and noise rises in one channel, which the least channel's rise already refuses; 16 were dropped as not neutral, as the scan's blur is wider in red than in blue and an opaque speck's blue sinks to the sensor's floor under the orange mask, so a speck's jump 2 pixels off reads its blue 1.5 to 5 times its red; summed over its blur, the light a speck takes is alike in every channel (0.72 to 0.96), and so is a porcelain glint's (0.8): colour told nothing apart; 11 were too soft, their jump read 2 pixels off the part past the window, on the speck's own body. Now a shape past the window shows a speck read whole (oni-measure/src/dust/speck.rs): the pixels joined to its peak whose least channel rises over the ground (median density 12 to 14 pixels off) by half the peak's rise. It is kept when its least channel rises 0.2 at rest down to 0.1 at full sensitivity, as before; when its ground, read off the shape and again off the speck, spreads at most half that rise (dust lies on an even image at its scale, where grain, a dense sky's noise and a patch of sky among leaves spread their ground as far as they rise); and when its edge makes 0.45 of its rise within 2 pixels (dust at the scan's focus 0.46 to 1, glints and lamps, softened by the camera's lens and the film, 0.26 to 0.39). The ring and the patch cover the whole speck. MIN_AREA and NEUTRAL go. On P1072734 at rest: 35 rings holding 48 of the 66 shapes (1-2 px 19/35, 3-8 11/13, 9-32 13/13, 33-128 4/4, 129-512 1/1), 63 by full sensitivity. Against the owner's 164 hand strokes on that frame: 29 ringed at rest instead of 3 (the veil shows 38 of them at rest, all ringed by full sensitivity), 99 by full sensitivity instead of 25; the 8 rings at rest off his strokes are specks left unpainted. The 25 frames of that roll read 44, 52, 168, 239, 387 rings at 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 % before, 256, 276, 708, 949, 1390 now. The 47 clean frames (roll #8, Lumix 2026-10-30) read 1, 1, 27, 72, 776 before, 2, 3, 13, 15, 211 now; both rings at rest are real specks. Known limit: a speck across a strong edge of the image stands on an uneven ground and is left to the brush (the hook on P1073201, which the former rule kept), and a speck that passes the window only where its ground passes too merges with it. Reading a frame takes 47 to 994 ms, median 201 (205 before), the specks read on all cores. Real app, dev build, ONI_BENCH=autodust on a test copy of P1072734: 35 rings at rest, 37, 83, 122, 200 along the track, 140 to 322 us a notch on the hand's thread, REMOVE writes 35 patches in 4.5 s, and a second reading over them finds none. Checks: dust tests with twins (one pixel to a flake or a hair ringed whole, a glint's soft edge against a sharp speck of the same colour, a lamp's slow fall against a step, a bright patch among leaves against the same on an even ground, every inset counting a speck once, a speck found inside the band a deep inset merges it with), each rule disabled failing its test; dust_census now counts the shapes the veil shows by size, those a ring holds, and a sidecar's strokes by the sensitivity the veil shows each and a ring meets it.

title: A dust patch costs its own pixels, however many patches the frame holds
detail: Owner's report on P1072734 (Lumix, 47 Mpx, 164 strokes by hand): a patch took 72 ms on strokes 1-20, 172 on 81-100, 253 on 141-160, 441 at 162. Measured cause: a search renders the framed frame over its window (about 2 800 px, 4 to 8 MP) with every other patch laid, and the graph ran each laid patch's blend as a pass over the whole window, so the k-th patch paid k window passes; on a dev build the search's render went 29, 53, 110 ms on strokes 1-20, 61-80, 141-160 (7.3, 12.0, 19.5 ms per MP of window). A stage may now declare the area outside which it returns its input (Stage::area): the graph runs such a stage, unless it is the last, through where the request misses that area (no dispatch, its auxiliary inputs unread) and over the part of its area the request holds, laid onto its input's texture when nothing else reads it, else onto a copy (Run, Put). The patch blend declares its placed patch, so the canvas, the loupe, the export and a search all lay a patch at the cost of its own pixels. Owner's frame, dev build, its 164 patches made again as it opens: the search's render 23, 23, 32 ms on strokes 1-20, 61-80, 141-160 (5.9, 5.2, 5.4 ms per MP), a whole patch 40, 42, 59 ms against 52, 73, 139 (the later strokes' windows are larger); the same binary with the area withheld, 27, 50, 111 ms. Checks: twelve placed patches render bit for bit as run whole over every kind of region, with a frontier cache and with an input another stage still reads; away from every patch a render writes what it writes without them, over two patches their areas twice; twins: run whole, each patch costs the whole region, and an area a column short is seen (oni-graph tests/area.rs). A search on a 4 800 px frame costs the same with 10 or 150 patches beyond its window and more with one inside, which it sees (render/kept_tests.rs).

title: A frame's strokes stay uploaded while it renders, however many
detail: The pipeline kept the last 128 stroke rows first in, first out: a frame of 164 strokes uploaded every row again at each recipe (3 ms a search at 160 strokes on a dev build), and the canvas's rows and a search's, each at its own scale, pushed each other out. A row now stays while one of the last eight recipes names it (KEPT_RECIPES): a search after another uploads nothing (render/kept_tests.rs: no texture made; twin: after eight recipes naming none, the 152 rows are uploaded again).

title: A stroke painted while a frame's patches are made heals before the rest of the batch
detail: Owner's report: after his 162 patches were purged, the app made them again in one batch of 40 s, his two new strokes waiting behind it. The batch was a snapshot of the settings taken as it started, healed in their order. A run now reads the frame's settings as the hand leaves them before each patch and picks the next with heal::next: the newest correction without a patch, after the earlier ones whose patch lies in its search window, and theirs, earliest first, so each search still holds every earlier patch of its window, as the list's order did, and a stroke waits for those alone. A run stops after its patch once its frame is left, letting go of the full resolution it holds; a failure marks its own correction alone. Owner's frame, dev build, ONI_DUST_DOTS: its 164 patches and a dot in 9.5 s against 19.5 s; a dot painted as the batch starts healed after 6.6 s (its window's chain then holds two thirds of the batch, each one a source it may copy from), at the middle (82 of 164 made) after 2.3 s while the rest took 5.4 s, near the end (152 made) after 0.2 s; the snapshot healed a stroke after all the batch, 23.4 s after it. The 2.4 GB the owner saw are not the batch's: the footprint stays flat over a batch, 2.2 to 2.4 GB between two patches before and after, as with one stroke once the full resolution is built: the 47 Mpx decode in half floats on the GPU (374 MB) and each search's window, freed after its patch (two or three 127 MB float textures, a 121 MB readback, its CPU copy and the cost kernel's copy of it). Checks (heal/tests.rs): the newest at once, an earlier stroke in its window first and the one in that stroke's window before it; twin: one outside its window is not waited for. A batch of 120 dots healed in that order lays every earlier patch of each window; a stroke painted with the left third healed comes next, before the right's sixty; painted among them, after exactly its chain; twins: the list's order serves it last, newest first runs searches before earlier patches of their windows. Bench: ONI_DUST_DOTS paints dots at the hand's brush, ONI_DUST_DURING once that share of the frame's own patches is made, and the result names the hand's patches apart.

title: One instance's quit leaves another's dust patches alone
detail: A bench without ONI_CACHES quit and purged Caches/Open Negative Initiative/Corrections, the folder every running ONI shared, under the owner's app, which then made his 162 patches again. Each instance now keeps its patches under Instances/<FNV-1a of its support folder>/Corrections: one instance at a time holds a support folder, so the folder is its own, and a quit purges it alone and removes it once empty; ONI_CACHES still gives a check its own caches. Real app: two instances on one caches folder, the second quitting while the first made its 165 patches: the first's stayed and none was made again; its own quit removed its folder. Check (patches.rs): a purge leaves a file another instance wrote; twin: one folder shared, as before, loses it.

title: Compare's before shows the dust its patches healed
detail: Owner's call: Compare must show the before of the dedusting. Its before, the bar's reset frame (oni-core compare::reference), carried the frame's corrections, so the patches showed on both sides and the dust on neither. It now leaves them out: the after shows each patch over the dust the before still holds. Check: oni-core compare test, the reference's corrections empty, twin: the after holds its patch.

title: A click on the picture lays a De-dust patch, as a stroke does
detail: Owner's report: a single click laid no patch, only a drag did. A stroke of fewer than two points was dropped (appendCorrection's rule); a click's lone point now becomes a dot of the brush's size, its second point a ten-thousandth of the frame off, under a pixel of any scan, as a stroke holds two points. Window check dedust_grid: a click lays a correction of two points; twin: a press off the picture lays nothing.

title: De-dust's corrections as a grid of their dust and numbers; the hand on one shows it alone, with the ring of its source
detail: Owner's asks: a denser corrections panel, the number of each, and the dust in question shown on hovering its card; and the patch's source, drawn as a full orange band of the brush's width, hid the picture. The list's rows (reminder, label, keys) become a grid of the reminders, five to a row in the pane, each with its number on a badge, warm when its patch is a shifted tile (its note says so), faded while the patch is coming; the hand on a tile brings its remove key and shows that correction alone on the canvas (Dedust.hovered-row, shown), with a ring where its patch was copied from and the dashed line to it; at rest every marker shows and no source. The source band (Canvas.source-shapes) goes for that ring (source-marks). Window check dedust_grid: the hand on the second tile leaves its marker alone with one source ring and its line, twin: the hand gone, every marker and no source; removed from its tile, the others keep their numbers and none stays held. The tab's brush and its callbacks' wiring move to dedusting/hands.rs, keeping dedusting.rs and wiring.rs under the file ceiling; the catalogues lose the tab's "Generating…", the faded reminder saying it.

title: De-dust's tiles: the number under the dust, a square key beside it, small corners
detail: Owner's report: the key removing a patch was broken and hard to see, the tiles' corners too round, the numbers so large they hid the dust. The key had no width of its own in a plain parent, so it spanned its tile, a 56-point bar over the dust and the number. Each tile now holds its dust whole, with Radius.picture (4 px) corners, and under it a row: the number as a caption (orange for a plain shifted tile, its note on hover) and the key, square, flat, red under the hand (destructive), seen while the hand is on the tile. The grid check drives real pointer moves and clicks: a square key beside its number, the dust bare with the hand on the key, a click removing its own correction.

title: A correction sliding under the hand after a removal shows alone
detail: With De-dust's rows now written one by one (#1720), a removal no longer rebuilds the tiles: the tile under the hand takes the next correction while its hand state stays, so its key showed but the canvas isolated nothing. A tile whose correction changes under the hand now names it shown in turn, as any tile the hand enters. The grid check's click on a key, with real pointer events, failed on the merge and passes.

title: De-dust's grid fills its pane, the gaps between tiles belong to a tile
detail: Owner's report: the grid stopped short of the pane's edge, and the hand crossing the few points between two tiles showed every patch again for an instant. The tiles now widen to fill the pane edge to edge, as many to a row as fit at their 56-point least side, and each tile's box takes the gap after it, so the hand is always on one. The grid check measures the row against the pane, twin the least side stopping short, and moves the pointer through a gap.

title: The folded column's tabs inset from its raised face's top
detail: Owner's report: slid over the card, the left column's Archive and Projects tabs touched its top. The tree's tab bar meets the canvas card's top when docked; on its own raised face it is now inset by the column's inset, as at its sides. The layout check reads the tab's place, twin flush with the top.

title: The tree's clip on whole device pixels, no sliver past the held roll
detail: Owner's report: past the roll held at the top of the editor's column, a line of what scrolls under it still showed. The tree's box, laid by the column, can start between two device pixels; femtovg's clip then leaves the edge pixel half to the rows under the held one and half to its ground, which blend through. The clip now starts and ends on whole device pixels inside the box. The window checks' software renderer never blends the clip, so the new column_pin check reads the geometry at 1.5 device pixels a point: the held row on a whole pixel, twin the box laid between two.

title: The roll card keeps its last read while a medal's write reads it again
detail: Owner's report: a medal given from the gallery made the right column flicker. Every sidecar write dropped the roll card's frames read, so the card fell back to its reading state, its note off, until the read landed. A write now marks the read due and the card keeps the roll's last read until the new one lands. The roll card check gives a medal and reads the card's note at once, through its read and its Undo; without the change it fails.

title: Settings with the board's header, as the other sheets
detail: Owner's report: Settings did not follow the other sheets. It now has the board's header (SheetHeader.bar): the title beside its DONE key over a rule edge to edge, its footer gone, and the rule between its pages' rail and the page shown runs from that rule to the sheet's foot.

title: A notch or a zoom rebuilds no tile of De-dust's corrections, whatever their number
detail: Owner's report: zooming and moving a parameter slowed on a frame holding many patches. Measured on his 208 strokes (P1072734, M2 Max, --profile app): the interface drew a frame in 70 ms (3 ms with no patch) while Exposure was dragged, 49 ms through a pinch, in every tab but De-dust. Cause: publish_dedust kept its rows' model only when the rows compared equal, and Slint holds no two empty images equal (ImageInner's eq has no arm for None): a row whose reminder is not rendered, every row outside De-dust, never matched, so each notch and each move of the view gave the grid a new model and built its 208 tiles again, their layers with them. The models (rows, marks, sources, waiting strokes, auto De-dust's rings) are now kept and written row by row where a row changed (dedusting/models.rs, held), a row's reminder compared as made or not made (same_row), and outside De-dust nothing of the tab is built at all. After: 2.8 ms a frame under the drag, 0.9 ms through the pinch, a zoom step on screen in 9.5 ms where it took 60. Checks: models.rs, the rows that hold are left as they were and the others written, twin: rows never held the same are each written again; two rows with no reminder yet are one tile, twin: Slint's own equality tells them apart. Window check canvas_switch reads the rows with the tab shown; twin: another tab's photo writes none.

title: The drag and zoom benches time a frame once its dust patches are made
detail: ONI_BENCH=1, zoom and midzoom started as soon as the frame was on the canvas, so on a frame holding corrections they timed its patches being generated, which a launch does again as the cache is purged at each quit. They now wait until every correction has its patch (bench::healed). ONI_BENCH_DEDUST walks the zoom bench with De-dust open, its marks on the canvas, and the zoom bench reports the interface's frames through the pinch.

title: A frame's dust corrections are laid together, in passes their number leaves alone
detail: After #1720 a drag on the owner's frame (208 patches) still showed 16 images a second where a frame with no patch shows 60, and a zoom step cost the render thread 6 to 10 ms. Measured (ONI_DUST_PROBE, each render drained on the GPU): a patch was eight passes of its own (reduce twice, move, stroke, blur twice, blend, put back), each about 10 us of GPU and 5 us of CPU whatever its pixels, laid again at every new scale, and the histogram's picture and the input readings laid them all again at every notch: 1 673 and 2 548 passes a notch, 721 a pinch event with one texture uploaded a stroke. oni-graph gains the batch (graph/batch.rs, laying.rs, instanced.rs): many small images read off one source, each through its own stages of one kind, and Laid, their stages laid on an image over their own areas, in the layers their meeting asks. Each step is one dispatch for every member, a work-group depth an instance, each reading its frame and its stage's parameters from a table (the stage's own WGSL, its uniform read from a storage cell), members of far apart sizes in dispatches of their own and, past 4 Mpx, in turns. The pipeline (healing.rs) gathers a frame's patches on a sheet (Graph::gathered), its strokes' points on another, and keeps the recipe a frame's corrections make at a scale, so a notch builds nothing. Same kernels, same order: at full resolution the owner's 208 corrections render bit for bit what each laid in turn does (middle half of the 47 Mpx frame), on a reduced copy within 1e-5, Metal rounding the reduction's sums apart in the two compilations. After, same frame: 28 and 36 passes a notch for the two readings, 34 a pinch event, a notch's readings 6 ms where they took 52, a pinch event's render 1.5 ms of CPU where it took 12 (dev build); in the app (--profile app) a drag over 60 notches shows 43 images where #1720 alone left 11 (46 with no patch), the render thread 0.2 ms a notch and 0.5 to 2 ms a zoom step, as with no patch, and a pinch event is on screen in 7 ms (60 before both). A batch laid last writes the render's own output even where the region shows none of its members, as a stage does: a search's window away from every patch would else have read the frame's half floats as they lie. Checks: oni-graph tests/batch.rs, a batch against its members chained (several sizes, two pairs meeting, the edge, a member with no stage), twins: the pair laid the other way, a member's shift moved; 4 and 200 members cost the same passes, twin: chained they cost 5 each; past a turn, laid last, kept as a source and on a sheet, twin: a member left out; laid last on a source in half floats, a region no member reaches reads the source's own pixels, twin: the region beside it. oni-pipeline tests/healing.rs: the corrections laid together against each in turn at scales 1, 0.37 and 0.06 (some masks stay hard), twins: none laid, one left out, a pair turned; 5 and 200 corrections cost 6 passes at full size and 8 reduced, twin: in turn 30 and 1 200; patches past one sheet keep their order, twin across the seam, and a subset gathers nothing again.

title: One dispatch's uniform blocks are staged as one
detail: A stage's frame, parameters and auxiliary frames were staged in the uniform ring one after another, and the bind group built after them took the ring as it stood then: had the ring been renewed between two of them (one submission staging past its 4 MiB), the first block lay in the buffer the dispatch no longer bound. Never seen, as a render staged far less, but a dispatch of many instances stages tables a hundred times larger. The blocks of one dispatch are now reserved together (Graph::uniforms), each at its aligned place of one buffer.

title: The batch and De-dust's corrections laid together hold on Windows: DirectX 12's software adapter, through FXC and DXC
detail: #1722 and #1723 had run on Metal only, and their instanced shaders (a stage's frame and parameters read from storage tables of structs, a cell aligned on 16 bytes, private copies, a work-group depth an instance) reach DirectX 12 through naga's HLSL. On a GitHub runner (windows-2025, Microsoft Basic Render Driver, wgpu compiling through FXC as no dxcompiler.dll is on the PATH, which is what the shipped app does too), commit e0c139c9: the whole suite as ci.yml runs it is green, 107 binaries and 1 504 checks, then the phone link's 8 and 70, with oni-graph's batch and oni-pipeline's healing in it, 3 checks each. Those two run alone with their output shown: no shader refused; a batch lies 0 from its members chained and the corrections 0 from each laid in turn at scales 1, 0.37 and 0.06, where Metal gives 1.0e-6, then 0, 1.5e-6 and 2.6e-7; the twins lie 0.06 to 0.80 away on both; 7 passes for 4 members as for 200 (chained 26 and 1 202), 6 then 8 for 5 corrections as for 200 (in turn 30 and 1 200, then 40 and 1 600). With the runner's own DXC 1.9 on the PATH, which wgpu then picks (shader model 6): the same six checks pass, 2.6e-7 and 6.2e-8 from their references at most. The tolerance (1e-5) stays as Metal set it. Not verified: a real Windows GPU, the runner's adapter being software, whose driver may round the two compilations apart as Metal does; the whole suite through DXC; any timing on Windows.

title: A choice holding one keycap holds keycaps alone
detail: Owner's rule: where a choice has one key as a keycap, every key of it is a keycap, the others on the face of the ground they stand on. Button gains `ground`, the face of a keycap beside the one that stands out. SheetFooter's Cancel, step back and remove, a question's Cancel and answers once one confirms, and the panel header's Cancel beside DONE are keycaps on the ground's face; a choice with no keycap, as a passing notice's OK or a question of options, stays flat. Tabs alike: every tab a key raised from the hollow, the one taken on the pill's face, in place of one pill sliding.

title: The tabs back to their one sliding pill
detail: Owner's call: the tabs had nothing to change. #1725 had raised every tab as a key; the tab bar is back as it was, one raised pill sliding under the tab taken, the keycap rule holding for keys alone.

title: A footer too narrow for its keys lays its commit on a line of its own
detail: Owner's report: in French the prepare panel's footer ran past the panel, Cancel and Back now keycaps beside PRÉPARER LA PELLICULE. SheetFooter measures its keys on one line in an unseen copy of no height, so the choice never follows the lines it lays; too narrow, it lays the commit under the other keys, as wide as the room. The prepare check names the last step's key as French does: every key inside the footer, the commit under Back at the footer's width, twin one line outrunning it; with the footer forced to one line the check fails.

title: An opening decode under a reading the frame has left never lands on the canvas
detail: The opening decode's landing checked only the frame's path: a decode already running when an edit changed the reading (Positive mode, the scan profile, the passes, the primaries) installed its negative and rendered the new settings on it, and the right decode then asked no render, its revision already asked. State::wants (path and reading) now gates the landing, Ok and Err alike, and the full-resolution build's landing uses it too. The window check opening_reading holds every decode place, opens a frame, changes its scan profile before the decode lands, and compares the picture with a re-render on the frame's own negative; twin: the two readings render apart. Without the fix the canvas kept the old reading's picture.

title: The previews kept are keyed by their whole reading, not the slide flag alone
detail: A preview read under one scan profile, passes or primaries was served to an asking under another, the key holding only the slide flag. Previews::get and insert take the Reading; the editor, the thumbnails, Edit Together and the export read it so. The previews test asks a slide preview under another encoding and finds none; twin: the slide flag cannot tell the two apart.

title: A render landed takes the failure card away
detail: The canvas's failure card was cleared only by opening a photo: a frame decoded again under another reading after a failure rendered under the stale card, and Auto De-dust dropped its ask on it. A render of the open frame that lands now clears the card and the conversion offer. The layout check opens an undecodable file, changes its reading (twin: still bad, the card stays over an empty canvas), mends the file and changes it back: the render clears the card. Without the fix the card stayed.

title: A decode failure and a render failure each say their own
detail: Both went through the render delivery's error arm, which called every failure a decode one and probed the file for Nikon HE before even checking the frame was open. The opening decode's failure now goes to Ctl::decode_failed, its error compared bare so a file cut short says so (the stem prefixed to it had made that card unreachable); a GPU render failure says the frame could not be rendered and probes no file. French and Spanish catalogues carry the new text.

title: One way out of the editor, which every exit takes
detail: Leaving the editor was coded four times and only ToggleMode let its memory and modes go. Trashing the open frame from the editor kept its full resolution (up to 1.6 GB), the engine's caches, Compare, the crop or De-dust tab and Together; the ONI Trash's row clicked beside the photo kept all of them with the frame; Move Out with no frame left skipped the modes, Together and the trim. Ctl::leave_editor is now the one exit: hover cleared, modes left, the gallery shown, Together left, the full resolution dropped, the engine trimmed, the tiles published. ToggleMode, a trashed open frame (closed_if_trashed), the trash's row (open_trash) and Move Out call it; leave_editor_memory is gone and only leave_editor and the launch set the gallery. Window check full_release::every_way_out_lets_the_editor_go leaves by the trash's row and by trashing the last frame of its roll with the full resolution, Compare and the crop held, twin asserting all three held before; the masks check moves the roll's last frame out with Compare on and finds it closed.

title: A full resolution under way keeps its mark when the editor is left
detail: The editor's exit cleared the full-resolution build's mark while its decode still ran: a return before it landed asked a second FULL decode of the same RAW, about 1 to 3 s and 0.4 to 0.7 GB wasted. The mark is now the build's own, set by ensure_full and cleared by its landing, which already drops a result landing in the gallery; the load bar says Loading full resolution while it runs. Window check full_release::a_full_resolution_build_survives_a_quick_return goes out and back before the landing, a notch at once asking a render, and counts one decode asked (decode_gate::Gate::asked), the bar shown in the gallery, twin the bar gone once it lands; the old exit asked two.

title: The canvas's last render let go with the editor
detail: The last canvas-sized rgba32float render (gpu.current, about 100 to 190 MB on a Retina window) stayed referenced in the gallery, so the engine's trim could not free it. leave_editor drops it with the full resolution; the next render in the editor sets it again.

title: Move Out moves before it closes the frame
detail: Move Out closed the open frame before touching the disk, so a refused move (a full disk, a copy that differs, a volume whose Trash refuses) left the editor on a closed frame: the old image over default settings, every control editing nothing. The sidecar is now flushed first, as the move takes it to the Trash, and the frame closed only once the move succeeded. The masks window check refuses the move with a read-only FlatField Presets: the notice is said, B stays open on its own flat-field, twin a step still edits it.

title: Move Out never replaces a file at its target
detail: flat_fields::Moving::through moved the original with std::fs::rename, which replaces silently on macOS and Windows a file that took the free name after the look. It now takes oni_library::roll_folder::rename_new, which never replaces. Unit check a_move_out_never_replaces_a_file_that_took_the_free_name plants a file inside the rename step: the move is refused, both files whole; twin a replacing rename overwrites it.

title: A High Efficiency NEF counts as converted only when the DNG this run wrote reads
detail: adobe_dng::convert counted a NEF by a file named like its DNG, the whole batch included, so 'Keep the new DNGs only' could trash the only real NEF beside a cut or empty DNG, which then hid the NEF from every new offer. A run now counts the files it handed over whose DNG LibRaw unpacks (oni_decode::reads, a decode's own reading without the demosaic) and removes one that does not, so its NEF stays listed and convertible; the person's own DNG is no conversion. The synthetic mosaic DNG writer moves to oni-fixtures to serve both crates. The conversion check's stand-in cuts one DNG half way through its strip: before the fix it is returned as converted along with the person's own, after it is not and its file is gone, twin the same run with no cut counting it; a_dng_reads_unless_cut covers reads on a whole, a cut and an empty file.

title: A roll resumed on RGB Passes groups its files again
detail: A Prepare the Roll draft walked on RGB Passes set the capture on resume without grouping the files, so PREPARE ROLL measured each single-colour pass as a colour frame and wrote a roll without passes. The capture, pass order and offset now have one setter, Roll::group_as, which regroups; the first frame's capture, the draft's values and the hand's three keys all go through it. A regrouping keeps each lead's tick and flag and counts the base step's frame among the new frames; a frame's EXIF lands on the sources too; a step's waiting draft is written even when the last file to land is a pass; the draft now carries passOffset, so a roll shifted by a file resumes on its own leads; the chips' pictures are read on resume without refitting the draft's order. Check: model.rs resumes a six-file roll in landing order and finds two leads holding their passes, the first flagged, the second on its own draft, the base frame back to 0, the offset restored; twins: the capture set alone leaves six frames, the sources alone hold no flag. Against the code before, the same resume left six frames.

title: The base and the slides' white are read on the decode their frames are measured on
detail: Prepare the Roll read the base (or a slide roll's white) on the base frame's own sidecar decode, while the frames were measured on the roll's start: a slide never prepared read its white at the negative's 5000 K and cast every slide, and a lead's base was read without its passes composed. measure.rs builds every frame's start in one closure, the base frame's too, and slides.rs reads the white on roll::slide; Measurer::base decodes and reads on one settings, key::bare strips it, and key::base lost its mode, mask and stops arguments, which the start already holds. Check: slide_roll.rs decodes warm at 5000 K and grey at 5500 K or composed; the white on the slide's start asks no gains and the base on the lead's start reads the composed grey; twins decoded on the sidecar read the cast. The app's calls before the fix failed both assertions.

title: ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z typed in a field step the field's typing, not the photos' history
detail: Slint serves the menu bar's shortcuts before the focused item, so Undo and Redo, live from the history alone, took ⌘Z from every field (the gallery's info fields, the export's EXIF and names) and undid a medal or a move out of sight. They now follow the rule the digits and ⌘⌫ follow: live only while no field holds the keyboard (`keys.held`). The field_undo window check labels a photo, types in a sidebar field and presses ⌘Z: the field's text comes back, the medal stays; twin, the photos holding the keyboard, ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z step the medal. Before the fix the check fails on the medal undone.

title: The unsaved-edits sheet has a Keep for Now key
detail: The sheet said ONI keeps the edits while it runs, yet offered only Discard and Retry: with the disk away, a Retry asks again and the mouse could only discard. Its AskSheet cancel is Keep for Now, the answer -1 that keeps them in memory, translated in French and Spanish. missing_original clicks it with the disk away: the sheet goes, the edits stay held and unwritten.

title: A sheet holds the keyboard, so Escape always reaches its own dismiss
detail: Escape under a sheet went to the sheet when its key held the keyboard, else to a hand-kept Rust list that lacked Unsaved and Converting; any press gave the keyboard to the window's monitor, so after a click the unsaved sheet and the DNG conversion ignored Escape. A sheet now takes the keyboard as it shows (its scope, then its field or default key), the monitor no longer takes it on a press under a sheet nor as the sheet shows, and a refocus under a sheet hands it back to the sheet. sheet_escape shows the unsaved sheet, the conversion at work, a removing question and the notice, presses beside each card and sends Escape: each answers its dismiss; twin, the DNG choice stays. Before the fix it fails on the unsaved sheet.

title: The Rust per-sheet Escape and Return lists go
detail: escape_sheet, return_sheet and the welcome's key branch are deleted: each sheet answers Escape through dismissed and Return through its default key, or `returned` where it has none (the welcome, whose commit would scroll it away, and the library catch-up). The key path keeps one rule for a sheet: no key reaches behind it. The sheets check now expects the sheet, not the monitor, to hold the keyboard under a confirm.

title: Checks for the sheets' keyboard and a field's undo
detail: New window checks sheet_escape and field_undo, and missing_original extended: Escape after a press beside the unsaved sheet keeps the edits, the keep key keeps them, twin Return is Retry's and leaves the sheet while the disk is away. Each was run against the code before its fix and failed there.

title: A preset is written through the app's atomic write
detail: shelf::save used its own write and rename: no flush, no Windows retry, a temporary left behind on failure. It now calls oni_library::write_atomically; the check refuses a save onto a directory and finds no temporary, fails on the old code.

title: A failed takeover keeps the legacy preset list
detail: migrate archived presets.json even when saves failed. It stops at the first failed save and leaves the list for the next launch; the check with an unwritable folder fails on the old code.

title: A preset file without an id keeps one identity
detail: decode gave a missing id a random one on every read, so edits duplicated and delete trashed nothing. The id is now Id::of_bytes of the file (128-bit FNV-1a); the check on load, edit and delete fails on the old code.

title: The presets takeover moves the list out of the way before it takes anything
detail: migrate renamed presets.json only once every preset was saved and shrank it in place otherwise, so a refused shrink (disk full) or a refused rename (the file held open on Windows) left the whole list, and every preset deleted since came back on the next reload; and an element decode refused was dropped from the shrunk list, the archive then holding only the last leftovers. The list now leaves its place first, in one rename through oni_settings::atomic::renamed with its Windows retry: the first one becomes presets.json.migrated whole, a later one a staging copy read then removed. Only the elements whose save failed are written back to presets.json; a refused write leaves them in the archive alone.

title: A refused takeover never brings a deleted preset back, and the archive keeps the list whole
detail: presets/tests/takeover.rs: a_preset_taken_then_deleted_stays_deleted_when_the_disk_refuses_the_rest takes [A, B, C] with C blocked and the write-back refused, then with the rename refused (error 32), deletes what shows and reloads: nothing deleted returns and the list is whole in place or archived; twin, with the write-back allowed C comes in once clear. an_element_the_takeover_cannot_read_stays_in_the_archive: [A, X, C] with X unreadable ends with the archive equal to the list. a_list_written_again_only_adds_to_the_shelf covers the held ids. On the code before (seam only) the first reads A and B back (disk full) and A, B, C (held), the second finds the archive [C]; the fix without the write-back, with every list renamed over the archive, or without the held ids each fails one of them.

title: The view turns sharp once the hand rests, on the timer's own clock
detail: A pan or zoom stored a std Instant and started a fresh single-shot timer per event, and the ask decided coarse again from the Instant. Slint's clock counts whole milliseconds, so the timer could fire up to a millisecond before the Instant reached SETTLE: the ask saw coarse, found the view unchanged and returned, leaving the light gesture render stretched on screen until the next move. Requests.hand is now one held slint::Timer restarted at each move, and coarse is whether it runs; a single-shot timer stops before its callback, so the settle always asks sharp. One timer replaces a timestamp and N timers a gesture.

title: A window check moves Slint's clock alone: the view rests sharp after the last move
detail: The window rig's platform clock can run ahead of the real one (Rig::advance). hand_rest zooms with the wheel, sees the view asked lighter, zooms again 100 ms later, and at 150 ms after the first move still sees it lighter (twin: the rest counts from the last move); at 150 ms after the last, on Slint's clock alone, the view is asked sharp. State::coarse reads the last ask. Run against the code before #1760, it fails on the last assertion.

title: 100 % is 1:1: the frame's full size is read on the full grid, not scaled up from the preview
detail: Engine::resident built the whole chain on the preview only to read its extent, then divided by the preview ratio: the preview's own rounding, stage 0's outer cut on its grid and a tilt's one-pixel bleed made the full size off by a few pixels, so at 100 % the full-resolution render was stretched (a turned 6048x4032 frame read 4031 wide; a crop off the preview grid a column wider). The size is now stage 0's cut of the full frame's rect, oni_pipeline::geometry::extent, and the preview chain built for it is gone.

title: Stage 0 reads one plan for its render and its extent
detail: geometry::apply and the new geometry::extent share cuts(): the orientation, the rotation's box and the crop's outer frame, each with the extent it leaves, so the size the view reasons on and the pixels stage 0 cuts cannot drift.

title: Checks for the 100 % size and stage 0's extent
detail: render::view_tests renders a turned frame cropped off the preview's grid at 100 % from its full resolution: its full size is stage 0's cut of the full rect and each texel lands on one drawable pixel; twin, the preview's cut scaled up says 900 against 899. geometry tests compare extent with apply's image extent for neutral, cropped, turned, mirrored, tilted and bypassed frames at two scales, and show the preview inference off for the off-grid crop and a tilt. Run against the code before #1762, view_tests fails with 900 against 899.

title: A recipe's key names everything a render reads
detail: oni-graph's Image::key returns the last node's key from flatten, which folds in every source, stage, parameter and auxiliary image: the proof and its cube, the hand Frontier table's source, each laid patch and the custom mask. The engine's caches below a render now hang on it instead of on the settings, so nothing a render reads beyond its settings can be missed. Check a_recipe_s_key_names_its_sources_stages_parameters_and_auxiliary_images, with twins for a parameter, an auxiliary image and the source.

title: The histogram's picture follows a proof, a table or a patch, and never another frame's count
detail: Engine::counted keeps its picture by recipe key and returns the same source while the key holds, never None: a reproof, a new Frontier table or a patch landing under unchanged settings counts again. The app's Counting slot in Requests takes a picture once by id, and a count read back lands only when the slot that started it still stands, so open_photo's Requests reset drops the last frame's count and leaving a sheet counts the open frame again. Gpu.uncounted is deleted. Checks: a_proof_changed_under_the_same_settings_counts_and_compares_again, a_patch_landing_under_the_same_settings_counts_and_reads_again, a_count_lands_only_on_the_canvas_that_asked_it and the window check the_histogram_after_a_sheet_is_the_open_frame_s_own, each with its twin.

title: Compare's before is kept by what it reads
detail: The worker's kept before, keyed on path, reference settings and view, is deleted with ViewKey and View::key. Engine::before composes the reference's recipe and keeps its texture while the recipe key and region hold, so a new proof or table draws the before again and a notch never does. resident and before share Engine::composed.

title: The input distributions are kept by their recipe
detail: The worker's measured gate on path, settings and held is deleted; inputs::Read keeps the entering settings, whose windows it is read through, and the recipe key, which names the copy, the mask and every patch laid. forget_patch no longer resets the readings, as a patch read again is a new source. The app drops a reading equal to the one shown.

title: The loupe asks again whenever the canvas is asked anew
detail: State::render_anew, the one door for a proof, a table or a patch changing what renders read, now clears the loupe's asked and shown; the patch paths call render_anew instead of clearing requested_view by hand. A custom mask import changes the settings, so it needs no such door. Window check a_new_proof_draws_the_loupe_again, twin: nothing changed draws no loupe. The proof, patch and window checks were each run against the code before the fix and failed there.

title: A frame held on the canvas ends with its overlay and its photo
detail: Slint drops a grab with the overlay that holds it and sends no release, so a crop or window drag left by Return, a tool key, a disarm or a walk kept its gesture and the store held: the next Escape laid the old crop or window on the open frame, the next drag after it moved nothing, every later edit joined one undo step and the crop's badge stayed. publish_framing, which decides both overlays, now ends a gesture whose overlay it hides, and open_photo ends one before the next frame opens; end_frame_gesture is the one way out, the release included.

title: One FrameGesture replaces the gesture tuple and its cancelled flag
detail: The frame handlers move from dedusting.rs to cropping.rs beside publish_framing. Esc's spent mark lives in the gesture itself, so a new press always starts unspent and frame_cancelled goes.

title: A handle's grab ends on a cancel as on a release
detail: Grab (ds/frame.slint) ignored PointerEventKind.cancel, which a TouchArea sends as it lets go of the hand on an Exit; it now calls released, as the canvas's paint area already does.

title: A De-dust stroke goes with its overlay
detail: A stroke cut short by leaving De-dust kept its points, drawn again as a ghost on the next De-dust; publish_dedust clears it where it hides the painting overlay.

title: Window check frame_gesture
detail: A stroke and a crop drag left mid-press by Return, then a window drag left by the walk to B: no stroke drawn again, Undo after the coalescing window takes back a later mirror alone, Esc beside the photo puts back no crop, no kept-size badge, the next window drag moves, B keeps its window under Esc. Twins: the stroke under the hand is drawn, and Esc under a live hand puts the crop back. Run against the code before the fix it failed at four steps, and without open_photo's end at the walk.

title: A hand on a control is a token the thumbnails' decodes count while it lives
detail: HandDown raises State.hands when made and lowers it when dropped. The slider's drag, a scroll along a track (State.scrolling) and a plot's press (State.plot_down) each hold one, so the three paired fetch_add and fetch_update(checked_sub) go. A double press no longer lowers a count it never raised, which could take another holder's hand. Unit check: two tokens count two, dropping one counts one; twin: a token forgotten leaves its hand counted.

title: A slider's drag is one owned value with one idempotent ending
detail: Slide.start, live and resetting become Slide.drag: Option<Drag> (where the knob stood, the value under the hand, the hand's token). Ctl::let_go(f) in app/hands.rs is the release's body, taking the drag; on_release calls it. let_go_all ends every drag, the plots' press and a scroll. A double press leaves no drag, so a late drag moves nothing.

title: A walk under a held slider lands the drag on the frame it was on
detail: open_photo and move_out, the paths that leave a frame, call let_go_all first: the hand's value is applied and recorded on its own frame before the store leaves it, and the slider's later moves and release find no drag. Before, the next move wrote the old frame's start plus the hand's travel into the new frame and its sidecar, and hands stayed up.

title: The left button lifted ends a drag whose slider Slint destroyed
