detail: Slint sends nothing to a grabbing item destroyed under the hand (HidePanel, the gallery, Export, Prepare), so the drag and its hand outlived the slider: the thumbnails' decodes waited for the session and the sidecar write was held back. The winit hook in main.rs calls Ctl::lifted on every left-button release, before Slint dispatches it. Window checks slider_hand: a walk under a drag (twin: the same travel with no walk moves the open frame) and a slider taken away under the hand (twin: the drag stands after the release until lifted). Both failed with the walk's let_go_all and lifted disabled.

title: A plot's press taken away under the hand ends with the button too
detail: Gestures::release takes no plot: the double click's size comes from the plot its hold names, and it clears the band knob. editors::let_go releases the held plot or band slider and let_go_all calls it, so the walk and the lifted button end a curve, levels, wheel or saturation press as they end a slider's. Window check editors::a_curve_taken_away_under_the_hand_lets_go_at_the_button (twin: the hand stands after the release until lifted); it failed with the plots left out of let_go_all.

title: The folder menu's writes run off the window, in a gesture's turn
detail: Rename, New Folder Inside and Make a Roll (and Back to a Folder) renamed, made or marked the folder on the interface thread, outside the one-at-a-time turn and its busy bar: on a stalled share the window froze for seconds. Each now runs through on_disk and lands back on the window; the open frame's flush stays before the rename. New Folder no longer spells its made path again: the parent is a row in the archive's spelling and the name is plain. disk_turns::the_folder_menus_writes_run_off_the_window asserts each gesture is under way once asked and done once landed; twin, a refused name runs nothing. The navigator, tree_hand, told and editor_leftovers checks now wait for these gestures to land before looking at the disk.

title: A mark or a walk reads its sidecars back on its own thread
detail: After a trash mark, a restore or an undo/redo walk, the landing re-read every touched sidecar into the index, then cut the opened folder's rows and the copies, on the interface thread. library::reread does it on the gesture's thread, on a connection of its own, and the landing only lays what it hands back; the medal keys, written in place, use the same split on the window's connection. Checked by a_reread_cut_where_the_writes_ran_lays_the_marked_photo_out (twin, the index not read again still shows the photo) and disk_turns::a_marks_rows_are_read_back_off_the_window, where the row reads trashed while the window is never pumped.

title: A navigator row opens with no look at the disk; a favourite takes the archive's spelling
detail: A row click, the Open line and the navigator keys canonicalised the row's path on the interface thread, though every row is already in the archive's spelling but a favourite kept in another (the Swift app's, or through /private). The favourites' listing, already off the thread, now also spells a favourite as the archive does, and one kept otherwise follows it in favourites.json and the navigator; open_asked then opens the row as spelt. disk_turns::a_favourite_in_another_spelling_opens_in_the_archives writes a /private favourite, waits for it to be respelt and opens its row under the archive's spelling; twin, the /private spelling is not a fixed point of canonical.

title: A gesture moving or writing files owns the opened folder until it lands
detail: A folder read could survey the folder while New Roll, an undo walk or a mark moved its files, dropping the moved photos from the picks and resetting their import date, as nothing ordered the two. on_disk now supersedes a read under way and marks it owed; read_folder, the one gate every read goes through, holds any read asked while a gesture runs as owed; the landing pays the owed read once, unless it read again itself. followed also carries the survey's paths, so the archive laid before the read keeps each pair and roll. disk_turns::a_read_asked_while_a_gesture_writes_waits_for_it (twin, a read with no gesture starts at once) and a_survey_follows_a_move_with_each_path_it_records (twin, the survey left as it was pairs no sidecar).

title: A superseded read writes no row after its file read
detail: read_rows checked its token at the loop's head only, so a read inside a file read when a move superseded it still wrote its row under the old path after the move rewrote it: a ghost row and a false copy. The token is now checked just before each index write, and look_again only reads, the loop writing for both kinds of row. a_read_superseded_during_a_file_read_writes_no_row_under_a_moved_path holds the read on a pipe sidecar while the move lands; twin, a read whose token holds writes the ghost row and one copy. Each new check was run against the code before the fix and failed there.

title: Stage 0's map between the scan and the frame is one table, read by the pipeline and the canvas
detail: oni-settings::geometry::placing holds the turn and mirror table, the rotation matrix and its bounding box that oni-pipeline::geometry wrapped privately, and Geometry::frame_extent, the whole pixels stage 0 cuts (kept_pixels is its size). Placing::on_frame and on_scan carry a point between the scan and the frame stage 0 hands on, so the pipeline and the canvas cannot diverge. oni-pipeline/tests/placing.rs: a bright scan pixel lands where on_frame says on every turn, mirror, crop, 3 degrees and the bypassed crop, and comes back by on_scan; twin, the scan's fraction read on a turned frame misses it.

title: A dust patch is found under its correction and the settings upstream of it
detail: A patch is cut from the scan after the capture stops and the flat-field, yet was cached under the correction's id alone and kept by id in the engine, the measuring graphs and De-dust's sets: after a capture-stops or flat-field change, Prepare's included, a patch of the old exposure was laid as a darker or brighter square. PatchKey (id, FNV-1a of capture_stops, flat_field, mode, rgb_passes, primaries_converted, source_encoding) names the file <id>-<upstream>.tiff and keys Engine.patches, Resident, Dust.patched and unhealable; the heal writes under the settings it ran with, so a change made meanwhile leaves the frame unhealed and the existing loop runs again. inputs_tests::a_patch_made_under_one_exposure_is_never_laid_under_another: under one more stop or a flat-field the patch is neither found nor laid, under a turn and crop it is; twin, under its own settings it is laid. With id-only keys it fails.

title: Dust strokes live on the scan and are laid before stage 0
detail: A stroke was kept in fractions of the cropped, oriented frame and laid after geometry::apply, as in Swift: a crop, turn, mirror or angle, the Crop tab's uncropped view and Prepare's uncropped reading put it and its patch off the speck. Pipeline::healed lays capture stops, flat-field and corrections on the scan; framed is healed, stage 0, the reciprocal. search_region reads healed, the heal's sizes are the scan's, auto De-dust maps each found stroke through on_scan, and the canvas maps strokes, marks, waiting strokes, sources and the reminder tiles through on_frame with the frame's own geometry; a painted stroke goes through on_scan. tests/placing.rs::a_patch_painted_on_one_framing_heals_its_speck_on_every_other heals the speck on nine framings; twin, a frame-kept stroke laid after stage 0 leaves it bright; with the old order the check fails on the first framing. Window check dedust_turn: a click on a turned, cropped picture is kept at on_scan, and its marker follows a turn and a mirror; with the canvas fractions kept as the stroke it fails.

title: Sidecar format 21 moves an older stroke onto the scan once
detail: codec::VERSION 21 (STROKES_ON_SCAN_VERSION), field names unchanged. strokes_on_scan::caught_up, chained after retired_matrices in sidecar::read: a stroke before 21 under a non-neutral geometry is moved by geometry.placing(size).on_scan, the size asked of an installed lookup (oni_app::strokes_on_scan, backed by oni_decode::full_size: a LibRaw header probe with the maker's crop and flip, the container's size, a plain file's header, the green pass of RGB passes); no size known keeps the strokes as read and the photo read-only. tests/strokes_on_scan.rs: converted strokes equal on_scan and are written as 21, a neutral framing or a current file asks nothing; twin, each moved stroke lies over 0.05 from the stored one; without the conversion both checks fail. oni-decode frames::the_full_size_is_the_whole_decode_s_without_decoding matches the decode on a cropped and a turned DNG; twin, the sensor's sides differ.

title: The scan-kept stroke recorded as a departure from Swift
detail: docs/parity/hidden.md gains a departed row for the scan-kept stroke and the keyed patch, README.md names it beside the keypad's step for the owner to confirm, and CLAUDE.md lists it among the decisions that look like mistakes. The dust census example reads the stored strokes on the frame through on_frame.

title: The presets takeover only adds, and its list keeps only what failed
detail: migrate runs on every shelf reload, and a takeover that stopped partway saved the whole list again on the next one: an edit or rename made since was overwritten and its file removed as a twin, a deleted preset came back, on every gesture while one save kept failing. migrate now reads the shelf's ids once and skips any it holds, carries on past a failed save, and writes back to presets.json only the elements it could not take, archiving the list once none is left.

title: A takeover rerun keeps the edits and deletions made since
detail: a_takeover_rerun_keeps_the_edits_and_deletions_made_since takes over A, B and C with C's path blocked, edits A, deletes B and reloads: the shelf reads A edited alone; twin, once C's path is clear C comes in and the list goes. On the code before the fix it reads A and B; with the list left whole (ids skipped but no shrink) it reads A edited and B.

title: A roll regrouped after its draft resumes on its last grouping
detail: The Prepare the Roll draft was written on the frames alone, so a file that stopped being one (a lead before Shift by One File, a pass after a switch to RGB Passes) kept the draft of the grouping before; landing first on resume, it regrouped the roll on the old triplets, or left it ungrouped, and PREPARE ROLL would write the wrong passes. Roll::drafts now covers every file the roll read: a frame takes the shared draft with its own tick and flag, any other file a clear, so no file keeps another grouping's draft and none gains a sidecar for it. drafts moved to model.rs beside step_drafts. Check: a seven-file roll walked at offset 0, shifted by one, saved as save_draft writes and entered again resumes on a2 and b2 at offset 1; a roll walked on Camera then switched to RGB Passes shifted by one resumes grouped; twin, the same drafts written on the frames alone resume on a1 and b1. Against the code before, the resume came back on a1 and b1 at offset 0.

title: A check that sees a regrouping keep each frame's tick and flag
detail: The RGB resume check passed whether or not a regrouping kept the frames' places, since the draft's tick and flag were laid after the regroup, and its two twins asserted nothing a regroup did. a_regrouping_keeps_each_frames_tick_and_flag flags a lead and leaves another out by hand, changes the pass order, then the capture: both keep a1 flagged and b1 out; twin, the same regroup laid from the sources loses both. With either call to placed in passes.rs replaced by the bare frames it fails. The empty twins are replaced by a Camera draft that leaves six frames, and the checks that group take turns on the process-wide hold of triplets.

title: Prepare's model checks in a file of their own, codec checks back under their ceiling
detail: model.rs had grown to 425 lines and codec_checks.rs to 736 with the draft's passOffset: model's checks move to model/tests.rs, the draft literal in codec_checks.rs is laid on two lines, and its grandfathered ceiling comes down to 725.

title: A quit waits for the export frame under way
detail: The export's thread is kept in Writer (export_card/writer.rs) with its stop, and Ctl::last_writes, which every quit path ends in, halts it and joins it: the frame under way lands whole, ledger note included, so no hidden temporary or unvouched file stays in the export folder. Check: writer tests a_quit_waits_for_the_frame_under_way and its twin a_stop_without_the_wait_cuts_the_frame; the first was run against a stop without the join and failed.

title: The window checks' list in a file of its own
detail: The bug hunt's merges brought tests/window/main.rs to 413 lines, past the 400-line ceiling. The checks' list moves to tests/window/checks.rs; main.rs keeps the modules and the runner's call. The prepare_ending check failed once under the full run's load and passes four times of four alone: a timing flake, logged here, not a regression.

title: One writer for every file the app writes whole: oni_settings::atomic
detail: oni_settings::atomic is public and the only write-then-rename: write_with(path, writer), write_atomically(path, bytes), written(path, bytes, rename) for checks, write_private (0o600 on Unix), staged(path, bytes) for the export's create-new landing, cached_with (no flush) for rebuildable files. Each write opens a new temporary (create_new) named by the target's hash, the process, the clock and a per-process serial, so two writes of one file in one clock tick never share one; it flushes with the plain fsync trusted for sidecars, renames through the retried rename and removes the temporary on any failure. Deleted: oni_library::write_atomically (preferences, library index files, bookmarks, kept folders, projects, flat fields, thumbnails, the Frontier look, the export ledger and presets now call the shared one; replace_readable stays over it), the export's staged, phone.rs's sibling and its writer body (a folder-making wrapper stays), patches.rs's .tiff.partial (cached_with), web.rs's .part download landing (write_with), profile.rs's .part placing (write_atomically). Durability: these files move from sync_all's F_FULLFSYNC on macOS to fsync, as sidecars already were; the export still never replaces a file it did not make. oni-localsend's inbox and the decode cache (wave 2) stay out.

title: One Finder numbering: oni_library::paths::numbered
detail: paths::numbered(name, rank): the name itself at rank 1, `P107 2.RW2` past it, `notes 2` for a name with no extension. Deleted: oni_export::file::numbered (landing.rs numbers through it), flat_fields::move_out's inline loop, which named `Panel 2.` for a file with no extension, and updates.rs free_name's rsplit_once split (a feed archive name always carries its extension; only a dot-file or a trailing dot would now number differently). roll_folder::units keeps its folder rule: a folder's dot is no extension's.

title: A preset save is whole or absent, each through its own temporary; a copy is numbered without a stray dot
detail: presets/tests/writes.rs: a_save_under_a_refused_rename_keeps_the_old_file_and_leaves_no_temporary (twin: the former fixed temporary renamed bare stays behind); two_saves_of_one_preset_never_share_a_temporary runs a second save inside the first's rename and finds two temporaries and the first save whole (twin: one fixed temporary taken by the second save leaves the first's rename nothing). atomic.rs: two temporaries in one clock tick differ (twin: the stamp alone names one), a failing writer through write_with or cached_with leaves the old file and no temporary (twin: the finishing writer lands), write_private is 0o600 (twin: a plain write is open to others). paths::numbered and move_out with an extension-less name, each with the former `name 2.` as twin. phone's write check now refuses through a read-only link folder, the unique temporary leaving no sibling to block.

title: no_crate_trashes_or_removes_a_library_member fails on presets/tests/takeover.rs
detail: oni-library/tests/swift_checks.rs reads `pass` as a member name, so takeover.rs's remove_dir_all(&pass.support) and remove_dir(&pass.blocked), from #1759, are reported as deletions of library members: the check fails on canvas before #1801. Left: rename the test's binding or list it as scratch.

title: An interrupted write's temporary is removed by the next write of its file
detail: Since #1801 every temporary had a unique hidden name, so a crash or force-quit mid-write left it for good: N interrupted DNG Converter downloads left N hidden 1.8 GB files in the caches, an interrupted host key write a copy of the private key. oni_settings::atomic now names a temporary from its target alone, `.oni-<hash of the target's name>-<rank>.tmp`, the rank the lowest no write of that target in flight in this process holds (a small static set, released when the write's `Staged` drops). A write removes whatever stands at that name, then creates its own: an interrupted write's leftover is taken by the next write of its file, one at most a rank, with no folder listing, and two writes of one file in flight in one process never share. Removing before creating, rather than truncating, keeps a leftover's mode or a link at the name out of the new file. `staged` returns the held `Staged`. The per-write clock stamp and the process serial are gone. Checks: a child process quits mid-write twice, one leftover stays and the next write leaves only its file (fails on 4c6582dc: three leftovers); a write in flight keeps its temporary, its twin letting go before the rename loses it. Review points: the presets, flat-field and atomic twins now run the code under test, the private-mode twin holds under umask 077, the phone check fails at the rename on every system and as root. Known limit: a second ONI process writing the same file at the same instant can take the same temporary.

title: Both copies of the measuring window's rule agree on a grid of rects
detail: oni-measure/tests/measure_window_grid.rs runs oni_measure::window's relative, absolute, in_crop, proposal and propose against oni_settings::geometry's on a grid of 625 rects (negative, zero and NaN positions and sides), every rect in every base, crop bypassed or not, frame and sheet: bit for bit equal. Twin: the settings' former relative, which computed through a side not a number, parts from the measure's on the grid. The proof before window's copy goes (#1808); it is then replaced by fixed expectations (#1809).

title: The settings' relative reads a side not a number as the whole window
detail: oni_settings::geometry::relative tested `base.width <= 0 || … || cut.height <= 0`, which lets a NaN through and computes a NaN window, while oni_measure::window::relative, the one the measures read, returned the whole window. The settings take the measure's form, `!(base.width > 0 && … && cut.height > 0)`, so one rule can serve both (structure plan, measure-window-once). Its other reader, the Crop tool's window placing (framing.rs), differs only on a crop with a side not a number.

title: The measuring window's rule lives in the settings alone
detail: oni_measure::window kept its own relative, absolute, in_crop, proposal, propose, MEASURE_WINDOW_INSET and FULL_WINDOW beside oni_settings::geometry's, the two already parting on a NaN (#1807). They go: measurement_windows reads Geometry::measure_window_in_crop and, untouched, geometry::proposal(Rect::UNIT, false) (bit for bit the inline rect it built); Prepare the Roll's resting and laid windows (prepare.rs, entering.rs) and slide_roll.rs call the settings. window.rs keeps the rect arithmetic, contains, contains_point, intersection, measurement_windows and the sheet's cells; its two tests of the deleted copy go with it, their cases held by #1809. window.rs 65 lines shorter, no change to what a measure reads (#1806 proved both copies equal before the deletion).

title: What a measure reads, on fixed expectations
detail: oni-settings/tests/measure_window.rs replaces the equality grid (#1806): thirteen windows and bases, inside, clipped, equal to the crop, outside, touching an edge, zero and negative sides, a base of zero, negative or NaN side, each with its literal relative, its measure_window_in_crop under the crop and under a bypassed crop, and None untouched; the frame's proposal a tenth inside, the sheet's the whole crop, a placed window kept. Twins: the settings' former relative, computing through a NaN, misses exactly the two NaN rows; a bypassed crop reads the window in the frame's fractions, not the crop's; a frame's proposal is not the sheet's.

title: tokens.slint is the hand-owned source of the design system's constants
detail: The file said it was generated from the Swift app's DSTokens.swift and never to be edited, yet the Swift checkout is absent and the file was edited by hand. The header and the three README mentions now say it is written by hand, and ds/README.md names no generator.

title: The token generator is deleted
detail: crates/oni-app/src/bin/oni-tokens (656 lines, the largest grandfathered file) with its [[bin]] entry and its GRANDFATHERED line in oni-core's architecture test; the generator's own check skipped silently without the Swift sources. swift_sources() stays for the two checks that still read Swift, its doc comment no longer names the generator. editors/geometry.rs keeps its own check of the lengths against tokens.slint.

title: Tokens named nowhere are deleted
detail: 99 of the 320 DS tokens were named in no .slint, .rs or catalogue file under crates/ (matched by word, hyphen and underscore alike); they are removed, leaving 221, with no other file touched.

title: The parity row of the token generator's test reads none
detail: docs/parity/checks.md row 155 (DS.Typo.selfCheck) pointed at the generator's test, which no longer exists; it reads none and the counts become 35 partial, 10 none.

title: Sprung lives in crate::motion beside Spring
detail: editors/sprung.rs moves into motion.rs whole, its two tests with it, and the editors' Shell imports it from there. Sprung gains step(now): the knob's place for this frame, None at rest, and the frame it lands on lays the target exactly and ends the spring, which a timer drawing several knobs needs to write each one's last frame once.

title: The panel's sliders spring on Sprung and one timer
detail: Slide { shown, arrival } becomes Slide { knob: Sprung }, and Ctl.arrivals, one Timer per field (32), becomes Ctl.arrival. place(f, at) is knob.aim(at, true) and one property write; spring(f, to) is knob.aim(to, false) and starts the timer if stopped, keeping the early return that places a knob with nothing to travel; arrive() walks the slides, writes set_fraction for each stepped knob and stops once none moves. The press and the scroll along a track read knob.at(now). Deleted: the inline spring arithmetic, 31 timers, Slide.arrival. Differences no one sees: a knob never placed is placed on its first aim where it sprang from 0, and startup's first publish places every knob (jump) before any spring reaches the window; a re-aim at the same target mid-flight keeps its curve instead of restarting it, and publish skips an unchanged value anyway; a drag starts from where the knob shows now rather than from the last frame written, up to 16 ms older.

title: A block's reset springs every knob home on one timer
detail: knob_arrival::a_blocks_reset_springs_every_knob_home_on_one_timer steps Exposure, Contrast and Shadows, rests, then resets Lighting: the timer starts once for the three knobs, each lands exactly on its target and the timer stops within settle's settled_after plus 250 ms. Twins: right after the reset no knob stands on its target yet, so a placing reset is seen; the starts counted differ from the knobs moved. Starting the timer on every spring fails it (3 starts), and aiming with jump fails it (nothing springs). State::arrivals and Ctl::arriving are read by the check.

title: A spring's landing frame lays its target
detail: motion::tests::a_spring_steps_each_frame_and_its_landing_frame_lays_the_target: a placed knob steps nothing, a sprung one draws a frame between its ends, the first frame past settled_after returns the target exactly and the next None. Twin: the frame before the landing stands short of the target, so a timer stopping on moving() alone would leave the knob there.

title: The presets takeover test names no library member
detail: swift_checks' no_crate_trashes_or_removes_a_library_member reads the word `pass` as a library member, so the takeover test's local named so (#1759) read as removing members. The local is now `run`; the check passes 9/9.

title: Prepare's ending check reads the status bar once it is idle
detail: prepare_ending read the hint 0.9 s after the first frame opened, at the edge of DWELL (1 s), when the editor builds the frame's full resolution ahead and the bar, busy with "Loading full resolution", gives the hint's row to it. Under load the read slipped into that build (2 of 20 runs failed with the bar busy). The check now waits for the frame's full resolution built and the bar idle, the condition the hint depends on; the app was right. 20 of 20 pass under the same load.

title: The shell's store is the editing model itself
detail: trait Store had one implementation: State.store is now an EditorStore and Shell::new, with_window and standing take one; editors/mod.rs takes &mut EditorStore. Deleted: the trait, its forwarding impl, the default stubs and the Settings and StoreGlobal aliases, so Store names the Slint global only. changed(&mut EditorStore) -> Vec<Field> and get(&EditorStore, Field) -> f32 are free functions in store.rs; open and open_adjusted map their error to a string at the call, set_archive is set_archive_paths. Tests and benches change only the constructor argument, the Store import and the accessor of a read.

title: The shell reads the store with no absent case
detail: About 56 `store.editor()` / `editor_ref()` sites carried a None branch no run could reach, with fallback values (an empty list, false, a default scope, an Undo title with no step). They use the store directly; roll_scope's reference-only scope, the menus' fallback titles and the phone's early returns went with them. Gestures::scanner, a one-field wrapper, is the field.

title: The store's tests read it through the free functions
detail: store.rs's drag and reset tests call changed(&mut s) and get(&s, field) in place of the trait's methods, and editors/tests.rs calls the store's own apply and can_undo; no expectation changed.

title: The decode cache's code stamp covers every source a decode runs through, built by build.rs; LibRaw builds in a crate of its own
detail: cache.rs hashed a hand-kept list (pinned.c, stream.cpp, lib.rs, source.rs, camera.rs) and missed neutral.rs, m3.rs, the rest of src/ and the LibRaw version, so retuning them kept serving older decodes. oni-decode/build.rs now prints ONI_DECODE_STAMP (src/stamp.rs: FNV-1a 128 over each file's name from the crate, written with `/`, its length and bytes, sorted, hidden files aside) over src/, ../oni-libraw/LIBRAW_VERSION, ../oni-libraw/csrc and ../oni-libraw/build.rs (the compile's defines), with one rerun-if-changed a part; CODE is env!("ONI_DECODE_STAMP") and the include_str! list is gone. A build script reruns whole, so LibRaw (11 s, 34 s of CPU) moved into the new crate oni-libraw (libraw/, csrc/, LIBRAW_VERSION, its build.rs and pinned_knobs.rs, by git mv), linked through `use oni_libraw as _`: an edit of oni-decode/src reprints the stamp in about 2 s and compiles no LibRaw. Paths updated in CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/research/libraw-knobs.md and oni-measure/build.rs. cargo hakari generate was already stale on canvas (vendored notify, resvg, usvg) and its manage-deps adds oni-hack to vendor/notify, a cycle: left untouched, oni-libraw depends on oni-hack by hand.

title: The decode cache writes through oni_settings::atomic::cached_with
detail: store() loses its own part name, rename and cleanup, the seventh write-then-rename copy: oni-settings becomes a dependency of oni-decode and the write goes through cached_with (no flush, a decode is made again when lost). trim() lets stale `.tmp` temporaries go after 600 s, and the `.part` of earlier builds that share the folder. Checks: a stale temporary and a former part go, a temporary in flight stays (twin); a write stopped midway leaves the kept decode whole and its temporary is taken by the next write of the frame (twin: two names before it, one after).

title: The decoder's stamp moves with one byte of any listed file and with nothing else
detail: stamp.rs tests: one byte changed in a nested source or in the version file changes the stamp, an unchanged tree keeps it, a file outside the parts or a hidden file inside them moves nothing (twin); one tree in two folders prints alike, a renamed file prints otherwise (twin), a missing part is an error; the built ONI_DECODE_STAMP equals the stamp of today's sources (twin: the former five-file list prints otherwise). Shown live: appending a line to src/m3.rs rebuilt oni-decode alone and the built stamp followed; a line in csrc/stream.cpp rebuilt oni-libraw and the stamp followed.

title: The open frame is one Frame the state owns
detail: State's open, negative, full, reading, requests, compare, placed, full_size, tool_entry, frame_gesture, straightening and painting_stroke are one app/frame.rs Frame, State.frame: Option<Frame>; negative, full and tool_entry carry no path tag any more. Compare's befores, a session count the checks read, stays in State as befores, beside building_full, full_failed, dust, viewport, loupe, together and framing_memory. Frame::opened is the only constructor: the full resolution stays for the same path, and the last picture's place and size stay until the new frame's render lands, as its thumbnail is laid by them. State::frame_for(path) is the only stale guard and every background landing goes through it (the opening decode, the full build, a render, a histogram count, the input distributions, a heal run and its patches, the loupe, a mask taken, a dust reading, the hovered preset's balance, the roll's requirement); wants(path, reading) is built on it. Ctl::close_frame is the only close (a frame trashed, a frame moved out to FlatField Presets): it lets a held crop handle go and takes Compare's split off the canvas with the frame. leave_editor calls frame.release_full(), redecode frame.reread(reading). toggle_compare's canvas half is show_split. What the structure alone changes: a frame closed leaves no place, full size, histogram or count behind, so the next opening lays its thumbnail at its own size; between an opening and its decode the Roll tab reads no undeclared encoding off the frame left; a crop handle held as its frame is trashed is let go at the close, not at the next opening. app.rs 479 to 465 lines, its ceiling 519 to 465; twelve State fields gone, two added.

title: A frame trashed or left owns nothing on the canvas
detail: tests/window/frame_owner.rs: after the open frame, alone in its roll, goes to the ONI Trash, placed() and full_size() read None (twin: both read Some before). A preview decode of A landed by hand (Ctl::opening_decoded) while B is open, every decode place held so B's own full resolution waits, keeps no full resolution and leaves B's size on the canvas after a notch; twin: the same decode landed under B's path and reading is installed, kept as the full resolution and lays A's size. With the landing's frame_for and wants guard removed the check fails on its first assertion.

title: Another frame opened finds only the last picture's place
detail: app/frame.rs: Frame::opened on a previous frame keeps its full size and nothing decoded or asked (negative, full, requests); twin: opened with no previous frame it guesses no size.

title: The headless check counts 28 tiles of the 38-frame test copy
detail: With ONI_RAW_DIR on the test copy of roll #8 (38 NEFs), headless::the_window_opens_roll_8_and_a_slider_drives_the_canvas failed at 'every cell of the roll is laid out': 28 tiles against 38. The app is right and the check was stale: see #1836.

title: #271's detail says what the opening resets
detail: #271 said the opening reset Requests, Dust and Compare whole; it resets Dust and Requests, Compare's split is turned off by leave_modes and befores counts across photos. The detail now says so, and where #1830 moved them.

title: Hakari unifies every command again, with no cycle through the vendored crates
detail: oni-hack's generated path to the patched vendor/notify made cargo adopt it as a workspace member, so `cargo hakari manage-deps` wired oni-hack into notify, a cycle; the workspace now excludes vendor/. The phone-link crates and oni-keys were traversal-excluded, so the features oni-app and oni-core pull through oni-link and oni-keys (serde alloc, tracing attributes, getrandom sys_rng, tokio...) were missing from oni-hack and `cargo test -p oni-settings` rebuilt slint and wgpu after `cargo build -p oni-app`; they are now final-excluded only: traversed, yet never wired to oni-hack, so no phone build sees it. generate, manage-deps and verify are clean; after `cargo build -p oni-app`, `cargo test -p oni-settings --lib --no-run` compiles oni-settings alone.

title: The headless check walks the gallery to meet every cell of a roll taller than its view
detail: Cause of #1833: the gallery gives Slint only the cells in view and one row either side (Layout::cells, since #11), and since #1095 (84dbbbe6) it opens on four columns. In the check's 1280 by 800 window the grid is 680 by 662 pt: at six columns the 38 frames took 601 pt and were all laid, at four they take 1178 pt and 28 are laid (seven rows), so the check's count of the laid tiles held on the ten-frame fixture and failed on a tester's whole roll from #1095 on, not from #1830. The check now scrolls the grid from top to bottom, waits for each laid cell's picture and meets every cell once, in index order, before counting and reading each face. Twin: where the content passes the view and a row of slack each side, the top's cells alone fall short (28 of 38), and a walk that never scrolls fails the count (28 against 38). Two more stale expectations met on the same runs: library::tests::roll_8_opens_as_one_named_roll_of_its_photos counted the contact sheet, which #1252 leaves out of the roll's photos (39 against 38), and now counts frames by the sidecar's sheet as the headless check does; the gallery_cell checks wrote their shots into a folder nothing made in a fresh target, so common::rig makes its shots' folder and the 124 checks' own create_dir_all go.

title: The folder shown is one Folder the state owns, the folder asked its heading
detail: app/folder.rs: Folder { path, rows, survey, copies, staged, read_done } replaces State.opened, rows, survey, copies, read_done and org.staged; State.folder is the folder the archive shows, State.heading the folder asked whose read has not landed. open_spelt sets the heading and leaves the shown folder whole; take_rows on a current read assigns a whole Folder and clears the heading. State::opened() (heading, else shown) serves the navigator's row, the openedFolder preference, the watches, Refresh, the banner, the load bar's condition and read_again; State::shown() serves the archive's lay, the band, the medal's reread (on the window and off it), the survey's marker and folder writes and the member rolls. read_done() is the asked folder read whole. The fresh unfold is taken by the first lay after the heading lands. Seen through it: a medal given while another folder's read ran reread the rows under the folder asked and laid them with the old survey; it now rereads the shown folder's rows under its own path. fingerprints stays in State, the tile keys of every surface (the ONI Trash's and the projects' too).

title: One Ticket type numbers the folder reads and the thumbnails' pass
detail: ticket.rs: Ticket (next, supersede, standing) and Asked (current). State.reads replaces the static READS and the read half of State.generation: open_spelt and followed supersede it, every read takes next(), the read thread and take_rows test current(). State.folder_turns replaces generation's other half: a folder opened or moved stops the thumbnails' pass and a settling read; fill takes standing(), so a read again leaves the pass running as before. Two tickets, not one: merging them would stop the pass at every read again.

title: A folder asked keeps the one shown whole until its read lands
detail: window check folder_owner: B asked while A shows, B's landings held unpumped: opened() is B, shown() A, the load bar counts A's 3 rows; a medal on A2's tile rereads A's rows under A's path, A's tiles and the bar stay, the medal shows; released, the first landing makes B asked and shown with no tile of A. Twins: the same rows reread under B's path hold none of A's; A2's tile is gone once B lands. With the medal's reread under the folder asked the check fails at 'the medal lands on A's tile'.

title: An ask stays current until a newer one or a supersession
detail: ticket::tests: next() and standing() current until another next() or supersede(); twins: the older asks read stale. architecture.rs: app.rs's ceiling lowered to 463.

title: Refresh tells what moved against the folder shown
detail: Review of #1840: ⌘R pressed while another folder's read was under way kept the shown folder's rows as the before and told the difference against the folder asked once it landed. Refresh now keeps a before only when the folder asked is the one shown. The folder_owner check loses a twin that ran nothing of the app (the mutation run already showed the check fails with the reread under the folder asked).

title: library/tests.rs back under its ceiling
detail: #1836 brought crates/oni-app/src/library/tests.rs to 401 lines; the roll #8 test folds its skip and its frame filter.

title: The panel's tab is a Slint enum
detail: PanelState.tab was an int that tabs.rs named ROLL to DEDUST while the Slint panes, the bar, the canvas and Rust (cropping, loupe, dedusting, menus, lab, plots, the benches and about a hundred check sites) compared 0 to 4. PanelTab { roll, crop, color, details, dedust } replaces it everywhere: tab-picked takes it, Route.shown and last_panel are PanelTab, tabs.rs loses its constants, and the tab bar's index tables become explicit conditionals. No tab number reaches oni-link (its own Tab) or the preferences.

title: The Info column's kind is a Slint enum
detail: Library.info-kind was set by the literals 0 to 4 in info_sidebar.rs and compared by them in the sidebar and the checks. InfoKind { none, roll, project, trash, collection } replaces them.

title: The roll's state is a Slint enum
detail: PanelState.roll-state was 0, 1 or 2 across rolls.rs, the Roll and Color panes and a check. RollState { alone, prepared, finding } replaces it, prepared the default as 1 was.

title: A slider's field index is checked against its Store fraction
detail: The 32 sliders of the panes name their field twice, `field: N` and `fraction: Store.<stem>-fraction`; a shifted index drew one field's slider on another's value with nothing failing. A source check reads every pane and asserts Field::from_index(N).slint_name() equals the stem, no `field:` standing without a fraction; its twin shifts Exposure's index and must be caught.

title: Checks and benches name tabs, kinds and states by variant
detail: The window checks and the crop and loupe benches set and read PanelTab, InfoKind and RollState variants where they wrote 0 to 4. #290's detail is corrected: the tab, the info kind and the roll state are enums; the sheets and the mode stay its work.

title: Supersession by Ticket in the group, trace and prefetch work
detail: Edit Together's group counter, the histogram and input trace counters and the neighbour prefetch's counter were statics beside Ticket; each is now a Ticket in State.asks (ticket::Asks), the threads taking an Asked and testing current().

title: The export card's supersession by Ticket
detail: The export card's pass, weighing and lines' reading counters and the paper page's reads are Tickets; every landing takes an Asked and tests current().

title: The preset form's serial and Report a Bug's round by Ticket
detail: shelf.serial and the report round are Tickets (Ticket::count keys the form's instance); the delayed write and the post answering a closed sheet test an Asked.

title: Ticket equality and count checked with their twins
detail: Asked equals itself and no later ask; the count moves with each ask and supersession.

title: app.rs ceiling lowered to 462
detail: The tickets moved into one Asks field of State, which leaves app.rs one line shorter.

title: Clippy installed as a lint gate: scripts/lint
detail: [workspace.lints.clippy] all = warn, every workspace crate opts in, and scripts/lint runs clippy on all targets with warnings denied; not part of scripts/check. Lints that fight the style or would touch float arithmetic are allowed once, at workspace level, with a reason.

title: Clippy findings fixed without touching arithmetic
detail: Copy clones, slice refs, Default impls, merged branches and the like; oni-pipeline, oni-render, oni-colour and oni-measure change only in Copy clones of two tests and their lints opt-in, never a float expression.

title: Dead functions removed
detail: roll_folder::name_for, History::redo_label, oni-keycap panel_button, scanner_key, plate_radius, release_motion, and the PanelHeight and TEXT_ON_FILL they left unused, plus two unused test helpers.

title: Architecture ceilings refreshed and a width ratchet
detail: GRANDFATHERED holds today's sizes without entries under 400; the count of Rust lines over 200 characters may only fall from 86, with a twin that counts a wide line.

title: CLAUDE.md names scripts/lint
detail: One line in the Build section.

title: Swift is dead: no rule imposes its behaviour
detail: Owner's call (2026-11-12): the Swift app is totally deprecated and every rule imposing a behaviour that comes from it is killed. CLAUDE.md no longer asks for a strict behavioural copy of Swift's result, Swift parity, proof against Swift's outputs, Swift-format sidecars or Swift attributions; docs/parity/ is history. Kept: reading the sidecars a person already has, Swift-written included, as their data.

title: The export surface takes every key: none reaches the editor or the gallery behind it
detail: Ctl::key answered Escape on the export surface and let every other key through: an arrow walked to another frame or moved the crop, Return applied the measuring window or opened a tile in the editor, Space left for the gallery and ⌘A picked the roll, all hidden. The router now gates the surface whole, as it gates Prepare: Escape closes its sheet or leaves it, any other key goes to Slint. export_escape no longer reads `shown`. Check: window export_modal, its twin the same keys acting once the surface is gone.

title: The menus go dark behind the export surface, as behind Prepare and a sheet
detail: publish_menus had a block for Prepare and one for a sheet, but the export surface only narrowed a few items through `modal`: Undo, Redo, Reset Settings, a preset, Paste, Mirror, Prepare the Roll and the rest kept editing frames the export had captured. One block now keeps only Open, Export, Refresh and the screen-gamut view on the surface; every scattered `!modal` term goes, and act()'s ToggleMode arm for the surface with them. Check: window export_modal (the menu's live flags, ⌘Z, ⇧⌘M and ⇧⌘R moving nothing; twin: ⌘Z takes the mirror back once the surface is gone).

title: The phone's presses land nowhere while the export surface covers the editor
detail: The phone link applied its steps, slides, faces and undos to the store behind the export surface. Link carries `covered`, set by phone_event from the surface, and a press then changes nothing while the phone is still told it was taken. Check: tests/link.rs a_press_while_the_host_covers_the_editor_lands_nowhere, its twin the same press landing uncovered.

title: Prepare the Roll never opens over the export surface or a sheet
detail: enter_roll, the one way into a roll (its key, a bare frame's requireRoll, the DNG conversion), never checked the export surface: Rolls > Prepare the Roll stayed live there, and a roll asked for just before ⌘E landed on top of it. enter_roll now refuses while Ctl::covered() (the export surface or a sheet), the predicate the Finder drop reads too; the menu item goes dark with #1871. Check: window export_modal (Prepare then Export in one turn: no roll after 1.5 s; twin: Prepare alone comes within it).

title: Every file written heals its strokes: an export or a contact sheet makes the patches not on disk
detail: A render lays only the patches on disk, and only the editor's open frame made them, so an export after a relaunch (patches purged at quit), after a roll-wide change of what they are keyed on, or of strokes never opened wrote the frame with its dust back and said nothing. The editor's heal loop is now one function, heal::ensure, with heal::pending; render_full_beside (the export, write_one included) runs it on the frame's whole decode before rendering, and the contact sheet runs it ahead (export::heal_ahead) for frames lacking a patch, decoding them whole only then. A patch that cannot be made fails the file with Failure::Dust, translated. render_full, which lays only what is on disk, is left to the tests. Checks: export/heal_tests.rs an_export_heals_strokes_whose_patch_was_never_made (never made, then purged as at a quit) and a_contact_sheet_heals_strokes_whose_patch_was_never_made, each with the bare render as its twin; both seen failing with the heal left out.

title: A heal run ends with the full resolution it cuts on
detail: The run's hand-off lived in Dust.healing beside the frame, and only another photo opened ended it: a close, a release on leaving the editor or a reread kept it going, holding up to 1.6 GB on the GPU, and after a reread it cut patches on the old decode and filed them under the new reading's key. The frame now owns its run (Frame.heal, a Healing whose drop ends the run) beside full: reread, release_full, a close or another frame let both go together, and the same frame opened again keeps both. Dust.healing and the stop in Dust::next_photo are deleted; State::healing reads the open frame's run; a run's end clears the frame's only when it is the same run. Check: frame.rs a_heal_run_ends_with_the_full_resolution_it_reads (reread, release, another frame, a close; twins: a frame held or opened again keeps its run), seen failing with the reread and release lines left out.

title: Reading lives in oni-settings, with its stamp
detail: render::Reading (the decode's choices: primaries converted, source encoding, RGB passes, slide) moves unchanged to oni_settings::Reading, re-exported by render, and gains stamp(), FNV-1a over its JSON, so the decode and the dust patch key can read one value. No behaviour change; the key moves to it in #1878.

title: Dust patches lie on the decoded scan, keyed on its reading alone
detail: Pipeline::healed lays the corrections first (Pipeline::patched, now public), then the capture's exposure and the flat-field, and the search reads Pipeline::patched, never a gain. PatchKey.upstream becomes PatchKey.reading, the stamp of oni_settings::Reading (PatchKey::under stamps once; corrections::upstream is deleted), so capture_stops, the flat-field and a Negative/Monochrome switch no longer re-key a patch: a flat-field Amount, Temperature or Tint drag no longer drops every patch while it moves nor heals the whole frame after, and no superseded generation piles up until quit. Both stages are per-pixel gains and the heal is linear in its scan, so the only change in a render: under a flat-field a patch takes the gain of the place it lies on instead of its source's, and under a capture exposure it moves by float rounding alone. Renders with dust corrections under a flat-field or a capture exposure therefore move slightly, inside the patches only. Sidecars are untouched; patch files of earlier builds are never found and go at the next quit. Checks, each seen failing on the former order and key: corrections.rs a_patch_key_reads_the_decode_alone (twin: each decode choice re-keys), oni-pipeline/tests/healed_order.rs a_patch_takes_the_gains_of_the_place_it_lies_on (twin: the former order gives 6, not 3, under a stop), inputs_tests a_patch_follows_the_exposure_and_flat_field_it_sits_under (rewrites the #1786 check; twin: another reading finds none), heal/tests.rs a_patch_scales_with_its_scan (twin: a curve is not a gain), window flat_drag::a_flat_field_drag_keeps_every_patch (20 Amount notches: no heal, no pending row, the same 3 files; twin: Positive cuts 3 more).

title: CLAUDE.md states where a dust patch lies and what keys it
detail: The dust stroke decision no longer says a patch's file names the exposure and flat-field; a new line says a patch lies on the decoded scan before the capture's exposure and the flat-field, keyed on the reading alone (#1878). docs/parity/ is history (#1865) and is left as it is.

title: A contact sheet on a paper lays each frame's Paper Correction on its own tile
detail: The sheet's file laid frame 1's correction on every pixel (contact.rs passed it to file_bytes once), while the panel shows each frame under its own. together::printed now takes the export space and, on a paper, lays each frame's gains on the pixels its tile was drawn on, the gaps, numbers and logo none; the whole-file step gets no correction. Checks: print.rs a_frames_correction_is_laid_on_its_tile_alone (twin: frame 1's gains on the whole band move tile 2 and the gaps) and window sheet_paper::each_frame_of_a_sheet_on_a_paper_takes_its_own_correction (failed before: tile 2's blue 78 against 177; twin: frame 1's own tile moves). The engine-fallback double proof the finding named is unreachable: apart() fails only on a poisoned engine, which the fallback is too.

title: The export date is the line's alone: a cleared Date writes none
detail: file_bytes fell back to the scan's capture date whenever the line's date was empty, so a cleared field still wrote 306 and 36867. The separate date argument is gone from oni_export::write, file_bytes (and its now unused source path), encoded and metadata::stated: the date is ExifMetadata.date like every other field, empty writes no tag. The line still opens on the scan's date (opening_row). Check: oni-export tests/dates.rs a_cleared_date_writes_no_date_even_from_a_dated_source (failed before; twin: the source carries a date a fallback would leak).

title: A typed date reaches the file in EXIF's nineteen characters
detail: dated::exif only swapped the dashes, so 2026-09-14 reached EXIF as ten characters and words verbatim. It now returns the 19-character form for a day dashed or in colons with an optional HH:MM[:SS] (midnight when none), empty for empty, nothing otherwise; a keystroke that reads as no date keeps the line's last. The field let go (Return or focus leaving) calls Exporting.date-settled and shows the line again, so it shows what the file will carry. Checks: dated.rs a_typed_date_reaches_the_file_in_exifs_nineteen_characters (twin: the old dash swap fails the EXIF shape); export_panel window check types words over the date and Return shows the date back (fails without the re-show).

title: The contact sheet carries the first line's date
detail: write_sheet built its metadata from the first line's artist and copyright and let the scan's capture date fill in. sheet_metadata now keeps the first line's artist, copyright and date, never a camera, lens, ISO or film. Check: contact.rs a_sheet_states_the_first_lines_artist_copyright_and_date_alone (failed on the former construction; twin: an empty first date gives the sheet none).

title: An export cut short takes no name and leaves no hidden temporary
detail: file::create held the destination with an empty create_new placeholder before renaming over it, so a process killed in between left a 0-byte file that later read as an original; and a cut write's .oni-<hash>-<n>.tmp was reclaimed only by a later write of the same name. create now renames the staged bytes where nothing stands in one step through roll_folder::rename_new (renamex_np RENAME_EXCL on macOS, a look before the rename where a volume refuses the flag, as frame moves already do), and file::put first calls the new atomic::reclaimed on its folder, which removes every temporary no write of this process holds. Checks: file.rs an_export_cut_short_takes_no_name_and_its_leftover_goes_at_the_next_export (a child quits before the rename; failed before on both halves; twins: an empty placeholder reads as an original, a file standing at the name is refused and kept); atomic.rs a_folder_reclaimed_loses_every_leftover_and_keeps_the_writes_in_flight (twin: only temporaries' names go).

title: Windows update: the new ONI.exe is laid before the app quits
detail: update_install::windows only wrote a PowerShell script and spawned it, then the app quit: write access, unpacking and the swap were first tried by a helper with no way to report. A Program Files install (oni.iss allows it) without rights relaunched the old build in a loop, with no word. `lay` now unpacks the archive's ONI.exe in process (the zip crate already in the workspace), writes it as ONI.exe.next, renames the running ONI.exe to ONI.exe.previous (Windows renames a running image) and the new one into place; any failure leaves ONI.exe as it was and returns Err, which reaches the existing 'install by hand' message. A helper that cannot be spawned puts the old one back. Checks on every system: a folder named 'Apps [portable]' takes the new bytes and keeps the old as .previous; twins: an archive without ONI.exe and a folder closed to writing leave it untouched; a lay that does nothing fails both.

title: Windows update helper: no wildcard path, the process it started judged, itself deleted
detail: SWAP_WINDOWS kept only what the helper alone can do: wait for the app, start the new ONI.exe, keep it if the process it started still runs after $Wait ms (8000), else put .previous back and start it. Every path goes through .NET calls ([IO.File], [Diagnostics.Process]), which read no `[` or `]` as a wildcard; no path-spelling compare decides liveness; the script deletes itself. A helper blocked by policy now leaves the new build in place for the next launch. A Windows-only check runs it in a bracketed folder with cmd (stays) and hostname (ends) as stand-ins; it waits for the Windows CI.

title: An offline network share reads as a disk away, not a file gone
detail: On Windows a path on //server/share was on no volume, so absence::refusal took the system's NotFound (ERROR_BAD_NETPATH 53, ERROR_BAD_NET_NAME 67) as Gone: 'Not found, moved, renamed or deleted', Locate and Remove from Library, and Locate forgot the share's rows. Computer::volume_root now names a share's root, //server/share (never a server alone nor a device path), so its root not being a folder reads as Unplugged. Checks: a share's root on a Windows computer, twins for the home's drive, a server alone, a device path and the Mac; refusal of NotFound on a share is Unplugged, twin Gone on the home's drive (fails before the fix); a Windows-only check names the system's mapping of 53 and 67, twin 5.

title: One definition of a disk that comes and goes
detail: absence::volume_root became Computer::volume_root and every caller (refusal, bookmarks, reach's caption, the locate window check) uses it; index pruning drops its own `starts_with("//")` and asks volume_root, so a share's rows wait for its read as everywhere else. is_on_volume keeps meaning a disk Computer's rows list, which no share is. Check: a share whose folder lists keeps its row while the home's is pruned; dropping the share case fails it.

title: The last render's full size is the canvas's, kept across a close
detail: State.full_size, beside the viewport whose scale it is counted in, written by lay when a render is placed and never cleared; Frame loses full_size, and Frame::opened carries only the same frame's full resolution, its place starting empty. A frame trashed or moved out no longer takes the size with it, so under Keep Zoom the next frame's thumbnail lies at its photo's size, not its own pixels. #1830's 'the next opening lays its thumbnail at its own size' is withdrawn; app.rs's ceiling goes 462 to 464 for the field.

title: A trashed frame leaves its size to the canvas; the next is laid at the kept zoom
detail: frame.rs: another frame opened takes no place from the last, twin a placed frame holds its place. Window: a_trashed_frame_leaves_its_size_to_the_canvas_and_no_place (was ..._no_place_or_size_behind); the_frame_after_a_trashed_one_is_laid_at_the_kept_zoom at 100 % with every decode place held, B's thumbnail 2400 wide, twin the thumbnail's own width under it. Both failed on the unfixed code (320 wide, size None).

title: An export keeps in the sidecar only the EXIF fields a hand set
detail: The line shown is the sidecar's fields laid over the scan's facts, the roll's body and stock and the artist and copyright remembered, derived at every opening (export::opening_line, replacing opening_row and its early return); an export keeps the line beyond what derives (Line::typed against the artist just remembered, export::keep_line, the one set_exif caller). A roll's stock or body set after an export now reaches that frame's line. ExifMetadata gains over and beyond. Same format; a full block from an older sidecar reads as typed. Limit: a derived field cleared by hand cannot be kept, it derives again.

title: set_exif writes nothing for an unchanged line
detail: The same EXIF as on file, an empty one beside no sidecar included, returns before writing, so exporting a never-edited frame with nothing typed gives it no sidecar.

title: Kept lines follow their roll; no sidecar for an empty line
detail: oni-settings: over and beyond round-trip, twin a blanked field comes back derived; an empty line gives an untouched frame no sidecar, twin a field writes one. oni-app export::line: a kept line follows its roll and a film picked by hand stays, twin the whole line kept freezes the body; the first line's artist is not frozen, twin against the earlier artist. Each failed on the unfixed code.

title: A hidden column's reveal ends with its column
detail: The reveal flags lived on the window while their column existed only as long as it floated, so the Opt+Cmd shortcuts, the gallery, export, Prepare the Roll or the trash brought a column back slid over the photo. The flags now clear whenever the column starts or stops floating (library-floats, panel-floats name its one condition), and the column keys' column-toggled callback, which cleared them at one caller, is gone. Check: a_column_removed_while_revealed_comes_back_hidden, with live-reveal twins.

title: A flush records a lifted hand's step before it writes
detail: EditorStore::flush recorded nothing of a step whose hand had lifted and still waited SETTLE_DELAY, so an export (and a quit, a file move, a folder rename) read the frames together and the roll without it. flush now settles that step first, a hand still down being left alone, and export_now flushes before it reads its targets. Check: a_flush_records_a_lifted_hands_step_on_the_frames_together_a_hand_still_down_is_left_alone, with its twins.

title: The second-launch refusal goes through the log's one writer
detail: instance::refused wrote the support folder's path, account name included, straight to stderr; it now says the notice through timing::shown, which scrubs every line, and leaves the path out. Check: only_the_log_writes_stderr (no source but timing.rs writes io::stderr, with a planted twin) and the second-instance launch check asserting the line names no folder.

title: A Scanner slider's hand is owned by the hands
detail: The Scanner sliders held the store with a bare hold and release, outside the hands, so a slider destroyed under the press (Escape, the face turned, the gallery, the panel hidden) left the store held: later edits merged into one undo step and the bar's Undo lagged. The hold is now a hand beside the scroll and the plot (hands::Down, which also shrinks app.rs), counted for the thumbnails and lifted with the button wherever the slider went; a normal release now also publishes. Check: a_scanner_slider_taken_away_under_the_hand_lets_go_at_the_button.

title: Measure checks stop reading Swift's dumps
detail: The roll #8 measure checks that compared with Swift's decode dumps, its written filters and roll reference, and its measure.json are removed; the second-press and pipette checks stay on LibRaw's decode of two frames.

title: Pipeline and decode checks stop comparing with Swift renders
detail: The roll #8 render comparison and the decode comparison against Swift dumps are removed; the adversarial branches now assert each reaches the render on LibRaw's decode, with the frame at rest as twin.

detail: The extended probe checks, the Swift help-string check and swift_sources() are removed; the Roll tab's block order is pinned on ONI's own titles.

detail: adversarial-dump, extended-dump, frontier-swift-dump, swift-probe, decoder-gap, sensor-colours and the decoder_gap example, which rendered Swift pairs, are removed; look_lab_strip no longer compares with Swift's render.

detail: ONI_REFERENCE and ONI_ADVERSARIAL leave oni-fixtures and the README; docs/parity/README.md is marked as history.

title: A line left alone is not pinned to the artist remembered before
detail: Line keeps what derived at its opening; Line::typed keeps a field only when it differs both from that and from what derives under the artist and copyright the export just remembered (ExifMetadata::beyond over several derived lines). Changing the first line's artist no longer writes the old remembered artist into the sidecar of every other frame, nor gives a sidecar to frames nobody touched.

title: A sidecar keeps an EXIF field cleared by hand
detail: The sidecar's exif block is TypedExif (oni-settings sidecar/exif_line.rs): each field optional, an absent key derives at each opening, an empty one was cleared. A block written whole by an older build or by Swift holds every key, so it reads as set in full and an artist, copyright or scanning camera cleared there stays cleared; an export keeps it as an empty key. No version bump: what was readable means what it meant. ExifMetadata stays the line an export writes; TypedExif::over lays the block over what derives.

title: The EXIF line: a line left alone and a cleared field
detail: oni-app export::line: a_line_left_alone_is_not_pinned_to_the_artist_remembered_before (twin: the diff against the new artist alone pins the old one) and a_field_cleared_by_hand_stays_cleared, from a block written whole and from a clear typed now (twin: a block without the key derives the artist); both failed on the code before (Alice pinned, the cleared artist came back). oni-settings: a cleared film round-trips, twin without its key it derives; a block written whole keeps its cleared fields, twin a sparse one derives the rest. The line tests' scratch folders are removed under a name the member-deletion check accepts. Window export_window: the artist typed on the first line is remembered, not kept in the sidecar; the film picked is.

title: A date read from a sidecar or a scan reaches the file in EXIF's nineteen characters
detail: #1882 settled only the typed date: a sidecar's stored date (a day kept in colons by an earlier build, words from an older one) and a scan's own malformed DateTime reached tags 306 and 36867 as they stood. The rule moves to oni_settings::exif::date_of, applied where a date is read, once: ExifMetadata's date deserialises through it (every sidecar read, envelope and decode alike), scan_metadata settles the scan's, and the field's keystrokes call it; what reads as no date is none, and the writers write the line as it stands. Checks: oni-settings exif a_sidecars_date_is_settled_as_it_is_read (failed before: 2026:09:14 kept; twin: the plain JSON keeps ten characters) and a_date_reaches_a_line_in_exifs_nineteen_characters (moved from dated.rs); oni-export tests/dates.rs a_date_read_from_a_sidecar_or_a_scan_reaches_the_file_in_exifs_nineteen_characters (failed before on the scan; twin: a line that skipped the reading writes its ten characters).

title: The Date field keeps the words being typed through a line published again
detail: A typed day is stored with its midnight, so a preview or size landing that republished the line while the field held the focus replaced the words with the stored form and the time typed next was lost. While edited, the Date field's value is its own text; let go by Return or by the focus leaving, Exporting.date-settled publishes the line and the field shows the date the file will carry. Check: window export_panel types 2026-09-15, publishes its line again as a landing does (publish_line), then types 10:30 and Return: the field reads 2026-09-15 10:30:00 (twin: the line published meanwhile carries 00:00:00; failed before with 2026-09-15 00:00:00 in the field); a click elsewhere settles as Return does.

title: A new export or a moved frame never replaces a file appearing at its name on Windows
detail: rename_new fell back to a look then std::fs::rename, which Windows makes with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING, so a file landing between the two (a sync client, another ONI) was replaced. Windows now renames through MoveFileExW without that flag, under a \\?\ path past MAX_PATH, refused in one step; the look stays only for macOS exFAT and SMB volumes, which refuse RENAME_EXCL and offer no refusing rename, and file::create's doc names that limit. Check: roll_folder::carry a_rename_onto_a_taken_name_is_refused_and_the_file_there_kept (twin: the plain rename replaces it); on macOS it passes through RENAME_EXCL, the Windows path compiles and passes clippy for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc but awaits a Windows run.

title: A reclaim takes only temporaries no writer holds, once a folder a run
detail: atomic::reclaimed knew only this process's writes, so another ONI's sidecar save in the folder lost its temporary; it held the in-flight lock over the listing and every removal, and file::put listed the folder again at each frame. A staged temporary now stays open and locked until dropped (created locked with O_EXLOCK on macOS, locked just after elsewhere), and reclaimed removes only a temporary whose lock it can take, which the system frees when a writer dies; it takes no in-process lock. put reclaims a folder at its first export of the run. Checks: atomic a_temporary_another_process_holds_is_never_reclaimed (failed before; twin: let go, it goes) and file an_export_cut_short_takes_no_name_and_its_leftover_goes_at_the_next_export (a leftover laid after the folder's first export stays; twin: a folder not yet exported to loses it).

title: Support files whose shape changes live under State/
detail: oni_library::state reads and writes <support>/State/, where no build before it looks: builds 1.4.0 to 1.5.6 set aside a support file they cannot parse (#1472), so a new shape never stands at a name they read. A file a newer build wrote reads as far as this one can and is never written: favourites cannot be starred and projects cannot be changed for the session, each refusal saying 'This was last written by a newer version of ONI and is left as it is.' An unreadable file is set aside at its first read. read_json loses its 100 ms sleep and second read, whose cause was the former app's write in place. Checks: a_newer_places_file_is_shown_and_left_as_it_is (twin: a reader that sets it aside leaves nothing at its name), an_unreadable_places_file_is_set_aside_at_the_first_read_with_no_wait (under 20 ms; twin: the retrying read fails the bound), a_file_from_a_newer_build_is_never_set_aside_or_written.

title: Favourites and bookmarks are one file, State/places.json, with one writer
detail: Favourites and Bookmarks become Places: each favourite's path, volume and file id in the order starred. ONI holds the instance lock, so what it holds is what the file says: Favourites::save_merged, the per-write read-merge of bookmarks::record and its mutex go. Identities are read off the interface thread and laid on the places still held (take_identities), then written; the lead for a folder out of reach reads the held places, no file. Checks: a_favourite_starred_is_there_at_the_next_launch (twin: a save that skips the write), a_disk_away_or_another_volume_keeps_the_identity_known, a_folder_s_identity_is_its_volume_and_its_file_id, the window checks of locate, navigator, visible and disk_turns on the new file.

title: Projects live in State/projects.json, format 5; the three-way merges go
detail: The file is plain serde_json of the projects, createdAt in ISO 8601, each member by its path and print. merge.rs and its tests are deleted (list, projects, save_projects, the 1.5.6-compatible writer with its texts, paths and exactMembers, the former files kept beside as projects-vN.json). The undo's lay of a step over the members as they stand keeps its list merge as project::gestures::laid_over. The readers of formats 1 to 4 (Incoming, Written, Writ, placeholders) move to oni_library::migrate::projects, read once.

title: Old favourites, bookmarks and projects imported once, verified, left as they are
detail: oni_library::migrate::places and ::projects: nothing when the new file exists; else the old files read with their readers, the new value built, written, read back and compared with what was built before returning, a mismatch removing the new file so the next launch tries again. The old files are never written nor set aside: an older build still finds what it wrote. Checks: places_import_keeps_the_favourites_order_and_lays_each_place_on_its_path (twins: a sorted import fails the order; favourites.json rewritten in the new shape fails the bytes and 1.5.6's reader), projects_import_each_former_format_to_the_members_its_reader_gave (formats 1 with a 1.5.6 placeholder, 2, 4; twin: ignoring exactMembers loses the copy's print), a_second_import_writes_nothing_and_keeps_a_star_added_since (twin: without the new-file test the star is lost), nothing_is_imported_where_no_favourite_was_ever_kept.

title: Thumbnails under one name; old-named tiles renamed once
detail: swift_name goes with its three uses (held, forget, persist) and its claim. migration::tiles renames once each Thumbnails/*.jpg whose name holds a byte file_name spells in hex to file_name's spelling, unless a tile as new or newer stands there, which wins; nothing to do on Windows. Checks: a_tile_under_its_old_name_takes_the_portable_one_unless_a_newer_stands_there (twin: a rename over the newer tile changes its bytes), a_tile_is_found_only_under_its_portable_name (twin: without the rename the tile is not found).

title: The former app's preferences imported once through plutil; prior::swift goes
detail: migration::defaults, macOS only: for exportSettings, exportArtist, exportCopyright, exportLastProfile, galleryColumns, correctionBrushRadius, soundMuted and lastLaunchedVersion, when preferences.json lacks the key, /usr/bin/plutil -extract <key> raw -expect <type>, each value checked (the export document read by Settings::from_raw_value, the ladder's rungs, the brush's range, a non-empty text). The plist is read, never written; where plutil fails nothing is imported. updates::prior::swift, SWIFT_DOMAIN, Updater::swift_prior and the defaults process at every launch go: a move from the former app counts as an update through ONI's own mark. Checks: the_former_preferences_land_once_never_over_a_value_held (binary plist from tests/fixtures/former-preferences.plist; twin: an import over the held value loses it), a_former_value_onis_readers_refuse_is_left_out (twin: the unchecked text is one the export card cannot read).

title: migration::support runs at launch before any support file is read
detail: oni_app::migration::support, called in main.rs after the instance lock and the log: places, projects, tiles and preferences, then the ledger <support>/State/migration.json {version: 1, support: 2}. A step that failed leaves the ledger as it was, so the next launch tries again; a newer build's ledger is left alone. Check: a_second_launch_writes_nothing (modification dates of the ledger and both State files unchanged; twin: a ledger that forgot the step writes again). The upgrade_check example brings a support copy up first, and the projects tab's former-file window check imports at launch and leaves the old file byte for byte.

title: The export preference is plain serde_json
detail: Settings::raw_value writes its fields by serde_json::to_string in place of the former encoder's mimicry (sorted keys, escaped slashes, whole numbers without .0); from_raw_value reads both. Check: the_preference_text_is_plain_compact_json, the former text reading alike, with a twin missing its resize.

title: A date kept on a frame's EXIF line is settled as it is read, on the line types fix/exif-zoom brought
detail: fix/export-files settled a date where read through ExifMetadata, while canvas had moved the sidecar's line to TypedExif (a missing key derives, an empty one was cleared by hand). Merging both, ExifMetadata.date and TypedExif.date are settled at deserialisation: a kept date that reads as no date is a date cleared (Some("")), never one left to derive, and an absent one still derives; the Date field writes exif::date_of over the row, the export writes the line's date as it stands and keeps what a hand set through keep_line. Check: exif a_sidecars_date_is_settled_as_it_is_read, on TypedExif (words read as cleared, an absent date as None, the whole line settled too; twin: the document read as plain JSON keeps the ten characters EXIF refuses). Two checks of the merged branch then failed on canvas, both fixed here. swift_checks no_crate_trashes_or_removes_a_library_member refused atomic::reclaimed's remove_file(entry.path()), entry being a member's name: the file is one of ONI's own .oni-*.tmp temporaries, now named temporary as every other removal of one in atomic.rs. atomic a_temporary_another_process_holds_is_never_reclaimed failed in 3 of 200 runs of the atomic checks and in none of 200 with the one check that spawns a child skipped: a child holds a copy of every descriptor open at its spawn until its exec, the test's lock included, so the reclaim after the lock was let go found it still held. The app is right (a lock still held keeps a leftover, never takes a live temporary); the checks judging a lock let go and the spawning check now take one mutex, 0 failures in 600 runs under load after.

title: The export's profile checks each read a stand-in profile file of their own
detail: every_format_declares_the_profile_of_its_space failed in a full run with 'Jpeg hdr false in ProPhoto RGB': the file declared the profile while the space's icc_data() read None. Both it and a_wide_green_survives_prophoto_and_clips_in_adobe_rgb wrote the same ROMM.icc in the same process; OutputProfile::loaded re-reads a file whose stamp changed, so one test caught the other's write between its truncation and its bytes and read the space as gone, which is the app's intended answer for a profile gone or unreadable. The app was right, the check shared a file: each stand-in is now a file of its own name. Reproduced once in 900 runs of the binary under load before, none in 900 after. Check: files a_stand_in_profile_rewritten_leaves_every_other_whole (failed with the shared file; twin: the stand-in caught halfway through its own rewrite reads as gone).

title: The phone check's restart listens on a port of its own, never the default every ONI wants
detail: phone::a_phone_pairs_from_the_sheet_and_steps_the_open_frame failed in a full run at the restart: the first launch listened on 53318, the restart on 58789. The runner starts checks in parallel processes and four of them (this one, the switch, phone_tabs, phone_canvas) start the link on a fresh support, so on phone::PORT, 53318: one took it between this check's two launches, and the app listened elsewhere as it should when its kept port is taken. The check is wrong, not the app: it now keeps a port the system gave it before the first launch, as a code keeps one, and asserts the link listens there. Passing alone three times before; after, it holds the default port itself across the restart. Check: the same window check, with the default port held across the restart (failed before: the restart could not take the code's 53318) and a twin launch while the code's port is held, which listens elsewhere. That open_pairing keeps the port is phone::tests the_link_listens_on_the_port_the_last_code_named.

title: A resize's 637 ms wait during an export in a full run was the machine's load, not the door
detail: render::door_tests a_resize_during_an_export_waits_one_submission_not_the_render failed once in the full run of canvas (longest hold 636.7 ms, p99 62.3 ms, median 0): the same export render took 10 409 ms there against 264 to 548 ms alone, 20 to 40 times slower, with every test binary and the window checks sharing the GPU at a load average of about 25. Alone, five runs in a row passed, longest hold 8 to 63 ms, the twin's whole-render gate 193 to 328 ms. No change: the check judges the door, a GPU shared by a hundred binaries makes one submission long; it stays as it is.

title: The export's profile checks are a file of their own, under the 400-line limit
detail: The stand-in check of #1931 took oni-export/tests/files.rs to 487 lines, past its grandfathered 470. The profile checks (every format declaring its space's, the wide green read back by lcms2, the stand-in rewritten) and their helpers move to tests/profiles.rs, the frame, settings and readers both use to tests/common; files.rs is 337 lines and leaves the grandfathered list. Check: architecture no_source_file_grows_past_its_ceiling (failed at 487; its twin twin_a_file_past_the_limit_is_caught), the 14 checks unchanged and passing.

title: An older build writing its favourites or projects after the import is said once
detail: The ledger keeps formerWritten, migrate::last_written at the import: the newest modification of favourites.json and projects.json (bookmarks.json carries no change of the person's). At each later launch a newer one shows one notice, 'Favourites and Projects', saying an earlier version's changes are not carried over, and the mark moves so it is said once. Re-importing additions would bring back the merge lot 1 removed; the notice is the simplest answer that hides nothing. Check: an_older_build_writing_its_files_after_the_import_is_said_once (twin: the mark set back says it again); the_old_files_last_write_moves_when_an_older_build_writes_them (twin: bookmarks.json moves nothing).

title: A failed import stays due: nothing seeds or writes over it, and it is said
detail: migrate::places and projects return Imported {Brought, Nothing, Unparsed} or an error; an old file the disk refuses to read is an error (it was Ok(false), which advanced the ledger for ever).
