An error leaves the ledger behind and migration::support returns Brought {places_due, projects_due, notice}, carried by Options to the navigator: the favourites shown are migrate::places_held (the old files' as they read, else the roots'), the projects the old file's, every change taken back and said, identities not recorded, nothing written under State/, so the next launch imports. An old file that does not parse is what its own build set aside: nothing is taken, said once, the ledger advances, as retrying it would hold every star back for ever. Checks: an_old_file_the_disk_refuses_keeps_its_import_due_and_nothing_is_written_over_it (twin: the roots seeded and written over the pending import lose the old favourites), a_failed_import_stays_due_writes_nothing_and_is_said (twin: a ledger advanced over the failure never brings it), an_old_file_that_does_not_parse_gives_nothing_and_stays, an_old_file_that_does_not_parse_is_said_once, an_import_that_does_not_read_back_is_taken_away_and_due_again (verified's failure path; twin: a file read back as built stays and the next import finds nothing); window check import_due::an_import_due_is_shown_from_the_old_files_and_never_written (twin: the next launch, nothing due, writes the same gesture).

title: The tiles check writes no colon on Windows
detail: a_tile_under_its_old_name_takes_the_portable_one_unless_a_newer_stands_there returns before it writes any name, as NTFS refuses a colon and Windows never wrote one.

title: The former app's preferences are taken only where this line of ONI never ran
detail: migration::defaults imports nothing where preferences.json or Logs/oni.previous.log stands (timing::PREVIOUS_LOG): a build of this line ran there, and a key it never set must keep reading as its default, or a 1.4.0 to 1.5.6 user's exports would change unseen. lastLaunchedVersion was no signal: it is written only once the installation ping answers. The per-key test goes, as no key can be held where nothing ran. Check: the_former_preferences_land_once_and_only_where_this_line_never_ran (twin: the values taken laid where this line ran change its export).

title: A favourite moved drops the identity of where it was
detail: Places::follow keeps a place's volume and file id only when its path is unchanged; a moved one is read afresh by the record its save starts, as noted keeps a known volume over a differing read for ever. Checks: a_favourite_moved_to_another_volume_takes_that_volume (twin: a place carrying the old volume keeps it through noted), favourites_star_beside_each_other_and_follow_a_rename.

title: The migration twins run the code they guard
detail: The newer-file twin reads through state::read blind to the version (it sets the file aside); the starred twin runs the same check with a save that skips the write; the defaults twin lays defaults::taken where this line ran; the refused-value twin reads each value through defaults::extracted; the tiles twin runs tiles::renamed over an old-named tile newer than the portable one; the second-import twin rebuilds through former_places. Each new check was seen to fail on the head's behaviour put back.

title: The rename check waits for the rename to land before it reads projects.json
detail: a_rename_moves_the_projects_recorded_path failed about one run in four beside other checks: its rename helper waited on read_done alone, which stands true while the rename runs off the window (on_disk), so it read projects.json before follow_folder carried and saved the member. The app writes the moved path (project::moved, save_projects); lot 1's guard, writer and laid_over play no part. The helper now asserts disk_busy and read_done together right after the commit (the twin: a wait on the read alone passes before the rename lands), then waits for rig.landed and the read again. Seen: 24 of 24 library_wide runs green under three parallel copies, against 1 failure in 4 before.

title: Two window checks build on Windows again
detail: Windows CI failed to compile the window checks: masks.rs refused the move to FlatField Presets through Unix permissions, editor_leftovers.rs named the macOS board on every system. The refused move is now a file standing where the presets' folder goes, refused on every system; the board's name is macOS only.

title: The sidecar corpus: forty real sidecars of every era, read to goldens by today's reader before the reader moves
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2, first step. A machine's sidecars, kept outside the repository, number 348 (one at format 5, one at 14, 266 at 19, 80 at 20); forty of them, chosen to cover every kind found (a roll draft, the five with Scanner halves, the Scanner face, the Frontier, slides, monochrome, contact sheets, the three with dust strokes and the one of them cropped, a per-frame roll, autoBalance, the EXIF line, the original's print, the ONI Trash mark), enter crates/oni-settings/tests/corpus/<era>/ as early, 19-plain, 19-rust, 20-rust, 21-rust (five written by this build's writer over copies, the cropped strokes among them) and broken (truncated, an array, a version as text, a version 23, a boolean as a number). Each carries <name>.facts.json (mosaic, retired camera matrix, scan size, from examples/corpus_facts.rs on the original's metadata, an original not on the disk left unread) and <name>.reading.txt, the output of examples/reading.rs (Loaded::said: the envelope, the EXIF line, the draft with its base by file name, then {:#?} of the settings) by this branch's reader. scripts/corpus-scrub rewrote only strings where they stand (EXIF fields to fixed words, a roll's name to Roll, the print's date to 2000:01:01 00:00:00, a draft base's folder), checking the parse moved nothing else; no image enters. The 348 and their goldens stay outside the repository (ONI_SIDECAR_CORPUS, ONI_SIDECAR_GOLDENS). Checks in tests/corpus.rs: every corpus file reads as its golden (40), the corpus holds every kind, the wide corpus (348 read as their goldens); twins: a golden with one digit changed is caught, a facts file without its matrix fails first on the gains.

title: The migration chain lives in oni_settings::migrate, asking its original through one Facts in place of two globals
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2, the freeze. Everything that knows what an earlier format meant moves, unchanged, into crates/oni-settings/src/migrate/: chain.rs (the raw steps of codec.rs at their stored names, the version constants, the merge over the resting document), before_1_0.rs (legacy.rs), lighting.rs (lighting_catch_up.rs, its least squares split into lighting/solve.rs so both stay under 400 lines; its grandfathered ceiling goes), density.rs (density_migration.rs), look.rs (ScannerLook, LookModel and the retired colour curves' folding, out of scanner.rs and curves.rs), matrices.rs and strokes.rs (retired_matrices.rs and strokes_on_scan.rs without their globals). migrate::Facts { mosaic, matrix, scan } and migrate::install replace retired_matrices::install and strokes_on_scan::install; the installed lookup is given the caller's mosaic, so asking it reads nothing the read did not need. migrate::converted(bytes, facts) returns today's reading in today's types (Decoded and whether the strokes found their scan); migrate::document replaces codec::decode for a preset, a paste or a share code; migrate::decoded replaces decode_with and Source. sidecar::read asks the installed facts and builds its Loaded through Loaded::of. In oni-app, migration/facts.rs takes the camera table, the scan size and the thumbnails' sweep of retired_matrices.rs and strokes_on_scan.rs, and main installs it once. VERSION stays 21. Checks: migrate::corpus every_corpus_file_reads_as_its_golden_through_migrate (the forty goldens of #1950 read through migrate::converted with each file's facts, no global), the wide corpus (348 of 348 as their goldens), both twins; every byte-identity check unchanged in its assertions: codec_checks 23, guarded_writes 5, real_files 8 of 9 on the reference roll's 19 sidecars as of 2026-10-18 (the marker check fails the same way on canvas: that copy holds no marker, and the owner's current roll is at format 20), swift_checks 9, retired_matrices, strokes_on_scan, kernel_oracle.

title: atomic::write_verified: a file replaced only once its bytes read back from the drive and its target has not moved
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2: the write lot 3's migration lands every converted sidecar with. The bytes are staged in a temporary beside the target (the same staged_with every write uses, fsync included), read back from the drive and compared with what was meant, then handed to the caller's verify; then unmoved says whether the target is still the file the caller read; only then one rename, and with keep_modified the target's date set back to the one it had, so index stamps and thumbnails hold. Any refusal (Unwritten::Io, Unverified, Moved) removes the temporary and leaves the target byte for byte as it was. verified_by takes its rename for the checks. Checks in atomic::tests: a_verified_write_lands_once_read_back_and_a_refused_one_leaves_the_target_as_it_was (a verify answering false and a rename refused each leave the old bytes, the old date and no temporary; accepted, the new bytes land under the old date; twin: the same bytes through write_atomically replace the target) and a_target_another_writer_moves_meanwhile_is_kept_whole (a writer landing between the read and the rename gives Moved and keeps its bytes; twin: with unmoved always true they are lost).

title: Prepare the Roll keeps its draft in one file a folder, .oni-prepare.json, its base named by file name
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2. A step wrote the roll's draft into every frame's sidecar (38 writes for roll #8, a base kept as an absolute path that a renamed folder, another mount or a drive letter left pointing nowhere, found again by name in draft_base.rs). oni_settings::prepare holds the folder's draft (version, id, step, film, capture, pass order and offset, flat field, window, the base as { file, x, y, radius } in the base's own folder only, each frame's tick and flag by file name), read and written atomically, None removing it. Prepare the Roll writes one file a folder at each step, resumes from whichever folder's lands first (each frame taking its place by name, a frame absent or of another id left out, the base joined to its folder's path, no search), removes the files when the roll is left or measured. While VERSION is 21 a folder with no file gathers the drafts its frames' sidecars keep (migrate::draft::gathered: the id most frames carry, its shared fields from the first of them, the base's path reduced to its name, each frame's tick and flag); those frames are remembered and their draft cleared at the next step's write. draft_base.rs goes; resume moves out of prepare.rs into prepare/draft.rs; the window check's helpers move to prepare_parts.rs to keep it under 400 lines. Checks: prepare::tests a_draft_reads_back_as_written_and_none_removes_it (twin: a newer file reads as none); migrate::draft the_id_most_frames_carry_wins_and_each_frame_keeps_its_place (twin: the folder is led by a stray, a first-frame rule gathers it alone); prepare::draft::tests a_draft_base_is_found_in_its_own_folder_wherever_the_folder_went (renamed, another volume, a drive letter, two folders of one name; twin: a base stored as its absolute path finds none), a_step_over_thirty_eight_frames_writes_one_file_and_leaving_removes_it_alone (one file changed for the step, every byte and date back once left; twin: the per-frame draft changes 38 sidecars), the_drafts_frames_keep_from_format_21_resume_the_roll_and_go_at_its_next_write; the model's three resume checks rewritten on folder drafts; window prepare (one file a folder, D left out, no sidecar carrying it, leaving moves no sidecar's date, a resume from drafts an earlier build left in the sidecars, the measure clearing both), prepare_walk and prepare_leftovers on the folder's file.

title: write_verified reads its bytes back through the handle that holds the temporary's lock, so Windows no longer refuses every verified write
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2 review. The temporary is created locked (O_EXLOCK on macOS, LockFileEx elsewhere) and write_verified read it back by its path, through a new handle: Windows' lock is mandatory, so that read was refused and every verified write failed there, while macOS' advisory lock let it pass. The temporary is now opened for reading and writing, and Staged::read_back rewinds and reads the held handle; the doc says what the read proves, the bytes as the file system holds them once flushed, no longer 'read back from the drive'. Checks in atomic::tests: a_verified_write_reads_back_through_the_handle_it_holds seals the temporary against every new handle by its mode (0o200) as Windows' lock does, then lands (failed on the head with PermissionDenied); its twin proves the seal bites, a read by path being refused. The first check's twin now runs write_verified itself: a verify wrongly expecting other bytes is heard, sees the bytes read back and leaves the target and no temporary (the former twin went through write_atomically and could not see an ignored verify).

title: Two rolls prepared in one folder each keep their own draft: the folder's file holds one draft a roll, a frame in one at most
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2 review. The folder's .oni-prepare.json held one draft, given to every frame of the folder on entering and adopted by resume without asking whether it listed the frame: preparing roll B in a folder where roll A's draft lay took A's step and grouping, then B's next step overwrote A's file and B's leaving or measure removed it. The file is now { version, drafts: [...] }, each draft a roll's id with its frames (prepare::Draft loses its own version field; VERSION stays 1, the file never shipped). prepare::write(folder, frames, draft) reads the file, takes the roll's frames out of every other draft there, lays the roll's draft in place of its id's, drops a draft left with no frame and the file with the last; a file of a newer version is never rewritten (sidecar::Error::Newer, said through refusal::said), one unreadable reads as none. prepare::read gives every draft. On entering, a frame takes only the draft that lists it by name, and the id most of the roll's frames carry alone resumes (draft::found), so a stray draft no longer sets the roll whichever frame lands first; a step, a leave and a measure each write the roll's Part a folder (its frames by name and its draft or none, Roll::dropped for a removal). Matches the drafts of format 21, where a frame's draft was its own and a roll's write took over only its frames. Checks: prepare::tests two_rolls_in_one_folder_keep_each_its_draft (B's step and B's removal leave A's; twin: a roll taking A's frames takes them out of A's draft, which goes) and a_draft_reads_back_as_written_and_its_removal_takes_the_file_with_the_last (twin: a newer file reads as none and is refused, byte for byte kept); prepare::draft::tests two_rolls_in_one_folder_resume_each_its_own_draft (A's draft reaches no frame of B, B's step leaves A's, B dropped leaves A's; twin: a roll of A's frames and one of B's takes them). The two parts that ran on the head failed there (B's frames given A's draft; A's frames given B's after B's step). Window checks prepare, prepare_walk and prepare_leftovers read the folder's drafts.

title: A draft of format 21 keeps its base only in the folder its stored path names, never on a namesake in another folder of the roll
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2 review. migrate::draft::gathered reduced the stored base to its file name in every folder's gathered draft, so a roll spanning X/ and Y/ with a DSC_0002 in each could resume with its base on Y's frame, a guess draft_base.rs used to refuse. gathered now takes the folder and keeps the base only where the stored path's folder has that folder's name (its last component, either system's separators), so a folder moved to another volume or drive letter keeps its base and a namesake elsewhere gets none; it also keeps each id's draft, the choice between ids moving to draft::found, which sees the whole roll. Checks: migrate::draft each_id_keeps_its_own_frames_and_the_base_stays_in_its_own_folder (twin: the roll's other folder, holding a namesake, keeps no base); prepare::draft::tests a_base_stored_in_one_folder_stays_off_its_namesake_in_another (Y's frames landing first, the base is X's DSC_0002; failed on the head, which put it on Y's; twin: a base stored under a folder of neither name is found on no frame). A folder renamed since the draft was stored loses its base pick, which is picked again; the step and every frame's place stay.

title: Prepare the Roll: a frame's draft an earlier build wrote after the folder's file wins; a refused step keeps the frames' own drafts for the discard
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2 review. A folder's file shadowed every frame's own draft: once one existed, an earlier build walking the roll further in the frames' sidecars was ignored and the newer build resumed the stale step. draft::found now takes a frame's own draft where its folder's file does not list it or where its sidecar was modified after that file (only an earlier build writes one). save_draft emptied the remembered frames whose sidecar keeps a draft of format 21 even when the folder's write failed, so a discard then left those drafts behind: Roll::step_drafts returns them and keeps them until a discard or a measure; draft::written clears them where the folder's write landed or was a removal, and says a removal's failure instead of dropping it. The comment on entering said nothing waits for the slowest file: the sidecars are read first, as a frame's draft is the roll's choice, then each framing lands as its scan's size is read; the comment says so. Checks in prepare::draft::tests: a_draft_an_earlier_build_wrote_after_the_folders_file_is_the_one_resumed (failed on the head, which resumed the file's step; twin: the file written after them is the one resumed) and a_step_whose_file_is_refused_keeps_the_frames_own_drafts_for_the_discard (a folder in the file's place refuses the step, no frame's draft is cleared, the discard clears them; twin: the stored frames taken at the step, as the head did, the discard leaves them); the_drafts_frames_keep_from_format_21_resume_the_roll_and_go_at_its_next_write updated: the stray's frame is given no draft.

title: The sidecar corpus dates no one's work: importedAt and trashedAt fixed by scripts/corpus-scrub
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 2 review. Five corpus sidecars kept the real day a photo was imported or trashed. scripts/corpus-scrub now sets importedAt to 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z and trashedAt to 2000-01-02T00:00:00Z where they stand (their order kept), refusing a date not written as text, and leaves a document that is no object as it is (it stopped on the broken corpus' array); run over every corpus file, it changed the five and their goldens (examples/reading.rs: imported Date(-31622400), trashed Date(-31536000)), nothing else; the truncated file is named and left, as it should. Task #1950's detail names no machine or private folder any more. Check in migrate::corpus: the_corpus_dates_no_ones_work (every importedAt and trashedAt is the scrub's; a trashed photo stays represented; failed on the head's corpus, naming the five; twin: a real import date is caught). The wide corpus, kept outside the repository, still reads as its 348 goldens.

title: The sidecar's document is ONI's own, oni-frame, written by plain serde_json from its types
detail: Cut the Swift cord, lot 3. oni_settings::codec becomes document.rs: Document { format: "oni-frame", version, original { print, tail }, importedAt, label (omitted when none), trashedAt, exifLine, autoBalance (typed, f32 digits), settings }, encode = serde_json::to_vec_pretty plus a newline, decode typed in one pass, version_of and sniffed read the top alone. Every settings container gains #[serde(default)], so an absent key reads its rest; no conversion parameter is renamed. json.rs (the former app's key order and number spelling, the typed Node tree, semantic_difference) and kept.rs (keys of a newer app carried through each rewrite) are deleted: a newer file is never rewritten, so nothing is carried. The roll marker keeps its name, keys and date scale, written by plain serde_json. Measured with examples/sidecar_bench.rs on the typical corpus frame: encode 8.8 us, decode 17.3 us, sniff 5.6 us (targets 12 and 35).

title: The Scanner keypad is kept in steps; halves go
detail: ScannerClicks serialises its five counts as they stand, in steps, and reads them back tolerant and clamped. A document of format 21 and under is read by migrate::reshape: steps = 2 x whole + the half step held to one, then the range's stop, exactly as the former reader computed. Checks: reshape whole_units_and_their_half_step_read_in_steps ({d: 3, halves: {d: 1}} is 7, -3/-1 is -7, past the range lands on the stop; twin: dropping the half reads 6), scanner steps_are_written_as_they_stand (twin: whole units read half the steps), oni-core scanner a_key_moves_half_a_unit (a key stores 1 step, twin 2).

title: The EXIF line is kept under exifLine, each field derived, cleared or set
detail: TypedExif is renamed ExifLine and the sidecar keeps it under exifLine: an absent field derives at each opening, an empty one was cleared by hand, a text was set. Renamed because the typed reader of 1.4.0 to 1.5.6 requires seven strings under exif and would call a whole sidecar unreadable; under another key it ignores it and opens read-only. A block of format 21 is carried with the meaning the reader before this one gave it (#1907: an empty string in a block written whole is a field cleared), so no line a person cleared comes back; the corpus goldens read every line over an empty derived one and hold.

title: migrate::file and migrate::folder bring a sidecar to this format in place, or leave it byte for byte
detail: migrate::standing (Current, Older, Newer, NotASidecar), converted (the frozen chain on the raw document, the merge over the resting one, reshape, the typed steps, then the camera matrix and the strokes on the scan asked of the original), file (held one writer a process, the original present, the roll draft adopted into its folder's .oni-prepare.json, then atomic::write_verified: the temporary read back must decode equal to the conversion and encode back to itself, the old file unmoved, one rename, its modification date set back) and folder (every X.json beside a file X right inside a folder, holding an object with settings). Refusal: Unreadable, Newer, ScanUnknown, CameraUnknown, Away (original kept in the cloud), Unwritable, Unverified, Moved; Facts now answer Result, so a camera the file cannot say now or an original away is refused, never taken for a camera without a matrix. migration/facts.rs installs those answers.

title: A sidecar read brings an earlier file to this format first, or shows it read-only and says why
detail: sidecar::read: Current decodes typed; Newer reads as far as these types do, read-only; Older runs migrate::file and reads the result, an unreadable one stays an error, never a new photo, and any other refusal shows the conversion in memory, writable false, Loaded::held_back saying why. Loaded loses roll_draft and gains auto_balance and held_back; a write meets an earlier file through the same path and never writes over one held back (Error::Held). The sidecar's hold is reentrant for the thread holding it, as a write migrates the file it reads. set_auto_balance is a field setter over the typed AutoBalance. The editor opens a held-back photo read-only with its reason (refusal::held_back, in French and Spanish too).

title: Roll drafts leave the frames: a migration lays each into its folder's file
detail: RollDraft and DraftBase move to migrate::draft as what format 21 kept; a frame's draft taken out by the conversion joins its folder's .oni-prepare.json (prepare::adopt: a frame the file lists keeps the file's word, a draft of the same id gains the frame, another id stands as its own). sidecar::set_roll_draft, WriteOptions::roll_draft and the Prepare machinery reading and clearing each frame's own draft go (draft::found reads the folders' files alone, Found and the stored set go, land_roll loses its prepared list).

title: The sweep brings every sidecar a person keeps in the background, one thread a volume; an opened folder is gated
detail: oni_app::migration::sweep: started once Shell stands (Shell::migrate) when the ledger owes it (sidecars under this format, or pending or refused places), it walks the folder last opened, the favourites (State/places.json or the old files), the roots, recursively by roots::survey, then the distinct folders of every index*.sqlite of the caches (oni_library::index::listed, opened read-only) and of the projects' members, a folder inside a tree left to the tree (migration::walk). One thread per volume (Computer::volume_root), one file after another; alive is read before each file, and a quit joins the threads. At its end the ledger, State/migration.json version 2, holds sidecars = this format, pending (what did not answer) and refused (folders with files left as they are, with their counts); a disk back starts it again. read_rows gates every folder its survey lists before any row is read, once a run. Logs name a photo by its token and a refusal by its kind alone.

title: The person is told: one sheet at the first launch, a line while the sweep runs, a notice if files were left
detail: migration::brought reports tell once, where the support folder held something (preferences, roots, favourites, projects, library, thumbnails, presets or State files) and the ledger's told is below this format; a fresh support folder records it silently. UpgradedSheet (notice.slint, drawn over the welcome): 'Your Edits, Brought Up to Date' and its four lines, GOT IT. The status bar shows 'Bringing settings up to date: {done} of {total} folders' in the gallery, beside a folder's reading when both run. At the end, only when files were left, the Told notice '{n} photos keep their earlier settings file' with its reason. All texts in French and Spanish. Release-notes line, the owner's to publish: 'This version keeps each photo's settings in a new format and converts the ones you have, by itself. There is no way back: an older ONI opens converted photos read-only.'

title: Presets are oni-preset files of this format; share codes ONI2, ONI1 read for ever
detail: A preset file is { format: "oni-preset", version, preset { id, name, parameters, tint, note }, settings }, plain serde_json. presets::migrate holds what reads earlier ones (legacy_rows, the retired row names, the single-file presets.json takeover) and brought(), which rewrites each earlier file in place through write_verified, run at every launch by migration::support (a newer file is skipped and never listed). A new share code is ONI2: over this format's departures, completed over the resting settings when read; ONI1: codes go through the settings' chain for ever. The paste board's text is this format's document.

title: The corpus migrates: each of the 40 files to this format and back to its golden, and the 348 of the wide corpus
detail: migrate::corpus: each corpus sidecar laid beside an empty original in a Roll folder of a scratch copy, migrate::file_with its facts, then sidecar::read and the folder's draft give the golden of the former reader, text for text; a migrated file is a fixed point (encode(decode(bytes)) == bytes) and a second pass is Current, bytes and date unchanged; a broken or newer one is refused and byte for byte what it was. Twins: dropping the half steps fails the files that have them; swapping d and c fails every Scanner frame; a field written under another name is no fixed point; a golden with one digit changed; facts without the matrix part in the gains. The wide corpus (ONI_SIDECAR_CORPUS, 348 sidecars, outside the repository, read only): every one migrated to its golden.

title: A migration is never half-written, and an older build meets a file of this format read-only
detail: migrate::checks: a refused rename leaves the old bytes and no temporary, the next pass brings it; a child process killed once the temporary is written leaves the old file whole and the next run takes the temporary and migrates (twin: a writer truncating the target then writing leaves half a file under the same kill); a read-only folder (0555) refuses Unwritable, the photo opens read-only with its edits as read and the file untouched, and migrates once writable (twin: a fresh photo's rest differs); the reader of 1.5.6 (its typed tail over its resting document, its guard at format 20) reads a file of this format and may not write it (twin: the line under exif makes that reader fail, which is why the key is exifLine); a file of a newer format is left as it is and never written.

title: The sweep over a scratch library; the gate; the telling; a window check of the whole path
detail: migration::sweep_tests: a library of 400 corpus copies in 20 folders ends with every sidecar in this format, no modification date moved (twin: a plain atomic write moves it), and no sweep owed after; a sweep stopped part way never says it ended, and the next brings the rest, each once (the two runs' counts sum to the file count); a root on a disk away is pending and brought once it answers (twin: a ledger that forgot it owes nothing and leaves the files old); a read-only folder is refused, counted for the end notice and listed in the ledger, then brought; an opened folder never known is gated before its rows land (twin: an earlier sidecar reaching the live decoder is refused). migration::tests the_new_format_is_told_once_and_never_to_an_empty_support_folder. Window check migration::an_earlier_library_is_brought_while_the_person_works: sheet shown and closed, the sweep brings three format-19 sidecars, each reading as before, double click, a notch, back: only the edited frame moves.

title: The sidecar's checks rewritten on this format's files
detail: real_files reads a corpus sidecar into a scratch copy (it becomes this format at its first read) for the round trip, the label and trash keeping the revision, a newer format read-only and the absent and unreadable cases; swift_form and the roll #8 byte-identity checks go with the former writer. guarded_writes: a written sidecar holds Document's keys alone and a format 21 file's unknown key is gone after migration. auto_balance on the typed value, f32 digits kept. codec_checks ages documents through migrate::reshape::as_stored (the shape format 21 wrote). foreign_sidecar, strokes_on_scan (an unknown scan size: read-only, file untouched, a write refused Held) and retired_matrices (written once by the read; twin: the chain run again moves the gains twice) follow the new reader.

title: examples/sidecar_bench.rs and examples/migrate.rs
detail: sidecar_bench times encode, decode, sniff and the conversion of a stored file (medians of 2 000 and 300 runs); migrate prints a sidecar's conversion to this format without writing (rewrite.rs goes); reading.rs prints a reading through migrate::reading with the draft as its folder gathers it.

title: A passes lead's sidecar is read with its own mosaic
detail: rgb_passes::framings read each lead's sidecar as a file outside the RAW engine; a read now brings an earlier file to this format, and a step of the chain depends on how the original decodes, so framings takes the store's mosaic rule.

title: CLAUDE.md names the sidecar format and its migration; comments of the value types say what, not where from
detail: The format line of 'Decisions that look like mistakes' names oni-frame, plain serde_json of oni_settings::document, the migration in oni_settings::migrate by the sweep or a first read, and an older build reading read-only. cg.rs, collation.rs and id.rs describe their values by what the sidecar and the index need.

title: The sweep's speed on a scratch library of synthetic sidecars
detail: On this Mac (M2 Max, internal SSD), the dev profile (workspace opt-level 1, dependencies 3), one volume: 30 400 sidecars of formats 19 and 20 copied from the corpus into 800 folders under one root, swept by migration::sweep_tests with ONI_SWEEP_FILES=30400: 18.2 s, 0.60 ms a file, every one brought to this format and none of their dates moved; the default run of the check, 400 files in 20 folders, takes about 0.6 s. A run of the real binary (ONI_BACKGROUND, scratch ONI_SUPPORT, ONI_CACHES and HOME) on a scratch copy of five frames of the reference roll's test copy: the gate brought the opened folder before its rows, the sweep then found nothing left, and each sidecar reads as its earlier file did.

title: Lot 3 lands at format 21's number: no build of the branch can write a file of format 22 before the last commit
detail: Every piece above is in this commit with document::VERSION still 21: a sidecar is Current only when it names itself oni-frame at this version, so files of format 21 written by earlier builds are Older and migrate. The flip to 22 is the lot's last commit.

title: Sidecar format 22
detail: document::VERSION moves to 22 in the lot's last commit, after every check passed at 21: every earlier file is Older and migrates, an older build reads a 22 file read-only. The demo scene oni-demos/scenes/P1071951.json is written again at 22 (examples/migrate). At 22: oni-settings (the corpus and the 348 of the wide corpus), oni-core, oni-library, oni-export, oni-i18n, oni-measure, oni-pipeline, oni-demos, oni-app --lib, every window check (260), architecture and scripts/lint pass.

title: One folder under two spellings is one folder to the sweep, and one sidecar is held by one writer whatever its spelling
detail: Found by the real app on a scratch library (scratch ONI_SUPPORT, ONI_CACHES and HOME; a copy of five frames of the reference roll's test copy, two in a read-only folder named as a root by its /private/tmp spelling): the sweep took that folder under both spellings and counted each refused file twice (the notice said 4 photos for 2), and the gate, by the opened folder's spelling, and the sweep, by the survey's, held one sidecar under two keys, so one file was refused as moved under the other's write. The plan spells every place as a survey does (paths::canonical); the hold keys a sidecar by its folder's resolved path; a file another writer brought meanwhile counts as current, not as left. Checks: sweep_tests' read-only folder rooted by its /private spelling (twin: without the spelling, 4 refused instead of 2), held's other spelling waits (twin: keyed by the spelling, it does not). The app again: 2 refused, the notice said 2, and the next launch, the folder writable, brought them; every sidecar reads as its earlier file did.

title: The sweep touches only ONI's sidecars
detail: Lot 3 review (data loss 1). migrate::folder took any X.json holding a settings key beside any regular file X, so another program's tool.json beside tool was rewritten as an oni-frame document with no backup. A sidecar is now X.json beside a file X the caller wants (the sweep passes library::is_importable, the survey's rule; hidden names skipped) carrying an earlier sidecar's marks (migrate::marked: a tolerant integer version and a settings object naming its mode). Check: oni-settings tests/sweep_pass a_pass_touches_only_a_sidecar_beside_a_photo_with_a_sidecars_marks (another program's file and a namesake JSON without the marks untouched; twins: the photo's own sidecar brought by the same pass, the converter alone takes the program's file).

title: No cloud original is downloaded for a migration
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 1). The sweep and the gate called decodes_via_mosaic on every original before any cloud check, so a first launch downloaded every iCloud or OneDrive original beside a 1.5.x sidecar. Facts::mosaic is now Mosaic::Known or Mosaic::Asked, asked only by formats under 15 (the chain's only use); every fact the installed lookup reads (mosaic, camera, scan size, the green pass of a lead included) first checks identity::in_cloud of the file it would read and answers Away. A refusal Away leaves the sidecar as it is and its folder pending. Checks: tests/sweep_pass a_format_that_asks_no_fact_never_asks_the_original_and_the_oldest_ask_how_it_decodes (format 20 asks nothing; twin: a format 14 sidecar asks and an original away leaves it byte for byte); oni-app migration::tests an_original_kept_in_the_cloud_is_asked_nothing (twin: on the disk the same facts are read).

title: A read writes nothing; a camera the table never named is never taken for one without a matrix
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 2). sidecar::read migrated and wrote the file, so tools (upgrade_check, sensor_colours, dust_census, look_lab_strip) rewrote whole folders, and with no facts installed Facts::bare answered no matrix, losing the compensation for good. Now sidecar::read reads an earlier format in memory and writes nothing (read-only with the reason when a fact is missing); a write by the person brings the file first through migrate::file (its draft adopted), and only the sweep, the gate and those writes migrate. Facts::bare answers MatrixUnknown; the installed table answers a matrix for a camera in cameras, none for one in unmatched (measured here, no fit), MatrixUnknown for any other and for no table at all (a fresh Mac, Windows), the file then left as it is and said once. Checks: tests/sweep_pass a_read_writes_nothing_and_no_table_never_says_a_camera_had_no_matrix (twin: a table that answers converts it, the gains moved); oni-app migration::tests a_camera_the_table_never_named_is_unknown_never_taken_for_one_without_a_matrix; checks.rs a_read_only_folder_reads_its_photo_as_it_read_refuses_a_write_and_is_brought_once_writable; retired_matrices and strokes_on_scan now bring the file at its first write.

title: Settings of format 22 go on the clipboard under their own type
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 3). The new build wrote a 22 document under app.opennegative.settings, which 1.5.6 pastes with no version check, doubling the keypad. Copies now go under app.opennegative.settings.2 (as ONI2: did for share codes), which replaces an earlier build's copy; app.opennegative.settings is still read, and kept across a framing or window copy. Check: pasteboard::tests settings_of_this_format_go_under_their_own_type_and_an_earlier_copy_still_pastes (twin: under the earlier type the copy reaches that build).

title: One writer for a folder's Prepare file; an unreadable one is never written over
detail: Lot 3 reviews (data loss 3, compat 4). prepare::read, write and adopt hold the folder's .oni-prepare.json from read to rename (one lock per resolved folder across the process), so the sweep, the gate, a write's migration and a Prepare step never drop each other's frames; a file that cannot be read (I/O error or not parsing) is an error for write and adopt, never rewritten as empty, and reads as none. A migration whose draft cannot be kept leaves its sidecar as it is (Refusal::Drafts). Check: prepare::tests an_unreadable_file_is_never_written_over_and_frames_adopted_at_once_are_all_kept (200 frames adopted from 8 threads all kept).

title: The sweep ends: pending only for a disk away, a file left said once and owing no sweep
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 5). A folder gone for good or one file that could never convert kept the sweep due forever, walking the whole library at every launch. Ledger 3: pending holds only places whose disk is away (presence Offline Disconnected) and folders holding a photo whose original is in the cloud; a place gone from a disk present is dropped, one refused by permissions logged; left lists each file left as it was by its original's path, with its reason (Why) and its sidecar's stamp, said once, and taken again only once its sidecar changed (skipped by a later pass otherwise). due is a whole sweep not yet ended at this format or a place pending; once one ended, a sweep takes the pending places alone. Checks: sweep_tests a_disk_away_is_pending_and_brought_once_it_answers_and_a_place_gone_is_dropped (a file laid in a swept folder is not walked again; twin: a place named pending is taken) and a_file_refused_is_said_once_owes_no_sweep_and_is_taken_again_once_it_changed.

title: The end notice says true reasons, once, after the sheet was shown
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 5, lower). The notice said read-only, full or not downloaded for every refusal, at the end of every sweep, and told was recorded before any window existed. The notice now counts the unsaid files of the ledger by reason, each line true of every file it counts (disk refused, settings or Prepare file unreadable, original not downloaded, original unreadable, matrix unknown here), is shown after the sheet closes or at the sweep's end, and marks them said; told is recorded when a window shows the sheet, so a bench or a launch that ended first tells again. Checks: migration::tests the_new_format_is_told_once_shown_and_never_to_an_empty_support_folder; window migration (twin: a sheet no window showed is told at the next launch).

title: The gate brings a photo's sidecar as its row is read, after the rows land
detail: Lot 3 review (compat 6). read_rows read every sidecar of the opened tree before the first landing at every launch, and GATED marked a folder before converting it. The gate is now per photo, on the sidecars a row read takes anyway (a new row before library::indexed, a row whose sidecar or file moved off the bytes refreshed reads): nothing is read before the rows land, nothing more when nothing changed; a standing row is left to the sweep. Check: sweep_tests an_opened_folder_lands_its_rows_first_and_brings_a_new_rows_sidecar_as_it_reads_it (first landing before any sidecar brought; a standing row's sidecar not read; twin: its stamp moved, it is read and brought).

title: A quit never waits on a sweep held by a mount that stopped answering
detail: Lot 3 review (compat lower). walk::planned reads alive before spelling each path; Sweep::drop waits for the sweep's end at most QUIT_WAIT (2 s), then leaves the thread to the process's end, which an unrenamed temporary survives whole: a network mount holds a read in the kernel as long as it likes. Check: sweep_tests a_quit_never_waits_on_a_sweep_held_by_a_disk_that_stopped_answering (a 30 s worker dropped in under 5 s; twins: a quick one is joined, planning alive spells both trees).

title: Another file's sidecar is never converted with this file's facts
detail: Lot 3 review (compat lower). migrate::file checks the sidecar's print against the original (identity::foreign_bytes) before the first fact is asked and before its draft is adopted, so a namesake copied in keeps the other photo's settings unchanged (Refusal::Foreign, not listed, set aside at the photo's first write); a conversion that asks no fact never reads the original for it. Check: tests/sweep_pass another_files_sidecar_is_never_converted_with_this_files_facts (twin: beside its own photo the same sidecar takes the matrix).

title: A Prepare base follows its folder renamed
detail: Lot 3 review (data loss 2). A draft's base was kept only where the stored path's folder name equals the folder's. It is now kept too when the stored folder is gone, its file in this folder is a frame of the roll (by its sidecar's draft or the folder's file), and no folder beside it holds a frame of the roll by that name. Check: draft::tests a_base_follows_its_folder_renamed_unless_a_folder_beside_holds_its_frame (twins: a folder beside with the frame, and the stored folder still there, keep no base).

title: A photo held back in the ONI Trash says its own reason
detail: Lot 3 review (data loss 4). set_trashed returned false for a sidecar held back, which trash::mark counted as written by a newer version. It now returns Error::Held with the reason, said by refusal::held_back (new texts for MatrixUnknown, Foreign and Drafts). Check: oni-library tests/trash_refusals a_photo_held_back_in_an_earlier_format_says_its_own_reason (twin: the newer file said apart).

title: Entering a roll brings its frames; a frame not brought resumes from its own sidecar
detail: As a read writes nothing (#1982), Prepare the Roll gathers a frame's draft from its sidecar of an earlier format (migrate::draft::found, read-only) and entering a roll first gates its frames, so the drafts its steps rewrite are their folders' alone and a later write never brings a stale one back. Check: draft::tests a_frame_not_brought_yet_resumes_its_roll_from_its_sidecar_unwritten (twin: the folder's file alone knows nothing of it); window prepare (a roll as an earlier build left it resumes).

title: The older-build check runs 1.5.6's own code
detail: Lot 3 review (compat lower). checks.rs the_shipped_build_reads_a_file_of_this_format_read_only_and_writes_nothing (ignored, about a minute: cargo test -p oni-settings -- --ignored the_shipped_build) archives crates/oni-settings/src at eac39604, builds it offline beside a small reader on the workspace's Cargo.lock, and runs 1.5.6's sidecar::read, set_label and write on a converted 22 file: read-only, both writes refused, the file unchanged; twin: on a format 20 file it reads writable and writes. The fast shipped_reader check stays.

title: A camera this computer never fitted reads as one with no matrix
detail: Lot 3 second review (blocking). Known::answer refused every camera the table did not fit and every camera with no table, so on Windows and on any Mac 1.4.0 to 1.5.1 never ran on every edited RAW negative of format 19 and under opened read-only and refused every write. Owner's lead: no build on a computer without a fit for a camera decoded it through a matrix, so the answer is none there, as 1.5.2 to 1.5.6 showed it: a camera in cameras keeps its matrix, any other (unmatched, never named, no table) none. MatrixUnknown now comes only from facts never asked (a tool with nothing installed), whose files are said with the originals that could not be read; the notice's matrix line is gone. Supersedes #1982's table rule. Check: migration::tests a_camera_the_table_fitted_keeps_its_matrix_and_any_other_reads_as_none (twin: the fitted camera keeps it).

title: A write laying its own settings needs no camera matrix
detail: Lot 3 second review (blocking, second part). A write of an earlier file converted it whole first, so one whose camera matrix could not be learnt refused even a write replacing the settings. When the conversion stops on the matrix alone (MatrixUnknown, CameraUnknown), the write keeps the old file's envelope and roll draft (migrate::draft::kept_from) and lays its own settings; a label, an EXIF line or the ONI Trash, which keep the stored settings, still refuse. Check: tests/sweep_pass a_write_laying_its_own_settings_needs_no_matrix_and_keeps_the_envelope (twin: a label on such a file refused, the file unchanged).

title: An original the opening downloads opens editable
detail: Lot 3 second review. The editor read an iCloud original's sidecar before its decode downloaded the file, so a frame needing a fact opened read-only for the session. Frame::away marks such an opening; once its preview lands (decoded or kept), the sidecar is gated and, unless it still waits on the cloud, the frame opened again on it, editable, its preview kept. facts::install_with takes the cloud test a check stands in for. Check: window migration::an_original_the_opening_downloads_opens_editable (twin: an original still in the cloud after its decode stays read-only, its sidecar untouched).

title: A Prepare file that does not parse is set aside, never blocking a frame
detail: Lot 3 second review. A malformed .oni-prepare.json refused every write of a frame still carrying an old roll draft, with no way out in the app. A write or adoption now moves such a file whole to .oni-prepare (unreadable).json, numbered when taken, and goes on; a read moves nothing and reads none; a file the disk refuses to read still refuses. Checks: prepare::tests a_file_that_does_not_parse_is_set_aside_whole_and_frames_adopted_at_once_are_all_kept (twin: a second one beside the first, never over it); tests/sweep_pass a_prepare_file_that_does_not_parse_never_blocks_a_frames_own_write (twin: a file the disk refuses still blocks).

title: The notice says what a file on a refusing disk does
detail: Lot 3 second review. As a read writes nothing, a sidecar the disk refused to replace opens with its edits and refuses a change; the notice said it opens read-only. Its line says so now, and an original in the cloud is converted once ONI opens it. Check: app::shell::migrating::tests each_reason_says_only_what_its_files_do (twin: a file held back for its original says read-only).

title: An original in the cloud owes no sweep
detail: Lot 3 second review. A folder holding an undownloaded original went back to pending at every run and was walked again whole at each launch. Such a file is now listed once with its reason like any other, no place pending for it; the gate brings it once ONI opens it (#1996) or reads its row again. Check: sweep_tests an_original_in_the_cloud_is_said_once_owes_no_sweep_and_is_brought_once_opened (twin: downloaded, the gate brings it).

title: A sidecar reads the same on every system: the reader's maths are libm's
detail: Windows CI read the corpus file early/001 with exposure 0.462294 where its golden, made on a Mac, says 0.46263927. Rust's powf, exp, exp2, ln, log2, log10, sin and cos call each system's own libm, whose last bit differs from Apple's to Microsoft's, and the Lighting fit (an f32 Gauss-Newton on finite differences) turns one last bit into the third decimal of the fitted print: the same document migrated to another Lighting on each system. Every such call in oni-settings outside its checks now goes to the libm crate (a pure Rust port of musl's), so the reader is bit for bit the same on macOS and Windows. Only the two early corpus files, the two fitted, read otherwise; their goldens were made again (exposure 0.4619318, curve points moving in the eighth decimal), and of the wide corpus's 348 the same two alone change. The codec check of the mosaic gains takes its expected log2 from libm too.

title: The reader's sources call no system maths
detail: the_reader_rounds_alike_on_every_system (migrate/corpus.rs) lists every line of oni-settings outside its test modules calling powf, exp, ln, log2, sin and the like by method or as f32::/f64:: paths, so a call that would read otherwise on Windows fails on the Mac. Twin: a planted powf and a map(f32::exp2) are both caught, the same call in a test module is not; the reverted exp2f of the former exposure was caught.

title: The door check waits for the released thread to finish, however slow the adapter
detail: the_holding_thread_passes_its_own_door_and_no_other gave the thread waiting at the door ten seconds once released. On the Windows runner's WARP adapter, beside the door checks' 12 MP export renders running at once, its 64 x 48 prepare took longer and the check failed with the door working. The check now waits for the thread's answer itself, which it always sends; its twin (no pass while the door is held) is unchanged.

title: The inputs checks wait for a job's distributions, its last delivery
detail: The asking helper of inputs_tests stopped listening one second after the render's last delivery, so on WARP the distributions, read after the render and the count, could arrive after it stopped: a_patch_landing_under_the_same_settings_counts_and_reads_again then found none. A job alone in the slot and not held always ends on its distributions (Worker), so the helper now waits for them, fails at once on a render error, and prints how long they took after the render.

title: The opening-reading check reads the canvas on the first render, before the full resolution can
detail: a_decode_under_a_reading_left_never_lands_on_the_canvas pumped 200 ms after the opening's render and required the full resolution not built, built once the frame stayed a second from its opening. On WARP the opening's render took 11 s, and under load on a Mac over a second, so the build was due at once and the check failed with the app right. The preview gate runs the two decodes in turn and the full resolution is asked only after a render lands, so the first render follows both decodes and no full-resolution render can land before the next pump: the canvas is read there, the drawn render asserted to be the preview's. Without #1730's reading check the canvas still shows the reading left (checked on the Mac).

title: The 1.6 welcome told in pages
detail: The welcome sheet becomes five pages over one 3:2 stage: the version photo and the release in four lines, then the calmer interface, Automatic De-dust, the edits brought up to date (format 22, no way back, two changed habits) and about 70 fixes. BACK, NEXT, Return, the arrows and the dots turn them; GET STARTED closes on the last. Scenes loop on a clock that rests on their last state under Reduce Motion. Edition 1.6, version 1.6.0. Checks: help (Return turns each page, the last closes; twin: a page before the last stays open), sheet_layout (GET STARTED on the last page fits or scrolls).

title: The welcome's interface scene: the window pressed into its calmer look
detail: Page 1 of the welcome shows the editor's miniature at six tenths: the look before (coloured keycaps on black plates, ALL in the bar, the parent and favourites keys and path pill, thick rails in full colour) presses flat group by group (bar in three clusters, column, sliders; press, a faint veil, six marks, settle, BACK and EXPORT rising back), the sliders morph in place, then the camera pushes to the real size, a hand types 0.30 into Temperature's field and the knob follows, the camera pulls back and the hand folds Computer. The picture is De-dust's daylight scene, upright, its hill edge to edge, its sky warming with the knob; in each swap the old leaves before the new arrives, and the column's breath lies on its header row, the sliders' at a lighter 0.06. Each turn but the first dissolves still from the last moment; Reduce Motion rests on it. Every length is drawn times the camera, as the software renderer draws no scale. Check: welcome_scenes_interface (t 0 and 1 the same frame, twin: the opening differs; yellow and red keycaps in the opening's bar, twin: none in the look now; the pouf between both looks; the focus ring close up, twin: none at rest); ONI_SCENE_FRAMES shoots every 100 ms.

title: The welcome's De-dust page, animated
detail: Page 2 of the 1.6 welcome loops Auto De-dust over 9 s after the animation direction, on a drawn daylight landscape, no photo: 18 specks, 11 dots, 5 flakes and 2 hairs, numbered in reading order. The pointer comes in from the right edge to DETECT and presses the keycap; the picture dims but for a 56 px band crossing it, and each speck's ring (white on a dark halo) lands as the band's trailing edge passes, the count stepping in fixed digit cells; REMOVE comes within reach once the reading ends. The pointer hops down to REMOVE and leaves; the specks heal one by one, three slow then every 110 ms, each tile landing in a 6 by 3 corrections grid. The loop ends on the clean picture with its 18 tiles and rewinds to the dust in a still dissolve; Reduce Motion rests on that end. Sizes, colours, times and specks in WelcomeDedust. Check: welcome_scenes_dedust (frames at 0 and 1 identical; speck 7 darker than the sky at 0.07, matching it at 0.90; twins: at 0.07 it is not healed, and the opening differs from the end); with ONI_SCENE_FRAMES=1 it also shoots a frame every 100 ms of the loop for review.

title: The welcome's scenes of the edits and the fixes
detail: Page 3 shows a row of still photos with a settings card each, turned from 1.5 to 1.6 and checked as a light passes, a status line counting the folders; page 4 ticks six areas one after another, their bugs leaving, while the count rises to 70. Both follow the animation direction: eight pictures in a 4x2 grid, a count in fixed digit cells, no colour for done, a rewind dissolve at each turn. Both are expressions of the scene clock, so Reduce Motion rests on the finished state. Check: welcome_scenes_pages (a card changes from start to end while its photo's pixels do not; twin: the same box on the cards sees the change).

title: One set of scene curves and one count for the welcome
detail: The four curves lived in Phase, in the De-dust scene and in the interface scene, and the fixed-cell count twice. Easing (pure functions) and Figures in ds/welcome.slint now serve every scene; Phase reads Easing. Checks: welcome_scenes_dedust and welcome_scenes_pages, unchanged pixels asserted.

title: The app stage: the real window and shell filmed offscreen on the app's own renderer
detail: oni-demos' offscreen FemtoVG-wgpu platform gains the event-loop proxy the shell's threads post to, and claims the system's menu bar as the app's macOS window does. AppStage hosts Shell::new and its MainWindow with the canvas texture shared with Slint (canvas: true, Display P3 as in the app): real pointer and key events through the window's own hooks, elements placed by accessible label or component, a film clock moved a frame at a time with the app left to rest at each (no render, write, heal or load in flight), real-pace gates, 8-bit snapshots and crops. World makes a folder of its own: photos copied under neutral names (Home / Scans / Roll 1), its own support and caches, a navigator rooted in it, no volume named, the roll kept as the last opened, the recalibration notice answered. The synthetic TIFF writer moves to oni_fixtures::tiff, shared with the window checks. Check tests/app_stage.rs: the canvas holds the photo's ramp (twin: the ground above it is flat), a bar key lights under the pointer, twin: a parked pointer changes no pixel. examples/app_stills shoots four states of the minimum window; against the running app driven through Slint's MCP server they are identical to the bit below the bar.

title: The welcome as a horizontal card
detail: WelcomeSheet is a 960 by 460 card in the sheet's fixed mode: a 560 by 460 stage on the left (WelcomeStyle.stage-width and DS.control-welcome-stage-height, tall enough for a film's crop to hold the bar down through a slider's row), a 400 column of words on the right (DS.control-welcome-words-width) with the footer at its foot. The card fits the 1100 by 680 window whole, so the sheet's own scroller never moves; in a shorter window the card takes the room between its margins, the stage crops (cover) and only the words scroll; narrower than 960 plus the margins, the words keep 400 and the stage takes the rest, and under 160 (WelcomeStyle.stage-least) the words take the card. Each page's words sit in a scroller of their own: a layout made by `if` inside the scroller's layout measured its wrapped lines unwrapped, so a long page could never be scrolled to its foot. Check: welcome_card (at 1100 by 680 on each page the words right of the stage, the key inside the card and the words still under the wheel, in each language the interface speaks; 1728 by 1017, 900 by 560 and 900 by 440 keep the key in the window; at 900 by 440 the last page scrolls and NEXT answers a click; twins: a page given a long heading scrolls, a 1100 by 300 window's card is shorter than the stage).

title: The welcome in four pages
detail: Cover, A calmer interface, Automatic De-dust, About 70 fixes and what changes. The conversion page goes: its three facts (converted on their own, a disk away converted when it comes back, 1.5 reads them read-only, two habits change) join the six fixes on the last page, Fixed on the left and Good to know on the right, the page without a stage. Each film page says three points, each one the film beside it shows. French and Spanish in the catalogues. Checks: help (Return turns the four pages and closes on the last), sheets, the catalogue.

title: The welcome's drawn scenes withdrawn
detail: The interface, De-dust, edits and fixes scenes drawn in Slint give way to films of the real app: welcome_interface*, welcome_dedust*, welcome_edits and welcome_fixes go with Cycle, Phase, Easing, Figures and SceneClock, and the three welcome_scenes window checks with them. ds/welcome.slint keeps WelcomeStyle, the stage and the dots; the photo's 3:2 token goes, WelcomePhoto takes the size it is given.

title: The welcome's film contract
detail: Help.welcome-clip, Help.welcome-clip-revision and Help.welcome-turned(int), as the plan fixes them: the film the stage shows on pages 1 and 2 is a texture rewritten in place, read through Picture.revision so the GPU path redraws it, empty until a player fills it, which leaves the stage's canvas ground. The sheet calls welcome-turned at each turn of its page; the shell names the first page as it opens and -1 as it closes.

title: A sheet no wider than its window
detail: Sheet's card takes its gauge or the window's width less its two margins, whichever is less, and says it as shown-width; the welcome lays its stage from it. Every other sheet is narrower than the smallest window, so none of them moves. Check: welcome_card at 900 wide (key inside the window), sheet_layout's centring of every modal sheet.

title: One clip player for Prepare the Roll's demos and the welcome's films
detail: Prepare's player decoded each frame on the interface thread. The shared player (app/player.rs) decodes on a thread of its own with one frame queued and the shown buffers handed back, writes each frame into one Rgba8Unorm texture and bumps a revision (read back as an image on the software renderer); a frame that moves nothing is neither written nor redrawn (Frames::next says whether it moved). Paces: once, resting on the last frame (Prepare), a loop (the welcome), still on the last frame (Reduce Motion). Dropping the player ends its decoder. Checks: app::player unit tests (once ends after every frame and an unmoved frame carries no pixels, twin: its neighbours do; a loop's fourth frame is the first, twin: the third is not; still hands the last frame alone, twin: not the first); window prepare waits for the demo's first frame, now a few milliseconds after its step.

title: The welcome's films by page and language, each under its ceiling
detail: oni_app::welcome: Film (interface on page 1, De-dust on page 2), the shipped table by film and language (empty until the films are made), the ceilings (1200 KiB interface, 900 KiB De-dust, 6 MiB for the six) and fits / weigh. Checks: every shipped film fits and ships in every language or none; twins: a file at its ceiling fits and a byte over fails, a width off the 1120 x 840 stage fails, a film in English alone fails, the six at their ceilings weigh over 6 MiB.

title: The welcome plays its page's film on the Help contract
detail: Help.welcome-clip, welcome-clip-revision and welcome-turned(int) (the page now shown, -1 as the sheet closes) declared as the lead plan fixes them; the card calls welcome-turned. Opening the sheet turns to page 0 and closing it to -1 from Rust too. A page with a film loops it, under Reduce Motion shows its last frame still, any other page or the sheet closing drops the decoder and the texture; a check hands its own films through Options.films. Check: welcome_clip on synthetic films (page 1 shows the film's size and more frames than it has on the rig's clock; twin: on page 0 the revision stands; page 2 its own film; Reduce Motion stands on the last frame, twin: not the first; closed, no picture and no frame asked).

title: The welcome's wipe: the before and the after joined in their real frames
detail: oni_demos::wipe joins two frames of one region by a hard edge travelling left to right: the after's pixels left of it, the before's right of it, no line, no mix. frames() gives the wipe at the film's rate, the edge eased, the first frame already moved and the last the after whole. Check wipe::tests: progress 0 is the before, 1 the after, halfway every column is its version's to the bit; twin: the halfway frame differs from both; frames of two sizes are refused.

title: The welcome's before: the real 1.5.6 window filmed on the app stage
detail: Lives on branch welcome/before-1.5.6 (cc93f509), cut from Version 1.5.6 and never merged: the app stage of #2010 laid into that tree and a before binary writing shot A's region of the real 1.5.6 window as RGBA8 PNG frames, the hand drawn, outside the repository. Only this entry reaches canvas.

title: The Help menu's surfaces held together; the welcome copy after the lead's R2
detail: State holds the console window, the welcome's film and where films come from as one help::Surfaces, and the clip player sits beside the help clips (help::player), so app.rs keeps its ceiling. Page 1 opens on 'Before, then now'; French names the edits 'réglages' and the dust patches 'retouches'. Checks: architecture (ceiling), welcome_clip, prepare, tutorial, catalogue.

title: A canvas tool's header shows its name whole in every language: over its keys when the line cannot hold both
detail: At the panel's fixed width (340 pt) the tool header laid its name, its '?' and two keycaps sized to their words on one line, the name the only thing that could give way: French 'Dépoussiérage' beside ANNULER and TERMINÉ elided to 'Dépoussié…'. ModeHeader moves into the design system beside the tool's ring (ds/modes.slint) and measures its one line unseen, as SheetFooter does: when the name and keys do not fit, the name takes a line of its own and the two keys share the line under it. It places its lines itself and offers its parent a height alone, so no layout around it asks a width of lines that follow their width (Slint's binding loop); the panel sizes the bar's room to the header. English keeps its one line. Checks: window mode_header (each tool's title laid at least as wide as its words want, at 1100x680, en/fr/es on the app profile; twin: a title longer than the panel is read cut, on HeaderProbe). A probe's import split left an empty import that stopped the interface's build; the names are split between two imports of ds.slint.

title: The welcome's stage at 502, its films 1120 × 1004, page 1's keycap point
detail: From the lead's R3: the stage is 502 tall so a film's crop ends in the free band under Tint's knob in 1.5.6 and 1.6 alike; the card is 960 × 502 and still fits 1100 × 680 whole; films are 1120 × 1004; page 1's third point says one keycap means the main action. Checks: welcome_card (card size, scroll twin), welcome::tests (size ceiling twins), catalogue.

title: The app stage withdrawn from the films
detail: The owner wants the welcome's shots staged from the real components, not the whole running app filmed: the app stage (app_stage.rs, world.rs, its stills example and its check) leaves oni-demos; the stage keeps its platform. Checks: oni-demos tests.

title: A demo names its stage's size and its photograph
detail: film::Demo gains size() and source(): the help cards keep their 244-point square and the demos' RAW by default, a welcome film takes the welcome's 560 by 502 stage and the photograph it is made of. Stage::instance() hands a timeline the scene's globals, keyboard and elements. Checks: oni-demos film, welcome.

title: An export shown as it is
detail: photo::plain::cover reads a JPEG export as the app reads a plain image (oni_decode::plain::read, the app's own Catmull-Rom reduction), its sRGB code values kept, cut to cover a box about a centre: never the conversion, never Prepare the Roll. The interface film's strip is bit for bit the 1.5.6 before's. Check: plain (a file's own values come back; twin: another centre is another cut). After R4: the strip is a window cut from the export reduced to 1600 on its long side (plain::window: 1600 by 1066, 440 by 1004 from row 28 about 0.24 of the width), past the film's black edge above and the holder's notches below, as the before cuts it; the films are shipped again from S2's frames recut alike. Check: plain (a window past the foot refused).

title: Every staged scene speaks the film's language
detail: Slint's interpreter reads @tr's English alone, so the stage compiles each scene through words::compile: every file it loads, the design system's and the panel's included, has each @tr text replaced by the catalogue the compiled interface bundles, a plural's two forms each their own, a text the catalogue lacks left English. One mechanism for the help demos, the welcome's interface and De-dust scenes. oni_i18n::translated is public for it. Checks: words (French texts, comments and plain strings untouched, the plural's forms; twin: English is the source), every scene compiles in every language (twin: a broken scene is seen).

title: The welcome's interface film in 1.6, staged
detail: scenes/welcome/interface.slint composes the owner's export as a 220-point strip beside a column at the panel's width: the bar's copy, paste, paste to the roll, Reset and EXPORT (glyphs alone, as the bar lays them short of room), the panel's tabs, the real ColorPane ended on a whole row. welcome::interface plays 6.7 s: the hand over copy and paste, onto Temperature's rail, a click on its number, -1.2 typed and Return, then down the panel's margin onto its ground. The components answer the pointer and the keys; the timeline answers Readouts and Store.step with the app's own slider_track and publishes as the app does. Checks: welcome (every scene holds layout and wiring only: no Path, colour, literal size or animation; twins for each), the typed figure changes Temperature's row and the Resets alone and lands the knob at -1.20's place, not its mirror; twin: without the click nothing changes; the photograph's pixels are the export's on every frame. The hand comes down from paste through the gap between Auto White Balance's keycap and the key beside it, over Temperature's number, so no keycap answers a hand only passing. The scene rule reads a token handed out to the timeline (an out property of colour) as no colour of the scene's; the De-dust scene's window ground is the column's Surface, not a colour of its own.

title: scripts/welcome shoots the interface film in three languages
detail: A thin script: ONI_WELCOME_PHOTO alone names the photograph, no path is written in the repository; the dev profile's interpreter speaks English, French and Spanish, so no compiled build is needed. The welcome binary writes each language's GIF, strip and stills; --before lays the 1.5.6 frames ahead (the wipe's join to come), --strip refuses a frame whose photograph is not the before's. The join: welcome::joined lays the 1.5.6 frames, wipe::frames' 0.9 s from the before's last frame to the film's first, then the film; the joined strip shows both and the edge. Check: joined (the before as shot, the edge begun on the wipe's first frame, landing on the after's first; twin: a hard cut has no frame of both). After R8b: the wipe's edge crosses the column alone, from the photograph's right edge, in 0.9 s eased (wipe::frames takes the column it starts from); each rest of the before's hand between two moves is held to 0.45 s (welcome::rested). A photograph the same on every frame is drawn once by the first frame's own colour table and never again, so the global palette goes to the interface and the rails run smooth (encode). The three films are shipped (resources/welcome/interface[.fr|.es].gif, 530 to 539 KB, 10.15 s) and welcome::SIZE is read from oni_app::welcome::SIZE. Checks: wipe (from a column, halfway is its middle; twin: over the whole width), rested (a short rest held, the opening and closing rests kept; twin: a frame of a move never held), film (a still photograph never drawn again, the rail given more shades; twin: a moving photograph shares the palette), welcome (shipped films fit and speak every language), welcome_clip.

title: The welcome's De-dust scene, composed of the app's own blocks

detail: The owner's review of 2026-11-16: the search pushed the column's content and its list was dense, its Add did nothing (the Row's key fires acted, which the view never heard; the window check called the callback and so never saw it), three components showed one piece, the To Validate list was odd, the service's mark was a word, Remove sat beside the positive keys, and the web pages were plain. Now: one PieceCard shows a piece in the Kit and in the search (KitMark kept, added, leaving, free); Add Gear opens KitSearchSheet over the window, its answers as cards two to a row with Add and Added; an added piece shows in the Kit at once, marked New, not saved yet, and a removal marks its card Leaves your Kit when you save, its trash a quiet glyph in the card's corner, Keep undoing it; KitSaveBar under the column counts the changes beside Discard and Save, Save asking first when a piece leaves; leaving the Kit with changes not saved asks Save Your Kit? (Later, Discard, Save), and quitting asks too. The Lens DB's mark is its own aperture icon (its disc and blades in the theme's inks) beside THE LENS DB. title: My Kit: a default body and lens for every export, compact Kit cards, the trash a key with its hover, the web sign-in as a two-step fold-out
detail: The owner's review of 2026-11-16. A Kit body or lens is set as default on its card (Set as Default, kept in collection.json while the Kit holds the piece): an export's line shows it where its sidecar keeps no camera or lens and its roll no body, over the scan's own camera and lens, which name the digitiser; nothing already named is ever replaced. Exported, a frame keeps the lens and the camera where a default showed, as written (a hand's change or clear included), so a later default moves nothing; a roll with no body takes the default body as the hand exports (one undo step, Set Camera Body), its frames then following the roll's body. A line's roll is read from the frame itself (its folder's marker, else its sidecar's film) when the archive gives none, so a project member outside the opened folder keeps its roll's body. Two adversarial reviews shaped it: defaults never enter what a line derives, and no rule holds a whole kept block, so an older build's block still yields to what derives. The Kit's cards are two short lines (name, Set as Default, trash; detail or state, a key to the service's page); the search keeps its full cards. The trash was a ghost key whose forced glyph ink cancelled its hover; it is the design system's destructive mini key. THE LENS DB stands as tall as the disc, so its capitals sit on its middle. Add Gear is a keycap. Kit is My Kit. The simulated site drops its breadcrumb for a fold-out: step 2 Authorize ONI shows folded from the first page, step 1 folds into a done row on the consent; its copy is shorter and plainer, its animation one fade. Checks: export::line tests (defaults, kept values, a frame's own roll) and the window check collection, which sets the defaults by click, exports and reads the roll and the sidecars.

title: The simulated sign-in: ONI joined to The Lens DB stands above the card

title: My Kit's cards in one short row

title: My Kit as a list ticked then acted on: clickable cards, a selection bar, sticky kind titles, a quieter head

A Kit card is one row: a box to tick, its name in the label face on one line and its detail or state under it, a Default badge when it is one; a click off the box opens its page on The Lens DB, so the arrow went. Ticked pieces raise a bar under the list: how many, Set as Default (one body and one lens at most, all saved; again on the defaults lets them go) and Remove (Keep when all are leaving), and a key that clears the ticks. The head stays still while the list scrolls under it: My Kit with Disconnect beside it, Add Gear, then Catalogue provided by and The Lens DB's mark; the account's line and the note at the foot went. title: My Kit: light cards with a menu and photo counts, Disconnect in Settings, the gear fields as Kit cards, the search's quick filters

The library index (schema 12) caches each photo's camera and lens its sidecar's EXIF line keeps and the body its folder's roll marker names, refreshed off the interface thread as an export writes each frame and as the app writes a marker (roll_written) or reads a folder again; LibraryIndex::gear_counts, a query reading no disk, counts a body by the kept camera, else the folder roll's body, else the sidecar's film, and a lens by the kept lens, trash, passes and sheets left out, a respelt row keeping its own line; the Kit counts again when its column shows and when an export ends. One design-system piece, GearCardBody (name, Default badge, detail, photos), shows gear in the Kit, the search and the fields: the roll's Camera Body and the export's Camera and Lens list the Kit's pieces as these cards, then the names typed in ONI the Kit does not hold.
