Checks: oni-library gear tests, kit words tests, oni-tldb brand search, and the window check collection (filters, menus, defaults, counts after an export, the Camera Body field's cards, Disconnect from Settings).

title: Sidecar format 23: an EXIF line releases the values that are only its scan's own facts
detail: The owner's decision of 2026-11-17. Builds 1.4.0 to 1.5.6 kept a frame's whole export line, and format 22 kept it as a hand's, so the digitiser's camera, lens, ISO and date won over the roll's body and the Kit's defaults in exports and in the Kit's photo counts (3 of 43 frames of roll #8). A sidecar of format 22 and under now releases each camera, lens, iso, date, artist or copyright whose trimmed value is not empty and equals the original's own fact as an export reads it (migrate::Facts::exif, oni_export::scan_metadata through the app's lookup); a clear ("") always stays (#1907), the film is never touched, a value that differs stays, and a scan that says nothing releases nothing. The original is read only when the line holds a value; away in the cloud or unreadable, the line stays as it is and the file still reaches format 23, writable. The library index reads a sidecar's line as an export does, released in memory, and each row keeps the sidecar format it was read from (schema 13): a folder's read reads again every row of an earlier format, so a file brought by any path (a measure, a race, a failed write) settles its row, and one that cannot be brought is read again, about 1 ms a frame; the sweep reads its folders' rows again at once, and an index write that fails is logged without a name. A named format-22 document reads as written. Two adversarial reviews shaped it (clears kept, no file held read-only, the index never behind its sidecars). Checks: oni-settings tests/scan_line.rs and the step's unit tests, the export line and Kit counts in oni-app, the gate's and the sweep's index re-reads, each with its twin; on copies of roll #8's three frames the line keeps only its clears and the export names the Leica M6.

title: Windows CI green again: two checks spelled Unix paths, the Kit check clicked under the export's toast, frame_owner raced the full resolution's dwell
detail: oni-settings: the corpus laid each original under the whole draft path on Windows (stem split on '/' only), now its file name through Path; held.rs stripped '/' off a Windows temporary folder, now the /private spelling is tried only where the path has that root. collection.rs clicked (500, 700) to come back to the Kit, where a slow runner still shows the export's toast; it clicks the gallery's empty room (800, 400) clear of it and says when the Kit is not shown. frame_owner::a_preview_landing_for_a_frame_left_changes_nothing held the decode places after B rendered, assuming B's own full resolution (built after a 1 s dwell) had not started; on WARP it had, so the check saw B's own full resolution. The check now waits for B's full resolution, leaves to the gallery (released), holds both places and reopens B, whose next full build then always waits. Proved by slowing renders and decodes locally: the old check fails 3/3 with CI's message, the new one passes; the twin (no wants guard) still fails. Not touched: full_release.rs:42 can meet the same dwell on a slow runner; medal_keys failed once in three runs on its animation sampling.

title: More Color Settings: each channel's own white and black point, under the Colour block (sidecar format 24)
detail: The owner's request for the Digital feature, lot L1. Print gains channelWhite and channelBlack, three values each (red, green, blue), laid on Lighting's White point and Black point in their units and on their tracks (white ±1/3, black ±0.2, a stored value past its track landing on its stop), per frame, travelling with Lighting in presets and paste (print.channelWhite, print.channelBlack), never written at zero. Print.reaching folds them per channel: each window takes the global pair plus its channel's own, held to the minimum span as the global pair is (Print::held_points_of, Print::channel_points); with every point at zero it returns the windows untouched, so no render moves (the render of two roll #8 frames as Negative, Positive and B&W, with and without Lighting's points, hashed bit for bit before and after). The roll's colour factor reads each channel's own reach; the points' saturation (points_curve) stays the global pair's, a channel's point being a colour move, not a contrast. Black and white shows no channel and reads none. The panel: a More Color Settings disclosure at the end of the Colour block (so on Negative and Positive, hidden on B&W), the design system's own fold, folded until opened, with its Reset; six ramp sliders tinted by their channel, whites then blacks as Lighting lays them (fields 32-37, block 11). Sidecar format 24: a format 23 document reads them at zero and is brought by the sweep (the newer-format corpus file moves to version-25, the goldens gain the two fields). tone.rs and app.rs split to stay under the size ceiling (tone/contrast.rs, tone/color_density.rs, tone/tests.rs, app/store_fields.rs). Checks: oni-settings tone tests and tests/channel_points.rs (zero writes no key, clamping, held sums, format 23 read at zero; twins), oni-pipeline conversion::points and decompression unit tests (one channel's point moves its window alone, the global fold to the bit at zero, black and white ignores them; twins) and tests/channel_points.rs (a channel's point leads the render's move on its channel on Negative and Positive, equal offsets reach the kernel as the global points, B&W bit-equal; twins), oni-core knob and the kept-balance looks, and the window check channel_points (the fold opens on its title, each slider by the pointer moves its own point and the Reset clears it, red's point lifts red's histogram, B&W lays none; twins). The folded row moves Lighting's title under the fold of a 680 pt window, so help_card's short-window check brings it up by the wheel first.

title: Digital, a fourth film type: ONI as a plain editor of digital photos, its white in kelvin and tint
detail: The owner's request of 2026-11-18 (lot L3 of the Digital plan). ConversionMode::Digital ("digital", sidecar format 25) reads on the positive axis and renders no film block: in the pipeline the capture's exposure, the flat-field, the reciprocal, the gains, the roll's windows (LevelsSet::neutral in their place, so Lighting's points still reach), the print's filters, chroma decompression, the dye separation and the Scanner face are left out, their stored values kept for a film mode. Its colour is a white (PipelineSettings.white, kelvin and DNG tint, + toward magenta): oni_settings::white ports the DNG SDK's dng_temperature on Robertson's 31 isotherms, and conversion::white lays one relative Bradford matrix on linear Rec. 2020 between framed and stage47 through the color_matrix kernel, from the white chosen to the decode's own (5000 K / 0 for a mosaic, D65 for any other file), so the decode stays pinned and the graph holds no new stage at the decode's white or on a film. A RAW's As Shot is read once from LibRaw's cam_mul (copied at the end of pinned.c's struct after open, no knob, no pixel) through its cam_xyz (oni_decode::as_shot), stored as PipelineSettings.shot when the frame first becomes digital by any gesture (the store's one write path: EditorStore::read_shots, set by the shell), its white resting there; a double click and the Colour block's reset return to it. Classification of the former Positive tests: reads_positive (invert, gain sense, resting black/mid/exposure, density rest, rendered ceiling, points saturation's sense, a folder's roll, no opening measure window, no slide roll of one in a balance), is_slide (5500 K decode and its Reading, Prepare's slide steps), is_film (every film block, the Scanner face). UI: Film Type's fourth tab; on a digital photo the Roll tab shows Film Type and Scan Profile alone, the bar no faces, the Colour block Temperature (K) and Tint (fields 38, 39, after More Color Settings' six) in place of the filters, no Auto White Balance; Prepare the Roll is disabled in the editor and its film step opens on a negative's for a digital frame. The phone link reads Digital as Positive, its Temperature and Tint move the white and its Roll tab shows no film block; the store refuses the Scanner face. app.rs's paint check moved to its own file to stay under its ceiling. Checks: white maths against the table's nodes, D65 and illuminant A by McCamy, the round trip and the decode's two neutrals bit for bit; the relative matrix is the identity at its white and neutralises a grey card under its light (twins: 10 K off, the inverse direction, the tint's sign); As Shot on roll #8 (5110 K, +10.5); a plain file in Digital at its white renders bit for bit as a Positive at rest, a prepared negative's blocks reach no Digital render, a white reaches no film render (twins: a tungsten white, a slide's blocks, a Digital white); store: two RAWs and a JPEG made digital together each rest on their own As Shot in one undo step, a roll's frame its own, a moved white survives Negative and back, the Scanner face refused; window check digital::digital_shows_its_white_and_none_of_the_films_blocks through the real Film Type tabs (twin: the negative's blocks). Measured once: twelve renders of two roll #8 frames (Negative, Positive and B&W at rest, their own sidecar, edited, an edited slide) hash bit for bit the same before and after. Merged onto More Color Settings (#2090): the white is fields 38, 39 after its six, sidecar format 25 follows its 24, knob.rs's tests moved to knob/tests.rs to stay under the size ceiling, and the window check channel_points also finds More Color Settings on a digital photo (its twin, B&W, lays none).

title: Grain: a film-like texture in stops on the scene before Lighting and Colour, anchored on the scan's full-resolution grid; sidecar format 26
detail: Digital lot L2. PipelineSettings.grain {amount, size} (amount 0..1 rest 0, size 0..1 rest 0.5), a look field (paste, presets, the preset row grain), per frame; sidecar format 26 (absent reads rest), the corpus' newer-format file moved to version-27. One per-pixel stage in Pipeline::chain between the framed image and stage47, laid in stage47's own pass, so it reaches the editor, the tiles, the export and nothing else at rest: at amount 0 or on a measurement the chain holds no grain stage (its recipe key unchanged). The field is value noise on a cubic B-spline lattice (no lattice pattern: a point's variance moves 8 % with its place, against a factor 4 for smoothstep value noise), standard normals from PCG-2D through four 16-bit uniforms (bit-equal on CPU and GPU, no transcendental), its cell GRAIN_FINEST = 1/6000 of the scan's full width (the one length every reduction keeps exactly) times 4^size. Each output pixel reads the field's exact mean over its footprint (the spline's integral per axis, at most 7 nodes an axis, a 3-cell cap past which the cap's mean is scaled to the whole footprint's spread), mapped back through the turns and the angle (geometry::scan_from; a crop keeps coordinates), so a pan, a region render, a crop or a turn leaves each scan pixel its grain and a reduced render (preview, half-size decode, gesture) reads the full one's grain averaged. Multiplicative and monochrome: v · 2^(0.5 · amount · G), G of spread 1 at full resolution. UI: a Film Effects block after Effects (Grain, Grain size, percent readouts), shown on every mode until the Digital lot gates it. The Store's setter table moved to app/store_fields.rs, app.rs back under 400 lines. Checks: oni-render kernel::grain unit tests (spline integral, normals, footprint spread, a mean over a footprint the mean of its quarters); oni-pipeline tests/grain.rs: GPU against the scalar reference on five branches and fused with stage47 (twin: lattice one node over; grain after the print), a region, a crop, two turns (twin: grain on the output grid), reduced renders exact at 1/2 and 1/4 (3.6e-7, twin: point sample) and within 15 % past the cap at 1/10 and 1/20 (twin: unscaled cap), the same spread in stops on three greys and every channel (twin: additive), rest and measure keys (twin: amount 0.01), contrast steepening it 1.6 times as it lies under the print (twin: grain on the print, unmoved); window check film_effects (a press on Grain's rail, the block's Reset, shots at fit and 100 %).

title: Halation: the highlights' red glow through the film's base, on the scene before the grain and the print
detail: The owner's extension of lot L2. PipelineSettings.halation {amount, size} (each 0..1, rest 0 and 0.5), a look field (paste, presets, the preset row halation), per frame; sidecar format stays 26 (absent reads rest). In Pipeline::chain: framed, then halation, then the grain in stage47's pass; absent at amount 0 and on a measurement (recipe key unchanged). Each channel's light past HALATION_THRESHOLD (0.6, linear) weighted by HALATION_COLOUR (red 1, green 0.3, blue 0: the red layer lies on the base) is blurred by the existing Gaussian (a new Before::Halation folds the source into the rows pass's taps, no pass of its own), deviation 0.001 to 0.004 of the scan's width (4^size; the same share at every scale, a region's margin the blur's own reach), and the pixel takes amount · (glow − its own source): light moved from the highlight to its edge, never added, so each channel's sum holds and a wide highlight keeps its light. Kernels: wgsl/halation_source.wgsl (the taps' step) and wgsl/halation.wgsl beside kernel/halation.rs. UI: Halation and Halation size join Grain in the Film Effects block, same visibility. Constants (threshold, colour, widths) await the owner's eye. Checks: oni-pipeline tests/halation.rs: GPU against cpu::gaussian and the reference (1e-7; twin: the glow of the whole picture), channel sums kept to 1e-4 and blue untouched, a red glow with a little green (twin: the glow added), reduced renders against the full one's means 2.6 % of the glow's peak at 1/2 and 5.9 % at 1/4, the threshold read on reduced pixels (twin: the full deviation, over 20 %), a region bit-equal to the whole frame's cut (twin: a blur reading no margin), rest and measure keys (twin: amount 0.01), two stops of print exposure raising the glow 1.16 times as it lies under the print (twin: on the print, 1.00); window check film_effects::a_press_on_halations_rail_makes_a_highlight_glow_red (presses on both rails, shots at fit and 100 %: an orange-red glow hugging the window, the lamp and the wire). Merged onto the Digital mode (#2100) and More Color Settings (#2090): Grain and Halation are fields 40-43 and Film Effects block 12 after their lots, sidecar format 26 follows 25 (the newer-format corpus file is version-27), and the two are a digital photo's alone (owner's call): the panel lays Film Effects only on Digital (Field::shown_in too) and Pipeline::chain lays neither stage on a film mode, the value kept. fields.rs's knob table moved to fields/knob.rs to stay under the size ceiling. Checks: film_effects opens its frame as Digital and finds no Film Effects on the same frame as a negative, its grain kept; the pipeline's rest checks render a negative holding a grain or a halation as the negative at rest (twin: the Digital one, a stage).

title: The full suite after the Digital merges: the preset sheet holds its boxes again, the Film Type card's text, the welcome scene's foot
detail: Grain and Halation had joined the preset sheet's Colour column, which then ran past the sheet at 1280 × 800 (presets check). They now stand in a Film Effects block of their own in the second column, as the panel shows them, and the Scanner Keypad joins the Settings block, which keeps its comment: the two columns end level and the sheet holds every box. help_demo_roll expects the Film Type card's text that names the digital photo. title: A film type changed by any gesture lands each value still on the old mode's rest on the new mode's rest
detail: The owner's polish list for Digital, item 2. A negative at rest (+1.50 EV) switched to Digital kept +1.50 EV while Digital rests at 0, and Positive the same: the open frame's Command::Mode laid parameters::carried, then put its print exposure back (a rule kept from the port), and a roll's frames took the mode alone through roll_settings::copied, their exposure never carried. The rule now lives once on the settings, PipelineSettings::carried (moved from oni-core's parameters): the density ceiling, each window's black and the print exposure still on the old mode's rest take the new mode's, a value the hand placed stays; Command::Mode is that rule whole, and roll_settings::copied carries the frame's own rests whenever it hands a frame the donor's mode, so the roll's frames, a frame joining a roll and the open frame all land alike. The white keeps its own rest, the file's As Shot, laid by the store's write path when a frame first becomes digital. Checks (oni-core store::tests::modes): every mode's rest carried to every mode, mosaic or not, stands on the new mode's rest whole, and an exposure, a ceiling and a black placed by hand stay (twin: the former open-frame rule, exposure kept, leaves +1.50 EV on a digital photo); a measured roll turned digital from its open frame lands the open frame and the roll's frame at rest on Digital's rest, a frame whose exposure was placed keeps it, and one undo takes every frame back to +1.50 EV.

title: A frame beside the open one keeps its own white when the open frame turns digital
detail: The owner's polish list for Digital, item 6, reported by the Digital lot. The frames edited together took a film type changed on the open frame as a structured write, its every moved leaf laid on them: the open frame's As Shot white, which the store's write path reads off that frame's own file when it first becomes digital, landed on a frame beside already digital, outside the open frame's roll, as if the hand had moved it (and, with #2130, the open frame's exposure would have landed on a negative beside that keeps its mode). The source: a mode change is no leaf to copy but a rule each frame applies to itself. title: Temperature's track is even in mired, its arrows a notch of 2 mired, a number typed landing on itself
detail: The owner's polish list for Digital, item 1. The kelvin slider was bent about 5000 K: its right half ran 5000 to 25000 K, as many mired as a sliver of its left, so the warm end crawled and the cool end leapt. The track now lays the existing range (2000 to 25000 K) even in mired, a million over the kelvin, as raw editors do: track::Bend (Even, Centre, Mired) replaces Spec.centre, the kelvin field takes Bend::Mired, the sharpening radius keeps its centre, and white::KELVIN_CENTRE goes. Daylight stands at 65 % of the travel. The stored value stays kelvin. An arrow's, accessibility's or the readout's minus and plus step was one unit of the readout's last digit, 1 K, a fiftieth of a mired near daylight: on a kelvin readout it is now a notch of 2 mired, landed on the round figure as fine as one notch there (1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten), 50 K a press near daylight, 10 K near 2000 K, 500 K near 20000 K; a wheel already moved a share of the track, now even in mired too. A number typed over a readout was counted in the same steps as an arrow's; it now goes its own way, Slider.typed and Store.typed (the store, the band, quality, roll, brush and sensitivity sliders and the keyboard probe wire it as their step was), so 5617 typed lands on 5617 K. Checks: oni-app track::a_mired_track_is_even_to_the_eye_and_its_own_inverse (every hundredth of the travel moves the same mired within 0.1 %, the inverse exact, 5000 K at 300/460; twin: the former track bent about 5000 K varies its mired a step more than 20 times); slider_track::a_kelvin_notch_is_even_in_mired_and_reads_a_round_figure (5000 to 5050 K and back, D65 to 6600 K, 2000 to 2010 K, 20000 to 21000 K, every press from end to end between 1 and 4 mired, held at both ends, a typed 5617 landing on itself; twin: the readout's digit, 1 K, moves under 0.05 mired); window check digital: an increment from a TIFF's D65 reads 6600 K; keyboard::a_number_typed_over_a_slider_readout_steps_it_there through the new typed path.

title: Prepare the Roll keeps its first step alone for a digital roll
detail: Owner's words: we keep the wizard but only its first step in Digital. Film type gains Digital in Prepare's film step; on it every step but Film is skipped (Step::skipped), the step tabs dark. One rule names the walk's end for every film type: walk_ends(step) is the step whose next is itself, its keycap PREPARE ROLL (key now takes capture and film), roll_advance commits there and measure_roll dispatches Positive to the slides, Digital to prepare_digital, film to the measure. set_film lands a skipped step on the window, or on the film step where the window is skipped too. Digitised with, the pass order, the grouping row, its caution and the passes note stand under !Preparing.digital (new property). The action is live on Digital while the roll holds a frame: the film step shows no frame grid, so every photo of the roll is prepared, as its detail says. title: PREPARE ROLL on Digital makes every photo of the roll digital, each on its own As Shot, in one step
detail: EditorStore::make_digital(paths) lays store::roll::digital (carried to Digital, roll_reference cleared, as a new preparation replaces the old) through lay_on: the open frame through lay_open and replace, the others through modify, each passing rested_white so every RAW reads its own As Shot; one history step labelled measure_label(n), every roll found again on the next ask. No journal entry: nothing was measured. prepare/digital.rs posts its landing on the drafts' serial thread, so the reads and migrations queued on entering never rewrite a sidecar after it (Stop until then writes nothing), then makes every file of the roll as it came digital (passes a grouping only proposed each on their own, as no measure registers them) and lands through land_prepared, the tail factored out of land_measure (drafts dropped, editor on the first frame alone or on the whole roll as Settings asks, message told), which the measure now calls too after prepare_ended. Check store::tests::digital::a_roll_prepared_as_digital_reads_each_as_shot_once_and_leaves_its_reference_in_one_step: three frames (open RAW, RAW beside, plain file) end digital with no reference and each white its own As Shot, one undo brings all three back on their roll, a redo with another frame open keeps the RAWs' As Shot read once (twin: the measure's land_roll writes the frame beside with shot None).

The make_digital check counts each RAW's As Shot read once through make, undo and redo; with the old lay_open it read a.NEF twice.

It now reads measured_or_slide, the rule the roll card and the navigator already use (measured, a slide or a digital photo). Window check prepare_digital: B, made digital by the commit, opens in the editor with no sheet (with the old gate the check fails there).

title: Prepare on a digital photo through the real controls, and Film Type's four tabs on Prepare's film step

Back on Digital, a click on PREPARE ROLL closes the sheet on A in the editor, both digital with no roll reference and no draft left; one undo brings both back on their roll, B a negative, and redo lays it again. film_type_fit now also measures Prepare's four film tabs in French, Spanish and English (252.6, 240.1 and 246.4 pt of a 292 pt track; twin: the three film tabs alone measure less). help_demo_roll's Film Type text follows the new help.

title: A digital photo's own levels on the picture, laid in the curves' tables; sidecar format 27
detail: PipelineSettings.picture_levels ("pictureLevels"): five windows, RGB, Luma, R, G and B, each a Levels resting at Levels::default() on 0 to 1, absent read as rest (PICTURE_LEVELS_VERSION 27, no migration step; the broken corpus file becomes version-28, read as Newer(28)) and unwritten at rest, so a film frame's sidecar carries none. Levels::transfer is the film window's B(t^γ) between black and white, 0 under the black (a negative value passes, the kernel reading it at the table's 0) and, past the white, a line at the slope it reached, γ/(w−b)·4(1−c3), so highlights past it keep their gradation; at rest it is the identity. finishing::curves(set, levels) composes each channel's table as C_ch ∘ L_rgb ∘ L_ch, the linked table as C_link with its contrast, the luma table as C_luma ∘ L_luma (luma is the kernel's last step, so Luma acts after the RGB curves and keeps the hue, one gain on the three); a curve read past its own 1 goes on at slope 1, as the kernel reads it. The kernel (curves.wgsl and its CPU twin) reads past 1 at rgb_at(1)[c] + (v − 1)·ends[c], luma at bent.w: ends are the levels' slopes there, 1 for curves alone, so every existing curves render is bit-identical. The pipeline lays them on Digital alone (a film mode keeps them stored, unrendered) and keys its tables on (CurveSet, Option<PictureLevels>). Measures rest them wherever they rest the manual curves. Look field: pasted, in Apply to Roll, preset row pictureLevels (25 handles) under the box Levels in Colour, before Curves as the panel lays them; one box more ran the save sheet's Colour column 9 pt past its footer at 1280 x 800, so the Carries boxes stand Space.xxs apart instead of Space.xs (2 pt a row), and the presets window check's fit now measures every box, not two named ones, as it had missed Halation's (a check that cannot see the bug); Field::PictureLevels joins ordered::bends, so a patched end is laid through set_black/set_white and never crosses that frame's other end. Knob::Picture(LevelsChannel, Handle): ends held to 0..1 and kept in order, inner handles on their ranges. LevelsChannel::is_density(mode) is true on film alone. Checks: oni-settings picture_levels (identity at rest on [−0.5, 2], continuity and slope past the white by finite difference, twin film's t − u; a format-26 document reads them at rest, twin a current one keeps them; rest writes no key, twin), finishing (tables bit for bit at rest for a resting and a bent set, twin a moved handle; R moves red alone, RGB the three, Luma keeps the hue, twin RGB turns it; ends equal the composite's slope, twin slope 1), branches::curves_with_picture_levels_go_on_past_one_at_their_slopes (GPU against CPU on values under 0, inside, past 1 and luma under 1e-4, twin the reference at slope 1), digital.rs (film modes keep key, stage count and pixels with levels stored, also with a curve; levels back at rest leave no stage; twin Digital lays the stage; B after A on one pipeline is a fresh B, twin A and B differ), oni-measure picture_levels and truncate (readings before the curves equal the resting frame's, twin past them), knob (a black at −0.3 lands on 0, twin a film black goes under), ordered (a patched black held short of the frame's white, twin the leaves cross), the corpus goldens and the presets' completeness checks.

title: Levels on a digital photo's Colour tab: RGB, Luma, R, G and B in the Levels editor, over the curves' input histogram
detail: The owner's words: in Digital the per-channel levels move to the Colour tab as a Levels block with a mode selector RGB / Luma / R / G / B, per frame, with the Levels editor's look and handles and its histogram; it stands beside More Color Settings and Lighting's points even where redundant. One editor: editors::levels::Windows is a film's three windows on the density axis or a digital photo's five on the picture, read by steps, rested, marked, readouts, the press, drag and scroll; Edit::Levels carries it, the reset rests each frame's own (rested_windows), the plots, gestures, knob springs and Reset::Levels are shared, the two blocks never showing together. LevelsEditor gains picture, its tabs RGB, Luma, R, G, B in the Curves' order, the tab held to those shown; Editors.picture-levels-folded is remembered under "Levels". The Colour tab lays the block before Curves on Digital alone. The levels histogram on Digital is the curves' input reading (what enters the levels), the film's Stage::Levels reading skipped. The reset key beside frames together reads each frame by its own windows. Checks: levels unit tests (five windows on the picture, the white at the track's end, a step names Knob::Picture, tabs lit; twin a film writes Knob::Level on three tabs), a gesture test on a real store (a drag writes the green window alone, a double click puts it back, the reset rests five; twin a negative's reset leaves a stored picture window), and the window check digital_levels::a_digital_photos_levels_move_each_mode_through_the_real_editor (each tab clicked, each white dragged by the pointer writes that window alone and renders, R lifts the red histogram alone, a double click puts it back, the block's Reset rests five; twin a negative lays no Levels on Colour and three tabs on Roll). Strings: Levels (Niveaux, Niveles) and its help.

title: Lens Corrections on a digital photo: Distortion, Red fringe, Blue fringe and Vignetting by hand; sidecar format 28
detail: Digital lot P3. PipelineSettings.lens_correction ("lensCorrection") {distortion, red, blue, vignetting}, each -100..100 rest 0, a look field (paste, Apply to Roll, the preset row lensCorrection, the box Lens Corrections in the Settings block, offered by a copy but left unticked by a new preset, as a preset is meant for other lenses' photos); sidecar format 28 (absent reads rest, chain::LENS_CORRECTION_VERSION), the corpus' newer-format file moved to version-29. A film mode keeps the values unrendered (PipelineSettings::lens and optical_vignetting are None there). The map is DNG WarpRectilinear's radial form per channel (oni_settings::lens::Radial, r_d = r_u (k0 + k1 r^2 + ...), the scan's half-diagonal the unit, read through the sides' ratio alone so every scale of one shape maps alike to the bit): k = -0.2 distortion/100 (a positive value corrects barrel), each fringe a channel scale 1 - 0.002 value/100 (deviation from the plan, which had +: the slider's red or blue end now enlarges that channel, its fringe moving outward toward the colour the end names, as Filtration's ends name the colour moved toward). Fill rule: the largest zoom z <= 1 with every channel's factor at most 1 at the boundary's extreme radii (the nearest edge and the corner), bisection 60 steps; a barrel correction keeps z = 1. Inverse by Newton on r P(r^2), held below green's fold. UI: a Lens Corrections block (block 13, fields 44-47, whole signed readouts, Readout::Tint renamed SignedWhole for both) on the Roll tab under PanelState.digital, after Film Type and Scan Profile, where P1's Source tab shows it after the merge; the phone shows none of the four on purpose. Checks: oni-settings lens unit tests (rest, fill to 1e-12 on four corrections with an unzoomed twin, aspect-only zoom with a square-scan twin, from_source undoing to_source to 1e-9 with an unzoomed twin, the fold at sqrt(1/0.6)); tests/lens_sidecar.rs (a format-26 file reads none, four values round-trip, twin: the key dropped; a paste carries them; a film mode renders none, twin: Digital); preset_parameters (a moved lens left unticked yet offered, twin: changed() names it); fields tests (readouts, the Roll tab's order, block 13's reset key).

title: The lens warp: stage 0's turns and angle and the radial map in one read, only while a lens correction is set
detail: oni-render kernel/warp.rs beside wgsl/warp.wgsl: each output pixel's centre through stage 0's map T (the turn table as points, then the rotation, as scan_from had it) onto the corrected scan, then each channel read bilinearly at centre + P_ch(r^2) d, alpha green's; one fetch while red and blue rest on green's map. oni-pipeline stages::Warped ("warp") replaces Oriented and Resample in geometry::apply only when PipelineSettings::lens is Some; with no lens the path, the stages and every recipe key are untouched. Its input_region is exact: the output's box through T, the channels' least and most factor on its radii (ends and the roots of P'), the box's corners scaled about the centre by both, outset a pixel. Edges repeat with no angle (the fill reads to the last half pixel), transparent with one. The extent, the crop and OpaqueEdge are unchanged. Optical vignetting: stages::optical_vignette reuses the vignette kernel circular in pixels (both half sides half-diagonal/sqrt 2, midpoint 0, hunt 0), 2^(-stops r^2) with stops -2 vignetting/100, on the scan after the patches in Pipeline::healed, Digital only. Grain stays anchored on the corrected picture (scan_from leaves the lens out). Checks: tests/lens_warp.rs: GPU against cpu::warp on barrel, pincushion, fringes alone, both, a turn with a mirror and 7 degrees (errors 2.7e-6 to 7.6e-6; twins red and blue read at green's place or k1 5 % off), a region on the tilted frame's edge (twin: edges repeated); the input region holds every tap on corners and middles of three corrections (twin: the turns' map alone misses a pincushion corner's taps); a lens-corrected Digital frame (distortion -80, fringes +-60, vignetting, 3 degrees, a crop) at half scale renders four regions, corners included, bit-equal to the whole's cut (twin: the cut a pixel over); fill: four strong corrections leave no clear pixel (twin: the pincushion unzoomed leaves its corners clear); film modes with a stored lens keep key and stage count, Digital at rest turned and tilted keeps the turns' stages, Distortion 30 lays one warp for two (twin), vignetting alone lays one stage on the scan. tests/lens_placing.rs: optical vignetting 4^u at the corner, circular on a 3:2 scan to 1e-5 (twin: the creative ellipse), a patch taking the gain where it lies (twin: ungained); the grain's arguments unmoved by a lens.

title: Dust stays on the scan under a lens correction: every marker and stroke maps through PipelineSettings::placing
detail: oni_settings Placing carries the lens's Radial (Placing::through): on_frame maps a scan point through from_source then the turns, on_scan the turns then to_source. PipelineSettings::placing(size) composes it; the app's State::placing (markers, strokes painted, reminders), auto De-dust's mapping back, dust_probe, dust_census and the demos read it; migrate/strokes keeps Geometry::placing, format-21 strokes predating the lens. Strokes stay on the scan and patches are laid before the warp, so a lens change moves no stroke. Checks: tests/lens_placing.rs: at distortion -60 a speck's rendered centroid lies 0.02-0.04 px from settings.placing's on_frame on five framings (whole, cropped, a quarter turn, mirrored, 3 degrees), on_scan undoes it to 1e-9, a point pushed off the frame maps outside it (twin: Geometry::placing alone misses by more than 3 px); a half-scale preview puts the speck 0.007 px from the full frame's with distortion and fringes (twin: the radius read in full-resolution pixels moves it more than 2 px). Window checks lens::each_lens_slider_lays_its_correction_and_moves_the_canvas (a drag on Distortion, presses on the three others, the sidecar written, the canvas moved, shots at strong pincushion and barrel corrections; twin: a negative lays no Lens Corrections, values kept) and lens::a_stroke_on_a_distorted_picture_is_kept_under_the_hand (a click near a corner at distortion -60 stores placing.on_scan of the click and its marker lands under it within 1 pt; twin: the geometry's map alone keeps a point more than 3 px away). Adversarial review of the placement and sidecar paths: markers re-map at every edit's publish and render landing, so a lens move redraws them; a point the map cannot reach (past a barrel correction's fold) lands off the frame, never on it; a stored value past -100..100 (a hand-edited sidecar) would fold the map inside the frame, so LensCorrection clamps its shares where the map is built (check lens::a_value_past_the_range_maps_as_its_end, twin: 99 against 100); format-21 strokes keep Geometry::placing, as they predate the lens. Merged onto Source and Levels (#2140-#2151): sidecar format 28 follows Levels' 27 (PICTURE_LEVELS_VERSION, then LENS_CORRECTION_VERSION), the newer-format corpus file is version-29 and every golden holds both pictureLevels and lensCorrection; the document's field counts (oni-core declared names, codec_checks keys) are 50 and the look's fields 20, each lot having counted its own alone.

title: Halation sensitivity: the threshold past which a digital photo's highlights glow, a slider beside Halation and Halation size
detail: The owner's words: Halation gets a Sensitivity, the level of highlight that starts to bloom. Halation.sensitivity ("sensitivity", stops, rest 0, SENSITIVITY_RANGE -1..2, absent read as 0): oni_pipeline::halation::threshold = HALATION_THRESHOLD x 2^-sensitivity, so -1 EV glows only light past 1.2 (past a JPEG's white) and +2 EV from 0.15 (the upper midtones); the knee stays hard and each channel keeps its own threshold. The constant leaves the shaders: halation_source(s, threshold) in WGSL and its CPU reference, the blur's pre-step reading it from the Gaussian's free lane (Before::Halation(threshold) writes bytes 8..12 as Coeff does) and the halation pass from its dose's second lane. At rest 0.6 x 2^-0 is 0.6 to the bit: 22 renders (two roll #8 frames, the four modes at rest, a sidecar's own, an edited negative, each mode bent with filters, halation, grain and channel points, an edited slide) hash identical before and after the whole change. A Sensitivity notch reruns the blur and the pass as a Size notch does (3.7 to 11.5 ms on 2000 to 3000 px wide, measured by the investigator). Field 48 Halation sensitivity (fr Sensibilité du halo, es Sensibilidad de la halación), Readout::Stops, after Halation size in Film Effects, Digital only, in the halation preset row and Apply to Roll; the Film Effects help names it. Checks: tests/halation.rs, the GPU against halation_source at 0.6 and 0.3 (errors 1.0e-7 and 1.2e-7; twins the unthresholded glow 0.53 and, at 0.3, the rest's threshold 0.12), threshold at rest bit-equal to 0.6 (twin 0.01 EV differs), a sensitivity at amount 0 lays no stage and moves the key once halation is on; knob (held to its track, writes Field::Halation); window check film_effects on the night TIFF: the ring beside the lit window reads red 3.8 unlit, 48.1 at rest, 3.8 at sensitivity -0.88 (threshold above the window's 1.0) and 73.1 at +1.79 (twin).

title: Each channel's own Mid and Contrast in the print, after Lighting's curve; sidecar format 29
detail: Print.channel_mid ("channelMid") and Print.channel_contrast ("channelContrast"), unwritten at rest, clamped on read to ZONE_RANGE (+-0.25) and CONTRAST_RANGE (+-0.5). The fused kernel's per-channel pass becomes the channel's own Tone after the RGB curve: Lighting's contrast family about its 0.18-grey pivot, then the filter's stops, then the Mids bump p + m 16p^2(1-p)^2 on 0..1 (midded), exactly Tone { contrast, mids }.shaped(p, filter); two rows more in Stage47 (own_contrast, own_mid, 16 rows). The luma renormalisation stays gated on a filter and holds the print with each channel's own tone but no filter, so Contrast and Mid move their channel alone, as the points do; Hunt and the follow read Lighting's curve alone. Monochrome passes zeros (it shows no channel); Digital renders them, its filters still forced to 0. The replica (Print::output, rendered) and the Lighting plot follow: Print::channel_tone and channel_moved, a channel drawn once any of its own pass moved. tone.rs split: its readers to tone/read.rs. Sidecar format 29 (chain::CHANNEL_TONE_VERSION, which also carries the halation's sensitivity; absent keys read as rest, no step), the newer corpus file moved to version-30 / Newer(30), the 36 goldens regenerated (each gains channel_mid, channel_contrast and sensitivity at rest). Both arrays travel in the levelsGlobal preset row with the points; balance_kept's looks are 35. Every value at rest renders bit-identically (the 22 hashes of #2170). Checks: branches (two cases, GPU against CPU 3.3e-6 and 3.4e-6; twin a kernel deaf to the tone 0.22), channel_points (red's, green's or blue's Contrast 0.4 or Mid 0.25 leads its own channel on a negative, a positive and Digital, e.g. Digital red's Mid [0.136, 5e-5, 5e-5]; twin the mids on all three leads none; monochrome renders none, twin a positive moves; conversion::stage47 at rest carries none in three modes), kernel_oracle (two toned prints at 3.1e-7; twin a replica ignoring the tone 0.24), channel_tone.rs (a format-28 document reads them and the sensitivity at rest; a current one keeps them; rest writes no key, twin 0.01 written; past the track lands on its end, twin 0.24 kept), knob, editors::print (a channel with only its contrast draws its curve, twin mono draws none). Merged onto the canvas (#2180-#2206): each channel's Contrast and Mid live in the printed half of stage47 (stage47_printed in WGSL, printed3 on the CPU), so a digital photo's print_px / cpu::print carries them after its Levels and Curves with the rest of Lighting; conversion::fused reads them from the print it is given, so unlit_print (Print::default) rests them in the picture and in a reading in front of the curves (truncate's ManualCurves), and lighting() counts them, its at-rest test comparing the lit kernel with the picture's. Monochrome still passes zeros. Checks: digital_lighting a_channels_own_tone_alone_rides_after_the_curves (the picture's kernel equals the untoned one, lighting() carries the tone; twin: a negative keeps it in its fused kernel and lays no Lighting), lit() now carries a tone, so picture-then-Lighting meets the former fused kernel at 5.7e-7 and the GPU chain the scalar one at 1.1e-6 (twin 0.17); branches: print_px against cpu::print with the tone 8.9e-7 and 9.1e-7 (twin a print deaf to it 0.24 and 0.25), print_reaches_every_branch over both toned cases (2.7e-6 to 4.1e-6, twins 1.7e-2 to 2.0e-2); truncate: a channel's tone rests in front of the curves, stays past them. Rest bit-equality: 128 whole renders (noise, DSC_6440 and DSC_6452 at 1200 px, the four modes at rest, lit, lit with curves and levels, with grain and halation, curves alone, each frame's sidecar on its mode and on Digital, displayed and measuring) hash identical on the canvas and on the merge. render/inputs_tests.rs (407 lines on the canvas) split: the readings' cadence into render/cadence_tests.rs.

title: More Color Settings in R / G / B tabs: each channel's white point, black point, mid and contrast
detail: The owner's words: More Color Settings gets tabs R / G / B (R / V / B in French) from the design system's tab component, each showing that channel's White point, Black point, and two new parameters, Mid and Contrast; it stays on Negative, Positive and Digital (not on Monochrome, as before). Tabs { R, G, B } under the block's title, the tab a ColorPane property starting on red; under it the channel's four StoreSliders in the owner's order: the points keep their ramp in the channel's colour, Mid is bipolar from the complement to the channel (as Paper Correction), Contrast plain as Lighting's. Fields 49-54 (Red/Green/Blue mid, Red/Green/Blue contrast; fr Moyens rouges / Contraste rouge, es Medios rojos / Contraste rojo, and green and blue alike) in Block::ChannelPoints, so the block's one Reset clears the three channels; each tab carries a mark while one of its four values stands off its rest, published from Rust (store::channel_marked beside is_modified) as Store.channel-marked, since a mark read from the springing fractions would flicker. fields.rs split: slint_name to fields/names.rs. French: the catalogue's G becomes V for every channel letter (Curves, Levels, measure and Prepare's pass letters alike, msgctxt being unused); RGB stays RGB, Spanish keeps G. The help of More Color Settings names the tabs, Mid, Contrast and the Reset of all three. Checks: store::channel_marked (green's contrast marks green alone, blue's mid adds blue; twin a red white point marks red alone; the block's reset clears all), fields wiring, the phone panel's missing list, the catalogue, and the window check channel_points rewritten: unfolded, each tab found between the title and Lighting (the Curves' share the names) shows its four sliders alone, each slider's press moves its own value alone, marks its tab alone and the block's Reset clears it (twin: Green white point not laid under R); the render's red follows red's white point; monochrome lays none, a positive and a digital photo lay it; digital_levels still finds one R tab with the block folded.

title: Levels: every handle drawn where it acts, each inner point between its neighbours, the midpoint included
detail: Owner's request: the Levels' points relative, the central one included. Read as Photoshop/Lightroom do: the midpoint sits on the value it renders as mid-grey (Levels::display_mid) and the ends carry it proportionally, as its stored share already did; the shadows sit between the black and the midpoint and the highlights between the midpoint and the white, linear on the window's gradation t = n^gamma (display_shadows = black + span * s^(1/gamma), display_highlights alike), so moving or resetting the midpoint carries both and none can cross (s < 0.5 < h). Before, the midpoint was drawn on its travel 0.15..0.85 stretched across the window (editors/levels on_track, now gone) and the quarter points on a straight share, so with the midpoint off 0.5 the three inner handles were drawn where they did not act and the readouts read values the handles did not sit on. Stored meaning unchanged (shadows and highlights were already shares of the gradation): no sidecar format, no migration, no render moves; at mid 0.5 the drawing is bit-equal to before (libm powf(x, 1) == x). One editor serves the film Per-Channel Levels and the digital photo's picture Levels, so both follow. New Levels::set_display_mid, set_display_shadows/highlights invert the gradation; readouts read where each handle is drawn. Checks (oni-app editors::levels::tests): the_inner_points_follow_their_neighbours_and_never_cross (a 15 x 9 x 9 grid of mid, shadows and highlights on a film density window and a digital picture window: strict order, a raised midpoint carries both quarters with their stored shares untouched, every handle written back from its place moves by under 1e-5); the_inner_handles_sit_where_their_quarter_renders (at rest quarters with mid 0.15..0.85 each inner handle sits on the input Levels::transfer renders as 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 within 1e-6; twin: the former straight share of the shadows renders more than 0.02 off; at mid 0.5 the places are the straight shares bit for bit); the median written back from its place within 1e-6 (twin: its former stretched place drifts by more than 0.01); each readout reads its handle's drawn value. For the owner: with the midpoint near an end, the shadows or highlights crowd that end (at mid 0.15 the resting shadows sit 6 px from the black on a 284 px track, behind it); the shadows and highlights readouts now read the input they act on, which differs from before whenever the midpoint is off 0.5; R, G and B windows stay independent of RGB's (reading c of the request, not built).

title: A digital photo's Levels and Curves come before Lighting, which acts on what they draw
detail: Owner's request: the Levels before Lighting in the pipe, the Curves too. A digital photo now renders white, halation, grain, then its picture (stage47 with Lighting and Saturation at rest: PipelineSettings::unlit_print, colour density at its base), then its Levels and Curves (the same tables and kernel, on the same domain: the display values the picture had with Lighting at rest), then Lighting: a new per-pixel kernel print_px / cpu::print (stages::print) takes the display value back to the print's scale (^(1/2.2)), lays each channel's black and white points as a window on 0..1 (the window lanes hold the points' reach on a unit window, conversion::lighting), then the print's own code (exposure, contrast, zones, Hunt, follow, Saturation). stage47.wgsl and kernel/stage47.rs are split into stage47_windowed and stage47_printed with stage47_px their composition, operation for operation. conversion::stage47 is fused(s, print, density): the frame's own on a film, the rested one on a digital photo; conversion::lighting is None on a film, a bypassed print, or where the lit and rested arguments are equal. The chain lays print in the picture's pass when the curves and levels rest (finishing::tabled false), else at the head of finishing's first run (with the spectrogram, the points' saturation, the saturation and the vignette), so it costs a pass of its own only when that run is otherwise empty. The film modes keep their order: no film edit moves. Bit-equality measured on this Mac's GPU before and after (a throwaway hash probe, not committed): the nine stage47_cases, and Negative, Positive, Monochrome and Digital renders at rest, lit (exposure, contrast, shadows, points, a channel white, density 0.3), curved, levelled and all together, on noise and on two reference-roll frames reduced to 480 px: every film render and every digital one with Lighting at rest identical to the bit; only Digital lit and lit-and-curved moved, as asked. With no curve between them, picture then Lighting is the former fused kernel within 3.1e-7 (relative, sweep 0..1.5, black points 0.03 and -0.1); only light under zero differs, where a negative black point now lifts the curves' black instead of reaching into negative-light values. Checks: branches::print_reaches_every_branch (GPU print against cpu::print, three print families x three reaches (points, a lifted black, at rest) x quarters resting and bent, on edges -0.25..3 and noise -0.1..1.3; worst 5.3e-6, twin a 1% green reach shift, refused at 1.7e-2 or more); digital_lighting.rs: the_picture_then_its_lighting_is_the_former_kernel_on_any_light (twin: a curve between them renders elsewhere, > 1e-2), a_digital_photos_lighting_acts_on_its_levels_and_curves (the chain on a lit, curved, levelled digital photo against print(curves(picture)) then the points' saturation, error 1.0e-6; twin today's order curves(fused), 1.15e-1), lighting_at_rest_lays_no_stage_and_a_film_keeps_its_kernel (twin: the digital photo's picture carries no Lighting and its lighting does), with_curves_at_rest_the_lighting_rides_in_the_pictures_pass (twin: after the tables, one more pass). Cost (ONI_BENCH_COST, 2000 x 1333, test profile, medians of 41, three runs): digital 1.11 ms, lit 1.55-1.69; curved 1.63-2.02 ms, lit 1.99-3.92; the GPU timing on this Mac is noisy run to run (one run read lit cheaper than rest). For the owner: Colour Density (Saturation in the Colour block) and Hunt belong to the print, so they now act after the Levels and Curves too; a negative Lighting black point fades the curves' black; the Colour tab still shows Lighting above Levels and Curves (a layout he did not ask to change).

title: A digital photo's Curves and Levels histogram reads the picture its curves receive, Lighting at rest
detail: oni_measure::truncate Stage::ManualCurves rests Lighting and Saturation on a digital photo (PipelineSettings::unlit), as they now act after the curves; a film's reading in front of its curves keeps its Lighting, and Stage::Curves keeps it on both. The app's input cache keeps the reading while Lighting slides, its entering settings and recipe unchanged. Checks: truncate in_front_of_the_curves_a_digital_photos_lighting_rests_and_a_films_stays (twin: past the curves, and on a negative, Lighting stays); oni-measure picture_levels a_reading_in_front_of_a_digital_photos_curves_holds_while_lighting_moves (GPU; twin: a negative's reading follows its exposure); oni-app inputs_tests a_digital_photos_curves_reading_holds_while_lighting_moves (an exposure step keeps both readings; twin: a 3200 K white moves the curves' reading).

title: Levels and Curves help texts say each handle follows its neighbours and, on a digital photo, that Lighting acts after them
detail: The digital photo's Levels help (Colour tab) and the film's Per-Channel Levels help (Roll tab) name the midpoint between the ends and the shadows and highlights on either side of it, each handle following those beside it; the digital one adds that Lighting acts on what they set. The Curves block shows a digital variant (PanelState.digital) saying they act before Lighting, which acts on what they draw; the film text stays as is. French and Spanish filled through scripts/i18n; the catalogue check passes.

title: Prewarm compiles a digital photo's Lighting passes
detail: prewarm::variants gains a digital photo lit (stage47+print in one pass), lit with a curve (print alone after the tables) and lit on the busy finishing (print fused with the spectrogram, saturation and vignette), so a first exposure notch on a digital photo compiles nothing; Kernels::total grows by nine, read only by the starter.

title: The grain is a pass of its own before the print, so a print notch reruns no grain
detail: oni_pipeline::Pipeline::chain laid the grain and stage47 as one fused pass, whose input (the haloed scene) was what Cache::frontier kept: every Exposure, Lighting, per-channel point or Hunt notch on a grained Digital frame reran the grain, 4 to 7 times a plain per-pixel pass (+2.7 ms at 2 MP, +4.4 at 6 MP, +12.9 at 13.5 MP on an M2 Max). The grain is now its own stage, the print the next, so the frontier keeps the grained scene and a print notch costs what an ungrained one does; a grain notch or an uncached render (export, counted, loupe) pays one more rgba32float pass, 0.5 to 1.6 ms. In the app at 5K fit (window 2560x1410 pt, drawable 5120x2820, canvas renders 2000x1333), GPU completion of an Exposure notch on a grained Digital NEF fell from p50 19.8 and 11.1 ms, p90 21.0 and 21.9 (two runs) to p50 5.8 and 6.8, p90 16.6 and 17.1, within the ungrained frame's spread (p50 6.5 and 13.2, p90 17.2 and 18.0) on a machine whose load average ran 4 to 19. Look: grained Digital pixels only move, by at most 1.1e-6 relative (the compiler's float contraction differs fused and apart); renders at rest and every film mode do not move. Checks: tests/grain.rs a_print_notch_through_the_frontier_reruns_no_grain (the grained chain is one stage longer than the ungrained one, which the fused layout fails at 3 against 4; an Exposure notch through Cache::frontier dispatches and writes as many pixels grained as at rest; twins: with no cache the notch writes more, a grain-amount notch dispatches one more pass); the_grain_matches_its_reference_on_every_branch now checks the chain's layout, grain then print, against cpu::stage47(cpu::grain(..)) (twin: the grain after the print).

title: The grain's PCG rounds written out: the grain kernel 30 to 45 % faster on Metal
detail: oni-render wgsl/grain.wgsl grain_normal ran its two PCG-2D rounds in a loop; naga bounds every loop on Metal (force_loop_bounding), which blocks the compiler's unrolling inside the 8x8 lattice loop. Written out, the grain alone falls from 2.76 to 1.63 ms at 2.2 MP and from 6.4 to 3.6-3.9 ms at 6 MP (size 0). The CPU reference kernel/grain.rs mirrors it, its values unchanged. Look: grained Digital pixels move by at most 2.8e-7 relative (about 2 ulp, float contraction), nothing at rest. title: The grain follows the Grain Curve on the picture's tone: a grained frame's look changes on purpose
detail: The grain pass (stage on the scene before the picture, Digital only) reads a share table: 64 nodes evenly spaced in stops of the scene's luminance (Rec. 2020) from 2^-14 to 2^1, 4.2 a stop, each the curve's share at the tone that light shows as the photo opens, before Lighting: its luminance through conversion::stage47 at the frame's own rest (cpu::stage47 on a grey), encoded at 1/2.2 as the Saturation Curve reads tone. No print slider reaches that pass, so a print notch keeps the grain's uniform and its cached pass; on a digital photo's Scanner face the tones are read without the picture's gains, which are the keys there, so a key notch keeps it too (tests/grain.rs a_key_notch_on_the_scanner_face_keeps_the_grain_s_shares, twin: the keyed picture's tones move the shares). The grain lies in chain.rs on both faces, before the machine's levels and print (scene 0.18 shows at tone 0.65; full grain from about -5.2 EV to -3.3 EV, 0.67 on 18 % grey, none from about -1.07 EV up). Grain.share is one row a node holding its share and the next one's, so the shader reads one row a pixel and indexes no vector lane (FXC); a light given no share returns its pixel untouched; the stops multiply as stops*share*field, exact at share 1. pipeline::grain::grain returns None at amount 0 or with no share anywhere, so a render without grain lays no stage and stays bit-identical. Every grained frame renders with less grain in the shadows and none in the upper highlights from now on, its exports included; thumbnails already drawn keep their former grain until the frame is drawn again (thumbnails::RENDER_VERSION is read by no render). Cost on the Mac (cost.rs, 3024x2016, before then after, same session): grain whole render +2.44-2.64 ms then +2.38-2.48 ms over rest; an exposure notch 7.12-7.63 ms with or without grain, before and after; the table's baking 11 us a render. Checks: the GPU against its reference with the rest table on every branch (none, both table ends, interior) and its twin the whole share; the spread by tone equals the curve's share at 0.02, 0.18 and 0.8 (0.93, 0.66, 0) with its twin the flat curve; a curve at amount 0 and a curve of no share lay no stage; a print notch keeps the grain pass's bytes, a curve notch moves them; oni-render's kernel unit test of the table (its twin a table read a node over).

title: Coloured grain: a saturation on a straight line along the tone, high at the black, neutral at the white; sidecar format 32
detail: Owner's request: the grain read too desaturated and too black in the shadows. crates/oni-render: grain.wgsl and kernel/grain.rs split the node hash (grain_hash/hash) from its shaping: the light's normal keeps its summation, three Hadamard combinations of the same four uniforms give the chroma (unit variance, uncorrelated with the light and each other), whose offsets about their mean (x sqrt 1.5, zero sum) colour each channel: out_c = s_c 2^(stops (L + sat D_c)), so the log mean Hunt reads stays the light's. sat = black + t (white - black), t the unlit picture's display tone at the pixel (grain_tone/tone: the green window, pedestal and guard of conversion::stage47, never the gains, which on the Scanner face are its keys). Grain::coloured(colour, GrainTone); one path, 0/0 the monochrome grain. crates/oni-pipeline/src/grain.rs: grain::tone(s), the one function a merge with the strength curve can share. crates/oni-settings: blocks/grain_colour.rs GrainColour { black, white }, RANGE 0..3, REST 2/0 (1: each channel moves as far as the light; 2 reads clearly coloured, 1.97 times the light at tone 0.013 on a flat grey, 0.04 at 0.98), tolerant read (absent, null or no number reads rest, the rest held in range), not written at rest. VERSION 32 (chain::GRAIN_COLOUR_VERSION; 31 is left to the strength curve), absent reads the rest, so every grained frame turns coloured at update, on purpose. The newer corpus file moves to version-33, Newer(33); 35 goldens and the newer file's gain the colour's rest. Measured, Digital at rest, Grain 0.6, Size 0.5, flat greys through the whole chain, before (mono) then after (2/0): luma spread 0.0039 then 0.0067 at shown 0.013, 0.0317 then 0.0438 at 0.144; chroma spread 0 then 0.0083 and 0.0529 (1.21 to 1.27 times the light under 0.15); pixels under half their tone 3.5 % then 10.2 % at 0.013 (0.01 % and 0.06 % with Sharpen off, so Sharpen's added gain makes the black pepper). On Roll #8 scans rendered as Digital (DSC_6440, 6445, 6450, P1072380; no shown tone under 0.2), tones 0.2 to 0.35: chroma 0.024 to 0.043, colour over light 0.72 to 1.08. Checks: kernel unit tests (chroma moments and correlations, twin a lane that is the light; zero log sum, twin the luma-keeping offset; 1024^2 flat casts 0.06 %, twin 5.7 %), tests/grain_colour.rs (GPU against CPU on 2/0, 1.5/0.7, 0/2 and 0/0 over noise -0.02..1.2, twins one node over and the line backwards; tone equals the unlit picture to 6e-8, twin a 2.2 gamma off 0.19; the colour follows its line within 0.08, twin a constant; the lightness lift over the mono grain under 1.5 L*, measured 1.36 at grey 0.008, twin the slider's top at 3.06), tests/grain.rs (the monochrome block at 0/0, twin the default; a colour notch reruns the grain's pass, a Scanner key notch none; a colour at amount 0 lays no stage; the reduced-render test on a dark grey), oni-settings grain_colour (format 30 and 31 read the rest, twin this format keeps 0/0; a moved value round-trips to the bit; the rest writes no colour; VERSION+1 refused as newer), knob tests, inputs_tests (a colour notch reads no distribution). Merge with the Grain Curve (canvas, #2220-#2223): format 32 sits on the curve's 31 (chain::GRAIN_COLOUR_VERSION after GRAIN_CURVE_VERSION, document::VERSION 32, the broken corpus at version-33, Newer(33), goldens regenerated with the reading example so they carry both rests). One tone for both: the strength curve's, the axis its editor shows (the node light's luminance through conversion::stage47 with the gains at 1, before Lighting, encoded 1/2.2), replaces grain::tone's green window; pipeline::grain::colours lays the line on the same 64 nodes as grain::shares, each node row holding its share, the next one's, its colour and the next one's, so the kernel reads one row a pixel: out_c = s_c 2^(stops share (L + sat D_c)), a light of no share kept to the bit. GrainTone, grain_tone and Grain::coloured(colour, tone) go; Grain::coloured takes the colour table. Checks moved with it: tests/grain_colour.rs's GPU check runs over noise -0.02..2.5 with the rest curve's shares (none, both table ends) and the whole share, its tone check reads the colour and the share on one tone to the picture's display luminance (twin a 2.2 gamma), the curve's two share tests move there from tests/grain.rs (under 400 lines); kernel unit tests: the colour passes through each node, the share scales the colour with the light (twin the colour laid whole). In Film Effects the colour line sits under the Grain Curve, its help saying so (fr, es).
