title: The grain's colour deepens the pixel's own hue where the grain darkens it, in place of a hue drawn at random each clump
detail: Where the RGB chroma speckle came from: grain.wgsl's grain_chroma and grain_offsets drew three more normals per lattice node (Hadamard combinations of the light's own hash), independent of the light L and of each other, made them zero-sum with unit spread and laid exp2(stops share (L + sat D_c)) on each channel, so every grain clump took a uniformly random hue at the light's cell size, its per-channel spread sat times the light's (twice it in the blacks at rest). Measured at Amount 1, Size 0.5, at the grain stage: a neutral grey got 0.064-0.082 u'v' of colour from nothing, hue spread 33-64 degrees on skin, sky and foliage, noise across the hue line as large as along it, the luma raised x1.05-1.11 by per-channel exp2 convexity; its 'saturation' was rectified noise (mean chroma up x1.4-2.0 on pale colours, down on saturated ones). The law now: a = stops share L (L a scalar field, accumulated in the same order as before, so a colour of 0 renders as it did); k = 2^a; where the grain darkens (d = max(0, -a) > 0) each channel's ratio to the luma r_c = s_c / Y is raised to gamma = 2^(colour d) (exp2(gamma log2 r), a channel at or under zero kept as it is) and the result rescaled to luma k Y; elsewhere, or where Y or the new luma is not positive, s k. A grey stays grey to the bit, the luma is the monochrome grain's exactly (the strength mapping untouched), the hue holds to a few degrees and its drift follows L, a non-negative input never goes negative. Same pass on the balanced scene before stage47, so a print notch reruns nothing; three accumulators per node fewer: the grain's cost on a 3024x2016 digital render falls from 3.56 / 2.72 / 2.75 ms to 2.9 / 2.26 / 2.25 ms at Size 0 / 0.5 / 1. crates/oni-render: wgsl/grain.wgsl (grain_laid), kernel/grain.rs (field returns f32, laid(s, a, colour)), its tests moved to kernel/grain/tests.rs: a grey stays neutral to the bit at the colour's top over 5 lights and 4096 places (twin: the random offsets part it over 0.01 stop), the colour in stops scales by 2^(colour d) where the grain darkens and is bit-equal to the monochrome grain where it lightens (twin: the symmetric law moves the lighter grains), the luma is the monochrome grain's within 1e-6 and channels keep their order (twin: the vignette's power-mean renormalisation, over 1e-3 off on a red), zero, negative, black and negative-luma inputs (twin: flooring at zero moves the negative channel), the share scales the stops the colour reads (twin: the colour read off the unshared stops). The Hadamard chroma, offsets and their three tests go.

title: The grain's colour checks read the photo's own hue: no random hue, a bounded deepening of the shadows, no lift
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/grain_colour.rs: the GPU-against-reference check adds rows of a zero channel, a negative one, a neutral grey and a black (both twins kept); the colour follows its line, now read on a flat skin as log2 of the power its red over its blue took over the stops the grain darkened it, within 0.08 of the line at every tone (twin: one colour of 1 on every tone, over 0.5 off); the lift check reads the grain stage then the unlit picture (cpu::stage47): every grey within 1e-3 L* of the monochrome grain (measured under 1e-6; twin: a hue drawn at random each pixel lifts a grey) and four dark colours within 1.5 L* at the colour's top (0.08; twin: a random hue at the top lifts a grey 2.76). crates/oni-pipeline/tests/grain_hue.rs (new): on five colours and a grey at tones 0.08, 0.2 and 0.45, across-hue under 0.015 u'v', hue spread under 4 degrees, a grey under 1e-5 (measured 0.0112, 3.36 degrees on the sky at tone 0.2, 1e-16; twin: a random hue at the line's colour, 0.058 and 66 degrees); skin's chroma in the shadows x1.05 to x1.35 at rest (x1.258) and under x1.5 at the top (x1.450; twin: the symmetric law takes a red under x1, x0.986); a quarter render's chroma within 5 % of the full render's 4x4 means (x1.170 against x1.211, the full render's own pixels x1.259: the mean of the darkening is not the darkening of the mean; twin: a quarter laid without its colour, x1.000). tests/grain.rs: the reduced check's comment says the grey stays grey. The investigator's twin for the reduced check (the full render's stops on the quarter) was dropped: under the footprint cap both renders have the same stops, so it passes.

title: Sidecar format 33: the grain's colour keeps its numbers under its new meaning
detail: crates/oni-settings: GrainColour's numbers (range 0 to 3, rest black 2 / white 0) now mean the exponent a stop of darkening raises the pixel's own colour ratios by, a grain d stops darker taking them to the power 2^(colour d); no mapping keeps a random hue's look, and the order (0 none, 2 rest, 3 top) holds, so a format-32 file's numbers are carried with no data step. chain::GRAIN_HUE_VERSION = 33, document::VERSION 33, so a format-32 build opens these files read-only rather than render the random hue; the broken corpus moves to version-34 (Newer(34) in corpus.rs); the readings' goldens do not move. tests/grain_colour.rs: VERSION is GRAIN_HUE_VERSION; a moved format-32 colour {1.5, 0.3} reads {1.5, 0.3}, standing Older(32) (twin: a rescaling step). The GrainColour docs say the new meaning.

title: Film Effects' help says the colour line deepens the photo's own colours where the grain darkens them
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/color_tab.slint: both Film Effects help texts (Digital and film) say the line under the Grain Curve deepens the photo's own colours where the grain darkens them, adding none of its own, its left point for richer shadows, its right for richer highlights; fr and es in oni-ui.po, scripts/i18n run. The colour line's labels (Grain colour at the black / white point, Saturated / Desaturated), the Grain Curve and its editor are unchanged and stay shown.

title: Each photo its own grain: the lattice's hash reads the photo's seed, so every grained render's pattern moves once
detail: crates/oni-render: wgsl/grain.wgsl's grain_hash adds the uniform head's x, y (the seed) to the lattice index before PCG-2D's first round, a translation of the same field, so its statistics hold; kernel/grain.rs: Grain.seed ([0, 0] from Grain::on), Grain::seeded, Grain::head, hash(i, seed); oni-pipeline stages::grain passes k.head() instead of the zero head. Seed [0, 0] is the lattice as it was to the bit, so the goldens hold and only the app's renders move: every grained render's pattern moves once (each photo its own arrangement), the grain's character (spread, size, curve, colour) unchanged. Checks in kernel/grain/tests.rs: seed 0 equals the former hash on 64x64 nodes (twin: seed [1, 0] moves every node); on three seeds mean within 0.01, variance within 0.01 of 1, neighbours under 0.01 (twin: the seeded index read with no round, neighbours 0.1+); three seed pairs correlate under 0.01 over 256x256 nodes (twin: a seed the hash ignores, 0.99+). tests/grain_detail.rs: the GPU against the CPU reference with a non-zero seed, error 6e-6 (twin: the seed ignored, 1.4).

title: A photo's grain seed is its file's print without its size or name: kept through a rename or a move
detail: crates/oni-settings/src/sidecar/identity.rs: seed(path) -> Option<[u32; 2]>, FNV-1a 64 over the print's date and digest (the library's fingerprint of three 16 KB blocks and the capture date, its size left out), split in two u32; None for a file unread or kept away by the cloud. No stored value, no sidecar format: a photo with no sidecar has its seed, a paste or a preset carries none (PipelineSettings holds no seed, so carry!(grain) copies no arrangement). ONI never rewrites an original, so only another tool rewriting the file's sampled bytes moves it; a copy of one file in two folders is the same photo and lays the same grain. tests/grain_seed.rs (new): a moved and a renamed copy keep the seed, another file and a byte changed in a read block do not, a byte no block reads keeps it, an absent file has none (twin: a seed salted with the file name parts at the rename).

title: The photo's seed travels from its decode to every render: the editor, the loupe, thumbnails, Edit Together, the contact sheet and the export
detail: crates/oni-app/src/render/decode.rs: Decoded.seed, read off the decoded file by each decoder (mosaic, linear scan, plain) and the lead's for RGB passes (composed), so decode, decode_for, decode_full and decode_alone agree at every size; [0, 0] for a file unread. engine.rs: Negative.seed from reduce (its facts tuple), tiles.rs tile_of copies it; kept.rs inputs_of(patches, custom, settings, seed) replaces the eight repeated Inputs lines (engine.rs, view.rs, tiles.rs, inputs.rs, originals.rs); search_region and framed_whole read before the grain and pass none. loupe takes (full, seed), the app's loupe reads the seed off the open frame's preview (a frame opened again waits for it); unproofed takes the seed: export/renders.rs carries the full decode's (render_full, render_full_beside) and sample the preview's; oni-demos' Photo keeps its full decode's seed, the welcome De-dust scan its preview's. oni-pipeline Inputs.seed, chain.rs seeds the grain from it; the measure readers (resident.rs, oni-measure reader.rs) pass none, as a measure lays no grain. engine.rs stays at 399 lines. Checks in render/seed_tests.rs (new): a PNG's four decodes, a renamed and moved copy share one non-zero seed and another file has its own; on ONI_RAW_DIR's first NEF the half-size, preview-side and whole decodes agree (DSC_6432: [1704908782, 3112797896] at all three); two photos' previews correlate at 0.0015 (twin: one seed, 0.999+); the export's full render 4x4 means against the preview at 0.9944 (twin: another photo's seed, under 0.05). tests/grain_seed.rs (new): two seeds and none correlate under 0.05 (-0.0053, 0.0055) with spreads within 0.3 % (0.1119, 0.1116, 0.1115; twin: one seed again, 0.999+).

title: Inside a coarse grain's clumps the scene gives way to its blur, so detail finer than a grain follows the grain
detail: crates/oni-render: grain_px(s, b, at) reads b, the scene blurred under a grain, and mixes base = s + dissolve × share(s) × smoothstep(0.5, 1.5, |F| / spread_full) × (b - s) before laying the grain on base as before; spread_full is mean_spread(per_cell), the field's spread at full resolution, sent in a new mix row [dissolve, 1/spread_full, 0, 0]; Grain.dissolve (0 from Grain::on), Grain::dissolving; the share and colour are read off the sharp pixel, so a light given no share is kept to the bit and a blur equal to the pixel gives today's grain to the bit. The mix is convex: no halo. CPU reference kernel/grain.rs grain(s, b, at, k) and mixed(); kernel/grain/dissolve_tests.rs (new): a blur equal to the pixel kept to the bit at the whole dissolve (twin: a blur unlike it moves 500+ pixels); no share kept however the blur differs (twin: the blur mixed before the share is read); under half a spread the pixel is today's to the bit, past one and a half it takes dissolve x share of the blur, the weight never past dissolve x share (twin: a mix linear in the field softens over half the pixels between clumps). Displacement along the field's gradient or toward each clump's centre was measured and refused: it softens evenly or folds pixels and rings on edges.

title: The grain's blur rides on Size and Amount: half a cell's side less a pixel, none at the finest grain
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/src/grain.rs: GRAIN_DISSOLVE = 0.5; dissolve(s, scan) = 0.5 x scan width x GRAIN_FINEST x (4^size - 1) render pixels, a share of the scan's width so fit, a zoom and an export dissolve alike; grained(image, k, sigma) reads stages::blurred(image, sigma) as the grain's auxiliary image past BLUR_FLOOR (0.1614 px), the image itself under it; grain() sets dissolving(amount). chain.rs grains through grained with the seed. No new control and no sidecar value: Size sets the blur, Amount its weight; an older build renders the grain as it was. The blur starts above Size 0.2 on a 6000-pixel scan (1.5 px at Size 1, 1.0 at 0.8, 0.5 at 0.5, 0.21 at 0.25) and is skipped under the floor, so a 320-pixel thumbnail and Size 0 to 0.2 render as before to the bit; its deviation reads only Size and the scan, so an Amount or a print notch reuses it from the cache. Rests at Amount 0 with no stage, so every render without grain is bit-identical. The investigator's plan expected Size 0.25 to keep all detail (1.000); the app's blur is integrated over each pixel, so at its 0.21 px it keeps 0.979 of a one-pixel line grid (0.947 inside clumps, 0.998 between): the bound is 0.97.

title: The detail follows the grain: inside clumps, between them, at fine grain, at reduced scales and through a print notch
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/grain_detail.rs (new): on a grid of one-pixel lines every three pixels at Size 1, Amount 0.8, the whole share and no colour, the base recovered as out / the grained flat grey, the Laplacian energy on sqrt light keeps 0.110 inside clumps (|F| past its spread) and 1.001 between them (under half) of the scene's own; bounds 0.25 and 0.95 (twin: the grain with no blur, about 1.0 inside). Measured at other settings: Amount 0.8 Size 0.5 0.338 / 0.993, Amount 0.6 Size 0.8 0.249 / 1.003, Amount 1 Size 1 0.052 / 1.002. Size 0 and 0.15 render to the bit as with no blur; Size 0.25 keeps 0.979 overall, bound 0.97 (twin: a blur of half a cell, 0.682). On a soft scene (value noise at 2 to 16 pixels), a half and a quarter render against the full one's 2x2 and 4x4 means: 0.0029 / 0.0142 and 0.0123 / 0.0540 stops (mean / 99th percentile) against the grain alone's 0.0025 / 0.0117 and 0.0119 / 0.0524, so the blur adds at most 0.002 / 0.01 (twin: the full render's blur in the reduced render's pixels, 0.0097 / 0.0652 and 0.0259 / 0.1540). tests/grain_seed.rs (new): a region and a crop through the chain keep each scan pixel's dissolved, seeded grain on a noise scene with the blur at 0.375 px (twin: a region a pixel over); the grain is one pass of the chain, an exposure notch through the frontier cache runs the passes of a render with no grain, an Amount notch one more (the grain's), a Size notch three (twin: the blur's two and the grain's). The existing grain checks pass unchanged but for their calls: tests/grain.rs, grain_colour.rs, grain_hue.rs read stages through grain::grained(image, k, 0.0) and cpu::grain(p, p, at, k).

title: Film Effects help names the grain arranged anew on each photo and its clumps taking in the detail finer than a grain
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/color_tab.slint: both Film Effects help texts (the machine face and Pro) say the grain is arranged anew on each photo, and that a coarse grain takes in the detail finer than a grain inside its clumps and leaves it sharp between them, so the effect riding on Grain size and Grain is named where its controls are; fr and es in oni-ui.po (msgid and msgstr edited in place), scripts/i18n run, 7 catalogue checks pass. No control, label or token changes.

title: The seeded, dissolving grain driven through the real app on a test copy of roll #8 made Digital
detail: --profile app build, ONI_BACKGROUND=1, ONI_SUPPORT and ONI_CACHES on a scratch folder, on a clone of the reference roll's test copy whose 38 NEF sidecars were set to Digital with Grain 0.8, Size 1 (the first frame 0.5 / 0.7), the contact sheet set aside; no original written. ONI_BENCH=flows: 3 frames picked, double-clicked open, edited through resizes and back in the gallery, no failure (graph textures peak 459 MB). ONI_BENCH=zoom at 1728 x 1080: full resolution 8 ms after the double click, 60 pans and the ladder at end to end p50 1.4 ms, p99 17.5 ms. ONI_BENCH=1 on the 1100 x 680 window (drawable 2200 x 1360): Exposure p50 1.0 ms end to end, Grain p50 4.5 ms (the grain's pass reruns, its blur kept), Grain size p50 0.7 ms (a gesture renders the lighter level). Through the app's own engine on DSC_6432 and DSC_6433: the half-size preview, the preview-side and the whole decodes read one seed each ([1704908782, 3112797896], [682009597, 3105001072]); the editor's fit render against the export's full render reduced to its pixels correlate 0.953 and 0.965 in the grain's stops; the loupe's 100 % region on a 3456 x 2160 drawable equals the export's same pixels to the bit; the two photos' grains at the same pixel correlate 0.0105; a renamed copy in another folder keeps its seed and renders its grain to the bit. Cost of that 100 % region (7.5 MP): 20.8 ms with no grain, 23.9 ms grained at Size 0.15 (no blur), 26.0 ms at Size 1 (blur 1.5 px), so the dissolve's blur adds about 2.1 ms (0.28 ms a megapixel) and runs only when Size moves. The app build and the probe were deleted afterwards.

title: ONI_BENCH=sweep times each zoom move to the GPU's end of the frame that shows it
detail: vendor/i-slint-renderer-femtovg: each recorded interface frame keeps when the GPU finished it (queue.on_submitted_work_done after its submit, a thread polling the device only while a bench records; ONI: comment). bench/chain.rs: the moves navigate applies and the view renders that land are recorded with the notches; a notch's line adds asked to the GPU's end of its frame; photon() closes a move at the GPU end of the first frame begun after it, as that frame is drawn on the same thread. bench/sweep.rs, Mode::Sweep: the full resolution built and the view held at 40 %, ONI_SWEEP pinch (120 Hz), wheel (8 notches a second) or keys (4 a second) zooms to 120 % and back three times; the report gives move to picture moved and to its render shown (p50/p90/p99/worst), each lighter and sharp render's stages, the renders landed at a scale the view had left, the frames' GPU-end gaps and those over 25 ms (three 120 Hz refreshes), the present gaps, present to GPU end, drawable acquire. Check in chain.rs: a move closes at the GPU end of the first frame drawn after it (twin: the present call reads it 48 ms early); a frame whose end is unknown closes nothing. docs/research/performance.md section 17 gives the method. Renders do not move. Measured before and after #2271-#2273 in performance.md section 17: on the built-in screen at full width, a pinch's move to the picture moved went from 70 to 21 ms p50 and 93 to 35 ms p99.

title: One render in flight is one the GPU has run: the render threads wait for the GPU before the next job
detail: A pinch between 40 % and 120 % sent a render per 120 Hz event: each costs 0.3 to 1 ms of CPU and 22 to 50 ms of GPU, so renders piled up on the one Metal queue and every interface frame waited behind them, the picture moved 50 to 100 ms late while the fps held. oni-graph: Graph::submit keeps its SubmissionIndex, last_submission() hands it out with the device, oni_graph::ran(device, index) returns once the GPU has run it, waiting in 1 ms slices with no limit, as wgpu-core 30.0.1 holds the device's snatch lock for reading through a poll's wait (device/resource.rs:797) and a window's present takes it for writing (present.rs:340): a render waited on whole would hold the interface's present 20 to 140 ms. Error::Lost reads 'the GPU did not finish its work'. oni-app: Renderer::ran (none for a renderer with no GPU), Shared::ran waits with the engine unlocked and says a lost device once; the render worker calls it after each job's delivery and reads, the loupe's and Edit Together's threads after each render, as all share the queue. Replaces #270 and docs/research/gpu-settle.diff, without its 100 ms timeout. Checks: oni-graph tests/ran.rs, ran returns once the GPU has run the graph's last submission (twin: polled at once, twelve passes over 4 MP have not run); render/ran_tests.rs, the worker takes no job before the GPU ran the last, a fake GPU ending 30 ms after each render, twenty notches over 100 ms collapsing to at most six renders, the last always rendered (twin: today's empty wait overlaps five renders or more). cadence_tests' Logged waits like the engine. Renders do not move.

title: A render landing after the hand moved is laid where the view now puts it
detail: With the worker waiting for the GPU (#2271), a render lands up to one render later than its ask: laid where the job's view had put it, the picture snapped back to an older zoom (9 to 20 renders of about 140 in a pinch, up to 1.8 %). render/worker.rs: Done carries the job's viewport and canvas size, and whether it rendered lighter. app/rendering/resizing.rs: moved(p, from, to) lays a placement made by one view of the image where another view puts the same part of it, the arithmetic navigate and a resize already used, now theirs too. app/rendering/landing.rs: deliver lays the render and Compare's before from the job's view to the current one. Check in resizing.rs: after a 1.1 zoom about a point, a render covering full-resolution pixels 1000 to 3000 lands exactly where the new view puts them (twin: the job's placement is a zoom step off, a tenth of its width). Renders do not move; only where a render is laid on the canvas.

title: A gesture keeps a whole reduction only as large as the canvas it renders
detail: render/engine/view.rs: a reduction holding at most KEPT_WHOLE canvases is made whole and kept, so a notch at fit reads it ready; under a hand the view renders lighter (at most GESTURE_PIXELS), but the budget was the full canvas's, so on a 5K canvas every gesture step between fit and 120 % reduced the whole frame again, up to 12 to 21 MP, and the one exact scale kept was never reused (engine probe at 5K: event to render done p99 94 to 50 ms, a render's GPU p99 52 to 30 ms with this step off). kept_whole(whole, size, lighter) compares the reduction with KEPT_WHOLE canvases rendered lighter; lighter(coarse, size) is the gesture scale composed() already used. A sharp render (lighter 1) keeps what it kept, so no render moves; a pan near fit keeps the reduction (#282): at fit on the 5K, 2.4 MP against 5.1. Check in view.rs: an 8000 by 5000 frame on a 3920 by 2640 canvas keeps nothing for a gesture at 100 %, keeps it for a gesture at fit and a sharp render at 60 % (twin: the canvas's own budget keeps the gesture's 10 MP at 100 %).

title: Compare's before lies where the after lies, moved in the same frame by a pan, a pinch or a resize
detail: The owner saw the before side of Compare lag far behind the after while panning ("1 fps at most"). Cause: the before had a placement of its own (Frame.compare.before_placed, Canvas.before-x/y/width/height) that only a landed render set, while navigate moves the after by arithmetic and asks no render within the 12.5 % pan margin; at 1728 by 1117 pt and 100 %, 233 of 240 pan moves asked none, so the before stood misplaced on 97 to 99 % of pan frames and caught up 190 to 200 ms after each move at median, up to 590 ms. The before is the same job's region at the same view, as the reference keeps the geometry, so its place is the after's: canvas.slint lays the before Picture on Canvas.frame-x/y/width/height, the before-x/y/width/height properties, lay_before and before_placed are gone, and Engine::before returns the source alone. A landing with no before while Compare is on, and an emptied canvas, let the before go (drop_before) rather than stretch an older region over the new place; Compare off is checked at every landing, the grid's included. gamut.rs stripes the before on the after's place. Checks: view_tests, the before's region and the reference's place equal the after's under a crop, a quarter turn, the Scanner face and a look away from rest (twin: a reference cropped otherwise holds another region at another place); window check compare_pan, at 100 % a pan inside the margin lands no render and the before's rectangle equals the after's within half a point, then after a resize and a pinch step (twins: the after moved by the pan, the before left its place, the pinch grew the picture); together_tools reads both pictures' rectangles. At 1728 by 1117 pt and 100 % (bench compare, on battery, load 5 to 9): on the RW2's drag pan the before stood off the after on 0 of 238 frames (232 of 238 before), each move showing it at p50 8.2, p99 43.4, worst 62.8 ms (198, 564, 582 before); on the NEF 7.9, 28.7, 29.8 ms (188, 573, 589 before); a pinch shows both sides in the same frame (the before caught up at 41 against 23 ms p50 before). Renders do not move.

title: Compare's before is held in a display texture sized by the after's steps
detail: The before was encoded into a texture of its exact extent, so a pinch made and imported a new one at nearly every render (9 to 10 over a 20-render pinch, against 4 for the after). compare.rs encodes it into landing.rs's stepped size (TARGET_STEP, 256 pixels), and canvas.slint clips the before with the after's frame-clip-width/height, both holding the same region. Check in compare.rs: over a 40-step pinch the before makes no more textures than the after, 4 at most (twin: an exact-size before makes one at every step). Over a 60-event pinch at 100 %: 4 before textures against 4 after ones on the RW2 (9 against 4 before), 4 against 4 on the NEF (18 against 4).

title: The Compare bench pans, pinches, drags Exposure and the split, timing both sides to the photon
detail: ONI_BENCH=compare moves to bench/compare.rs: the full resolution built, Compare on and the view at 100 % (ONI_AT), a drag pan and a trackpad pan of 240 events out and back, a 60-event pinch, a 60-notch Exposure drag and a split drag at 120 Hz. bench/chain.rs records the canvas's states (whether the before shown holds the after's region, the display textures made); per phase the report gives each move's time to the GPU end of the frame showing the after moved and the before on it, the frames whose before is off the after's region, view renders, textures made and GPU-end gaps.

title: The Lens DB is asked only where the app names it: no check, no bench and no other launch reaches thelensdb.com
detail: Options gains tldb: TldbSite (None, Real, Simulated(url)), None by default, so every window check and bench that hands no service reads no token and makes no call, and Connect opens nothing (one log line). Only main.rs resolves ONI_TLDB once: fake starts the simulated service in the support folder, a loopback address names a running one, unset is the real service, and a bench is None. The Kit's state holds its site: the Keychain or Credential Manager is read only for Real, a simulated token lies in the support folder. The collection check hands its fake's address instead of setting ONI_TLDB in its environment. Check: kit_failures a_run_naming_no_service_asks_none_and_connect_opens_nothing (a token left in the folder, no call, no page opened); twin: the firewall check names the service and its launch reads the Kit once.

title: The client reads a firewall's page as the service unreached, names no address in a failure, follows no redirect
detail: failure() decides by the body: a 401 signs out whatever it carries; any other status without the API's {error} (a firewall's HTML at 403, 429, 503, a 302) is Down; with it, 429 waits Retry-After (60 s without), 5xx is Down, the rest Refused. reqwest follows no redirect, and a call that got no answer reports reqwest's error without its URL, whose query held the words searched. Account.displayName may be null. On the token address a 401 is Refused(invalid_client), never a sign-out; the revocation bears the token as every call does, besides naming it in its form. Checks: api statuses_stand_for_their_failures (twins: a firewall's 429 is no wait, its 403 no refusal), an_unreached_service_never_names_the_words_searched (twin: the raw error names them), oauth a_401_of_the_token_address_refuses_the_client_and_signs_no_one_out (twin: the same 401 on a partner call signs out).

title: A change of more than 200 entries goes in calls of 200, the removals first
detail: Client::change sends every removal, then every addition, 200 entries a POST /kit/changes, merges each call's notFound and returns the Kit and ETag of the last; a failure stops the rest, the service taking a repeat as nothing. The app's own batching goes. Check: contract a_long_change_goes_in_calls_of_two_hundred_removals_first (202 entries in two calls, a key removed and added ends present, 199 unknown ids reported; twins: one raw call of 201 entries is refused 400, and a removal after an addition leaves the key absent).

title: The simulated The Lens DB keeps to the v1 contract to the letter
detail: Every address under /api asks User-Agent ONI/<version> (<system>), else a firewall's HTML page at 429 with no error object, the token and revocation addresses included. The token address answers RFC 6749 errors with error_description: 400 invalid_request for a missing field, unsupported_grant_type, 401 invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant. A search ignores words past the tenth. ETags are weak (W/"…") and compared whole. The rate is the account's, all its tokens together, with a second account for checks (stranger). New controls: set_firewall(status) answers HTML without an error at that status, set_silent closes every connection unanswered, merge(from, into) folds a record into another in the catalogue and every Kit, and journal() lists every API request with its method, path, query, agent, bearer, Origin, status and instant. Its header comments no longer speak of a service yet to open.

title: The partner API's letter checked point by point against the simulated service
detail: tests/tldb/contract.rs: every call after a real sign-in (token, search, Kit, change, revoke) names ONI and a plain system's name, bears its token but the exchange, carries no Origin (twins: curl's agent meets the firewall's 429 HTML, read as Down; a write with an Origin is refused 403 with an error); a weak ETag gives 304 sent whole (twin: stripped of W/ it reads afresh); a 429 waits its Retry-After; a revoked token signs out on every call (twin: another token reads); a firewall's 403, 429, 200 or 503 and a silence are Down and apply nothing; the token address's RFC 6749 errors; a merged record comes back as the one kept; unknown fields ignored and null displayName read (twin: a piece without a name is refused). partner.rs: words past the tenth ignored (twin: a wrong word within the ten narrows to nothing), the rate per account (twin: another account is served), the firewall on every address for a foreign or missing agent.

title: A 429's Retry-After holds every call to The Lens DB, and the latest search is asked once it ends
detail: The Kit's state keeps not_before from a Wait: a search, the launch's read and Done send nothing until it passes; the search waiting asks the latest words once, on a timer for what is left, and Done says how long to wait. Check: kit_failures a_429_holds_every_search_until_its_end_then_asks_the_latest_once (one call in ten seconds, the launch took it: the first search is answered 429 and said in the sheet, more words typed send nothing, then one search of the latest words lands after the wait; twin: a search sent inside the window is refused, so the hold is what kept the app's).

title: The search sheet's Done saves to The Lens DB: one call for what was added, and a removal sent once confirmed
detail: The owner's request: Done is the save, with no second step. Add picks a piece in the sheet; Done, and Escape, send the picks in one POST /kit/changes and close once the service holds them, the copy replaced by its answer; with no pick, or signed out, they just close. Signed out at Done, the copy stays, the picks go with the sheet and the offer says why; unreached, waiting or refused, the sheet stays open with its picks and its note, and Done sends them again. A card's Remove from My Kit asks first (the notes kept on the site go with it), then sends that removal at once. The column lists the Kit as the service holds it. Withdrawn: the save bar, Save and Discard, the question on leaving the Kit, Later, the leaving mark and Keep in My Kit, and the question on quitting with changes. Checks: collection (Add sends nothing, Done one call and closes, Escape one call; Cancel of a removal sends nothing, Remove one call), kit_failures done_unreached_keeps_its_picks_and_sends_them_again and done_signed_out_keeps_the_copy_and_says_why_on_the_offer.

title: A sheet's exit key can be held, Escape then doing nothing
detail: Sheet gains exit-enabled: false greys its bar key and makes Escape do nothing. The Kit's search holds it while its Done is sending, its footer then saying Saving to The Lens DB…, so the key keeps its width. The Kit's sheet is counted among the sheets shown (sheet_count.slint), so it covers the window as every sheet does: its default key and Escape, the bar's menus, and Tab kept inside it.

title: A ghost key shows the hover's veil under the hand as every key does
detail: The owner's request: no key without a ground under the hand. button.slint draws the hover veil for ghost keys too; a ghost still neither presses nor sounds, so its veil never darkens to the pressed one. It reaches the Kit card's ..., the help mark, the fold chevron, a row's star and the readout steppers. Checks: states, keycap, button_group, toolbar_keys and tooltip window checks; shot kit-hover.

title: A search card opens its piece on The Lens DB from an arrow key before Add
detail: The owner's request: the search card's ... becomes a square key with an arrow pointing up and right (icons/arrow-up-right.svg, Trinil's stroke, Icons.open-out), its help See <piece> on The Lens DB, laid before Add, Added or In your Kit; it opens the piece's url with utm_source=oni. The Kit's cards keep their ... menu. Checks: oni-ui icons; collection (the arrow opens the FM2's page with utm_source=oni; twin: Add opens none).

title: The search's filters: the kind as tabs, the brand from the brands its answers hold
detail: The owner's request: simpler filters. One row under the field: the design system's Tabs All · Bodies · Lenses, and a Picker Any Brand whose choices are the brands of the answers asked without one, most frequent first, sent as the service writes them; the API lists no brand, so the picker shows once the answers hold two brands or one is chosen, its room kept meanwhile so the tabs never move. A search asks 50 answers, the service's most. The fixed brand and focal-length keys go. Checks: words the_brands_offered_are_the_answers_most_frequent_first (twin: the answers' order alone); collection (50 spans several brands, Nikon picked keeps Nikon's answers and is sent as brand=Nikon, Any Brand gives several back).

title: Why the Kit may be behind the service is said wherever the Kit shows
detail: The note (unreached, waiting, refused, signed out, pieces left out) shows in the caution's ink in the column, the search sheet above its answers, the offer and the sign-in's wait. Checks: kit_failures (Done unreached: the note in the sheet, the picks and the token kept; signed out at Done: the note on the offer, kit.json kept, the token forgotten; a firewall's 403 at launch: the copy shown, signed in still, the note in the column, the Kit read once).

title: Catalogue provided by The Lens DB beside its mark
detail: The contract's mention: TldbMark credited lays Catalogue provided by The Lens DB beside the mark, wrapping in the room left, or under it in the narrow column; the whole is one button for assistive tools, opening the site with utm_source=oni. It shows on the offer, the column's head, the search sheet's footer and Settings > Connected Apps. Check: collection finds it in the offer, the column and the sheet.

title: The EXIF convention: Model and LensModel keep the full name, Make and LensMake the brand
detail: kit/facts.rs states ONI's choice, which the contract leaves to it: Model and LensModel stay the full name, brand included, as typed, as rolls, defaults and photo counts name a piece, and as Canon, Nikon and Leica write Model themselves; a piece without a brand writes no Make or LensMake (oni-export skips an empty one); FocalLength stays a prime's. Check: facts the_model_is_the_full_name_and_a_missing_brand_writes_no_make (twin: the model alone is not what Model keeps).

title: The Kit's new texts in French and Spanish
detail: scripts/i18n laid the new texts and dropped the withdrawn ones (save bar, leaving, quitting, the brand and focal keys); French and Spanish filled: Catalogue fourni par The Lens DB / Catálogo proporcionado por The Lens DB, Any Brand, See {} on The Lens DB, Saving to The Lens DB…, the footer's texts and the empty search's. Checks: oni-i18n catalogue, oni-app anonymity templates.

title: The Kit's window checks drive Done, Escape, the brand filter, the arrow key, the removal's question and the protocol
detail: collection.rs rewritten over a shared stage (tests/window/kit): the offer, the sign-in, Search Gear with the arrow key, Add and Done, the sheet opened again bare, 50 filtered by brand and Escape sending its pick, a removal cancelled then confirmed, defaults and the export, the Camera Body field, the card's page, Disconnect revoking the token, and every journal entry naming ONI with no Origin. kit_failures.rs (five checks): no service named, the 429 hold, Done unreached, Done signed out, a firewall at launch. Shots: kit-offer, kit-signed-in, kit-search, kit-search-failed, kit-hover, kit-defaults, kit-field.

title: The Kit driven in the real app against the simulated The Lens DB
detail: scripts/check (151 binaries, none failed, ONI_CHECK_LIMIT=900) and scripts/lint in the worktree. The app built with --profile app (with Slint's MCP server to drive it) and run with ONI_BACKGROUND=1, ONI_TLDB=fake and a private support and caches folder, over the simulated service holding 101 real catalogue pieces: the sign-in made through the simulated pages and token address as a browser would (Connect itself is not pressed, as the system browser would take the focus; the window check drives it), the column's Kit read, a search of 50mm filtered by kind (Bodies: nothing matches) and by the brand picker (Nikon), Add, Done saving the pick in one change and closing, a removal asked then sent, a relaunch reading the Kit unchanged (its copy not rewritten), Disconnect revoking the token and dropping the copy, and a service unreached at launch keeping the copy with its note (the log names no address). ONI_BENCH=flows on the test copy of roll #8: no failure. Nothing was sent to thelensdb.com.

title: The Lens DB's credit reads "Catalogue provided by" and then its mark
detail: TldbMark credited lays the words before the disc and the name, on one line or over them in a narrow column, so the service is named once; its accessible label is unchanged. The offer's password note and the sheet's empty-picks line are gone; the count of picks and Saving stay.

title: The Kit search filters by Type and Mount, two selects
