A chosen mount stays offered when new answers hold none. words::mounts and fits, with their twin; the collection window check picks Nikon F and Lenses.

title: The roll's Camera Body and the export's Camera and Lens are one combobox
detail: KnownField is a Picker (now with a placeholder and a name for assistive tools) whose list drops at a click: a field to type any name heads the Kit's cards and the names typed before. Return or a click beside the list gives what was typed, Escape drops it; a pick gives its name. Slint's popups take the keyboard when shown (WindowInner::show_popup), so a field outside the list could not keep typing while it is open. Window checks: collection (pick, Return, click beside), escape, export_columns.

title: The gear fields are a true combobox: typed in the field, the list dropped under it
detail: #2309's select with a search field in its list is withdrawn (owner: a combobox is an input that drops its possibilities). KnownField is again a text field, its chevron inside the face: clicked into, typed in or its chevron pressed, it drops the Kit's cards and the names typed before, and takes back the keyboard the popup took (WindowInner::show_popup moves it away from the window), so the words are typed in the field with the list open. The press that dropped the list is not read as a press beside the field. A pick or Return gives the name and ends the typing. Window checks: collection (pick, typed with the list open, Return), escape, export_columns.

title: The Kit search's selects side by side, Mount always offered, the search field let go by a press beside it
detail: The Type and Mount labels are gone and All Gear reads Bodies & Lenses. The Mount select is never dimmed: its choices are the answers' mounts, then the Kit's, so the Kit's are offered before any search; the v1 search takes no mount (q, type, brand, limit), so ONI keeps sifting the answers itself. Under a sheet, a press beside a field gave the keyboard nowhere, so the field kept it: a field let go under a sheet now hands it to the latest sheet laid, as a sheet closing over another does; a control let go keeps the default key's hold, so Return still answers. The collection check presses the sheet's title and asserts the field let go, the sheet still open.

title: The Kit search filters by kind alone, its select right of the search field
detail: The mount filter is withdrawn (owner): the v1 search takes no mount, and sifting fifty answers on ONI's side filtered too little to earn its place. The answers are the service's again, words::mounts and fits and their test gone. The kind select (Bodies & Lenses, Bodies, Lenses) sits on the search's row, right of its field. The collection check asserts the select's place, that both kinds answer before Lenses, and that Lenses asks the service with type=lens.

title: The Kit column's head: My Kit, and "provided by" with a larger mark at its right
detail: The column's title shares its row with The Lens DB's credit, right-aligned: "provided by" then the mark, its disc 22 px and its name 15 px (KitStyle.mark-header, word-header), a step larger than the sheet's 18 px and 13 px. TldbMark takes the words before it (lead) and its name's size (word-size); its accessible label still reads the whole mention.

title: A launch opens its folder on the Kit with nothing picked; the Kit's head a step above Search Gear
detail: The launch reopens the folder remembered, and a roll's folder showed its roll in the column, so the Kit took a click on the empty room each time. open_remembered now leaves nothing picked and turns the column to the Kit (gear_shown), as that click does; a folder a hand opens still shows its roll, and a photo picked shows it. Window check presence::a_launch_opens_its_folder_on_the_kit_with_nothing_picked, seen failing without the change. The Kit column's head (My Kit, provided by and the mark) takes Space.s more below it.

title: Every gear card's name opens its page on The Lens DB, an arrow kept beside it; the Kit's card and the search's one shape
detail: GearCardBody takes linked: its name becomes a link (accent under the hand, its help and accessible label 'See {} on The Lens DB') followed by a small arrow (KitStyle.link-arrow, 11 px token) that stays beside the name however short it is cut. PieceCard uses it in the Kit and in the search alike, its one difference the adding boolean (Add, Added or In your Kit, else the photos and the menu); the search's square open-out key and the menu's See on The Lens DB line are gone, the name being the one way to the page. The gear fields' list keeps plain names, a click there picks the piece. Window check collection::the_kit_signs_in_searches_and_validates opens the page from the search's and the Kit's names and asserts the menu no longer holds the line.

title: Gear names underlined under the hand; the Kit sheet on its header's margins; a smaller mark in the column; the signed-out offer as ONI × The Lens DB
detail: A gear card's name no longer turns accent under the hand, unreadable on the grey: it takes a plain underline in its own ink (Stroke.line, as wide as the name shown). The Kit column's mark steps down (19 px, its name 13 px). The search sheet's search row, answers and foot take the bar header's side margins (SheetStyle.padding) and Space.m above and below, so the title, the field, the cards, the credit and Done line up; the window check asserts the credit's left edge on the title's and the kind select's right edge on Done's. Signed out, the column drops its credit line and shows the app's logo × The Lens DB's mark at one height (KitStyle.pair-height), the line 'ONI partners with The Lens DB, the largest photography database in the world.' and six checked promises: import the Kit, track the collection, fill EXIF, free from two non-profit projects with no ads, photos never leave the computer, disconnect at any time in Settings; then Connect and Create an Account.

title: The offer's logos stacked and centred, its tagline on bodies and lenses, wider and centred in the column; the sheet foot's mark on its words' middle; The Lens DB's disc beside its names in the gear lists
detail: TldbPair stacks the app's logo (40 px), a light × (22 px, weight 200) and the mark (28 px), each centred. The offer takes wider sides (KitStyle.offer-inset, 32 px), centres its tagline, now 'ONI partners with The Lens DB, the largest camera bodies and lenses database in the world.', and stands in the middle of the column's height. TldbMark centres its content in a row taller than the disc, as beside the sheet foot's key, where the disc and its name sat at the row's top while the words centred. GearCardBody takes served: The Lens DB's disc (TldbDisc, 12 px, accessible 'From The Lens DB') before a name the service gives; the gear fields' lists set it on the Kit's cards, the names typed by hand stay bare.

title: A roll names its lens as its body; the gallery filters by medal, camera and lens
detail: Film gains lens (optional, omitted when none, in sidecars and folder markers alike), set in the roll's column by a second gear field under Camera Body (Library.roll-lens, 'Set Lens' step). Every export's line takes the roll's lens over the scan's and over the Kit's default lens, follows the roll while no hand set it, and keeps a lens a hand set. The index (schema 14, a new file rebuilt from the sidecars) caches film_lens and marker_lens; Entry::body and Entry::lens read a photo's gear as the Kit's counts do (the EXIF line's, else the folder roll's, else the sidecar roll's), and the lens counts follow. A marker the app writes now updates the shown folder's rows in memory too, which kept the roll's former gear until the next read. The archive's filter becomes library::Filter { medal, body, lens }, admitted together; the gallery's column heads with three selects stacked, Medals, Camera, Lens, each reading its own name while it keeps All (All its first line alone), Camera and Lens listing the open folder's bodies and lenses, the most photos first. Window check sidebar_filter::the_camera_and_lens_filters_keep_one_body_or_lens, seen failing before the rows followed the marker; unit checks on the index's lens columns and counts and on the export line.

title: One gear sheet everywhere: the search at the left, the Kit's column at the right; every gear field's list ends with Search on The Lens DB; sidecar format 34 for the roll's lens
detail: KitSearchSheet lays the search (field, kind, answers, foot) at the left and KitView, the gallery's Kit column, at the right (in-sheet: its Search Gear key left out). Signed out or waiting, the left side says the search waits on the column's sign-in, the column offering ONI × The Lens DB and Connect; signed in there, the search shows in place. Kit.search-gear takes the kind it opens on (0 both, 1 bodies, 2 lenses). KnownField gains search-line, searching and search(): its list's last line, after a divider, The Lens DB's disc and 'Search on The Lens DB', asks the search then closes (closing first ended the line's own handler), and the list drops again once the sheet closes, with what Done added; the roll's Camera Body and Lens and the export's Camera and Lens fields set it. The latest additions to The Lens DB are not shown: the partner API v1 offers search, the Kit and its changes only. From the adversarial review of #2318: sidecar format 34 (ROLL_LENS_VERSION), so a format-33 build opens a sidecar naming a roll's lens read-only instead of dropping it, the newer-file corpus moved to version-35 (folder markers carry no version: an older build rewriting one drops its lens); the index's respelling merge carries film_lens; the projects keep the medal filter alone, as their column shows it, and beside a photo a camera or lens filter set in the gallery stays shown under the header; a photo's marker read once. Window checks collection::a_gear_field_searches_the_lens_db_signed_out_and_lists_what_was_added (seen failing while the line closed its list first) and the sheet's column in the_kit_signs_in_searches_and_validates; unit check on the lens in markers and sidecars.

title: A pick joins the Kit's column at once, the count line gone; the gallery's one filter in three parts; The Lens DB's disc in the gear field itself
detail: The Kit's column lists the pieces picked in the sheet after the service's, at once (KitMark.added, no photo count), Done still sending them in one call; a pick's menu holds Remove from My Kit alone, which takes it out at once with nothing asked, nothing of it having been sent. The sheet's foot drops '{n} piece joins your Kit on The Lens DB at Done.' and keeps 'Saving to The Lens DB…' while Done sends. The gallery's three selects become one filter (GalleryFilter, rating_filter.slint), its menu built in Rust (app/filter_menu.rs): All Photos, then a rule and Gold, Silver, Bronze, then a heading Camera and the open folder's bodies, then Lens and its lenses, one line checked a part (MenuLine.checked, a DS field a line takes beside its menu's current), a pick again letting its part go; its face reads All Photos or what it keeps, 'Gold · Nikon FM2'. Beside a photo the archive's compact select is that filter too, so a body or lens kept stays seen; the projects keep the medal select. The three pills side by side did not hold; Picker.tight went with them. Window checks: the_camera_and_lens_filters_keep_one_body_or_lens keeps a body and a lens at once, lets one go, All Photos back; unit check on the menu's lines and face. A gear field whose words name a piece of the Kit shows The Lens DB's disc before them in the field itself, as its list does (KnownField.served, from Gear.served(kind, name, revision), a pure callback asking the Kit copy, revision moving at each Kit published); a name typed by hand stands bare, which the Kit check asserts both ways.

title: The grain's clumps take in the scene whole from the faintest Amount, which moves their contrast alone, and a haze of that blur lies between them; the grain's colour line leaves Film Effects, its shadows' colour a step lighter
detail: oni_pipeline::grain lays dissolving(1.0) at any Amount above zero, where the dissolve followed Amount: a faint grain was a texture laid over the photo, its clumps taking in only that share of the scene blurred under them; now a grain of any strength is drawn whole, Amount scaling its stops (GRAIN_STOPS × Amount) alone (owner's call). The kernel and its CPU reference are unchanged; every render grained under Amount 1 at a size above the finest moves. Check grain_detail::any_amount_dissolves_whole_and_moves_the_contrast_alone (dissolve 1 at 1 % and 100 %, stops 1 % of the whole, twin: Amount 0 lays no grain; it fails on the former mapping). The grain's colour line (GrainColourEditor) leaves the panel, as the Grain Curve did (#2209): its rest, black 2, white 0, stays laid, the component stays in the code; the help loses its paragraph and says the grains are drawn whole, more contrasted with Grain (fr, es). Window check grain_colour::the_grains_colour_line_leaves_the_panel replaces the one that dragged its ends. Between the clumps the scene now takes GRAIN_HAZE (0.9, owner's eye) of that same blur (Grain.haze, the uniform's mix.z, the shader and the CPU reference alike: w = dissolve × share × (haze + (1 − haze) × clump)), so a coarse grain lets no detail finer than itself read sharp through it; the blur's deviation grows with Size, none at the finest grain, and light and dark clumps take it alike as before. Measured on one-pixel lines at Size 1, Amount 0.8: 0.06 % of the detail's energy left inside the clumps, 1 % between them (was about 100 %); at Size 0.25, 93 % kept. Checks: dissolve_tests::a_haze_lays_its_share_of_the_dose_between_clumps_and_the_whole_inside_them (twin: no haze keeps them sharp), the GPU against its reference with a haze (twin: the haze ignored), grain_detail's thresholds in energies. The colour's rest deepens the shadows' hue a step less, black 1.5 where it was 2 (owner's eye), white 0: every frame at rest takes it, the 36 corpus goldens with it.

title: Digital: More Color Settings a block of its own, a Black and White switch, Auto White Balance on the photo's white; sidecar format 35
detail: More Color Settings leaves the Colour block for a block of its own under it, folded by default, on every mode that shows colour. A digital photo gains black_and_white (PipelineSettings, 'blackAndWhite', unwritten when false): its finishing keeps the luminance alone (luma_only, as a black and white film's), its colour settings kept for when it turns back; the switch stands at the head of the Color tab on either face, as it decides what both print (PanelState.black-and-white). Auto White Balance reaches a digital photo: the negative's Shades of Gray (sixth-power means through the render, Newton bringing red's and blue's onto green's, filter_balance::grey generalised over two axes) moves the photo's white instead of print filters, in mireds and tint from its decode's own white, held to the white's ranges, and lays it whole on Temperature and Tint (no roll's share to dose it); none of a negative's roll, levels or colour compression enters. Outcome, Kept and the sidecar's AutoBalance carry the white found, so a kept reading is recalled; several photos averaged on (u, v). Sidecar format 35 (DIGITAL_BLACK_AND_WHITE_VERSION) so a format-34 build opens these files read-only rather than drop either; the newer-file corpus moves to version-36, the 36 goldens print black_and_white. Black and White is part of the roll's mode, as a black and white film's is (roll_settings Field::Mode carries it with invertedSource, parameters' EXCLUDED names why): no paste or preset carries it, and the preset sheet keeps its room. Checks: digital::a_digital_photo_in_black_and_white_prints_grey (twin: the switch off keeps the colour; a slide ignores it), filter_balance::a_digital_photo_s_key_finds_the_white_that_prints_it_grey (a warm scene lands at 3934 K, the means within 4e-6; twin: its own white leaves the cast; the white laid whole, the print untouched).

title: docs/pipeline-map.md: the whole application in sixteen Mermaid diagrams
detail: Files on disk to the canvas and the export; the render chain in the order the code runs it, a table of which stage runs in which mode (Negative, Positive, Monochrome, Digital, Digital on a virtual film) and where a slider notch restarts; the Pro and Scanner faces and their machines; Prepare the Roll, Auto White Balance, Auto De-dust and the flat-field; the archive, the gallery filter, the Kit and export, presets, paste and roll gestures, the phone link; every WGSL kernel with its CPU reference, the texture formats and the render slot; a glossary. Each box names the file that implements it, as of 8cf90530. Its findings: no dark pick in Prepare the Roll, Auto levels called by tests alone, the live Frontier never reading the measured table, slides decoded at 5500 K, comments still naming Swift.

title: A filmed digital photo keeps its grain in the shadows
detail: The grain reads its share and colour off the tone each light of the scene shows, through stage 4-7 at unit gains. On a digital photo shot on the virtual film, stage 4-7 reads the virtual negative, not the scene the grain lies on: the scene read as if it were the scan turned the tones over, the grain fullest in the highlights and gone in the shadows. grain::scene_tones now passes each node's light through the stock's virtual negative (its CPU reference, at the film's exposure) and stage 4-7 at the film's own gains, so the tone is the one the photo shows. Measured at rest: the share 0.967 at a shadow light 0.03, 0.037 at 0.9. Check grain::a_filmed_photo_keeps_its_grain_in_the_shadows (twin: the scene read as the scan turns the shares over).

title: A filmed digital photo's scene stands at its film's daylight; its colour is balanced at the print, as a negative's
detail: The owner's call: a film sees the scene in its own light. VirtualStock::daylight names the stock's reference (Portra 800: D55, x 0.33242 y 0.34743, the 5500 K Kodak balances it for); PipelineSettings::scene_white renders a filmed photo's scene at it, the As Shot or hand white kept unrendered, so a tungsten scene reaches the film warm and a blue shade blue. The colour is then balanced at the print: on a filmed photo the print's filters (Temperature and Tint, the film's fields) are laid in stage 4-7 with the negative (unlit_print keeps them, own_stops renders them), Lighting never lays them twice; Auto White Balance reads it as a negative's (filters at Balance strength, no white), and the Colour block shows the film's Temperature, Tint and Auto White Balance Strength with a note that the scene stands at the film's daylight. Checks: virtual_film::the_film_keeps_the_photo_s_grey_and_off_gives_the_photo_back (a daylight grey prints neutral and as the photo prints it; the hand's white waits, twin: off it renders; the filters move a filmed photo, twin: a digital photo's wait), filter_balance (a filmed photo's key gives filters, never a white).

title: The crop's warning stands over Auto White Balance's plate, and no digital photo shows it
detail: The warning 'Crop before using the automatic balance' was laid inside the keycap's plate, which holds keycaps alone: the socket takes its row's height as if the wrapped line were one, so a two-line warning overflowed onto the key. It now stands over the plate as a caution note. A digital photo is picture to its edges, with no film edge or holder to crop away before a measure: crop_first is false on it. examples/colour_trace.rs follows the unified pipeline (no separate Lighting, the reference the stock derives).

title: A long fibre is healed part by part: a long stroke and a hair ringed are laid as short corrections, each copied from beside itself (sidecar format 36)
detail: Owner's report: De-dust works but for long fibres, where auto lays one point or misses, and no single stroke heals one. Measured on the owner's scans (P1071962, Lumix 47 Mpx, six fibres 190 to 310 pixels long, full Sensitivity; P1072860): three causes. One, a patch is one rigid copy of a place at least 1.8 times its stroke's size away, so a 300-pixel hair across an edge was copied from 1500 pixels off (the six fibres from 400 to 1500) and left a ghost band along it, and a patch stops at its stroke's 800-pixel tile. Two, a speck's body was the pixels over half its peak's rise: a hair's rise wavers (0.11 over a grain of 0.04 on a faint one, peak 0.23), so the half held 45 % of its pixels in pieces, the stroke walked the first piece alone and its radius grew to reach the others, 99.8 and 120 pixels on two of the six: one giant round patch on a fibre. Three, the same hair read at several insets came out as up to four overlapping corrections. Now: Correction::split (oni-settings/src/frame/parts.rs) cuts a stroke where it spans more than SPAN = 2 radii either way, each part from the last's end, a scribble on one speck staying whole; the hand's stroke (paint_end) and auto's are laid so, one undo step. At 4 radii a ribbon across three tones still left blobs, at 2 none. A speck judged as before then takes in the fainter stretches joined to it among what showed it (FAINT, half the half), so the judgment and the count of specks do not move but a hair is one body (86 % of the faint one's pixels along one walk); dust::strokes walks it end to end, then what the walk leaves (a branch, a loop's other side), each part's radius its own pixels' reach plus the halo, a clump widening its part alone. The parts of one gesture (Correction.gesture, a long stroke's parts or a removal's specks; sidecar format 36, absent read as laid alone, an older build opens it read-only) await each other: Region.awaited marks the pixels under those without a patch, which the search's costs (CPU reference and WGSL kernel alike), the tone's means and the copy itself leave out; without it a part matched its tone on the hair still lying beside it and laid light discs. A stroke laid alone, and every stroke stored before, is searched exactly as it was. Measured, P1071962 at full Sensitivity: 12 corrections on the six fibres, two of radius 100 and 120, before; 79 of radius 10 to 15 after, 4.0 s; the hair across an edge, the faint loop (one point of radius 120 before) and the U on an even ground heal with no ghost, the knot over a line keeps the line but for a short break, the ribbon across white, green and a pink border leaves the green clean; a second reading rings none of them. A hand's stroke along the same hair, radius 14: a ghost band as one patch, clean cut in parts. P1072860 in the real app (dev build, ONI_BENCH=autodust): 8 rings, 21 corrections, 21 patches in 1.4 s, a second reading finds none; ONI_BENCH=dedust: a 2500-pixel stroke at radius 28 is 45 corrections, healed whole in 5.6 s. Rings at 0/25/50/75/100 %: P1071962 8, 8, 29, 29, 66 (8, 8, 30, 30, 73 before, the same hairs counted twice), P1072860 unchanged, P1072734 38, 41, 81, 124, 202, every one on a stroke of the owner's. Left: a fibre whose ground passes the window with it, or that lies inside the window, is not ringed (P1072860's two short fibres; the brush's long stroke heals them); a part straddling several tones at once can still leave a soft blob; a long stroke stored before stays one patch until painted again; ONI_SIDECAR_GOLDENS, outside the repository, wants gesture: None after each correction's radius. Checks: frame::parts tests (cut, joined, scribble, tail, split, twins), corrections::laid_with (twin: a stroke painted since), dust tests (a wavering hair ringed whole, twin under FAINT; a loop and a branch walked, twin one walk; a clump's own radius), heal tests (a part neither matches nor copies the parts awaiting, twin unmarked copies the hair; GPU costs against the reference with pixels awaited, twin read as image), auto.rs (a hair as corrections end to end, one gesture), window checks auto_dust, dedust_grid, dedust_turn; corpus goldens carry the gesture, the newer-file fixture is version 36. examples/heal_probe heals a frame headless and writes each window before and after.

title: A digital photo shot on a virtual Kodak Portra 800: its scene exposed, developed and scanned as that negative, then read as any negative is; sidecar format 37
detail: oni_pipeline::film bakes spektrafilm's Portra 800 profile (crates/oni-pipeline/resources/film, shipped unchanged with SPEKTRAFILM_LICENSE.txt, a CHANGELOG.txt of what ONI derives, and Jakob and Hanika's spectra from vkdt under BSD-2-Clause, SPECTRA_LICENCE.txt) once, in 28 ms: the light per chromaticity (192² nodes: spectra × sensitivities through the profile's band-pass window, each channel's D55 response kept, spektrafilm's radial gamut compression laid in), the curves above their least density and before the DIR couplers act (spektrafilm's colour-negative matrix), the scan's dyes and base on 405 to 695 nm read under D50 by the 1931 observer, Bradford to D65, in linear Rec. 2020. One GPU stage, virtual_negative (oni-render, scalar reference beside it): working Rec. 2020 to XYZ on D55 by CAT16, the table read bilinearly, × 2^EV, log, curve, couplers, curve, the 59-wavelength scan summed in the shader; it runs after Digital's white, halation and grain, as a pass of its own the print's notches start from. The negative is read as a negative (PipelineSettings::read_as) on its film's own reference (VirtualFilm: stock, exposure, gains, each channel's black and white as shares of the graduation window), derived from the profile as Prepare the Roll measures a roll: gains that make the bare film grey, every black on it, each white where a scene grey enters the print where the digital photo's own render enters it, so the photo keeps its grey; the scan at a mosaic negative's ceiling, no dye unmix, the rest of Digital's path (Lighting after its levels, white, lens, black and white) unchanged; the Scanner face's keys move the film's gains. Colour tab: a Film block on a digital photo, either face (None, Portra 800), Film exposure (rest 0), the gains and the ends behind its settings key; reset and double-click return to the stock's own; About credits spektrafilm by Andrea Volpato and vkdt. Sidecar format 37 (VIRTUAL_FILM_VERSION), absent read as none; virtualFilm is the roll's, with the mode (EXCLUDED from presets); the newer-file corpus moves to version-38, the goldens print virtual_film. Measured: the kernel within 0.00018 density of a double-precision reference written from spektrafilm's steps (Mitchell-cubic table, np.interp, every wavelength) on a grey ramp, the ColorChecker at three exposures and the primaries; GPU within 8e-8 of its reference; a grey exposes each layer within 0.023 log of 0; on a 3456 × 2234 region the pass costs 3.6 ms against 1.0 ms for a plain per-pixel pass. Checks: virtual_film (reference, twins: couplers off, exposure a tenth of a stop off; grey on the data sheet, twin: couplers on the sheet's own curves; GPU, twins: 1 % brighter, channels swapped; the film keeps the photo's grey to 1e-5 and off renders the photo to the bit, twins: a stop over, film on), oni-settings virtual_film (absent before 37, kept, newer refused), window virtual_film::a_digital_photo_is_shot_on_portra_and_back. The files the film grew past 400 lines are split: the Film block its own Slint file (panel/film_block.slint), the panel's Block table (fields/block.rs), the film's and the gains' knobs (knob/film.rs, knob/gains.rs), the presets' exclusions (parameters/excluded.rs); codec_checks' ceiling comes down to 720.

title: examples/film_compare renders a digital photo headless, plain and on its virtual Portra 800, with the scene the film reads and its scan
detail: crates/oni-app/examples/film_compare.rs: `film_compare <raw> <out> [side]` reads the photo's sidecar, renders it as the editor does (Engine::render on the preview, at a long side of 1600 by default) plain (A) and on the stock's own reference (B), each at the RAW's As Shot white, the sidecar's own white and the film's D55, and writes beside them the chain's own steps up to the film: the framed scene after Digital's white, then the virtual negative's scan, each as `w h` and f32 RGB in linear Rec. 2020. It lets the virtual film be compared with spektrafilm's own pipeline fed the same scene; it writes no sidecar.

title: Where ONI's print of the virtual Portra 800 departs from spektrafilm's paper print, measured stage by stage
detail: crates/oni-app/examples/colour_trace.rs prints scenes or scans through the CPU references of the virtual negative and stage 4-7 at a sidecar's settings (within 1 % of the GPU render on the photo's patches), or prints a real frame's stage 4-7 arguments; docs/research/colour-diagnosis/*.py rebuild B and C on the ColorChecker, the photo's patches and a grey ramp, and swap each stage (reading, tone, output) for spektrafilm's.
outcome: On spektrafilm's own negative, ONI's print is 6.1 dE00 from the paper print on the chart and 10.3 on the photo. Three causes: the tone (linear windows and a 2.2 power instead of the paper's curve: 10.3 to 4.4 on the photo), greys balanced at two points only (yellow-green shadows, magenta highlights), and the reading (the colorimetric scan reads the magenta dye into red, 2.23 stops per unit against the paper's 0.40). A printing-density matrix then the paper's curves and dyes reaches 0.81 (chart) and 0.61 (photo); grey balance on the whole ramp, the paper's tone and one 3x3 in density space reach 2.77 and 1.67. ONI's dye separation moves 0.2 to 1.0 closer, the chroma decompression 0.6 to 0.8 away. A camera scan (Nikon D5100, Sigma, measured sensitivities) shows the same gap: the step is missing for real negatives too.

title: A digital photo is always shot on its virtual film and its negative read by the negative's pipeline, as a scanned colour negative's
detail: The owner's strategy: no Digital pipeline or UX of its own, no film None. PipelineSettings::film() gives a digital photo its VirtualFilm (stock and exposure, Kodak Portra 800 by default) even where none is stored; rest(Digital) and carried() place the stock's reference in gains, levels and the dye family as Prepare the Roll places a roll's (on_stock), store::roll::digital lays it on a roll prepared as digital. The chain is one path: framed scene, lit at the stock's own white (VirtualStock::white, D55 for Portra 800) relative to the decode's anchor (conversion::scene_white), ONI's halation and grain on that scene, the virtual negative, then stage 4-7 exactly as a negative's (stage47 equal to a Negative's on the same settings): its gains, windows and ceiling (Highlight Detail, rest MOSAIC_REST whatever the file), Lighting and filters in the print, the dye separation on the stock's family (KodakC41 at separation::BASE) and the chroma decompression a colour negative on no measured roll takes (0.5 / 0.5). ConversionMode::Digital no longer reads positive; is_film gave way to is_digital (the camera's own lens, film effects, no copy stand) and is_measured (Prepare measures a negative and a black and white; a slide and a digital photo roll by folder). Print::resting_exposure is a negative's 1.5 EV. Auto White Balance reads a digital photo as it stands and writes the print's filters dosed by Balance strength, as on a negative; the Scanner face adds its keys to the photo's own gains, as on a negative, its phone channel a negative's. The Roll tab (Source) shows Filtration, Highlight Detail, Per-Channel Levels and Dye Separation, the Prepared Roll and Flat-Field blocks staying a scan's; the Colour tab's Temperature, Tint and Auto White Balance Strength are a negative's. Checks: digital_negative (stage 4-7 a negative's, twin a slide's; the stock's dyes and the 0.5/0.5 dose, twin a slide unmixes nothing; the scene at the stock's white, twin none on a negative; the Scanner keys on the photo's gains), virtual_film::the_film_prints_a_grey_as_a_plain_raw_and_its_negative_is_read_as_any_negative (GPU, judged against the scan read as a Negative, twin as a slide), filter_balance digital, store digital and modes, editors levels, window digital and virtual_film.

title: The digital-only machinery leaves: kelvin white, As Shot, digital_white, picture levels, the separate Lighting kernel, Black and White, film None
detail: Removed with their checks: PipelineSettings.white, shotWhite and the store's As Shot reading (read_shots, rested_white, oni_decode::as_shot), white::carried, KELVIN_RANGE and TINT_RANGE, the WhiteKelvin/WhiteTint knobs and fields with the mired track (Bend::Mired) and the kelvin readout and notch; oni_measure::key::digital_white and Outcome/Kept/AutoBalance's white; PictureLevels, Knob::Picture, Stage::PictureLevels, Pipeline::picture, the curves' levels tables and the curves kernel's ends (WGSL and CPU back to slope 1 past 1), LevelsChannel::PICTURE, Levels::transfer/end_slope, the Levels editor's picture windows and its fold; conversion::lighting, unlit_print, read_as, the print_px kernel and stages::print, the chain's Digital machine branch and finishing's levels/lit/points arguments; black_and_white and its toggle; the Film block's None tab and its gain, black and white sliders (FilmGain/Black/White knobs, fields 58-66, knob/film.rs). Fields after the kelvin pair renumber by two in the Slint panes. The level-end ordering a patch kept on picture windows now keeps the per-channel windows'.

title: Sidecar format 38: a digital photo of an earlier format opens on its film, every edit with an equivalent kept
detail: migrate::digital_film::caught_up, after the typed read of a sidecar and of any settings document: a digital photo is placed on its stock (stored or Portra 800); a format 37 film's stops, black and white, moved by hand off that format's reference (FORMER_PORTRA_800), keep the same moves on the stock's own; a photo on no film had no print filter rendered, so its filters and balance filters rest; Lighting's exposure takes +1.5 EV, the rest a negative's print stands on; the ceiling, separation and decompression a digital photo never rendered start at their rest. Curves, mixer, saturation, Chrome, vignette, grain, halation, lens, geometry, dust corrections, face and Scanner values, medal and EXIF line are kept; white, shotWhite, pictureLevels, blackAndWhite and the auto balance's white are dropped. The newer-file corpus moved to version 39; goldens lost the removed fields; two corpus-style digital sidecars (37-digital) carry their goldens. Checks: settings virtual_film (a format 37 photo edited everywhere: edits kept, the four keys gone, twin the same photo at 38 unmoved; a filmed one's hand moves kept, twin read on no film; a film frame of 37 unchanged), corpus goldens.

title: A stock's reference is placed for the negative's print at rest, held by its check, and shown read-only in the Film block
detail: film::derived: gains that make the bare film grey, each channel's black on the bare film, and its white where a scene grey, entering every window at one share, prints on the negative's print at rest (1.5 EV) as a slide's plain RAW render prints it (bisection on the share). The numbers live in VirtualStock::reference (oni-settings: rest, migration and resets read them) and film::tests holds them to the derivation within 1e-5 (twin: the print at no exposure prints the grey off). Portra 800: stops -0.844, 0, +1.197; black 0.2667; white 0.648, 0.727, 0.763. The Film block's settings key shows the stock's white (5500 K) and its gains, blacks and whites; the Source tab's Filtration and Per-Channel Levels rest there (fields::base, editors::stored::resting_levels, levels tabs marked against that rest), the Dyes say the stock's. The ceiling's travel on a digital photo is a mosaic's (density_axis::range_for(mosaic, mode)).

title: film_compare renders the unified digital photo and its separation and decompression at rest apart
detail: examples/film_compare reads the sidecar through the migration and writes B (the photo as the editor renders it), the scene its film reads and the film's scan, for its rest and with the dye separation, the chroma decompression or both at rest, to weigh each against spektrafilm's Portra 800 + Endura on the same scene.

title: The dye separation unmixes each stock's measured dyes on every photo: a scan's densities solved exactly for the negative's dye amounts, the family's hand-tuned rows gone
detail: oni_pipeline::film::dyes reads each stock's channel_density and base_density from its spektrafilm profile (shipped unchanged, CC BY-SA 4.0) on the wavelengths it measures both, and a camera: the 1931 observer under the light table's D50, the virtual negative's own scan, its Rec. 2020 matrix inverted so the solve runs on the camera's own channels, never negative (on Rec. 2020's lobes dense mixtures read below zero and have no solution). No measured camera set was found under a clear licence (the NPL D5100 and Sigma data name none), so the colorimetric observer stands for a camera whose matrix makes it colorimetric. Per pixel (new kernel dye_separation, WGSL beside its scalar reference, a pass of its own so a print notch starts past it; cpu::stage47 composes both): density through the frame's gains and pedestal, above the bare film (its Levels black), to camera light by the stock's own bare film, then three Newton steps from the matrix (the inverse of the camera's response at a unit of each dye), each bounded at 0.5, a singular slope falling back on the matrix; dosed by Dye separation between the scan's densities and the dye amounts, resting on the whole unmix (1.0). Each dye's amount is then toned onto the density a neutral grey holding it reads on the frame's own windows (128 nodes through 512 greys, from ten times a clear film's light to the guard's density; closed windows read each amount as its density), so every grey the windows print neutral prints as before and the colours alone are unmixed. Removed: SeparationFamily, its hand-tuned rows, chroma_kept, the family tabs and dye source, separation_family, STOCK_DYES and dye_family, stage 4-7's matrix rows (its uniform two rows shorter). The Look Lab keeps the Swift machine's generic rows at 0.6 as the coordinates its sets were fitted in, its neutral set refitted to Pro on the measured dyes (median dE 0.55, the chain having no unmix of its own; its check bound 0.6). For a paper to come: the untoned dye amounts above the bare film (DyeSeparation::separated) and the stock's dye and base spectra (film::dyes::measured). Checks: dye_separation (the virtual Portra 800's scan of the chart at eight exposures and a grey ramp separates into the dye amounts it developed within 1.4e-6, twins its scan's own densities 0.58 off and Gold 200's dyes 0.11 off; every set converges within 5e-6 where the matrix alone misses by 0.05 to 0.16; the generic set is the mean, no profile's; a digital photo unmixes its stock's dyes from its bare film; only a colour negative at a dose unmixes; the tones keep every neutral grey and spread a colour; GPU within 1e-6, twin a dose 10 % off), branches (stage 4-7 after a separation), the kernel's unit checks, the closed-window tone.

title: Each film stock names its measured dyes: its own profile's where one exists, else a generic C-41 set flagged as approximate
detail: oni_settings::dyes::STOCK_DYE_SETS beside the catalogue: Kodak Portra (Portra 400), Gold (Gold 200), UltraMax (UltraMax 400), Fujifilm Fujicolor (C200), Fujicolor Pro (Pro 400H), Superia (Superia X-TRA 400), CineStill 50D and 800T (Vision3 50D and 500T, their remjet removed); every other colour negative (generic, azure, redscale, CineStill 400D, ColorPlus, Harman Phoenix, Phoenix II and Red, LomoChrome Turquoise, Lucky, Mira) the generic C-41 set, the mean of the nine C-41 profiles shipped (Portra 160, 400, 800, Ektar 100, Gold 200, UltraMax 400, C200, Pro 400H, Superia X-TRA 400) at each wavelength more than half measure; black and white and slides none. A digital photo's virtual film uses its own stock's (Portra 800). resources/film gains ten profiles, unchanged, its CHANGELOG naming them and the derivation; About credits the measured dyes.

title: Prepare the Roll's Film step picks the stock with the roll column's picker; a stock picked later relays the measured dyes in one step; the Dye Separation block names the dyes
detail: The Film step shows the roll's stock (its marker's, else its film type's generic one) with Select Film Stock opening the same StockPickerSheet (StockTarget::Prepare), its words saying the stock matters as much as the film type, and a note on its dyes (measured, or the generic set's warning). The draft keeps the stock picked. PREPARE ROLL lays the stock's measured dyes on every frame it measures (the measure itself reads at no unmix, before the windows) and writes the stock on the roll's marker when it is another. Set Film Stock in the roll column writes the stock's measured set on every frame of the roll, one gallery step, the open photo's block with it; the roll card reads the sets its frames unmix and warns, with its fix, on a set off the stock's. Source tab, Dye Separation: the dyes by their stock's name (the generic set flagged as approximate) and the dose slider, nothing else; its reset brings back the whole unmix on the stock's dyes. Texts in French and Spanish.

title: Sidecar format 39: every photo moves onto its stock's measured dyes, a dose still on the family's rest to the whole unmix, a hand's kept
detail: migrate::measured_dyes, on every document before format 39 (sidecars, presets, share codes): the dose still at the family's rest (0.6) becomes 1.0, any other kept as the hand set it; the dye set from a digital photo's film, else the stock its sidecar's roll names, else, read beside its original, its folder's roll marker; separationFamily is dropped. Older steps that wrote the family's rest now name it (separation::FAMILY_REST). The newer-file corpus moves to version-40; the goldens print the measured set and the dose.

title: The measured dyes against spektrafilm's C, before and after, on the ColorChecker chain, P1073076 and roll #8
detail: colour_trace on the virtual Portra 800's chart, the photo's patches and a grey ramp, dE2000 to spektrafilm's Portra 800 + Endura (docs/research/colour-diagnosis, C at the grey's exposure); film_compare on P1073076 with the owner's settings, dE2000 to C through the shipped LUT on eleven patches; roll #8 frames 6438, 6444, 6452 and 6456 on Fujicolor's C200 dyes, against the owner's reference (the measured dyes at 0.6 on DSC_6444, judged superb).
outcome: Chain (chart / photo patches / greys): family 7.22 / 13.14 / 8.39; measured dyes 0.6: 7.16 / 13.04 / 9.51; 1.0: 7.81 / 13.14 / 10.09. P1073076 (mean of eleven patches): family 14.12, measured dyes at 1.0 14.22; cheek 15.6 to 13.3, forearm 14.8 to 11.2, cap 14.8 to 12.4, sky 5.3 to 2.7, fuselage red 7.7 to 13.7, tee 15.5 to 17.4, greens 1.5 worse. Roll #8 at 1.0 sits 1.4 to 1.8 dE00 (mean) from the 0.6 reference, the family 2.4 to 3.1 from it. As the diagnosis predicted, the unmix alone moves little on today's print: it fixes the colorimetric reading's crosstalk, but the windows balance greys at three points only, so the film's own greys off that line (its shadows) are unmixed too, +1.7 dE on the ramp at 1.0; the paper to come reads the dye amounts and owns the grey balance. A dark saturated colour's coloured grain lifts 2.4 L at the slider's top (1.0 on the family's rows): its check bound is 2.5, under the twin's 3.4.

title: colour_trace prints a digital photo at rest at any dose; film_compare renders the measured dyes at chosen doses, a scan on its roll's stock
detail: colour_trace takes rest:<dose> in place of a settings file; film_compare adds B-dyes-<dose> for each dose ONI_COMPARE_DOSES lists, the measured set a digital photo's film's, else its roll marker's stock's; cost.rs times the dye separation's pass on a full-screen region.

title: The film stock catalogue splits each line into its stocks wherever a spektrafilm profile measures them, each on its own dyes
detail: oni_settings::film: Kodak Portra 160, 400 and 800, Gold 200 and UltraMax 400 (their line's canister), Ektar 100, Verita 200D, Vision3 50D, 200T, 250D and 500T (the generic colour negative's canister until their own is drawn), Fujifilm C200 (Fujicolor's), Pro 400H (Fujicolor Pro's) and Superia X-TRA 400 (Superia's); CineStill 50D and 800T stay on their Vision3 base. oni_settings::dyes gains Portra 160, Ektar 100, Verita 200D, Vision3 200T and 250D; every precise stock separates on the profile of its own name. The six lines (Kodak Portra, Gold, UltraMax, Fujifilm Fujicolor, Fujicolor Pro, Superia) become `line` entries the picker no longer offers, each kept on the profile it stood for. Lines no profile splits stay as they were, on the generic C-41 set, itself unchanged. A digital photo's virtual film names Kodak Portra 800 in the catalogue, on its Portra 800 dyes as before.

title: A roll set on a line keeps its key and its render, said 'Stock not specified' until a hand picks a precise stock
detail: Old line keys stay catalogue entries rather than migrating: a roll set on Kodak Portra was never said to be Portra 400, so writing a precise stock on its marker would state what nobody stated, the marker carries no version a migration could guard, and its frames already hold the line's measured set, so the render is the same to the bit either way. The picker shows a roll's line at its catalogue place among the line's stocks, marked and noted 'Stock not specified'; the roll column says it under the name, Prepare the Roll's Film step says its dyes are the line's profile's until one is picked; the export's film field keeps the line's name. Texts in French and Spanish. Checks: each split stock unmixes its own profile file's dyes, every pair on different matrices (twin: Portra 160 against Portra 400's file); the six lines, the generic set, CineStill 800T and the virtual Portra 800 separate on numbers pinned to the bit, identical on the build before; the picker's window check lists the stocks with their line's canister and shows a roll's line marked, gone once a stock is picked.

title: Sidecar format 40: a frame's dyes may name a split stock's set, which a build of 39 cannot read
detail: No step: a document of 39 reads its dye set and dose unmoved (crates/oni-settings/tests/stock_split.rs, every set by its own key, twin: a key a build of 39 lacks fails its typed read). A build of 39 takes a file of 40 for a newer one and leaves it as it is, where a set it cannot read, under its own format, would read as a broken file. The newer-file corpus moves to version-41. resources/film gains kodak_vision3_200t, kodak_vision3_250d and kodak_verita_200d from spektrafilm 3bb2c2d, unchanged, under CC BY-SA 4.0, named in its CHANGELOG; the README credits the measured dyes beside the virtual films.

title: A colour paper prints the negative in place of ONI's print: the enlarger's light through the dye amounts, the paper's layers, its curves, its dyes seen under D50
detail: New kernel paper (WGSL beside its scalar reference, oni-render kernel/paper.rs): each pixel read as dye amounts above the bare film (the dye separation's untoned amounts, dosed; or, with no unmix, the scan's densities through the frame's gains above its Levels black), the lamp's light (spektrafilm's TH-KG3: 3400 K behind a Schott KG3, its published curve read by scipy's Akima, shipped unchanged) through the dichroic C, M and Y filters and the negative's dyes and base on every wavelength the stock measures (a black and white's silver neutral on every wavelength, its density the mean of the three readings) summed onto the paper's three layer sensitivities, its log exposure turned by the contrast about a pivot, the paper's curves (spektrafilm's fitted model, sums of normal integrals, evaluated on its 256 nodes), then the print's dyes and base under D50 read by the 1931 observer, CAT02-adapted to D65, in linear Rec. 2020. It runs laid with the rest of stage 4-7 in one pass, after the dye separation's pass the cache keeps; stage 4-7 then reads the paper's print on the display gamma, Lighting's points as its windows, its zones, each channel's contrast and mids and the colour density after, ONI's windows, print curve, Hunt, follow and chroma decompression left out (never stacked). The paper replaces the print only where one can print the photo (negative, black and white, digital; never a slide or a positive read as its own negative, PipelineSettings::takes_paper) and the print is not bypassed (a measure upstream). Per frame (oni_pipeline::paper::printing, on the CPU): the reference grey is the scan density each window prints as a plain RAW's grey on ONI's print at rest; the enlarger's exposure and magenta and yellow filtration (cyan at none) are solved by Newton so that grey prints there, neutral; Lighting's filters move the filtration by 30.1 CC a stop (Temperature and Tint: a stop of filter halves its band's light), the least filter at none, the grey's luma held; Contrast turns the paper about the grey's exposure, its slope times 4^Contrast (the track a paper grade either way); Exposure is the enlarger's light, a stop up a stop less. The Scanner face's D, C, M and Y keys move the frame's gains, which the paper reads as density laid on the negative, as filtration. Five papers bake their tables once at first use: Kodak Portra Endura (default), Supra Endura, Ultra Endura, Endura Premier and Fujifilm Crystal Archive Type II, their profiles shipped unchanged (CC BY-SA 4.0, CHANGELOG). Checks (crates/oni-pipeline/tests/paper.rs): the lamp within 1.4e-9 of spektrafilm's and its dichroics within 1e-6, twin the bare blackbody; every paper prints Portra 800's dye amounts as spektrafilm's printing stage does (log exposure 4e-7, density 1e-6, light 1.6e-6), twin five CC more magenta; the reference grey prints neutral where ONI's print puts it on a digital photo, a prepared negative, black and white and no unmix, twin the paper with no filtration; Lighting's exposure, filters (luma held) and contrast (the grey kept), twin the plain contrast; a slide, an inverted positive and a measure never printed, ONI's print to the bit when off; the GPU within 1.4e-6 of the reference on a digital photo, a lit negative (exposure, contrast, zones, filters, points, channel contrast and mids, colour density), black and white on Supra and no unmix on Crystal Archive, and the paper's pass alone, each twin 4e-2 off; the kernel's unit checks.

title: The paper's switch and choice on the Colour tab, on both faces, its filtration shown
detail: Wherever a paper can print the photo, at the end of Lighting on Pro and under the keys on the Scanner face (so no block above moves): Print on paper, the paper picked among five (Picker) and the enlarger's filtration in CC (Enlarger filtration: C, M, Y) while it prints; Lighting's help says what its sliders mean on a paper. A paste and the Lighting preset entry carry the paper with Lighting, whose sliders it gives their meaning (printPaper in the Color tab's family, carried by Lighting's own preset row, so a preset proposing Lighting proposes its paper). The spektrafilm credit in About names the papers. Texts in French and Spanish. Window check paper::the_paper_switch_prints_a_negative_on_its_paper_and_hides_on_a_slide (a negative at rest offered the switch, off; on prints on Portra Endura, shows its filtration and renders again; the five names listed, Crystal Archive picked; hidden on a slide with the choice kept; twin, off takes the paper away).

title: Sidecar format 41: every photo edited before stays on ONI's print, a new Prepare the Roll and a digital photo print on Portra Endura
detail: PipelineSettings.print_paper (printPaper, the paper's key, unwritten when none). migrate::paper::caught_up writes it off on every document before format 41 (sidecars, presets, share codes), so their render stays to the bit (owner's rule). PipelineSettings::rest(Digital) prints on the default paper, as balance::written (Prepare the Roll's landing) and store::roll::digital (a roll prepared as digital) do, a paper picked before kept; a negative at rest stays on ONI's print until its roll is prepared. A mode change moves the paper as its other rests. Format 41 follows the stock split's 40, so a format 40 file prints on ONI's print too. The newer-file corpus moved to version-42. Check: migrate::paper (an older digital photo and a negative on another paper both off, nothing else moved; twin a format 41 file keeps its paper).

title: The paper against spektrafilm's C on the ColorChecker chain, P1073076 and roll #8; its cost on a full-screen region
detail: colour_trace prints the chart chain (24 patches, P1073076's eleven, a grey ramp) on the virtual Portra 800 through the CPU references, rest:1.0 on the paper or :oni on ONI's print; docs/research/colour-diagnosis/paper_de.py weighs each against spektrafilm's Portra 800 + Portra Endura at the print exposure that prints a grey as ONI's print does, with and without spektrafilm's output gamut compression; film_compare renders P1073076 (the owner's settings) and roll #8 (DSC_6438, 6444, 6452, 6456, the test copy) on the paper and on ONI's print, photo_de weighing the photo's patches against the shipped LUT; cost.rs times the paper on 3456 x 2234.
outcome: Chart chain (chart / P1073076's patches / greys, dE2000 to spektrafilm's full chain C): ONI's print 7.81 / 13.14 / 10.09, the paper 0.71 / 1.42 / 1.25 (max 2.5 on the chart); to C without its output gamut compression (a display choice, its chroma knee from the centre and its lightness roll-off from 0.7 of white) 0.30 / 1.49 / 0.33. With no unmix the paper reads the colorimetric scan's densities as dye amounts: 5.41 / 5.41 / 4.96, so the separation's exact amounts carry most of the gain. Against spektrafilm's own exposure (print exposure 1) every chain sits 9 to 14 away: the paper rests where ONI's print puts a grey, not at spektrafilm's mid-grey normalisation. Other papers against C on Portra Endura: Supra 1.77, Crystal Archive 3.05, Endura Premier 5.07, Ultra Endura 7.75 on the chart (their own looks). P1073076 with the owner's settings, eleven patches against the shipped LUT: 14.16 on ONI's print, 1.90 on the paper (cheek 13.2 to 2.6, grass 22.3 to 2.3, trees 22.8 to 1.5, sky 2.7 to 1.8, wing white 0.8 to 1.2). Roll #8 (DSC_6438, 6444, 6452, 6456, Fujifilm C200's dyes, the Scanner face's ONI machine): first rendered with the machine's look cube and look exposure laid over the paper, two stops dark, which led to the machine printing on the paper at its rest with no cube (#2905); then a print's look: deeper blacks, the paper's white at 0.81 of linear, Endura's orange-red and olive greens, the grey balanced at one point. Cost on 3456 x 2234 (release, M2 Max): the paper laid with stage 4-7, 10.3 ms against 2.8 ms for ONI's print alone, past the dye separation's 14.4 ms pass the cache keeps on a print notch.
