title: The dye separation's bare-film check reads zero to a float's round trip, not to the bit
detail: kernel::dye_separation's narrow set read its bare film back through exp2 and ln, 2e-8 off zero, so the check held to the bit failed on the merged tree; it holds 1e-6 now, its twin a density of 0.1 above the bare film holding a dye.

title: A colour paper prints at a fixed rest per frame, the frame's black, grey and white laid through ONI's window on its print; Lighting's sliders on ONI's print curve inside it
detail: oni_pipeline::paper::printing solves the enlarger's exposure and neutral magenta and yellow filtration on the reference grey as before, then freezes them: Exposure and Contrast no longer move the enlarger nor the paper, whose contrast and pivot leave the kernel (its slope its own, 4^0). paper::anchors reads the frame's three anchors as the paper does, dye amounts above the bare film through the separation where one runs: each Prepare window's black (the dark pick), its white, and the reference grey; paper::anchored prints them at that rest, at Lighting's rest filtration, and lays the window on the print's linear light: per channel the printed black on 0, the white on 1, a gamma putting the grey on a plain RAW's grey (GREY_PRINT, 0.398), neutral by construction (gammas 1.25 to 1.31 on Portra Endura); a black and white print one window on its luma. Linear light, not the display code: the window is a scale of the paper's light, its black's offset felt in the deep shadows alone (their density slope at 0.02 of light 1.75 against 2.5 on the code). The kernel paper (WGSL beside its reference) lays the window after the print's dyes. Stage 4-7 reads the windowed print on the display gamma as before, Lighting's points moving the print's ends, and runs ONI's print curve from its mode's rest: Exposure is printed() at the exposure less the mode's rest (1.5 on a negative and a digital photo), brightness with its ends held; Contrast the S about 0.18 of light, its ends held; Shadows and Highlights its zones; each channel's contrast and mids; the colour density after. At rest the curve is the identity, so the paper at rest renders the windowed paper. Temperature and Tint stay the enlarger's filtration, 30.1 CC a stop, the least filter at none, the windowed grey's luma held, inside the window laid at the rest filtration. Hunt, follow and chroma decompression stay off; the Scanner face's keys move the gains the paper reads. No sidecar field changes, so no format: a format 41 photo on a paper renders anew on purpose, every older one being on ONI's print (migrate::paper). Checks (oni-pipeline tests/paper.rs): the anchors print black, white and the plain RAW grey on every channel on a digital photo, a negative, black and white and no unmix (twin the paper without its window, its white 0.80 to 0.81, its black 0.003 to 0.017); Exposure a stop either way holds the black at 0 and the white at 1 while the grey goes from 0.398 to 0.570 and 0.249 (twin the enlarger's stop lifting the black); Contrast 0.3 either way holds the ends, a darker tone moving with it (twin a straight slope about the grey pushing the white past 1.1); at rest the print is the windowed paper within 1.8e-7 (twin ONI's rest curve stacked); Temperature at half its track warms the grey to 0.53, 0.36, 0.19 through the enlarger, its luma held, the whites within 0.027 of white and the blacks within 0.0035 of black (twin the window laid again on the moved filtration, the grey neutral); the GPU within 1.7e-6 of its reference on a digital photo, a lit negative, black and white on Supra and no unmix on Crystal Archive (twin 5e-2 off), the paper's pass alone within 4.3e-7 (twin a steeper window); the kernel's window and curve unit checks.

title: Lighting's help says what its sliders do on a paper
detail: color_tab.slint: Black point and White point move the scan's ends, on paper the print's; on paper the enlarger rests where the scan's grey prints neutral, the paper's black and white laid on pure black and pure white, the sliders acting on that print as on ONI's, Temperature and Tint on the enlarger's filters, 30 CC a stop. French and Spanish.

title: The anchored paper against spektrafilm's C on the chart chain, roll #8 and P1073076; a Lighting notch's cost on a full-screen region
detail: colour_trace and paper_de.py as in #2903 on the same chart, photo patches and grey ramp; film_compare renders the paper, ONI's print and now the paper on the Pro face a stop under, as it is and a stop over (B-paper-under, B-paper-pro, B-paper-over); cost.rs also times a Lighting notch's paper arguments on the CPU.
outcome: Chart chain (chart / P1073076's patches / greys, dE2000 to spektrafilm's C): the paper before its window 0.71 / 1.42 / 1.25, the anchored paper 4.56 / 5.23 / 5.31 (max 6.7 on the chart), no unmix 6.27 / 7.07 / 6.72, ONI's print 7.81 / 13.6 / 10.09. The ends move as intended (C keeps the paper's white at L* 87, the window lays it at 100; the deepest grey L* 8.5 to 1.0), and the window's gamma (1.25 to 1.31 in linear light, the paper's grey sitting at 0.49 of its white once that white is laid on 1) steepens the mid-tones by about 0.3 in density and saturates the colours (the chart's orange b* 65 to 85). Measured, not shipped: resting the enlarger so the windowed grey lands on a plain RAW's grey with a gamma of 1 (the paper's own slope kept) gives 3.21 / 2.81 / 4.27 and lighter shadows (grey at -3 stops L* 11.2 against 5.7). Roll #8 (DSC_6438, 6444, 6452, 6456) and P1073076: the blacks black and the whites white on every frame; Exposure a stop either way moves the mid-tones, the ends held. Cost on 3456 x 2234 (app profile, M2 Max, mains): the paper laid with stage 4-7 7.45 ms before and 7.50 ms after; a notch's arguments on the CPU 0.043 to 0.048 ms before, 0.046 ms after.

title: The paper's enlarger rests where its window lays the grey on a plain RAW's: the paper keeps its own slope, the window black and white alone
detail: Owner's pick after #2952. #2950 solved the grey on the bare print, whose white is 0.81, so the window laid that white on 1 and lifted the grey to 0.49, and a gamma of 1.25 to 1.31 pulled it back, steepening every tone and saturating colour. Fixed at the source: paper::printing runs one Newton over the enlarger's exposure, magenta and yellow (cyan at none) on each channel's miss ln((grey - black) / (white - black)) - ln GREY_PRINT, the three anchors printed at each step, so the windowed grey is neutral and on a plain RAW's grey by construction; a black and white print sets the exposure alone on its luma, through no filter. The window's gamma is gone from Paper, its rows, the WGSL and the scalar reference: the window lays the printed black on 0 and the white on 1, a straight line in the print's light. Lighting's filters keep the windowed grey's luma held. The rest sits about 0.18 stop over #2950's (0.26 in black and white), its filtration within 0.4 CC (digital 66.15 M / 65.64 Y). Checks (tests/paper.rs): the windowed grey on GREY_PRINT on every channel within 3.3e-7 on a digital photo, a negative, black and white and no unmix (twin the enlarger set on the bare print, the windowed grey at 0.48 to 0.49); Temperature at half its track, the whites within 0.034 of white and the blacks within 0.0075 (twin the same warmth as a gain on the print's channels, red's white at 1.41); the kernel's window check without its gamma; the GPU within 1.4e-6 of its reference, the paper's pass alone 4.9e-7 (twin a wider window).
outcome: Chart chain against spektrafilm's C (chart / P1073076's patches / greys): 3.18 (max 6.3) / 2.74 / 4.20, against 4.56 / 5.23 / 5.31 for #2950 and 0.71 / 1.42 / 1.25 for the paper before its window; no unmix 5.69 / 5.49 / 6.25. The grey at -3 stops L* 11.1 (C 15.8, #2950 5.7), the chart's orange b* 77 (C 65, #2950 85), the white L* 99.8 (C 87, laid on white on purpose). Roll #8 (DSC_6438, 6444, 6452, 6456) and P1073076 re-rendered on the paper and ONI's print, and a stop either way on the paper: blacks black and whites white throughout, the shadows lighter than #2950's.

title: On a paper Temperature and Tint tone ONI's print curve as on ONI's print, the enlarger at its rest; Hunt follows Exposure and the zones, never Contrast
detail: Owner's call after #2953, whose enlarger move drifted the whites 0.034 and the blacks 0.0075 off at half Temperature. paper::printing no longer moves the filtration: the enlarger's exposure and neutral magenta and yellow stay where the solve sets them whatever Lighting says, so the Enlarger filtration line shows the rest filtration; CC_PER_STOP and the luma-held exposure solve are gone. conversion::printed_on keeps the frame's own_stops (Print::filters) and Hunt: Temperature and Tint act inside the window as on ONI's print, each channel's filter on the print curve and the luma held by the own_stops branch of printed3, so black stays black and white white. Stage47 gains hunt_contrast, the share of Contrast Hunt reads (row 11, lane 2 in WGSL beside its scalar reference): 1 on ONI's print, whose output is unchanged to the bit, 0 on a paper, so Exposure and Shadows/Highlights lower the colour density as on ONI's print while Contrast leaves it; black and white carries no Hunt; follow and the decompression stay off. Auto White Balance reads the paper's own print (the frame rendered through stage 4-7 with Lighting at rest but its filters, the paper kept), Newton on Temperature and Tint now toning the same curve as on ONI's print. No stored field changes, so no format: photos before format 41 are on ONI's print. Lighting's help on paper says Temperature and Tint act on that print, the enlarger's filtration left at its rest (French, Spanish). Checks, in oni-pipeline tests/paper_lighting.rs (the paper's frames now shared with tests/paper.rs in tests/paper/frames.rs, so neither file passes 400 lines): temperature_and_tint_tone_the_print_as_on_onis_and_the_ends_stay_black_and_white (Temperature and Tint at half and full travel either way: ends exact on the paper, ONI's print within 8e-5; grey toned the filters' way, luma within 1e-5; twin the former 30.1 CC move, ends off by 0.034 / 0.0075 at half Temperature, 0.12 at its end), the_enlarger_stays_at_its_rest_filtration_whatever_temperature_and_tint_say (twin the CC move 15 to 60 CC away), exposure_and_the_zones_lower_the_colour_density_on_the_paper_as_on_onis_print (Exposure +1: log colour density -0.120 on the paper, -0.117 on ONI's print; Shadows and Highlights +0.2 lower it; twin Hunt off), contrast_leaves_the_colour_density_on_the_paper (twin Hunt reading the contrast, 0.047 / -0.059), onis_print_is_unchanged_to_the_bit (FNV of ONI's print over ten settings, equal to the fold before the change; twin hunt_contrast 0); branches.rs Hunt blind to Contrast on the GPU (3.1e-6); the paper GPU check within 1.55e-6 on the lit negative (twin 5.6e-2); oni-measure filter_balance on_a_paper_the_key_balances_the_papers_own_print (means within 8.6e-5; twin ONI's print's filters part them by 0.10); the window check help_demo_color reads the new help.

title: The paper's Temperature, Tint and Exposure before and after #2970 on roll #8 and P1073076
detail: film_compare adds Temperature half its track either way on the paper (B-paper-cool, B-paper-warm). DSC_6438, DSC_6452 (test copy) and P1073076 rendered before and after #2970.
outcome: ONI's print identical to the bit on the three files; the paper at rest identical where Lighting rests (DSC_6452, P1073076), DSC_6438 (Exposure 2.01) 0.03 at most from Hunt. Temperature half either way: the darkest 1 % before up to 0.0046 off black in one channel, after 0.001 at most; highlights tinted far less, the warmth reading weaker than the enlarger's at the same travel. Exposure +1: colour density lowered by Hunt, up to 0.09 in a channel.

title: On a paper Lighting's Black point and White point hold the colour they stretch as on ONI's print, on a measured roll and on none
detail: Owner's report after #2970: the paper had lost ONI's hold on the points. On ONI's print the points narrow each channel's density window by its reach (1 - black - white), and the chroma decompression holds the colour against that stretch, the luma kept: on a measured roll its weight is the colour factor, which reads each channel's reach, so a global point leaves the colour at the window unchanged (factor x0.95 a point of 0.05); on no roll (a digital photo, a negative off its roll) the factor is 1 and the weights the dose, 0.5 of the colour stretched with the window and 0.5 the film's own held in density. Hunt does not read the points; the points' saturation curve (finishing) is shared by both prints. On the paper printed_on set the windows plain (decompression 1, film 0), every channel stretched by 1 / reach. Fixed at the source: conversion::paper_hold gives the paper's display window ONI's weights relative to the points at rest, so the paper at rest prints as before to the bit: on a roll the colour factor's ratio to its value at rest, the film's share none; on no roll the windows' share dose / (dose + film share x the windows' mean density span), the film's the rest; none while the points rest. printed_on lays them on the paper's own window (balance 0 to 1 on the display code); the kernel is unchanged, its decompression already on the paper's path in WGSL and the scalar reference. colour_factor reads the reach through factor_reaching, ONI's print unchanged to the bit. Contrast stays uncompensated. No stored field changes, so no format. Checks (oni-pipeline tests/paper_points.rs): the_points_stretch_the_colour_on_the_paper_by_onis_ratio (Black point, White point, both at 0.05 and 0.15, red's white and blue's black, on a roll, off a roll and on a digital photo, three tints at five printed tones: the colour at the window changes by ONI's ratio within 0.014 where ONI's window leaves the patch off its black, a global move within 0.01, exact on the roll; twin the plain windows 0.030 off or more on every global move), the_ends_stay_black_and_white_under_the_points (black at 0, white at or past 1 and neutral on a global move, both ends equal to the plain windows'; twin the hold against ONI's density windows tints them), onis_print_under_the_points_is_unchanged_to_the_bit (FNV over the three frames and every move, equal to the fold before the change; twin the factor x0.95), the_gpu_holds_the_papers_colour_as_its_reference (lit negative on and off a roll, Exposure, Contrast, Shadows and four points moved: 1.13e-6 and 9.9e-7; twin the plain windows 6.5e-2 and 3.5e-2). The window check help_card reads Lighting's help as #2970 wrote it.

title: The paper's Black point and White point before and after #2975 on DSC_6452 and P1073076, against ONI's print; whether ONI's follow is live
detail: film_compare adds Black point and White point +0.05 on the paper and on ONI's print on the Pro face (B-paper-points, B-oni-pro, B-oni-points). DSC_6452 (test copy, on its roll) and P1073076 (digital, no roll) rendered before and after #2975. A throwaway probe rendered ONI's print with follow shipped (0) and skipped (1) at rest, Exposure +1, Contrast +0.3 and Highlights -0.5 on both files and the chart chain.
outcome: ONI's print and the paper at rest identical to the bit before and after. Points +0.05 (CIELAB C* over the frame at rest, whole frame / L* 20 to 80): DSC_6452 ONI's print x0.921 / x1.046, the paper before x0.964 / x1.106, after x0.873 / x0.998; P1073076 ONI's print x1.034 / x1.063, the paper before x1.084 / x1.097, after x1.020 / x1.032. Blacks black and whites white throughout. At the window the paper now moves as ONI's print; on the print the two still part, ONI's points acting before its print curve (1.5 stops), the paper's after its print: on the checks' patches by log chroma a Black point +0.05 raises ONI's colour x1.17 to x1.33 and the paper's x1.06 to x1.08 (plain windows x1.11), a White point lowers ONI's x0.92 to x0.95 and the paper's x0.95 to x0.97 (plain x1.00). Follow (Print::FOLLOW 0) is live: it only takes colour where the print curve is steeper than the identity (the base, Tone::NEUTRAL), keep = min(1 / slope ratio, 1); at rest and Exposure +1 the 1.5-stop curve is flatter everywhere, so nothing moves (0 to the bit on the three); Contrast +0.3 C* -19 % on the chart (worst patch dC* 35), -20 % on DSC_6452 and -21 % on P1073076 (max 0.18 and 0.08 in a channel); Highlights -0.5 only above display 0.75: -0.4 % on the chart, -0.3 % on DSC_6452 (max 0.09), nothing on P1073076. On CPU patches it also bites at Shadows -0.5 and at Exposure below -1.5 stops.

title: A stronger Exposure on the print: the odds gain at k times the slider's stops, against the same gain on the display code, on roll #8 and P1073076
detail: Today's Exposure is an odds gain on the print's linear light, v' = g v / (1 + (g - 1) v), g = 2^stops, black and white held: analytic, monotone and C-infinity for any g. A prototype rendered strips at -2 to +2 slider stops through the app's engine, Hunt reading each curve, on ONI's print for DSC_6438, DSC_6452 (test copy) and P1073076 and on the paper for DSC_6452: the gain at k = 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5 times the slider's stops, and the same gain on the display code at k = 2.25, where the grey moves a stop at +1. A tapered pure-gain zone was dropped at the owner's call for one analytic curve.
outcome: The grey (0.398) at -4/-2/-1/+1/+2/+4: k = 1 -3.33/-1.49/-0.68/+0.52/+0.87/+1.20; k = 2 -7.27/-3.33/-1.49/+0.87/+1.20/+1.32; k = 2.5 -9.27/-4.30/-1.93/+0.99/+1.26/+1.33; the grey cannot pass +1.33 (white). The gear k is today's curve with its slider geared: k = 2 at +1 renders to the bit as k = 1 at +2. On the display code the push lands in the shadows (+3.7 stops at 0.01 of light for +1, the frames black at -2): refused. The owner chose k = 2, the track kept at -4 to +4 (#2981).

title: Exposure takes its distance from the rest twice on the print's curve; sidecar format 42 halves every earlier document's distance, its render kept
detail: Print::EXPOSURE_GEAR (2): the curve's stops are rest + 2 (Exposure - rest) on ONI's print and 2 (Exposure - rest) on a paper, Print::on_curve laying them, the Hunt base's alike, in conversion::stage47 and in the Pro face's curve drawing; the kernel and its WGSL twin unchanged. Values that meant the curve's own stops follow: the Scanner face's entry exposure (Print::exposure_at, the look's curve still at none), Auto White Balance's unlit press (its curve at none), the Lighting demo's move halved. migrate::exposure (format 42) writes rest + (exposure - rest) / 2 on the frame's Exposure and its Hunt base on every older sidecar, preset, paste and share code; the newer-file corpus moves to version 43; the goldens' exposures follow.
outcome: exposure_gear: the grey moves -7.272/-3.326/-1.489/+0.866/+1.199/+1.321 stops at -4/-2/-1/+1/+2/+4 (twin: the ungeared curve, the k = 1 table); every mode at rest reaches the kernel to the bit (twin: a hundredth's notch reaches it twice); an older document on ONI's print, on the paper and in black and white renders within 5.3e-6 of its former kernel arguments (twin: unmigrated, 0.22 to 0.45 apart). GPU against the CPU reference at Exposure +2 3.1e-6 and -2 1.1e-5 (twins 6.2e-3, 4.4e-2). ONI's print hash on the paper's settings unchanged, its exposures halved. scripts/check green but the two exFAT false failures (swift_checks presets, sweep_pass).

title: The help card's window check reads Lighting's help as #2970 wrote it
detail: help_card's LIGHTING constant still held the paper's former Temperature and Tint sentence; it now matches color_tab.slint and help_demo_color.
outcome: window help_card passes.

title: Contrast's colour is a saturation curve the Saturation Curve's plot shows, on ONI's print and on a paper; follow is gone
detail: The owner read the Print readout's dashed mirror (the RGB curve's exact inverse, a drawing only) as an inverse saturation curve answering Contrast; the render held Contrast's colour by follow instead, inside stage 4-7 and shown nowhere. finishing::contrast_curve (oni-pipeline) is now that curve: at the five resting tones of a saturation curve, the window value the RGB curve prints there (the curve read backwards by bisection, as the mirror draws it), then the slope on logarithmic light of the RGB curve without Contrast over the slope with it (read 1 % either side), y = half that, held to the plot; 0.5 at the black, none at Contrast's rest, on black and white or a bypassed print. finishing::print_saturation (the points' curve, then Contrast's) is the one definition the render's finishing pass composes (Pipeline::finishing, look_lab::pro_code) and the Saturation Curve's plot draws as a dashed guide under the hand's curve (editors::saturation::laid, each pass scaling the colour by twice its value); the Saturation Curve's help says what the dashed line is (French and Spanish). It acts on the paper too, since the interface shows the print's curves there (print_stops: the paper's own Exposure distance from its rest). Removed at the source: Stage47.follow, base_stops, base_contrast and base_zones (CPU kernel and WGSL, the uniform block now 13 rows), Print::FOLLOW, CONTRAST_STEP, Print::hunt_base (huntBase, which only fed follow: ignored on read, no longer written; no format bump, no stored value changes meaning), Print::output's bent flag and Print::rendered's follow; the Lighting fit no longer sets the base. Older photos with Contrast moved change chroma on purpose (owner's call): no migration.
outcome: Checks: tests/contrast_saturation.rs renders flat patches through the whole pipeline at Contrast -0.3 and +0.3 on ONI's print and on Portra Endura: within 1.7e-6 of stage 4-7's reference with the shown curve laid from the plot's own spline (twin, the curve not applied: 3.8e-2 to 8.0e-2), and at rest within 1.8e-6 with no curve; Contrast's curve on the GPU within 4.7e-7 of its reference (twin, not applied: 0.29 and 0.55); +0.3 lowers the mids, -0.3 raises them, the black at 0.5, none on black and white or bypassed (twins). editors::saturation: the dashed guide is drawn from print_saturation exactly (twin: the curve's departure doubled; Contrast at rest draws none). paper_lighting's bit check now folds ONI's print with Contrast at rest: 0x96406606c56de2e5 before, 0x33746d46e618f2e6 after; follow ran its identity arithmetic at a keep of 1 on every colour frame, so removing it moves ONI's print at rest by at most 6.6e-7 of linear light on DSC_6452 and 4.8e-7 on P1073076; the paper at rest is identical to the bit. paper_points' bit check on ONI's print under the points, which follow also touched, is pinned again (0x9a8bd567adf2dadb to 0x3986934315153ddd). kernel_oracle, branches, roll8 and balance_kept drop follow and the base.

title: Contrast -0.3 and +0.3 before and after #2990 on DSC_6452 and P1073076, on ONI's print and on the paper
detail: A scratch probe rendered both photos on the Pro face (DSC_6452 from the test copy, P1073076 with the owner's settings), on ONI's print and on Portra Endura, at Contrast -0.3, 0 and +0.3, with follow (before) and with Contrast's saturation curve (after); JPEGs side by side, before left.
outcome: Saturation (CIELAB C*/L*, median of each pixel's ratio to the frame at rest, L* 20 to 80): DSC_6452 ONI's print -0.3 x0.616 before, x0.935 after; +0.3 x1.295, x1.105; paper -0.3 x0.692, x1.003; +0.3 x1.417, x1.025. P1073076 ONI's print -0.3 x0.687, x1.007; +0.3 x1.155, x0.897; paper -0.3 x0.706, x1.027; +0.3 x1.347, x0.973. Before, Contrast softened the colour by a third and hardened it up to 40 % (follow only took colour, and little); after, it keeps each tone's saturation within 3 % on the paper and 11 % on ONI's print, where Hunt still reads Contrast. In C* alone, which falls with the lightness Contrast takes from the shadows, +0.3 now reads x0.78 to x0.86 of rest over the frame.

title: On a paper Contrast's saturation curve gives back half the colour its slope takes; ONI's print keeps it whole
detail: finishing::PAPER_CONTRAST_HOLD = 0.5 (owner's call): contrast_curve lays on a paper the hold's ratio raised to that share (contrast_curve_held), so a paper's Contrast keeps some of a grade's bite; the Saturation Curve plot draws the same curve. Check: contrast_saturation::a_paper_gives_back_half_of_contrasts_colour (each point the whole hold's square root on a paper, twin the whole hold; ONI's print whole). swift_checks' bare density axis takes the curve at none under the Exposure gear (Print::exposure_at(0, rest)), as it did before #2980.

title: Lighting's Colour compensation, a per-photo switch on both faces: off, the print lays no colour in answer to Lighting's tones; sidecar format 43
detail: Owner's request: a button that turns the Hunt effects off whole, scoped with him to every colour compensation Lighting's sliders carry. Print.colour_compensation (key colourCompensation, written only when off; read on from every older document), on Lighting so a paste, Apply Settings to Roll and Lighting's preset row (levelsGlobal) carry it, and a Lighting reset puts it back on. Off, cut at each source: Hunt (conversion::unprinted lays hunt 0, on ONI's print and on the paper; Print::rendered skips hunt_factor), the points' saturation curve (finishing::points_curve none) and Contrast's (finishing::contrast_curve_held none), so finishing::print_saturation lays nothing and the Saturation Curve's dashed guide, drawn from it, goes; the points' colour hold: on a paper paper_hold gives the plain windows (1, 0), on ONI's print on a measured roll factor_reaching reads every channel's reach as 1, so the decompression keeps the roll's own colour factor (own spans over the roll's) and drops only the points' share, and on no roll the film's share is divided by the points' reach (decompression::points_reach, the geometric mean of 1 - black - white over the channels), so the points stretch the film's share of the colour as they stretch the windows'. Left on: the roll's colour factor, the roll-less dose and the film's share at rest, the vignette's Hunt (Effects, not Lighting), Temperature and Tint's luma hold, the colour density slider. The Scanner face's ONI machine carries the switch into its print (scanner::on_oni_machine). Interface: a design system Toggle, Colour compensation, with its own help mark (HelpMark) saying what it holds, at Lighting's end on Pro and under the keys on the Scanner, beside the paper's (PaperRows became PrintRows), hidden in black and white; the Saturation Curve's help says its dashed line goes with it (French, Spanish). Lighting's help card stays as it was: a fifth paragraph took it past a 680-point window. Format 43 (chain::COLOUR_COMPENSATION_VERSION): no step; a build of 42 refuses a document of 43 as newer; the newer-file corpus moves to version 44. film_compare renders both prints at rest, Exposure +1 and Contrast +0.3 with the switch on and off.
outcome: Checks, oni-pipeline tests/colour_compensation.rs on a measured roll, off a roll and a digital photo, on ONI's print and on the paper, under Exposure ±1, Highlights and Shadows ±0.5, Contrast ±0.3, Black and White point +0.05: off, no Hunt, no print saturation, the paper's windows plain (twin: on, Hunt reads every move and Contrast and the points lay curves); a neutral's luma within 3.7e-4 of the switch on, a tinted patch's median within 4.8e-3 (worst 0.17 on ONI's print at Exposure +1, Hunt's colour density keeping the luma as a power mean only; twin: the move itself shifts the luma 0.11 to 4.4); each slider's colour parts from the compensated one the way the cut says (Hunt's lower density gone, Contrast's and the points' holds gone); off, the roll's colour factor (0.849 at rest) and the roll-less film share (0.5, divided by the points' reach under Black point +0.05) still act (twin: cutting the whole decompression moves the frame 1.1e-2 to 3.1e-2); the GPU kernel within 2.4e-6 of its reference off (twins, the switch on, 9.9e-2 to 2.7e-1); the whole render off lays no saturation curve, within 8.3e-7 (twin 2.9e-2 to 9.0e-2); on, every render of these settings folds to 0xe179bedf98cd0226, the fold computed on canvas's code (twin: off moves it). oni-settings tests/colour_compensation.rs: written only off and read back, every older format reads it on (twin: the key off reads off), a document of 43 is one past 42 and a reader refuses the version past its own (twin: today's reads). oni-core parameters: Lighting's row and a paste carry it, Colour's does not. Window colour_compensation: the switch shows in Lighting, off it renders again and the dashed guide goes, on it returns. The 38 corpus goldens read the field on; panel_frame's window grows to 1440 and film_effects' to 1860 for the switch's row.

title: Whether Lighting's sliders leave the colour's strength with the compensation off: measured on patches and on DSC_6452
detail: oni-pipeline tests/colour_compensation.rs prints each slider's colour (median over tinted patches of their log spread around their neutral, moved over rest) with the compensation on and off, on a measured roll, off a roll and a digital photo, on ONI's print and on the paper; film_compare rendered DSC_6452 (test copy, Portra 800, on its roll) at rest, Exposure +1 and Contrast +0.3 on both prints, on and off (CIELAB C*/L*, median of each pixel's ratio to its frame at rest, L* 20 to 80; JPEGs side by side, on left).
outcome: The expectation that the sliders leave the colour's strength alone with the compensation off does not hold: the compensation is mostly holds, so cutting it lets each channel's curve move the colour. Patches, colour over rest on ONI's print (on / off, on a roll): Exposure +1 x0.42 / x0.53, -1 x1.99 / x1.55; Highlights +0.5 x1.04 / x1.18; Shadows +0.5 x0.67 / x0.69; Contrast +0.3 x1.07 / x1.33, -0.3 x1.01 / x0.76; Black point +0.05 x1.05 / x1.15; on the paper Contrast +0.3 x1.08 / x1.21, Black point x0.99 / x1.08. DSC_6452 (C*/L*): ONI's print Exposure +1 x0.543 on, x0.676 off; Contrast +0.3 x1.039 on, x1.520 off; the paper Exposure +1 x0.553 / x0.680, Contrast +0.3 x1.150 / x1.398; mean L* moves alike on and off (+18.1 / +18.2, -5.9 / -6.0). At rest the paper is identical to the bit; ONI's print is x1.14 more colourful off, Hunt reading its curve's resting 1.5 stops.

title: A printer's rest on the paper, the base at maximum black, against the grey's rest: measured on roll #8 and P1073076, refused
detail: Owner's ask: rest the enlarger as a printer does, the minimum time for maximum black (the bare film, Prepare the Roll's dark pick, at the paper's Dmax on all three layers) and the magenta and yellow filtration that prints the reference grey neutral, its lightness where the paper's curve puts it; against #2900's rest, the time and filtration that print the grey at a plain RAW's grey (0.398), neutral, on the bare print. crates/oni-app/examples/paper_rests.rs solves both on each frame (Portra Endura, Lighting at rest) and prints the filtration, the time apart, and the base, the densest read (Prepare's white) and the grey as light, luma and each layer's density against its Dmax; the threshold is a share of each layer's density range on its least reached layer, 0.98 (every paper's curves there at about a tenth of their steepest slope, 0.966 against 0.976 log exposure on Portra Endura's red), weighed against 0.95 and 0.90. Renders through the app's engine on the Pro face: DSC_6438, 6444, 6452, 6456 (test copy) and P1073076, (a) left, (b) right.
outcome: The printer's rest fails the eye: it meets its definition (base at 0.992 / 0.980 / 1.000 of red, green, blue's range on roll #8, grey neutral) but takes 1.651 stops more light than the grey's rest on roll #8 (1.309 on P1073076) and prints the grey at 0.0227 (L* 16) on roll #8 and 0.046 on P1073076 against 0.398: three to four stops dark, the frames near black. Weaker thresholds: base at 0.95, +1.118 stops, grey 0.070 (roll #8) / +0.757, 0.141 (P1073076); at 0.90, +0.567, 0.194 / +0.198, 0.321. The grey's rest leaves the base at 0.883 / 0.825 / 0.965 of the range on roll #8 (layer densities 2.17 / 1.71 / 1.76 against Dmax 2.46 / 2.07 / 1.82, its light 0.0066 against the paper's Dmax 0.0032) and 0.900 / 0.877 / 0.949 on P1073076; the densest read prints at the paper's white (0.813) in both rests' reach. The negative's base-to-grey distance (0.72 of density on roll #8) is shorter than Portra Endura's shoulder-to-grey, so no time puts both the base at Dmax and the grey near middle grey. Stage stopped as the brief asked: the grey's rest ships (#3011), the printer's rest stays in the probe; the owner decides. All four roll #8 frames share their roll's windows, so their rests are equal.

title: Lighting on a paper in true density, the paper's own ends, no ONI window or colour compensation: the enlarger rests where the grey prints neutral
detail: Owner's decisions of 2026-11-22. ONI's window leaves the paper (Paper's window rows, paper::anchored and grey_shares gone): the print's ends are the paper's own white (0.813) and Dmax light (0.003) and move with the settings. Rest (#3010): paper::printing::resting solves the time, magenta and yellow (cyan at none) that print the reference grey at a plain RAW's grey on the bare print, neutral; black and white by the time alone on its luma. Lighting acts in density before the paper (paper::lighting): Exposure is the enlarger's time, a slider stop a stop of light (log10 2 of log exposure), from the mode's rest, ungeared: print_stops and the paper branch of curve_stops are gone, the paper takes s.print.exposure - resting_exposure itself and stage 4-7 runs no print curve on it (print_on 0, hunt 0); Temperature and Tint the enlarger's filtration, 30.1 CC a stop (paper::CC_PER_STOP) on the rest's, the least at none, the time then holding the grey's luma, the ends left where the paper prints them; Contrast the paper's grade, each layer's log exposure turned about the reference grey's at rest by 4^Contrast (paper::GRADE_BASE), each channel's contrast added to its own layer; Black point and White point read on each dye's range from the bare film (0) to the densest the windows read (1): a black point p reads the density p of the range as bare film, a white point the density 1 - p as the densest, the range stretched between (u' = (u - b) / (1 - b - w)); Shadows and Highlights lay one density along that range by its mean tone (ONI's quarter passes on u, ends held), as dodging and burning lay one light; each channel's mids its own bend on its u. Saturation stays after the print, on the paper's own light, as the colour density it is (a power of each channel's light, the luma held). No colour compensation on a paper: no Hunt, no points' or Contrast's saturation curve (PAPER_CONTRAST_HOLD, contrast_curve_held and paper_hold removed), so the Colour compensation switch has nothing to cut there. The kernel paper (WGSL beside its scalar reference) takes the tones, the grade and the print's ends in its rows; Stage47 loses hunt_contrast (always 1 on ONI's print) and its paper branch passes the paper's light as it is. Auto White Balance reads a paper at its enlarger's rest (filter_balance::unlit). Paper photos edited at formats 41 to 43 change look on purpose (no release carried them; owner's call): no migration of their render.
outcome: Checks (oni-pipeline tests/paper.rs, paper_lighting.rs, paper_points.rs; oni-render kernel/paper/tests.rs): the grey at 0.398 neutral within 2e-6 on a digital photo, a negative, black and white and no unmix, the base above the paper's Dmax and the densest read at most its white (twin unfiltered off neutral, twin ONI's window laying them on 0 and 1); stage 4-7 is the paper's print to the bit, the colour density alone following (twin ONI's curve stacked); Exposure ±1 and +2.5 move every layer's log exposure by exactly log10 2 a stop (within 9e-8), the base lifting above its rest brightening (0.0096 to 0.054 on the negative) and falling toward Dmax darkening, never past (twin the k = 2 gear, twin the window); Temperature and Tint at half and full travel move the filtration by 30.1 CC a stop within 1e-4, the grey's luma within 1e-5, the ends tinted with it (Temperature +1: the white's blue 0.800 to 0.739; twin the window re-anchoring them); Contrast ±0.3 a slope of 4^C about the grey within 1e-4 (twin the plain slope); no Hunt and no saturation curve on a paper for every move (twin ONI's print); the points' densities print and expose as the rest's ends to the bit, Shadows and Highlights lay 0.084 of the range at their peak against 0.009 at the other, one share on every dye (twin each channel by its own tone), mids and channel contrast per channel; ONI's print to the bit (paper_lighting fold 0x33746d46e618f2e6, paper_points 0x3986934315153ddd, colour_compensation's ONI-only fold 0xbfb6c50737ed0fec equal to canvas c8569f8e's); the GPU within 1.34e-6 of its reference on a lit negative with every slider, Brightness and True blacks, on black and white and with no unmix (twin 5.6e-2), the paper's pass alone within 1e-6. Updated with their reasons: paper.rs (window anchors and windowed rest gone), paper_lighting (Hunt, the gear and the ONI-curve toning gone), paper_points (the hold gone, the points in density), contrast_saturation (no curve on a paper), colour_compensation (ONI's print alone; on a paper nothing to cut), exposure_gear (a paper ungeared, its older renders change on purpose), branches (Hunt blind to Contrast gone).

title: A paper's Brightness and True blacks, per photo, on the print between the paper's own Dmax and white; sidecar format 44
detail: Print.brightness (key brightness, written when moved, track ±4) is an odds gain on the paper's print between its Dmax and its white, both held, at Print::EXPOSURE_GEAR times its stops as ONI's Exposure curve takes them: on a paper Exposure moves the enlarger and lifts the blacks with the grey, Brightness lightens the print with its ends kept. It is shown on a paper alone: on ONI's print Exposure is that curve already (Field::shown_in reads the settings, so Lighting's reset key reads it only there). Print.true_blacks (key trueBlacks, written when on, off by default) lays the paper's Dmax on pure black and keeps its white, each channel a straight line in light between them: black point compensation, a constant per paper; brightened by Exposure the blacks still lift above it. Both ride with Lighting (paste, Apply Settings to Roll, the levelsGlobal preset row) as printPaper does, and the Scanner face's machine carries True blacks. The kernel lays them last (Paper::ended). Format 44 (chain::PAPER_ENDS_VERSION): no step, older documents read Brightness 0 and True blacks off; the newer-file corpus moves to version-45, the goldens' Print gains both fields. Export (later): a Screen profile keeps True blacks off, a Print profile turns it on and lays the paper's white on the file's white, so the switch is already the print's own, per photo.
outcome: Checks: tests/paper_ends.rs, True blacks on every frame lays the Dmax on 0 and keeps the white within 1e-6, monotone and at or above black along the negative's range and past both ends, its largest step halving as the sampling doubles (3.07e-3 to 1.53e-3: continuous, C0 at the paper's nodes, the map itself linear), Exposure +1 still lifting the base (twin off, the Dmax at its own light; twin a jump of 0.01 keeping its step); Brightness -1, +0.5, +1 and +1 with True blacks hold both ends and move the grey exactly as the odds gain at twice the stops (0.398 to 0.159, 0.535, 0.645; twin ungeared). oni-settings tests/paper_ends.rs: written only when moved and read back, every older format reads them at rest (twin a document carrying them), a paste carries them, a document of 44 refused by a build of 43.

French and Spanish.

title: Every slider stands between a − and a + key, a press three of its value editor's steps: the Scanner face's step keys generalised in the design system
detail: Owner's call, the first step toward removing the Scanner face. ds/slider.slint: the StepKey keycaps, once a stepped slider's alone, stand at every Slider's rail ends, so every panel, editor, the export's Quality, De-dust's brush and sensitivity, Prepare the Roll's sliders and Crop's dial take them with no use site changed. A press nudges SliderStyle.press steps (DS.control-slider-press, 3) through the slider's own step callback, the one its value editor's mini − and + call with one step: three units of the readout's last shown digit on a continuous slider (slider_track::stepped and each family's own step), three steps on a stepped one (a Scanner letter: a point and a half). ⇧ no longer changes a key's press (the arrows keep ⇧ for three or ten); no repeat while held, as before; the keys leave Tab's path, as the value editor's. Each key's tooltip and accessible label names the slider, the way and the press: Slider.press-reads asks Rust (Readouts.pressed, slider_track::pressed: the readout's last figure, its places and unit, or the stepped slider's step-reads) and the default helps read "{} −: lower by {}" / "{} +: higher by {}" ("lower"/"higher" alone where the readout holds no number); the Scanner's keep their colour's way with the press ("D −: toward dark, by 1.5"); the D and C/M/Y help notes say a point and a half a press; LabSlider's ⇧ help removed. French and Spanish laid. Layout: the keys sit on the rail's row, so the name and the readout above keep their width; the rail is 68 points shorter in the 340-point panel at every window size. A level's handle on the Per-Channel Levels plot, five knobs on one rail with no value editor, is no Slider and takes no key.
outcome: slider_track a_keys_press_is_three_shown_units_and_its_tooltip_names_them (twin: one step names a third); window check slider_keys: every slider shown, blocks unfolded, keyed on its own row and the keys counted against the sliders (digital photo: Colour 25, Source 9, Details 6, Crop 1, De-dust 2; the Scanner face's Colour tab 17; a negative's Source tab 8; the export's Quality 1), a press of + and − moves Exposure, Tint, Vignette, Grain, Texture, Distortion, Angle, Brush size, Ceiling and Quality by three shown units and D by three half points, the value editor's + by one (twin), Exposure's press renders and one undo takes it back alone (twin: the next undo is the film type's), the tooltip's text is the catalogue's with French and Spanish (twin: a text outside it has none); twins: the level handles, keyless sliders, fail the count, and the interface before the change failed it on its first slider. Scanner, digital Scanner, tooltip, slider hues, slider rest, slider hand, dial, lens, film effects, channel points, auto dust and the welcome film's checks follow the keys and the rail between them (common::rail, common::slider_key); the Button's ⇧ flag, read by no key any more, removed.

title: The Frontier SP-3000 as a paper: its measured table refitted on the paper kernel's own sums
detail: Owner's decisions of 2026-11-21/22: the Frontier becomes one more print in the Paper list, taking the dye amounts every paper takes and Lighting in true density, no Hunt, no window, no resting offset. The table's x is the synthetic negatives' own density above base, without crosstalk, so the print reads the dye amounts as x at scale 1 (today's cube path stretches by 1.3 / green window and unmixes with the Swift generic rows at 0.6). Model: a 3 x 3 with rows summing to one (negative density to paper exposure), each layer's sensitometric curve a sum of three normal integrals, nine virtual print dyes each a density per layer, a base and a linear Rec. 2020 light. It runs in the existing paper kernel: three negative bands (one a layer, each dimmed by its own filter alone, so a CC is a hundredth of density on that layer) and nine print bands in place of wavelengths. Fitted by docs/research/frontier/frontier_print_fit.py (numpy, Levenberg-Marquardt, unclipped model against the table's clipped code so it keeps inside sRGB) to crates/oni-pipeline/resources/scanner/frontier_print.json. Note docs/research/frontier/frontier-paper.md.
outcome: Against frontier.cube's constrained nodes (1440, spread under 0.6): dE Oklab x100 median 1.04, p90 2.41, p99 4.46, max 7.08; mostly read (3584) 1.44 / 3.20; whole reach 2.41 / 7.30. The Look Lab model reads 1.19 / 2.99 on the same nodes; the curves linearised (twin) 33.4 / 51.8. The 63 renders' data is not on this machine: not measured against them (the cube reads them at 0.27). Least light of any density mix -1.6e-5, white 0.98. Variants left: two negative bands a layer, non-negative lights (1.28), a light-above-none penalty (1.21 to 1.39).

title: One face: the Scanner face, its machines, keypad and keypad screen leave; one edit per photo
detail: Owner's decisions of 2026-11-21/22. PipelineSettings loses face, scanner, scannerMachine and scannerFinish (as_scanner, storing_scanner_edit gone); oni-core loses Command::Face, Command::Finish and Command::Scan (Command::Walk keeps the phone's walk), EditorStore::scanner_face, face(), face_view(), the Took face flag of Edit Together, the face rows of presets and fields (Field::LegacyPrint in their place, carried with Lighting by paste, Apply Settings to Roll and the levelsGlobal row), parameters::reset_blank's face argument. The app loses its Lab controller (app/lab.rs, its sliders and tests), the bar's Pro/Scanner switch, the remembered face, Act::Emulator/FacePro/FaceScanner, the Scanner Emulator menu item and the keypad's hand; the walk keys move to keys.rs unchanged. The hand's Frontier look (frontier_table, app/frontier_look.rs, Settings' Frontier Look page, Act::Frontier*) goes with the Frontier machine it stood in for. The phone link stays compiling: the desktop publishes Pro's face with the keypad at rest; the phone's keypad, machine and face keys find no field and land nowhere (link::command_of returns None for them), its panel sliders, walk, undo and redo work as before; the phone panel's Scanner rows go. Pro's order stays, Colour then Lighting: the keypad's density-first was a minilab operator's order of keys, and on the one face Exposure sits right under Colour, the Auto White Balance key acting on Colour.

title: Sidecar format 46: a photo the Scanner face rendered keeps that edit, its machine's print in Lighting's fields and a legacy print; a Pro photo keeps Pro's whole
detail: migrate::one_face (chain::ONE_FACE_VERSION = 46, after FRONTIER_PRINT_VERSION) reads the retired keys off the stored settings (one_face::Scanner: Face, Clicks, Machine, Finish; a key of the wrong shape refuses the document as its typed read did), the < 22 path through reshape (keypad in steps, scannerFinish's retired curves folded) and every later one through the raw settings, last after every other step. A face of Scanner (a digital photo before format 30 reads Pro, the former digital_face step folded in) lays what on_oni_machine laid: the Scanner finishing in Pro's fields (contrast, curves, Colour Mixer, Saturation Curve, vignette, Chrome), Lighting at the machine's rest (Print default but Contrast, colour compensation and True blacks; Exposure the looks' entry exposure, or the paper's rest on a paper), Colour Density 0, Pro's Auto White Balance result dropped (balance_filters None, so a roll's strength never re-doses it), and PipelineSettings.legacy_print (key legacyPrint: machine, D, C, M, Y, TEMP steps, laid, written when present) unless the photo prints on a paper with every key at rest, where it lays nothing. A Pro photo drops the Scanner keys alone. Presets and share codes: a keypad row saved off the Scanner face becomes levelsGlobal, the filters, Colour Density and the finishing's rows; the face row goes. The keypad's clicks cannot become a slider: they move the gains, which are the roll's (Roll tab Filtration), so they stay in the legacy print, read-only on screen. The newer-file corpus moves to broken/version-47 (Refusal::Newer(47)); a build of 45 refuses 46 as newer. Corpus goldens rewritten: Pro frames lose the four keys and read legacy_print None, nothing else moving; the 11 Scanner frames read their machine's print and a legacy print.

title: The legacy print renders the former Scanner chain: its keys in the gains, the machine's look cube and TEMP's warmth, the Frontier's rest on the cube's path alone

Off (laid false) the photo prints as its sliders say. A measure in front of the print and the balance read no legacy print, as they read Pro's face; Compare's before leaves it out. Prewarm compiles a legacy print's looks on a negative and a digital photo.

title: Colour's filters shown as Temperature and Tint or as an enlarger's C, M and Y, a Settings choice
detail: Settings > Editor > Colour Filtration (preference filtrationCmy, Act::FiltrationCmy): Temperature and Tint, or C, M and Y. A display choice, so it sits with the app's other reading choices: a switch beside the sliders would be the only control of Colour that edits no photo. Knob::Filtration(channel) reads Print::filtration(): each filter's stops as CC (tone::CC_PER_STOP, 100 log10 2, the paper's own, now one constant for both), red's as C, the least at none, the neutral density ONI's held luma and the enlarger's time take back; a C, M or Y edit lands as Temperature and Tint moves (Print::filtration_moves: C − Y and (C + Y)/2 − M over 30.1), so both views write the same two values and switching moves nothing. Same meaning on ONI's print and on a paper (the filters' filtration over the rest); on a paper the enlarger's dial, rest included, stays on the note under the paper. Track 0 to 80 CC, a press 3 CC, readout whole CC. Not shown on the phone.

title: A paper's print holds the frame's pick: every Lighting slider leaves Prepare the Roll's black where the rest prints it, True blacks lays it on pure black, Brightness runs between it and the paper's white
detail: Owner's report and decisions of 2026-11-22: on a paper the slightest Lighting move lifted the blacks above the black picked in Prepare the Roll, and True blacks laid the paper's Dmax on black while the pick prints above it (at rest the base 0.0066 against Dmax 0.0032 on Portra Endura). The paper kernel now ends its print at the source, per channel: its light v read from the printed pick K to the paper's white W, u = (v - K) / (W - K), laid from the anchor A to W by Brightness's odds gain g u / (1 + (g - 1) u) at EXPOSURE_GEAR times its stops (straight past W), and under K by v A / K so the print never falls under no light; continuous and monotone. K is the print, at its colour density, of the pick (anchors[0]) without Lighting's points, zones and mids, so Black point and White point still move the ends while Exposure, Contrast, Temperature, Tint, the channel filters, contrast and mids, Shadows, Highlights, Saturation and Brightness leave the pick at A; W is the paper's own white as the current filtration shows it, so the whites stay free (crushing brightening, greying darkening). A is where the enlarger's rest prints the pick (the rest's time and filtration, untoned, ungraded), or 0 with True blacks. Brightness thus never moves that black nor the white. The colour density (Saturation) moves into the paper kernel before the ends (Paper::density; stage 4-7 runs at density 1 on a paper), so Saturation keeps the pick too; stage47::coloured is the one colour density both prints call. The filtration's time solve holds the grey's luma as the print shows it, ends included. Paper loses dmax and true_blacks and gains density, pick and anchor (CPU reference and WGSL, one more uniform row); paper::lighting::ended lays them. ONI's print unchanged to the bit. The Frontier paper takes the same ends. No stored field changes: no format bump; paper photos already edited change look on purpose (owner's call).
outcome: See #3091 for the checks, #3092 for the owner's roll.

title: The paper's ends: the pick held under every Lighting slider, True blacks on pure black, the whites free, Brightness between, the points still moving the ends
detail: oni-pipeline tests/paper_ends.rs on a negative, a digital photo, black and white and a negative on the Frontier: 22 Lighting moves (Exposure, Contrast, Temperature, Tint, a channel filter, Shadows, Highlights, channel contrast and mids, Saturation, Brightness, each either way, and two mixes) keep the printed pick at its rest per channel (twin: unanchored, the time, filters, grade and colour density lift or sink it); True blacks puts it at 0 at rest and under each (twin: the Dmax laid on black leaves it above); Exposure ±1 moves the densest read as the unanchored print does within a hundredth of the move (twin: a white anchored too); Brightness ±1 and with True blacks holds the pick and the paper's white, the grey on its odds curve (twin: the curve between the Dmax and the white); Black point ±0.05 crushes or lifts the pick, White point lightens the upper range with the pick held (twin: anchored through the points); the print continuous (largest step halving as the sampling doubles) and monotone from past the pick to past the white (twins a jump and a dip). paper_lighting: Exposure lifts the paper's base unanchored and the print holds it (Temperature: the grey's luma held as shown, the densest read tinted, the pick held). paper.rs: the colour density the paper's own; the GPU on a lit negative with its pick on its rest. oni-render kernel/paper/tests.rs: the ends and the colour density against their formulas.
outcome: The pick within 2.7e-8 of its rest under every move on every frame (unanchored it moves up to 6.1e-2, Exposure +1 on the negative; 15 of the 22 moves lift it on colour, 6 on black and white; the zones and mids none, as before); True blacks 0 (7e-10 on the Frontier; on the Dmax's black it printed up to 7.9e-3); the densest read under Exposure -1 0.064 down, 2.3e-4 off the unanchored move (Frontier 0.11, 3.6e-4); Brightness's grey within 3e-8 of its curve (twin 1.6e-4 to 4.2e-3 off); Black point +0.05 sinks the negative's pick 0.0110 to 0.0077, -0.05 lifts it to 0.0163; the print's largest step halves with the sampling, its largest fall 4.8e-7 (Frontier's fit 1.1e-5, its own), never under no light (the Frontier's fit -1.6e-5). ONI's print folds unchanged (paper_lighting, paper_points, colour_compensation). GPU within 1.62e-6 of its reference on the lit negative with True blacks, 1.10e-6 with its pick on its rest and Brightness -0.7, 1.07e-6 on the Frontier (twins 4.1e-2 to 0.22). scripts/check: 160 binaries, every failure confirmed outside the change: sweep_pass and swift_checks on the exFAT build disk (permissions and ._ files in CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR), instance timed out under the full run and passes alone; scripts/lint clean.

title: A wait on the GPU that runs out while another thread empties the queue is a timeout, never a panic of the render thread
detail: Under a full scripts/check the render thread died in wgpu-core 30.0.1 (device/resource.rs:948, 'If the queue is empty, the current submission index (393) should be at least the wait submission index (395)') and editor_routes timed out waiting for the canvas. Cause, upstream: Device::maintain reads the fence after a wait that ran out, then asks the life tracker whether the queue is empty; any other thread's poll or submit (every queue.submit maintains) can retire the waited submission between the two, so a stale fence meets an empty queue and the defensive assert fires. ONI's oni_graph::ran waits in 1 ms slices (#2251) while Slint's frames, the other render threads and the graph's own ended() poll the one device, which loads open that window. Fixed upstream by gfx-rs/wgpu#9958 (merged 2026-08-07, on trunk for wgpu 31, absent from 30.0.1 and 30.0.2); Slint pins wgpu 30, so vendor/wgpu-core is 30.0.1 with that change alone (the wait's outcome kept, an empty queue after a wait that ran out reported as WaitSucceeded or Timeout from the fence), [patch.crates-io] beside wgpu-hal, named in CLAUDE.md; the copy goes with wgpu 31. No ONI-side alternative removes the race: an unbounded wait holds the snatch lock a window's present needs for the GPU's whole time (#2251), and every submit of every thread maintains the device. crates/oni-graph/tests/polls.rs (new): one thread submits 8 copies of 32 MB and drains to an empty queue, five wait on its latest submission (one through oni_graph::ran, four in zero slices) for 2 s; no thread may panic and the waits must have run out by the thousand over 20 drains or more (twin: a race with no waiter is refused by that judge).
outcome: On wgpu-core 30.0.1 the race with zero slices panicked on all 8 runs (copies of 4 MB, 32 x 32 MB and 8 x 32 MB; the very assert, from submission 6 onward, within 0.5 s); oni_graph::ran alone, its 1 ms slices rarely ending in the microseconds the window lasts, passed 3 runs of 3 s on an idle Mac, as the app's render thread met it only under the full check's load. Vendored with #9958 the check passed 3 of 3 (about 1 200 submissions, 1.8 to 2.0 million waits run out).

title: A paper's Brightness is the enlarger's light as Exposure gives it, on the tones above a knee over the pick: the blacks and the first shadows hold
detail: Owner's request of 2026-11-22: Brightness was an odds gain on the print between the pick and the paper's white, which on a paper (pick held under Exposure too) looked like Exposure itself. It now moves each tone's log exposure as Exposure does (a slider stop a stop of the enlarger's light, ungeared, as a paper takes Exposure), by one shift on the three layers, as far as the tone's mean log exposure x lies under the pick's: nothing up to the knee k, then on the excess e past it (eased: e = y²/2k over the first knee's worth, y − k/2 after, so the slope stays continuous) a gain falling from PAPER_KNEE_SLOPE (4) to one, e → 3e − 9e²/4·lift, reaching the whole lift from 2·lift/3 of excess on; darkening is that curve's inverse in closed form, 2e / (4 + √(16 − 9e/fall)), the whole fall from 5·fall/3 on. Every slope lies within ¼ and 4 at any slider value (no tone passes another; a layer moving up to a quarter slower than its tone's mean never turns back, roll #8's neutrals differ by a twentieth), the map rises with the slider at every tone, C1 throughout. The knee (paper::lighting::BRIGHTNESS_KNEE_LIGHT) is where the frame's neutral from the pick to its reference grey prints L* 5 above the pick on its own range (the pick on black, the paper's white), solved per frame by bisection in lighting::ended under the frame's own Lighting, so it follows Exposure, the grade and the filtration and ignores the anchor (pure black or Paper blacks); Paper gains pick_log and knee (the pivot and slope rows' w), kernel::paper::kneed and excess beside the WGSL's, Paper::brightened between the exposure and the grade. Paper::ended loses the odds gain: a straight line in light from the printed pick on its anchor to the paper's white. The pick, its anchor, the paper's white and every tone under the knee print to the bit as without Brightness. ONI's own print has no Brightness (Field::shown_in shows it on a paper alone), unchanged. Lighting's help on paper says Brightness is Exposure sparing that black and the first shadows (French, Spanish; as long as the sentence it replaces, so the help card still fits a 680-point window). No stored field changes, no format bump: photos with Brightness ≠ 0 on a paper move, as asked; of the owner's 1834 sidecars on the T7 two carry it, one on a paper (Portra Endura, +2.17, then True blacks, now pure black), the other on ONI's print where it does nothing.
outcome: See #3131 for the checks, #3132 for the measures and the knee's choice.

title: Brightness's knee: the shadows under it held to the bit, the tones past it as Exposure prints them, every slope within ¼ and 4, the GPU on its reference

title: Brightness's shape and knee measured on roll #8 on Portra Endura: three candidates against Exposure, the knee at L* 5
detail: crates/oni-app/examples/brightness_knee.rs prints, per photo laid on its paper (Portra Endura where it has none), its pixels' L* at rest on the print's own range, the neutral ramp, three candidate shapes against Exposure at ±0.5 and ±1 on a neutral ramp (−3/−2/−1/0/+2 scene stops for a negative of gamma 0.6) and a ColorChecker laid on the negative, the toe's moves by L*, and with RENDERS the frames at Brightness and Exposure ±1. Candidates: A a gain on the print's light above a knee (u = τ + m, τ + g·m), B today's odds gain faded in by a smoothstep on u, C Exposure's shift of the log exposure above a knee (chosen); A and B calibrated to Exposure's grey.
outcome: A blows the highlights past the paper's white (L* 104 to 135 at +0.5/+1) and flattens the chart (C* 10 to 55 against Exposure's 18 to 41); B reverses at every darkening (largest fall 4e-6 to 6e-5) and needs gains of 0.1 to 9; C prints the grey within 0.6 L* of Exposure at ±0.5 and +1 on DSC_6438 and DSC_6440 (−1: 44.3 for 44.8, 38.2 for 35.9), never falls, the neutral's chroma drift at most Exposure's. Mean shift against each layer on its own: the mean keeps neutrals closer at ±4 (C* drift 3.0 and 3.3 against 4.9 and 4.3 on DSC_6438, 1.7 and 1.9 against 3.0 and 3.2 on DSC_6452), alike at ±1. Knee: on well-exposed frames 8 to 17 % of pixels lie under L* 5 above the pick (DSC_6438 7.7 %, 6435 12.4, 6442 12.2, 6464 13.7, 6466 14.4, 6440 17.1), the dark ones up to 65 %; a smoothstep from the pick moved L* 5 by 19 to 21 at +1 whatever its width (10 to 25), so the knee is a dead zone: at L* 5 nothing moves; at +1 L* 8 moves 0.8 to 1.3 and L* 12 4 to 7 (Exposure +27, +30), at −1 L* 12 1 to 1.7 (Exposure −10). It lies 0.13 to 0.36 of log exposure under the pick (−3.4 to −2.2 scene stops from the grey). The fade's slope bound caps darkening: past −1 the grey darkens less than Exposure (−4: L* 28 on DSC_6438 against Exposure's 6.5) as the mids fold onto the knee; brightening reaches the paper's white. Before and after renders of DSC_6452 and DSC_6440 kept in the scratch folder, never committed (roll #8).

title: Brightness's knee on the reversal paper: a slide's mids and highlights take more light as its Exposure gives them, its densest film and first shadows held
detail: On Kodak Ektachrome Radiance III more light prints lighter and the pick is the densest film, the least exposed. Paper::toward_light reads a tone's mean log exposure from the pick's toward a lighter print, under it on a negative paper and over it on a reversal one; the knee (lighting::ended, the neutral from the densest film to the reference grey printing L* 5 over the pick) and Paper::brightened read it so, and brightened lays its move with that sense, more light brightening on a reversal paper (the WGSL reads the reversal flag already in points_white_reversal.w). Merged with integrate: True blacks retired for Paper blacks (pure black by default), the checks' anchors follow; Brightness's sentence stays in Lighting's help, after paper-ui's Paper section.
outcome: oni-render kernel/paper/tests.rs: on a reversal paper Brightness +1 gives each layer log10 2 more exposure past the knee, holds tones within the knee over the pick and on its dark side, darkening takes light away (twin: read as a negative paper the same tone is left). oni-pipeline tests/positive_paper.rs on the slide at rest and the prepared slide: the knee prints L* 5 over the pick within 1e-3, every neutral tone under it to the bit at Brightness −3 to +3, the 424 tones past the lift's excess print as Exposure's own time with the ends kept within 2e-5 relative, Exposure taking more light to lighten (twin: the light taken the negative paper's way misses), the grey lightening with +, darkening with −; the slide's print monotone from its densest film to its bare film at ±1 and ±4 (largest fall 1.2e-7; twin a dip of a hundredth refused). tests/paper.rs: the GPU on its reference on a lit slide at Brightness −3 (4.4e-7) and +3 (1.6e-6; twins 3.5e-2, 1.0e-1). legacy_print to the bit, no fingerprint recorded again.

title: Grain size is a grain's width on the film, in micrometres of a 35 mm frame, shown in the photo's own full-resolution pixels; sidecar format 47
detail: Grain size was a share of its track, its lattice cell 4^share pixels of a scan 6000 wide (6 to 24 µm of the scan's width read as 36 mm). It is now the mean width of a grain on the film, in µm, the scan's long side standing for a 135 frame's 36 mm (Grain::FRAME_LONG), so a portrait lays the same grain as a landscape and every resolution the same grain on the picture. The cell the kernel lays is the size over Grain::CLUMP_CELLS = 2.64, the field's mean run of one sign along a line, measured on the CPU reference (tests/grain_size.rs, 300 rows of 4000 px: 2.641 cells). The blur a clump takes in keeps its floor, a pixel of a scan 6000 wide. The slider stores µm on a track of 10 to 60 µm (film grain's 10 to 30 µm, Vitale 2010, to twice its coarsest), its readout writes px of the open photo's full-resolution long side once its decode lands (Field::figure, slider_track::stepped_on): 0.1 px a digit, so a ± key moves 0.3 px; µm until the decode lands. The Effects help says what the size is, in French and Spanish too. Migration (migrate::grain_size, format 47): a grain laid keeps its exact cell and blur, its share becoming 6·4^share·2.64·(width/long side) µm, the scan's shape asked of the original as the strokes' step asks it, held while the original cannot say (read meanwhile as on a photo wider than tall, never in the former units); a grain off takes the new rest; a document of no file (preset, paste) reads its photo as wider than tall.
outcome: The field's mean grain width measured 2.641 cells (constant 2.64; twin: the cell taken for the width is refused). On the real app (window checks with ONI_RAW_DIR): roll #8's Nikon Z f NEF, a scan 6048 px long, reads Grain size 3.4 px at 20 µm; the Lumix RW2 copied from the owner's digital photos, 8368 px long (47 Mpx), reads 4.6 px; the ± keys move 0.3 px and the value editor 0.1 px on both. The owner's 47 Mpx sidecar (format 46, Grain 40%, size 0.5) migrates to 31.68 µm, its cell 2.789 px as before. Cross-check: the former 40% is 27.6 µm, 4.6 px at 24 Mpx and 6.4 px at 47 Mpx (lattice cell 1.76 and 2.43 px); the former law already laid a share of the scan's width, so a size looked the same on the picture at 24 and 47 Mpx for a landscape, never twice as big; a portrait laid its grain two thirds as coarse, which the long side now corrects. The physics rest, 20 µm, is 0.73 of the former 40% (former share 17%); the owner's hand-placed sizes on his digital photos span 0.18 to 0.45, 20 to 30 µm. Corpus: 37 sidecars at amount 0 read size 20 µm, the digital one with grain 31.68 µm (5776 x 4336). All 291 window checks pass.

title: A digital photo opens with its grain on, Grain 25% at the physical rest of 20 µm
detail: PipelineSettings::rest lays Grain::DIGITAL_AMOUNT (0.25, owner's call) on a digital photo, at Grain::SIZE_REST, 20 µm, the middle of film grain's 10 to 30 µm (Tim Vitale, 'Film Grain, Resolution and Fundamental Film Particles', v24, 2010, table 1: film grain 10-30 µm, dye clouds 1-15 µm, silver halide 0.2-2 µm); no stock publishes its own, so one constant serves every stock. A mode change carries the amount as it carries every value still on its rest. Negatives keep grain off; every edited photo keeps what its sidecar says (amount and size are always written).
outcome: A negative TIFF turned Digital in the window opens on Grain 25% at 20 µm, its Film Effects block at rest; checks reading the digital rest as grain-free now say the grain off themselves (pipeline grain, grain_seed, virtual_film, one_face, lens_sidecar).

title: Grain size rests on the owner's 40%: 27.6 µm
detail: The owner set a digital photo's grain at 25% and size 40% of the former track; on a landscape scan that is 27.6 µm on the film, film grain's coarse end (Vitale's 10-30 µm), an ISO 800 stock's. SIZE_REST moves from 20 µm (the range's middle) to 27.6 µm: 4.6 px on a 24 Mpx Z f, 6.4 px on a 47 Mpx Lumix. Checked against migrate::grain_size::microns(0.4, 1.0), with the former 50% rest as its twin.

title: Every spektrafilm colour negative and reversal profile ships unchanged in resources/film
detail: At spektrafilm's commit 3bb2c2d the profiles are 16 colour negatives (Portra 160, 400, 800 and its Push 1 and Push 2, Ektar 100, Gold 200, UltraMax 400, Verita 200D, Vision3 50D, 200T, 250D and 500T, C200, Pro 400H, Superia X-TRA 400), 4 colour reversals (Provia 100F, Velvia 100, Ektachrome 100, Kodachrome 64), 6 papers (Portra, Supra, Ultra Endura, Endura Premier, Crystal Archive Type II, Ektacolor Edge) and 2 cine print films (Vision 2383, Vision Premier 2393); no black and white. Newly shipped, byte for byte: kodak_portra_800_push1/2 (their dyes and sensitivities are Portra 800's, their curves their own) and the four reversals, which nothing reads yet. CHANGELOG.txt names them, the papers and print films left out, and the tungsten lamp.

title: A digital photo can be shot on any of the 16 colour negatives spektrafilm profiles, each baked at its first use; sidecar format 50
detail: oni_settings::VirtualStock lists every colour negative profile, Portra 800 first and the default, each by its key (the dye sets' own, kodak-portra-800-push-1/-2 for the pushes) and one table entry: name, catalogue stock, dye set (a push develops Portra 800's dyes), profile, balance and reference. Balance::Tungsten is the profile's reference_illuminant "T" (Vision3 200T and 500T): NIST's incandescent lamp as colour-science 0.4.6 ships it, the spectrum spektrafilm reads for T (film::cie::INCANDESCENT, x 0.45073 y 0.40805, about 2800 K); every other stock D55. film::bake reads the stock's light for its window, light table and adaptation; film::stock bakes in a OnceLock per stock, so nothing is baked before a photo uses it. A key a build of 46 cannot read moves the format to 50 (migrate::chain::VIRTUAL_STOCKS_VERSION, no step: every older document names Portra 800; corpus newer file version-51); the format 37 migration reads any other stock on its own reference. Portra 800's reference, kernel and table are unchanged to the bit, so no photo moves: a read-only scan of the owner's 161 digital photos found all on Portra 800.
outcome: Bake per stock 21 to 30 ms (dev profile), its table 776 KB in memory and on the GPU once uploaded; 0 at startup.

title: The scan's band uniform holds every wavelength of a profile's grid: a cine stock's 76 measured wavelengths overflowed its 64
detail: VIRTUAL_NEGATIVE_BANDS was 64 and the Vision3 profiles measure their dyes and base on 76 (Vision3 50D on 71): DyeSeparation::rows padded with 64 minus 76, an overflow, so a roll on Vision3 or CineStill 50D/800T could not render its dye separation, and a Vision3 virtual film could not bake. It is now 81, the 380 to 780 nm grid's every wavelength, in the kernel and both WGSL uniforms (virtual_negative, dye_separation), as the paper's PAPER_BANDS already was. Check dye_separation::the_gpu_separates_every_sets_every_band: every set fits one uniform size and the GPU unmixes each as its reference (Vision3 within 7.4e-7, twin dose 0.9 at 1.2e-2 or more); it failed on 64 (76 wavelengths measured).
outcome: No owner roll is on a Vision3 or CineStill 50D/800T stock (read-only scan of 1 715 sidecars), so none rendered through the overflow.

title: The film catalogue states each stock's speed and type, lists Portra 800 Push 1 and 2 and Kodachrome 64, and an undrawn stock shows its type's generic canister
detail: FilmStockKind gains iso (the speed the roll is exposed at, a push's EI: 1600, 3200; none for a line, a generic stock, AgfaPhoto APX or LomoChrome Turquoise) and kind (FilmType: ColourNegative, CineNegative, ColourSlide, BlackAndWhite); FilmType::generic names the generic stock whose canister stands in. New stocks: kodak-portra800-push1/-push2 (Portra 800's dyes, Portra's canister) and kodak-kodachrome64 (no dyes, the generic positive's canister). Provia 100F, Velvia 100 and Ektachrome 100 profiles map to the existing Fujifilm Provia 100, Velvia 100 and Kodak Ektachrome. Checks: a colour or cine negative names its dyes and nothing else does (by type, replacing the name heuristics), every canister is the stock's own, its line's or its type's generic, a precise stock states its speed (twin: a cine negative stands on the colour negative's canister).

title: A canister arrives by dropping its SVG in the stocks' folder: the artwork table is listed by the build script
detail: oni-app's build.rs lists crates/oni-ui/ui/stocks/*.svg into ARTWORK (rerun when the folder changes); the owner's hashes stay checked for the 41 shipped canisters, and any other SVG must name a catalogue stock. A dropped SVG then asks its catalogue line to read stock(…) (a_stock_with_its_own_artwork_draws_it names it), the one line it takes.

title: Every virtual stock measured on a neutral scene: grey, white and chroma on the default paper, CPU table and GPU, with twins
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/virtual_stocks.rs, table-driven over VirtualStock::ALL at the digital rest on the stock (paper included): a neutral ramp lit at the stock's white, -3 to +2.3 stops, printed through the CPU references; its grey within 2e-3 of a plain RAW's, its white's luma within 0.06 stop of Portra 800's, its CIELAB chroma under 4 (under 2 from L* 80 up); twin, the red gain 0.2 stop off the reference, 12.8 to 16.8. The GPU renders the same ramp through Pipeline::render (twin: lit at the other light, C* 40 or more). A tungsten stock turns a D55 grey blue (b/r 2.0 on 500T), a daylight one keeps it neutral; each stock's white is the chromaticity of the spectrum its bake reads. virtual_film's kernel-against-reference and grey checks run on every stock (in-gamut scenes within 0.001 density, the locus' primaries within 0.004: 0.0028 on 500T; a grey within a sixth of a stop of log 0, Portra 400's blue 0.037; the couplers' grey ramp within 0.03 density, Push 2 0.028).
outcome: Grey 0.3985 on every stock (a plain RAW's). White luma 0.753 (Verita 200D) to 0.795 (Push 2), Portra 800 0.766. Neutral chroma: grey 0.0 everywhere; from L* 80 up at most 1.6 (Vision3 200T); the shadows carry each stock's own toes, at most C* 3.7 (Pro 400H at -2 stops), 3.4 (Superia at -1), 3.2 (Verita at -2), 3.0 (Portra 160, C200), Portra 800 1.2.

title: A stock's canister is drawn by the stock's own key everywhere: a roll on a stock of a line or a stock still undrawn shows its canister in the tree's rows
detail: crates/oni-app/src/stocks.rs: icon and row_icon took the artwork's key, yet the tree's rows (library::default_stock, the navigator's stocks) passed the stock's key, so a roll on Kodak Portra 400, Gold 200, Fujifilm C200 or an undrawn Vision3 drew no mini canister. Both now resolve the stock through the catalogue to the canister its icon_name names (its own, its line's, or its kind's generic one, as `undrawn` lays the colour negative's), so every caller passes the stock's key. Group.stock and the archive's second writer of Library.stock, which the info sidebar overwrote, are gone. Check: library::tests a roll on kodak-portra400 draws its row icon (twin: an unknown key draws none, stocks::tests).

title: One stock hero, the canister large over its name, its line and the key to the sheet, in the gallery's sidebar, Prepare the Roll and the editor
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/stocks.slint: struct Canister (name, note, artwork) and component StockHero, the info sidebar's heroStock made a component with a slot for what a place adds (the sidebar's dyes warning and fix). Library.stock, Preparing.stock and PanelState.stock are each one Canister built by stocks::canister; the gallery's and the editor's roll note by info_sidebar::roll_canister (picked, line unstated, or the mode's default said so). Prepare the Roll's Film step shows the hero in place of the small row, its line still naming the dyes the stock separates on.

title: The editor's Roll tab changes the roll's film stock: every photo of the roll follows as one undoable step
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/roll_tab.slint: a Film Stock block under Film Type for every photo but a digital one, the hero on PanelState.stock. Its key is Act::SelectRollType through Ctl::act, which in the editor opens the sheet on the open photo's roll (StockTarget::OpenRoll), the gallery's roll else; a pick runs set_stock_of_roll_at on the open photo, the same path as Prepare's measure and the sidebar's update_roll_of: the folder's marker and the stock's measured dyes on every frame, the open one included, one history step labelled Set Film Stock. The hero, the Dye Separation block and the render follow at once.

title: A digital photo's virtual film is picked from the Colour tab's Film block, among the virtual films alone, its white always in sight
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/film_block.slint: the one-tab stock row gives way to the hero and its key, which opens the sheet on the stocks VirtualStock::ALL names (stocks::virtual_by_brand, StockTarget::Film), so a stock added there is listed with no interface change; a pick writes picked_film (the stock's own reference, the exposure kept) as one step of the editor's history, the pipeline baking the stock's negative on first use. The white the stock locks the scene to moves out from behind the settings key to the key's row, so a change of film shows where its light moved; the key keeps the reference. Help in English, French and Spanish.

title: Window checks: Prepare's hero picks the stock, the Roll tab's pick is one undoable roll step, the Film block lists the virtual films alone
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/stock_hero.rs (new, three checks, shots stock-hero-prepare, stock-hero-roll-tab, stock-hero-film), driven by clicks on the hero's key and Ctl::act: Prepare's default then Kodak Portra 400 named with its dyes (twin: Done changes nothing); in the editor Fujifilm C200 laid on the marker and on both photos' dyes, the render, the hero and Dye Separation following, one Undo taking all back and Redo laying them again (twin: Done writes nothing; the gallery's sidebar shows the editor's pick); a digital photo's sheet lists exactly VirtualStock::ALL (twin: fewer than a roll's), each film picked placing its reference and white, one Undo back (twin: a stock no digital photo is shot on, chosen anyway, changes nothing). stocks.rs, row_marks.rs and virtual_film.rs read the Canister; the hero taller than the old row, film_effects opens at 2160 px and panel_bindings at 1080 px so the rows they press stay in sight; fields::tests lays Film Stock in the Roll tab's order.

title: slider_hand presses Exposure where the Colour tab now lays it: the window tall enough, the rail asserted in sight
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/slider_hand.rs: with the Paper section open by default between More Color Settings and Lighting (#3110), Exposure's rail fell under the 800 px window, so the press reached no slider and both checks failed on their first hand (deterministic alone, not load). The window is 1000 px and the rail is asserted inside it, so a later layout change fails on its cause.

title: The Save a Preset fit check counts the card's own boxes, not the panel's switch beside it
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/presets.rs: fits() took every checkbox of the window; the panel's Print on paper switch, now at y 696 to 709 right of the card, was read as the card's lowest box. Only boxes left of the commit key's right edge count; the sheet itself was laid right (shot presets-save-sheet). Its twin (a card taller than its content) is kept.

title: More Color Settings' folded check reads the section after it, Paper, where it once read Lighting
