detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/channel_points.rs: the check measured Lighting a row under the folded title; Paper now stands between (#3110), 148 pt. The next section's title is the measure again, for the folded gap, the opened gap and the band the block's tabs are searched in.

title: The Film block's sheet is checked in its brand order against the sixteen virtual films
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/stock_hero.rs: the check expected VirtualStock::ALL's order, true for one stock only; the sheet lists by brand in the catalogue's order (stocks::virtual_by_brand), and the check now asserts that order and, apart, that the set is exactly VirtualStock::ALL. With sixteen stocks the pick, render, reference and white, and Undo loop runs for each and passes.

title: What a slide prints on: a reversal paper, Kodak Ektachrome Radiance III, from Kodak's own data sheet
detail: A slide was printed positive to positive on a reversal paper (Ilfochrome/Cibachrome silver dye bleach, Kodak Ektachrome Radiance R-3, Fujichrome Type 35/R) or through an internegative onto a negative paper. spektrafilm at 3bb2c2d holds no reversal paper: its six papers and the two print films are all negative-working (info type negative), and its runtime prints a positive film on them as it prints a negative. No internegative film is profiled either. Ilford's Ilfochrome Classic sheets found online (TDS 305US) give no spectral dye densities. Kodak publication E-1766 (Ektachrome Radiance III Paper, February 2003) gives characteristic curves (Status A reflection, R-3), spectral dye densities and spectral sensitivities, all three as vector drawings, so each curve reads at the points Kodak drew. Kodak's own starting pack for it is 10M + 20C, no yellow.
outcome: Radiance III chosen: a measured reversal paper, its three curves complete, printable by ONI's existing paper machinery once laid in spektrafilm's profile layout. Status A's spectral products taken from ANSI/ISO 5-3-1995 (IT2.18-1996, Table 3) to turn Kodak's integral densities into each layer's dye amount.

title: Kodak Ektachrome Radiance III as a paper profile read off Kodak's data sheet, and spektrafilm's E-6 profiles for a slide's dyes
detail: docs/research/positive-paper/radiance_iii.py reads page 5 of E-1766 (digitise: the 0.72 pt stroked paths inside each figure's frame, mapped by its ticks, into radiance_iii.csv) and builds crates/oni-pipeline/resources/film/kodak_ektachrome_radiance_iii.json (fit): dyes on 400 to 700 nm scaled to a Status A density of 1 in their own channel; a flat base (Kodak publishes none) at the density leaving the fully exposed least layer with no dye (0.061); Kodak's integral R, G, B densities turned into each layer's dye amount by Newton's steps; the log exposure moved so the neutral scale reads 1 over its floor at 0, as spektrafilm's layout reads a unit exposure; each layer three falling normal integrals (negative spreads) and its stain; log sensitivity on 380 to 780 nm, past each plotted end its last 10 nm slope, never rising. kodak_ektachrome_100, fujifilm_provia_100f and fujifilm_velvia_100 shipped unchanged (CC BY-SA 4.0); a slide's dyes are their mean (film::dyes::slide), and the camera reads them as it reads a negative's (slide_dyes). CHANGELOG.txt names the sources.
outcome: The profile's Status A print of a neutral scale lands within 0.016 of Kodak's R curve and 0.009 of G and B over log exposure 0 to 3.8 (the fit's worst: cyan 0.016, magenta 0.006, yellow 0.006). Analytic Dmax 2.02 C, 1.35 M, 1.64 Y over the base; Kodak's own R, G, B curves part by up to 0.125 in natural log of light between densities 0.15 and 2.

title: A slide prints on the reversal paper in true density, its densest read anchored black, the paper's white free, Lighting before the paper's curve; sidecar format 52
detail: PaperStock::KodakEktachromeRadianceIII (key kodak-ektachrome-radiance-iii), reversal(), listed(positive), default_for(positive); PipelineSettings::paper() prints a reversal paper on a slide alone and a negative paper on the rest, fitting_paper() the paper a print takes (balance::written, roll::digital, the slide's Prepare). takes_paper() now refuses only a positive read as its own negative. Kernel: Paper.reversal (points_white.w on the GPU) reads Lighting's tones from the print's black end, a slide's densest film, so points, zones and mids keep their sense; CPU reference and WGSL alike. Pipeline: film_ends reads a slide's windows (DMAX less the density, its white its bare film); anchors put the pick at the densest read; the reference grey is read with the mode's inversion; the enlarger holds Film::Slide, the E-6 dyes, the slide's scan unmixed whole into dye amounts for its paper only (ONI's print still reads a slide as a plain RAW); a stop of Exposure and a filter's stop take the reversal paper's sense (more light, CC taken away); the paper's white is its fully exposed end. The rest solves its pack with one filter at none, cyan first as a negative enlarger's, else the one leaving the others no less (the slide rests on C 0.37 Y 20.1, magenta at none; Kodak starts at 10M + 20C): every negative's rest unchanged. Format 52, no step: no older document names the key; the broken corpus file version-47 became version-53.
outcome: A slide at rest prints its reference grey at a plain RAW's grey within 2e-6 on every channel (both test slides); its densest read at 1.3 to 2.1 times the paper's Dmax light with True blacks off, on 0 with it; its bare film within 0.2 % (at rest) to 5 % (a hand's windows) of the paper's white. A neutral wedge from bare film to densest read stays within 0.116 natural log of a channel over green (Kodak's own curves part by 0.125); unmixing the slide's dyes brought it from 0.137. GPU against CPU on a slide and a lit slide (points, zones, mids, filters, Brightness): 4.0e-7 and 5.7e-7, twins 2.8e-2. A slide on no paper or a negative paper renders as before, its stage 4-7 arguments equal to the bit.

title: The paper's list on the Colour tab holds the papers of the frame's film; a prepared slide roll prints on its paper
detail: roll_tab: the switch is offered on a slide too, its list Radiance III alone (a negative's every other paper), a pick indexes that list, the switch on takes fitting_paper. prepare/slides: each prepared slide takes Some(fitting_paper()), as a prepared negative takes its paper (owner's call for negatives); a slide edited before keeps print_paper as it is, so its render does not move. The trade name is not translated, no new shown text. tests/window/paper.rs drives it: a slide offered the switch off, on prints Radiance III with Brightness and True blacks; back on a negative the reversal paper prints nothing and the switch takes Portra Endura.
outcome: Window checks green: paper (the switch on a slide and back), slides (every slide of a prepared roll on Radiance III), prepare, prepare_measure and one_face.

title: The reversal paper measured on the owner's slides: tone and colour against ONI's slide render, its gamut against Portra Endura
detail: crates/oni-app/examples/slide_paper.rs renders a slide as edited on ONI's print, on Radiance III at rest and with True blacks. Four frames of the owner's slide roll (Sony ARW, copied to scratch) rendered at 1600 px, judged in Oklab. tests/positive_paper.rs measures each paper's two-dye primaries at half Dmax.
outcome: Against ONI's own slide render the paper keeps the tone range (Oklab L 5 to 95 percentile range 0.58 to 0.70 against 0.59 to 0.75; True blacks 0.64 to 0.75), lifts the deepest shadows at rest (L p1 0.21 against 0.14 to 0.17, the densest read printed where the rest prints it) and holds about half the chroma (mean 0.044 to 0.064 against 0.082 to 0.105). The primaries hold 0.60 to 0.70 of Portra Endura's chroma (Oklab 0.128, 0.119, 0.132 against 0.184, 0.198, 0.202): Kodak's R-3 dyes absorb more outside their bands. Without the slide's unmix the chroma fell further (0.027 on one frame); a steeper sensitivity past the plotted ends moved nothing (0.0436 to 0.0442).

title: Each virtual stock's personality measured at every stage against spektrafilm's own chain: ONI keeps all of it
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/examples/stock_chart.rs prints a chart (ColorChecker 24, 14 saturated Rec. 709 primaries and secondaries, a grey ramp) through each virtual stock at the digital rest on the CPU references: the scene lit at the stock's white, its dye amounts, its scan, its print on the default paper and on ONI's own print. crates/oni-app/examples/stock_strip.rs renders a photo headless on each stock (paper, ONI's print, the scene each film reads), and the photo as its sidecar holds it against the same edit placed on its own film. spektrafilm 3bb2c2d ran the same scenes as a benchmark (LUT mode, Rec. 2020 linear in and out, Portra Endura, each print's time and filtration solved so the 18.4 % grey prints neutral at a plain RAW's grey). Stocks: UltraMax 400, Verita 200D, Portra 400, Ektar 100, Portra 800, Portra 800 Push 1, Gold 200, Vision3 250D; five of the owner's digital photos copied to scratch (sky and foliage, skin and a red and white plane, skin in a mirror, an office with skin and saturated chairs, a lit shop front).
outcome: Mean pairwise CIEDE2000 between stocks on the chart's colours: spektrafilm 2.67 (UltraMax to Verita 1.42, UltraMax to Portra 800 0.67, largest Push 1 to Verita 4.57); ONI on the paper 2.91 (UltraMax to Verita 1.49), the two matrices correlated at 0.9994, ONI's 8 % larger, each stock within 1.4 to 2.1 of spektrafilm's print; ONI's own print 3.50. The negatives agree: dye amounts within 0.01 density of spektrafilm's, scans 3.49 against 3.37. On the five photos: spektrafilm 2.42, ONI on the paper 2.30 (UltraMax to Verita 1.87 against 1.78), correlated at 0.967. Verita is not an intense stock in spektrafilm's data: its mean chroma on the paper is among the lowest (C* 51.3 against UltraMax 52.9, Ektar 55.6, Push 1 59.5). Decomposed on Portra 800 in spektrafilm, grey held neutral: another stock's sensitivities move the print 0.6 to 2.0, its curves 0.2 to 3.9, its dyes 0.2 to 1.0, the whole stock 0.7 to 3.9; the DIR couplers' interlayer terms, one matrix for every colour negative in spektrafilm, move it 3.6 to 3.7 at half or one and a half their strength (C* 43 or 60 from 52.4) and 6.7 off (C* 35.5).

title: A digital photo reads its negative on its own film's gains, windows and dyes: its folder's roll never lays another film's
detail: A digital photo's roll is its folder (RollKey::Slides), whose rule leaves the film type and the windows out; a film picked on one photo moved its gains and its dye set, roll fields, so every other digital photo of the folder took the picked stock's gains and dyes on its own film and windows. oni_settings::settings::roll_settings::on_own_film places a digital photo back on its film's gains, windows and dyes after any roll copy (those it held when its film stands, its film's reference when it took another), called by roll_settings::copied and by Edit Together's step on a frame (oni-core store/together.rs); a slide alone takes the roll's gains as an offset. Checks (oni-core store::tests::digital): a film picked on one photo leaves the folder's others on their film's own reference; a dye dose moved on one still reaches the folder, each on its own film's dyes. Both fail with on_own_film laying nothing (twin run by hand: 2 of 4 failed), and each carries a twin asserting another film's gains and dyes read off the reference.
outcome: Read-only scan of the owner's 161 digital photos: 159 carried another stock's gains and dyes, one per folder (Vision3 200T on the 97 photos of one session, UltraMax 400 on the 64 of the other) whatever their film: 91 on Portra 800 read through Vision3 200T's dyes, a Verita photo through Vision3 200T's. Placed on their own film, five of them move by a mean CIEDE2000 of 1.2, 2.4, 2.7, 5.9 and 9.5 (95th percentile up to 16.4): the Verita photo loses a blue cast. More than a stock's whole personality on the paper (2.3), so the library showed every photo of a folder through the last stock picked in it.

title: Sidecar format 56: a digital photo standing on another stock's gains and dyes whole moves onto its own film's
detail: oni_settings::migrate::own_film: a digital photo of a format before 56 whose gains are another stock's reference within 1e-6 and whose dye set is that stock's takes its own film's gains and dyes; its windows, its own, and every other value stay. A hand's gains, a photo already on its own film's (a push on Portra 800's), and a file of format 56 stay as they are (twins in its test). The corpus's newer file moves to version 57.
outcome: 159 of the owner's 161 digital photos move (count on copies of their sidecars), each onto the film it names: the owner asked for each stock's personality, and these photos were read on another stock's by a fault, so their render moves on purpose.

title: The Film section's Exposure against Lighting's on the paper: half the brightness per stop, the negative's latitude besides
detail: stock_strip with ONI_FILM_EXPOSURE and ONI_PRINT_EXPOSURE at -2, -1, +1 and +2 on three of the owner's photos on Portra 800 and the default paper; CIELAB L* mean, 2nd and 98th percentiles, interquartile range and mean chroma, and each film move against the Lighting move nearest in mean L*.
outcome: A stop of film exposure moves the print's mean L* by about 13 to 15, a stop of Lighting's Exposure by 21 to 24: the negative's contrast, about 0.6, halves the light the enlarger sees. Film -2 lands within CIEDE2000 3.0 of Lighting -1 and Film +2 within 2.4 to 3.0 of Lighting +1; at a matched brightness the film move keeps more of the tonal range (interquartile L* 37 against 29 at +1 on the plane) and 10 to 20 % more chroma, and its extremes reach the film's toe and shoulder (lifted, milky shadows at +2, deeper blue skies at -2). As a brightness control it repeats Lighting's; what it alone shows is a negative over or under exposed. Unchanged by #3261.

title: Brightness on a paper looked at against Exposure on four frames: the knee's held blacks and 4× band cut the image, its ¼ floor flattened the mids
detail: Owner's verdict of 2026-11-22: the Brightness of #3130-#3133 destroys the image; redo it from zero, Exposure everywhere but the blacks and the very start of the shadows. crates/oni-app/examples/brightness_strips.rs (replacing brightness_knee.rs) renders each photo on its paper (Portra Endura where it has none) at Exposure and Brightness −1, −0.5, 0, +0.5, +1 through the app's engine, a crop of its darkest third, and plots and measures its neutral's transfer (L* out against L* at rest, its slope, the largest slope step, falls, the neutral's chroma) at ±0.5, ±1, ±2, ±4. Run on copies of DSC_6440 and DSC_6452 (roll #8 test copy), DSC_6438, DSC_6464 and two digital photos of the owner's (Lumix, copied read-only), never committed.
outcome: The knee held every tone under L* 5 to the bit and laid the whole stop within 0.2 of log exposure past it: at +1 on DSC_6440 L* 8 moved +1.9, L* 12 +8.8, L* 20 +26.9 (Exposure +26.5, +29.3, +32.6), the band L* 8 to 20 stretched about 3× while the blacks under it stayed put; by eye a black sweater, a backlit silhouette and a crowd's shade print as cut-out black blobs against lifted mids. Darkening hit the ¼ slope floor right at the knee: at −1 on DSC_6452 L* 20 moved −4.9 and L* 30 −11.7 (Exposure −16.4, −23.8), the mids folded onto the knee, a flat muddy print (a lamp's glow, a tarmac's shade). Candidates then (#3281): S, Exposure's shift faded in from the pick by a smoothstep in log exposure, darkening its inverse, its width where the neutral prints L* 20, 25, 30, 35 or 50; T, Exposure's print laid over the rest's by a smoothstep of the rest's L* (a luminosity mask), composed from the renders. S at L* 20 to 30 and T look alike by eye at +1 (blacks deep, the shade's folds kept, the rest Exposure); T needs two prints a pixel and its weight's slope times Exposure's darkening (−14 L* at L* 15, −4) outruns the print's own slope, so it turns tones back at strong darkening; S keeps one print and never does. L* 20 left L* 5 a third of Exposure's move at +1, L* 35 and 50 kept the lower mids short of Exposure (L* 20 +31 and +17 for +33); L* 25 chosen.

title: A paper's Brightness is Exposure's shift faded in from the pick by a smoothstep over the deep shadows, darkening its inverse: the knee and its slope caps gone
detail: kernel::paper: Brightness moves each tone's mean log exposure x from the pick toward the light (Paper::toward_light, one shift on the three layers, the reversal paper's sense kept) by lifted(x, lift, reach): brightening x + lift·share(x, w), share a smoothstep from none at the pick to the whole at w; darkening that map's inverse, found by 24 halvings, so −b undoes +b, no tone passes another and the pick, the tones beyond it and every tone past w + |lift| print as before and as Exposure. The width w = fade(lift, reach) = max(reach, √(|lift|·log10 2)), never under √stops stops, so every slope stays within 1 + 1.5·√stops and its inverse (4 and ¼ at ±4): a layer up to ¾ slower than its tone's mean never turns back, and the map still rises with the slider at every tone (the width's elasticity in the lift ≤ ½). The reach (Paper.reach, the slope row's w) is where the frame's neutral prints L* 25 over the pick on the print's own range (paper::lighting::BRIGHTNESS_REACH_LIGHT 0.044155), solved per frame by bisection under its own Lighting at rest as the knee was. Removed: PAPER_KNEE_SLOPE, kneed, excess, Paper.knee, BRIGHTNESS_KNEE_LIGHT, KNEE_REACH; the WGSL's paper_kneed and paper_excess for paper_share and paper_lifted. Settings and the sidecar unchanged (no format bump): photos with Brightness ≠ 0 on a paper move, as asked; Lighting's help sentence (Exposure sparing that black and the first shadows) still says what it does.
outcome: On the neutral (#3280's example): at +1 DSC_6440 L* 3 +2.7, 5 +6.9, 8 +12.6, 20 +30.7, 50 +28.2 (Exposure +18.8, +23.0, +26.5, +32.6, +29.2), DSC_6452 L* 3 +4.6, 20 +34.0 (Exposure +16.2, +34.3); at −1 DSC_6440 L* 3 −1.1, 20 −12.3, 50 −30.3 (Exposure −2.6, −17.2, −32.5); the transfer's slope at +1 0.08 to 3.3 against Exposure's 0.06 to 7.1, the neutral's C* within 0.5 of Exposure's at ±0.5 and ±1, no fall. By eye (before / after / Exposure strips in the scratch folder): the shade, a black sweater and a silhouette keep their depth with their folds, the rest prints as Exposure; at −1 the glow and the mids darken as Exposure with the shadows kept apart. Checks in #3282.

title: Brightness's fade: the pick to the bit, the deep shadows a fraction of Exposure's move, the mids on Exposure, slopes within ¼ and 4, −b undoing +b, the GPU on its reference
detail: oni-render kernel/paper/tests.rs, on reaches 0.3 and 0.05 (the floor setting the width) and lifts −4 to +4 stops: the pick and beyond to the bit; past the width and the fold Exposure's shift within 3e-7; a tone a tenth of the reach from the pick moved under 3 % of the lift (twin: a straight fade moves it a tenth); every slope within the smoothstep's steepest and its inverse and inside ¼ and 4 (twins: darkening by the same smoothstep turns tones back at −4; a fade held at a reach of 0.05 steepens past 8); C1 at the pick, the width and the fold's end (twin: a corner keeps its kink); −b undoes +b within 2e-6 (twin: the fold misses by 0.05); rising with the lift at every tone (twin: a width proportional to the lift moves the deepest tones back); brightened one shift on the three layers (twin: each layer by its own distance), the reversal paper's sense (twin: read as a negative paper). oni-pipeline tests/paper_ends.rs on a negative, a digital photo, black and white and the Frontier: the reach prints L* 25 over the pick within 1e-3 under each of the 22 Lighting moves, independent of the anchor (twin: read on a lifted anchor it lies elsewhere); at Brightness −4, −1, −0.5, +0.5, +1, +4 the pick and beyond to the bit; tones 0.5 to 3 L* over the pick move at most a third of Exposure's L* brightening (0.03 to 0.32) and 0.7 darkening (0.37 to 0.66, Exposure crushing them on black), each under a straight fade of the same width by 0.05 or more (twin), the twin's print the kernel's own when it moves as Brightness; the grey within 1.5 L* of Exposure's own print past the fade (16 cases), no darker than it nearer the pick; the 570 tones past the fold as Exposure's time with the ends kept within 2e-5 relative (twin: twice the stops). tests/positive_paper.rs, the same on the reversal paper (the reach, the dark side to the bit, past the fold as Exposure's light, a deep tone moved under 3 % of the lift while Exposure moves it all). tests/paper_ends.rs's monotone print now holds at Exposure +2 with Brightness −1, where a fixed width fell 4.5e-5. tests/paper.rs: the GPU within 2.2e-7 of its reference at Brightness −4, 6.8e-7 at +4, 3.2e-7 and 1.3e-6 on the slide at −3 and +3 (twins 2.8e-2 to 1.3e-1). tests/legacy_print.rs unchanged: the four paper cases carry no Brightness and their GPU fingerprints hold, none recorded again.
outcome: oni-render lib and every oni-pipeline test green; scripts/lint green.

title: Why a slide on Radiance III lost its colour, and what prints a slide well: Radiance III checked for a construction error, then an internegative onto a negative paper on the owner's slides
detail: Five of the owner's slides (test Positif 334, 336, 340, 343, 358, their sidecars as the app now reads them) rendered at 900 px on ONI's print, on Radiance III and through a virtual internegative onto each negative paper, judged in Oklab against ONI's render and by eye. Radiance III's construction re-read: ISO 5-3 Status A as tabulated (blue from 420 nm, its slopes past each end), the dyes scaled to a Status A density of 1 in their own channel, the analytic amounts, the curve fit within 0.016, the rest's filtration (C 0.37 Y 20.1 against Kodak's 10M + 20C start), the black anchored on pure black: no error found. A spectral simulation of a slide (E-6 mean dyes) printed on it, against the slide on a D50 light table, keeps 0.47 to 0.80 of its chroma (green 0.47, blue 0.53, magenta 0.59 to 0.70, red 0.80) and turns yellow and magenta by 12 degrees: two passes of unwanted absorptions with no interimage effect, which Kodak's sheet does not give. The internegative: the slide's scan, through its gains, exposes a virtual colour negative with its reference grey at the film's grey, printed on the paper as a digital photo's negative is; spektrafilm profiles no internegative stock, so seven of its colour negatives were tried on Portra Endura (Vision3 50D and 250D, Portra 160 and 400, Ektar 100, Gold 200, C200).
outcome: On the five slides Radiance III held 0.49 to 0.63 of ONI's chroma on the vivid quarter of the picture; the internegative on Portra Endura 0.83 to 1.06, its lightness within 0.016 to 0.053 Oklab L rms of ONI's (Radiance III 0.045 to 0.053). Among the stocks Vision3 50D turned the faded slides' blue-violets least (-4 to -12 degrees of Oklab hue against -5 to -26), kept chroma 0.85 to 1.06 and lightness closest: chosen. Every other paper keeps 0.75 to 1.29 (Endura Premier the most saturated, the Frontier warmest). Renders and figures: scratchpad slide-print/final/<frame>/before-after.png and papers.png, the stock sweep in stocks/.

title: A slide prints on every colour paper through a virtual Vision3 50D internegative; Kodak Ektachrome Radiance III retired; sidecar format 58
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/paperless.rs: the grey on a plain RAW's and the pick on pure black whatever Paper blacks says (twin: the paper's anchor), each dye moving its own channel alone (twin: the paper's crosstalk), the curve ONI's print node by node on both papers (twin: Portra Endura's own layers), a frame whose windows agree printing as on ONI's print within 1e-3 (twin: the paper 0.02 off at least), Contrast about the grey, Exposure and Brightness, the GPU against its reference on six frames (twin: the time 10 % off). crates/oni-settings/tests/paperless.rs and crates/oni-app/tests/window/paper.rs (the three states, the neutral print's own histogram).
outcome: Every negative, black and white and digital photo prints as before: their stage 4-7 arguments come from the same code once the reversal flag is gone, the rest's solve the cyan-at-none one it was. A slide off its paper renders on ONI's print unchanged.

title: A slide through its internegative: grey, ends, neutral scale, colour kept, Lighting and the GPU, with twins; the format's step; the window check on every paper
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/slide_print.rs replaces positive_paper.rs: the copy only for a slide on a paper (not bypassed, off the paper, a negative, an inverted positive); its reference grey prints a plain RAW's grey within 1 % (the copy unmixes its dyes, the stock's reference was placed without), its densest read under L* 3, its bare film near the paper's white, Paper blacks lifting it, twin a copy whose grey is not brought to the film's; a neutral wedge within 0.08 natural log of a channel over green above a hundredth of the light, twin the copy without the slide's gains; six colours keeping 0.8 to 1.6 of ONI's chroma, twin the print at colour density -0.5 refused; Exposure, a filter, Contrast, Shadows and Brightness acting as on a negative, twin the reversal sense; the GPU against the CPU (matrix, virtual negative, stage 4-7) and the editor's chain against it, twins a 10 % brighter paper and ONI's print. migrate::slide_paper's tests (each case and the newer format refused), the retired key reading as the default paper. tests/window/paper.rs: a negative switched to a slide keeps its paper, renders, lists every paper, shows the filtration, Brightness and Paper blacks; off then on takes Portra Endura. crates/oni-app/examples/slide_paper.rs renders a slide on ONI's print and on every paper.
outcome: Measured: the slide's grey at 0.3958 against a plain RAW's 0.3985; its densest read at luma 0.0019 (L* 1.7); a neutral wedge's worst cast 0.055; chroma kept 0.83 (green) to 1.21 (yellow); GPU 8.7e-7 against its reference, twin 4.2e-2.

title: A digital photo's film and a roll's stock drop a menu in the editor, each stock it lights shown on the photo unwritten
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/ds/stocks.slint (StockMenu, StockLine), crates/oni-ui/ui/stocks.slint (StockHero drops), crates/oni-app/src/app/stock_picker.rs. The Film block's and the Roll tab's key, and the canister and name above it, drop a menu under the key listing the stocks by brand, each with its canister at a tree row's side, the one in use checked; it scrolls within the window's room under the key. The line under the pointer or the arrows is lit and told at once (`Stocks.lit`): the stock rides in `State.stock_lit`, laid over the settings by `previewed` as a hovered preset is, so the canvas renders it through the one render path (one in flight, the latest waiting) with no write, no step and no sidecar. Leaving the menu, Escape or any close lights none, the photo's own again. A click or Return writes the stock as before (`picked` is the one function the light and the Film pick share; a roll's pick stays set_stock_of_roll_at, one step for every photo of the roll). Prepare the Roll, the gallery sidebar and the export's field keep the sheet; the editor's sheet route (StockTarget Film and OpenRoll, PanelState.select-stock, select_open_stock) is gone. A light that changes nothing the photo shows (a stock naming no dyes on a negative) asks no render, and a pick after its light renders nothing again: the light already showed what is written.

title: The menu's stocks are baked off the interface thread at its first light, never at launch
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/src/lib.rs bake_ahead, paper::Film::of (shared with printing). At the first stock lit after each drop, a thread bakes the virtual film's tables and its paper's enlarger for every listed stock, as each would render; a table already baked costs nothing (OnceLock).

title: The stocks' menu checked under the pointer, the arrows, Escape, a click and Return, with no write while lit
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/stock_hero.rs: a_stock_under_the_pointer_shows_on_the_photo_unwritten (pointer on a line renders it, store, Undo and sidecar unchanged; another line follows; leaving the menu and Escape restore; ↓ ↑↑ Return writes the stock lit; a click writes as the light showed; Undo; twins: the preview differs from the photo's own and a pick does write the sidecar), the Roll tab's (a lit stock shows its dyes, none written; one naming no dyes shows nothing; forty ↓ scroll the lit line into view while the first leaves it; pick, Undo, Redo) and the Film block's (lines by brand, the one in use checked, every film picked and undone); stock_picker unit checks of `picked` with twins.

title: ONI_BENCH=stocks: each stock lit timed to its photon, cold, warm and in a sweep
detail: crates/oni-app/src/bench/stocks.rs: lays the open photo's menu, lights every other stock in turn (600 ms apart) twice, then sweeps every line at 120 Hz; each light's time to the GPU's end of the first frame showing its render, and how many renders a sweep asked.
outcome: App profile, 2560×1440 window on the 5K screen, mains power, machine loaded by three other builds: on a 47 Mpx Lumix RW2 shot digital, hover to photon p50 69 ms warm, 72 ms cold (first light 61 ms, the bake ahead absorbs it): 1.5 ms to the encode, 5.6 ms to the next frame, 62 ms the frame's GPU work, i.e. the photo's sharp render from the film stage on; a 120 Hz sweep over 15 lines rendered 3 times. On a 24 Mpx Nikon Z f NEF negative (Roll tab, 21 of 51 stocks move its dyes): p50 57 ms, of which 50 ms the frame; a sweep of 51 lights rendered 8 times.

title: The stocks' menu check in a file of its own, two bench lines broken under the width
detail: Merged together, the Roll-tab and menu checks took stock_hero.rs to 415 lines, past the file ceiling, and the Brightness strips' and stocks bench's format strings ran past 200 characters. The menu's hover check moves to window/stock_menu.rs with stock_hero's helpers shared; the two strings break with a continuation.

title: Print on paper becomes Virtual enlarger, and a second switch, Print on paper, takes the spektrafilm paper away
detail: Owner's experiment: see what the paper's bricks bring by taking them away. Three states: Virtual enlarger off (ONI's print, unchanged); on with Print on paper on (the paper print, unchanged); on with Print on paper off (new): the enlarger prints on a neutral paper (crates/oni-pipeline/src/paper/neutral.rs) holding no paper's data, one band a dye, each layer exposed by its own dye alone behind the filter that holds it back and printing its own channel alone, its characteristic curve ONI's print at rest (the mode's rest, 1.5 stops on a negative, 0 on a slide, reversal on a slide), the same on the three layers, its log exposure axis the frame's mean range (the anchors' span, as a window spans its own), the reference grey at the share that prints a plain RAW's grey. The enlarger's rest still solves the grey neutral at a plain RAW's grey by its time and M/Y filtration, the pick lies on pure black, Lighting and Brightness act as on a paper, the colour density and the ends the same code. The kernel is unchanged: the neutral paper is three bands of table data. Paper blacks is hidden there and lays nothing: the neutral paper's own black is ONI's print's, light 0.

title: The sidecar keeps Print on paper as `paperless`, the paper kept as chosen; format 60
detail: crates/oni-settings/src/settings.rs: `paperless: bool`, unwritten while false, beside `printPaper` (the enlarger on with its paper; none on ONI's print). No migration step: an older sidecar has none, so every paper print reads on its paper and nothing moves; the format moves to 60 so an older build opens a paperless print read-only. A paste and Lighting's preset row carry it with the paper; a Prepare prints on its fitting paper with Print on paper on (`PipelineSettings::on_paper`, used by the roll's reference, a digital roll and a slide's measure). The corpus's readings carry `paperless: false`, its newer file is now version 61, the field counts are 47.

title: The Paper section shows Virtual enlarger, then Print on paper while it is on, the paper's picker and Paper blacks while both are
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/color_tab.slint and state.slint (`enlarger-on`, `on-paper` and their callbacks), crates/oni-app/src/app/roll_tab.rs. The enlarger's filtration and Lighting Brightness stay while the enlarger is on, Colour compensation while it is off. The section's help and Lighting's say what each switch does; French Agrandisseur virtuel / Tirer sur papier, Spanish Ampliadora virtual / Positivar en papel.

title: The neutral paper's checks, its GPU on every branch, the sidecar's switch and the window's three states
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/paperless.rs: the grey on a plain RAW's and the pick on pure black whatever Paper blacks says (twin: the paper's anchor), each dye moving its own channel alone (twin: the paper's crosstalk), the curve ONI's print node by node on both papers (twin: Portra Endura's own layers), a frame whose windows agree printing as on ONI's print within 1e-3 (twin: the paper 0.02 off at least), Contrast about the grey, Exposure and Brightness, the GPU against its reference on six frames (twin: the time 10 % off). crates/oni-settings/tests/paperless.rs and crates/oni-app/tests/window/paper.rs (the three states, the neutral print's own histogram).

title: Film profiles written from the makers' data sheets
detail: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py reads the owner's emulsion dataset (curves traced from the official Kodak and Fujifilm sheets) and writes one profile per colour negative with complete data (46 stocks, Portra 800's two pushes besides) into crates/oni-pipeline/resources/film/datasheet/, each naming its sheet, URL and SHA-256 and listing what is measured and what is inferred, and the table the bake includes (film/datasheet.rs). Sensitivities as printed, each layer scaled at bake so a grey under the stock's light exposes it at log 0 (the curves' common log H; profile flag layers_as_printed, bake::balanced); curves Status M less D-min on log H less the grey, the grey 1.03 log over the ISO 5800 speed point (Kodak Gold 200's printed Log H Ref over its own), a push n x 0.30 log under; dyes: Vision3's printed C/M/Y, every other stock's split of its printed neutral less D-min on the Vision3 sheets' mean dyes moved and widened, each dye at a Status M density of 1 in its channel (Status M approximated by normal bands); D-min printed; no band-pass window. A profile holding a number not finite is refused.

title: Every data-sheet colour negative as a roll stock and a virtual film, the 16 current stocks' twins beside them
detail: 48 catalogue entries, virtual films and dye sets: 32 new stocks (Fujifilm Pro 160C/NC/NH/NS/S, 160NC/NL/NPC/NS, Pro 800/800Z, New Pro 400, 200, 400, Fujicolor 100, Superia 100/200/1600/Premium 400/Reala/Venus 400/Venus 800/X-TRA 800, Natura 1600, Nexia 400/A200/Zoom Master 800, Reala Ace, Kodak Portra 160NC/160VC/400NC/400VC) and a data-sheet twin of each of the 16 current virtual films, keyed -datasheet, listed right after its spektrafilm entry; every current key keeps its profile, so no photo moves. A twin carries sheet_twin: the editor's menu, the info sidebar and the paper menu name it '<stock> · Datasheet', the stock sheet and the hero show 'Datasheet' under its name (translated). Undrawn canisters stand on the generic negative's. Each stock's reference is derived and held as the others'.

title: The colour papers and display materials whose own sheet prints their curves
detail: Kodak Endura Premier (a twin beside spektrafilm's), Endura Premier Metallic, Ektacolor Edge, Royal Digital, Photo Book; Fujifilm Crystal Archive Digital Type DP II and Digital Pearl (curves and log sensitivities from their older editions, AF3-212E and AF3-0220E) and the display material Fujiclear, each written whole from its sheet: sensitivities as printed, Status A curves less D-min sampled on 256 nodes, their log H origin where green prints an 18 % grey (the enlarger's time absorbs it; the solve starts there), a curve hidden under the others on its sheet taking their mean there, peak-normalised dyes at a Status A density of 1 (approximated by normal bands), the base their own dyes at the curves' least densities. Fujiclear prints as a paper, its densities read as its transmittance under the viewing light, as a light box shows it. The paper bake reads sampled curves beside spektrafilm's fitted model, which a spektrafilm paper keeps. Left out: Fujiflex and Fujitrans, whose layers, levelled for a laser, find no neutral rest in the enlarger (filtration off its range, the grey unprinted; Fujitrans's traced dyes never fall to zero); and, their sheets printing no characteristic curve, Crystal Archive Type CA, Super Type P, Digital Super Type CN and PDN, Supreme, Maxima, Textured, Deep Matte Velvet, Album, Album High Definition, the 2004 Crystal Archive Paper.

title: Every data-sheet film and paper bakes and renders finite on CPU and GPU
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/tests/datasheet_stocks.rs: every data-sheet profile reads (twin: a curve node past any double is refused, film and paper alike); a digital photo on each data-sheet film prints finite through the CPU reference without paper and on the default paper, each data-sheet paper prints finite under Portra 800 and its twin, and each film and paper renders finite on the GPU (twins: a NaN in a print or a render is seen). The virtual film check's reference balances printed layers as the bake does, a data-sheet tungsten stock's locus bound 0.015 (0.0142 on 500T, its red layer through no band-pass window); the neutral ramp checks hold spektrafilm's stocks and print the data-sheet ones (widest C*ab 1.6 to 12.6) for the owner to judge; the paper window check reads the longer list by position and the twin's label.

title: What the data-sheet profiles are and the licence they ship under
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/resources/film/datasheet/SOURCES.txt: what each file measures and infers, its sheet credited and linked, no PDF shipped, nothing from spektrafilm; the numbers are the makers' published measurements and ship under the repository's GPL-3.0 with that attribution, spektrafilm's CC BY-SA files kept for every stock and paper still naming them.

title: The dye sets' and virtual stocks' tables in files of their own
detail: The datasheet stocks took oni-settings' dyes.rs to 527 lines and virtual_film.rs to 513, past the 400-line file ceiling. The catalogue's dye-set table moves to dyes/stocks.rs, the virtual stocks' entries to virtual_film/entries.rs, and each file's tests to a tests.rs beside it; nothing else moves.

title: Lighting on the negative: a kernel reading each layer's log exposure back through its stock's development
detail: oni-render's negative kernel (CPU reference and WGSL): a pixel's density above the bare film read back to each layer's log exposure through the stock's two curves and its DIR couplers (Newton's steps), Exposure and Contrast laid there before the couplers pull, each channel's contrast and filter on what its layer develops on after they pull, the film developed again, then the points, zones and mids on its density and the print's tone. Under the toe's foot a density takes the foot's move, less the nearer the fog, which no move leaves; over the shoulder the shoulder's.

title: Lighting on the negative in every pipe, each print at its rest
detail: conversion::stage47 prints with Lighting at rest (Print::unlit) and lays crate::negative's Negative before the windows or the paper: ONI's print (its windows unreached, its print curve, Hunt and colour density at rest), the enlarger on a paper or the neutral paper, digital photos, scanned colour negatives, black and white, slides on ONI's print and slides through their internegative. The film developed again is the virtual stock's (digital), the dye set's profile (scans), the C-41 profiles' mean (generic), its mean layer uncoupled (black and white), the slide's own light (a positive). The paper keeps its rest's time and filtration; the print's pick is the bare film as Lighting develops it, anchored as before. The points' and Contrast's saturation curves and the points reaching the windows go: their colour is the negative's own.

title: Sidecar format 61: Lighting on the negative, a legacy print reading its machine's entry itself
detail: Every photo keeps its Lighting values and, where they move off rest, its render moves (owner's call). A photo on a laid legacy print off a paper kept its machine's entry in Lighting's Exposure, which ONI's print curve read: the legacy print lays that entry itself (one_face::look_entry_stops) and the migration moves Exposure to Lighting's rest by it, so a legacy photo at rest renders to the bit as before; its Scanner-face contrast, now on the negative, moves it. The corpus goldens of the eleven legacy sidecars read Exposure 1.5, the newer-format fixture is 62, and the legacy fingerprints of the 29 cases off Lighting's rest are format 61's.

title: Lighting on the negative proven on every pipe
detail: tests/lighting_on_negative.rs: every pipe at Lighting's rest folds to the bits of the build before it, a legacy print at its entry; Exposure ±1 on a scanned negative within ΔE 1.2 (median 0.2) of that negative shot a stop over, the enlarger's time 8 to 16 off; on a digital photo within ΔE 0.6 of the Film section's Exposure; colour lighter than the grey kept as the film keeps it; Contrast holding the grey's negative; the filters tinting with the grey's weight held; every print finite and monotone past the curves' ends; the GPU its reference. The kernel's own checks read back through the couplers and keep a channel's own move on its layer. Tests whose subject left (the exposure gear, Contrast's and the points' saturation curves, colour compensation's answer to Lighting, the paper's grade and filtration) go; the others read Lighting on the negative.

title: Lighting on the negative reads each pipe's own neutral
detail: A digital photo's negative is the model's own: Lighting reads its dyes' amounts (ONI's print takes the dyes' pass untoned and the separation's tone after the moves) and develops them again on its virtual stock's three coupled layers, its Exposure within ΔE 0.5 of the Film section's. A scan's negative is not the model's: the couplers, read back, turned its small departures from the model's neutral into colour on every move. It is read on its stock's mean layer (the C-41 profiles' for the generic set), each channel scaled so the frame's reference grey sits on that layer at the speed's exposure, ONI's print reading the density its windows read: every common move keeps the frame's neutral to the bit. Under the toe's foot a density takes the foot's move, less the nearer the fog, which no move leaves; over the shoulder the shoulder's; foot and shoulder lie where the curve rises 0.1 of density a log, a scan's hundredth of grain then reading within a tenth of a log.

title: Every film stock is its maker's data sheet: spektrafilm's sixteen profiles retired
detail: Owner's call: each of the sixteen spektrafilm stocks (Portra 160, 400, 800 and its two pushes, Ektar 100, Gold 200, UltraMax 400, Verita 200D, Vision3 50D, 200T, 250D and 500T, C200, Pro 400H, Superia X-TRA 400) is replaced by its data-sheet twin, which takes the stock's plain name and key; the twins' keys and the '· Datasheet' labels go. Every use reads the data sheet: a roll's per-stock dye separation (each line and CineStill 50D and 800T on the matching profile), a digital photo's virtual film (Portra 800 by default), a slide's internegative (Vision3 50D), the Frontier's dye amounts, and the generic C-41 set (the mean of the same nine still stocks, now their sheets'). The profile names lose their datasheet/ prefix; spektrafilm's film profiles, Kodachrome 64's, which nothing read, included, are deleted. Renders move on purpose.

title: Every paper is its maker's data sheet: spektrafilm's five papers retired, Endura Premier by default
detail: Portra Endura, Supra Endura, Ultra Endura and spektrafilm's Endura Premier read as the data sheet's Kodak Endura Premier, now the default paper (the paper Kodak folded the three Endura papers into, its professional line's own), under the plain key kodak-endura-premier; Crystal Archive Type II reads as Crystal Archive Digital Type DP II, the digital paper of its line. The paper bake keeps sampled curves alone (spektrafilm's fitted model goes). The Frontier SP-3000 rests on its own measured table (frontier.cube refitted by frontier_print_fit.py, its own virtual dyes), never on a spektrafilm paper: its fit does not move; what it reads, a frame's dye amounts, follows the stock's data-sheet dyes.

title: Format 60: a digital photo moves onto its stock's data-sheet reference, every retired key read as its successor
detail: crates/oni-settings/src/migrate/datasheet.rs: a digital photo before 60 on a stock spektrafilm profiled has its gains and its windows' ends moved from that profile's reference (kept for the sixteen stocks) onto the data sheet's, a value on the former landing on the new exactly and a hand's distance kept; a photo keyed as a twin (-datasheet) stood there already and moves nothing; every other setting stays. The steps before (formats 37 and 55) now lay the former reference, so a document crosses the move once. Every retired key reads by alias wherever a settings document is read (sidecars, presets, share codes, pastes): a stock's twin as its stock, the Endura papers and Radiance III as Endura Premier, Crystal Archive Type II as DP II; a roll marker's, a Prepare draft's or a frame's film stock key keyed as a twin reads as its stock's (film::stored_key). A build before 60 refuses the file as newer. Owner's files, read-only: of 161 digital photos on a film, 158 move (Portra 800 146, Gold 200 2, UltraMax 400 2, Verita 200D 2, Ektar 100, Portra 400, Vision3 50D, 200T, 250D and 500T one each), the two on twins (Portra 800, UltraMax 400) and the one on Superia Reala keep their gains; papers: 386 sidecars on Portra Endura (347 negatives, 38 slides, 1 black and white) and 157 digital move to Endura Premier, 1 on Endura Premier changes profile, 1 on Crystal Archive Type II moves to DP II; scanned frames' dye sets moving to their sheets: Gold 200 565, UltraMax 400 208, Portra 800 37, Superia X-TRA 400 40 (38 of them slides, which unmix none), the generic set on 787 negatives and black and white frames; presets: 1 Gold 200, 1 UltraMax 400, the rest generic; no roll marker names a twin.

title: The bake without spektrafilm's band-pass window and balance flag, every profile as printed
detail: Every profile is a data sheet's: its layers' levels as printed, which the bake now always balances on the grey, and no band-pass window (its parameters held it at exactly 1). film::profile drops both fields, bake::windowed_sensitivity becomes bake::sensitivity, scripts/datasheet-profiles.py writes neither, and the 48 film profiles are written again by it, their numbers unchanged to the bit.

title: The checks on the data-sheet stocks and papers, each re-derived with its twin
detail: Paper: each of the eight data-sheet papers prints Portra 800's dye amounts as a double-precision reading of its own profile file does (log exposure within 4.3e-7, density 3.3e-6, light 5.8e-6; twin: five CC more magenta), in place of spektrafilm's print, whose fixture keeps its lamp and dichroic filters alone. Virtual stocks: every stock's grey prints neutral (C*ab under 0.5) where a plain RAW prints one, its white within 0.06 stop of Portra 800's, its ramp's crossovers under a ceiling (C*ab 14, 4.5 in the lights; widest 13.1 on Vision3 500T, 4.1 on Verita 200D; twin: the red gain a fifth of a stop off prints the grey at C*ab 2 or more); the GPU within the same ceiling (13.5 at most; twin at the other light 69.6 at least). The virtual negative within 0.015 of its reference on the locus for every stock (0.0142 on 500T). The dye sets' pinned fingerprints re-derived; the data-sheet smoke checks on every stock and paper; the corpus's two format 37 digital goldens moved by the new reference, the newer-file fixture at 61; settings checks for every retired key and its twin. Elsewhere, re-derived on the data-sheet stocks and Endura Premier, each bound at its measure: the print folds pinned to the bit (colour compensation, paper Lighting, paper points, the legacy prints' 50 cases, every colour one moving and every black and white and slide one keeping its bits); a format 41 digital photo's Exposure gear on its former reference; the grain's low mids a stop under the grey (Endura Premier prints its fullest there); on a paper a channel's own tone leads by 1.4 (1.49 for green's contrast); Brightness under a straight fade by 0.02 (0.027), 0.4 brightening and 0.8 darkening at most (0.38, 0.76), ten greys past the reach; a white point read at 0.6 of the range (Endura Premier prints black and white's 0.7 on its white); the pick's Dmax twin at 1e-4 (9e-4 measured); a slide's neutral scale neutral from its grey to its bare film within 0.08, its shadows under 0.6 (0.57 in Vision3 50D's toe), its Saturation twin at -0.7.

title: What ONI keeps from spektrafilm, credited
detail: resources/film/CHANGELOG.txt lists what remains: the spectra table, Schott KG3's curve, spektrafilm's model in ONI's own bake, and the former references the migration keeps (derived from its profiles, so SPEKTRAFILM_LICENSE.txt stays). SOURCES.txt, README, CLAUDE.md (every stock and paper a data sheet; spektrafilm's chain a benchmark outside the app on its own profiles) and the pipeline map follow; Settings' credits name the data sheets and spektrafilm's model, in French and Spanish too; the twin label's translations go.

title: The enlarger's rest found on a steep paper: the time bracketed first, every Newton step damped
detail: On the data-sheet dyes the rest solve lost the Frontier SP-3000 (Portra 800's digital grey printed at 0.975, its filtration stuck at M10 Y50) and Fujiclear: from the time's guess a full Newton step crossed the root onto the paper's flat white, where no step returns. crates/oni-pipeline/src/paper/printing.rs: the time is first bisected about its guess (10 in ln either way, more light always printing darker), then each Newton step is shortened whole within its bounds, keeping its direction, and halved until it lowers the miss (squared, or absolute for the time alone), the solve stopping where none does. Every stock now rests on every paper within 2e-5 of a plain RAW's grey but Fujiclear (a display material, three stocks off) and Fujifilm Pro 160C on Ektacolor Edge and Royal Digital (2e-3: its layers want a cyan filtration no pack holds); checked in tests/paper.rs with its twin.

title: The Look Lab's neutral set refitted to Pro on the data-sheet dyes
detail: examples/look_lab_fit run again: resources/scanner/lab.json's neutral set against Pro at rest median ΔE 0.561 (0.55 on spektrafilm's dyes, its bound 0.6), its Frontier set unchanged to the bit (it fits the cube alone).

title: The Colour tab's paper drops the stocks' menu, each paper it lights shown on the photo unwritten
detail: crates/oni-ui/ui/panel/color_tab.slint (PaperPicker), panel/state.slint, ds/stocks.slint, crates/oni-app/src/app/stock_picker.rs, stocks.rs papers_by_maker. The paper's field drops the film's StockMenu under it, the papers of the catalogue by maker (a paper's trade name leads with its maker's), the one in use checked; a line without a canister takes no icon room. The line under the pointer or the arrows is lit and told at once: the stocks' light becomes one `Lit` (a stock or a paper) in `State.lit`, laid over the settings by `previewed`, so the canvas renders it through the one render path (one in flight, the latest waiting) with no write, no step and no sidecar. Leaving the menu, Escape or any close lights none. A click or Return writes the paper as one step through `menu_picked`, which writes `Lit::picked`, the function the light shows, so a pick renders nothing again; a paper changes the one the enlarger prints on and never turns the enlarger on, so a light outliving its section shows nothing. The paper menu's lines are laid at each drop (`paper-dropping`), no longer at each publish.

title: The papers are baked off the interface thread at the menu's first light, never at launch
detail: crates/oni-app/src/app/stock_picker.rs bake_menu: the stocks' bake ahead takes the lit menu's lines, every paper of the catalogue printed on the open photo's settings for the papers' menu, once a drop; oni_pipeline::bake_ahead bakes each paper's enlarger (OnceLock, a table already baked costs nothing).

title: The papers' menu checked under the pointer, the arrows, Escape, a click and Return, with no write while lit
detail: crates/oni-app/tests/window/paper_menu.rs a_paper_under_the_pointer_shows_on_the_photo_unwritten, on a digital photo printed on its paper at rest, the papers read from the catalogue so its contents may change: every paper listed once under its maker, the one in use checked (twin: a maker's line names no paper, each maker once); the pointer on a line renders it, store, Undo and sidecar unchanged; another line follows; leaving the menu and Escape restore; the arrows toward the longer side and back light the paper beside the one in use, Return writes it as one step, Undo; a click writes as the light showed, its render the light's alone, Undo (twins: the preview differs from the photo's own; a pick does write the sidecar). tests/window/paper.rs reads the menu's lines as it drops. Unit checks: stocks::the_papers_are_listed_once_each_under_its_maker (twin: grouped by another word, more lines than makers) and stock_picker::a_photo_lit_on_a_paper_is_what_its_pick_writes (twin: the lit paper moves the photo).

title: ONI_BENCH=papers: each paper lit timed to its photon, cold, warm and in a sweep
detail: crates/oni-app/src/bench/stocks.rs: the stocks' bench takes the menu it lights (`Lights`), the papers' laid by `paper-dropping` and lit by `paper-lit`; a photo printing on no paper says so.
outcome: App profile, 2560×1440 window on the 5K screen, mains power, machine loaded by two other agents' builds (load 5 to 7): on a 47 Mpx Lumix RW2 shot digital on Portra 800 and Portra Endura, the 13 other papers each moving the photo, hover to photon p50 62 ms warm (p90 65, worst 68), cold p50 47 ms (first light 36 ms, the bake ahead absorbing it): 2.2 ms to the encode, 3.5 ms to the next frame, 55 ms the frame's GPU work; a 120 Hz sweep over 13 lines rendered 3 times, its last shown in 56 ms. The stocks' menu on the same photo, run just before: warm p50 57 ms, cold p50 62 ms, 63 films.

title: Kodak Royal Digital is the default paper
detail: Owner's call: PaperStock's default moves from Endura Premier (green 10-90 % range 0.61 log H, slope 4.37) to Royal Digital (0.86, 3.18), Kodak's softest data-sheet paper, nearest the former Portra Endura (0.96, 2.49). Every default use follows by itself: a digital photo's rest, Prepare the Roll and the enlarger's switch (fitting_paper), a slide's paper. The retired keys of the former defaults, kodak-portra-endura and Radiance III's, now read as Royal Digital, so a photo left on the default stays on it: of the owner's sidecars (read-only), 386 scans and 157 digital photos on Portra Endura land on Royal Digital; Supra, Ultra and spektrafilm's Endura Premier stay on Endura Premier (the one sidecar naming kodak-endura-premier, of format 58, keeps it). No format change: the key a file stores is read anew. CLAUDE.md names the new default.
outcome: Renders on the default paper move on purpose; the owner judges Royal Digital on the reference roll.

title: The checks on the default paper re-derived on Royal Digital, each with its twin
detail: paper.rs: the default is kodak-royal-digital, its twin Endura Premier's key another paper; Portra Endura's and Radiance III's keys read as the default and never Endura Premier, Supra, Ultra and the former datasheet key as Endura Premier. Tests that used Royal Digital as a chosen, non-default paper (paperless, one_face, migrate::paper, slide_paper) take Ektacolor Edge so a fall back to the default still fails them; the GPU paper frames print the black and white frame on Endura Premier so every paper stays covered. Format 46's legacy fingerprints: the two cases on Portra Endura (oni-digital-on-paper, oni-paper-keys-temp) re-drawn on Royal Digital, every other case to the bit. Virtual stocks on the default paper: widest C*ab 13.4 on Pro 160NH (CPU and GPU, ceiling 14 kept), lights' 4.7 on Verita 200D, its bound 4.5 raised to 5.0; the window checks' paper switch takes Royal Digital.

title: Black and white negatives' profiles from their makers' data sheets
detail: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py writes 27 black and white negatives (Foma 8, Fujifilm 4, Ilford 9, Kodak 6) into resources/film/datasheet/: one layer's log sensitivity as printed (Kodak's 0.3 criterion; Ilford's and Foma's wedge heights read as log, one axis unit a log; Tri-X 320's taken from Tri-X 400, same sheet), its visual density curve less base and fog, smoothed over 0.05 log H (raster traces climb in pixel steps), on log H less the grey's. Development: the sheet's reference developer (D-76 where printed, else the sheet's own) at the time whose ISO 6 average gradient is nearest 0.62, among the curves traced from their foot; grey 1.01 log over its ISO 6 speed point (ISO 6 speed and ISO 2720's meter), which holds on a relative axis; checked on the absolute sheets against the box speed within about 0.1 log. Every other development kept in `developments`, unread (developer choice to come). Left out: ADOX HR-50 (no log exposure scale), Neopan SS (toe untraced, a 0.13 D jump), Rollei's 8 (no curve).
outcome: Colour profiles written unchanged.

title: A black and white virtual negative: the colour kernel on one layer, neutral silver
detail: film.rs bakes a silver stock as the colour negative's sibling: profile::Silver read, its layer on the three channels of the light table (balanced to a grey), its curve before and after with no coupler, the silver neutral in one scanned band carrying the camera's whole D50 weight, each channel a third of its density. The kernel, its WGSL and CPU reference are unchanged; on_reference reads a silver stock as a monochrome roll. Every reference derived: stops 0, black and white neutral.

title: A digital photo on a black and white film is read as a monochrome roll
detail: PipelineSettings::is_monochrome (mode Monochrome, or a digital photo's film silver) replaces mode.is_monochrome in every settings-based branch: stage 4-7, decompression, separation, the paper's Film::Silver enlarger and its time-only rest, finishing's luma, colour compensation, knob ranges, the balance's filters, the panel's mono levels and separation key, the link. The mode stays Digital (set by hand only). Switching back to a colour stock restores colour: on_stock writes gains, windows, dyes and the stock, nothing else holds the state.

title: 27 black and white virtual films in the stock menu, each on its roll stock
detail: VirtualStock gains 27 silver stocks (keys foma-fomapan-100 ... kodak-tri-x-400), each mapped to its catalogue stock: existing canisters for HP5, FP4, Delta 100/400/3200, Pan F, SFX, XP2, Ortho, Acros, Fomapan 200/400, Tri-X 400; 14 new catalogue stocks drawn with the generic black and white canister until their SVG arrives (foma-fomapan100, foma-fomapan-cine100, foma-fomapan-cine400, foma-ortho400, foma-cine-ortho400, foma-retropan320, fujifilm-neopan400, fujifilm-neopan1600, fujifilm-neopan-ortho, kodak-320txp, kodak-tmax100, kodak-tmax400, kodak-tmax-p3200, kodak-double-x). A silver stock rests on the generic dye set, as a black and white roll does.

title: Format 56's own-film catch-up ignores the black and white films
detail: own_film::caught_up matched a photo against every stock's gains and dyes; a silver stock's neutral gains on the generic set would have moved an older hand-made state. Silver stocks, absent then, are left out; twin in its test.

title: The black and white virtual negative's checks, each with its twin
detail: tests/virtual_silver.rs: every scan neutral (twin Portra's mask); ortho vs pan on sRGB red at a grey's luma: ortho at least 0.35 D thinner, prints under 0.2 of the grey (0.14-0.18), pan at most 0.15 thinner and over 0.7 (twin Ortho Plus against HP5); monotone ramp over 20 stops, rising across the grey's 3 stops (twin a dipped curve); GPU against CPU on Ortho Plus and Tri-X 400 (twins exposure 1 % and another film's layer); a digital photo on HP5 is its scan read as a monochrome roll pixel for pixel, paper and paperless (twin read as a colour negative), back on Portra prints colour. virtual_film.rs, virtual_stocks.rs, datasheet_stocks.rs, settings tests take the silver stocks.

title: Window check: a black and white film lit and picked in the stock menu
detail: tests/window/bw_film.rs: on a digital photo, HP5 then Ortho Plus under the pointer show the canvas grey, nothing written, the ortho reds darker; Escape the colour film again; a click writes HP5 with its canister, one Undo takes Portra back, colour again.

title: Lighting on a black and white virtual film develops its own curve
detail: negative::Film::of takes a digital photo's stock before the monochrome roll's C-41 mean, so a photo on a black and white film is Film::Stock: its development is its own profile's curve on one layer, uncoupled, scale 1 (its density is its curve's), and the kernel's mono branches read PipelineSettings::is_monochrome. A scanned black and white roll keeps the mean. Check in virtual_silver.rs: HP5's development within 0.004 of its sheet (the least slope lifting its foot), the mean 0.235 off; Contrast holds the grey, a filter tints nothing, Exposure moves it (twin).

title: Why the renders turned too contrasty: the system's tone response measured brick by brick, and two construction errors found
detail: crates/oni-app/examples/tone_response.rs renders synthetic neutral ramps (-8 to +6 stops by 1/4) and a chart through the engine in every pipe (a digital photo on paper, on ONI's print and on the neutral paper; a scan's ramp, its stock's mean layer read through the frame's own measure, on each; a slide through its internegative given its curve), traces the paper's received log exposure per layer on the CPU references, and reads each file's L* spread. Run on 44fcc040 (spektrafilm films and papers, each data-sheet twin swapped in one brick at a time) and on 26114d09, on copies of DSC_6440, DSC_6452, DSC_6464, two digital photos and one slide, and with throwaway unmixed profiles never committed.
outcome: Digital photo on Portra 800, grey printed at L* 69, slope L*/stop at the grey / mean over -3..-1 / mean over +1..+3, L* at -3 stops, print density gamma over -3..-1: spektrafilm film and Portra Endura 15.4 / 19.2 / 4.9, 12.9, 1.83; data-sheet film alone 17.8 / 19.6 / 4.3, 9.2, 2.03; Royal Digital alone 17.7 / 20.7 / 3.7, 6.7, 2.26; data-sheet film and Endura Premier (91524013) 23.4 / 19.2 / 2.4, 1.3, 3.14; data-sheet film and Royal Digital (4db46ef4 and 26114d09, equal to 0.02 L*: Lighting on the negative moves nothing at rest and at most 0.3 L* of a filtered frame's percentiles) 20.3 / 20.3 / 2.9, 4.1, 2.50; ONI's print 10.1 / 16.6 / 6.2, 24.8, 1.29. Two errors: every data-sheet profile, film and paper, takes its Status M or Status A curves (a neutral's integral densities, each dye's unwanted absorptions in them) as the dyes' amounts, so a neutral reads 8-25 % denser on a film (green 1.17-1.25) and 10-31 % on a paper than its sheet prints: the negative hands the paper 1.2 times its log exposure range (0.644 against the sheet's 0.53 a log on green) and the print's densities rise again by as much. The curves unmixed through each dye's own Status band (throwaway): 16.9 / 19.7 / 3.8, 10.0, 2.00, the data-sheet film then printing as spektrafilm's did; with Paper blacks on 15.2 at -3 stops, 1.63. The rest is true physics: Royal Digital's sheet is steeper than spektrafilm's Portra Endura (10-90 % 0.87 against 0.97 log H); the enlarger's rest puts the grey on the paper's 10 % point, its toe, so the highlights clip from +2.5 stops; True blacks lays the paper's own black on pure black. Film stocks: every stock's +-4 stops lands inside its drawn curve (Portra 800 Push 2 under its toe at -4), the grey 1.03 log over each sheet's own speed point whatever the axis' origin (Fujifilm's sheets print relative axes, implied ISO 0.2 to 4.8 times the nominal, harmless), 25 Fujifilm sheets end on the slope at +1.5 to +1.7 log and are held flat there, a hard clip 5 to 5.6 stops over the grey.

title: Lighting's Exposure rests at 0 EV in every pipe: the slider is the departure from the pipe's rest
detail: Print.exposure is stops of light off the frame's pipe's rest, 0 on a negative, a slide, black and white and a digital photo alike. Print::RESTING_EXPOSURE, resting_exposure(mode), exposure_at, curve_stops, on_curve and EXPOSURE_GEAR go, with every conversion they fed: PipelineSettings::rest lays no Exposure, a mode change carries none, Print::unlit and rests_on_negative take no mode, Lighting on the negative takes the stored value as its stops, a slide's internegative takes the slide's Lighting whole, the grain's tones, the filter balance's press and the paper's rests read Print::default(). ONI's print curve keeps its own rest inside the pipeline (conversion::NEGATIVE_PRINT_STOPS, 1.5 on a negative, none on a slide; a legacy print's machine entry 1.5 under it). The reset, the tick, the double click, the ± keys, the value editor, presets and the phone's steps all read the rest, so 0.00 EV at rest everywhere; the welcome scenes show 0.00 EV. Exposure's track stays ±4 EV, now about the rest.

title: Sidecar format 64: every stored Exposure becomes its departure from its mode's former rest
detail: migrate::departure: a document before 64 (sidecar, preset, share code, paste) has its Exposure less its mode's former rest (a negative's 1.5, a slide's 0), after every older step, which keeps its own format's units on that former rest (the gear of 42, the Scanner face's entry of 46, the legacy print's of 61, the digital film of 38). reshape::as_stored and departure::stored_at write an older document in its era's units for the checks; departure::read_back reads what the Exposure steps make of it. The newer-file fixture is 65.

title: Exposure at 0 proven: every pipe renders to the bit across format 64
detail: tests/exposure_departure.rs: twelve pipes (ONI's print on a negative, with Contrast, a legacy Frontier, digital, black and white, a slide; the paper on a negative, digital, black and white, the Frontier, the neutral paper, a slide through its internegative) stored as format 61 at the former rest and ±0.5/−0.75 off it fold to the bits format 61 printed, stage 4-7 on the CPU and the whole chain on Metal; twin: read unmigrated they move. Each stored Exposure reads as its departure (+1.5 → 0, a slide's 0 stays). A negative at Exposure 0 prints its reference grey at a plain RAW's on ONI's print, the paper and the neutral paper; twin: the former rest's 0 prints it far darker. A slide through its internegative at a value f32 rounds on the former 1.5 (+0.6) prints within 4.2e-7 of format 61, which took that rounding. legacy_print's fingerprints (every corpus sidecar and Scanner case, CPU and GPU) and lighting_on_negative's fold hold unchanged. Window check slider_rest: Exposure reads 0.00 EV on its mid-track tick at rest and after Lighting's Reset, on a negative and a slide.

title: The tone response example in a folder of its own, on Exposure's rest at 0
detail: Merged after exposure-zero, examples/tone_response.rs still called Print::resting_exposure and ran 462 lines with two lines past 200 characters. Its pixel helpers move to tone_response/image.rs, the two format strings break with a continuation, and its rest Lighting takes Exposure 0, the rest of every pipe.

title: Every colour data-sheet profile develops its dyes' amounts, its sheet's Status M or Status A curves unmixed
detail: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py: a sheet's characteristic curves are a neutral's integral densities, each dye's unwanted absorptions in them, and were taken as the dyes' amounts, so a grey developed 8-25 % denser on a film and 10-31 % on a paper than its sheet prints (#3540). At each node the amounts are now solved (Newton on the band integrals) whose spectral density over the base reads the sheet's curves less D-min through ISO 5-3's Status M (films) or Status A (papers) spectral products, transcribed from ANSI/ISO 5-3-1995 tables 3 and 4, which replace the normal-band approximation in the dyes' unit too (each dye scaled until its own channel reads exactly 1). A paper's base is its dyes in the amounts that read the curves' least densities, solved the same way. Each colour profile keeps the sheet's curves as sheet_density_curves; the 27 black and white profiles, one silver layer, are unchanged to the byte. No migration: renders move on purpose (owner's call). Check: datasheet_stocks, each of the 48 films' and 8 papers' neutral reads its sheet within 0.02 D (1e-4 on most; the traces' small disagreements on a shoulder draw dips the converter holds, as an amount never falls, Fujiclear's at D 2.8 the widest), its twin (the printed curves as amounts) missing by 0.31 D or more.
outcome: tone_response on copies (B = canvas fe8b869e, A = this branch): digital Portra 800 on Royal Digital, shadow print-density gamma over -3..-1 stops 2.50 -> 2.00, L* at -3 stops 4.1 -> 9.7, at -2 19.1 -> 26.3, highlights flat from +2.50 -> +3.00 stops, paper white L* 90.7 -> 92.2, grey held at L* 69.3; with Paper blacks 2.12 -> 1.60, L* -3 6.9 -> 15.4. Scan DSC_6440's ramp on Royal Digital 2.41 -> 2.17, L* -3 4.6 -> 6.5, flat from +2.50 -> +2.75; on the neutral paper 1.12 -> 1.11; ONI's print unchanged (a scan's render within 1/255, the separation's dye units alone moving). Black and white profiles unchanged to the byte (one silver layer: nothing to unmix). Owner's sidecars (read-only scan, 1834): 161 digital photos move (format 66 moves their reference), 428 negatives, 38 black and white and 38 slides on a data-sheet paper move, 35 negatives on the Frontier move by the separation's dye units alone (its fingerprints moved, the size not measured), 599 negatives on ONI's print within 1/255, 500 black and white and 35 slides on ONI's print unchanged.

title: Sidecar format 66: a digital photo's gains and windows move onto its stock's reference of the unmixed curves
detail: migrate::unmixed: a document before 66 on a colour virtual film has its gains and windows moved from the reference formats 60 to 65 derived (MIXED, its 48 colour stocks) onto the stock's new one, each hand's distance from it kept, as format 60's move did; datasheet::caught_up now lands a pre-60 document on that mixed reference, so every older document moves once per step. A black and white film, a scan and a file of this format stay as they are. Renders move on purpose: no migration keeps the old contrast (owner's call). The newer-format fixture is 67.

title: The checks re-derived on the unmixed profiles
detail: Every stock's StockReference re-derived (48 colour stocks moved, the 27 black and white unchanged); pinned folds and fingerprints re-drawn (dye separation, exposure departure CPU and GPU, Lighting at rest, legacy_print 42 of 50 cases, the 8 unchanged its monochrome and slide ones; corpus goldens of the two digital photos). Ceilings re-read on the printed numbers, the owner judging them: virtual stocks' widest ramp chroma 10.9 (Pro 800, ceiling 14 to 12), lights' 5.4 (Verita 200D, 5.0 to 6.0), the GPU twin at the other light 44.8 at least (3.5 times the ceiling, was 4), a silver film's Lighting twin 5 grey gaps (was 10, the paper softer); a slide's grey through its internegative within 1.5 % (1.3 %, was 1 %); a scan's lights brightened on the negative keep 85 % of the time's chroma (86.4 %, was 88 %). A silver scan's Lighting reads the C-41 sheets' own curves (sheet_density_curves, now in Profile), a density, as before: black and white renders unchanged.

title: tone_response split into its parts, under the source ceiling and the width
detail: examples/tone_response/ (main, patches, curve): the example was 462 lines with two lines past 200 characters, failing the architecture check; a scan's ramp reads the stock's sheet curves, the density a scanner sees, not the dyes' amounts.

title: Two data-sheet limits left as printed: Fujifilm's curves ending on the slope, Portra 800 Push 2's toe
detail: Measured on the profiles, nothing changed. 25 Fujifilm sheets print their curves to +1.5..+1.7 log over the grey (Pro 800 +1.27), still rising at 0.4-0.85 a log, and the converter holds them flat past it: a hard clip 5 to 5.6 stops over the grey, under Royal Digital's own (+3 stops) but reached on ONI's print, the neutral paper and with Exposure on the negative. Portra 800 Push 2's chart starts at -4.85 stops; at -4 its layers stand 0.015-0.025 over D-min at a slope of 0.05-0.09 (Portra 800 0.09 and 0.29-0.37), the push's real loss of shadow speed.
outcome: Options for the owner: Fujifilm, keep the hold (honest, a clip only far over), extend each layer at its last slope to a ceiling (inferred, unbounded guess), or graft a measured Kodak shoulder matched in slope (inferred, labelled so in the profile); Push 2, keep (the sheet's physics), or re-check that Kodak plots its push curves on the normal exposure axis, the one thing that could double the 0.6 log offset.

title: Saturation on the negative: the layers spread about their neutral, the paper bounding every colour
detail: Negative::coloured_on (CPU reference) and wgsl/negative_colour.wgsl: each layer's density, Lighting's moves and filters laid, is read as the log exposure a grey develops it at (Development::as_grey, equal on the three layers where they print a neutral); Saturation spreads its chroma about the luma-weighted neutral by 2^travel, the scene's luminance held, then it is read back (from_grey) and developed. Stage47's and the paper's print-side colour density are gone, so the print, ONI's or a paper, bounds every colour. Hunt's colour stays on ONI's print. Black and white takes none. A slide on a paper carries it to its internegative.
outcome: 0 changes nothing to the bit (every pipe, Lighting at rest or moved, CPU fold and the GPU folds of exposure_departure and legacy_print). Mean Oklab chroma of 144 colour patches at -100/-50/0/+50/+100 % against the former print-side Saturation: ONI's print digital 0.100 0.132 0.164 0.191 0.207 (0.110 0.136 0.164 0.193 0.217), paper digital 0.049 0.068 0.092 0.114 0.130 (0.051 0.070 0.092 0.118 0.146); at +100 % the former Saturation laid colours 0.6 to 5.0 of density past Endura's dyes, now none.

title: Colour Mixer on the negative: hue, saturation and luma per hue range on the grey-equivalent exposures
detail: The eight bands' hue, weights and doses read on the negative's chroma (log exposure), faded in over PRESENCE = 0.1 log; the turn about the grey axis, the boost and the luma's lift in stops (LUMA_STOPS 2) laid there, the luminance held before the lift. The print-side spectrogram pass, its WGSL and CPU reference are removed.
outcome: A Blue move changes Blue's range only: every other colour and grey within 2e-5 on eight pipes; its twin (Aqua) reaches past it. On the strips a cast no longer counts as a colour, so a blue move turns the blues, not a cyan-cast wall.

title: Saturation Curve on the negative, read on the print's own lightness of a grey
detail: The curve spreads the negative's chroma by the spline at x, the print's luma on a display gamma of a neutral at the pixel's neutral exposure: a 128-node table (LIGHTNESS, -4..+4 log about the reference grey) baked per frame by conversion::printed on the frame's print without the curve (a grey takes no colour tool), so x is the histogram's axis.
outcome: A grey's x within 6e-3 of its print's (1.1e-2 for a slide's internegative), twin two nodes off 6e-2 or more; greyer shadows keep 0.26-0.52 of their chroma, the highlights 0.99-1.01.

title: Lighting alone keeps its own shader: the colour tools a second variant of the negative's pass
detail: wgsl::NEGATIVE (negative.wgsl + negative_plain.wgsl, negative_scene the identity) and NEGATIVE_COLOURED (+ negative_colour.wgsl), chosen by Negative::colours(): any colour code in the one shader moved Metal's bits on Lighting-only renders.
outcome: exposure_departure's GPU fold unchanged to the bit.

title: Colour tools on the negative: rest to the bit, the paper's gamut, a band alone, the curve's lightness, ramps, black and white, GPU
detail: oni-pipeline/tests/colour_on_negative.rs (+ colour_on_negative/scenes.rs), kernel tests in kernel/negative/tests.rs; each with its twin. Fixtures moved by the owner's call: legacy_print's 7 documents with Saturation off rest redrawn, lighting_on_negative's rest fold re-derived on the base code with Saturation at rest, paper_ends' pick check (nothing lifts the unanchored pick now; twin the enlarger's time), kernel_oracle judged at Saturation's rest.
outcome: Colour ramps up to one stop over the grey stay monotone within 5e-3 under Saturation, the mixer and a moderate curve; a curve swinging 0 to 1.8 within a fifth of the lightness, or everything with Lighting, turns a strong colour's ramp back by up to 2.4e-2 on a paper (its dyes darken a strong colour more than a grey of its luminance).

title: The owner's sidecars per colour tool, read only
detail: Every ONI sidecar under /Volumes/T7/Scans, /Volumes/T7/Photos Digitales, the reference roll and its test copy.
outcome: Scans: 1672 sidecars (538 black and white), 129 colour photos with Saturation off rest (-0.57 to +1.0), none with the mixer or the curve. Digital photos: 162, 1 with Saturation (+0.07). Roll #8 and its copy: none. These 130 move.

title: Saturation's and the Colour Mixer's help say they act on the negative
detail: color_tab.slint, French and Spanish written.

title: Prepare's window read on the dye layers (CMY) before the paper: measured on prototypes, a design for the owner
detail: docs/research/cmy-window.md. Throwaway prototypes laid a per-layer window in the dye separation's tone table between the separation and the paper (roll #8 DSC_6440/6452/6464 and the digital ramp, Royal Digital, Endura Premier, the Frontier; examples/tone_response). Prepare's ends on the paper's ends cut mid contrast 8 to 35 % and squeeze the highlights (L* at +2: 77 against 89); the bare film on the paper's black in exposure adds 49 % of mid contrast; the window at the enlarger's rest (each layer read about its grey, bare film, grey and densest on one mean amount, the paper's neutral axis) keeps today's tone within 1 L* and cuts the grey ramp's channel spread 4 to 17 times on a scan. Design: levels on a dye-amount axis measured by Prepare's unchanged roll code with the separation on, laid after Lighting in the Negative's per-layer table, rest at the enlarger's grade; the enlarger a constant per paper, the black anchor Print lift's presentation step; migration by separation::toned's carriage, edited photos on a legacy flag. Nothing of the app changed.
outcome: Awaits the owner's decision; images kept outside the repository (roll #8 not publishable).

title: Print lift: off lays a paper's white on pure white with its black, the rest showing the grey where a plain RAW does
