detail: The paper kernel (CPU reference and WGSL) lays the paper's white on its own anchor beside the pick's: off, the pick on 0 and the white on 1 by one straight line in light, to the bit; on, both the paper's own, every bit as before. The enlarger's rest is solved on the print as shown, through its ends, so the reference grey stays at a plain RAW's grey, neutral, once the white is lifted; its time is bracketed on the print before its ends, where pure ends read the pick and the grey both at the paper's white. The neutral paper's ends are pure already (its white 1.0, its pick laid on black whatever the switch), so Print lift means nothing there and stays hidden, as on ONI's print.
outcome: Measured on Royal Digital at the former rest, the grey moves +0.28 to +0.29 stop laid in light and +0.24 to +0.25 in density (the Frontier, its white at 0.98: +0.016 and +0.010), so neither keeps it: the rest takes the ends instead, the time 0.13 stop longer on a digital photo and its filtration 1.6 M and 0.6 Y lighter, the paper base's tint no longer seen; the line in light, the black's own form, keeps ratios. Checks: kernel pure ends and twins, pipeline pick 0 and white 1 under every Lighting slider, grey within 2e-6 of a plain RAW's, Print lift's ends the paper's, the GPU on every branch; the format 61 and Lighting-at-rest folds re-derived (the neutral paper and an off slide among their pipes).

title: Sidecar format 67: Paper blacks stored as printLift, every older document read as it printed or with its white lifted
detail: The field `print.paper_blacks` becomes `print.print_lift`, stored `printLift`. A document of format 53 to 66 reads its `paperBlacks` as Print lift: on keeps its render to the bit, off gains the white end (the owner's request); before 53 True blacks is read as before. The corpus's newer file moves to 68.
outcome: Read-only scan of the owner's 1833 sidecars (all format 66): 699 print on a paper, 134 with Paper blacks on (Scans) keep their render, 565 with it off (404 Scans, 161 Photos Digitales) gain the white on pure white; 1134 on ONI's print and none on the neutral paper are untouched.

title: The Paper section's switch is Print lift, its help in two sentences, translated
detail: Label Print lift; help: on, the print keeps the paper's own ends; off, its black lies on pure black and its white on pure white, the grey kept. French 'Noirs et blancs du papier', Spanish 'Negros y blancos del papel': 'lift' has no settled photographic word in either language outside grading software, and the former labels already named what the switch keeps. The window check toggles it both ways, each a render and the second its own histogram.
outcome: Window check, catalogue check and lint green.

title: The spill a masked negative leaves on a camera scan after per-channel windows, and one generic 3x3 against it
detail: docs/research/dye-spill.md, scripts in docs/research/dye-spill/. Each stock's dyes read as window shares (rows summing to 1) on Status M, the scan's Rec. 2020 and drawn cameras, for the 48 data-sheet profiles and spektrafilm's former ones; real scans bound each layer's purity from pictures (five rolls, 86 frames). Proposal: one generic spill as shares in the stock file with a dose, off by default, laid as I + dose x (inverse - I) on the window shares. No product code changed.
outcome: The mask leaves 3 to 7 % of spill on Status M and 19 to 33 % on a camera's channels (overlap, not mask). Real frames (a red-lit column, a blue-green tank, UltraMax 400) cap cyan in green at 0.20 and magenta in red at 0.13 per unit: both models overstate the largest term by two. Proposed shares R 0.88 0.12 0.00, G 0.16 0.80 0.04, B 0.09 0.06 0.85. Awaits the owner's eye; images outside the repository.

title: dye_spill example: a scan on ONI's print with no separation, a 3x3 on the window shares, and the separation on former or current dyes
detail: crates/oni-pipeline/examples/dye_spill.rs, the CPU reference only: off, now (data-sheet dyes), old (a former spektrafilm profile read from a path), each named matrix, and the density over the bare film that hull.py reads.
outcome: The former separation and the inverse of spektrafilm's mean spill render alike on nine frames: the separation was one 3x3 to first order.

title: The Kit's token read from the vault at its first use, on a thread of its own, never at launch
detail: The launch read the Keychain on the interface thread (Ctl::wire, wire_kit), and a new build's signature makes the Keychain ask the person first: the interface waited on that prompt and the window never settled. The vault (Keychain, Credential Manager, the simulated service's file) is now a trait behind one thread of its own that runs its calls in order, started at the first; no read, write or erase runs on the interface thread. Who is signed in at launch comes from a non-secret mark in the Kit's copy (kit.json, `signed`), written at sign-in and at a sign-out by the service, the file removed at the person's sign-out; a copy written before the mark presumes a token where it holds an account, which the first use settles. The token is read once, at the account's first use (the search sheet opening, Done, a removal, Disconnect), what waits on it running once it lands; the Kit is read again from the service then rather than at launch. A vault with no token turns the link out and marks the copy. Disconnect is out at once, the vault read on its thread only to revoke a token this run never read.
outcome: Window checks with a counting vault: the launch reads no vault and asks the service nothing; the search sheet reads it once, off the interface thread, and a search after reads nothing; sign-out erases once off the interface, sign-in writes once and marks the copy; a sign-out never read reads once to revoke. Twins: a read on the interface thread is counted as the interface's; the Kit never read on a lone sign-out. The copy's mark round trip and its older-copy reading in oni-tldb, each with its twin.

title: Every film stock and paper is one file: crates/oni-settings/stocks/<key>.json, read into a catalogue keyed by the keys sidecars store
detail: One JSON file a stock (identity, aliases, brand, type, ISO, canister, offered, line, dyes, the virtual film's key, light, dyes, reference and data-sheet profile, its pushes as developments, the generic C-41 set as a mean) and one a paper (a data sheet's profile, or the Frontier SP-3000's fit with its provenance), 111 in all, built into the binary by oni-settings' build script; the SVG canisters moved beside them. FILM_STOCKS, STOCK_DYE_SETS, the VirtualStock, DyeSet and PaperStock enums, entries.rs, datasheet.rs and the include_bytes profiles are gone: the three are key types (`of`, `key`, `all()`, `entry()`) read through `oni_settings::stocks::current()`, serialised as the same keys, retired keys read through each file's aliases. A key no file defines is kept as stored (a sidecar holding one no longer fails to read) and renders on the default stock, paper or generic set. The defaults stay the app's constants (Portra 800, Royal Digital, generic-c41): a photo storing none reads them, so no file may move them. The menus list stocks by generic first, brand, then name read as a person reads it (50D before 200T), papers by brand and name. Sidecar format unchanged.
outcome: Every shipped stock, dye set and paper renders bit for bit as before on the CPU and the GPU: 753 fingerprints (each film with and without the default paper, each dye set on every paper and none, silver and a slide on every paper, every catalogue line) equal before and after (examples/preset_fingerprints.rs).

title: The person's own stock files, in the support folder's Stocks, read at the shell's start and watched while the app runs
detail: oni_pipeline::stocks::Loader reads the folder (every .json a stock or a paper, every .svg a canister), checks each film's profile by baking it, derives a reference a file leaves out, and builds the catalogue: a file of the person's with a shipped key stands in for it and must keep every key the shipped one defined; one that does not read, clashes, names missing dyes or does not bake is refused with why, the version of it taken before staying in use. The app (app/stock_files.rs) reads it before any photo renders, then watches it (FSEvents, polling on Windows), and on a quiet burst installs the new catalogue on the interface thread: menus and the picker sheet laid again, any lit stock let go, the heroes and the open photo shown again; bakes are keyed by key and file content (baked.rs), so an edit bakes anew and a table lent to a kernel stays valid. Refusals are told once by file name, masked in the log; a missing key is shown as such in the film hero and the paper title. Generic stocks' names and brand are translated where shown, trade names never.
outcome: Proven by tests/stock_files.rs (add, derive, edit re-renders, broken edit told with the last version kept, removal) and the window check stock_files::a_stock_file_dropped_edited_and_removed_updates_the_menu_and_the_photo.

title: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py and frontier_print_fit.py write into the stock files
detail: The converter lays each profile into the file holding the profile of its name, every other field kept, and has the reference of a film whose profile moved derived again by examples/stock_references.rs; a profile no file holds yet gets a file of its own to check. The Frontier fit writes the SP-3000 paper file's frontier block, its provenance kept. The dye-spill research reads the profiles out of the stock files. stocks/README.md tells how to add or edit a stock or a paper without building the app.

title: Dye separation removed from both pipes
detail: The owner's call (2026-11-23): the film's orange mask already removes most spill on a white-light scan, and the data-sheet dyes carry no mask, so the separation over-corrected about three times. Gone: the kernel and its WGSL, its pass, Stage47.dyes, the settings `separation` and `separationByHand` (dropped at format 69; the old steps that moved their rests removed), its block, knob, field, demo, preset entry and phone row (the wire index kept). The stock (`dyeSet`) stays: Lighting reads a scan back through its curve.
outcome: ONI's print on roll #8 moves only by the separation: tone within 1 L* (mean dL* -0.8), mean chroma down a third (C* 13.5 to 8.6 on DSC_6440, mean dE76 5 to 8). Black and white and slides unchanged to the bit.

title: A digital photo's virtual negative codes each layer's density on its own channel
detail: No camera scan of the virtual dyes: each developed layer's density is read on its own channel, as a masked negative's scan reads it, so the print reads the film's own per-channel densities. Every stock's reference re-derived; a digital photo of formats 66 to 68 moves its gains and windows onto it, every hand's move kept (migrate::layer_densities, format 69).
outcome: Digital photos on ONI's print move by mean dE76 1.9; the stocks' references read a clear bare film on every channel.

title: The paper prints the window's shares: each channel's density exposes its own layer
detail: One window for both prints: stage 5 reads each channel's density through Prepare's window (black, white, mid); ONI's print takes its decompression and print curve on the shares, the paper lays the shares back on density (the windows' mean span, a power that sets the mean grey on its own density) and exposes the matching layer (red the cyan-forming), the Frontier's scanner matrix on the densities, a seat for a 3x3 later. The spectral negative, the TH-KG3 lamp, the dichroic filters and schott_kg3.csv are gone.
outcome: Kernel, WGSL and CPU reference with their checks; the neutral paper prints a frame exactly as ONI's print (DSC_6440 identical).

title: A neutral negative prints neutral: one filtration per paper, one time per frame; black and white alike
detail: The window aligns the three channels at black, grey and white; each paper's filtration is solved once on its own layers where they print a grey neutral on its white (one for Print lift, which shows that white), shown in the paper block; a frame's time shows its reference grey at a plain RAW's grey. Black and white takes the same filtration and prints its luma.
outcome: Grey ramps neutral on the paper's own white on every paper and stock (grey C*ab 0.0, Royal Digital's scan ramp spread 0.23 to 0.14); with Print lift the grey takes the paper's white, laid on pure white it is neutral within a thousandth. Black and white on Royal Digital goes from 18.6 to 32.3 L*/stop at the grey: balanced, its layers print the negative's own density, and its roll's window spans 2.37 of density against colour's 1.44.

title: Lighting re-seated on per-channel density
detail: The negative kernel reads each channel's density above its bare film and codes the result back on the bare film's own; the tone table is gone. A scan's channel reads back through its stock's mean layer curve, scaled so its reference grey lies on the curve's speed point; a digital photo through its stock's own three layers and couplers; black and white through the C-41 sheets' mean.
outcome: Lighting's and the colour tools' checks hold on every pipe.

title: Contrast before and after the density pipe
detail: tone_response on roll #8 (DSC_6440, 6452, 6464), a black and white roll (P1071630, 6135), a digital photo (P1073289) on Portra 800 and HP5, ONI's print and Royal Digital; logs in the scratch folder.
outcome: Royal Digital at the grey: scans 23.6 to 20.0 L*/stop, digital Portra 800 20.8 to 17.5, black and white 18.6 to 32.3, digital HP5 16.4 to 24.1; ONI's print unchanged (10.9, digital 10.2 to 10.6).

title: The Look Lab's neutral set fitted again to Pro at rest, the separation gone
detail: examples/look_lab_fit.rs run on the density pipe; the Frontier set's fit is unchanged.
outcome: Neutral set against Pro at rest: median dE 0.56 to 0.19 on 9948 negatives; the check's bound 0.3.

title: A .cube 3D LUT in the Stocks folder is a film of its own for digital photos: read through the cube in display sRGB in place of the virtual negative, printed on the paper through the internegative
detail: oni_settings::stocks::cube reads a .cube (size 2-128, domain 0-1, nodes red fastest) into a Look; the Stocks loader makes each one a film file on the default film's data under the key lut-<name>, brand LUT, offered to digital photos alone; the chain reads its scene through exposure, scanner_encode, color_cube and scanner_output, no scene white, then the internegative and the paper where one is laid (internegative::copy at unit light). No format change: the photo stores the film's key as before; a missing cube renders on the default film. ONI ships no look.
outcome: tests/looks.rs: a photo through its look against the kernels' references 1.95e-7 (twin 1.36e-1, the film's exposure left out); printed on its paper 5.97e-7 (twin 2.85e-1, no paper).

title: Portra 800, Portra 400 and UltraMax 400 develop through their own DIR coupler matrices, fitted on the reference charts of each stock
detail: A film block's optional couplers field (stock file and catalogue) is read by the bake (film::couplers, layers, derive) and by Lighting's development (negative::developing); a file without one reads the common matrix. The six cross terms of each matrix fitted by examples/coupler_fit.rs: a digital render's colour crosstalk (a colour against its channels each sent alone through the grey response, in Oklab) matched to the reference's on 88 chart colours, the diagonal and the data sheets' curves kept. The derived references move by 4e-5 at most, so no photo's gains or windows move.
outcome: Crosstalk error (Oklab² mean) common to fitted: Portra 800 0.00127 to 0.00038, Portra 400 0.00141 to 0.00035, UltraMax 400 0.00119 to 0.00031; implied interimage ratios 1.0-1.33, Kodak's band for negatives made to be scanned. tests/couplers.rs: grey 6.6e-6 apart, a red 0.26 (twin). Owner's verdict on the sheet: the fitted renders are the best.

title: C, M and Y are each band's filter alone, in stops either way on bipolar tracks; moved together they move the photograph's light
detail: Owner's call: in place of the enlarger's C, M and Y in CC from none (a view of Temperature and Tint), Knob::Filtration reads and writes one channel's filter in stops on Print::FILTER_RANGE, the same filters at the same place on the negative; Temperature and Tint keep reading their differences. The filters' shared move, which Temperature and Tint leave out, is told under Tint (Store.filters-shared). Readout::Cc and Print::filtration removed. No format change.
outcome: knob tests: one band moved leaves the others, the three a stop down move the mean a stop and leave Temperature and Tint (twin: Temperature shifts two bands).

title: Fifteen colour films develop through their own couplers fitted on the reference charts; a digital photo is offered a colour film only once its couplers are measured, and one on a film offered no more reads on the menu's first
detail: examples/coupler_fit.rs, now fitting from the common matrix and from no cross term and keeping the better, run on the reference charts of Fujicolor C200, Pro 400H, Superia 1600 and 200, Ektar 100, Gold 200, Portra 160, 160NC, 160VC, 400 and 800 (its pushes sharing its matrix), UltraMax 400 and Vision3 200T, 250D and 500T; references derived again (0.0011 at most). VirtualEntry::offered: a colour film holding its couplers, a black and white one or a look; the digital menus list those, and a photo on a film offered no more reads on the menu's first (PipelineSettings::on_offered_film at the sidecar's read; a key no file defines keeps its key). Vision3 50D keeps the common matrix: it is the slides' internegative, and its fitted one turned a slide's colour ramp back by 0.071 under the Red and Blue mixer (colour_on_negative). The neutral-ramp twin's bound lowered to 2.5 times the chroma, the weaker interimage tinting a mislit grey less (Portra 160 at 39.9).
outcome: Crosstalk error, common to fitted (Oklab² mean): from 0.0007-0.0030 to 0.00017-0.00063, every fit under both the common matrix and no cross term; implied interimage ratios 1.00-1.38.

title: A digital photo on a colour reversal film is projected: Velvia 50, Velvia 100 and Ektachrome E100 from their sheets, their slide's dyes filtering a 3200 K lamp on a white screen
detail: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py convert_slide: a reversal sheet's profile (Status A, curves held non-rising, the dyes unmixed from the densest end, the log H origin where green transmits an 18 % grey) laid as the virtual film of its stock file, dyes generic-c41; Provia 100F left out (its blue and green traces stop at log H -2.16 and -1.50). VirtualEntry::reversal; bake::curves_falling develops the couplers on the first developer's negative image; bake::folds and film::derive refuse a matrix folding a layer's curve. New kernel projection (oni-render, WGSL and scalar reference): the layers' amounts, the dyes and base over 81 bands, a 3200 K Planck lamp through the 1931 observer, Bradford-adapted to the bare film's light, Rec. 2020, a 0.5 % veil (film::projection). Pipeline::projected after the virtual negative; the positive shown as it is, or printed on a paper through the internegative; on_stock lays no paper on a slide and the default back after one. Couplers fitted on the reference charts (coupler_fit, the diagonal left out on a slide, folding refused). A reversal film's reference is the windows' rest. Negative-only checks scoped, the slides' tolerances widened for their steeper curves.
outcome: tests/projection.rs: the GPU projection against its reference 2.1e-7 (twin: no veil); a photo on Velvia 50 through the chain 6.4e-6 (twin: unlit at its daylight); a grey through its couplers 2.5e-5 off the sheet, a red 0.24 (twin). Crosstalk error to the reference charts: Velvia 50 0.0018, Velvia 100 0.0008, Ektachrome E100 0.0006 (no cross term 0.0047, 0.0029, 0.0026).

title: A photo picked in the gallery is picked in the library column every time: its folders unfold, a hand's fold since included, and its row comes into view; on the projects, its project
detail: The column's reveal was kept per photo (tree_reveal::Reveal), so a photo picked again in the gallery, the one already followed, found its folders as a hand had folded them: no row to pick, unfold or scroll to, on the archive beside the photo and on the projects in the gallery. A fold made by hand beside the photo still stays through edits and clicks in the column.

title: While a roll is prepared, the gallery's decodes stand still and the roll's come first: its frames no longer wait seconds behind the thumbnail pass
detail: Cause: Prepare the Roll's previews worker (roll_previews::run) marked its decodes as background work, so its tiles, card and base scan shared the gate's one background place with the gallery's thumbnail pass, the balances read ahead and every other background thread, the condvar handing it to any of them (the 1.6 log: a background decode waited 5741 ms for its place). decode_gate: a thread's kind is Hand, Roll or Background; Roll::set_shown holds the gate while the roll is shown (decode_gate::hold_for_roll), and no background decode takes a place until it is left; the roll's decodes yield to a waiting hand alone and run beside the hand's, at most DECODES - 1 of their own, so the base scan no longer waits for the loupe's full resolution. The roll previews and its neighbours' full resolutions are Roll; the log says when the gallery stands still and resumes.
outcome: decode_gate::a_roll_held_stills_every_background_decode_and_never_its_own (twin: the roll's work asked as background work waits; a second roll decode never takes the hand's last place). Window check prepare_first: 8 scans, Prepare opened over a waiting thumbnail pass, every preview lands with no background decode taken (twin: the hold removed, 8 taken; the roll left, the gallery's decodes and thumbnails resume). Real app on a copy of roll #8 (38 NEFs, measured, empty caches), ONI_BENCH=prepare: the base scan shown in 1105 ms (8654 ms before), the loupe's full resolution 2518 ms (65500 ms), the flow 27 s (123 s); no thumbnail drawn between the hold and the roll's landing.

title: A paper is its curves: every colour paper develops its sheet's three Status A curves and reads each layer through a pure dye on its own Rec. 2020 channel, as the neutral paper does; the spectral viewing is gone
detail: Cause (paper-review audits): a scan hands a paper no masked separation, so the real paper dyes' unwanted absorptions cost a third of the chroma and turned reds, pinks and skins toward yellow. Removed: the print and view band tables of paper::Sheet and Paper, their bake under D50 in paper::baked, the kernel's band loop and its 162 uniform rows (cpu viewed and paper.wgsl), PAPER_BANDS, Paper::head, the neutral paper's own dyes, the paper profiles' wavelengths, sensitivities, dye and base spectra and unmixed amounts (scripts/datasheet-profiles.py writes a paper's Status A curves alone, D-min included: data.log_exposure and data.density_curves; the nine paper files 365 KB to 156 KB). oni_render::viewed reads 10^-density per channel; own_grey, the ends and the neutral paper use it. The Frontier SP-3000 refitted on the new kernel (frontier_print_fit.py: the scanner's matrix and three normal integrals a layer, no virtual dyes, the neutral axis weighted 20): against its table, neutral axis median 0.70 (0.81 before), constrained median 1.85 p90 5.02 (1.04 and 2.41 before); its own white is now pure white, its fit leaving no density past the table. No sidecar step: papers arrived after 1.6 and their settings keep their meaning. Pins moved, only on paper pipes: colour_on_negative, lighting_on_negative, exposure_departure (CPU, GPU) and legacy_print's four paper cases (oni-digital-on-paper, oni-paper-keys-temp, frontier-paper-at-rest, frontier-on-frontier-paper); the 45 other legacy cases and the neutral paper (Delta E00 0 on 278 frames) are bit-identical. Ceilings moved to what pure dyes show: virtual stocks' neutral ramps C*ab 20.1 (Venus 800 shadows, 11.9 before), lights 8.6; Exposure on a scanned X-TRA 400 on a paper worst Delta E 5.4; a slide's copy keeps 1.8 to 2.2 times ONI's print's chroma (0.8 to 1.6 before); the slide's greys on the saturation curve 1.6e-2; the digital photo with Exposure +2 and Brightness -1 falls 2.0e-4 by its pick, its blue layer 60 % slower than its tone's mean where Brightness lays one shift on the three (left to Brightness's own design).
outcome: Measured on the owner's scans read only (sidecars copied beside symlinks): 278 colour negatives of the 1.6-prepared rolls at 512 px, pooled means, today / curves and pure dyes / neutral paper. Royal Digital: C* 15.0 / 21.8 / 22.0, L* 47.7 / 47.6 / 49.5, Delta E00 to the neutral paper 6.81 to 4.65 (skin 5.69 to 2.76, red 10.75 to 3.41, orange 9.03 to 3.90, pink 8.67 to 4.36, greys 3.96 to 4.58, their C* 2.8 to 4.0). Endura Premier: C* 16.7 / 24.4 / 22.0, L* 44.2 (5.3 under the neutral, its contrast kept), Delta E00 7.62 to 6.84. Fuji DPII: C* 13.4 / 22.0 / 22.0, Delta E00 6.88 to 3.95 (skin 6.45 to 2.38, red 10.33 to 2.60). Frontier: moved Delta E00 2.71 from today (red 4.51, orange 4.58, skin 2.27, greys 2.11), C* 12.0 to 12.2. The audit scans P1073182, P1072245, P1072386, P1072457 at 1600 px: Royal Digital C* 25.9 to 35.7 (neutral 32.5), L* 40.3 to 40.8 (neutral 50.3, Royal's own contrast). Sheets « Aujourd'hui », « Courbes + colorants purs », « Papier neutre » per scan in the scratch folder. cargo test oni-render, oni-pipeline, oni-settings green; window checks paper, paper_menu, paper_sheet_window, export_paper_window, sheet_paper green.

title: A reversal film's projection holds each dye and the base over the bands its sheet leaves unmeasured: a projected Velvia black reaches its sheet's D-max
detail: film::projection read a band the profile leaves empty (about 380-395 and 705-780 nm) as no dye and no base, so the lamp's ends passed every black: Velvia 100's densest showed at D 2.58 / 3.86 / 2.55 on the screen, Ektachrome E100's green went past the lamp's end. Cause fixed where the table is built: `held` gives an unmeasured band its nearest measured neighbours' line (held at the ends), for the projection and the new scan solve alike.
outcome: tests/projector.rs: Velvia 100's densest on the screen D 3.16 / 3.39 / 3.11, the veil and a hair more (twin: the bands read as clear, red and blue under D 2.8); film::projection unit check on `held` (twin: the ends read clear). A digital photo on a reversal film moves by ΔE00 mean 3.3, p95 5.4-6.2 on Velvia 50 and 100, mean 6.2, p95 10.1 on Ektachrome E100 (measured on the owner's slides' dye amounts); no pinned digital check moved.

title: A scanned slide is projected on a white screen: its scan read back to its film's dyes, Lighting re-exposing it through its stock's curve
detail: New kernel dye_amounts (oni-render, WGSL and scalar reference): the scan over the backlight (the frame's gains put a sprocket hole on 1) and the bare base, solved per pixel by eight Newton steps for the three dyes' amounts whose light through base and dyes over 81 bands under a 5500 K scanner lamp, seen by the 1931 observer adapted to the bare film, is that light; coded as 10^-amount for the projection kernel, which shows it under the 3200 K lamp with the 0.5 % veil (film::projection::scanned, projector). The film: the roll's reversal stock where its sheet is profiled, written in the frame's dyes' key (dyes::slide_dyes, PipelineSettings::projector), else Ektachrome E100 (VirtualStock::SLIDE: Kodak's general-purpose slide film, its sheet whole, the closer of the two to the owner's slides' former render). Lighting and the colour tools act on the dyes through negative::slide, the Negative kernel on Film::Slide's development: each layer read as the neutral density holding it under the scanner's lamp, along the green layer's curve, so a grey stays grey; the moves turn about the stock's speed. A measure upstream of the print (print bypassed) still reads the scan through the windows by stage 4-7; a slide kept on a legacy print keeps its render; stage 4-7's positive path stays for both and for the grey every print rests on (film::plain_grey). A digital photo on a reversal film shows through the same projector (Pipeline::on_screen).
outcome: tests/projector.rs: the GPU solve against its reference 1.3e-6 on every branch, the floor, both clamps, alpha (twin: gains 1 % off, 2.7e-2), a table no dye moves 2.3e-7; the chain 8.0e-7 (twin: no gains, 6.9e-2), lit with the colour tools and Projected blacks 3.5e-6 (twin 0.39), the measure through the windows 1.1e-7. Exposure +1 lays a grey on its sheet's grey a stop over within 1e-3 of amount and of screen light, at log exposure -1 to +0.5 (twin: each layer on its own sheet curve, 3.9 % off the neutral's colour). tests/projection.rs: a photo on Velvia 50 through the chain 7.6e-7 (twin: unlit at its daylight, 5.4e-2), with Projected blacks 7.6e-7 (twin: pure ends, 5.6e-3). Owner's seven Velvia 100 frames through render_corpus: Projected blacks on matches the prototype's B (ΔE00 to today's render 6.72 against 6.74); Exposure +1 lifts the whites from L* 85.7 to 95.1 and keeps the film's densest black.

title: Projected blacks, a slide's switch in its Projector section: the screen's own black and white, off at rest for pure black and white
detail: Print::projected_blacks (key projectedBlacks, written only on): on, the film's densest under the veil and the bare film's white as the screen shows them; off, laid on pure black and pure white channel by channel (projection::pure), as Print lift off lays a paper's. Off at rest: as Paper blacks, for a picture shown on a display, and the closer to the owner's slides' former render (ΔE00 5.9 against 6.7 on the seven Velvia frames). Colour tab: a Projector section in the Paper section's place on a slide or a digital photo on a reversal film, naming its film and lamp, the switch and its help; Colour compensation, Highlight Detail and Per-Channel Levels leave, as the projector reads none. Texts in French and Spanish.
outcome: tests/projector.rs: off, the film's densest lands within 1e-4 of black and the bare film within 1e-3 of white; on, the screen's black and the veiled white (twin: the screen's black is no pure black); Exposure leaves the densest within 2e-3 of black. Window check paper: a slide shows the Projector, Projected blacks off at rest and rendering anew each way it turns, no paper switch, no Brightness, no Colour compensation (twin: back on a negative, the Projector leaves and its stored paper prints again). Catalogue check green.

title: A slide takes no paper and no internegative; the internegative serves a film's look alone
detail: takes_paper is false on a slide and on a digital photo on a reversal film: the virtual enlarger and paper choice leave them, a paper they named stays stored for a return to a negative. paper::internegative keeps the .cube looks' copy alone (its slide gains and pedestal and its identity light gone), its branches in chain.rs and conversion.rs reduced to it. Prepare the Roll no longer lays a slide on a paper and writes the roll's reversal film; a roll's stock picked writes it on its slides (roll_card::dyed), a stock no sheet profiles taking a former reversal key off and leaving a negative's. Older migration steps read a paper as their formats did (chain::papered). Checks re-pinned: the colour tools', Lighting's and Exposure's CPU folds without the removed slide-on-paper pipe, each verified equal on the canvas build with the same pipes; the GPU fold moves by the slide alone (equal without it); the legacy fixture's four Pro slides take their projector's GPU fingerprint, every legacy slide and digital photo unmoved. tests/slide_print.rs removed with the internegative's slide.

title: Sidecar format 70: a slide opens on the projector with every edit kept, its roll's reversal film read off its folder
detail: No stored value moves: a slide's Lighting, colour tools, gains and paper stay as written. migrate::slide_projector::marked: a slide of an earlier format takes the profiled reversal film its folder's roll marker names, else its sidecar's own roll's, on the read paths and the on-disk sweep; any other stock leaves its dyes' key. A build before 70 opens these files read-only. Measured move against the canvas build's render through render_corpus at 1500 px, the prototype's crop: the seven Velvia 100 frames (Lighting at rest) ΔE00 mean 5.9, p95 13.7, Projected blacks on 6.7 / 13.0; the eight 1.6 slide copies (Lighting edited, their copy's roll naming a negative stock, so on Ektachrome E100) 7.9 / 11.9, on 7.7 / 11.7. The move is the projector's own, mid-tones L* 3 to 6 darker and its dyes' colour, at rest as edited; Exposure and filters scaled by 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 move further (14.9, 10.5, 9.1), by 1.25 and 1.5 nearer (6.95, 6.8) only by offsetting that darkening, which would treat edited and unedited slides apart: no mapping applied. Adversarial review for data loss: none found; a negative's key on a slide frame is replaced by its roll's reversal film, as a roll's pick replaces it.
outcome: migrate::slide_projector: an edited slide of 69 reads back whole, its paper kept and unprinted, a digital photo on a reversal film too; the round trip at 70 keeps projectedBlacks (twin: off, unwritten); the marker's film taken, a stock no sheet profiles leaving a negative's key, a sidecar's own roll read with no marker (twins: 70 and a negative untouched); on disk, a slide of 69 brought to 70 beside its marker, its edits whole, Current on the next pass. Corpus goldens: every reading gains projected_blacks: false alone; the newer fixture moved to 71.

title: Fujifilm Fujiclear leaves the papers
detail: The owner's call (2026-11-24): a display material read as a paper, its tone printed negatives badly. Its stock file goes and the data-sheet script no longer writes it; a frame naming it keeps the key as stored and prints on the default paper, as any key no file defines.

title: A projected slide's black stays black under Lighting: Exposure and every slider brighten or darken the picture without lifting the film's densest
detail: Cause: Lighting re-exposes a slide through its stock's curve, and the development's fog, where no exposure moves a density, is the neutral the green layer's D-max holds, denser than the film's own black on red and blue (Velvia 100: amounts 3.03 / 3.41 / 3.58 against the sheet's 2.92 / 3.41 / 3.27) and denser still than a scan's black, which the copy's veil lifts (2.70 / 3.40 / 2.87 on the owner's roll); the foot sits 0.01 above the fog, so the black took the whole move and Exposure +2 lifted it to 0.015 / 0.002 / 0.036 of the screen's white, purple. Fix, the papers' rule (#3090, #3281): the screen lays the lit slide back onto the slide at Lighting's rest by its rest's light over the screen's black, none of a slider's move at the black, the whole from Brightness's reach (L* 25 of light) up, a smoothstep between (new kernel held_black, WGSL and scalar reference; projector::held; Pipeline::on_screen; the saturation curve's lightness axis read the same way). One rule for every slider and both Projected blacks; a slide at Lighting's rest renders as before to the bit. Projector help text in English, French and Spanish.
outcome: tests/projector.rs: the film's densest and a scan's black hold within 5e-5 of their rest from Exposure -2 to +2, with and without Projected blacks (twin: unheld, +2 lifts them by 2e-3 to 4e-2, blue the most); over 300 tones past the reach at rest follow Exposure -2 to +2 as unheld within 1e-6 relative; a deep shadow (L* 3.6) takes 2.5 % of a +2 move (twin: unheld it takes it all); GPU held_black against its reference 1.1e-7 (twin: reach doubled, 0.38); the chain with Lighting and the colour tools 2.8e-6. Seven Velvia 100 frames through render_corpus: at rest identical to the bit; the blacks (L* under 5 at rest) at L* 1.53 / C* 5.8 at rest, 1.64 / 6.1 at +1, 2.06 / 6.6 at +2, against 9.27 / 19.2 unheld at +1; the mids (L* 30-70) move +21.4 L* at +1 held and unheld alike, +39.0 at +2. Eight edited 1.6 slides (their own Exposure about +1): ΔE00 1.93 mean, 6.8 p95 against the merged projector, their blacks from L* 3.2 / C* 9.4 to 1.7 / 6.0. Pinned GPU fingerprints: the four Pro slides of the legacy fixture and the Exposure fold's slide moved, every other entry equal to the canvas build (the fold without its slide verified equal).

title: A scanned slide's dyes are solved as the observer sees the scan: no more green and blue speckles in a dense blue on the projector
detail: Measured on the owner's P1073157 (Velvia 100, roll 2026-10-30), the Folies Bergère sign: its scan, after the gains, holds red 7.5e-4 ± 6.2e-4, green 1.3e-3, blue 9.8e-3, so its red crosses zero on one pixel in ten. The solve read that light in working Rec. 2020, whose functions have negative lobes: for a dense blue the model's own red is zero or under at any amounts (f = -1e-3 at cyan 6), so its log was floored at 1e-12, its Jacobian meaningless, and eight clamped Newton steps wandered from box edge to box edge (median log miss 6.6 on the sign, none converged); a pixel landed on cyan 6, magenta -0.25, yellow -0.07 and projected green (0.32 G, 0.78 B against its neighbours' 0.001), another on yellow -0.5 and projected bright blue. The path was chaotic: the same solve in another float order moved an amount by 1.6, and GPU and CPU parted by 0.022. The solve now reads the light as the 1931 observer under the scanner's lamp (DyeAmounts::to_seen, the inverse of the working matrix, each function scaled so the bare film reads 1; the table's second row holds those positive functions): the same equations, so a light the dyes reach keeps its amounts, but the model's light is positive and its log convex in the amounts. The steps are Levenberg–Marquardt's (DYE_DAMPING 1e-3, tenfold on a refused step, a tenth on a kept one; DYE_STEP_LIMIT gone), an amount on a bound the descent pushes past held there, so a light out of the dyes' reach settles on the nearest light they reach; a step is kept where the miss falls or, near the root where misses differ under f32's grain, where the slopes' trapezoid says it falls. Still eight steps after the first guess (one evaluation each, nine in all against eight): on P1073157, 99.9 % of the picture within 0.017 ΔE of a 64-step solve, the worst 1.2; twelve steps would bring the worst to 0.06 for 40 % more time (full frame 11.7 Mpx: about 100 ms for eight, 145 ms for twelve on the M2 Max).
outcome: P1073157 through the editor's chain at its decode (4184 × 2792), the picture inside the mount (5.8 Mpx): pixels more than 10 ΔE (CIELAB) from the median of their 5 × 5 neighbourhood 188,701 before, 2,698 after (more than 20 ΔE: 168,045 to 7); the rest follow the scan's own noise. The render moves elsewhere by a median 0.05 ΔE, p90 1.5. GPU against CPU on the whole frame: largest amount gap 1.4e-4 (was 0.022). tests/projector.rs: the GPU solve against its reference 4.0e-6 on every branch, a dense blue past the dyes' reach added (twin: gains 1 % off, 8.1e-2), a table no dye moves 5.3e-7; a ramp of the sign's red from 1.8e-3 to -2.5e-4 moves the screen at most 0.041 ΔE a step (twin: the solve read in working Rec. 2020 leaps 166 ΔE); the sign's blue with its measured noise on 8,836 pixels shows 3 speckles past 10 ΔE, the scan's own noise (twin: 3,493). Re-pinned GPU fingerprints, slides only: exposure_departure's fold, legacy_print's 040-P1073163 and the three P1073169 copies; every CPU fold unmoved. Crop sheet before/after at 2× on the sign and the trousers kept outside the repository.

title: Exposure holds Prepare's black and white: on the negative, before any print, it gains every tone share's odds by what the film's own stop lays on the grey
detail: The owner's call (2026-11-24): Exposure stays on the negative, in the chain before the print or the paper, but anchored on Prepare's window. Cause: Lighting laid Exposure in the film's log exposure, which on its straight line is one density offset, a global gain on the negative's light: the window's densest end moved with it (ONI's print's white to 1.108 at +1, 0.955 at -1) and the tones a few hundredths over the bare film jumped (x8.4 at 5 % of the window against x1.39 at the grey on DSC_6432, +1). Now the negative kernel develops Contrast, the filters and the colour tools again as before, then lays Exposure on each channel's tone share u (0 the bare film, 1 the window's densest) as an odds gain, u/(1-u) times e^odds, the same on the three channels: both ends stay, each end's tones scale about it as by a gain, any travel stays monotone. The gain per stop is the one the film's own stop, through its development and couplers, lays on the reference grey's mean share (half the odds between a stop up and a stop down), so the grey lands where the film's stop puts it. Every negative pipe (ONI's print, the neutral paper, every paper, digital photos on a virtual film, black and white, a positive read on ONI's print); a projected slide keeps its own Exposure and #3742's hold. Contrast, the zones and the points keep their moves: Contrast still turns the white about the grey, the zones and points already hold or move the ends by name. Kernel `Negative::exposed` with its WGSL twin (`negative_exposed`), the gain passed as e^odds.
outcome: Checks: kernel unit check (ends held, a gain by each end, odds taken by e^odds over the share, monotone; twin: a log shift moves the white); lighting_on_negative's new check on every pipe at -2, -1, +1, +2 (black within 1e-5, white within 1e-3; grey within 0.07 stop of the film's stop a stop away, 0.28 two away; the mids 0.3-0.7 within 0.45 stop a stop away; by the black between the rest and the film's stop, on ONI's print within 0.25 stop + 0.25 per stop of a gain; twins: the film's own stop moves the white on 8 or more pipe-stops and jumps by the black); GPU against its reference (worst 7e-7, an odds twin in stages). Re-pinned after checking only Exposure-departed cases moved (folds without Exposure equal before and after): legacy_print (13 of 49 documents, every one off Exposure's rest), exposure_departure, colour_on_negative. Halation: Lighting's two stops within 15 % of the film's (10.4 %), its twin 95 % off. paper_ends' free whites read on Contrast. On DSC_6432, ONI's print +1: x2.62 / 2.53 / 2.39 under 3 % of the light against x15.3 / 8.0 / 4.6 before, x1.69 at the grey; the frame's rebate stays black. 1.6-era corpus (233 sidecars of formats 19-20): 26 Exposure-edited negatives move, Oklab dE x100 mean 2.65, median p95 5.5, worst p95 14.1 (P1073209, Exposure +0.87); its 16 Exposure-edited slides (projected) and every frame at Exposure's rest unchanged to the bit; the 513 c16-now copies hold no Exposure off its rest.

title: A paper reads its dyes' Status A crosstalk: each layer develops its dye amount, each channel reads the three dyes through the paper's crosstalk over its D-min, a grey still exactly on the sheet's curves; colours keep 77 to 86 % of #3750's chroma
detail: Cause (owner: saturations go too far since #3750): a sheet's Status A curves are a grey's integral densities, each channel holding the other dyes' absorption in it; #3750 laid that whole curve on each layer alone, so a colour's layer carried its neighbours' share too. Not a gamut bound: only 0.25 to 0.6 % of the 1.6 negatives' pixels lay past the old spectral gamut. scripts/datasheet-profiles.py writes each paper's crosstalk again from its sheet's dyes (data.crosstalk: the Status A densities each unit dye reads, a row a channel; off-diagonals 0.01 to 0.17). paper::Sheet::new unmixes the sheet's densities over the D-min to each layer's amounts through it (held where a trace's dip would make one fall, 0.004 D at most), and the kernel (Paper::amounts, dyed, developed; paper.wgsl) prints D = D-min + crosstalk x amounts through the pure dyes; 4 uniform rows. The neutral paper and the Frontier take the identity (paper::PURE_DYES): the neutral paper is bit-identical, the Frontier moves 4e-7 at most (f32 rounding of its D-min). Checks: a grey prints on every sheet's curves within 4e-3 D (twin: the densities read as amounts miss by 0.54 to 0.82 D); a cyan keeps 0.72 to 0.85 of its pure dyes' chroma, within 0.06 of what the crosstalk's densities predict (twin: pure dyes over no D-min print the sheet's densities to the bit); each paper's dye reaches the other channels, the neutral paper's none; the profile read in doubles through the crosstalk within 3.5e-6 D; the CPU and GPU kernels on every branch. Pins re-pinned after checking only paper cases moved: colour_on_negative, lighting_on_negative, exposure_departure (CPU, GPU) and legacy_print's four paper cases.
outcome: Measured on the 278 colour negatives of the 1.6 rolls at 384 px, rendered by the pipeline (old spectral / #3750 / crosstalk, pooled means). Royal Digital: C* 14.9 / 21.7 / 18.5 (skin 14.2 / 19.9 / 17.6, red 24.4 / 41.1 / 34.8, pink 14.3 / 24.9 / 18.7, greys 2.8 / 4.0 / 3.8), L* unchanged, Delta E00 to the old render 4.76 to 3.33, to #3750 1.98. Endura Premier: C* 16.7 / 24.3 / 20.9, Delta E00 to old 4.93 to 3.56. Fuji DPII: C* 13.4 / 21.9 / 16.8, Delta E00 to old 5.49 to 3.17. Chroma over the old render now 1.11 to 1.32 at every saturation (1.32 to 1.77 under #3750). Frontier unmoved. Four-column sheets « Aujourd'hui (#3750) », « Diaphonie Status A », « Ancien spectral », « Papier neutre » for P1072245, P1073182, 040-P1072826 and 054-P1072786 in the scratch folder. cargo test oni-render, oni-pipeline, oni-settings green (502); the paper window checks left to the merge.

title: The former library's welcome and catch-up sheet leave: ONI no longer reads library.json
detail: Both served only a library.json from before roots (a Swift-era flat list of files), which a fresh install never has: the welcome's folders came only from roots::suggested over that list, and the sheet showed only while it held photos. No edit depends on it: sidecars lie beside the photos and the favourites import from roots.json (Places::seeded, places_held). Gone: navigator/catch_up.rs, the Nav fields welcome, former, catching_up and catch_up_folders, the five callbacks and their Navigator properties, Welcome and RootsCatchUpSheet in navigator.slint, WelcomeLine and CatchUpLine, Ctl::add_starred, library::load and LibraryFile, roots::suggested with its three tests, the upgrade check's library.json line and 17 catalogue texts each in French and Spanish. The rootsCatchUpShown preference is left unread; a leftover library.json stays on the disk, unread.
outcome: The navigator window check now stars and opens Old through Add Folder… with a picker answering it (Add stars the folder it opens, as before); oni-library tests green, catalogue check green.

title: The stepped Slider and the lab's Scanner keypad leave with the Scanner face
detail: No app screen or demo scene set Slider.stepped since the Scanner face left (one-face call, 2026-11-21); only the hue probe and the lab did, and step-reads was never set, so Readouts always took per = 0. Gone: the stepped branches of slider.slint (press, drag, release, double click, type-in, held and hand), the unused Typing global and its export, the per parameter of Readouts.steps and Readouts.pressed (typed_steps and pressed in slider_track.rs, the demos' welcome interface), the lab's LiveStepped, StepKey, StepKeyRow, BandKey, KeypadRow, its STEPPED SLIDER, LABSTEPKEYS, SCANNER KEYPAD, STEP KEYS and Pro/Scanner bar specimens, and the 15 lab-only tokens they used (scanner-band-*, scanner-key-*, scanner-keyboard-width, scanner-wide-key-width, control-mode-bar-width). #3063 kept the lab's keypad as a scoping note of the face removal, not an owner's call. The hue probe's C and D are continuous sliders, C's fraction following its count. Every typed number and key tooltip reads as before.
outcome: slider_track's unit checks green (the per rows gone, a new twin: a readout's tenths count tenths); the lab compiles; window checks slider_hues, slider_keys, slider_rest, slider_hand, slider_relief, dial, keyboard's typed number, design_system and tooltip green (19).

title: The hidden Grain Curve editor leaves: its view, gestures, reset key and fold
detail: #2209 took the Grain Curve out of the panel; GrainEditor had no instance in any .slint file since, yet Rust still drew its lines and dots on every editors publish, tracked its drag, owned Reset::Grain and read its fold. Zero anticipation keeps nothing for later. Gone: editors/grain.rs, Plot::Grain (the last plot, so the others keep their numbers), Reset::Grain (the last reset, so beside[0..3] keep theirs), Edit::Grain, the grain branches of the five-point gestures, the drawing cache and beside's grain arm, the Editors properties grain-lines, grain-dots, grain-modified and grain-folded, the Grain Curve fold, the grain half of the reset-beside test and two catalogue texts each in French and Spanish. The render, GrainCurve, its serialisation and its propagation between frames are untouched; the sectionFold.Grain Curve preference is left unread.
outcome: oni-app editors and folds unit checks green; window checks editors, editor_leftovers, together, together_all, together_moves, together_tools, grain_colour, film_effects, picture_plots, whole_roll, balance_kept green (17).

title: The vertical rail and knob leave with the lab's upright slider
detail: No app screen or demo sets Rail.vertical or Knob.vertical; only the lab's UprightSlider (a mirror of Swift's DSSlider(axis: .vertical)) and a vertical knob specimen did. The property goes from both components and each ternary keeps its horizontal arm as written, so every rail and knob the app draws is the same; the lab loses UprightSlider, its DSSLIDER, VERTICAL row and the vertical knob specimen, the DS README its line on the vertical rail.
outcome: The lab compiles; window checks design_system, slider_*, dial, toggles, levels, plots, guides, compare and welcome green (27).

title: A design-system value one style alone reads lives on that style: 114 single-use DS tokens collapse
detail: tokens.slint mirrored the Swift tokens, so a value one style alone used had two names (DS.control-kit-mark-large and KitStyle.mark-large) and a change two places; with Swift dead the mirror has no reason. Each DS token named exactly once, by a whole `property <T> x: DS.token;` line in ui/ds/, and by nothing else (no screen, lab page, Rust getter, check or script) moves its literal onto that line and leaves tokens.slint: 114 of 224, in theme.slint (37), theme_views (31), forms (9), wrapped (9), theme_fields, theme_scanner, theme_type (5 each), roll, theme_sliders (3 each), theme_tabs, welcome (2 each), badge, folders, splash (1 each). Every literal is a plain value moved as written (deck-depth's 3 binds an int as before); the slider press keeps its owner's-call note on its style line. Tokens read from Rust (geometry's check, tree_column, the window checks' getters) or by the lab stay. The DS README's rule and theme.slint's and tokens.slint's headers say it: a value of one style is written there, a shared one is a DS token.
outcome: The lab's five pages render byte-identical before and after (KeysPage, TabsPage, FieldsPage, SlidersPage, MiscPage at 2800 x 4800); the catalogue check (Inter on a family line) and the lab compile green; window checks in the final run.

title: A digital photo's negative is scanned as a real one is: a white lamp through its dyes and orange base, seen by an RGB camera, then read by the negative pipe on a reference derived on that scan; format 71
detail: Cause (two adversarial reviews): the virtual negative handed each layer's density as transmittance on its own Rec. 2020 channel, a perfect negative no scan produces: on the 64 Session vol photos Portra 800 printed 2.1x the reference's chroma (reds 4.5x) and turned blues 28 degrees toward teal. Fix, the owner's model taken literally: the developed layers (virtual_negative, unchanged) are scanned under the slide scanner's 5500 K lamp through the stock file's own dyes and D-min, every band held, by the 1931 observer standing in for an RGB camera balanced on the open lamp (film::projection::scanner), on the slide projector's kernel and table layout with no veil: one light-through-dyes path for slides and digital negatives, no new kernel. The bare film scans orange (Portra 800: 0.51 / 0.29 / 0.12) and its reference, derived on the scan as Prepare measures a roll's, lays it on grey (stops -0.83 / 0 / +1.22). No mask model: the profile's dyes are the sheet's image dyes and its D-min the masked film's, the amounts unmixed from the sheet's Status M neutral on exactly these dyes, so the scan of a grey reads the sheet; a spektrafilm-style mask (each dye's unwanted Status M absorptions removed) would cut cyan's green crosstalk in the camera from 0.25 to 0.07 of its own but no longer reproduce the sheet's neutral without unmixing the amounts again. Film::Stock carries the scan (none on a slide, projected, or on silver, whose neutral density a white lamp reads alike); Stock::shot and Stock::scanned are the CPU reference every check reads; Pipeline::filmed uploads and lays the scan; the grain's tones read it. Every film's reference derived again (46 colour negatives moved; silver and slides unmoved). Format 71: a digital photo of formats 69-70 moves from the per-channel reference (migrate::digital_scan, its 48 entries) onto the scan's, every hand's move kept; layer_densities now lands on that per-channel table. Removed: the per-channel read-out as the digital negative's scan; the duplicated table-building loops in film::projection (one tabled).
outcome: tests/digital_scan.rs: GPU filmed (negative and scan) against Stock::shot 1.2e-7 (twin: the read-out alone, 0.45); the bare film orange, laid grey by the stops within 1e-4 (twin: the read-out alone near clear); the grey ramp on the paperless pipe at C* 6.5 at most, bound 7 (twin: the read-out alone 9.1); with ONI_CHART_DIR, Portra 800's chart against its reference, grey matched: ColorChecker chroma 0.949, mean dE00 8.01, bounds +-10 % and 8.8 (twins: the read-out alone 1.393 and dE00 11.1, no cross term 0.570). Format 71 migration with its twin. Merged with canvas 9cd9fa03 (#3745 Exposure anchored on Prepare's window, #3751 paper crosstalk): Lighting's own check passes on the scan, the former Exposure-is-the-film's tolerance gone with its test. The grey ramp is now judged lit at the film's own white, as a daylight scene reaches it (#2325's convention, kept): its grey neutral (C* 0.01), its ends 5.7 at most, green shadows and magenta highlights where the two-point windows (black on the bare film, the grey) meet layers of other shapes; a RAW's 5000 K neutral prints warm (1.056 / 0.983 / 0.935 at the film), by that convention. Every stock's neutral ramp: widest C* 12.2 (Superia 1600) against 20.1 before, bound 21 to 13. Re-pinned on the merged build, digital and paper only: legacy_print's four digital documents of 50, the three folds. 64 Session vol photos, Portra 800, today: ONI print C* 21.6 L* 58.7 C*/L* 1.36x the reference's, blues -10.7 degrees, dE00 18.9; paperless 21.9, 1.37x, -16.1, 19.1; Royal 26.3, 1.81x, -15.1, 17.0, against the fit-time Royal (0ae9c4e0) 20.5, 1.42x, -12.3, 15.3. At matched grey the photos' chroma follows the tone's local contrast: 2.4x the reference's at Oklch L 0.3 where ONI's print is 2.1x steeper in L* per stop, 0.52x at L 0.8 where it is 0.35x as steep; the chart's patches sit in the mids, hence 0.95x. sweep_pass and swift_checks' presets fail on the exFAT build volume alone (permissions, AppleDouble files).

title: The fifteen colour negatives with a reference chart refit their couplers on the scanned negative, printed by the enlarger on no paper, against the reference on a chart at matched grey
detail: Cause: #3730 fitted the cross terms at rest on Royal Digital with a crosstalk-only loss blind to absolute chroma and tone, on the per-channel read-out; the paper changed since (#3750). Fix: examples/coupler_fit.rs renders with Print on paper off (the paper is laid over a render, never part of it) and fits the six cross terms (common diagonal, fold refusal kept, two starts) to an absolute objective: the Oklab distance of each chart patch (ColorChecker's 18 chromatic, Oklch rings, a 9-step grey ramp weighted 2) to the reference applied to the same chart, the render's mid grey matched to the reference's channel by channel. The chart and its judging (CIEDE2000, chroma, ramp) live in examples/chart, shared with tests/digital_scan.rs. New matrices in the fifteen files (Portra 800's pushes take Portra 800's); every film without a reference chart keeps the common matrix, closer to each reference than no cross term on all fifteen (loss common 0.0047-0.0084 against none 0.0051-0.0095).
outcome: Chart against each reference, paperless, grey matched, before (per-channel read-out, former couplers) / after (scan, refit): mean dE00 Portra 800 9.46 / 8.01, Portra 400 9.70 / 8.57, Portra 160 8.78 / 8.01, Gold 200 10.25 / 8.70, UltraMax 400 9.58 / 8.16, Ektar 100 10.30 / 9.44, C200 8.30 / 6.75, Pro 400H 8.80 / 7.96, Superia 200 8.48 / 6.77, Superia 1600 9.18 / 8.48, Vision3 250D 9.99 / 8.51, 200T 11.95 / 8.99, 500T 11.38 / 8.55, Portra 160NC 9.11 / 9.20, 160VC 9.01 / 9.69; ColorChecker chroma after 0.84-1.02 of the reference's (Portra 800 0.949). About 7 L* of the remaining dE00 is tone, ONI's print against the reference's, which no coupler moves. Tungsten films' ramps stay blue (C* 9.4-9.8): a daylight scene on Vision3 200T and 500T, as before. On the 64 photos the refit brings back the chart's chroma, so the photos' pooled C* (21.6, 2.0x the reference's) stays near the former; it is the lift ONI's print gives the mids and shadows (L* +18), the saturation C*/L* 1.36x the reference's against 1.45x before.

title: film_group keeps only the folder heading: the retired roll-and-day feed and its hand-placed order go
detail: The gallery and the sidebar cut by folder (folders::group, trash::groups), the only two places a FilmGroup is built, both on a folder with its heading. The library cut into rolls and capture days (grouped, key, keyed, day_start, start_of_day, day_label), the drag order (order, root_order, behind, detied), untitled and UNTITLED_STEM, is_explicit, explicit_name, info::resolved_roll and LibraryIndex::set_manual_order had no caller outside their tests. FilmKey gives way to a plain `folder` path, `start` (computed for nothing) goes and `heading` is a String. Nothing stored moves: Entry.manual_order, Film.manual_order and the index's columns are read and written as before.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-library green; oni-app's library tests green. The five Film.selfCheck tests in swift_checks.rs and roll8's day half go with what they tested; index tests keep their twins (file_tests' index-only twin now writes a label).

title: oni-measure drops the withdrawn AUTO LEVELS key's machinery: key::placed, levels and ends, Measurer::reduced, auto_levels' Balance, two_steps, keyed, applied, carried, mean and composite
detail: The key was withdrawn (#1053); what it left had no caller outside oni-measure's own tests. The roll measure keeps Classic's two steps inline (roll::measured), and Measured now carries the gains it lands on (`stops`) instead of a Balance whose levels and shift nothing read; the placement stays as the gate a flat channel fails. key::slide_read returns the histogram itself, and Prepare's slides build oni_core::balance::Balance directly, the same stops and resting windows. Nothing stored or rendered moves; ONI_READING_CODE changes with oni-measure/src, so kept Auto WB outcomes are read once again, to the same values.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-measure green. The piled-channel check runs on roll::measured over the simulated densities (a reading's tails laid on them); roll8's second-press check runs on key::roll_measured on the reference roll (gains 0.0018 / 0.0015 st, tails 2e-4; twin read after the levels 0.47 / 0.55 st), and filter_balance compares the roll measure under a legacy print. Tests of the deleted helpers alone go (a selection's strategies over the dead applied and mean, keyed against two_steps, composite).

title: The index drops its respelling pass and its dual-spelling keys: every row of a per-schema index file is keyed in the archive's spelling
detail: Since each schema keeps its own index-N.sqlite and open refuses any other user_version (#1569), upsert, the only writer of photos, has keyed every row with paths::normal, unchanged since the pass was written. So respell's search always came back empty and the `WHERE path IN (?, ?)` pairs (the path as given and its normal spelling) could only ever match the second. index/spelling.rs and its call go; each lookup, update and delete of photos and stamps keys on `path = normal(path)`. Should paths::normal ever change, a SCHEMA_VERSION bump rebuilds the cache. The index is a disposable cache: no sidecar or render moves.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-library green; the two respelling tests go with the pass.

title: The library's test-only tree and navigator API goes: archive_tree's flatten, first_path, Node::entries and count, project_tree's Node::entries, folders::tree_and_groups, ProjectGroup's display_title and explicit_name, Navigation::toggle_trash
detail: The app lays its tree through archive_tree::walk and find, and filters its own first photo and counts (Archive::first_shown, shown_count); it calls folders::tree and groups_of apart, and folds the trash row through `unfolded` itself. The removed functions were the unfiltered twins of those or forwarders, reached only by their own tests. folders::groups calls groups_of on the tree directly.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-library green. archive_tree's fold test now reads walk alone, with its twin; the tree-and-groups check compares groups_of on a tree holding the survey's empty folders with groups, with its twin. roll8's an_index_rebuilt_from_the_sidecars_finds_every_frame fails on the reference roll on a line this change does not reach: the folder's marker on disk names another roll id and stock than its oracle (folders::rolls, untouched).

title: migrate::density leaves the settings crate: no migration used the oracle, and its 'kernel' window had drifted from the kernel
detail: The windows' move onto the density axis runs in before_1_0::in_density, on the raw JSON; migrate::density held a second copy of that x DMAX and two closed forms of stages 4-6 that only tests read. Its apply_levels still clamped under the black where the stage 4-7 kernel passes a density on (stage47.rs). Each outside check now states what it means: codec_checks writes the x DMAX expectation inline; the real-frame check (oni-pipeline swift_checks) takes its windows from migrate::document on a document aged under the density axis, so it renders through the step that runs, and keeps its frozen clamping kernel as a local oracle; its closed-form residue, a copy of the stage 4-7 CPU-GPU check, goes; auto_levels' simulation measures the density over its window itself; oni-app's levels checks read the window as the kernel's scalar reference runs it, the floored-track twin through pipeline::clip. No migration's output moves.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-settings, oni-measure auto_levels and oni-app's levels tests green. On the reference roll's DSC_6432 the migrated windows render the frozen kernel within 2.4e-7 on the GPU thumbnail and 1.8e-7 on the full frame's CPU reference; the unmigrated twin parts by 0.93. The always-on proof of the two closed forms' identity (density.rs's own tests) goes with them: the identity is proven on a real frame only, with the reference roll and a GPU.

title: Two dead stored fields go: lensCorrected and rollReferenceDeclined
detail: lensCorrected was only ever written (its default, the copy on import, before_1_0's mark on a document with dust strokes): the lens warp runs on the separate lensCorrection block, and the pinned decode applies no lens profile. rollReferenceDeclined was never set true nor read, only reset to false or copied. Each leaves its struct member, default, field-table row, frame family entry, preset exclusion, the frame's OWN entry, its copies in imported and unconverted, and its lines in the corpus readings. A sidecar holding either key still reads: PipelineSettings ignores unknown keys, and an older build fills a missing one from its struct default. No migration or render reads them; kept Auto WB fingerprints move once with the settings' shape, to the same outcome.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-settings, oni-core and oni-measure green; the corpus goldens lose their two lines each. New codec check: a document holding both keys at version 0, 3 and 70 reads equal to one without them and is written back without them (twin: a key the settings read, captureStops, moves the frame). The out-of-repo wide-corpus goldens (ONI_SIDECAR_GOLDENS) need the same two lines dropped.

title: One field table names each field's family: the three hand-kept name lists, the hand-written look copy, the placement checker and the frame's OWN list go
detail: Each PipelineSettings field was named in the struct, in the fields! table, and again in look_settings::FIELDS, FRAME_FIELDS or roll_settings::FIELD_NAMES; Field::family searched those lists by string, and two tests existed only to keep them in step. The table now carries each field's family in its row (`Mode => "mode", mode, Roll;`), so a field has one family by construction and family() returns Family. The table and FieldSet move to oni-settings (fields.rs, ordered.rs beside it; oni-core re-exports `fields`), so look_settings::copied becomes a loop of Field::carry over the Look family, the same 18 members cloned. Edit Together's OWN (the frame family plus sourceEncoding, which a roll field never reaches outside a slide's own) is the frame family. Serde names and the struct are unchanged: no sidecar byte moves.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-settings and oni-core green; the workspace's tests build. The table test (every declared field in order, with its twin) stays the guard; the codec check now holds the serialised document's keys to the table's names (twin: a table short of one field). Preset boxes and lens/paperless pastes read the Look family.

title: The pipette keeps the one aggregate ever used, the density mean: Space, Statistic and their median and transmittance arms go
detail: Every call passed RETAINED_SPACE (density) and RETAINED_STATISTIC (mean); the median and the transmittance mean were a research alternative the constants had already refused, and the mode a read took served only the transmittance arm. pipette::read takes the plane, the point and the radius; its mean folds each channel in the same order and bounds the answer onto the window as before, so the base pick, the key and every roll's black read the same.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-measure green (the example sensor_colours builds); the test of the two spaces goes with them, the rim and edge checks keep their twins.

title: blocks::Report and the cell naming (A1, F5...) go: nothing outside the tests read them
detail: Each reading carried three name vectors and a copy of its grid for the Blocks self-check's diagnostics, which no reader took. With Grid::name, name_of, Report and Reading.report gone, the ends are a fold of the kept cells' tail values by the same `<` comparison from the first kept cell on, so they are bit for bit the values first_min and first_max chose, NaN included.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-measure green; the naming asserts go, the window check reads the grid over the window itself (Grid::new(right).columns == 8).

title: One ordered list of the typed migration steps: reading and both branches of document run the steps past the grain's through typed_steps
detail: migrate::reading and the two branches of migrate::document each re-listed the same twelve typed steps (digital film to departure), so a new step had to be added three times. They now call one private typed_steps, each passing what it passed before: the stored settings to the digital film's step (none on a document's earlier branch) and to the datasheet's, its scanner and its former print. A pure refactor: every step, its order and its inputs stay as they were. The fuller fold the proposal sketched (one read_through for sidecar and document, unfiled facts) was not done: it would refuse a named document whose envelope fields do not type and read a current one with a malformed scanner key, where today the opposite holds, and the facts-asking steps (matrices, strokes, grain, scan line) and the two envelopes still differ by path.
outcome: cargo test -p oni-settings green but for sweep_pass's unix-permission twin, which cannot hold where the build's scratch folder lies on exFAT (the T7): no step's output moves, the corpus readings unchanged.

title: The one-off look and probe examples leave: brightness, colour and Lighting strips, paper black, enlarger states, slide paper, heal probe and the dust census
detail: Each served one investigation whose outcome is logged (Brightness #3280, the heal #2400, auto De-dust #1075/#1700/#1982, Paper blacks #3066/#3092, the slide paper #3234, the Lighting and colour strips #3610-#3616, the enlarger states #3340-#3343); no script, doc or check runs them, yet every API change had to keep them compiling under scripts/lint. 832 lines; any one comes back from git when an investigation needs it. No render or setting moves: they are auto-discovered examples, outside the app and the tests.

title: The Apple-against-LibRaw decoder research tools leave: decoder_fit, blocks and dump
detail: decoder_fit fitted LibRaw to the CIRAWFilter dumps the Swift app wrote, blocks and dump wrote the matching LibRaw grids and RenderDump files; they served the camera-matrix decision, withdrawn on 2026-11-02, and their driver scripts/decoder-gap is gone. 208 lines; nothing in crates or scripts ran them. docs/research/decoder-apple-vs-libraw.md stays as history with a line saying where they went. No render moves: examples only.

title: The sensor-colours prototype leaves with the decode colours only it read: examples/sensor_colours.rs, Colours and decode_in
detail: sensor_colours compared the roll in three decode colours against the Swift app's base and rendered the removed faces; its proposal (#181) was never adopted, and it was the only caller of decode_in with Colours::Sensor or SensorUnbalanced. The decode now has its one conversion, the camera's matrix: Colours, decode_in, the colours parameter of converted_on, decoded and decoded_by, and the two Sensor checks go; the singular-matrix check reads the matrix conversion (still refused on a zero matrix, its twin accepted on the Z f). The cache key keeps the literal Matrix, so every decode kept on disk stays valid; the Matrix arm is unchanged, so no render moves. docs/research/sensor-colours.md stays as history with a line saying where the prototype went. cargo test -p oni-decode --lib green (38).

title: The keycap's comparison against the Swift bench's sheet leaves, with the parameters only it varied
detail: reference.rs loaded the dead Swift KeycapLab's export, absent on every machine, so its check and both twins returned before testing anything, and its sweep and dump were ignored. Sigmas, SIGMAS and compose_with (its backing colour and sigmas) existed only for it: compose now reads BLUR_SIGMA_PER_RADIUS and SHADOW_SIGMA_PER_RADIUS where it blurred through SIGMAS, and solid loses the clip every caller passed as None. The png dev-dependency goes (hakari unchanged). Every keycap pixel stays bit for bit: the same f64 products, and a coverage once multiplied by 1.0 now taken as is. cargo test -p oni-keycap green (16).

title: One scratch-folder helper in oni-fixtures for the 26 identical copies across the checks
detail: The same six-line function (a folder named after the check and the process, removed then created) was written out in 26 test files. oni_fixtures::scratch(label) holds it once (temp_dir()/oni-<label>-<pid>); each site keeps its old prefix in its label (scratch("corpus-killed")), so no two checks of one test binary share a folder, and the sibling modules that borrowed a helper (oni-decode's frames, oni-settings' migrate checks) call it the same way. oni-tldb takes oni-fixtures as a dev-dependency (hakari unchanged). The 11 sites that built under CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR (decode, colour and core swift_checks; library trash_refusals; settings grain_seed, swift_checks, foreign_sidecar, scan_line, guarded_writes, real_files, sweep_pass) now write in the system's temporary folder, as the other 15 did: a library cannot read that variable, and a target directory on exFAT no longer sees the sweep and swift checks fail there. The 9 helpers of another shape (a file written, a roll mirrored, support and caches made, a folder never created, a canonical path, a thread id) stay. Test code only.

title: One launcher for the window checks: 88 hand-made app launches become common::launch
detail: Each window check opened the GPU, made a temp root of its own, built an empty archive's store, the engine and Options { support, caches, picker: None }, set the scale and size and showed the window, then read the folder and double-clicked its first frame: about 25 lines copied into 118 files. common now holds it once: rig() reads ONI_SHOTS itself (else the target's shots folder, so 25 checks that wrote to the temp folder land beside the others), Root names a check's folder, empties it and removes it when it drops (canonical() spells it as the app keeps paths), launch(root) with .with(|o| ...) for the options a check changes, .size and .scale in points, .show() returning an App whose fields drop the shell before the root and the GPU, and App::read and edit_first for the opening steps. 88 launches are ported (panel_bindings::opened, film_effects::opened, stock_hero, full_release and their callers among them), with the closing drop(shell); remove_dir_all(&root) lines the guard makes redundant; a launch that drops its shell midway, builds its own store or engine, or relaunches in one process keeps its own code. Every assertion and twin stays as written; only the launch and its cleanup move.
outcome: 163 files, 1270 lines in and 2781 out (net 1511 fewer). The window binary passes 303 of 303 before and after on this Mac; each pass ran its checks first (19, then 38), clippy on the window target is clean.

title: The Scanner face's density stage leaves the GPU: its kernel, stage and rows, the unread SCANNER_LIFT and the CPU replica of a render nothing lays
detail: No recipe laid stages::scanner_density: a legacy print renders through stage 4-7, then oni_finish or warmed_paper (encode, cube, scanner_output); only tests/stages.rs and tests/branches.rs called it. scanner::replica ran the measured table on the CPU 'as the GPU renders it', which the GPU never did; only its own test in scanner_tests read it, the keypad's offset and on_legacy_print keeping their tests. oni_render::SCANNER_LIFT had no reader: scanner::LIFT is the one read. Gone: scanner_density.wgsl, wgsl::SCANNER_DENSITY, its kernel and stage, ScannerDensity::rows, SCANNER_LIFT, replica and its test, the two GPU checks of the kernel. The CPU scanner_density, ScannerDensity and fitted_density stay for the Look Lab (look_lab/pro.rs, examples/look_lab_strip.rs).
outcome: No render moves: legacy_print's CPU and GPU fingerprints of format 45 unchanged; stages, branches and the pipeline's unit tests green.

title: The Scanner output loses the Contrast lane no render sets
detail: Every production call of stages::scanner_output (looked, oni_finish, warmed_paper) passed a contrast of 0, so the kernel's k.z != 0 branch never ran; only the removed replica and the offline examples/look_lab_strip.rs passed print.contrast, the example now printing without that bend. Gone: ScannerOutput.contrast, the stage's argument, bent() and the branch in the WGSL and its CPU reference; the branch check now separates warmth at share 0 and 0.1, its twin the share 0.02 off.
outcome: No render moves: legacy_print's CPU and GPU fingerprints of format 45 and looks unchanged; stages and branches green.

title: Pipeline::image lays the chain itself: no drawn, no chain taking the legacy print's settings apart
detail: image called drawn, which called chain with the frame and a precomputed copy of it, behind a clippy allow on too many arguments. That copy was always scanner::on_legacy_print(frame), which moves only the gains, so legacy.and_then(PipelineSettings::legacy) always equalled the frame's own legacy(). image now derives the laid settings itself and reads s.legacy(); every stage reads the same settings, so the graph is the same. tests/scanner_positive.rs renders through Pipeline::image with a default request (scale 1, reference 128, as the bench passed); its test 'a negative on a legacy print renders as before bit for bit' compared a render with itself, former adding 1.5 − 1.5 stops on a negative and a monochrome, and leaves; the slide's twin renders the frame 1.5 stops over, as on_legacy_print reads no print exposure.
outcome: No render moves: legacy_print's CPU and GPU fingerprints of format 45 unchanged; scanner_positive green, its twin still refusing the slide 1.5 stops over.

title: Texture's ten-pass stages leave: the moments and coefficients passes, kept only as a GPU oracle
detail: The pipeline's Texture folds both steps into the blurs' taps (Before::Moments, Before::Coeff, on TEXTURE_MATH); stages::texture_moments and texture_coeff, the MOMENTS and COEFF kernels and their two WGSL wrappers served only fused.rs's GPU-against-GPU ten-pass oracle, two per-pixel checks in stages.rs and the cost bench. fused.rs now judges the seven-pass Texture against the chain step by step on the CPU (cpu::gaussian, texture_moments, texture_coeff, texture), a reference independent of the GPU, its twin at gain × 1.1; the fold checks of each step, with their twins, stay. The cost bench compares the seven passes with one per-pixel pass.
outcome: Texture against its CPU chain: at 780 px (narrow blur under its floor) error 1.80e-7, twin 5.96e-3; at 4000 px error 2.15e-7, twin 9.36e-3. fused and stages green; no render moves.

title: Stage 4-7 loses the print shaping Lighting on the negative replaced: Contrast, zones, each channel's filter, contrast and mids
detail: Stage47 is built from settings only by conversion::unprinted, reached only through lit() on print.unlit(), which zeroes contrast, shadows, highlights, the three filters and each channel's contrast and mids; every other producer copies it or starts from Stage47::rest(). So contrasted(x, 0) returned x, and the zones, the mids and the filters' luma levelling never ran. Gone from the kernel, its CPU reference and its uniform (13 rows to 9): print_contrast, print_zones, own_stops, own_contrast and own_mid, the WGSL quarter_pass, quartered and midded, the contrast family of both preludes, which nothing else read, the levelling block, the branch cases 'negative contrast, double quarters', 'channel tone with filters' and 'channel tone', and each_channel_s_own_tone_reaches_the_kernel. The carry held + (p − held) stays in both: a share past 2 rounds through it, and the pinned renders keep that rounding. The Rust quartered and midded stay for kernel/negative.rs. kernel_oracle.rs keeps judging the 1.0 migration's replica (Print::rendered) against an independent reference: the former print block frozen in the test file, on the kernel's own windows (cpu::windowed). oni-colour's roll #8 fixture no longer passes its sidecar's Contrast to a kernel that has none.
