outcome: Every pinned render is bit for bit unchanged: colour_on_negative and lighting_on_negative at rest, exposure_departure CPU and GPU (format 61), legacy_print CPU and GPU (format 45). kernel_oracle: the replica against the frozen print 2.98e-7 (twins unfiltered 6.1e-2, apart 8.1e-2, untoned 2.7e-1); a former document through it worst 0.0599 against 0.1188 unmigrated. branches, stages, channel_points and digital_negative green.

title: The window checks' launcher in a file of its own, under the size ceiling, and the masks check's options on lines of their own
detail: common/mod.rs had grown past 400 lines with the shared launcher (#3780): Root, App and Launch move to common/launch.rs; the masks check's one 300-character launch line is split, the wide-line ratchet held at 78.

title: The black and white profiles drop the other developments nothing read
detail: Each of the 27 black and white stock files carried every other development its sheet prints, 57,000 lines built into the binary that no code read (Silver::read takes the chosen curve alone). The data-sheet script no longer writes them; the chosen development and every render unchanged.

title: Fujifilm Provia 100F from its sheet: its green and blue, hidden under red's stroke, take red's points; offered to digital photos and projected
detail: scripts/datasheet-profiles.py convert_slide takes, for each reversal film, the curves its sheet hides under another's stroke: past its last traced point such a curve takes the covering one's points, listed under inferred in the profile's provenance. Provia 100F (AF3-036E) joins SLIDES with green and blue under red (the dataset: traced to log H -1.50 and -2.16, coincident with red within line width below), its profile spanning log H -2.48 to 1.74 written into fujifilm-provia100.json's new film block fujifilm-provia-100f (daylight, generic-c41, the windows' rest as its reference, as every reversal film's). Only Provia's profile was generated; Velvia 50, Velvia 100 and Ektachrome E100 rebuilt by the changed function are byte-identical to their files. Couplers fitted by examples/coupler_fit.rs on the Provia 100F reference chart (slide mode: no diagonal, folding refused). A roll on Provia now projects on Provia instead of Ektachrome E100; the checks naming a slide stock no sheet profiles take Kodachrome 64. Counts: 79 virtual films, 79 sheet films.
outcome: Provia 100F's couplers [[0, 0.181, 0.18], [0, 0, 0], [0.132, 0.053, 0]]: the chart's loss to its reference 0.0021 (mean dE00 5.28, ColorChecker chroma 1.06 of the reference's) against 0.0031 with no cross term and 0.076 on the common matrix. Its scene's 18 % grey projected at a* +3.49 b* +0.28 (Velvia 100 +6.10 -1.22, Ektachrome E100 +5.53 -3.90). A digital photo (P1073074) on Provia against the reference: mean dE00 6.94, chroma 0.83 of the reference's (common matrix 19.4, 2.03). tests/projection.rs: Provia's profile reads, falls with exposure (4x the grey passes over twice the light) and projects its bare film as the screen's white within 1e-3; its range spans 4.22 log and holds green's 18 % grey (twin: green and blue as the sheet traces them hold none). oni-settings and oni-pipeline tests pass, oni-app's stock, slide and roll card unit checks (42) and the window checks on stock and slide (29 of 29).

title: A digital roll is measured as a scanned roll is: Prepare reads each photo's lights on its film's reference, the windows' white at the roll's lights, the bare film the black
detail: Cause (owner's investigation on Session vol, 2026-11-24): a digital photo stood on its stock's fixed reference, its windows spanning the film's whole latitude (Portra 800: the bare film about six stops under a scene grey, the white about five over), while a scene spans far less (the aerial cliffs about four stops, from -2.5 to +1.5): the photos used some 40 % of the window and printed flat and washed. The owner's own Prepare of the exported virtual negatives looked right. Fix: PREPARE ROLL on Digital reads every photo off the measure's thread, with progress and Stop, at its film's gains (the bare film neutral, exact): key::digital_lights takes the reference channel's light end in front of the levels as a share of the film reference's span; roll::digital_lights reads the roll's at DEPTH[1], where a scanned roll's white is read; store::roll::digital lays StockReference::spanned(lights), each channel's white scaled alike so a grey keeps one share, the black on the bare film (owner's pick over a measured black). A photo never prepared keeps the film's own reference.
outcome: Cliffs roll (P1073080-103): lights 0.60-0.77 of Portra 800's span per photo, the roll's 0.755. On Royal, six cliffs, mean L* / C* / L* 1 %-99 %: fixed reference 45.7 / 23.7 / 19-87, measured white on the base 64.2 / 22.0 / 36-95 (a measured black too gave 52.8 / 25.5 / 20-92, not kept). Checks: the spanned reference keeps a grey on one share (twin: one channel moved tints it), the roll's lights at the white's depth whatever one glaring photo (twin: the brightest photo), a digital roll lands on the spanned windows (twin: never the film's own span).

title: Every print is made on a paper, Prepare's window on the paper's useful range, no grey placed; ONI Standard, the data sheets' mean curve on a neutral paper, is the default
detail: Owner's decisions (2026-11-24). (1) One print path: ONI's print without a paper, the Virtual enlarger switch, Print on paper and the neutral paper (paper::neutral, PipelineSettings::paperless) are gone; a frame naming no paper prints on the default, a positive read as its own negative too; a legacy print keeps its own render to the bit, its former grey-anchored time moved verbatim into paper::legacy (all 26 legacy fixtures unmoved). The exact-inversion print curve begun earlier (Stage47::inversion, NEGATIVE_GAMMA) was dropped as dead code. (2) ONI Standard (stocks/oni-standard.json, scripts/oni-standard-paper.py): D(s) = 2.484 / (1 + exp(5.587 (s - 0.354))) over the window share, one curve on the three layers, pure dyes, no D-min, its file's useful_range [0, 1]; PaperStock::default. Royal Digital and the others stay selectable; Portra Endura's key still reads Royal. (3) Convention A (paper::placing): every paper's useful range is D-min + 0.04 to 0.9 Dmax on its neutral (or its file's useful_range); the bare film exposes the black end and the window's white the white end, frame-independent, no time solved and no grey placed; each layer's log-exposure offset (the CC filtration shown) is solved once per paper by Gauss-Newton so equal shares print neutral along the whole range, between each channel's own ends, on a cube root of light (before: a Newton solve per paper on the layers' exposures printing a plain RAW's grey neutral on the paper's white, then per frame a time solved to show the reference grey at that grey). Brightness's reach is sought from the pick toward the window's white. (4) A digital stock's reference lays each channel's black on the bare film, no light, and its white on the sensor's saturation, the decode's 5000 K neutral at the white level, 2^0.48 (oni_settings::white::DEFAULT_BASELINE_EV, moved there from oni-decode); nothing solved on greys, a film's cast its preset's. The grey Lighting turns about stays the window's one share for every frame. Sidecar format 72 (migrate::every_paper, migrate::sensor_white): Print on paper off lands on ONI Standard, a digital photo moves onto its stock's new reference with its hand's moves kept, a legacy print keeps its own. Interface: the Paper block shows on every frame printed on a paper (picker, Print lift, filtration), help texts rewritten in English, French and Spanish.
outcome: Checks (tests/every_paper.rs): ONI Standard prints s = 0 on black and s = 1 on white and follows the logistic within 1.9e-4 (twin: Royal Digital 0.067 off it); every paper lays the bare film at 0.9 Dmax and the window's white at D-min + 0.04, the same whatever the frame (twin: the legacy grey-anchored time lays the bare film 0.7 log H elsewhere); a neutral ramp prints neutral on ONI Standard to 0 (twin: Royal Digital 0.014, its filtration halving the unfiltered 0.027). Pinned folds moved only on non-legacy pipes. Headless at 900 px, mean L* / mean C* / L* 1 %-99 %: P1073094 (digital, its sidecar prepared under #3789) ONI Standard 36.4 / 23.8 / 5.2-90.7, Royal Digital 33.2 / 20.9 / 4.6-87.7; DSC_6452 (roll #8) ONI Standard 23.6 / 11.1 / 0.7-97.0, Royal Digital 21.8 / 8.6 / 0.7-96.5. Portra 800's grey ramp shows its film's own crossover in the mids, 160NC's up to C* 24: left to the presets. The Frontier's fit reaches D 4.7-5.3, so its black end lies at D 4.6 and its shadows print far deeper than a data-sheet paper's.

title: Prepare on a digital roll measures nothing on its photos again (#3789 reverted): the roll lands at once on its films' own references
detail: Owner's call (2026-11-24): nothing is measured on image content. key::digital_lights, roll::digital_lights, StockReference::spanned, the lights argument of store::roll::digital and the measure job of app/prepare/digital.rs are gone with their checks; a digital photo's window is its sensor's range, black the bare film, white the sensor's saturation (#3790).
outcome: The code of #3789 reversed whole; scripts/check and scripts/lint green.

title: A photo on Royal Digital, the default paper before format 72, leaves it: no paper at format 73; a legacy print keeps its Royal
detail: Owner's call (2026-11-24): Prepare laid Royal Digital on every frame while it was the default, so nearly every photo named it without the person choosing it; format 72 left them there. Begun as a move onto ONI Standard at format 72 and never committed: the same evening the owner made a paper a choice (#3793), so migrate::optional_paper takes the paper away instead. A frame holding a legacy print, laid or not, keeps the paper it names, so its render stays to the bit; any other paper stays.
outcome: Check (migrate::optional_paper): a pre-72 Royal photo names no paper (twins: Royal named at format 72 stays, Ektacolor Edge stays, a legacy print keeps Royal). The pins the first form left failing hold again (tests/lighting_on_negative.rs BEFORE, tests/exposure_departure.rs BEFORE_CPU and BEFORE_GPU): their stored pipes name their paper again after the read, the migration's own move checked apart.

title: The render is the pure inversion; a paper is a choice laid over it, none by default
detail: Owner's decision (2026-11-24, on Roll #8 rendered outside the app): a negative already holds the log of the light, so the render is its pure inversion, as a black and white negative's; a paper is a choice laid over it, and ONI Standard does not suit him, on real negatives too. This reverts #3790's rule that every print is made on a paper and keeps its placement for a paper named. (1) Render: oni-render's inversion kernel (kernel/inversion.rs, wgsl/inversion.wgsl), laid past stage 4-7's window in the same GPU pass, where a paper's would be: each channel's window share, held within 0 and 1, read as the display's sRGB code and decoded to light in the Rec. 2020 working space, no other curve. Stage47::paper (an Option) became Stage47::shown: Shown::Curve (a legacy print's own curve, or a measure's shares as they are), Shown::Paper, Shown::Inversion. (2) Settings: print_paper absent is no paper. PipelineSettings::paper() is the paper named where the frame takes one and a file defines it (a key no file defines prints on no paper until its file is back); shows_inversion() says the rest; fitting_paper() and on_paper() are gone, so rest(), a digital photo's included, Prepare the Roll (balance::written, store::roll::digital) and on_stock() name none. Brightness and Print lift are read by a paper alone and stay stored. A legacy print, a projected slide, a measure upstream of the print and a look shown as it is are unmoved; Lighting acts on the negative as before, Exposure holding Prepare's black and white. (3) Interface: the papers' menu opens on No paper, first and checked at rest (Lit::Paper holds an Option, a line's index its place past that first); the Paper block shows on every frame a paper may print (PanelState.paper-offered), with Print lift, the filtration line and Lighting's Brightness on a paper alone; Colour compensation shows on a laid legacy print's own curve alone; the Paper and Lighting helps rewritten in English, French and Spanish. The launch prewarms the inversion's passes and a paper's. (4) Sidecar format 73 (migrate::optional_paper, in place of every_paper): a frame on its format's default paper names none, ONI Standard at 72 and, before 72, Royal Digital (#3792) or Print on paper off; any other paper stays; a frame holding a legacy print keeps the paper it names, the neutral paper where it printed with Print on paper off; a build before 73 opens such a file read-only. (5) Documents: CLAUDE.md's decisions, stocks/README.md, the research examples' headers. One line of film.rs's own check changed, its twin: a scene a stop over the sensor's saturation no longer prints past white, the share being held at 1, so a stop under it prints under white.
outcome: Checks: kernel::inversion's own check and tests/inversion.rs (the scalar reference against the owner's formula written on its own, within 2.5e-3 of light on its gains and windows; Prepare's black on pure black and its white on pure white; twins a display gamma's power, the share as light, ONI Standard, a legacy print's curve; the graph against the reference, the kernel alone and under Lighting; which frames show it; Exposure holding the ends), migrate::optional_paper (three checks, each with its twins), the papers' menu and the Paper block in the window (tests/window/paper.rs, paper_menu.rs). Pins: with the former rules emulated in this code (a frame naming none on ONI Standard, the former step), all 225 oni-pipeline checks passed on their pins untouched, so papers, legacy prints and slides render to the bit as before, on the CPU and the GPU. Then colour_on_negative.rs, lighting_on_negative.rs and exposure_departure.rs name ONI Standard where they relied on the default (their pins unmoved) and each gained three pipes on no paper (their pins moved by those alone); legacy_print/fingerprints.json: 23 of 50 moved, every one a frame holding no legacy print and naming no paper, the 27 others unmoved. Roll #8, 38 frames, the app's code against the owner's reference (sans_courbe.py) on the same framed scans: the GPU's print stage is the app's formula within 1e-4 of an 8-bit code; against the reference it stands 0.33, 0.85 and 3.67 codes off at worst on red, green and blue (0.18, 0.50 and 1.99 on average), all of it the density guard's pedestal, which the app reads over and the reference past, largest on blue where the gain is +1.23 stops; median L* 37.4 against the reference's 37.3, 0.26 apart at worst on a frame. The app driven on copies of Roll #8 (profile app, in the background): the launch migrates the 38 sidecars to format 73, no paper; ONI_BENCH=flows picks, opens by a double click, edits and returns on three frames with no failure; ONI_BENCH=papers lights the nine papers over a frame on no paper, each moving the photo, nothing written; an Exposure drag renders on a frame on no paper, on Ektacolor Edge, on a legacy print's own curve and on a legacy print laid on Royal Digital, each sidecar keeping what the migration says. scripts/check and scripts/lint green.

title: The pure inversion bounds nothing: a share past the window's ends carries on along the sRGB code, the output clip alone holding it
detail: The inversion's kernel (#3793) held each window share within 0 and 1 before decoding it, as the owner's reference script did for its own display; the chain's rule is that the output clip is the only place information is bounded (axis::pipeline::clip). Nothing downstream needs a bounded input: Curves hold their table's index themselves, the vignette, the saturation curve, Texture and the detail stage each floor their own powers and logarithms, and a paper or a legacy print's curve already hands them light past white. The share is now left free: under the bare film the code's straight foot carries on, past the window's white its power does, monotone all along; between the ends the render is the reference's, and on screen, past the output clip, the same everywhere. A highlight past Prepare's white is kept for a later stage (Curves, the vignette) to bring back. film.rs's own check is as it was before #3793: a scene a stop over the sensor's saturation prints past white again.
outcome: Checks: kernel::inversion (the curve rising from under none to past one; twin, a share held at the window's white); tests/inversion.rs (past the output clip the stage is the owner's reference within 2.5e-3 of light; under the bare film it shows under none and past the white over one, the clip laying them on black and white; the graph against the reference on shares from -0.3 to 1.4). oni-measure's dust check holds its twin on no paper again, a dust past white keeping its colour. Pins: with the three pipes on no paper left out, colour_on_negative, lighting_on_negative and exposure_departure fold to the constants of before #3793, so papers, legacy prints and slides are unmoved; with them the four pins move; legacy_print/fingerprints.json: 22 of 50 on the CPU and 19 on the GPU, every one a frame holding no legacy print and naming no paper.

title: The neutral film: a digital photo's default virtual negative, its window's share the screen's code of the scene's light, first in the film list
detail: Owner's decisions (2026-11-24). A film of no character (stocks/generic-neutral.json, key neutral, VirtualStock::NEUTRAL): each layer's density above a clear bare film is its range times the sRGB code of its own working-space channel's light over the sensor's saturation; no spectrum, no coupler, pure dyes, the scene's own light (Balance::Scene, no lighting matrix). A tabled curve on a log exposure cannot lay no light exactly on the bare film, nor a spectral table give each layer its own channel, so the film has its own analytic kernel (oni-render neutral_negative, WGSL and CPU reference, a FilmBlock's neutral flag, its profile holding range alone); stage 4 adds a pedestal to every scan, which bends a film's share by 1.2e-3 at mid-window, so the neutral film's scan is written less that pedestal and its read density is the code exactly. Range 1.0, a real colour negative's window (Portra 800's green spans 0.99), as gains and filters lie in density. PipelineSettings::rest shoots a new digital photo on it; a photo storing no film or an unknown key still reads Portra 800 (VirtualStock::default unchanged), so no stored photo moves and no migration is needed. Lighting reads it back through its own curve tabled on log exposure (negative::developed). The film panel names its light ("The scene's own light, as its decode balanced it"); Neutral is translated (Neutre, Neutra) and listed first, under Generic, never offered to a roll. migrate::own_film leaves the neutral film out of the films a photo of then could stand on.
outcome: tests/neutral_negative.rs: GPU against CPU within 1e-4 (twins: 1 % more exposure, the pedestal kept, channels swapped); the window's share against the code of light over saturation 1.8e-7 at worst over 13 stops, black and saturation included (twin, pedestal kept: 1.2e-3); the app's reading against the definition 0; the pure inversion gives the scene back within 0.0012 % (twin, a window 0.01 D off: 2.2 %); another range reads the same shares; the film's exposure is the light's. On two real photos through the same CPU references, by a tool kept outside the repository (decoded scenes of P1073094 and P1073076, 1200 px): share against the code 1.8e-7 at worst, round trip 0.00001 % median, 0.00006 % at the 99th centile, 0.0001 % at worst, median share on the negative 0.254 and 0.249; the resting grain's relative strength 5 %, 8.5 %, 15 %, 20 to 28 % at 1, 3, 5 and 7 stops under the white. Re-pinned for the new default: counts of shipped files and stocks (112 files, 105 films, 80 virtual films), tests that named Portra 800 as a new photo's film now pin it (tests/paper/frames.rs digital(), digital_negative, virtual_film, measured_dyes, settings virtual_film) or name the neutral film (store digital, levels editor).

title: The grain lies on the developed film, uniform in the share of each layer's window; its curve by tone rests flat
detail: Owner's decision (2026-11-24). The grain was a texture in stops on the scene before the film; it now lies on what the film hands the chain: a negative's scan (data sheet's or neutral), a slide's dyes before the projector, a look's positive. On a negative the kernel reads each layer's light as its share of its window (its bare film, the reading's pedestal and each window over their mean: GrainedNegative), lays the same stops on the three, deepens the hue where the picture darkens, and codes the film back: one share of every layer's window moves, so a grey stays grey on a masked film (laid as plain stops, 160NC's neutral ramp gained 4 C*ab). Amount's top spreads a sixteenth of the stock's window (GRAIN_WINDOW, the approved prototype's 0.0629 rounded), 1.6 % at the Grain a digital photo opens with; GrainCurve::REST is the whole grain at every tone. Its tones are the print of the grey holding each film light. grain::grain returns none on a frame shot on no virtual film: a scanned negative takes no grain at the source. Halation stays on the scene before the film. Pipeline::projected is folded into the chain.
outcome: tests/neutral_negative.rs: at Amount 1 the share's spread is 0.0626 at every tone from 7 stops under the white to 1 (within 3 %), the pure inversion's relative spread 93 %, 57 %, 33 %, 19 % (twin, the same field on the scene: 14.5 % at every tone); a negative, a black and white and a slide roll take no grain. Kernel checks: a grey's layers stay within 2e-5 of one share on a masked negative (twin, plain stops: over 5e-3), the hue deepens where the picture darkens. Every legacy print of a scanned negative renders to the bit (tests/legacy_print.rs, CPU and GPU). Re-pinned because the grain moved: exposure_departure BEFORE_GPU, legacy_print's one digital photo with grain (corpus/37-digital/001, GPU), 38 corpus goldens (the rest curve's five points), grain passes rerun by a notch (1 instead of 3), the shadow chroma bound at the colour's top (1.7, the flat rest laying the whole grain there). Grain checks written for the scene now read the film's light (tests/grain*.rs).

title: A new digital photo renders its scene end to end: the neutral film through the pure inversion's own kernel, with no paper
detail: The neutral film (#3800, #3801) merged with the pure inversion (#3793, #3794). PipelineSettings::rest lays a new digital photo on the neutral film and on no paper; the check that redid the sRGB decoding by hand now reads the render's kernel (cpu::inversion), and a_photo_on_the_neutral_film_renders_its_scene_through_the_pure_inversion renders scene pixels over 13 stops through the chain's CPU references and whole on the GPU (Pipeline::render, grain and neighbourhood stages off).
outcome: The render lies within 0.0012 % of the scene's light over the sensor's saturation on the CPU and 0.0034 % on the GPU, no light on black (twins: on ONI Standard 66 % off, on Portra 800 216 %). Re-pinned after the merge, each for the grain's new place alone: exposure_departure BEFORE_GPU (its CPU fold is canvas's to the bit; its three digital pipes carry Grain 0.25) and the GPU fingerprint of legacy_print's one digital photo with grain (corpus/37-digital/001; its CPU fingerprint and every other document's two are canvas's).

title: A still colour negative is read by its paper's gaze, under its own filtration and uncoupled: Portra 800 and forty others from their two sheets; sidecar format 74
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-25, "ligne 1"): image = Reader ( Gaze x Film ( scene ) ). The film is its sheet as before; the gaze replaces the camera's scan (5500 K lamp, 1931 observer): an enlarger's 3200 K lamp through the bare film and its dyes exposes its paper's three layers on their spectral sensitivities, each channel the density its layer sees above the bare film, which reads one (film::gaze, the projection kernel's table and matrix, no new kernel). scripts/datasheet-profiles.py lays the sensitivities of four papers in their files ("sensitivity"; Endura Premier and Ektacolor Edge beside their curves, Crystal Archive Super Type P and Supreme alone, read-only papers no menu lists), by the usual rule past the printed points, and pairs each of the 41 still colour negatives holding a profile with its paper ("read_by": the film's own sheet where it names one, else the owner's choice, said in the profile's provenance), couplers of zero. The film's filtration, each layer's exposure offset laying a scene's mid grey on one share of the three windows (bare film to the sensor's saturation), is a constant of the film derived from the two sheets like its reference (gaze::filtration, bisected a layer in turn; stored to 1e-5 log exposure) and laid in the bake as a gain on each layer's light. Cine negatives (Verita, Vision3), named by no paper, keep the camera's scan and their couplers: the looks' internegative, Vision3 50D, is unchanged. Sidecar format 74 (migrate::paper_gaze): a digital photo moves from its stock's former reference onto the new one, its hand's moves kept; migrate::sensor_white now lands on format 73's references. Tests written for Portra 800's camera scan, couplers and reference chart now read a cine stock (digital_scan, couplers); the reference comparison is gone with the fit it checked.
outcome: tests/paper_gaze.rs: Endura Premier's gaze on Portra 800 at mid scale within 0.004 of the prototype's (twin, the camera's scan: 0.58 off); every bare film reads one; every film's stored filtration is its sheets' derivation and lays a mid grey within 2e-3 of one share (twin, Portra 800 unfiltered: 0.019 apart); against the prototype's 41 filtrations, Kodak's within 0.0003 log, Fujifilm's up to 0.71 log on Fujifilm 400: its papers' sheets start at 405 nm, where the prototype fell 0.05 log a nm, and the prototype's solve cycled on Fujifilm 400 and Superia 100, whose stored values did not equal the shares. Portra 800: filtration +0.286 and +0.533 stop, grey scale within C* 4.4 (5.6 stops under saturation to white), 6.4 unfiltered. Its window share against the prototype's on six photos, from the layer exposures the app wrote: mean 0.0005 of the window at worst, 99th centile 0.0012, worst 0.0056. Each film's grey scale is printed by the test. Re-pinned for Portra 800's new reading: the CPU and GPU folds of colour_on_negative, lighting_on_negative and exposure_departure (their digital pipes), legacy_print's four digital documents (both fingerprints; every scanned negative's hold), two corpus goldens (37-digital), the shipped files' count (114), a Lighting bound (0.45 to 0.47).

title: Halation is a dose of each film layer's exposure laid before the film's curve, with no threshold; its sensitivity slider gone; sidecar format 75
detail: Owner's request (2026-11-25): each layer's exposure plus a dose of its blurred exposure, before the film's curve, no threshold: the curve alone shows it around the highlights. The virtual negative's kernel is split into its exposure (virtual_exposure: the scene on the film's light per chromaticity, the film's exposure and filtration in) and its development (virtual_development: the curves and couplers), the fused kernel their composition, so a stage may lie between them (Pipeline::filmed takes the scan's extent where effects lie; the film stays one pass at rest). The neutral film's layers are the scene's channels. The halation kernel reads E' = (E + d blur(E)) / (1 + d) per layer, d the dose times the layer's share (red 1, green 0.3, blue 0; a silver film's one layer the same on its three channels): divided by 1 + d so an even exposure stays as the sheet measured it, halation included, and neither a flat patch's tone nor the window's white moves. A look holds no layer: its halation lies on the scene it reads. Halation's Amount is the dose itself (0 to 0.25, a quarter of a layer's exposure), its Size the glow's deviation on the film in micrometres of a 135 frame (25 to 250, rest 125: a triacetate base's thickness), so it follows the photo's resolution as the grain does. Halation sensitivity and the threshold left the settings, knobs, fields, presets, the phone link's panel and the store; HALATION_SOURCE and Before::Halation went with them. Sidecar format 75 (migrate::halation): Amount and Size keep their place on their tracks, a halation at amount 0 takes its film's rest.
outcome: tests/halation.rs: the kernel against its reference within 1.5e-7 on a colour film's layers and a silver film's (twins, the dose added on top: 0.05 to 0.13; the other film's layers: 0.10 to 0.21); a flat patch moves 0 under the top dose through the whole chain on the neutral film, Portra 800, Ektachrome E100 and Fomapan 100 (twin, a frame with a lamp: 0.20 to 0.42); a point source's halo over its light is 0.0112216 from 0.05 to 16 times the saturation, within 1.4e-6 (twin, the former threshold's: spread past 0.5); on Portra 800's layers within 2.5e-7 of the reference (twins: on the scene's channels 0.025, past the curve 0.32); a reduced render glows as the full one's means within 0.002 at 1/2 and 0.079 at 1/4 of the peak (twin, the full scale's width: past 0.2); a region's glow is the whole frame's, to the bit; at rest or measured no stage. tests/film_layers.rs: the exposure and development passes within 1.3e-6 of their references on Portra 800, Ektachrome E100 and Fomapan 100 (twins: a film 1 % faster, curves 0.015 log along), their two passes within 5.9e-7 of the fused negative, the reference's two steps its one to the bit. migrate::halation keeps each track's place (twin, a document of format 75 read as it is). The slider step now counts in the digit the readout writes, rounded as it writes it (a tie to the even one): a value at half a unit stepped four units where its readout showed three. Window checks: a press on Halation's rail glows, a fainter dose glows less but glows, Bloom's press lays the blur. Re-pinned: exposure_departure's GPU fold, legacy_print's four digital documents on the GPU (their CPU folds unmoved: the effects are neighbourhood stages), 38 corpus goldens (the halation's size, no sensitivity, a Bloom line; the two 37-digital ones take Portra 800's rests), the newer-format fixture to 76.

title: A film's effects in its file: halation, its emulsion's own blur (Bloom, from the sheet's MTF) and its grain's width (from the sheet's RMS granularity), laid when a film is picked
detail: Owner's request (2026-11-25): each film gives the rests of its effects when it is picked, the sliders free on top. A film block may hold "effects" (halation dose and size, bloom, grain_size, each optional), which scripts/datasheet-profiles.py writes: Bloom, a Gaussian's deviation in micrometres, the one whose response meets the sheet's MTF where it first falls to one half (green layer on a colour film), on 53 of the 79 films; the grain's width where the sheet publishes a diffuse RMS granularity (48 um aperture, x1000), read back through the grain kernel's own granularity at a photo's resting Grain (examples/grain_granularity.rs: 2.85 at 10 um to 11.5 at 60 um), on 30, the seven Foma films past Grain size's top held at it; the halation by a rule per family of base, on no sheet: a cine negative's rem-jet absorbs it (0), an anti-halation layer leaves 0.01, a base with none 0.08, its size the 135 base's thickness where the sheet states it, else 125 um. Bloom is a new effect, a film's own blur laid on its layers' exposures before the halation and the curve (pipeline::layers), its slider in Film Effects (0 to 20 um), a stage only past the blur floor. PipelineSettings::picking lays a film's rests where the hand picks it (the Film block); Prepare's on_stock keeps a photo's own; a field's rest in Film Effects is its film's. Format 75 lays each effect still at its former rest on its film's (a new rest reaches every frame left on it). The block's help says the grain lies on the developed film, translated.
outcome: Measured on the sheets (scripts/datasheet-profiles.py, lay_effects): Bloom 1.5 um (T-Max 100) to 4.9 um (Ektachrome E100), Portra 800 3.4 um, 0.57 pixel on a 24 Mpx frame decoded whole; grain from 10.6 um (Pro 160NS, RMS 3) to 28.6 um (Natura 1600, RMS 7); the seven Foma films' RMS 13.5 to 17.5 lie past what the grain reaches at its resting Grain (11.5 at 60 um), held at Grain size's top. Halation: rem-jet 0 on the five cine negatives, 0.01 on every other film, none of today's virtual films without an anti-halation layer; New Pro 400's base 122 um, every other 125. tests/film_layers.rs: a film's blur on its layers within 2.5e-7 of its reference (twin, on the developed negative: 0.32); no stage at rest, under the blur floor or measured (twin, a blur and a halation are stages); Bloom's and the halation's widths in pixels follow the scan's long side, half on a half-size decode (twin, a width fixed in pixels). tests/grain_size.rs: a RAW at half size lays as many cells along its long side as decoded whole. virtual_film tests: picking a film lays its effects and its reference (twin, Prepare's on_stock keeps the photo's own); migrate::halation lays a film's rests on each effect at its former rest (twin, a hand's grain size and halation kept), none on the neutral film. Window checks bw_film and stock_menu pick and light a film as picking writes it.

title: CLAUDE.md: halation has no threshold and each film's file gives its effects' rests
detail: The grain paragraph said halation stays on the scene before the film; since #3804 and #3805 it is a dose of each layer's blurred exposure before the film's curve, its rests (halation, Bloom, grain width) from the film's file.

title: Halation is progressive: each layer's light weighted by the square of its share of the saturation feeds a glow added on the layers; each film's dose from the level photographers report
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-25). The halation divided by one and the dose and fed by each layer's whole exposure blurred every frame's red as the dose grew. Its glow is now fed by src = E clamp(E / saturation, 0, 1)^2, the saturation each layer's exposure at the sensor's (the digital window's white, at the film's own exposure, so the weight is the scene's share of what the sensor held; the scene's own on the neutral film and a look), blurred and added: E' = E + dose_c blur(src), the layers' shares unchanged (red 1, green 0.3, blue 0; a silver film's one layer). A mid grey rises dose x (0.184 / 1.394)^2, 1.7 % at the top dose; a clipped lamp glows its whole dose. Two passes: halation_source then the blur and the add (stages::halation_source, stages::halation). Halation's Amount is the dose, 0 to 1; its Size rests at 200 um (25 to 400). Each film's dose comes from scripts/halation-levels.json (a web survey of 97 films, its sources kept), none 0, low 0.10, medium 0.31, high 0.92, every width 200 um; scripts/datasheet-profiles.py reads it, the base-thickness rule gone. Sidecar format 76 (migrate::film_effects): a halation at format 75's rests (0 or 0.01, 122 or 125 um) takes its film's new one, a hand's keeps its place on its track (x4).
outcome: tests/halation.rs: the source and add passes within 1.4e-7 of their reference on a colour film's layers and a silver film's (twins: every light feeding the glow whole, 0.015 to 0.055; the other film's layers, 0.10 to 0.38); a lamp's red and green gain their dose of the light it feeds, within 1e-3, blue never moves; under the top dose a mid grey's red rises 0.0174, its dose over its share of the saturation squared, a clipped light's its whole dose (twin, 50 times the grey's); a point source's halo over the light it feeds is 0.0561 from 0.05 to 16 times the saturation within 1e-5 (twin, a threshold's: past 0.5); past a clipped lamp at the medium dose and 200 um, the red excess is 0.515, 0.149 and 0.026 of a mid grey's exposure at 150, 300 and 450 um (prototype 0.51, 0.15, 0.02; twin, 125 um, off by more than 0.1); a reduced render glows as the full one's means within 0.021 at 1/2 and 0.076 at 1/4 of the peak; a region's glow is the whole frame's; on Portra 800's layers within 1.7e-7 (twins: on the scene's channels 0.17, past the curve 0.39). Levels: 76 films low, 11 medium, 7 high, 3 none in the survey; of the files, Portra 800 and its pushes, Fujifilm 400, Superia Venus 800, Fomapan 400 and Cine 400, Retropan 320 and Double-X medium, Foma Ortho 400 and Cine Ortho 400 high, Velvia 50 and 100 and Provia 100F none, every other low. Bloom left the measures' readings too (oni_measure::truncate), as the grain and halation already did: a Bloom notch read the distributions again (twin in render::inputs_tests). Re-pinned: exposure_departure's GPU fold, legacy_print's four digital documents on the GPU (their CPU folds unmoved), the corpus goldens.

title: Grain made of grains: a jittered lattice of grains, each four soft clouds, sampling the film at their centres, each layer its own grains through the paper's gaze; the grain's curve, colour and dissolving blur gone
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-25), after the prototype vrais_grains7. On the developed film, in each layer's window share: grains on a jittered lattice (pitch 0.7 r, r half the size) anchored on the scan's full-resolution grid, each the soft union of four clouds (radius 0.62 r, offsets a triangular draw of deviation 0.32 r); a pixel's share is the weighted mean of the shares read at the centres of the grains covering it, so detail finer than a grain goes and edges follow the grains. Each layer has its own grains, each grain a Gaussian deviation of its window's share, the same at every tone (red 0.85 of green and blue), the three mixed by the paper's gaze rows normalised; a silver film one layer on its three channels; a slide or a look on its light's screen code. A render whose pixel spans f full-resolution pixels widens the clouds to hypot(0.62 r, f / 2), at most eight lattice cells a side, its deviation then scaled as the grains' mean; each pixel reads only its neighbouring cells (stages::Grained, its input region the grains' reach). Amount's top lays 0.1454 a grain, so the rest, 0.25, lays 0.0364, the 0.014 of green's window a real Portra 800 scan measures in 32-pixel tiles of a 47 Mpx frame, at 30 um, every film's size now (the sheets' granularity widths gone). The grain's curve by tone, its colour line (sliders, fields, knobs, store properties, the unused editor) and its dissolving blur went: nothing left them an effect. Format 76: a grain width at a former rest (27.6 um, or a film's format-75 width) takes 30 um; the curve and colour keys are dropped as read.
outcome: oni-render kernel::grain tests: a flat film is its own share where grains stray by none (2e-6; twin, straying grains move it); a 30 um grain on a 47 Mpx grid spreads 0.0176 of the window in 32-pixel tiles per 0.037 of deviation through no gaze (twin, a draw a pixel spreads 0.037 whole); a one-pixel checker's spread falls from 0.100 to 0.048 under the grains (twin, a 32-pixel checker keeps over 0.8 of its own); red's and green's grains correlate 0.03 (twins: silver's 0.999, a mixing gaze's over 0.95); a seed rearranges the grains at one strength, the same seed to the bit. tests/grain.rs: the GPU within 3.3e-6 of the reference on a negative, a positive, silver past the cells' bound, turned and mirrored, angled at half (twin, the next seed: 0.067 to 0.81); at rest on a 47 Mpx grid the green share spreads 0.0140 in 32-pixel tiles, the real Portra 800 scan's 0.014 (twin, Amount's top four times it); a reduced render's grain spreads 0.0276 at 1/2 and 0.0192 at 1/4 where the full one's means spread 0.0263 and 0.0171 (twin, each pixel reading the full grain at its centre: 0.0324 and 0.0327); off, at rest or measured no stage, one pass when on. Timing on this Mac (M2 Max), the grain's pass over a whole screen, 3456 by 2234: 39 ms on a 24 Mpx scan at 100 %, 36 ms on a 47 Mpx scan fitted. tests/grain_seed.rs: a seed rearranges the grain at its strength, a region and a crop keep it, a print notch reruns no grain, an amount or a size notch the grain's pass alone (twin, a Bloom notch develops the film again). Removed: the grain's curve and colour line (fields, knobs, sliders' store properties, the unused editor, their tests), its dissolving blur and haze, the grain's width from the sheets' granularity and its example.

title: The neutral film reads with a colour negative's contrast: its tone curve the mean of six colour negatives' sheet curves, the same on its three layers
detail: Owner's request (2026-11-25): the neutral film mirrored the screen, its scene back as its decode held it, a mid grey about 1.3 stops under Portra 800's virtual one. Each layer's density above its clear bare film is now a colour negative's tone curve of its own channel's light: the mean, over Portra 160, 400 and 800, Ektar 100, Gold 200 and UltraMax 400 and their three layers each, of their sheets' Status M density above D-min on log H about a grey, on the span all six cover (log H -1.86 to +1.93), nought at its foot, toe and shoulder included, no colour of its own; scripts/datasheet-profiles.py (neutral_curve) writes it into generic-neutral.json, its provenance said. The curve is laid so the sensor's saturation reaches the range, its window unchanged: black on the bare film, white on the saturation. The kernel reads 64 nodes in log of the light over the white, held at the ends (GPU and CPU references); Lighting reads the same curve back.
outcome: tests/neutral_negative.rs: the window's share is the curve within 1.8e-7 (twin, the pedestal kept: 1.2e-3); a grey's share 0.593 (the screen's code it mirrored: 0.40); the kernel on the GPU within 1.6e-7 of its reference; end to end through the pure inversion within 0.0013 % on the CPU and 0.0040 % on the GPU (twins, on a paper 66 %, on Portra 800 155 %). Against Portra 800's virtual film at rest, through the pure inversion: a scene grey shows at 0.311 on the neutral film and 0.331 on Portra 800, 0.09 stop under (the mirror it was: 0.132, 1.33 stops under); its contrast about the grey, the stops shown per stop of scene, 0.751 against 0.708 (the mirror's 1.000). The full check did not run (owner's rule during a work in progress); the app was built --profile app and laid in the presets test app.

title: A RAW can be read in its camera's own channels, with no colour matrix: a per-photo switch in the Roll tab's Camera Matrix block; sidecar format 77
detail: Owner's request (2026-11-25): Adobe's matrix LibRaw holds for each camera (cam_xyz) may give the Lumix S1R a look of its own (on P1073099 its sea lies 20 degrees off macOS's preview, its blues turn cyan). A photo's reading now holds camera_channels (sidecar key cameraChannels, unwritten at rest): off, the RAW is read as before, LibRaw's channels balanced at 5000 K then carried into Rec. 2020 by the camera's matrix adapted by Bradford; on, the same balanced channels are the working space as they are, scaled so the 5000 K white still reads (1, 1, 1) at the baseline exposure: the decode's matrix is replaced by its own row sums on the diagonal (oni_decode::decode_with, unconverted), so the kept half or whole decode on disk serves both. Everything after the decode is unchanged: a digital photo's scene is shot on its film in those channels, a scan's negative is inverted in them, so a roll prepared one way reads its windows the other way. The reading's stamp is unchanged at rest (a dust patch already cut stays), another with the switch on, and the open photo is read again on a change. Legacy prints: the switch rests off and nothing migrates it, so every photo laid on a legacy print renders as it did; switched on for such a photo, its legacy print reads the camera's channels as any print would, a change the hand made. Only a RAW shows the block. Sidecar format 77, no step: an older build refuses a document holding the key as newer.
outcome: oni-decode: without the matrix the 5000 K white reads (1, 1, 1) at the baseline within 1e-5 and a saturated colour lands on the camera's own balanced channels within 1e-5 (twin, through Z f's matrix it lands over 0.05 elsewhere); oni-settings: a reading at rest writes no key, so its stamp stays (twin, the switch on stamps another); the corpus goldens gain the field, the newer fixture moves to 78. The full check and lint did not run (owner's rule during a work in progress); oni-settings, oni-decode and the app's field tests ran; the app was built --profile app and laid in the presets test app.

title: The full check starts its longest binary and its longest window checks first, one window check a core
detail: Measured on the M2 Max with another session building: scripts/check took 928 s, 894 of them the window binary (303 checks, six at a time); every other binary under 30 s. A window check costs 0.04 s to start a process, 3 s for the live-preview interface's compile, the rest its own waits (springs on the real clock, 900 ms a settle) and renders. Running checks one after another in a few processes was measured and dropped: it saves only the 0.04 s start, while a check's background decodes outlive its shell and hold the process-wide decode gate, so later checks timed out on thumbnails and Slint's animation clock jumped. Kept instead: the window runner orders the checks by their last run's seconds (target/tmp/window-timings.tsv), longest first, and runs one a core (12: 540 s, 8: 681 s, 6: 773 s); it prints its ten slowest checks. scripts/check starts the binaries by their last seconds (target/tmp/check-times.tsv), prints the ten slowest, and its watchdog rises from 240 to 1800 s, which a whole window run fits.

title: Each film's grain in its file: Grain's Amount and a grain's width beside its halation and Bloom, laid when the film is picked; sidecar format 78
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-25). A film's effects may hold grain { amount, size }, which a photo picking that film takes as its rest, as it takes its halation and Bloom; a person's own file in Stocks carries it too, read again as the folder is watched. scripts/datasheet-profiles.py (lay_effects) writes it from scripts/grain-levels.json, a survey of photographers' reports (97 keys, intensity and size 1 to 5, sources kept): each grain's deviation 0.016, 0.025, 0.037, 0.055 or 0.083 of its window, written as Amount over grain::GRAIN_TOP (0.1454), and a width of 19, 24, 30, 38 or 48 um. The owner's corrections for Kodak's colour negatives by their Print Grain Index: Ektar 100 and Portra 160, NC and VC at intensity 1; Portra 400, NC and VC at 2; Gold 200, UltraMax 400 and Portra 800 at 3 (Portra 800 keeps size 3); the generic keys kodak-portra, kodak-gold, kodak-colorplus and kodak-ultramax hold no virtual film, so no effect is written for them. Only the files' effects blocks moved. A film whose file gives no grain keeps a new photo's (Amount 0.25, 30 um). Sidecar format 78 (migrate::film_grain): a digital photo's grain still at that common rest takes its film's; a hand's stays.
outcome: Every one of the 79 films holding a virtual film is in the survey and takes its grain (for instance Portra 160 Amount 0.110 at 19 um, Portra 400 0.172 at 24 um, Portra 800 0.2545 at 30 um, Delta 3200 0.571 at 48 um). oni-settings' tests ran (picking lays the film's grain, the migration's twin keeps a hand's grain); oni-app and oni-pipeline compile. The full check and lint did not run (owner's rule during a work in progress); the presets test app was not rebuilt (the colour session does it).

title: A colour negative's virtual film is read by ONI's scanner: a D850's measured sensitivities under a D50 lamp, decoded as a RAW is
detail: Owner's call of 2026-11-25. film::scanner replaces the paper's gaze (film::gaze) and the 1931-observer camera scan: a D50 lamp through the dyes and the D-min, the Nikon D850's sensitivities (resources/film/scanner_nikon_d850.json, rawtoaces-data, Apache-2.0), then oni_decode::working_from_camera, the conversion a RAW's decode lays (LibRaw's matrix, 5000 K, Bradford to D65), through the projection kernel unchanged. Stock files: read_by gone from 43 still negatives, the five cine negatives uncoupled as they are, each filtration and reference derived again by examples/stock_references; a paper's sensitivity and the two reading-only Fujicolor papers gone; borrowed dyes say what they cost (3 degrees of hue at most). The Film block names the scanner under its reference. Validated outside the app on two real Portra 800 rolls (bare film within 0.1 D, channel contrasts 0.82 : 1 : 1.24 against 0.86 : 1 : 1.3 measured). Checks owed at the end of the work stream: a scanner test in place of tests/paper_gaze.rs, the stocks' counts and pinned renders.

Portra 800's red channel now sees 0.31 of the magenta dye's grain beside 0.68 of the cyan's, as a camera's broad channels do on a real scan.

detail: Grain: the real Portra 800 scan's 0.014 of green's window is now met on Portra 800 at its own rest through the scanner's gaze (0.0130 before), GRAIN_TOP 0.1563 and the survey's deviations a factor 1.075 over, each film's Amount unchanged. Tests brought to the scanner: the stocks' counts (112 files, 9 papers), every shipped film offered, paper_gaze landing on format 78's references and migrate::scanner's own test, the corpus's newer file at format 80 and its two digital goldens, the legacy prints' two digital cases re-pinned, the couplers' grey checked at no filtration, the Saturation twin pushed twice as far. cameraChannels listed among the excluded fields (missed by #3810).
