title: A pan renders only what its region newly shows: the canvas's last render is copied where both cover
detail: Every pixel's value depends only on where it lies, so a pan of the same recipe copies the last render's overlap and evaluates only the strips the new region adds (Graph::materialise_over, Engine::resident keeping the shown render). Measured on a 47 Mpx RW2 at 100 % on a 3456 x 2034 canvas, Portra 800 with halation 0.5 and grain 0.25 (stage_cost example): a pan of a tenth of the canvas 155 ms -> 5.7 ms p50; a scanned NEF 15 -> 4 ms. The panned render equals a fresh render of its region to the bit (worst 0), its twin a pixel over differs by 0.23; the graph's check compares four pans with a fresh render, and the same strips over another recipe's render must differ. No full check (owner's rule during a work stream).

title: The grain's layers' field drawn apart, over the framed scan, so a notch on Amount, the halation or the film keeps it
detail: Each layer's grain draws, their weights' mean in standard normals, depend on the lattice, the size, the scale and the seed alone: a pass of their own (GrainField over the framed scan, field_rows naming nothing else) that the canvas's cache keeps, read by the grain's laying, which samples the film and lays the field through each layer's deviation and the gaze. 47 Mpx RW2 at fit on a 3456 x 2034 canvas: a Grain notch 21.3 -> 6.6 ms, a Halation notch 25-28 -> 11-13 ms; a whole render the same at fit, +4 ms at 100 % for the field's texture. Against the build before, on the neutral film and on Portra 800 with halation 0.5, at fit and at 100 %: 99.98 % of values within 1e-5, mean difference 2e-7 to 2e-6, a handful of isolated pixels up to 1.5e-3 where the deviation, now multiplied after the mean, meets an ill-conditioned spot of the film's coding. The reference splits the same way (cpu::grain_field, cpu::grain_on); a check counts a notch's pixels on Amount and the film against a size notch, which draws the field again. No full check (owner's rule during a work stream).

title: The canvas keeps its last lighter and its last sharp render, so the sharp render a pan gesture ends on reuses the one before it
detail: A pan gesture renders lighter while the hand moves, then sharp: keeping one render, the sharp one found only the lighter recipe and rendered whole. Two kept, one a recipe (SHOWN), the sharp render after a quarter canvas pan at 100 % on a 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800 (halation 0.31, bloom 3.4, grain 0.25) takes 20.8 ms p50 against 165-196 ms for a whole one (stage_cost). Memory: one canvas texture more while a gesture runs (graph peak unchanged at 1.3 GB RSS in the zoom bench). No full check (owner's rule during a work stream).

title: stage_cost: notches one way, a pinch's lighter renders and each film effect's share of them
detail: Notches alternating back and forth met a render the canvas now keeps (#3862) and read 0.5 ms: they step one way. A pinch's lighter renders, a new scale each, on a 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800 at its rests: 46.3 ms p50, 21.4 without grain, 32.9 without halation, 43.9 without bloom, 9.7 without any, against 9.1 for a scanned NEF: the grain (25 ms, its field and its laying at each scale) and the halation's blur (13 ms) are what a digital photo's gesture pays. Tried without gain and withdrawn: precomputed blur weights, a blur and a grain by work groups in workgroup memory (no faster at best, the grain's 50 % slower at fit), square distances in the grain.

title: A pan's render in a file of its own, graph/over.rs, under the source files' ceiling
detail: Graph::materialise_over moved out of graph/rendering.rs, which it had taken to 420 lines past the 400-line ceiling (oni-core's architecture check). The full check at the end of the digital performance stream (#3860-#3863): 168 of 169 binaries green, the architecture check the one failure, green after this move; 59 checks skipped without ONI_RAW_DIR and the other sample folders.

title: A Halation notch blurs nothing again: the glow's source holds no dose in its uniform
detail: halation_source never reads the dose, yet its uniform carried it, so each Halation notch changed its node's key and the canvas's cache blurred the glow again on both axes. Its uniform now holds the saturation alone: a notch reruns the halation's laying, the film's development and scan and the grain's laying. 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800 at fit from the preview: a Halation notch 13.1 -> 9.4 ms p50; the blur it saves is 17.6 ms at fit from the full frame. Renders equal to the bit at fit and at 100 %; a check counts a dose notch's passes against a size notch's, which blurs again.

title: Benches for what a digital photo costs beyond a notch: its export, a render at fit from the full frame, a neighbour scale's lighter render
detail: export_cost times a photo's full-definition export stage by stage: on a 47 Mpx RW2, 2.9 s on Portra 800 at its rests (decode 1.39 s, render and readback 1.00 s, convert 0.23 s, encode 0.25 s), 2.4 s on the neutral film, 1.3 s for a 24 Mpx NEF (render 0.15 s). stage_cost adds the render at fit from the full frame, the canvas's once the whole decode is in: 75 ms on Portra 800 (grain 36, halation 18, film and scan 6, reduction 6, finishing 7). ONI_COST_NEIGHBOUR measures the open question of a gesture's lighter render taken from a neighbour scale's, stretched: at x1.19 its display code is off by 0.005 mean and 0.024 at p99, its grain's pixel-to-pixel spread 0.91 of the exact one's, against 0.009 and 0.054 for a scanned NEF stretched alike.

title: The full check at the end of the digital performance night: green but a line of stage_cost's past the width, broken
detail: After #3865-#3866, 168 of 169 binaries green; the architecture check counted 79 lines past 200 characters against 78, stage_cost's list of cases (232): laid one case a line, the check green. 59 checks skipped without ONI_RAW_DIR and the other sample folders.

title: The halation's glow drawn once on the film's plate, the photo's whole frame at the preview's side, and read at every scale and place
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-26): the glow, wide and smooth, is drawn on the scan's own frame at the preview's side (2000 px, a fourth of a 47 Mpx frame), lit and exposed as the scene is, blurred there, kept by the pipeline while its recipe holds (Pipeline::glow) and read bilinearly by each render where its pixel lies on the film (halation_laid, its CPU reference cpu::halation_laid); a zoom, a pan or a pinch draws none, the dose stays a factor (#3865), a size, exposure or light change draws it again on the plate. 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800 at its rests: a pinch's lighter render 46.4 -> 35.0 ms p50, a first render at 100 % 200 -> 131 ms, a size notch 13.6 ms with the plate drawn again. Against the render before on P1073214 (a slide's lamps, shot as digital) in display code: at 100 % mean 1.8e-5, p99 1.7e-4, max 6.5e-4; at fit p99 2-3e-4 and up to 1e-2 on the crop's edges alone, where light past the frame now feeds the glow as on a film halated before its cut; on P1073071 under 1.3e-5 everywhere. The neutral film, a look and a slide read the same plate; a recipe laid with no plate (filmed, tests) draws it on its own image, as before.

title: The grain laid once on the film: its layers' field drawn on the scan's grid as a pyramid, read by every canvas render at its footprint
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-26): grains lie once on the film and a zoom enlarges them. The layers' field is drawn once a photo, grain size and frame size on the scan's full grid, four texels across a grain (the field's kernel at that pitch), each next level the mean of its 2 x 2 texels down to a texel across the frame (Pipeline::grain_plate). A render reads it where its pixel lies: under twice the finest pitch smoothly, past it the mean of the texels under its pixel's box on the level whose pitch is under half its footprint (grain_plate in WGSL, cpu::plate_read), its gain measured every half octave of footprint as the plate is drawn so it lays the grain a render drawing its field at that footprint did; the sampling of the film where the grains are centred stays a render's own. Amount stays a factor; a zoom, a pan, a crop, an exposure or a film notch draws nothing; the canvas's renders read the plate, a thumbnail or an export draws its field for itself. Measured: Portra 800's green at 100 % 0.01390 of its window against the scan's 0.014; at the zooms a ladder and a fit take the plate lays within 2.3 % of the grain drawn for itself, its contrast moving 0.4 % at most with a sub-pixel pan (7-10 % at a footprint exactly a level's pitch, a point a pinch passes); a reduced render reads the full grain averaged as before (1/2 0.0367 against 0.0368, 1/4 0.0255 against 0.0256). 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800 at its rests, in the app: a pinch's move to its render shown 108 -> 35 ms p50, frames past 25 ms 118 of 356 -> 2 of 360; stage_cost: a lighter render 47.6 -> 17.4 ms, a first render at 100 % 205 -> 89 ms, a grain size notch 116 ms with the plate drawn again. Memory: graph textures' peak +176 MB in the pinch bench, the plate 330 MB at most for a 47 Mpx frame at 30 um. The pattern of grains is drawn anew, its statistics kept: renders differ from before by 3e-3 mean, 7e-2 at most in display code, the grain's own amplitude; boards in scratch/perf/planches.

title: The grain's plate drawn only when the canvas asks a grain again at another footprint, never for a film lit in its menu, a grain size dragged or the histogram
detail: Each film its grain size, a light in the films' menu drew a plate (116 ms): hovering went from 57 to 147 ms p50 after #3869. The plate is now drawn when the canvas asks the same grain on the same film again at another footprint, as a zoom or a pinch does; a first ask, a film lit, a grain size dragged (21 ms a notch) or the histogram's picture (now drawing its own) draws its field for itself, over the framed scan so a notch at one footprint keeps it. A render drawing its own field is #3861's again (grained_over). Measured in the app on a 47 Mpx RW2 on Portra 800: hovering the films 54 ms p50, 63 p90 (55 before #3868); a pinch's render shown 33 ms p50, 2 frames of 362 past 25 ms; RSS 1.28 GB.

title: Dead code out: two public functions no code calls and a script for a check that no longer exists
detail: film::bake::view_matrix (and the CAT02 cone space only it read) and paper::printing::layer_shares had no caller in any crate, example or test; scripts/synthetic-sources.py wrote the sources of a decode parity check gone since; oni-fixtures' description no longer names the Swift app's dumps. Nothing renders differently: no caller existed. Proof: cargo check of oni-pipeline and oni-fixtures on every target, no warning.

title: The source files' ceilings: the entries of files gone or under the limit dropped, the others at their size today
detail: architecture.rs still listed oni-settings/src/json.rs and tests/window/extended.rs, both gone, and editors/mod.rs, now 369 lines; decode's swift_checks (466 -> 460) and pipeline's (728 -> 722) come down to their size. The files other streams may grow before the freeze (editors/tests.rs, codec_checks.rs) keep theirs. Proof: the architecture check and its twins green.

title: The full check and the lint at the end of the film effects' plates (#3868-#3870)
detail: 167 of 169 binaries green at load 70: the window checks stopped at their 30-minute limit, their 302 checks green run alone after; stock_files fails in parallel and passes alone and on one thread, its two tests each installing a global catalogue (a race already there, to be fixed apart). The lint refused a mem::replace on an Option in Pipeline::grain_plate_asked: Option::replace.

title: The ONI 2.0 welcome: the whole window, four wrapped gifts to untie (the livelier interface, the Collection with The Lens DB, digital photos on real film, the Wrapped), then the message
detail: Replaces 1.6's paged card (its six scenes and their assets go). Edition 2.0, shown once to everyone, first installs included, again from Help > What's New. A gift's page plays a scene built from the design system: the window in miniature opening a photo, the Kit filling, the virtual negative step by step with a before/after drag on the app's own renders (examples/welcome_stills), the year's deck. The message: paid converters, 'You already paid for your film', spread the word (Ko-fi, Instagram once known), the monthly splash contest (its form and hashtag). Sheet gains `full`. Version 2.0.0.

title: While development pauses (2026-12-15 to 2027-01-15), the gallery's status bar says so in its quiet hint, and nothing on other days
detail: help::PAUSE and paused(), today in the machine's calendar; Help.pause-line feeds CardStatus's hint in the gallery.

title: The welcome's Collection gift says only what The Lens DB can confirm, and one constant takes it out
detail: 'Two independent projects' where 'non-profit' was unproven (the Kit's offer too); The Lens DB sees the list of gear, never the photos, so nothing contradicts the contest's upload; the gift's scene shows cards as the Kit column draws them. help::KIT_GIFT hides the gift and skips its page both ways, the dots counting five (window check welcome_card, with its twin). Validation file for The Lens DB's owner outside the repository.

title: Gallery to editor: the column's photos rise from its foot under the rows, the gallery's filter tucks under the tab bar; back, they sink
detail: One list of rows in both modes (NavigatorSection), the photos laid once at their resting height inside a part that grows from the column's foot (Tree.unfold on Motion.travel, Ease.weighted), so no row is laid again while it moves; the rows keep their folder centred as they shorten. The photos stay laid while they sink, so entering the editor centres the column from tree-moded too, not only from a new list's shown.

title: The photo flies between the screens: the tile lifts into the canvas, the canvas shrinks into its tile, the canvas moves onto the export's lone preview and back
detail: Flight (ds/flight.slint, app/flight.rs): Rust names the thumbnail, the route and where it leaves; the window lays the landing place live (the canvas's frame, the tile the grid lays, the export's preview) and springs the picture there, turned back midway as a gesture reverses it; the place under it stands back until it lands and fades. Nothing waits on it; Reduce Motion flies nothing. ONI_BENCH=motion at 3456 x 2034 px: every journey 120 Hz at the median while it moves, draw p50 under 3 ms, no spike the screens lacked laid at once.

title: Pop-ups move: menus, pickers and popovers grow out of their anchor; sheets rise on a spring, and the scrim of the last one closed lightens behind it
detail: Popover (every menu and popover) grows from its tail or top edge on Motion.pop; Sheet comes in on Ease.weighted. A closing sheet goes at once, so every press and key reaches the window behind it, and ScrimFade lightens its scrim on overlay-out: a sheet kept laid while it sank swallowed the presses and keys of the next gesture (gallery, gestures, migration and sheet checks).

title: Edit to export morphs: the bar slides up out of its room, the export card opens out of the editor's card, the export panel slides in; back, the bar, the column and the panel slide in
detail: One spring (MainWindow.exporting, Ease.firm) drives the bar, the card's frame (its content laid once at its own place, clipped while it opens) and the columns, each moved in its own slot so no layout changes while it travels.

title: A section folds and unfolds sliding, its chevron turning; the tooltip fades in
detail: Section's content laid at its own height, the block's height sliding on the hand's fold alone (Ease.firm, Motion.travel), a content changing height laid at once; FoldMark one chevron turned by Button.turned, which turns on Motion.quick; TipView fades in on Motion.quick.

title: A canvas tool's ring fades out as it leaves and the rings inside close in; the help card rises into place
detail: Held (ds/containers.slint) keeps a ring laid while it fades on overlay-out, its inset sliding on Motion.quick; the rings take no press. HelpLayer comes in as a popover does, on Motion.pop.

title: An export preview fades in over the sweep it replaces
detail: PreviewSlot's picture comes in on Motion.quick as it lands; a lone photo's is already covered by the photo flown from the canvas, which waits for it.

title: Prepare the Roll: a step's body comes in from the side the walk goes
detail: RollPanel shifts the new step's body by Space.l, forward from the right and back from the left, then slides it home and fades it in on Motion.travel (Ease.firm), the next frame after it is laid; nothing waits on it. Its next-frame timer started with start(): a Timer laid stopped ignores restart(), which left the body shifted and unseen once a step changed; motion.rs now walks two steps and finds the first step's body shown.

title: A digital photo's virtual negative made once into a scan, read on as a scanned negative's; the halation red alone
detail: Owner's go (2026-11-26). The chain splits in two: Pipeline::scan shoots a digital photo's scene on its virtual film on the scan's own grid, before any crop or turn (healed scene lit at its film's white, film with its bloom and halation, development, scanner or slide, grain over the healed scene), and Pipeline::on_scan reads a scan as a scanned negative's frame (geometry, then the inversion, the projector or a look's print, then the finishing); Pipeline::image composes the two, one path. The engine keeps the scan once made, in half floats as a decode: from the preview always, from the full frame when the view reads it (Engine::scanned), each under its recipe's key, the last full scan let go before the next is made; under a hand holding a film's setting the preview's scan stands in and the worker renders the frame again sharp once the hand rests (Renderer::hold_scan, provisional). The histogram reads the kept scan too. Lighting on a digital photo now reads its scan as a scanned negative of its film does (Film::of: its dyes' mean layer, a silver film's one curve): Film::Stock, the virtual film's own curves developed again, is gone; a roll card still names no stock for a digital photo. The grain is back to #3861's field over the healed scene, its plate, pyramid, gains and asks gone (#3869, #3870), the scan holding it once made; the halation's glow is still drawn on the preview's plate so a full scan blurs no full frame. HALATION_COLOUR is [1, 0, 0]: the red layer, the deepest, alone takes the light the base sends back. Renders of digital photos move (geometry now after the film, Lighting as a scan's, the red halo); the two digital legacy-print fingerprints are taken anew. Checks: oni-pipeline green but stock_files' race (passes alone), oni-app's unit tests, 29 window checks on digital photos.

title: The full check and the lint at the end of the film effects' plates (#3868-#3870)
detail: 167 of 169 binaries green at load 70: the window checks stopped at their 30-minute limit, their 302 checks green run alone after; stock_files fails in parallel and passes alone and on one thread, its two tests each installing a global catalogue (a race already there, to be fixed apart). The lint refused a mem::replace on an Option in Pipeline::grain_plate_asked: Option::replace.

title: The welcome built from the design system alone: a full sheet is fixed to the window by itself, its flat ground a component of the welcome's pieces
detail: design_system::screens_use_only_the_design_system refused welcome.slint's literal 1px card height and its ground colour. Sheet's `full` now implies a fixed height; WelcomeGround (ds/welcome.slint) lays the flat ground. Window checks design_system (and its planted twin), welcome_card, help, sheets, sheet_stack, migration green.

title: Wrapped 2.0: the year on film told as a half-frame strip of scenes, read off the journal, the library, its sidecars and its thumbnails, each scene a card to save
detail: Show My Year on Film (Act::Wrapped, December's offer) read only the journal and dealt nine cards. It now reads, off this machine alone, the journal (oni_library::wrapped::Darkroom: photos opened, gestures, favourite rows and preset, hours, longest sitting, gestures by hour, days, longest run of days), the library's rows with each frame's sidecar (Frames: frames by month and kind, rolls and the longest, films, papers, cameras, lenses, medals, dust healed, crops, grain and halation) and the thumbnails (Palette: each photo's own colour, the heaviest hue weighted by chroma, gathered in Oklab around five), and names a character (Persona: twelve traits, each against its own bar, the one furthest past it, its measure shown). A frame is dated by its roll's shot date, else its file's, else its import. oni_app::wrapped::scenes lays up to seventeen scenes, one with nothing to tell left out, an empty year an invitation. The view is a half-frame strip (ds/wrapped.slint: WrappedFilm, four perforations a frame, edge print; WrappedFrame, 9 by 16, every size a share of its width) advanced through the gate by a click, the arrows or by itself after a 7 s hold, a press holding it; figures count up, bars grow, prints land askew. Save This Card and Save All Cards cut the frame, drawn alone as large as the window holds, out of the window's own picture into a JPEG (wrapped::share), never over an earlier one. In January the menu tells the year just ended. ONI_WRAPPED_SAMPLE tells a sample year on the library's own photos.

title: The year on film read without opening an original, on every core; its cards cut, encoded and written off the interface thread
detail: Reading a year probed each original's bytes to learn how it decodes (decodes_via_mosaic): 688 ms of the 865 ms a year of 417 frames took on the test copies, and a wait on a disk away. A frame's sidecar is now read on its name alone (is_raw), the sidecars and the thumbnails' colours on every core (gather::spread): 191 to 275 ms for the same year (sidecars 78 to 101 ms, colours 111 to 171 ms, both on an external exFAT disk), each step timed in the log (wrapped: N frames of M and K thumbnails read in ...). Save All Cards held the interface 0.37 s for fifteen cards: the window's pictures are taken on the interface thread and each card is cut, brought to sRGB, encoded and written on another (save_wrapped_into answers through a callback). The Loyalist's share is the top film's frames over the year's, the figure its film's own scene shows. ONI_BENCH=wrapped shows the year in the real window, holds each scene until it is told and saves every card into ONI_WRAPPED_SHOTS: 13 scenes at 120 frames a second, drawn in 2.6 ms p50 and 5.6 ms p99 on the M2 Max, window 1100 x 680.

title: Space pauses the year on film and starts it again; a roll's and a preset's name in its scenes are marked for the log
detail: The film advanced by itself with no way to stop it but a held press: Space now pauses it and starts it again (it was a second key for the next scene, which Return and the right arrow still are), the line under the strip saying which; where motion is reduced it starts paused. The scenes naming a roll (The longest, {name}, holds {count} frames) and a preset ({name}, laid {count} times) mark the name with oni_i18n::named, as the anonymity check asks of any template naming something bare; the template of the card this replaces leaves its list of texts never logged.

title: December's offer of the year never opens over the welcome, and the year opened from the welcome or the menu in its December is that offer made
detail: At the launch that shows the 2.0 welcome in December, the launch also offered the year: the summary opened at once over the welcome whose mystery gift it is. The offer is now not made at a launch whose welcome is due (Ctl::offer_wrapped reads welcome_due), and a year shown in its own December, by the offer, the menu or the welcome's gift, writes wrappedShownYear (Ctl::show_wrapped), so the next launch does not offer it again; a person who closes the welcome without opening the gift is offered the year at the next December launch. The rule is one function, offer_due, with its check and twin.

title: A digital photo's full scan made only when the view reads past the preview, in bands, and sharpened at rest
detail: The full scan is made only once the view asks past the preview's resolution, as at 100 % (Engine::composed): at fit a digital photo reads its preview's scan, so a film lit in its menu or a film's notch rebuilds the preview's scan alone; a film's settings moved let the kept full scan go. Graph::materialise_half evaluates its frame in bands of at most 4 MP, packing each into the half-float texture, so a full frame's chain holds one band's textures (the full scan's build peaked at 3.2 GB of textures). Under a hand the worker holds the full scan back and renders it once the hand rests (Renderer::hold_scan with the sharpening job alone). Check: a half-float render made in bands reads as one made whole, a gain apart its twin.

title: Film exposure named Shooting exposure
detail: The Film block's exposure slider is the exposure at capture, the camera's on the virtual film: Shooting exposure, Exposition à la prise de vue, Exposición en la toma, its help sentence with it; the window check reads the new name.

title: A tungsten film turns a daylight scene blue, its two lights in sight
detail: Measured first: the scene already reaches every film in its decode's light (5000 K on a RAW), the film's balance its layers' alone, so a daylight grey prints blue on Vision3 500T and 200T (R 0.29, G 0.38, B 0.57 at mid grey, pure inversion) and near neutral on 250D; nothing in the render changes. What said otherwise is rewritten: scene_white's, the stock white's and the chain's comments and the Film block's help no longer say the scene is lit at the film's white. The Film block's light line names both lights, 'A 5000 K scene on a film balanced for 2810 K' (fr, es), so the cast comes from a state in sight. Proven by virtual_film's a_tungsten_film_prints_a_daylight_grey_blue_and_the_filtration_takes_it_away: blue on 500T, near neutral on 250D, the twin grey lit at the film's own white neutral, and the Source tab's Filtration (R -0.92, B +1.20 stops) brings the ramp within 0.005 of neutral; stock_hero reads the film's light in the line.

title: A digital photo's preview scan made again from its own stages' cache: a film notch reruns only what follows it
detail: Each film notch made the preview scan again whole, the grain's field and the lit scene included, which no film slider moves: Graph::materialise_half_cached keeps a frontier cache a band (the view's, Cache::frontier), and the engine holds the preview scan's; the full scan, made at rest, keeps none. Measured on Portra 800, 47 Mpx, app profile, load 7 to 10: grain notch p50 43 to 13-16 ms, halation 38-80 to 22-36 ms, shooting exposure 50-53 to 26-57 ms (too noisy to call); textures' peak 1923 MB as before. The GPU bench of the scan alone (8 Mpx): halation 77 to 26 ms, exposure 84 to 40, grain 79 to 16. Proven by pool's a_banded_render_made_again_from_its_caches_reads_as_one_made_afresh: bit for bit, every band keeping a stage, twin: the first recipe's render differs.

title: A digital photo's virtual negative written as a linear TIFF, for the person to convert it as a scanned negative
detail: examples/virtual_negative writes a digital photo's frozen scan on a stock, as the chain makes it after the scanner and before any window or inversion: 16-bit linear in the working space under a linear Rec. 2020 profile (oni_colour::space::linear_working_icc), so a plain file reads its codes back as that light, framed by a 4 % margin of bare film for Prepare's black; grain and halation off, or at the stock's rests. The owner's test photos written on Portra 800, Gold 200 and Vision3 250D, on the chain before and after #3878, under the test copy's Négatifs virtuels.

title: A colour negative's virtual film exposes its three layers alike and reads the scene's gamut as it is: two points a channel (format 80)
detail: Owner's call, spec by the colorimetry session (spec-deux-points.md): the film's filtration (each layer's exposure offset laying a mid grey on one share of the three windows, film::scanner::filtration and its field in 48 films' files) and the input gamut compression (bake::compressed) removed; CAT16 and bake::balanced kept. Each film's reference is its two points, black on the bare film and white where a neutral at the sensor's saturation reads, derived again (examples/stock_references); a person's own file still holding a filtration reads, the field left aside. Format 80 moves a digital photo of format 79 onto its stock's new reference, every hand's move kept (migrate::two_points). Measured against the spec: ranges R/G, B/G Portra 0.827 / 1.203, Gold 0.845 / 1.145, 250D 0.831 / 1.061, within 0.01; a grey leaves the black on Portra's three channels within 0.1 stop. Proven by scanner's a_grey_leaves_the_black_on_the_three_channels_together (twins: format 79's ranges, a grey lit by the former offsets leaving apart) and two_points' migration check.

title: A digital photo's render written stage by stage from the app's own chain, for the process board
detail: examples/digital_stages writes every stage of a digital photo's render on its film at rest, from the sensor's counts (oni_decode::mosaic, a LibRaw unpack read through oni_mosaic in pinned.c, no knob touched) through the demosaic, the camera matrix, the editor's reduction, the scene seen at the film's white, its XYZ for the film, each layer's exposure, bloom, the halation's glow and dose, the development, the scanner's own channels and their decode, the grain, the frozen scan, then stage 4-7 laid out on the CPU (Lighting, gains, density on its two points, shares, inversion) and the finishing on the GPU, with the bare film's and a saturated neutral's readings and the open lamp (film::scanner::open_lamp) for the owner's transmission scale. It checks itself: the exposure against its CPU reference (1.3e-5), the frozen scan against the stages (4.9e-4, half floats), the inversion laid by hand against the fused stage (0).

title: An export written invites, quietly, to post the photos on Instagram with #madewithoni
detail: No sheet: the export's notice (Toast's aside) carries one line and three mini keys, Copy #madewithoni, Open Instagram and Don't Show Again, which hides it for good (exportInviteHidden); Settings > General > Sharing brings it back. The hashtag is one constant (help::MADE_WITH), the link ONI's Instagram (help::INSTAGRAM). Proven by export_invite: shown after a written export, hidden for good, twin: absent on the next export, back from Settings.

title: The year's cards are a story's picture, 1080 by 1920 with ONI's mark, #madewithoni and the account in its safe area, saved in one click into Downloads, copied, and laid out on a share screen
detail: Owner's asks (2026-11-26): ONI recognisable on every card, and the cards as easy as possible to get off the computer and post as a story. A frame is now a half-frame's 3 by 4 (360 by 480 units) and its card the frame in its piece of the strip, 9 by 16 (WrappedCard): the rebates, perforations and edge print lie over the top and bottom 12.5 % a story's players cover, the scene and the brand's band (ONI's logo, #madewithoni, @open.negative.initiative) between 16 % and 85 % of the height. A card is always 1080 by 1920, whatever the window: it is laid at its full size and the window's own picture taken a view's worth at a time, from where the view lies in the window (share::tiles, share::lay; the view says its place, so a window holding its menu bar, as on Windows, cuts no bar into a card, which the first cut did). Save All Cards and Save This Card ask nothing: they write ONI Wrapped <year> - NN.jpg into Downloads/ONI Wrapped <year>, a card saved again taking its own place, then show the folder or the file in the Finder or the Explorer and say so under the keys; Copy This Card (or C) lays the card on the pasteboard as a TIFF, and as a device-independent bitmap on Windows (pasteboard::write_picture, the app's own copies kept beside it). Past the last scene a share screen lays every card out, says to post them in a story and tag the account, and saves a card on a click. Cards are taken one a turn of the interface's loop and encoded and written off its thread as they come: saving fifteen held the interface 2.7 s in one go, and no longer trips the watchdog. Not built: dragging a card out of the window, which neither Slint 1.18 nor winit offers on either system. The Windows clipboard path is written and unit-checked on its bytes, not run on Windows.

title: The year on film in parts under the 400-line limit: its controller in three, its scenes' words apart, its design system pieces in four files
detail: architecture::no_source_file_grows_past_its_ceiling refused app/year.rs (545 lines), wrapped.rs (503) and ds/wrapped.slint (806). app/year.rs keeps the journal's notes, the state and December's offer (212), year/showing.rs the year read, laid, advanced and closed (215), year/cards.rs the cards taken, saved and copied (146). wrapped.rs keeps the scenes (361), wrapped/words.rs the counts, the names and each character's words (151). ds/wrapped_parts.slint holds the scene's types, the measures and the print, words, figure, line and brand (240), ds/wrapped_scenes.slint and ds/wrapped_portrait.slint one component a kind of scene (275, 204), ds/wrapped.slint the frame that picks one, the strip, the card and the share screen's pieces (212); a part's rise is one function of the style. Nothing is meant to move on screen: the sample year's fifteen cards, saved before and after, look the same. design_system::screens_use_only_the_design_system's breach (a border-radius: 0px in ui/wrapped.slint) left with the still frame #3904 replaced by the card.

title: A panel's pane taken from the tab bar slides in from the side the tabs were crossed, as the Swift app's DSPanel
detail: The Swift app (1.3.1, DSPanel.entry) inserted a clicked pane with .move(edge:), trailing when the tabs were crossed rightwards, leading else, the pane left removed at once, on DS.Motion.grab (response 0.22 s, damping 0.62). The panes now slide in a whole width on Motion.pane (the pill's 220 ms) and Ease.lively (spring 0.38, the same spring); a tool's pane, entered from the bar, shows in place. Shot step by step by motion.rs; ONI_BENCH=motion times each pane taken.

title: Walking to the next or the previous photo: the photo left steps aside and fades as the next comes in from the other side
detail: Ctl::walk_from, at the head of open_photo beside a photo alone: the left photo's thumbnail, where the canvas showed it, steps Motion.walk-step the way the walk goes (the gallery's order) and fades on Motion.travel (Ease.firm); the canvas's picture comes in from the other side faded in (WalkIn). Nothing waits on it; Reduce Motion lays the next photo at once. Shot by motion.rs both ways.

title: ONI_WRAPPED_ONLY shows the year on film alone, reading a library without writing in it; a scene's photo with no thumbnail is made, and a camera or a paper on a handful of frames is no headline
detail: The owner asked to try the Wrapped on his real data. A launch with ONI_WRAPPED_ONLY set opens no folder, shows no launch sheet, runs neither the facts' sweep nor the migration's, offers no phone, asks neither The Lens DB nor for an update, shows the year at once and quits as it closes (wrapped::alone, main.rs): the year is read off the index, the sidecars and the thumbnails alone, sidecar::read migrating in memory. Run three times on a copy of the 1.6 support folder and of its index-14 (1,834 rows of /Volumes/T7/Scans and Photos Digitales, the reference roll's taken out of the copy): 1,732 frames of the year, 42 rolls, Kodak Gold on 549; of the 3,132 files of the real rolls (1,356 sidecars and markers hashed, the originals by size and date) and of the real support and caches, none added, removed or changed. Found on that year and rectified: a scene's grid showed blank paper for a photo with no thumbnail on disk (196 of 1,834 rows, the six latest gold among them): such a photo is now made as a thumbnail is, its scan for a frame never converted, and a print with no picture is not laid; a camera named on one frame was the year's faithful companion and a paper on three its signature's headline: both now need twelve frames (persona::ENOUGH); a long lens name ran over its value: a line's label gives way. A bench copies to a board of its own, the person's clipboard left alone. Known: the interface paused 0.4 s once in two of three runs while a large RAW was developed for a print.

title: ONI's faces become Zalando Sans: ONI Sans for every word read, Zalando Sans Expanded Black for titles and headings
detail: scripts/oni-fonts.py writes crates/oni-ui/fonts from Zalando Sans (OFL 1.1, ZALANDO-SANS-OFL.txt): ONI Sans, its normal width at 400, 500, 600 and 700, figures laid tabular in the default map (Slint asks no OpenType feature), the eight signs it lacks (↔ ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌫ ✓ Δ σ) drawn from Inter at the same weight, renamed as the reserved name Zalando requires of a modified version; Zalando Sans Expanded Black ships as it is. Type.family is the text face, Type.display and Type.display-weight the display face, which Roles.family gives the title and heading roles; Inter is no longer embedded. The fit checks stay green (toolbar_fit, film_type_fit, mode_header, settings_rows, states); typeface.rs shoots the main screens at the smallest window in each language.

title: The welcome on a stage the GPU draws: four gifts of lit foil untied in real time, the huge one's film told as a strip exposed, developed, scanned and inverted
detail: The 2.0 welcome's flat sheet gave way, on the owner's word, to a stage: a WGSL compute pass marches four signed-distance gifts (silver, copper, gold, holographic foil; satin ribbons; a studio of strip lights mirrored in the brushed metals) into the texture the sheet shows, a second pass shares each edge pixel between the faces it covers, a third finishes (glow, curve, dither). `stage::direction::frame` is one function of the cue (act, seconds, hand), so `welcome_reel` steps the film on a held clock and writes its sheets. Each gift comes undone its own way (`stage::unwrap`); the huge gift's page is all stage: the photo in the gate of a 35 mm strip laid flat in the ray (perforations and edge print cut to the pixel), a latent picture, the negative coming up, the scanner lifting its orange mask, every tone crossing to its opposite, the print, a second stock with the camera's photo laid back over it, a third, the three side by side. The stage's cost is measured once off the interface's thread (`Stage::pace`) and its pixels fitted to the screen's frame, one picture in flight. Keys name where they lead; the steps are named and clickable. Blind reviews after each capture: /10 on six criteria by five roles, rounds 1 to 4 kept outside the repository. Checks: stage unit tests with twins, window checks welcome_reel, welcome_card, help, sheets, sheet_stack, sheet_layout, migration, design_system, collection; catalogue; architecture. Not run: the full check, the lint, Windows (FXC's compile time of the stage's loops is unmeasured).

title: The faces screen by screen: the export's title in the display face, a renamed title typed in its own face, the contact sheet's numbers in ONI Sans, keycap legends 0.2 pt apart
detail: RenameField types in its role's face (Roles.family), so a title renamed stays in the display face; the export's panel title in the display face. The contact sheet's numbers (together/plate.rs) set in ONI Sans at the nearest of its four weights instead of Inter's axis. Keycap legends 0.5 → 0.2 pt apart: ONI Sans's bold capitals run about 4 pt wider over CANCEL, BACK and PREPARE ROLL, which pushed Prepare's commit onto a line of its own. The lab's shots load ONI Sans. The 308 window checks pass in ONI Sans.

title: The welcome's contest as the owner set it: its page on the site, always offered; monthly top five, the winner opening the next version with its author's name; #madewithoni to spread the word
detail: help::CONTEST is the site's contest page (https://open-negative-initiative.com/contest), which holds the form and the rules, so the key Enter the Contest always shows and the app depends on no form id. The message's note says: every month the community's top five, the winning photo opens the next version of ONI for everyone with its author's name, anyone can enter with a photo where no one is recognisable, one step (the form), #ONIsplash to share; a line under 'spread the word' names #madewithoni (help::MADE_WITH). Clippy: three needless borrows in welcome_card.rs and the stage thread's send whose large error is dropped. Checks: clippy on oni-app's lib, examples and window tests; help unit tests (both hashtags well formed, links pages not addresses); window checks design_system, welcome_card, help, sheets, welcome_reel; catalogue translated (its one failure, 'Zalando Sans Expanded' in theme_type.slint, is canvas's own).

title: ONI_BENCH=motion never waits without end: it opens any tile the gallery lays and stops, naming the step, past 30 s
detail: It double-clicked the tile at a fixed place, which a gallery landed on its open photo far down never laid: it waited forever, logging the editor-to-gallery journey anew at each tick. It now opens a tile of the open photo's own folder (a photo of a roll never prepared opens on Prepare the Roll) through the grid's own two clicks, as the window checks do, never at a point on screen, which the grid's row laid past its edge or a window over it would miss; it waits for the disk's gestures to land, and a step whose window never comes ends the bench past 120 s with motion: stalled, and why.

title: ONI_BENCH=screens takes the main screens at the smallest window, in the language spoken, from the app's own build
detail: The editor's three panes, the export, Settings, the gallery and Prepare the Roll at 1100 × 680, each taken off the window (take_snapshot) into ONI_SHOTS as <language>-<screen>.jpg: the app's build bundles its translations, which a debug build's interface lacks, so French and Spanish are judged there.

title: The faces named in the design system's tokens, which the catalogue knows name fonts, never words shown
detail: Type.family, Type.display and Type.display-weight bind to DS.typo-text-family, DS.typo-display-family and DS.typo-display-weight in tokens.slint: a family's name written in theme_type.slint read to the catalogue's check as a word left outside @tr.

title: The year on film in a new art direction: each scene's photo fills its card, the giant figure in the photo's own ink laid over it
detail: The owner found the first Wrapped a stock exchange dashboard: no graph is left. A card is black, 9 by 16; its scene's photo fills it (HeroScene, Bleed), exposed in a white flash, veiled only under the words that stand on the brand's band and rise from it (Column): a tag in the scene's ink, the giant figure or word in the display face (Type.display, set as large as 292 units hold by wrapped::fit, a number's groups never broken), the bold headline and one line with a wink. The ink is the photo's own hue made vivid (palette::vivid), white for a photo with no colour. A scene whose subject is its photo (the most edited) lays it whole as a tilted print over the photo's blurred light (wrapped::backdrop); the gold medals are a wall of six from one edge of the film to the other; the year's colours are slices of the photos nearest each (Palette::picks) on blocks of the colour; the summary is the year, the character and four poster lines. No photo comes back while the year has others (staging::Pool), a month, a film, a roll and a camera each showing a photo of theirs (Frames::picks). All that is read lies between 15.6 % and 80 % of the height, clear of a story's players; the film's perforations run down both edges; the brand's band holds ONI's mark and name, #madewithoni in the scene's ink and the account. Judged by blind evaluators over five rounds (scratch/v2/wrapped-reviews): boldness and typography 8, fun and urge to share 7, photos and legibility 6 on 200 px thumbnails, no score rising for two rounds; the owner has the last word. The bench also films one scene's coming in, frame by frame (motion-NN.jpg). French and Spanish texts for every new line.

title: The year on film's perforations are a 135 film's: Kodak Standard, in their true proportions to the film's width
detail: The owner judged the new Wrapped right but for its sprocket holes: not a film's shape, and out of proportion with the film's band. A frame is now a 35 mm film as wide as the card (WrappedStyle.mm, 360 units over 35), and every measure of its edges is the standard's, in millimetres: a perforation 1.981 mm across the film by 2.794 mm along it with corners of 0.5 mm, one every 4.75 mm, 2 mm in from the film's edge, the band outside the 24 mm image 5.5 mm each side. The perforations run on from frame to frame down the strip, a frame's own beginning where the strip has come to (Perforations.along), so a card's foot may cut one as a strip's cut does; a card 1920 px tall holds 13.1 of them. A scene's words, its wall of photos and its colours lie inside the 24 mm image (pad 60, a figure fitted to 240 units). Measured on three saved cards of 1080 px: holes 1.977 by 2.787 mm, pitch 4.748 to 4.764 mm, 2.009 mm from the edge.

title: The year on film is opened from the gallery through December and January
detail: The owner asked for a way back to the Wrapped once the welcome is closed. From the first of December to the last of January the gallery's library column opens, under its tabs and on either tree, on one line (ds/year_entry.slint, YearEntry): the year struck on the holographic seal the app's gifts wear, "Your year on film" in the section face, a chevron; a flat key under the hand, the seal's glint swept on hover. A click is Act::Wrapped, so January tells the year just ended (year::season, told_year). It is the column's head rather than the bar or the status line: the first place read as the gallery opens, out of the bar whose keys are fitted to the narrowest window, and gone beside a photo, where the work is. It offers nothing by itself: the launch's December offer stays the only showing nobody asked, made once, and a year shown from the entry in its December is that offer made. Out of the two months the line is not laid; the menu's item stays the year round. The season is read at launch and each time the gallery shows. Checked on the window with the date given: December and January lay the entry and tell 2026, a click shows the year; November and February lay none.

title: The welcome as a path of gifts: one screen a gift, opened before the next, its demo left and its words right; plain type on black; the huge gift's demo shoots one photo on three films
detail: On the owner's word the keynote stage gives way to a sober path: a vertical run of screens, the gift alone in the middle (lower detail: one gift a picture, no beams, no film in 3D), opened by a click, Return or Space, then its demo in a frame on the left and its words on the right (the display face for titles, no coloured text). On is never past a wrapped gift: the wheel, the arrows and the key stay; back is always open; Escape leaves only if help::ESCAPE_LEAVES (false, the owner's answer pending); only the message's key enters the app. The gifts opened are kept (welcomeProgress), so a welcome closed midway resumes on the first still wrapped. Where the GPU cannot draw the stage, or until its shader lands, each gift is its still (ui/welcome/gift-*.jpg). The huge gift's demo picks the picker's own cells in turn and the photo becomes what the app renders on Ektar 100, Velvia 50 and Tri-X 400; scripts/welcome-assets makes those pictures and the stills again from the app's own renders, so a change of render is one command. Checks: stage unit tests (one gift a screen, in the middle; each untying), help unit test (progress kept for this edition alone, with twins), window checks welcome_reel (the lock, each gift opened, Escape refused, the last key), welcome_card, sheet_stack, help, sheets, migration, design_system; catalogue; clippy on oni-app.

title: The year on film's perforations lie the right way, punched through the photo, and its scenes are back at their size
detail: #3908 drew each perforation a quarter turn off, its long side along the film, and scaled the film to the card's width: bands 57 units wide that pushed every scene's words inward and set its figures 18 % smaller. A Kodak Standard perforation's long side lies across the film: 2.794 mm across by 1.981 mm along, corners of 0.5 mm, one every 4.75 mm, 2 mm in from the edge. The scale is the film's edge itself, the 30 units a frame's band always was standing for its 5.5 mm (WrappedStyle.mm), so a scene's margin (34), its figures' box (292) and every size are those of #3907 again, as the owner validated them. The band holds no ink of its own any more (owner's call): the photo fills the frame from edge to edge and the perforations are punched through it, black as the ground, a faint light rim letting them be read on a dark photo as on a light one. They still run on from frame to frame down the strip. No edge print was left to keep. Measured on saved cards of 1080 px, a millimetre being 16.36 px.

title: The welcome's mystery gift lays the person's own first Wrapped cards on its screen; no way out of the welcome before its end, Escape included
detail: Owner's calls: no exit before the end (Escape included), the Collection's screen stays, the mystery gift shows the person's real cards. The welcome reads the year as it opens (Ctl::ready_wrapped: the Wrapped's own reading and cards, not shown); its mystery screen lays the first three frames as the Wrapped draws them (WrappedFrame), a promise while the year is read. Open My Wrapped shows that story from its start (show_wrapped reuses a story read for the welcome); closing the Wrapped over the welcome only steps aside, so the cards stay; the welcome's close forgets a year it read and nobody showed. A scene's photos and light now land on a story read and not yet shown (the told counter alone guards a stale one). The welcome's sheet is never dismissed by Escape. Checks: window checks welcome_reel (the year read, its cards on the welcome and not the Wrapped), wrapped, welcome_card, sheets, help, design_system; oni-app lib tests; catalogue; clippy on oni-app.

title: CLAUDE.md: a digital photo's virtual negative is a scan made once, its two points a channel with no layer offset and no gamut compressed, a tungsten film blue in daylight, the halation red alone
detail: The virtual film paragraph says the scene reaches layers balanced for the stock's own light, so a tungsten film turns daylight blue (#3875), and that a neutral exposes the three layers alike with each channel's black on the bare film and its white at the sensor's saturation, in place of the filtration (#3878); a new paragraph tells the scan made once and read as a scanned negative's (#3872) and the halation on the red layer alone.

title: The welcome's two small gifts play films of the real app, shot by a script on a held clock; the huge gift's pictures made again on the new virtual negative
detail: welcome_films (a window check, run by scripts/welcome-assets with ONI_WELCOME_FILMS) launches the app on the welcome's own photos as digital photos on the neutral film and films, on a held clock at twice the pixels, the photo flying from the gallery into the editor, the editor turning into the export and back, then the Kit (The Lens DB simulated) taking a Nikon FM2 through Search Gear. Each film is one JPEG of its frames and a list of holds (ui/welcome/film-interface.*, film-collection.*); help::reels decodes them off the interface's thread and the welcome plays the screen's film from the moment its words come (Reduce Motion: the frame held longest), its drawn scene where a film cannot be read. scripts/welcome-assets now makes every welcome picture in one command: the huge gift's photo and prints (re-run on 96df856a's virtual negative), each gift's still, then both films. Checks: welcome_films, welcome_reel, welcome_card, sheet_stack, sheets, help, design_system; oni-app lib tests; catalogue; architecture; clippy on oni-app.

title: A block of the interface thread past 5 s writes where it waits: the system's sample, its main thread's heaviest path, innermost first
detail: The owner's app froze after a sleep and left no trace: its log lay on the T7, which unmounted, and two relaunches rotated it out. Not reproduced here: the display slept and woke (pmset displaysleepnow, caffeinate -u) without a block; a volume holding the support, the caches and a roll, force-detached mid-journey and mid-edit (hdiutil), blocked nothing, SQLite answering at once and its writes failing at once. The watchdog now runs /usr/bin/sample on its own process once a block passes LONG_BLOCK and writes the main thread's frames, function and module, never a path or an address, so the next freeze names its wait.
